# Decision Log

Record decisions that future agents or maintainers must understand. Prefer short entries over long narratives.

Some entries reference Arinco-internal development aids — agent-harness configuration, agent skills, local eval tooling — that are deliberately not part of the delivered repository (see "What this repository deliberately does not contain" in `CONTRIBUTING.md`). The decisions stand on their own; only those aids live outside this repo.

## Format

```markdown
## YYYY-MM-DD — Decision Title

**Status:** proposed | accepted | superseded

**Context:** What forced the decision?

**Decision:** What did we choose?

**Rationale:** Why this over the alternatives?

**Consequences:** What changes because of this?
```

## 2026-05-19 — Use Markdown Frontmatter and Manifest-Based Discovery

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Arn needs project memory that works across AI coding agents without locking into one vendor or overloading context windows.

**Decision:** Use markdown docs with YAML frontmatter, aggregate live docs into `docs/_manifest.yaml`, and require agents to update documentation as part of code changes.

**Rationale:** This keeps context human-readable, version-controlled, token-efficient, and portable across agents.

**Consequences:** Every live doc needs frontmatter, and the manifest must be regenerated after meaningful documentation changes.

## 2026-05-19 — Keep Bootstrap Documentation Lean

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The first scaffold created too many placeholder docs and repeated the same maintenance workflow across several files before Arn had a defined purpose or implementation.

**Decision:** Keep only `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/_manifest.yaml`, `docs/canonical/project-brief.md`, and `docs/canonical/decisions.md` until the project has real architecture, reference, or operations facts.

**Rationale:** Fewer files reduce token overhead and drift risk while preserving the useful manifest-first discovery pattern.

**Consequences:** Architecture, reference, operations, archive, skill, and path-scoped instruction files should be added only when there is concrete content to maintain.

## 2026-05-19 — Import PoC Codebase As the Initial Baseline

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Arn is the productionisation project for an existing proof of concept in `~/Coding/ArnBulletinGenerator`. The fastest reliable path is to preserve the working implementation first, then harden and rename deliberately.

**Decision:** Copy the PoC implementation into the repository as-is, excluding git metadata, local secrets, dependency directories, build outputs, logs, Azurite state, and generated archives. Keep current `ArnBulletinGenerator.*` names temporarily.

**Rationale:** A direct import creates a buildable baseline and avoids mixing source import with risky namespace/project renames or architecture changes.

**Consequences:** Future work should first verify build/test parity, then plan production hardening and optional renaming as separate changes.

## 2026-05-19 — Create Real Architecture, Reference, and Operations Docs After Source Analysis

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The initial lean scaffold deferred architecture/reference/operations docs until actual facts existed. The work order, presentation, and PoC now provide enough durable context.

**Decision:** Add `docs/canonical/architecture.md`, `docs/reference/source-context.md`, `docs/reference/poc-inventory.md`, `docs/reference/productionisation-backlog.md`, and `docs/operations/local-development.md`.

**Rationale:** These files now contain project-specific facts, not placeholder guidance, and will help future agents avoid re-reading large source documents unnecessarily.

**Consequences:** The manifest includes these docs, and agents should use them before diving into the full PoC codebase.

## 2026-05-19 — Sanitize Imported Webhook Parameter

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The imported PoC `deployment/main.bicepparam` contained a live-looking Power Automate webhook URL with a signature query parameter.

**Decision:** Replace the committed webhook value with an empty parameter and document that webhook URLs must be injected through CI/CD variables or secure parameter files.

**Rationale:** Webhook URLs with signatures behave like secrets and should not be preserved in source control.

**Consequences:** Deployments need a secure source for `webhookEndpointUrl`; local/default parameter files intentionally disable webhook notifications unless configured.

## 2026-05-19 — First Cleanup Pass Preserves Behaviour

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After importing the PoC baseline, the repo contained generated build artifacts, dependency folders, duplicated/imported documentation, a standalone partner-admin script, production assembly test mocks, environment-specific deployment parameters, and baseline warnings.

**Decision:** Apply only low-risk cleanup that preserves product behaviour: remove generated artifacts, delete duplicate/orphaned imported files, move test-only in-memory repositories into the test project, fix nullable interop warnings, sanitize deployment defaults, and split frontend vendor chunks.

**Rationale:** This improves repository hygiene before git initialization and productionisation work without renaming projects or refactoring core orchestration logic.

**Consequences:** The production Infrastructure assembly no longer contains test-only mock repositories, the root architecture source is `docs/canonical/architecture.md`, deployment-specific values must be injected securely, and future cleanup should still avoid broad namespace or orchestrator refactors until the baseline is production-validated.

## 2026-05-19 — Defer Toolchain Unification Until Dependency Policy Is Explicit

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The imported repo mixes npm lockfiles with Bun-oriented root convenience scripts. A second cleanup review identified this inconsistency, but converting the root scripts to npm-compatible commands would require adding and locking additional root dependencies such as `concurrently` and `azurite`. Separately, removing `web/.npmrc` caused `npm ci` to fail because the current React 19 dependency set still needs `legacy-peer-deps=true`.

**Decision:** Keep the current root Bun convenience scripts and retain `web/.npmrc` for now. Treat toolchain unification as a deliberate follow-up once the team chooses the root package-manager policy.

**Rationale:** This avoids unnecessary dependency churn during cleanup while preserving a working install/build path.

**Consequences:** Contributors should treat Bun as optional except for the current root convenience scripts; backend and `web/` workflows remain npm-compatible. Future cleanup can revisit root script portability after deciding whether to formalize npm-only or Bun-supported workflows.

## 2026-05-19 — Remediate Semantic Kernel Vulnerability With Minimal Patch Upgrade

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The build was warning on `GHSA-2ww3-72rp-wpp4` because `Microsoft.SemanticKernel` and `Microsoft.SemanticKernel.PromptTemplates.Handlebars` were pinned at `1.70.0` in `ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure.csproj`.

**Decision:** Upgrade both Semantic Kernel packages to `1.71.0`, the first fixed version for the advisory, without changing the surrounding template-rendering integration.

**Rationale:** Arn uses only a narrow Semantic Kernel surface area (`Kernel`, `KernelArguments`, and Handlebars prompt rendering), so the smallest fixed-version upgrade removes the vulnerability with minimal compatibility risk.

**Consequences:** The .NET build now passes with 0 warnings and 0 errors, and the non-integration test suite still passes unchanged.

## 2026-05-19 — Make Deployment Defaults Safe For First Commit

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The final secret/config audit found no live secrets in tracked files, but it did identify deployment and test defaults that could mislead first-time deployers or test runners: `deployment/main.bicepparam` defaulted to `prd`, the `owner` tag was too vague, `deployment/README.md` still referenced non-existent Logic App / Teams-ID setup, and a test `appsettings.json` used dead `${VAR}` placeholder strings that .NET would not interpolate.

**Decision:** Make deployment and test defaults explicitly safe and honest: switch `main.bicepparam` to `environment = 'poc'`, set `owner` to a placeholder, remove stale Logic App/Teams guidance from deployment docs, replace dead `${VAR}` strings in test config with empty values, and mark optional frontend Vite env vars as optional in types.

**Rationale:** These changes reduce first-commit and first-deploy risk without changing application runtime behavior.

**Consequences:** Production naming and notification settings must now be chosen explicitly at deploy time, test config no longer implies fake env interpolation, and the repo is clean for git initialization from a secret/config perspective.

## 2026-05-19 — Prefer Truthful Docs and Minimal Config Over Legacy PoC Residue

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After multiple cleanup passes, the remaining issues were tiny but misleading: a duplicate H1, outdated deployment wording, stale clone instructions, redundant `.gitignore` and Prettier entries, and one frontend typing mismatch introduced while making Vite env vars optional.

**Decision:** Apply a final tiny hygiene batch to keep documentation truthful and configuration minimal, while fixing the frontend env-token nullability to match runtime behavior.

**Rationale:** Small inconsistencies create avoidable confusion for future contributors and agents, even when they do not break runtime behavior.

**Consequences:** The repo now has no known stale path references, deployment wording matches the actual IaC, and optional Vite env vars are modeled consistently in types and code.

## 2026-05-19 — Use Autonomous Backend Cleanup Waves Starting With Safe Mechanical Slices

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After repository hygiene was largely complete, the remaining improvement space shifted to backend architecture and code cleanliness. Large refactors would be risky without first improving local clarity, nullability honesty, centralized messaging, and domain invariants in small verified steps.

**Decision:** Use autonomous backend cleanup waves that alternate between discovery and implementation. Start with the safest mechanical slices first: remove obsolete helpers, simplify option defaults, fix misleading nullability, centralize repeated literals, and harden write-once domain properties.

**Rationale:** This improves code quality continuously while keeping each change small enough to verify cheaply and back out mentally if needed.

**Consequences:** The backend cleanup plan now favors repeated small verified improvements over immediate large orchestrator refactors. Bigger architectural changes remain deferred until the low-risk cleanup surface is exhausted.

## 2026-05-19 — Prefer Verified Zero-Behavior Backend Cleanup Slices Before New Testability Seams

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Later backend-cleanup discovery waves surfaced several similarly small candidates: broaden not-found error constant reuse into repositories, remove a dead `BroadcastOrchestratorTests` mock setup, or add a `TimeProvider` seam to `CronParser` for more deterministic tests. A follow-up attempt to remove two supposedly stale infrastructure namespace imports failed because that namespace also exposes extension methods used by those files.

**Decision:** Sequence waves around zero-behavior candidates first, but validate namespace-based extension dependencies before treating a using as stale. Defer the `CronParser` seam until the safer cleanup surface is thinner.

**Rationale:** This keeps the cleanup waves aligned with the original strategy while avoiding false-positive cleanup that changes compilation behavior through hidden extension-method coupling.

**Consequences:** Waves 6-10 remain accepted verified cleanup steps, and future discovery should treat namespace imports that carry extension methods as semantic dependencies rather than formatting noise. Wave 8 added `VoiceCalibration` constructor-backed fields and provider string to `init`-only, consistent with the wave-5 `Job` hardening pattern. Wave 9 introduced `ProviderNames.ElevenLabs` as a shared domain constant, replacing the literal in three production files across Infrastructure and Application layers. Wave 10 added an optional `TimeProvider` primary constructor parameter to `CronParser`, enabling deterministic scheduling tests with zero behavioral change to existing callers.

## 2026-05-20 — Adopt Progressive Agent Context Harness

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Arn's documentation system was reviewed against current LLM IDE/CLI practices. The existing manifest-first model was strong, but future agent work needs clearer tool adapters, prompt storage, on-demand project skills, richer doc metadata, and local validation without adding CI wiring yet.

**Decision:** Keep `AGENTS.md` as the canonical always-on instruction file; add thin adapters for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot; move reusable prompt artifacts into `.agents/prompts/`; create portable project skills under using `SKILL.md` as the universal source contract; enrich live-doc frontmatter with volatility/source-of-truth/routing metadata; and use `./scripts/docs.py check` for local validation.

**Rationale:** This preserves the token-efficient progressive-disclosure pattern while preparing the repo for skills/plugins and multiple agent frontends without duplicating instructions or locking project memory to one vendor.

**Consequences:** Prompt artifacts should no longer live under `docs/` unless they are live docs with frontmatter. Tool-specific instruction files should stay as adapters. New repeatable agent workflows should start in, with provider-specific metadata generated or stored outside the portable source skills. Docs/skills can be checked locally with `./scripts/docs.py check`.

## 2026-05-20 — Use a Documentation Harness as the Index Source

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Arn's manifest-first documentation system now has richer generated indexes, universal skills, and enough metadata that manual index maintenance would create drift risk.

**Decision:** Use scripts/docs.py as the primary harness for creating docs, appending durable decisions, creating portable skills, regenerating indexes, and validating documentation health. Keep generated files downstream of source Markdown docs and SKILL.md files.

**Rationale:** LLM agents are better at editing structured source files than maintaining duplicate indexes by hand. A single deterministic harness improves searchability, keeps generated artifacts fresh, and preserves the progressive-disclosure architecture.

**Consequences:** Agents should use `scripts/docs.py new-doc`, `add-decision`, `new-skill`, `generate`, and `check` for documentation workflows. Generated files such as `docs/_manifest.yaml`, `docs/_search.jsonl`, `docs/_sections.yaml`,, and `llms.txt` should not be edited manually.

## 2026-05-20 — Use Routed Discovery and a Single Documentation Harness

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The documentation system had grown stronger generated indexes, but old wrapper scripts and multiple discovery entrypoints made the agent-facing interface more ambiguous than necessary.

**Decision:** Use scripts/docs.py as the only documentation harness interface and use scripts/docs.py route as the default discovery path before opening detailed docs. Remove alternate wrapper scripts and do not document alternate harness entrypoints.

**Rationale:** LLM agents work best with a small number of deterministic commands. A single route command reduces decision overhead, while generated indexes still provide rich search and section metadata underneath.

**Consequences:** Future agents should start substantial work with CONTEXT.md plus scripts/docs.py route, create sources with new-doc/add-decision/new-skill, regenerate with generate, and validate with check or doctor. Additional generated indexes may evolve, but they remain implementation details behind the harness.

## 2026-05-21 — Defer Static Fallback Audio File — Requires ARN Business Decision

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Productionisation review identified that when the primary pipeline fails and no prior broadcast exists (first broadcast of the day or cascading failure), the system has no fallback audio to air, resulting in silence. A static prerecorded traffic announcement stored in blob storage would guarantee something airs as a last resort.

**Decision:** Defer implementation. This is not purely a technical decision — it requires ARN to specify: who records the file, what it says, how often it's refreshed, and who owns the content. Log as an open question for the next ARN engagement session.

**Rationale:** A static audio file is content, not infrastructure. ARN must own the recording, script, and refresh cadence. Implementing it without ARN input risks producing inappropriate or stale content.

**Consequences:** The dead-air risk exists until ARN provides a static fallback file. Documented as a known ops gap. All other fallback paths (reuse prior broadcast) remain active.

## 2026-05-21 — Implement Private Endpoints for AI Services — Requires ARN Network Coordination

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Azure AI Services endpoint (Azure OpenAI) is publicly accessible with key-based auth. VNet integration is already available but private endpoints would eliminate public exposure entirely. The security team has flagged this as a priority.

**Decision:** Implement private endpoints for AI Services. This requires coordination with ARN's network team to provision private DNS zones and allocate subnet space for the private endpoints.

**Rationale:** Eliminates public exposure of the AI Services endpoint. With VNet integration already in place, the plumbing is ready — only the endpoint configuration is needed.

**Consequences:** ARN's network team must: (1) provision private DNS zones for AI Services, (2) allocate IP space in the integration subnet, (3) approve the change. The Bicep module already accepts virtualNetworkSubnetId; private endpoint resources can be added when the network prerequisites are met.

## 2026-05-24 — Apply First-Sprint Productionisation Hardening

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Cloud architecture review identified critical and high-severity gaps in the imported deployment: Function App HTTP triggers were anonymous behind a header-only middleware check that could be spoofed because Easy Auth was conditional on an empty default param; data-plane services were reachable on public endpoints; storage replication was LRS; staging slot shared queue connection with production; ~40 app settings were duplicated between slots; key services had no diagnostic settings; the webhook URL was passed as a plain app setting; the AI model name was hardcoded in three places; and the CI/CD pipeline had no environment approval gate and silently swallowed frontend lint/test failures.

**Decision:** Land the first-sprint hardening items in one pass: (1) make aadClientId and aadTenantId required Bicep params with no defaults; enforce Easy Auth requireAuthentication=Return401 with /api/health excluded; harden AuthorizationMiddleware to validate the X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL JWT and fail-closed when AAD config is missing. (2) Add a private-endpoints module covering Storage (blob/table/queue), Key Vault, and AI Services, with optional private DNS zone wiring; gate via deployPrivateEndpoints=true and dataPlanePublicNetworkAccess=Disabled in prod/preprod bicepparams. (3) Parameterise storage SKU and default prod/preprod to Standard_ZRS. (4) Disable queue/timer trigger functions on the staging slot via slot-sticky AzureWebJobs.<name>.Disabled settings. (5) Extract shared app settings into a commonAppSettings var consumed by both slots. (6) Add diagnostic settings on Function App, Key Vault, and AI Services. (7) Resolve the webhook KV-reference bug by passing webhookEnabled as a bool and emitting the @Microsoft.KeyVault reference only when enabled. (8) Promote the AI model name to a single aiModelName param. (9) Remove continueOnError from frontend lint/test, convert prod's first deploy job to a deployment job with environment: 'arn-prod' for manual approval, and scaffold a Deploy_Dev stage on the develop branch.

**Rationale:** These nine items are the production-correctness floor identified in the review. They are independently small but together close the auth bypass, end public-internet exposure of data services, give the system a chance of surviving an AZ failure, prevent staging from competing with prod for queue work, and make the CI/CD pipeline honest about test failures. All cross-environment values that the team must supply (AAD tenant/client IDs, PE subnet ID, private DNS zone IDs) are explicit placeholders that will fail Bicep validation if not replaced, which is the desired fail-closed behaviour.

**Consequences:** Bicep validation will fail until ARN supplies AAD client/tenant IDs in every bicepparam. Prod and preprod deploys additionally require the private-endpoint subnet ID and five private DNS zone resource IDs; the network team owns these. The Function App will reject all non-/api/health traffic without a valid AAD principal. Storage prod cost rises slightly with ZRS. The CI/CD pipeline now blocks Deploy_Prod behind a manual approval check on the 'arn-prod' environment, which must be created in Azure DevOps before the next prod deploy. A Deploy_Dev stage now runs on develop branch pushes and requires Arn-Dev-Vars + Arn-Dev-Secrets variable groups and an arn-dev-sp service connection. The webhook KV-reference bug fix changes how Webhook__Enabled is computed: it is now driven by whether webhookEndpointUrl was supplied to main.bicep, not by the resolved KV reference string.

## 2026-05-24 — Use Azure DevOps as Sole CI/CD Target

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The imported PoC carried both .github/workflows/ (ci.yml, deploy.yml) and the agent-built .azuredevops/azure-pipelines.yml. Maintaining two pipelines doubles drift risk and CI cost.

**Decision:** Remove .github/workflows/ entirely. Azure DevOps Pipelines is the only CI/CD target. Build once in CI, publish functions-package + web-dist artifacts, consume them in every deploy stage.

**Rationale:** ARN's existing tooling is Azure DevOps; pipeline already exists with two-gate prod approval, slot warmup with auto-rollback, Bicep what-if review, and post-deploy autoscale/alerts. Maintaining a parallel GitHub Actions flow added nothing.

**Consequences:** PR validation and deploys run from Azure DevOps only. Engineers do not need to keep GitHub Actions in sync. If the org later requires multi-platform support, restore a thin adapter pipeline.

## 2026-05-24 — Identity-Based Storage Throughout — No Connection Strings in Production

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The PoC used AzureWebJobsStorage connection strings for Functions queue/timer triggers and direct connection strings in DI. This required shared-key access enabled on the storage account, which is incompatible with the production posture of allowSharedKeyAccess=false.

**Decision:** Function host triggers use Connection=AzureWebJobsStorage with AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName env var so the host resolves identity-based access. Application-layer DI reads StorageOptions.AccountName and constructs BlobServiceClient/QueueServiceClient with TokenCredential. Local dev falls back to UseDevelopmentStorage=true via Azurite.

**Rationale:** Eliminates a class of credential-rotation risk, allows storage networkAcls.defaultAction=Deny, supports private-endpoint-only access, and integrates cleanly with the Function App managed identity already granted Storage Blob/Table/Queue Data Contributor and Storage Blob Delegator.

**Consequences:** Local devs need an Azurite container or storage emulator. Prod and preprod deployments require the Function App MSI to hold the four storage data roles (already in role-assignments.bicep). Any new storage interaction must go through the DI-registered clients, not new connection strings.

## 2026-05-24 — Operator/Admin RBAC Enforced in AuthorizationMiddleware

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Easy Auth + the original middleware only verified that a caller presented a valid AAD principal — it did not distinguish between read-only operators and admins. Anyone in the tenant who could obtain a token reached every endpoint including POST /broadcast and DELETE /schedules.

**Decision:** Define two AAD app roles, Operator and Admin. The middleware parses the X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL JWT, extracts the roles claim, and enforces a route → required-role matrix (RouteRoleMatrix). GET → Operator; POST /jobs/{id}/{approve,reject,publish,regenerate} → Operator; everything else mutating → Admin.

**Rationale:** Defence in depth: even if Easy Auth misbehaves, the middleware short-circuits on missing roles. The same principal-parsing helpers are unit-tested via internals-visible-to. The role names are configurable in the AAD app registration without code changes.

**Consequences:** AAD app registration must define Operator + Admin app roles and assign them to users/groups before the next deploy. Frontend should display role-aware UI (hide admin actions for Operator). Tests for new endpoints must verify the right role is enforced.

## 2026-05-24 — Two-Gate Approval for Production Deploys

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The single arn-prod approval gate was triggered at the start of Deploy_Prod, then every subsequent step (infra → KV sync → staging deploy → slot swap → frontend) ran unattended. The slot swap is irreversible without auto-rollback; a single approval at the start gave operators no opportunity to inspect staging before committing to prod.

**Decision:** Two distinct Azure DevOps environments gate the prod pipeline: arn-prod (approve start, runs infra + KV + staging deploy) and arn-prod-swap (approve the irreversible swap after staging has been tested). Post-swap health check runs auto-rollback (swap back) on failure and fails the pipeline.

**Rationale:** Mirrors industry pattern for high-risk deploys (e.g. canary + manual promote). Operators get a structured opportunity to confirm 'staging looks good' before promoting. Failure path is automatic so a broken deploy doesn't sit in prod waiting for manual intervention.

**Consequences:** Both arn-prod and arn-prod-swap environments must be created in Azure DevOps with manual approval and Exclusive lock enabled. Total prod deploy time grows by the second-approval wait. If urgent deploys are needed, operators must be reachable for both gates.
## 2026-05-26 — Reuse Existing CI/CD Service Principal

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** PoC has service principal `be809355-19e4-4cad-b3a7-a4148919d801` with Contributor on PoC RG.

**Decision:** Reuse the same SP for all environments. Assign Contributor per new resource group.

**Rationale:** 14-week engagement, two-gate approval already in place. Per-environment SP adds overhead without proportional security gain.

**Consequences:** If ARN security later requires per-environment SPs, it is a config change not a code change.

## 2026-05-26 — Environment Model: dev / test / prod per SOW

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Bicep was written with dev/preprod/prod. SOW line says 'Development, Test, and Production'.

**Decision:** Align to SOW naming. Rename `preprod` to `test` across Bicep param files and deployment pipeline.

**Rationale:** Contractual alignment with the SOW.

**Consequences:** Bicep param files need `test` not `preprod`. Pipeline stages and variable groups referencing `preprod` must be updated.

## 2026-05-26 — Workshops Reduced to Two Synchronous Sessions

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Originally planned 4 workshops (scope, playout, Azure, approval). Many items have objective answers that do not require group discussion.

**Decision:** Reduce to 2 synchronous sessions: (1) scope alignment + delivery plan; (2) operator workflow + UI design. Move everything else to async with named owners.

**Rationale:** Workshops should only exist for genuine multi-person collaborative discussion. Factual questions with objective answers do not need a meeting.

**Consequences:** Async items must be actively chased by the Arinco deploy operator. Remaining workshop topics are assigned to specific owners with deadlines.

## 2026-05-26 — Edit-Before-Approve Is NO for Release 1

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Question of whether operators can edit generated scripts before approving.

**Decision:** Release 1 supports approve, reject, and regenerate only. No inline editing.

**Rationale:** Editing introduces audit complexity — which version actually played? Reject + regenerate covers most cases without compromising the audit trail.

**Consequences:** If an operator genuinely needs to fix a single word, they reject with feedback and the system regenerates.

## 2026-05-26 — ATN Transition Is ARN's Responsibility

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Early workshop planning included ATN cutover approach as a workshop topic.

**Decision:** Remove ATN transition from Arinco's scope entirely.

**Rationale:** SOW says deliver the platform. How ARN decommissions ATN is their business decision.

**Consequences:** We can be informed of ARN's transition plan but do not design or recommend a cutover approach.

## 2026-05-26 — Pilot Station Name Is Configuration, Not a Planning Dependency

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Early planning treated pilot station name as a workshop output blocking architecture.

**Decision:** Station identity is configuration — name, market, format, and schedule are all dashboard-configurable values. Not blocking and not a workshop item.

**Rationale:** Code is market-agnostic. Configuration work happens in weeks 4–5 of the engagement. No architecture or design work depends on knowing the pilot station name.

**Consequences:** No architecture or design work depends on knowing the pilot station name. Configuration implementation is deferred to the scheduled config work phase.

## 2026-05-27 — Prompts as Files, Not Compiled Code

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** System/draft/review/refine prompts were embedded in C# code, requiring a rebuild for any prompt change.

**Decision:** Extract prompts to `prompts/*.md` files. `LlmScriptGenerator.cs` loads them at startup via `LoadPrompt()` and throws `FileNotFoundException` if any file is missing, with no compiled-in fallback.

**Rationale:** Allows prompt iteration without rebuild. Fail-fast on missing files prevents silent degradation.

**Consequences:** Prompt changes no longer require a .NET rebuild. The `prompts/` directory contains four files: system.md, draft.md, review.md, refine.md. Deployment must include these files.

## 2026-05-27 — IContentSafetyFilter in Domain, Not Application

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Infrastructure could not reference Application due to Clean Architecture dependency rules. The content safety interface was needed by `BroadcastOrchestrator` in the Application layer.

**Decision:** Place interface `IContentSafetyFilter` in `Domain/Interfaces/` with `ConfigurableContentSafetyFilter` implementation in Infrastructure.

**Rationale:** Domain has no dependencies on outer layers. Infrastructure implements domain interfaces. This preserves the Clean Architecture dependency inversion principle.

**Consequences:** The orchestrator references `IContentSafetyFilter` from Domain. Infrastructure wires the concrete filter at startup. Content safety rules are not yet populated (blocked on the ARN content lead).

## 2026-05-27 — Logic App Notification as IaC

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** PoC used a manually configured Power Automate webhook for Teams notifications. This was not repeatable or version-controlled.

**Decision:** Inspect the PoC Power Automate webhook, then codify as `deployment/modules/logic-app-notification.bicep` with Teams API connection, access policy, and Adaptive Card template.

**Rationale:** Infrastructure-as-code makes the notification pipeline repeatable, reviewable, and deployable across environments.

**Consequences:** One-time manual OAuth consent per environment is required. The Logic App module is optional and gated by `webhookEndpointUrl` being non-empty.

## 2026-05-27 — Direct HTTP Trigger as Default Test Mode

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The broadcast dedup check in `BroadcastQueueTrigger` incorrectly blocked jobs in `Requested` status. The schedule poller test path took ~90s for feedback.

**Decision:** Fix the dedup bug to allow jobs in `Requested` status through. Default `scripts/test-bulletin.sh` to direct HTTP trigger mode (~23s) over the schedule poller path (~90s).

**Rationale:** Faster feedback loop for developers testing the broadcast pipeline. The schedule poller remains the production path.

**Consequences:** Test script uses `POST /api/broadcasts` by default. Schedule poller path is tested separately in integration tests.

## 2026-05-27 — LikeC4 Architecture-as-Code

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Standalone HTML diagrams (`docs/diagrams/system-architecture.html`, etc.) were manually maintained and not source-controlled in a diffable format.

**Decision:** Maintain architecture diagrams as `.c4` source files in `architecture/` directory with 4 named views. Export to PNG via `scripts/export-diagrams.sh`. Replace standalone HTML diagrams as the canonical architecture model.

**Rationale:** Source-controlled `.c4` files are diffable, reviewable in PRs, and can be exported to multiple output formats.

**Consequences:** The `architecture/` directory contains spec.c4, model.c4, views.c4, and likec4.config.json. Exported images go to `architecture/images/`. PRs involving architecture changes must update the `.c4` files.

## 2026-05-27 — Voice Calibration Seeded on Startup

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ElevenLabs TTS requires initial voice calibration before producing accurate speech duration predictions. This was previously a manual step.

**Decision:** Seed default voice calibration on first startup. `scripts/local-start.sh` auto-calibrates the default voice.

**Rationale:** Eliminates the manual calibration step, making the local dev experience zero-config after initial setup.

**Consequences:** First local start takes slightly longer due to calibration. Subsequent starts reuse cached calibration data.

## 2026-06-01 — Pilot scope direction from Workshop 1

**Status:** superseded (2026-07-13 — pilot station identity and market clarified; see below)

**Context:** Workshop 1 (Scope Alignment), 1 Jun 2026, with ARN business owners (facilitated by Arinco) confirmed the Release 1 / pilot boundary that SDD section 4.5 was waiting on.

**Decision:** The leading pilot-market candidate is Hot Tomato (Gold Coast, QLD) — agreed in the room but **not locked**; it needs internal approval (it is a #1 station) and ARN is taking it away to confirm. It is favoured because ATN does not service it (ARN is contractually barred from airing AI traffic on ATN-contracted markets), it is a decent-sized market, and ARN already produces its own traffic there. A second small regional market not serviced by ATN (e.g. Scottsdale) will also run to observe low/no-traffic behaviour (a traffic clock would need building; mainly to hear scripting and voice, going to air TBD). Mandatory controls that cannot be deferred: operator approval / human-in-the-loop (a board-signed-off control) and content-safety checks. Deferrable if output quality is met: automatic Zetta delivery, full dev/test/prod (a single environment is acceptable for the pilot), and notifications. The whole clock's bulletins are replaced (not a subset); build with variables, never hard-code a station, as clock structures vary per station.

**Rationale:** The 4 July gate is the ATN contract termination-notice date, not a go-live date; it only requires ARN to be internally confident (a small review group) that the output is good. Putting a bad product to air is worse than missing the date. The two gating quality measures are voice quality and script/content quality, which must be same or better than ATN.

**Consequences:** SDD section 4.5 updated; RISK-04 (pilot station not named) downgraded but not closed — a leading candidate is identified, pending approval; task board Workshop 1 marked concluded; success-criteria SC-01 notes updated. Hot Tomato needs internal ARN approval. The Gold Coast operator is the on-the-ground SME.

## 2026-06-01 — Weather and fuel are in-scope content sources alongside traffic

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN is contracting HERE for traffic, weather and fuel (about 10k AUD over 3 years). Workshop 1 (1 Jun 2026) discussed which sources bulletins should cover per market. This supersedes the project-brief non-goal that listed weather as not committed for Release 1.

**Decision:** Weather and fuel are in scope as bulletin content sources, selected per market. Default ordering: exhaust traffic (including planned roadworks) before weather and fuel, but major weather (e.g. a hurricane) overrides and is covered immediately, since it also affects traffic. Operators can steer or override via the existing reject-and-regenerate-with-notes workflow.

**Rationale:** Regional markets often have little or no traffic, so weather and fuel keep the bulletin useful; some metros already pair weather with traffic. HERE provides all three sources cheaply.

**Consequences:** project-brief Non-Goals updated to remove the weather exclusion; SDD content sources reflect weather and fuel; ACMA/compliance implications for weather and news under the broadcast code flagged to the ARN content lead.

## 2026-06-01 — Dead-air fallback policy for the pilot

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Workshop 1 (1 Jun 2026) agreed what should air when a fresh bulletin cannot be produced in time.

**Decision:** Reuse the most recent same-day bulletin (never the night-before's, to avoid stale data). If the first bulletin of the day cannot be produced, play a generic pre-recorded filler cart. Traffic carries no compliance obligation (unlike news), so worst case the slot is simply skipped. Failures should be monitored, with an operator option to play the filler.

**Rationale:** Avoids dead air without ever airing stale traffic. Aligns with success-criteria SC-04 (fallback uses only non-expired traffic data).

**Consequences:** SDD fallback section and the section 13 open item updated; the task-board fallback-hardening task references this policy. ARN to provide the generic filler audio content.

## 2026-06-02 — Operator workflow & review-screen direction from Workshop 2

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Workshop 2 (Operator workflow + UI), 2 Jun 2026, with ARN content/playout SMEs (facilitated by Arinco) defined how the mandatory human-in-the-loop step works and what the review screen needs. SDD sections 4.2 and 4.7 were waiting on this.

**Decision:** (1) The review screen supports click-word-to-audio, inline script edit + regenerate, direct editing of the prioritized traffic list (reorder / include-exclude / omit stale), reject-to-fallback, positive "good-run" reporting of priority arterials, and a per-market priority-roads list. (2) Bulletins are information-only — never advise or assume the listener's situation. (3) Access is two-tier (Admin / Operator) with per-market/station scoping via an in-app admin assignment page, plus audit logging; operators are local to their market. (4) Notifications: dashboard primary + Teams channel + shared escalation channel/alert; no phone/SMS for the pilot. (5) The bulletin is 30s pure traffic; co-located same-market stations may share one script/audio (each its own cart), pending the per-station-tag decision. (6) Scheduling, the ~8-minute approval window, and Zetta's fire-and-forget delivery are addressed by a separate options brief (fixed-event anchoring, multi-candidate generation, mandatory fallback-fill cart) for SG2 ratification.

**Rationale:** The approval window is tight and live-radio timing drifts; the review screen must support a correct approve/reject decision fast, and the system must never air stale (>30 min) or wrong content. Per-market scoping prevents the near-certain error of approving the wrong station. Pure-traffic scripts make bulletin sharing safe and cheap.

**Consequences:** SDD sections 4.2 and 4.7 added/updated and section 13 open items updated; the scheduling/delivery options brief created for SG2; RISK-08 (Zetta delivery) and RISK-28 (dead-air) linked; open decisions routed — Zetta delivery-confirmation capability to ARN playout, cadence/punctuality to content, HERE incident-detail richness to an Arinco investigation, per-station tags to ARN.

## 2026-06-03 — Standardise all diagrams on LikeC4, including CI/CD

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-05-27 decision moved architecture diagrams to LikeC4 but left the standalone HTML diagrams (`docs/diagrams/*.html`) in place, and the Stage Gate 2 SDD still embedded PNGs rendered from those HTML files. The LikeC4 model also had no CI/CD view, so the pipeline diagram stayed an HTML one that had drifted from the actual `.azuredevops/azure-pipelines.yml` (it depicted the superseded single-environment root pipeline rather than the multi-stage one with environment promotion and two-gate prod approval).

**Decision:** Use LikeC4 as the single source for every diagram. Added a `cicd-pipeline` view (and `stage` / `approval` element kinds) modelling the real pipeline: CI build/test/lint, Deploy to Dev on the development branch, Bicep what-if on main, and a two-gate production path (staging-slot deploy, swap, post-swap health check, auto-rollback). Re-pointed the three SDD figures to the LikeC4 exports and removed the `docs/diagrams/*.html` set.

**Rationale:** One diffable, reviewable source removes the drift that left the SDD shipping a pipeline diagram that no longer matched the deployment code, and brings CI/CD under the same architecture-as-code model as everything else.

**Consequences:** Diagrams regenerate with `./scripts/export-diagrams.sh`; the SDD figures are copied from `architecture/images/`. `solution-design.md`, `stage-gate-2-sdd-deliverables-plan.md`, `sg2-review-pack.md`, and the SDD README now reference the LikeC4 exports. Model summaries that render in client figures were de-identified (no model IDs) and had em dashes removed. The duplicate root `azure-pipelines.yml` (imported PoC baseline) remains a separate cleanup item.

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Our plan was to adopt the existing PoC RG (ARN-AUE-RSG-TNP) as dev to save effort, lifting the Arinco deploy operator's access there to Owner + Key Vault Administrator. On 4 Jun, the ARN Technology Lead (ARN Technology) responded to the Azure outreach: happy to grant Owner on the PoC, but prefers to rebuild dev/test (and prod) clean using ARN's standard environment-reflecting naming convention rather than reuse the PoC RG.

**Decision:** Adopt ARN's Azure naming convention for all new environments and stand up fresh dev/test/prod resource groups. Project code is IBP (Information Bulletin Platform), region Australia East. Per the ARN Technology Lead's confirmed list (4 Jun) the form is ARN-AUE-[Env]-[Type]-IBP01 (environment before resource type, project code and instance number last), e.g. dev RG ARN-AUE-DEV-RSG-IBP01 and dev Key Vault ARN-AUE-DEV-KYV-IBP01. The AAD app registration remains the longest-lead dependency (ARN identity team).

## 2026-06-04 — Raise LikeC4 diagram quality (boundaries, legends, edges, layout, file split)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Web research into LikeC4 best practices (the official docs, the `likec4/template` repo, and community examples) found concrete quality gaps in our model: opaque container fills made nested components hard to read (blue-on-blue), exports omitted the legend and title, parallel relationships merged into unreadable `[...]` labels, layouts had avoidable edge crossings, three tags were declared but never used, and `model.c4` mixed the platform, external services, and the CI/CD pipeline in one file.

**Decision:** Apply the high-value improvements within LikeC4 (no draw.io round-trip): translucent boundaries via `styles.defaults.group` opacity in `likec4.config.json` plus per-view element `opacity` on the system/pipeline boundaries, and `opacity` on the deployment node kinds; bake the legend and title into the live export with `--notation --description`; split merged edges with `multiple true` on the `async` kind and a new behaviour-only `data` relationship kind; tune layout with `rank source`/`rank sink` and explicit `autoLayout` separation; add request/response (`<-`) return arrows to the bulletin lifecycle; remove the unused tags (prod-only, pending, disabled); and split `model.c4` into `externals.c4` and `cicd.c4`. Keep the `network-topology` deployment view sparse by suppressing inherited internal relationships and showing only the three topology-level paths (Entra to dashboard, dashboard to Functions, Functions to Zetta); detailed SaaS and private endpoint fan-out belongs in focused companion views. The SDD figures use a separate clean export (no legend or banner) so they sit under their Typst captions.

**Rationale:** These are textbook LikeC4 readability levers we were not using. Translucent boundaries and de-merged edges are the biggest legibility wins; baked-in legends make shared images self-documenting; the file split and tag cleanup keep the model maintainable as it grows.

**Consequences:** `architecture/` now contains spec.c4, model.c4, externals.c4, cicd.c4, deployment.c4, views.c4, and likec4.config.json, with eight views (system-context, platform-architecture, bulletin-lifecycle, security-overview, cicd-pipeline, network-topology, data-plane, delivery-path). The live `./scripts/export-diagrams.sh` set carries a legend and title banner; the SDD `assets/` copies are exported clean (see the SDD README). `architecture/.likec4/` (the layout cache) is gitignored. The canonical LikeC4 project is `arn-traffic`, so the LikeC4 MCP tools must be called with `project: "arn-traffic"`. The SDD PDF was recompiled with the refreshed figures. Orthogonal/straight edges remain unavailable in LikeC4's renderer (an open upstream feature request), so overview diagrams should reduce relationship count rather than try to force orthogonal routing.

## 2026-06-09 — AI Synthetic-Voice Disclosure: Traffic Is Carved Out

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The ACMA Commercial Radio Code (effective 1 Jul 2026) requires disclosing AI synthetic-voice use for recurring/news programs. The compliance/legal call (9 Jun 2026, ARN Legal) confirmed how it applies to traffic.

**Decision:** Treat AI-generated **traffic** bulletins as **not** requiring mandatory disclosure — the Code explicitly carves out content broadcast during a regularly scheduled / news program "including weather, traffic, music and Advertisements." Weather and fuel-within-a-traffic-update ride the same carve-out. ARN will likely **disclose voluntarily** anyway as editorial policy/marketing (the ARN content lead to confirm with Legal); build no in-product disclosure obligation, but keep a config seam for a voluntary disclosure if ARN elects one.

**Rationale:** The carve-out is explicit; industry rationale is that this content is often outsourced and the licensee can't control third-party AI use. Voluntary disclosure is a brand choice, not a legal requirement.

**Consequences:** No mandatory AI-voice disclosure work for the pilot. Fuel is safe only while self-contained inside the traffic update. Revisit if ARN decides to disclose voluntarily. (CC-001).

## 2026-06-09 — Compliance Retention: 90-Day Audio, 2–3+ Year Audit Logs

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The audit/retention configuration (`deployment/modules/storage.bicep` lifecycle, SDD §8.3) was blocked on a confirmed retention answer. Confirmed on the 9 Jun call (ARN Legal).

**Decision:** Retain **bulletin audio for at least 90 days** (Code requires audio kept 60 days after a complaint; complainants have 30 days to complain → 90 covers it). Retain **approval/audit text logs for ~2–3+ years** (cheap text, useful for a later court case). Only the **aired** bulletin must be retained for the 90 days; retaining other generated candidates is optional and only if it adds no real cost. Limit audit-store access to **ARN Content / Legal** via AAD group. Exact figures to be confirmed by ARN Legal by email.

**Rationale:** Anchors audio to the Code's complaint window and the longer text logs to defamation limitation exposure, while keeping storage cost proportional (audio is the heavy artefact; logs are not).

**Consequences:** Set the storage lifecycle to 90-day audio and long-lived (2–3+ yr) audit logs; wire an AAD group for audit access. Updates SDD §8.3 retention/immutability rows. (CC-002).

**Addendum (12 Jun 2026):** Ratified from the ARN technology side. The ARN technology sign-off's SG2 SDD review markup (10 Jun, the only comment) confirms WORM/immutable audit storage is **not required** and adds that ARN already logs all aired broadcast traffic — but **not scripts or approval evidence** — making the platform the system of record for scripts and approval decisions. (MWR-001/MWR-002).

## 2026-06-09 — Defamation Liability Sits With ARN; Log Approver Identity As Evidence

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Open question on who is liable for a defamatory bulletin and what approval evidence to capture. Confirmed on the 9 Jun call (ARN Legal).

**Decision:** ARN bears publication liability for everything it broadcasts — "the AI wrote it" is **not** a defence. Retain the **approver identity** (AAD principal + timestamp) per bulletin primarily as **evidence** (not for blame; ARN indemnifies employees). Treat the human approval step as the publication-decision control. **Open:** whether bulletins are delivered under a **named individual voice** — doing so creates personal defamation risk for that individual; defer until ARN decides the voice/persona model.

**Rationale:** Matches how ARN already treats published content; the human-in-the-loop is the meaningful control and the audit trail is the evidentiary record.

**Consequences:** Keep mandatory human approval and per-action identity stamping (already implemented). The named-voice decision is gated on ARN's voice/persona choice (see voice-strategy). (CC-003).

## 2026-06-09 — Content-Safety Rules Are Editorial; Place-Name False Positives Use Human-in-the-Loop Exception List

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The content-safety layer (`IContentSafetyFilter`) needed its actual rules and a strategy for legitimate place names that trip a profanity/restricted-term filter. Confirmed on the 9 Jun call (ARN Legal + the ARN content lead).

**Decision:** There is no legal banned-word list — the canonical banned/approved-phrasing list comes from ARN's **content team** (editorial), augmented by the **CRA guidelines** (suicide / domestic violence / reporting on Indigenous people; ARN Legal to share). Handle place-name **false positives** by flagging for a **human reviewer** and **persisting the decision** (allow/deny) so the system learns — a growing exception list — never auto-suppressing genuine news. Accept a **competitor-name blocklist** from ARN to strip competitor mentions at the AI level (nearest street name as fallback phrasing). Use the **listener-known** name for sponsored landmarks/stadiums (place reference, not advertising).

**Rationale:** The rules are editorial judgement, not statute; a learning exception list resolves the slur-vs-legitimate-name problem without dropping real incidents.

**Consequences:** Content-safety layer ingests an editorial list + CRA guidelines + competitor blocklist; the reviewer UI must let an operator persist a place-name exception that feeds back into generation. (CC-004).

## 2026-06-09 — Emergency Broadcasting Stays in Zetta

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN Legal raised ARN's obligation to carry emergency-services messages, which override normal programming. The call and follow-up confirmed how this sits with the platform.

**Decision:** Emergency broadcasting is handled in Zetta, exactly as it is today with ATN. The platform delivers files in the same way, so the existing Zetta emergency override applies unchanged and the platform adds no emergency-suppression behaviour of its own.

**Rationale:** Delivery to Zetta is identical to the current ATN arrangement, so the existing control already covers emergencies. Building a separate suppression path in the platform would duplicate it and take on responsibility that sits with ARN and Zetta.

**Consequences:** No emergency-override build item. Operator documentation can note that emergency handling is an ARN/Zetta function. This corrects the initial capture, which had over-stated a platform override requirement. (CC-005).

## 2026-06-09 — Traffic Data Is Fetched Near Playout (No Separate Freshness Check)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The call asked what freshness threshold the platform should enforce.

**Decision:** Traffic data is fetched shortly before each bulletin, usually around 15 minutes before playout, and cached, so it is current when broadcast. No separate compliance freshness threshold is enforced. The existing staleness safeguard (the Workshop 2 rule that traffic older than ~30 minutes never airs, enforced at playout) remains as the safety net.

**Rationale:** Fetching close to playout keeps the data current without a separate check, and comfortably inside the ARN content lead's ~1 hour editorial expectation. A separate threshold would add machinery for no practical gain.

**Consequences:** No ~60-minute compliance freshness guard is added; the existing staleness safeguard is unchanged. This corrects the initial capture, which had described enforcing a ~1 hour staleness check. (CC-006).

## 2026-06-10 — Hybrid diagram pipeline: LikeC4 model + manual orthogonal presentation renders

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** LikeC4 auto-layout (and every evaluated engine: ELK, dagre, D2) cannot produce orthogonal edge routing with intentional node placement. Bezier spaghetti does not scale with diagram complexity, making auto-layout exports unusable for client-facing structural diagrams such as the network topology in the SDD.

**Decision:** Keep LikeC4 as the single source of truth for the model (elements, relationships, deployment hierarchy, interactive dev server, MCP queries). Add a presentation layer at architecture/renders/: per-view YAML specs with manual coordinates rendered to orthogonal SVG by renders/render.py, which validates every FQN and edge against the likec4 JSON export and fails the export on drift. Every manual render must have a companion LikeC4 view covering the same scope. scripts/export-diagrams.sh runs both pipelines; manual renders overwrite the auto-layout PNG of the same name so document references are unchanged.

**Rationale:** Manual coordinates give presentation-grade output (straight lines, no crossings, stable layout across regenerations). Validating specs against the model export prevents the classic failure mode of hand-drawn diagrams rotting silently as the architecture evolves. Auto-layout remains for exploration, dynamic views, and querying where it works well.

**Consequences:** architecture/renders/ contains render.py, views/network-topology.yaml, an icons/ library, and README.md documenting the decision rule. network-topology.png in architecture/images/ is now the manual render (rasterised at 2x via rsvg-convert). A model change that breaks a presentation spec fails ./scripts/export-diagrams.sh with named drift errors and requires a deliberate spec update.

## 2026-06-10 — Ad Insertion Stays Outside the Bulletin Generator (Pre-Recorded Credits via Aquira & Zetta)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Ads/Aquira had been an open scope question since Workshop 1 (to investigate, not committed for the pilot; an ARN content SME async item on the integration model; RISK-27 tracked the Phase A effort risk). On 10 Jun 2026 the project manager emailed the Arinco deploy operator and the ARN technology sign-off after catching up with the ARN content and commercial teams.

**Decision:** Ad insertion is kept separate from the bulletin generator. Commercial credits are pre-recorded with the pre-determined voices and loaded into Aquira & Zetta through ARN's normal commercial sponsorship process, with no platform involvement. The agreed clock flow is: traffic intro (pre-set in Zetta) → commercial pre credit (pre-recorded) → bulletin playout (latest AI-created version) → commercial post credit (pre-recorded). ARN will model the future-state clock structure on this flow.

**Rationale:** Cleanest for inventory management and credit-line instructions, and it lowers the QA demand on the HITL operator, who reviews only the AI bulletin. Pre-determined voices make pre-recording credits practical, matching ARN's existing sponsorship process.

**Consequences:** No Aquira/ad integration build in any phase: the platform's delivery obligation remains bulletin audio to Zetta only. The an ARN content SME async item (Aquira integration model + effort estimate) is resolved and RISK-27 is closed. The extensible delivery seam in the architecture remains but has no planned consumer. (ADI-001..ADI-004).
