## 2026-06-12 — Domain Models Are Factory-Only Construction (Obsolete Constructors Removed)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An earlier cleanup wave added validating `Create(...)` factories returning `Result<T>` to `Job`, `MarketSchedule`, and `CoverageArea` but left the throwing public constructors behind as `[Obsolete]`, producing 250 CS0618 warnings across 6 production call sites and ~25 test files. The half-migrated state meant two construction conventions coexisted.

**Decision:** Complete the migration and delete the obsolete constructors. Domain models follow one pattern, established by `VoiceSettings`: a public static `Create(...)` returning `Result<T>` as the only public construction path, plus a `[JsonConstructor] private` parameterless constructor for object-initializer use by the factory and JSON reconstitution of already-validated persisted data. `MarketSchedule` lost its primary constructor entirely. Two behavioural by-products were kept deliberately: `ScheduleService.ApplyUpdate` now validates update-command overrides through `Create` (invalid updates fail instead of writing through), and `BroadcastQueueMessage.ToBroadcastRequest` returns `Result<BroadcastRequest>` so a corrupt queue payload throws in the trigger and routes to the poison queue with a precise reason instead of an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

**Rationale:** One construction convention; validation cannot be bypassed; `Result` failures replace exception-based validation consistently with the rest of the codebase; the `[JsonConstructor]` private ctor keeps STJ reconstitution working (deleting the public ctors without it broke `CoverageJson` deserialization and the in-memory deep-copy repositories — caught by 20 test failures during the wave).

**Consequences:** Solution builds with zero compiler warnings (was 298: 250 CS0618, 30 CS8602, 14 CS8604, 4 CS0105). New domain models should follow the same factory pattern. WireMock tests gained null-safe `LastRequest()`/`LastRequestBody()`/`RequestTo(fragment)` helpers on `WireMockTestBase` instead of per-test nullable chains. TimeProvider seams for classes that lack them remain deferred per the existing cleanup-wave decision.

## 2026-06-17 — gpt-5.4-mini is the default LLM; generation model is per-station (superseded 2026-07-06)

**Status:** superseded — see "2026-07-06 — Per-station LLM model selection removed" below. The per-station selector never had a working second option (`gpt-5.4-nano` was selectable but no environment ever deployed it), and the un-deployed ad-hoc `/broadcast` override followed the same pattern; both were removed in favour of one centrally-configured model.

**Context:** A bulletin-quality eval (`scripts/eval.sh --model`, n=9/model) compared gpt-5-mini, gpt-5.1, gpt-5.4-mini, and gpt-5.4-nano on the ATN corpus. gpt-5.4-mini won on duration adherence, AU-reporter idiom, and fabrication discipline (5.1/nano invented drive times). Reasoning effort is model-specific (`LlmScriptGenerator.ResolveReasoningEffort`: `gpt-5.` → `none`, `gpt-5-` → `minimal`).

**Decision:** gpt-5.4-mini is the global default (`main.bicep` `aiModelName`, `function-app`/`ai-services` defaults, `appsettings.json`, dev `local.settings.json`). Operators select the **generation** model per station (`MarketSchedule.LlmModel`, allowed set `LlmModels`: gpt-5.4-mini / gpt-5.4-nano). The **Safety** review stays on the global default for a consistent bar. The unused gpt-5.1 trial deployment was deleted from `cog-arntraffic-prd-aue`.

**Rationale:** Trial-winner on the metrics that matter for the 4 Jul gate; per-station selection lets a market trade cost for quality without touching code; keeping Safety global avoids interface churn and an inconsistent compliance bar.

**Consequences:** Legacy schedules without a model deserialize to the default. Future model swaps follow the documented trial sequence (deploy candidate → eval on the ATN corpus → cut over). Eval pulls the model from `local.settings.json` (`--model` overrides).

## 2026-06-17 — Generalised bulletin data model: congestion corridors, monitored drive-time routes, per-station good-runs, gated detours

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ATN parity needs more than incident corridors: drive-time headlines, incident-free congestion, all-clear "good runs", and the occasional detour. The agreed target shape is (the canonical spec; §7 implementation status, §8 locked decisions).

**Decision:** (1) **Flow congestion is a first-class corridor source** — HERE `/flow` jamFactor segments (≥~5) build incident-free corridors, dedup against incident corridors, and join the same ranked pool; road+direction anchoring is sufficient (never fabricate a cross-street). (2) **Monitored drive-time routes** are per-market config (`MonitoredRoutesOptions`); the self-imposed FC≤3 route-enrichment gate is lifted. (3) **Good-runs are a per-station road list** (`MarketSchedule.GoodRunRoads`, empty = off), separate from the per-market priority-roads *boost* list, ranked below all bad-news — the all-clear bulletin is the emergent result, not a mode. (4) **Detours** are emitted only behind a safety gate (HERE `segmentRef` present, route has start/end, avoided-segment alternative faster and ≤50% longer). (5) **Lead with the worst** corridor and voice its magnitude (qualitatively); a monitored drive-time leads only when it is the worst. (6) **No `jamTendency` trend** — the field is absent from real HERE flow responses, so "building/easing" is deferred to snapshot diffing.

**Rationale:** One generalised, station-agnostic bulletin per market with per-station content toggles matches how ARN wants to scale; ranking (not modes) keeps the structure universal; the detour gate prevents unsafe/invented reroutes; lead-with-worst is core ATN behaviour.

**Consequences:** New domain surface: `CorridorAggregator.BuildCongestionCorridors`, `HereOptions.CongestionJamFactorThreshold`, `MonitoredRouteReporter`/`MonitoredRouteStatus`, `IDetourRoutingProvider`/`DetourSuggestion`, `FuelPriceSummary.LatestModifiedUtc`. Prompts (`system`/`draft`/`review`/`refine`) carry these rules. Per-station styling stays **out**. Canonical detail lives in the spec; this entry is the durable summary.

## 2026-06-17 — Bulletin quality is iterated via an agent-judged review pack, not an automated LLM judge

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An automated ATN-primed LLM judge was added to the eval, then found to self-grade leniently (the author model judging its own output) and to be a weak proxy. The user directed that the agent itself be the judge.

**Decision:** Remove the automated/API LLM judge. The eval emits an **agent-judged review pack** (`eval.sh --review` → `output/eval/review-<ts>.md`) pairing the **source data the writer saw** with each script and the deterministic scores; the agent reads it, scores against the ATN samples, names the weakest layer, tweaks one prompt/data layer, and re-runs. Deterministic scorers (target shape, fabrication, style, safety) remain a coarse net, not the judge. Safety stays rule-based + human gate (never an LLM judge).

**Rationale:** A self-grading author model drifts and inflates; pairing source data with the script is what lets the judge check fidelity; keeping a human/agent in the judging loop matches that the 4 Jul gate is judged by the ARN review group.

**Consequences:** No API judge to maintain or trust. The eval measures **draft** output only (review/refine run in the orchestrator, not the eval). The review-pack workflow is documented internally. Validation breadth (more scenarios, synthesized audio, ARN human sign-off) remains the real parity signal.

## 2026-06-17 — Corridor Magnitude Tiering Replaces Flat Severity for On-Air Emphasis

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** HERE marks almost every major-road incident "critical", and `DeriveSeverity` floors every freeway/highway corridor at severity 1. The summarizer tiered and labelled corridors by that flat severity, so an entire metro market collapsed into one undifferentiated "Major" block with every bullet reading "severity 1" — the model had no signal to rank the worst corridor. Two defects compounded it: per-incident "Location:" anchors that merely restated the corridor road ("At Epping Road" on the Epping Road corridor → the tautology "Epping Road ... at Epping Road"), and full multi-line bullets for throwaway minor items inflating length.

**Decision:** Add `CorridorMagnitude.Classify` (Domain) — a commuter-facing tier (Severe/Major/Moderate/Minor) from the richest available signal: measured delay first, then real queue length (standing roadworks footprints excluded), then an incident-type floor so blocking crashes/closures stay prominent before routing attaches a drive time. `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` now tiers and orders by magnitude (worst delay leads within a tier), prints the magnitude word instead of "severity N", suppresses self-referential anchors (abbreviation-robust token-subset match), and renders minor corridors as one compact line. Raw `Severity` still feeds `ImpactScore` (corridor selection); magnitude is a separate on-air axis.

**Rationale:** The delay/queue signal that actually differentiates corridors already existed but was used only in the impact label — never for tiering, ordering, or the headline. Deriving the on-air tier from it (rather than HERE's flat criticality) fixes differentiation at the source without disturbing corridor selection.

**Consequences:** The data the LLM sees now ranks corridors by felt magnitude and leads with the worst; "severity 1" no longer appears; tautological road echoes are gone; minor items are terse. `FormatImpact`'s no-delay/no-queue fallback also derives from the tier rather than raw severity. Covered by `CorridorMagnitudeTests` (Domain) and extended `TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests` (Infrastructure). Live-HERE eval remains the real-world confirmation (replay corpus has no flow payloads).

## 2026-06-17 — Delay Is a Separate Ranking Term at Final Corridor Selection

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `CalculateImpactScore` (road importance + severity + extent + density) carries no delay term and runs in `CreateCorridor` before routing/flow enrichment attaches `DriveTimeMinutes`/`FlowDelayMinutes`. So the final corridor cut in `HereTrafficProvider.GetCorridorsAsync` ranked by a delay-blind score — a genuine high-delay jam on a lesser road could lose its slot to an idle major road.

**Decision:** Add `CorridorAggregator.CalculateDelayScore(Option<int>)` and rank the final, post-enrichment corridor union by `ImpactScore + CalculateDelayScore(DelayMinutes)`. Bands mirror the magnitude thresholds (≤5/≤15/≤30/>30 → 15/40/70/100). ImpactScore stays a pure structural signal; delay is added only at selection, where it is finally known, covering incident, congestion, and flow-enriched corridors uniformly in one place.

**Rationale:** Recomputing ImpactScore mid-pipeline would have to be threaded through both the routing path and `BuildCongestionCorridors`; a single additive term at the one ranking site is simpler and keeps the structural score meaningful on its own.

**Consequences:** A real jam now out-ranks an idle major road of equal structural impact in the final cut. The pre-enrichment `Take(maxCorridors)` inside `AggregateByRoad` still picks candidates delay-blind (a possible future widening), and single-incident corridors get no routed drive time by nature, so the term mainly benefits multi-incident queues and flow congestion. Covered by `CorridorAggregatorTests`.

## 2026-06-17 — Eval Scorer Made Fairer; Closure-Ordering Rule Tried and Reverted

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live-HERE eval (n=3, gpt-5.4-mini) surfaced two things. (1) The `TargetShapeScorer` `direction`, `anchors`, and `drive-time-lead` dimensions penalised congestion-heavy markets and closure-led bulletins for behaviour that is actually correct: congestion/flow corridors are road-name-only (no cross-street to anchor, no direction), and leading with a road closure is canonical ATN — yet the scorer counted unanchorable corridors in the denominators and did not recognise "closed/shut" as a strong lead. Genuinely good Sydney/Gold Coast bulletins scored ~80%. (2) A reproducible mis-lead: the summarizer's within-tier ordering (by measured delay) sorted a shut motorway below a congestion crawl, because a closed road carries near-zero measured delay.

**Decision:** (a) Fix the scorer — exclude congestion corridors (no incidents) from the `anchors` denominator and direction-less corridors from the `direction` denominator (N/A when none), and credit a road-closure lead as a strong lead. (b) Do NOT add a closure delay-floor to corridor ordering. It was implemented and tested, but the live eval showed it collapsed ordering AMONG multiple closures (all floored to the same value), so the highest-`ImpactScore` closure — not the highest-magnitude one — led, dropping Melbourne to 64% (it led a "short queue" closure over a "heavy delays" one). Reverted.

**Rationale:** Closures have no numerically comparable magnitude (a "heavy delays" closure and a "short queue" closure both report ~0 measured delay), so any blunt data-ordering rule mis-ranks them. The model's prompt-guided "lead with the worst" judgment, reading the qualitative impact labels, ranks closures better than the data layer can. The scorer fixes are pure measurement honesty with no behavioural risk.

**Consequences:** Target-shape scores are now fair and trustworthy across markets (~90% all three, n=3). Corridor ordering is unchanged from commit 41b84a8. The closure-vs-congestion lead remains an editorial nuance for the prompt + ARN review, not a data rule. Caveat: a market's target-shape % is only comparable across runs with a similar closure/congestion corridor mix.

## 2026-06-17 — Corridor Magnitude Exposed on the API DTO; Operator Map Colours by It

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The operator console's map (`LocationMap`) coloured corridor pins and its legend by HERE's raw `severity` (1=critical…4=minor) — the same flat signal `DeriveSeverity` floors at 1 for nearly every metro corridor, so a congestion-heavy market rendered as a uniform wall of "critical" red. The commuter-facing magnitude tier existed only inside the backend pipeline (`CorridorMagnitude`), never on the wire.

**Decision:** Add a `Magnitude` field (Severe/Major/Moderate/Minor, the `MagnitudeTier` enum name) to `TrafficCorridorDto`, set by both `ToCorridorDto` mappers — the live `TrafficCorridor` path and the persisted `JobCorridor` path (the latter via a new primitive `CorridorMagnitude.Classify(primaryType, functionalClass, delayMinutes, totalLengthMeters)` overload, since a `JobCorridor` is not a `TrafficCorridor`). The frontend colours/labels corridors by `magnitude` (new `corridorDisplay*` helpers reusing the severity palette via a tier↔severity map), falling back to `severity` only for cached jobs predating the field.

**Rationale:** One source of truth — the tier is computed once in the Domain and serialised, never re-derived in TypeScript. The operator map now agrees with what goes to air, and an at-a-glance market view differentiates instead of reading all-critical.

**Consequences:** Future UI must colour corridors by `magnitude`, not raw `severity` (kept on the DTO for the fallback and for the incident-vs-corridor scale distinction). Corridor selection/order was already conveyed via `rank`/`isSelected`, so no UI change was needed there. Covered by `IncidentMappingExtensionsTests` (both mapper paths) and `incident-labels.test.ts`.

## 2026-06-17 — Self-Service Guidance & Memory (layered, governed prompt config)

**Status:** accepted (backend + prompt + API; frontend + versioning specced as follow-on)

**Context:** ARN needs to evolve bulletin quality on their own without Arinco writing code. The pipeline already had the seed of this — the `marketFeedback` corpus auto-accrues operator reject/regenerate notes and auto-replays them into the draft (`{{marketFeedback}}`), plus `PriorityRoads` and `goodRunRoads` — but it was market-only, uncurated, auto-trusted, and invisible.

**Decision:** A three-layer instruction model (after the OpenAI Model Spec / instruction hierarchy): (1) **Engineered Core** — `system.md`/`safety.md`/JSON contract, immutable to ARN; (2) **Standing Guidance** — typed (`GuidanceType`: Style/Editorial/Lexicon/Prohibition/HouseStyle), scoped (`GuidanceScope` Global/Market/Station) directives in the new `guidance` Table, admin/operator-editable; (3) **Accrued Memory** — operator feedback (the existing `marketFeedback` store), promoted into Layer 2 by an admin gate (`POST /guidance/promote`, source `promoted:{jobId}`). `system.md` now declares a **chain of command** (BOUNDARIES > OUTPUT CONTRACT > PRODUCER FEEDBACK > STANDING GUIDANCE > STYLE DEFAULTS) with a hard/steerable split. Composition (precedence Station>Market>Global, newest-first, cap 8, dropped-tail report) is a pure `GuidanceComposer` domain service; `IGuidanceRepository`/`TableStorageGuidanceRepository` is pure persistence (partition `{Scope}:{scopeId}`, no dual-write). `StationId` is threaded from `schedule.Station` through `BroadcastContextBase` (the poller orchestrates directly, so no queue-message change needed; ad-hoc/regen → None → global+market only).

**Rationale:** This is the OpenAI Model Spec / instruction-hierarchy pattern applied to ARN's own prompt: the engineered core *declares and ranks* the config it expects, so additive guidance is anticipated and bounded rather than bolted on. Composition is a pure domain service (testable against adversarial scenarios without I/O); the repository stays pure persistence. Reusing `marketFeedback` as the candidate store avoids a duplicate table, and the human promotion gate is the consensus defense against memory poisoning. Station/market/global scoping mirrors the existing `PriorityRoads`/`goodRunRoads` precedent.

**Two safety mechanisms (the heart):** (a) **Delimiter sanitisation** — `PromptSafe.Sanitize`/`StripDelimiters` strip the reserved `<guidance>`/`<data>`/`<producer-feedback>`/`<operator-notes>`/`<house-style>` tokens from every admin/operator/provider string, so an author or a HERE incident field cannot close a block early and escape into instruction space; data is wrapped in `<data>` and the prompt forbids following instructions inside it. (b) **Immutable boundaries** — guidance/feedback compose only into STEERABLE layers; BOUNDARIES + the separate `safety.md` pass are never reachable from config. Producer feedback (per-bulletin) outranks standing guidance, both below BOUNDARIES (fixes the old `system.md` rule 14 over-permission that made feedback "highest priority" full stop).

**Handlebars gotcha (load-bearing):** SemanticKernel Handlebars HTML-encodes `{{value}}` interpolations, so `<data>` rendered as `&lt;data&gt;` — mangling the delimiter scheme the model receives. The delimiter-carrying, already-sanitised values (`traffic`, `guidance`, `houseStyle`, `operatorNotes`, `rejectionFeedback`) are now rendered with **triple-mustache `{{{ }}}`** in `draft.md`/`review.md`/`refine.md` so the model sees real tags. Safe precisely because the values are delimiter-sanitised first. (Literal template tags like `<guidance scope="">` are not interpolations and were never encoded.)

**Consequences:** ARN can add station/market/global tweaks and promote recurring feedback into durable, always-applied guidance, governed by an admin gate, without code. Verified by 38 domain tests (composer precedence/cap/disable/scope-isolation, sanitisation, the named adversarial scenarios) + 2 end-to-end render tests proving real `<data>`/`<guidance>` reach the model. Road emphasis and pronunciation deliberately stay on their existing mechanisms (`PriorityRoads`, ElevenLabs dictionary) rather than becoming dead guidance enum values. Frontend admin cockpit and guidance versioning are specced (spec §10, §12 Phase 4-5), not yet built.

## 2026-06-18 — Content-safety banned words as a governed admin UI (distinct from guidance)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The deterministic content-safety banned-word list lived only in `ContentSafety:BannedWords` config (Key Vault), was empty, and could only change via redeploy — blocking ARN from populating it. It was being conflated with the guidance "Prohibition" type, but they are different controls: guidance is soft editorial steering composed into the prompt; content safety is a hard regulatory gate that blocks a finished script before synthesis.

**Decision:** Make banned words (and place-name exceptions) a repository-backed, admin-only management surface, co-located as a "Banned words" tab in the guidance area but kept architecturally distinct. New `SafetyTerm`/`ISafetyTermRepository`/`TableStorageSafetyTermRepository` (table `safetyTerms`) + `SafetyTermsHttpTrigger` (`/safety/terms`, every route Admin via `RouteRoleMatrix`). `ConfigurableContentSafetyFilter` is now market-aware and enforces the UNION of the engineered config baseline and the repository terms (global ∪ market); allowed exceptions are masked before the banned-word scan.

**Rationale:** Self-service without code (the project principle) unblocks the empty banned list. Three deliberate differences from guidance preserve the compliance posture: (1) **admin-only** governance — compliance owns it, not casual operator edits; (2) **additive union** composition — a narrower scope may only ADD prohibitions, never weaken the global floor (the opposite of guidance's station-overrides-global precedence); (3) **no Station scope** — safety is a network/regulatory floor, set globally with optional per-market additions. The config baseline (`ContentSafety:BannedWords`/`AllowedPhrases`) is the immutable floor merged in by the filter and is not removable via the UI; a store outage degrades to that baseline (never fail-open). Place-name exceptions are the one subtractive case and are admin-gated + audited (`CreatedBy`).

**Consequences:** ARN can maintain the banned list + exceptions live, per market, without a redeploy. The per-bulletin "Safety cleared" review badge was deliberately NOT built — the gate is pre-review so the verdict is a constant; only the fail-open ("review unavailable") case is review-screen-worthy (deferred). Verified by 19 filter tests (union, market scoping, exception masking, store-outage degrade-to-baseline) + 63 orchestrator tests + 4 frontend schema tests; full backend build + frontend suite green; dev:mock smoke (render + add across scopes). The `safety.md` LLM reviewer layer and the still-empty production banned list (pending ARN editorial + CRA terms) are unchanged.

## 2026-06-18 — Market priority roads live in the Bulletin-rules hub, not the schedule wizard

**Status:** superseded (2026-06-30 — "Remove per-station GoodRunRoads; good-run eligibility is market PriorityRoad.FlowTier only" folded the station-scoped good-run list back into this same market-scoped Priority roads tab)

**Context:** Per-market priority roads (a corridor-ranking weight) were edited inside the per-schedule `ScheduleStudio` wizard — a market-scoped setting reached via a per-schedule surface, re-fetched/diffed per wizard session. With the guidance + banned-words hub now market-scoped, a more correct home existed.

**Decision:** Move market priority roads into a "Priority roads" tab on the `/guidance` hub (renamed **Bulletin rules**; tabs: Editorial guidance · Banned words [admin] · Priority roads). `ScheduleStudio`'s step becomes "Good-run roads" — the per-schedule `goodRunRoads` only — with a pointer to the hub.

**Rationale:** Scope-correctness: market-level config belongs on a market-scoped surface alongside the other per-market tuning (guidance, banned words). Good-run roads stay in the wizard because they are genuinely per-schedule (a `MarketSchedule` field), not per-market — so the two road editors split by scope, not by accident. Priority roads are mechanically a selection weight (not prompt text or an output gate), so the hub now spans selection → prompt → safety; the tab is labelled to say so. No backend change — reuses `/markets/{m}/priority-roads`.

**Consequences:** One "tune this market's bulletins" home; the schedule wizard is leaner. Operators (not just admins) get the Priority roads + Editorial guidance tabs; Banned words stays admin-only. Verified: full frontend suite green (363), tsc + eslint clean, dev:mock smoke (tab renders, market switch reloads roads, save present).

## 2026-06-19 — Backend auth accepts the SWA-forwarded client principal (linked-backend topology)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The deployed topology proxies /api/* through the SWA linked backend to the Function App. SWA terminates auth with its built-in AAD provider and forwards the SWA client-principal format (identityProvider + userRoles + claims, no auth_typ). AuthorizationMiddleware and ClientPrincipal only parsed the App Service Easy Auth format (auth_typ==aad, claims[].typ==roles), so every authenticated /api/* call was rejected 401 with the App Insights trace 'principal auth_typ is not aad' (observed dev, 19 Jun 2026). Separately, the SWA built-in provider authenticates against the platform shared app, not the API app registration that carries the Operator/Admin app roles, so the forwarded principal only has the anonymous/authenticated pseudo-roles and no app roles flow.

**Decision:** Centralise principal parsing in ClientPrincipal to accept BOTH wire formats: Easy Auth (auth_typ==aad; direct bearer calls and the local-dev mock) and SWA client principal (identityProvider==aad; roles from userRoles minus the anonymous/authenticated pseudo-roles, oid/name back-filled from userId/userDetails). AuthorizationMiddleware delegates to it. Add a dev-only authorization fallback (app setting Auth__DevFallbackRole; bicep param devAuthFallbackRole, set to Admin only in main.dev.bicepparam, empty in test/prod) that grants every authenticated AAD caller the named role so the operator console is usable before Entra app-role assignments exist. The middleware logs a once-per-process warning when the bypass is active. Production RBAC requires SWA to use a custom Entra provider against the API app registration (so the roles claim is issued and forwarded) plus ARN assigning Operator/Admin.

**Rationale:** The linked-backend single-origin design is the deliberate, deployed architecture; the fix belongs in the principal parser, not in abandoning the proxy. The platform Easy Auth still fail-closes direct Function App access (verified: direct anon call returns 401 Bearer), so trusting the SWA-forwarded principal does not weaken the boundary. The dev fallback unblocks integration testing now without weakening test/prod (empty there) and is impossible to miss in logs.

**Consequences:** Test/prod stay 403 until ARN assigns Operator/Admin and the SWA is wired to a custom Entra provider against the API app reg (redirect URI + client secret are ARN-owned prerequisites). Dev grants Admin to any authenticated caller via devAuthFallbackRole. Frontend role-aware UI (useIsAdmin) still reads SWA userRoles and will not see app roles until the custom provider is wired, so admin-only controls stay hidden in dev even though the backend allows them.

## 2026-06-19 — Surface HERE operator `comment` into bulletins, advisory-stripped and Major/Moderate-only

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** HERE incidents carry an undocumented operator `comment` free-text (road-authority entries with cross-streets, direction, lane effect, ops status) richer than the structured `description`, present on ~38% of live AU incidents — the pipeline discarded it. It also carries advisory imperatives ("Seek Alternative Routes", "Exercise Extreme Caution"), HTML entities, and website referrals, and its road sometimes disagrees with HERE's own `description` (the reverse-geocoded corridor road tends to agree with the comment instead).

**Decision:** Parse `comment` into `HereIncidentDetails`, normalize it in a new `IncidentCommentNormalizer` (HTML-decode, drop advisory + referral sentences, collapse whitespace, sentence-bounded 140-char cap, suppress when the description already states it), carry it as `TrafficIncident.Comment`, and emit it as a `Source detail:` line in `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendCorridorBullet` — Major/Moderate corridors only (the condensed Minor bullet never calls that method, so standing-works comments like "Vms Trailer" stay out). `codes` and `criticality` stay dropped (redundant / unreliable respectively).

**Rationale:** The comment is the richest cause/anchor detail HERE offers and lifts script + UI evidence specificity toward ATN style; advisory-stripping preserves the system-prompt no-advice boundary; the structural Major/Moderate gate keeps busy markets' construction noise out without a separate flag.

**Consequences:** Bulletins gain cross-street/direction/ops anchors on significant corridors and the UI evidence index (incidentAnchor) surfaces the operator detail. Scripts run noticeably longer where a comment is surfaced — watch the word budget on busy markets. Verified by 9 normalizer tests, 2 summarizer Major/Moderate gate tests, and 1 end-to-end provider test (advisory stripped through deserialize → MapToDomain → normalizer); full backend build green.

## 2026-06-19 — Persist the full fetched incident pool separately from the bulletin's selected subset

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A deployed Melbourne bulletin showed only 6 incidents in the review Evidence index with no "Not in this bulletin" omitted list, although HERE returned 20 corridors (App Insights `[TrafficAggregation] SelectedCorridors=6, TotalCorridors=20`). This regressed the 2026-06-10 corridor-visibility fix: `BroadcastOrchestrator.StoreIncidentsOnJob` had since been narrowed to persist only `selectedCorridors.SelectMany(c => c.Incidents)` into `job.Incidents`, and both `Traffic.incidents` and `SelectedIncidents` map from that one collection — so the frontend evidence pool equalled the included set and the omitted/`available` partition was always empty. `job.Incidents` cannot simply be widened: it seeds regeneration (`JobMessageBuilder`) and the incident delta, which legitimately want the selected set.

**Decision:** Split the two meanings. Add `Job.AllIncidents` (the full fetched pool) alongside `Job.Incidents` (the selected subset). `StoreIncidentsOnJob` populates it from `allCorridors.SelectMany(c => c.Incidents).DistinctBy(Id)`; it persists as `AllIncidentsJson` (additive — legacy rows deserialize to empty). `MapTrafficData` sources `Traffic.incidents` from `AllIncidents` (falling back to `Incidents` when empty), while `SelectedIncidents` stays the selected subset. The frontend partition is unchanged — `use-bulletin-review` already keys "in bulletin" off `corridor.isSelected` and computes `available = pool \ included`.

**Rationale:** The evidence index was always designed to show the full pool with non-selected incidents under "Not in this bulletin" (its own header comment said so); the data just stopped arriving. Splitting pool from subset restores that without overloading `job.Incidents` and without touching regeneration/delta semantics. The fallback keeps pre-migration jobs rendering their selected set rather than nothing.

**Consequences:** The review UI again surfaces every fetched corridor's incidents, with the dropped long tail visible under "Not in this bulletin" — operators no longer mistake a tight selection for a quiet market. Short deployed scripts remain a separate, by-design effect of the schedule's `TargetDurationSeconds` (a 30s slot is ~53 words / 6 corridors), not this bug. Verified: backend 94 Application + 21 Infrastructure tests (orchestrator full-pool capture, mapping full-pool + legacy fallback, repository round-trip + legacy-null); frontend `tsc` clean + 126 jobs-feature tests.

## 2026-06-22 — Duration acceptance, retry, and voice calibration key off the SPOKEN span, not the padded file

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deployed job `e866746b…` aired a 30.0s Melbourne bulletin whose speech ended at ~21s — ~9s of trailing dead air (App Insights `Delta=0.00s, accepted`; served-WAV RMS envelope silent 21→30s; word timings end 20.88s). An under-length take is filled to the slot with a trailing-silence pad (asymmetric duration-fit: never slow a fast reader). The orchestrator's duration gate, the retry word-budget recompute, and the per-voice calibration EMA all measured the PADDED file length (always ≈ target), so the gate accepted on attempt 1, the retry never grew the script, and calibration recorded 83 syll ÷ 30.0s = 2.77 syll/s instead of 83 ÷ 20.9 ≈ 3.97 — a self-poisoning loop that drove `radioVoiceCalibrations` ever slower (Peter Michael `oKDz3nEzNfwKIVvUwPs0` → 2.94 syll/s, RunCount 11), shrinking every future word budget and worsening the dead air.

**Decision:** Measure the SPOKEN span — `WavDurationProcessor.GetSpokenDuration` (uncapped; end of last voiced block) — on the final audio and surface it as `AudioSynthesisResult.SpokenDurationSeconds`. `BroadcastOrchestrator` gates acceptance, sizes retries, records voice calibration, and records synthesis history off the spoken span, not the padded file. The persisted audio is still the slot-length WAV — only the acceptance/learning signals changed. (Superseded 2026-06-24: the asymmetric trailing-silence pad is replaced by bounded slow-to-fill + an exact-slot requirement.)

**Rationale:** The pad was correct on-air; the defect was measuring the result of that pad. The spoken-span measurement already existed (for karaoke timing rescale), so one signal fixes the gate and the calibration. A failed generation falls back to the last good bulletin — far better on air than 9s of silence.

**Consequences:** A short read now triggers a regenerate-longer retry instead of shipping dead air; a chronically mis-budgeted voice fails to a fallback rather than airing silence. Calibration converges to the true read rate. The 5 existing `radioVoiceCalibrations` rows are biased slow and self-heal only slowly via EMA — they MUST be purged AFTER the fix is deployed (purging before redeploy is re-poisoned by the still-buggy code). Verified: backend gate-reject, calibration-records-spoken-span, small-pad-accepted, and pad/spoken-span-recoverable guards.

## 2026-06-22 — ElevenLabs v3 delivery is a per-station, versioned audio-tag policy applied by a director pass

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** On eleven_v3 the script is the expressive control surface — `speed` is ignored and `stability` buckets to three modes (verified 2026-06-15) — so emphasis, pacing and emotion come from inline audio tags (`[urgent]`, `[calm]`, …), capitalisation and punctuation in the script text, which the TTS receives untouched. ARN wants expressive on-air delivery but operators are time-poor, so it must be set-once-applies-automatically with an optional, low-effort per-bulletin override.

**Decision:** Three layers. **(1)** An `IScriptDirector` LLM role (`prompts/director.md`, a sibling of generator/reviewer/safety/attributor on `LlmScriptGenerator`) runs after generation+safety, before synthesis, adding tags per a `DeliveryStylePolicy` — never changing the spoken words (enforced by `DeliveryTags.WordsPreserved`; fail-open to the plain script), v3-only, with a safety re-check on the tagged text. The audio pipeline strips tags before all word/syllable/duration measurement so the recently-fixed calibration/duration behaviour is unaffected; the job stores plain `ScriptText` + `TaggedScriptText` + style provenance. **(2)** Delivery styles are a versioned shared library (`DeliveryStyle`, append-only, table `radioDeliveryStyles`) mirroring the voice-profile library; a station picks one default via `MarketSchedule.DeliveryStyleId`, resolved live by the poller. Unassigned/neutral reads exactly as today; the global config default (`Delivery` section) is off by default. **(3)** Operators see clean words by default with a reveal toggle for the tagged read (chips, never raw syntax), and re-direct a bulletin in plain language ("read it calmer") via a "Delivery / tone" change that becomes the regenerate `deliveryIntent` (a permissive operator-directed palette applies when the station style is neutral). Delivery-only edits preserve words.

**Rationale:** Reuses the established multi-role LLM + repo-root `prompts/*.md` pattern, the versioned VoiceProfile library pattern, and the existing reject→regenerate feedback flow — no parallel conventions. Tag-stripping at measurement keeps duration-fit and per-voice calibration intact. The word-immutability guard + v3 gate + safety re-check make the director strictly additive and fail-safe: it can only improve delivery, never block a bulletin or alter content.

**Consequences:** Every bulletin can carry an on-air tone with zero per-bulletin operator time; tones are authored once, reused across stations, versioned for rollback, and iterated offline via the new `DeliveryStyleScorer` against the ATN corpus. Out of the box nothing changes (neutral default). Verified: backend 1774 pass / 28 skip / 0 fail (new DeliveryTags, DeliveryStyle, DeliveryStyleScorer, DeliveryStyleService + orchestrator delivery-path tests); web `tsc` clean + 369 vitest + production build.

## 2026-06-22 — The delivery-style editor exposes plain-language intent, not ElevenLabs internals

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The first delivery-style editor made a time-poor traffic operator hand-type raw v3 audio tags (`[urgent]` in a monospace box) and set an unexplained 0–3 intensity slider — the opposite of the feature's thesis that operators describe intent and the director LLM owns the tags.

**Decision:** Rebuild the `Delivery` rules-hub tab as a master-detail console (`web/src/features/delivery`). The operator picks a **station-safe preset** (describes how a station sounds, never the traffic event; system-seeded, not user-editable), writes one plain-language "How should this sound on air?" direction (= `toneDescription`), sets a 3-stop **Strength** control (Light touch/Balanced/High colour = intensity 1/2/3; intensity 0/Neutral is chosen only in the schedule, never authored here), and toggles humanised **Permitted delivery cues** chips (the `allowedTags` guardrail, ≥1 always required, raw `[brackets]` never shown). **Audition** (A/B vs Neutral, cue-count + duration + a "Words unchanged" badge) is the centrepiece and is **required before every save**. Edits mint a live new version (no Draft state); editing a style assigned to stations requires an explicit live-edit confirmation because the poller resolves the current version on the next bulletin. Restore = save an old policy as a new version. Backend gains archive/unarchive (status flip, no version mint). `assignedStations` is derived on the frontend from the schedules list (`useStyleAssignments`) because the backend stores the field but never populates it from a schedule's `deliveryStyleId`. The backend policy contract `{toneDescription, allowedTags[], intensity}` is unchanged — only how the operator arrives at those values.

**Rationale:** Keeps the audio-tag vocabulary out of operators' hands per the feature thesis and ARN's "Simplify to elevate"; mirrors the proven VoiceProfile versioning + reject→regenerate patterns (no parallel conventions). The conclusive spec (`web/src/features/delivery/REDESIGN-SPEC.md`) was co-designed with ChatGPT as UI/UX designer over two rounds.

**Consequences:** Operators author a tone in seconds from a preset and verify by ear, never learning tags. Frontend-derived assignment is a deliberate localised shortcut; if other consumers need `assignedStations`, add backend reconciliation (compute it from schedules referencing the style id). Verified: backend Domain 551 / Application 338 / Functions 153 pass; web `tsc` + eslint clean + 380 vitest (11 new form-helper tests) + production build. Not yet deployed.

## 2026-06-22 — Delivery styles are their own top-level tab, authored in a Voices-style gallery + Studio

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The delivery-style editor (previous entry) lived as a master-detail tab inside the `Bulletin rules` hub and felt verbose — a single long scrolling form pane. The operator wanted it to feel like the established Voices feature and be discoverable as its own thing.

**Decision:** Promote Delivery to a top-level admin sidebar route (`/delivery`, ⌘7, `web/src/pages/DeliveryPage.tsx`) and rebuild it on the exact Voices pattern: a `SpotlightCard` gallery (`DeliveryStyleCard` — plain-language tone as the focal line, permitted-cue chips, assignment, Edit/Duplicate/Archive) plus a focused `DeliveryStyleStudio` on the shared `web/src/components/studio/Studio` scaffold with free-nav steps (Style / Delivery / History), rail value-summaries + validity dots, and the audition-required gate on the footer `StudioSubmitButton`. The master-detail components (`DeliveryStyleManager`/`DeliveryStyleListPane`/`DeliveryStyleDetailPane`/`DeliveryStyleForm`/`PresetPicker`) are deleted and the tab removed from `Bulletin rules`. No audition on gallery cards (a fresh synth costs money) — the operator hears it in the Studio.

**Rationale:** Reuses the proven gallery+Studio convention (no parallel pattern beside Voices) and keeps every piece of delivery domain/audition logic unchanged (`lib/delivery-form`, `cues`, `presets`, `strength`, hooks, `useStyleAssignments`, `AuditionPanel`, `VersionHistory`, `LiveEditConfirmationDialog`, `StrengthControl`, `PermittedCueSelector`) — a re-housing of the UI, not a logic rewrite. Backend contract untouched. Supersedes the master-detail shape of the previous entry; `web/src/features/delivery/REDESIGN-SPEC.md` is now historical.

**Consequences:** Delivery is discoverable as a sibling of Voices and reads consistently with it; the editor shows one concern at a time instead of a long form. Verified: web `tsc` + eslint clean, 382 vitest pass (3 skip), production build green. Not yet deployed.

## 2026-06-23 — Pronunciation is a per-station, versioned ElevenLabs dictionary library (model-aware: alias everywhere, phoneme v2-only)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Pronunciation was a static, per-market `ElevenLabsOptions.PronunciationDictionaries` config (disabled, empty, redeploy-only) — ARN could not own or evolve region pronunciations. The voice profile a station reads with also selects the TTS model, and ElevenLabs applies **alias** dictionary rules on every model but **phoneme/IPA** rules only on the v2-family (eleven_v3, the production default, silently skips phoneme rules).

**Decision:** Add a fourth per-station library mirroring VoiceProfile/DeliveryStyle: `PronunciationDictionary` (alias + phoneme rules, append-only versions, owns its ElevenLabs dictionary id) → `IPronunciationDictionaryProvider` on `ElevenLabsClient` (add-from-rules / add-rules / remove-rules; every edit mints a new ElevenLabs `version_id` we persist) → `PronunciationDictionaryService` (uploads the rule diff then mints a domain version) → `radioPronunciationDictionaries` table → `PronunciationDictionariesHttpTrigger` (CRUD + version restore + model-aware preview) + `/pronunciations` gallery/studio UI. A station assigns one via `MarketSchedule.PronunciationDictionaryId`; the poller resolves the current version live into `BroadcastContext.PronunciationLocator`, threaded through the audio pipeline → synthesizer → client and attached at synthesis. One dictionary per station holds BOTH rule types; ElevenLabs applies what the resolved model supports. The static config path is retained as a fallback when no per-station dictionary resolves.

**Rationale:** Reuses the proven versioned-library pattern (Domain aggregate + repo + service + HTTP trigger + gallery/studio + per-schedule assignment + live poller resolution) — no parallel convention. Pronunciation is bound to the model + the attached dictionary, not the voice, so a cloned voice needs nothing new. Keeping both rule types in one dictionary makes the synth path model-agnostic (attach the locator; ElevenLabs filters); the model-awareness is operator guidance, surfaced in the studio (phoneme rules flagged "won't apply on eleven_v3 — add an alias respelling") and the preview (pick the model; see applied-vs-skipped counts). Alias is the universal baseline; phoneme/IPA adds precision on a v2-family voice (e.g. a future PVC on multilingual_v2).

**Consequences:** ARN creates, edits, versions, previews, and assigns per-region pronunciations live, and an operator's pronunciation-reject feedback deep-links into the studio to add a rule — closing the evolve loop without code. Per-region rule content (Warringah, Lachlan, …) is still to be populated/verified with the ARN voice consult, and synthesis-time dictionary-application telemetry is deferred. Verified: backend build clean; new Domain (PronunciationRule/PronunciationDictionary), Application (service diff/version logic with a fake provider), and Infrastructure (client wire-shape + resolved-locator attach) unit tests pass; web build/lint/tests green.

## 2026-06-23 — Good-run gating is deterministic; the flow pool is operator-curatable in a Flow tab

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Good-run ("flowing well") roads were auto-derived (station good-run list matched, else top free-flow roads) and shown read-only in review — operators could curate the problem side (incidents/congestion corridors) but not the clear side, and the full HERE free-flow pool was discarded (only the aired subset persisted). Inclusion was a soft LLM decision with no firm rule.

**Decision:** (1) Deterministic gating via `GoodRunPolicy.SelectForGeneration` — **no problem corridors → MUST fill** with the top flowing roads; **incidents present → station-weighted roads only** (station good-run list ∪ market priority roads), with generic flowing roads added only as last-resort fill when the problem corridors don't fill the slot (the hybrid resolution, so a quiet-but-not-empty bulletin never ships dead air). (2) Persist the full ranked pool as `Job.FlowRoads` (weighted + selected flags) → `FlowRoadDto` → web `traffic.flowRoads`. (3) A **Flow tab** in the review Adjust surface lets operators toggle which flowing roads air; the pick rides the regenerate path (`SelectedGoodRuns` → `CuratedGoodRunRoads`) and overrides the policy. **Data-backed only** — the picker offers solely roads the live HERE flow confirms (or the station list); no free-text, preserving the no-fabrication boundary. The draft prompt branches on `goodRunsAreFill` (fill = "they ARE the bulletin"; secondary = brief clear-run mention after incidents).

**Rationale:** Mirrors the existing incident/corridor curation path (`SelectedCorridors`) rather than inventing a new convention. The weighted-vs-generic split encodes ARN's editorial intent (busy bulletins aren't diluted with good news; quiet ones lean on it) while the slot-capacity fill threshold respects the 30s duration contract. Data-backed-only keeps every on-air "running well" evidenced, which matters because ARN bears publication liability.

**Consequences:** Operators see and curate the full flow pool per bulletin; good-run inclusion is predictable, not LLM-discretionary. New `FlowRoad` (Domain) + `GoodRunPolicy` + `CorridorAggregator.RankFreeFlowingRoads`; `ITrafficProvider.GetFreeFlowingRoadsAsync` now returns `FlowRoad`s. Verified end-to-end against real HERE/OpenAI/ElevenLabs: a busy Melbourne bulletin persisted an 18-road pool and aired no good runs (slot full, none weighted); an operator pick of Monash Freeway + EastLink aired exactly those as a secondary "running well" mention. Backend 1850 tests + web 385 tests green; typecheck/lint/build clean.

## 2026-06-23 — Server-Side Aggregate Endpoints + Narrow Shell Polling for Operator-Console Load

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Bulletin-rules (`/guidance`) page took ~10s to load (28 API calls, measured live) because the client fanned out one HTTP request per market for both guidance and priority roads, eagerly mounted all three tabs (`forceMount`), and the app shell polled the full job list (`TableStorageJobRepository` static `Job` partition, ≤1000 rows) every 10s on every page. Other pages issue ~3 calls.

**Decision:** Compose per-market inventories server-side behind single endpoints — `GET /guidance/inventory` and `GET /priority-roads/inventory`, markets supplied via `?markets=` and intersected with the caller's allowed markets (`MarketScopeRequest`). Filter the job list server-side (`GET /jobs?status=`, comma-separated wire statuses) and give the app shell a narrow `useActiveJobs` query scoped to the notification-trigger statuses. Drop eager tab mounting on the Bulletin-rules hub. Code-split all routes with `React.lazy`.

**Rationale:** Turns O(markets) client requests into O(1), removes the full-list poll from every page that does not show jobs, and keeps the heavy leaflet/map and per-page bundles off the initial load. Fixing at the API boundary beats client-side parallelism, which cannot escape the browser's per-host connection limit.

**Consequences:** New aggregate endpoints + `MarketScopeRequest` helper + `IJobRepository.ListJobsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<JobStatus>)` overload + `JobMappingExtensions.ParseStatusList`. New GET routes inherit the Operator role from the existing GET rule in `RouteRoleMatrix` (no auth change). The full unfiltered job list remains for the On-air board and History; the shell and other pages no longer poll it. Backend 0-warning build + all non-integration tests pass (incl. new `ParseStatusList`, `MarketScopeRequest`, and `ListJobs` status-filter tests); web build clean + 393 vitest tests green.

## 2026-06-23 — Per-station voice rotation & time-of-day voices

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Stations had a single fixed VoiceProfileId. ARN wants a station to cycle between several voices, and optionally use different voices in different local-time windows.

**Decision:** Added an additive, backward-compatible VoiceRotationPolicy (Single | RoundRobin | TimeOfDay) on MarketSchedule plus a persisted int VoiceRotationCursor. VoiceProfileId stays the required primary/fallback. ResolveVoiceAsync picks the run's profile (round-robin via cursor % candidates, or the active local-time window), falling back to the primary then the default voice. Cursor advances once per completed run in CompleteRun. Windows are half-open station-local ranges, may wrap midnight, must not overlap, and gaps fall back to the primary. Decisions taken: persisted cursor (not stateless); windows may hold a set but the UI binds one voice each; cursor preserved across edits and reset only on mode change; round-robin allows a single voice. Manual /broadcast and regeneration are out of scope (regen keeps its resolved voice). Persisted as additive VoiceRotationJson + VoiceRotationCursor columns; legacy rows reconstitute as single.

**Rationale:** Mirrors the proven additive per-station pattern (ContentSelection/DeliveryStyle): zero data migration, every existing schedule and the dangling-reference guard keep working, and single-voice stays the zero-config default. A persisted cursor is the lowest-complexity correct round-robin and piggybacks on the existing ETag-guarded CompleteJobAsync write.

**Consequences:** MarketSchedule, ScheduleContracts, ScheduleCommands, ScheduleService, ScheduleHttpTrigger, TableStorageScheduleRepository, SchedulePollerService.ResolveVoiceAsync, ScheduleMappingExtensions, and the web schedules feature (types, zod schemas, VoiceRotationEditor, ScheduleStudio) all gained rotation wiring. ## 2026-06-24 — Drop the SPA /.auth/me Bearer-token interceptor; rely on SWA-injected principal

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A browser performance check showed /.auth/me was fetched 4-6x per cold page load (250-1150ms each) and gated every /api call behind it, doubling cold-load settle time. The axios request interceptor in web/src/lib/api/client.ts fetched /.auth/me to attach an Authorization: Bearer token, with a 60s cache that only dedups AFTER a fetch resolves — so parallel queries on mount stampede.

**Decision:** Remove getSwaAccessToken() and the /.auth/me fetch entirely. The interceptor now attaches only an optional dev VITE_API_TOKEN; production requests carry no Bearer. Auth in prod rides the X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL header the SWA linked backend injects on every /api/* request (and the Vite dev proxy injects locally), which AuthorizationMiddleware already authenticates. Also added immutable Cache-Control for /assets/* in staticwebapp.config.json.

**Rationale:** The backend AuthorizationMiddleware authenticates solely off X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL; no HTTP trigger reads Authorization. The Bearer token was therefore dead weight that added a per-call /.auth/me round trip and a cold-load stampede with zero functional benefit. Removing it roughly halves cold-load settle time on every page. The aggregate /api/bootstrap endpoint and Functions-warmth items were deprioritized: the plan is already alwaysOn PremiumV3 (warm), GetAllowedMarketsAsync short-circuits for admins, and shell queries fan out in parallel over HTTP/2, so an aggregate yields ~no wall-clock win while adding complexity and touching the security-scoping path.

**Consequences:** Cold/hard-refresh loads no longer issue 4-6 /.auth/me calls or wait on an auth waterfall. useAuthData() in auth.ts still fetches /.auth/me for identity (userName/roles) — unchanged. Do NOT reintroduce a Bearer-token fetch in client.ts for /api calls; the SWA proxy already forwards the principal. AuthData.accessToken is now unused by the API client.

## 2026-06-24 — Bulletins MUST be exactly slot length; fill underruns by slowing the read, else fall back

**Status:** accepted (supersedes the trailing-pad disposition of the 2026-06-22 spoken-span decision)

**Context:** ARN requires every aired bulletin file to be EXACTLY the slot length (e.g. 30.0s) with at most 0.3s of trailing silence, and never a sub-slot file. The 2026-06-22 spoken-span fix correctly stopped a padded file from masquerading as a perfect fit, but it left two unacceptable outcomes for a content-limited market: an accepted short take padded with multiple seconds of silence (deployed Gold Coast job `fd4c7ff4…`: 26.7s spoken in a 30.0s file, 3.3s dead air), or — under the interim 2026-06-24 trim — a file shorter than the slot. Neither meets the exact-slot requirement.

**Decision:** A layered fill ladder, agreed with the business: (1) grow CONTENT to the word budget first (unchanged); (2) if still short, SLOW the read toward the slot, pitch-preserving (WSOLA), up to `SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSlowDownFactor` (1.10 = ≤10% slower); (3) close any residual ≤ `MaxSilencePadSeconds` (0.3s) with trailing silence so the file is exactly the slot. The pipeline reports `AudioSynthesisResult.SlotFilled` — true only when the file is at target within the silence budget. The orchestrator accepts ONLY when `SlotFilled`; the old overrun/dead-air arithmetic gate and the `MaxTrailingSilenceSeconds`/`HardDurationToleranceSeconds` constants are removed (overruns the pipeline cannot compress already return failures). When content + slow-fill still cannot reach the slot within the cap, the orchestrator FAILS the job rather than ship short — the existing two-tier fallback (last good same-day bulletin, else the configured filler cart, via `ProcessFallbacksAsync` / `RejectToFallbackAsync`) covers the air slot. This reverses the 2026-06-22 "never slow the read" stance for the underrun-fill case only. `AudioSynthesisResult.SpokenDurationSeconds` now carries the NATURAL pre-fill read span (not the stretched/padded length) so voice calibration and the retry word-budget never self-poison; word timings rescale onto the post-stretch span so karaoke stays aligned with the slowed speech.

**Rationale:** "Exactly slot length" is a hard playout requirement; a short file or seconds of embedded dead air are both worse on air than a brief, near-imperceptible ~10% slow or a clean fallback. Slow-fill is bounded so the read never drags audibly; the floor reuses the established fallback rather than inventing a new path. Splitting natural vs delivered span keeps the 2026-06-22 calibration fix intact under stretching.

**Consequences:** `SpeechDurationOptions` gains `MaxSlowDownFactor` + `MaxSilencePadSeconds`; `AudioSynthesisResult` gains `SlotFilled` and redefines `SpokenDurationSeconds` as the natural span; `AudioPipelineService` slow-fills both underrun branches and computes `SlotFilled`; `BroadcastOrchestrator` gates on `SlotFilled` and fails content-limited slots to the fallback. Content-first sufficiency (raising the corridor cap / pulling more sources / sizing the word budget to fill the slot) is the recommended follow-up to reduce how often slow-fill or the floor fire — it does not change this hard guarantee. Open dependency: whether Zetta/Aquira playout expects exact-slot files or back-fills the clock itself (ties to the ARN playout playout-spec question). Verified: 357 Application + 751 Infrastructure tests pass (slow-fill within/beyond cap, SlotFilled gating, fail-to-fallback, calibration-keys-natural-span, word-timing-rescale). Not yet deployed.

## 2026-06-24 — Table repos degrade transport failures to Result.Failure; StorageOptions.MaxRetries

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The bulletin eval harness (`scripts/eval.sh --live-here --review`) threw `System.AggregateException : Retry failed after 4 tries` out of `BulletinEval` → `SafetyScorer` → `ConfigurableContentSafetyFilter.CheckAsync` → `TableStorageSafetyTermRepository.GetForMarketAsync`. Root cause was NOT test-only: `TableRepositoryBase.ExecuteAsync`/`GetEntityOrDefaultAsync` caught only `RequestFailedException`, but a transport-level outage (DNS/socket) surfaces — after the Azure SDK exhausts retries — as an `AggregateException` (inner `RequestFailedException`/`SocketException`), which escaped the catch. This defeated `ConfigurableContentSafetyFilter`'s documented "never fail open / degrade-to-baseline" guarantee: a transient Table Storage blip would throw out of the safety filter (and every other table repo) instead of degrading, potentially failing a bulletin in production.

**Decision:** (1) `TableRepositoryBase.ExecuteAsync` (both overloads) and `GetEntityOrDefaultAsync` now rethrow `OperationCanceledException`, keep the detailed `RequestFailedException` log, and add a general `catch (Exception)` that logs and returns `Result.Failure` — so any storage failure becomes a failure Result, never an unhandled throw, honouring the Result-pattern contract the base class promises. (2) Added `StorageOptions.MaxRetries` (default 3 = SDK default; preserves prod behaviour), threaded through `TableClientFactory` via `TableClientOptions.Retry.MaxRetries`. (3) The test/eval config (`TestConfigurationHelper`) sets `Storage:MaxRetries=0` so the dummy `test` account fails fast — the eval runs on the REAL repositories (no test doubles) and the new degrade path carries it through gracefully.

**Rationale:** A persistence base whose whole purpose is Result-pattern error handling must not let a transport exception escape; cancellation is the one exception that should still propagate. Failing fast in tests (MaxRetries=0) keeps the eval faithful to the production generation path while removing the ~20s-per-call retry stall. The knob also lets operators tune prod retry behaviour later.

**Consequences:** `TableRepositoryBase` is more resilient (storage outages degrade, not crash) — the content-safety filter now actually reaches its degrade-to-baseline branch under a real outage. `StorageOptions` gains `MaxRetries`. New `TableStorageSafetyTermRepositoryTests` lock the contract (transport `AggregateException` → `Result.Failure` on read + write; cancellation propagates). The live `scripts/eval.sh --script-only --live-here --review` loop is restored as the canonical script-quality iteration tool.

## 2026-06-24 — Bulletin draft prompt: hard item cap + delay-minute magnitude honesty; effort=none beats low

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live 8-category script-quality probe (none → oversubscribed traffic) exposed three draft-prompt failures: (1) oversubscribed markets (10–14 corridors) ran 35–43s for a 30s slot — the writer crammed every item instead of dropping minors; (2) the writer escalated a vague severity *word* into an invented magnitude (Perth voiced "the best part of an hour" for a corridor whose data showed +1 min / "heavy delays"); (3) it asserted a time of day ("this morning") and a direction not present in the data. Hypothesis was that `reasoning.effort="none"` (the gpt-5.x default) starved adherence.

**Decision:** Two layers. PROMPT (`prompts/draft.md` lead/cover rule): voice AT MOST 4–5 items and DROP the rest entirely (a tight bulletin that fits beats cramming and running long; the word ceiling is a hard limit); base voiced magnitude on the DELAY MINUTES, not the severity word (a closure with little delay is "shut"/"closed", not a big time loss); if every item is roadworks, lead with the worst roadworks. BOUNDARY (`prompts/system.md`): never state time-of-day or assert a direction unless the data provides it. CONFIG: added `AzureAIOptions.ReasoningEffort` (nullable; null = model-derived) so effort is tunable — but the A/B refuted the hypothesis: with the new prompt, **effort="none" beat "low"** (low produced *more* verbose, number-happy output — Brisbane voiced 5 figures, length grew, +~30% latency). Default stays model-derived ("none" for gpt-5.x).

**Rationale:** Measured on the deterministic replay corpus (no regression) and the live 8-category probe: melbourne 43s→29s, brisbane 42s→32s, adelaide 35s→26s, sydney 38s→26s; the Perth oversell disappeared; zero style/fabrication FAILs at effort=none. The hard item cap, not reasoning budget, is what fixes cramming — a low-reasoning model honours a concrete "voice ≤5, drop the rest" far better than a soft "prefer fewer". Residual draft defects (occasional "as well" clean-close, low anchoring on sparse data) are caught by the production review pass (`review.md` #6) which the draft-only eval does not exercise.

**Consequences:** `prompts/draft.md` + `prompts/system.md` updated; `AzureAIOptions` gains `ReasoningEffort` (leave unset). The draft-only eval critique reflects the pre-review draft — making the eval run the full review→refine pipeline is the recommended next harness step. Data-side follow-ups still open: severity-label vs delay-bucket contradiction in the summarizer, "Neranwood near Neranwood" self-anchor, road-name extraction artifacts ("Hill Freeway").

## 2026-06-24 — Full-pipeline eval mode; review.md must not force an undelayed drive-time headline

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The bulletin eval judged the raw DRAFT (`GenerateScriptAsync`) only — the production review→refine loop (`BroadcastOrchestrator.ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync`) was never exercised, so we were tuning a prompt whose output is downstream-corrected. Added a full-pipeline eval mode and ran it across the 8 density categories. It immediately exposed a regression the review pass INTRODUCES: `review.md` #7 said the bulletin "should lead with" any monitored drive-time route present, with no delay qualifier — so review→refine forced an undelayed route to the front (goldcoast "Pacific Motorway … just 1 minute slower … 26 minutes"; melbourne "Monash … one minute quicker than typical"; sydney "M4 … 1 minute quicker"), burying the real worst incident and voicing pointless "X-minute run, normally X" deltas. This contradicted `draft.md` (a monitored route leads only when it is the worst/delayed).

**Decision:** (1) `BulletinEval` gains a full-pipeline mode (`ARN_EVAL_FULL_PIPELINE=1` / `eval.sh --full-pipeline`) that runs draft → review → refine (mirrors the orchestrator loop, minus the deterministic style gate/director) so the review pack judges the SHIPPED script; `BulletinScenario` gains an optional `MaxCorridors` (default 5) so a probe can oversubscribe the writer. (2) `review.md` #7 realigned to `draft.md`: a monitored drive-time route leads ONLY on a meaningful delay (materially slower than typical); a route at/near typical must NOT lead and must NOT be voiced as "X-minute run, normally X" — lead with the worst actual incident.

**Rationale:** Measured on the live 8-category full-pipeline probe: overall target-shape 78% → 88% after the fix; goldcoast 100%, sydney 95%; goldcoast/adelaide/brisbane/sydney now lead with the real worst, and brisbane correctly voices a genuinely delayed run ("a 24-minute run in the usual 16"). Lengths stayed in-band through refine (the draft item-cap holds). The full-pipeline mode is the honest measurement surface — it found a defect the draft-only eval structurally could not.

**Consequences:** `prompts/review.md`, `scripts/eval.sh`, `BulletinEval`/`BulletinEvalTests` updated; the 3-market replay default is unchanged (probe scenarios are temporary, reverted after a run). Minor residual: melbourne can still open on an undelayed monitored route as a positive aside ("the best run in town") before the severe lead — borderline, not chased. Data-side follow-ups unchanged (severity-vs-delay contradiction, self-anchor, road-name artifacts).

## 2026-06-24 — Summarizer: drop the contradictory per-bullet tier word; closures state condition, not invented delay

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The data block the writer receives carried two clashing magnitude signals per corridor: the bullet header tier word (`CorridorMagnitude.Label` → "major") and a separate delay-minute Impact line ("delays ~5 min (minor delays)"). They use different axes — the tier is promoted by stretch length / incident-type floor (a 4 km standstill or a closure ranks Major), while the Impact bucket is pure delay-minutes — so "congestion, major" sat beside "(minor delays)". Worse, `FormatImpact`'s no-measured-delay fallback mapped a Major/Severe tier to "heavy delays"/"severe delays" — so a closure with zero routed delay read as "heavy delays", which is exactly what let the writer voice "the best part of an hour" off a +1-minute road (the Perth oversell).

**Decision:** (1) Remove the redundant per-bullet tier word — the section header (Major:/Moderate:/Minor:) already conveys the ranking tier, and the Impact line carries the honest delay-driven magnitude. The condensed minor bullet already worked this way. (2) `FormatImpact`'s no-delay fallback now states the CONDITION ("blocking — no measured delay") instead of inventing a time magnitude; a Major/Severe tier with no measured delay/queue can only be a closure or blocking crash (incident-type floor), so it never asserts "heavy/severe delays". (3) Deleted the now-unused `CorridorMagnitude.Label`.

**Rationale:** Ranking and spoken magnitude are different axes — `CorridorMagnitude.Classify` still tiers for selection/sectioning (a long standstill rightly ranks high), but the data must not hand the writer a tier WORD it reads as time-magnitude. This kills the oversell at the source (defence in depth with the draft.md delay-minute-magnitude rule). Locked by `TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests` (no "congestion, major" beside "(minor delays)"; closure → "no measured delay", never "heavy/severe delays").

**Consequences:** `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` + `CorridorMagnitude` updated; 614 Domain + 753 Infrastructure non-integration tests pass. Remaining data-side follow-ups: the "Neranwood near Neranwood" self-anchor (road-name extraction) and road-name artifacts ("Hill Freeway") — both `CorridorAggregator`/`ResolveDisplayRoadName`, separate from this magnitude fix.

## 2026-06-24 — Sparse/all-clear bulletins fill the 30s slot with good-runs; eval wires good-runs; no internal jargon

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The product needs EXACTLY-30s bulletins (the slot-length pipeline pads ≤0.3s then fails to fallback), so the script must carry ~30s (~75-90 words) of content. The category probe showed sparse/all-clear markets producing 2-12s scripts — unusable. Root cause was two-fold: (1) the eval (`BulletinEval`) never populated good-runs (flowing roads), the very mechanism that fills a quiet bulletin, so it tested an impoverished input; (2) the generator set `goodRunsAreFill` only when `corridorCount==0`, so a sparse (1-2 incident) bulletin hit the "keep the clear-run mention short" branch — contradicting the "fill the slot" rule. Two eval scorers also false-flagged: `FabricationScorer` didn't know good-run roads (flagged them as fabricated) and the imperial check matched "Mile" inside road names ("Ten Mile Track").

**Decision:** (1) `BulletinEval` now fetches free-flowing roads + `GoodRunPolicy.SelectForGeneration` and sets `GoodRunRoads`/`FlowPool` (mirrors `BroadcastOrchestrator`; live-only, replay has no flow) — permanent fidelity fix. (2) Generator: `goodRunsAreFill = corridorCount == 0 || isLowCorridorCount` so a sparse bulletin uses fill-mode good-runs. (3) `draft.md` fill branch + `system.md` reworded: sparse traffic FILLS the slot with the flowing-road good-runs (never pad with invented content; the old "write a shorter bulletin" licence removed). (4) `system.md` BOUNDARY: never voice internal data labels ("corridor", "good run(s)" as a noun, "monitored route", "listed as"). (5) Eval scorers fixed: `FabricationScorer` takes good-run roads into its allowed vocabulary; `TargetShapeScorer` imperial regex is lowercase-only (road names like "Ten Mile Track" no longer trip it).

**Rationale:** The fill mechanism existed in production but was untested and mis-gated for sparse. With it wired, V0 all-clear went from a 6-word echo to a real "Upper Bird Road's flowing well, … running smoothly …" naming flowing roads, and sparse bulletins use them as the body. Confirmed live across 5 categories: V2/V3 fill 30s; jargon leaks gone; honest scorecard (no false fabrication/imperial fails).

**Consequences:** Honest ceiling — road-data-only fill reaches ~20s on a genuinely-quiet market; a full 30s there needs supplementary content (weather/fuel, not yet wired into the eval) OR is a product decision (pad to 30s vs accept a ~20s all-clear + bed vs generic filler — the dead-air fallback already exists). 753 Infra + 614 Domain tests pass. Recommended next: wire weather/fuel into the eval to complete the V0/V1 fill story.

## 2026-06-24 — Weather + fuel complete the 30s fill; eval wires + enables them; numeric budget exempts them

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Good-runs got sparse/all-clear bulletins to ~20s but not a full 30s — the honest ceiling of road-data-only fill. The supplementary sources (weather, fuel) are the rest of the answer (ATN's KIIS bundles traffic + weather), but the eval never fetched them, and `WeatherOptions.Enabled`/`FuelOptions.Enabled` default false so the providers hard-stop. Direct probe confirmed the HERE key HAS weather access (200, real data).

**Decision:** (1) `BulletinEval` now fetches weather + fuel (`IWeatherProvider.GetWeatherAsync` / `IFuelPriceProvider.GetFuelPricesAsync`) and sets `context.Weather`/`Fuel` (mirrors `BroadcastOrchestrator`; live-only). (2) `TestConfigurationHelper` sets `Weather:Enabled=true` + `Fuel:Enabled=true` so the eval exercises them (these default false platform-wide; a real market enables per the SoW). (3) `draft.md` weather rule tightened to ONE clause — conditions + temperature only; skip wind/humidity/rain-% unless a weather ALERT. (4) Eval `TargetShapeScorer` numeric-budget now EXEMPTS weather/fuel numerics ($-prices, "N degrees", "N%") — matching the prompt's exemption — so the ≤2 budget reflects TRAFFIC figures only and price decimals no longer trip the "decimals!" flag.

**Rationale:** With weather + fuel wired and enabled, all five categories now produce a complete ~26-32s bulletin (overall target-shape 90%): V0 Scottsdale = good-runs + "clear and cool, 6 degrees … Unleaded's cheapest at $1.73"; V1-V3 all in-band. The numeric-exemption fix removed the false 50-75% scores the weather/fuel numbers were causing.

**Consequences:** The eval now exercises the FULL market-content set (traffic + monitored routes + good-runs + weather + fuel) — faithful to production. Under replay the weather/fuel providers aren't replay-wrapped, so they 401 on the test key and degrade to None (no script change, minor wasted call). 753 Infra + 614 Domain tests pass. Minor residual: the model still occasionally voices wind/rain-% despite the prompt (could trim `ContentFormatters.FormatWeather` at source); the V0 opener still echoes "No significant traffic incidents to report."

## 2026-06-24 — Eval covers every content permutation: Traffic/Weather/Fuel toggles × density

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The eval had been run with everything-on. We need confidence the pipeline behaves across ALL content permutations a market can be configured with — Traffic/Weather/Fuel each on or off — at every traffic density (none / sparse / sufficient).

**Decision:** `BulletinScenario` gains `Traffic`/`Weather`/`Fuel` toggles (default `true`/`false`/`false` = production `BulletinContentSelection.Default`, traffic-only). `BulletinEval` gates each fetch on the scenario's toggle (mirrors `BroadcastOrchestrator` content gating) and sets `request.Content`; the generator already branches on `context.Content.Traffic` (→ `noTraffic`) and `context.Weather/Fuel.HasValue`, so any permutation renders correctly. The scorecard/output label shows `[TWF]`. The all-off combo is excluded — `BulletinContentSelection.HasAnySource` rejects it upstream (no bulletin). The 3-market canonical baseline stays traffic-only; permutations are a temporary probe (explicit toggles + MaxCorridors), then reverted.

**Rationale:** A 10-scenario live probe confirmed correct gating for all 7 non-degenerate combos × densities: TW- voices weather not fuel, T-F voices fuel not weather, T-- quiet markets fall back to good-runs only, and no-traffic combos produce weather/fuel-only bulletins. Faithful to production per-market content selection.

**Consequences:** COVERAGE FINDING — no-traffic bulletins under-fill badly (weather-only ≈ 6s, fuel-only ≈ 10s, weather+fuel ≈ 12s): a single weather observation + fuel prices cannot fill a 30s slot. Open product question: is a 30s no-traffic bulletin a real requirement? If so it needs richer data (multi-period forecast/outlook); otherwise traffic-off is an edge config. T-- quiet markets (no weather/fuel) also sit ~16-19s — weather/fuel are the fill. Minor LLM glitches observed: a duplicated road word ("Upper Bird Bird Road"), fuel-only voicing station counts, weather voicing wind. 753 Infra + 614 Domain tests pass.

## 2026-06-24 — Every bulletin targets the full slot: slot-floor budget + draft prompt band + all-clear expand backstop

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Quiet markets shipped under-length (an all-clear Newcastle at 20s / 47 words). The product airs in a fixed slot (exactly slot length): a read below the slow-fill floor (≈ `(slot-0.3)/MaxSlowDownFactor` ≈ 27s for a 30s slot, ~90% of the word target) cannot be stretched to the slot and falls back (dead air, no bulletin). Root cause: `DraftWordBudget.Compute` deliberately shrank the word floor for low-corridor bulletins (0 corridors → `target/4` ≈ 18 words) under an obsolete "quiet = short bulletin" philosophy — predating the good-runs fill mechanism. The floor was also dead in practice (`draft.md` never surfaced `targetWordsMin`, and nothing gated under-length).

**Decision:** Every bulletin targets the full slot regardless of density. (1) `DraftWordBudget.Floor` is now the slow-fill floor (`max(10, target*9/10)`) for ALL corridor counts; `IsLow` (corridors ≤ 2) still drives the good-run fill tone. (2) `draft.md` and `refine.md` surface the band explicitly — "keep it between `{{targetWordsMin}}` and `{{targetWordsMax}}` words; under the min leaves dead air and is rejected, over the max runs long" — so both the draft and the review→refine pass hold the floor (refine previously trimmed expanded drafts back below it because it only saw the ceiling). (3) Deterministic backstop in `GenerateScriptAsync`: when an all-clear/sparse draft (≤ 2 corridors, matching `goodRunsAreFill`) lands below the floor and good-runs exist, it expands once via `RefineScriptAsync` using the real flowing roads — honest fill only, never fabrication. Incident-heavy markets are left to review→refine. The backstop is gated on `GoodRunRoads.Count > 0`, so minimal unit-test contexts never trigger it.

**Rationale:** A live full-pipeline probe across all-clear → oversubscribed (Scottsdale/Newcastle all-clear, Perth/Gold Coast moderate, Sydney 14-corridor) confirmed the SHIPPED scripts now land 27-34s — the two all-clears that previously shipped 20-25s both hold at 27s, elaborating real flowing roads with Aussie colour instead of a terse list. An initial over-correction (zealous "MUST fill" wording + an untargeted backstop pushed busy markets to 35-40s) was fixed by the [min,max] band and the ≤2-corridor gate.

**Consequences:** Traffic-bearing markets (all-clear, sparse, busy) now reliably fill the slot, so they stop failing `SlotFilled` and falling back. The audio `SlotFilled` gate remains the final hard guarantee. Genuinely no-traffic bulletins (weather/fuel only, 0 good-runs) still can't fill 30s — the backstop correctly doesn't fire there (no fill material); that case needs richer data (forecast/outlook) or is an edge config. `DraftWordBudgetTests` rewritten (floor is the slot floor regardless of corridors). 755 Infra + 614 Domain non-integration tests pass.

## 2026-06-24 — ATN data-quality + honest-measurement pass: drive-time, road-name, no-traffic forecast fill, eval slot-fill gate

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live full-pipeline critique surfaced four issues. (1) A closure with no real delay voiced a pointless drive-time ("a 5 min drive time instead of the usual 5"). (2) Self-anchors and duplicate road names ("the Neranwood area near Neranwood", "Reid Highway … the same stretch at Reid Highway") — credibility-killers an ATN reviewer flags instantly. (3) No-traffic bulletins (weather/fuel only) under-fill at 6-17s. (4) The eval scored length softly, printing PASS for sub-floor scripts that production rejects via `SlotFilled`.

**Decision:**
- **Drive-time (`TrafficNarrativeSummarizer`):** the per-corridor "Drive time: N min (normally M)" line emits only on a meaningful delta (`DriveTime − Normal ≥ 2`); the monitored-route headline surface is untouched.
- **Road names (`TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` + `CorridorAggregator`):** the " near {suburb}" anchor is suppressed when the road name already contains the suburb (case-insensitive); closure/status words ("closed", "shut", "blocking", …) join the anchor-filler set so "At Reid Highway - Closed" is recognised as self-referential; same-road corridors are merged by road name, folding directionless incidents into the highest-impact direction (outbound vs citybound stay separate, placeholders never merge).
- **No-traffic fill (`WeatherOptions`/`HereWeatherProvider`/`WeatherReport`/`ContentFormatters`/`draft.md`):** weather now requests `forecast7daysSimple`; the provider builds a short `Outlook` ("reaching N later today; tomorrow …"); the data block renders it; the draft prompt voices it as fill on quiet days (`noTraffic` or `goodRunsAreFill`) and forbids it in busy bulletins. The combined-products response returns three separate `places[]` (`observations` / `dailyForecasts` / `alerts`), so the parse now scans ALL places — which also fixed a latent bug where weather alerts (under `places[].alerts`, not top-level) were never surfaced.
