- **Eval slot-fill gate (`BulletinScorers`/`BulletinScorecard`):** length is now a hard PASS/FAIL — `DurationResult.IsUnderfilled` when `EstimatedSeconds < TargetSeconds × 0.9` (the slow-fill floor) flips the overall verdict to FAIL and renders `UNDERFILL`, mirroring production's `SlotFilled`.

**Rationale:** Verified across repeated live full-pipeline probes (Perth/Sydney busy, Gold Coast moderate, Scottsdale all-clear, Melbourne no-traffic). Perth now reads "Reid Highway's closed at Altone Road, blocking through traffic" — voiced once, real cross-street, no self-anchor; Melbourne voices "heading for 16 later today, with a sunny, cool 15 tomorrow"; weather alerts ("heavy rain flagged later") now lead correctly. Three streams (two parallel subagents + this agent) integrated and gated together.

**Consequences:** No-traffic bulletins improved (outlook voiced) but still ~15-18s — a weather+fuel-only bulletin genuinely cannot fill a 30s slot, and the eval now honestly FAILs it as UNDERFILL rather than a false PASS; closing it fully needs multi-day forecast/more content or is an edge config (the slot's `SlotFilled` fallback handles it). 765 Infra + 619 Domain non-integration tests pass (+14 new across the four fixes).

## 2026-06-24 — Eval mirrors production word-target compliance via shared SlotFitPlanner

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live spread showed traffic-bearing markets the eval marked UNDERFILL at ~26.8s (Newcastle, Gold Coast). Investigation: production's generation loop ALWAYS sets `TargetWordCountOverride` (from voice calibration), so `BroadcastOrchestrator.EnsureWordTargetComplianceAsync` runs for every shipped bulletin and expands an under-length final script toward the slot. The EVAL set no override and omitted that step, so it under-reported — showing short drafts production would have filled. (Overshoot is corrected downstream by the audio pipeline's measure-then-trim, not at the script level.)

**Decision:** Extracted the shared decision into `SlotFitPlanner` (Domain): `NeedsExpansion(words, target)` (true below `target − Tolerance`, Tolerance 5) and `ExpansionFeedback(target)` (expand using flowing roads / weather outlook / fuel already in the data; never invent). `EnsureWordTargetComplianceAsync` now sources its threshold + feedback from it (behaviour-identical: same tolerance; the feedback string is enriched, asserted by no test). `BulletinEval`'s full-pipeline mirror now runs the same compliance expansion after review→refine, computing the target from the slot duration × WPM — so the eval reflects the SHIPPED length.

**Rationale:** With the mirror in place, a live full-pipeline spread (Scottsdale all-clear → Sydney 14-corridor) lands traffic-bearing markets at 30-36s — the previously-failing under-fillers (Newcastle 26.8→32s, Gold Coast 26.8→30s) now clear the slot, confirming production already expands them. Busy markets at 34-36s are trimmed to 30s by the audio measure-then-fit. Single source of truth prevents eval/production drift.

**Consequences:** Every traffic-bearing bulletin now clusters near 30s end to end. The only remaining UNDERFILL is the genuine no-traffic ceiling (weather+fuel only ≈ 20s, content-limited — the compliance expands as far as the data allows, then accepts best). 765 Infra + 627 Domain + 357 Application tests pass; orchestrator refactor verified behaviour-identical (no test regressions).

## 2026-06-25 — Reproducible regression corpus: persist generator input, replay flagged bulletins

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Iterating on bulletin quality needs a way to prove a prompt/code change actually fixes a script we were unhappy with — not just "looks better once". The deployed job record (`radioJobs`) already persisted the data, but only as reduced *review* DTOs (corridors without full incidents, `MonitoredRoutes` not stored at all), which can't faithfully rebuild the writer input.

**Decision:** Capture the **complete writer input** per job and make it replayable:
- `GeneratorInputSnapshot` (Domain) — a round-trippable record of everything the generator consumes (corridors+incidents, monitored routes, weather, fuel, good-runs, flow pool, content selection, guidance, feedback). `FromContext`/`ToContext`; routing-only corridor coords stripped (writer ignores them; they don't serialise). Serialised with the Option-aware `JsonDefaults.Storage`.
- Persisted per job as `Job.GeneratorInput` → `radioJobs.GeneratorInputJson` (best-effort: the orchestrator capture is wrapped in try/catch and never fails the job; read tolerates legacy/null).
- `test/corpus/regressions/<label>.json` — committed fixtures (snapshot + original script + flag reason). `RegressionEval.ReplayAsync` rebuilds the context and runs the LIVE generator + the **shared** review→refine→compliance pass (`BulletinEval.ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync`, extracted so eval and regression can't drift), scores it, and writes a before/after pack. `RegressionCorpusTests` ([Integration], `ARN_EVAL_LIVE=1`) iterates the corpus.
- `scripts/capture-regression.sh <jobId> <label> [reason]` promotes a deployed job into a fixture from its `GeneratorInputJson`. Old jobs (pre-snapshot) are reconstructed by hand — see `MilduraFixtureBuilder` (the first fixture, `mildura-flowlist`, rebuilt from job `62475adce79e4c77a03f138430a89d6b`).

**Rationale:** Hold the writer input constant (the captured snapshot) so the only variable across a re-run is the prompt/code — that isolates and proves improvement. Replaying at the generator level (not re-aggregation) matches what's persisted and targets the writer/summarizer/prompt layer where bulletin-quality defects live. A live replay of the Mildura fixture reproduced the flagged defects (8-road enumerated good-run list, recited fuel), confirming faithful capture.

**Consequences:** Any unsatisfactory bulletin becomes a permanent, version-controlled regression case. 770 Infra (+5: snapshot round-trip ×2, persistence ×2, fixture builder) + 627 Domain + 357 Application tests pass; snapshot capture is additive and best-effort (no hot-path risk). Future jobs capture losslessly; pre-snapshot jobs need manual reconstruction. Routing coords + audio aren't reproduced (writer doesn't use them).

## 2026-06-25 — Rundown table: flow scored with incidents; priority roads typed by boost axis

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The job-view Adjust surface was verbose and split incidents from flowing roads; market priority roads only boosted incident corridors (a flat `string[]`), and flowing roads had no comparable score.

**Decision:** (1) Score flowing "good-run" roads on the same primitives as incident corridors via `CorridorAggregator.CalculateFlowScore(fc, lengthMetres)` (road importance + length; severity/density/delay are zero for a clear road) **but damped by `FlowImpactFactor` (0.5) into a band below incidents** so flow reads as slot-filler; the market priority ×1.3 boost can lift a well-flowing priority road back into contention. Both rank in one `RundownTable` (drag in/out, road-class column, whole-row expand, no per-row rationale). (2) Make per-market priority roads typed — `PriorityRoad{ Name, BoostIncidents, BoostFlowing }` end-to-end — so a road can boost incident corridors, flowing good-runs, or both; the operator chooses per road. Legacy `string[]` entries migrate to boosting both.

**Rationale:** A clear road is less newsworthy than a problem, so flow should generally rank below incidents and only fill when incidents are sparse — yet a priority road flowing well is worth airing even amid incidents, which the per-road boost expresses. "This road matters when flowing" is a distinct intent from "boost it when it has incidents", hence the two axes.

**Consequences:** `FlowRoad`/`JobFlowRoad`/`FlowRoadDto` gain `Score`, `FunctionalClass`, `PriorityBoosted`; `IPriorityRoadsRepository`/`PriorityRoadsDto`/`PriorityRoadsHttpTrigger`/`TableStoragePriorityRoadsRepository` carry typed roads (tolerant read of legacy strings); `BroadcastOrchestrator` gates the ×1.3 incident boost on `BoostIncidents` and the flow score boost + watch eligibility on `BoostFlowing`. Web: `RundownTable` rewrite, typed priority-roads hooks/manager (per-road boost pills), mock updated. The old Adjust components remain on disk for revert (knip flags them). Backend builds + Domain/Application/Infrastructure tests green; web tsc/eslint/build + Playwright jobs-review/a11y/guidance green.

## 2026-06-25 — Rundown: unified incident + good-run selection (supersedes same-day grouping)

**Status:** accepted (supersedes the "separate bands" note in the entry above)

**Context:** Showing incidents and good-runs as two separate score-ranked bands was coherent but the operator wanted them ranked TOGETHER, with good-runs competing for the slot — included only when they out-rank a (minor) incident or are a priority road. The earlier separate-bands display was a workaround for the fact that good-runs were selected by a *different* rule (the count-based `GoodRunPolicy` gating) than incidents (the corridor cut); interleaving them then produced low good-runs above higher below-cut incidents.

**Decision:** Make selection itself unified. New `BulletinContentSelector.Select(corridors, flowPool, slotCapacity, maxGoodRuns)` ranks incident corridors (impact score) and flowing roads (damped flow score + priority boost) together and takes the top-N for the slot; on a tie an incident wins. The orchestrator now builds the flow pool BEFORE the cut (`BuildFlowPoolAsync`, hoisted out of `EnrichWithMarketContentAsync`) and uses the unified selector for the automatic case (initial + non-curated regenerate). Operator curation still overrides on regenerate (corridor pick via `CorridorCurator`; good-run pick via `GoodRunPolicy` operator selection). The web `RundownTable` is one interleaved score-ranked list (on-air / below-the-cut), so on-air always out-scores below-the-cut; per-road checkboxes are removed (drag a row in/out), and the only checkboxes are the per-incident "which to mention" toggles inside an expanded road.

**Rationale:** The operator reasons about one ranked rundown. Damped flow scores mean good-runs read as filler and only surface when incidents are minor (quiet bulletin) or a market priority boost lifts them — matching the editorial intent without a separate supplementary track. Replacing the count-based gating with score ranking is the deliberate evolution of the 2026-06-23 good-run policy.

**Consequences:** `GoodRunPolicy.SelectForGeneration` is now used only for the operator-curated good-run override (its automatic count-based branch is bypassed for fresh generation). `EnrichWithMarketContentAsync` no longer fetches/selects flow (callers set `FlowPool`/`GoodRunRoads`). A weighted/priority good-run is no longer *guaranteed* to air in a busy bulletin — it competes on its (boosted) score; the priority ×1.3 boost is the lever. New `BulletinContentSelectorTests` (5) + existing Domain (635) / Application (357) suites green; web tsc/eslint/build + Playwright jobs-review/a11y green. Mock job `arn-job-00008` good-runs set below-the-cut for coherence (Melbourne's incidents all out-score them).

## 2026-06-25 — Corridor is the bulletin unit: collapse directional corridors by road name

**Status:** accepted (supersedes the directional-separation behaviour in `MergeSameRoadCorridors`)

**Context:** `CorridorAggregator` grouped incidents by `(RoadName, Direction)` and deliberately kept directional corridors apart (e.g. "Gateway Motorway outbound" vs "westbound" as two corridors). But every other layer is road-name based: `selectedCorridors` matches by name, operator curation toggles by name, and the LLM voices a road once. Result (seen on deployed brisbane job `ecf53c80…`): 8 corridors selected for only 5 distinct roads — the duplicates collided on the operator UI drag id (dragging one row moved both), wasted bulletin slots, and crowded out higher-impact roads (rank-1 Centenary Highway dropped).

**Decision:** `MergeSameRoadCorridors` now collapses ALL corridors sharing a display road name into one bulletin unit (via `MergeCorridorGroup`: best corridor + unioned incidents + recomputed impact). Directional nuance survives per-incident (each incident keeps its heading in its description) and in scoring — `ApplyTimeWeighting` runs after the merge and boosts the merged corridor's dominant direction. Frontend `buildCoverageGroups` also dedupes corridors by road name (keep highest-impact representative) so jobs stored before this fix render one row per road.

**Rationale:** At the bulletin's granularity (a 6-road, 30s read; road-name curation/selection; LLM voices a road once) one road = one unit. The directional split predated the road-name curation/selection/slot model and only produced duplicates and wasted slots. Brisbane script eval after the change: 5 distinct roads voiced (was duplicating), and previously-crowded-out roads (Warrego Highway, Pacific Motorway) now make the cut.

**Consequences:** `SameRoadDifferentDirection_*` test updated to assert collapse (`CollapsesToOneCorridor`); Domain (635) + Application (357) suites green. Web `CorridorFixture.DriveTimeMinutes` made optional (latent type hole: the mock corpus omits drive time on un-routed corridors; vite had shipped it because it skips typecheck). Deployed to dev (frontend SWA + Functions). NOTE: the directional time-weighting boost now applies to the merged corridor's dominant direction rather than each direction separately.

## 2026-06-25 — Flowing priority roads compete by operator-set tier (replaces fixed ×1.3)

**Status:** accepted (generalises the fixed flow boost; supersedes `PriorityRoad.BoostFlowing` bool)

**Context:** All flowing good-run roads scored the same (~42.5 on the deployed job) — `CalculateFlowScore(fc,length)` ignores how much a road matters to listeners, and the only lift was a fixed `BoostFlowing` ×1.3 (binary). Operators had no way to say "this clear road is worth mentioning even on a busy day." Considered HERE `typicalDuration` recovery ("normally busy, now clear"), but the ATN sample reads (docs/reference/atn-bulletin-style-samples.md) treat flowing roads qualitatively (a watched-road roll-call), never "vs normal" — so that was over-engineering. The operator's editorial judgement, expressed as a per-road weight, is the right model.

**Decision:** `PriorityRoad.BoostFlowing` (bool) → `FlowTier` (`FlowPriorityTier`: None/Normal/High/Critical). The tier is an ADDITIVE bonus on the incident-impact scale (`PriorityRoads.FlowTierBonus`: Normal +15, High +50, Critical +110), added after the damped flow score in `BroadcastOrchestrator.MarkWeightedFlowRoads`. So a flowing road lands predictably against the incident bands — High reaches minor-incident contention (~90), Critical reaches moderate (~150) — and still competes in the unified `BulletinContentSelector` (a stack of bigger incidents buries it; never a guarantee). Incident axis unchanged (`BoostIncidents` ×1.3). Additive, not multiplicative, because the damped flow base (~30–62) is far below incidents and hidden from operators, so a multiplier would be large and unintuitive.

**Rationale:** Deterministic, operator-controlled, zero HERE cost, matches ATN's watched-roads model. The tier dominates ranking; road length/class only nudges within a tier.

**Consequences:** Wire/contract: `PriorityRoadDto.BoostFlowing` (bool) → `FlowTier` (string "none"|"normal"|"high"|"critical"); web `PriorityRoadEntry.boostFlowing` → `flowTier`; `PriorityRoadsManager` swaps the Flowing pill for an Off/Normal/High/Critical select. Storage (`TableStoragePriorityRoadsRepository`) tolerant-reads three shapes (string[] → tier High; legacy typed `BoostFlowing` false→None / else High; current `FlowTier` as-is). Enum serialises as a string via `[JsonConverter(JsonStringEnumConverter)]`. New tests: FlowTierBonus monotonicity + band landings, High-flow beats-minor-not-major selection, legacy-typed migration, tier round-trip. Domain (639) + Application (357) + Infrastructure (777) green; web tsc/eslint/build + Playwright guidance-rules/a11y green. Deployed to dev (SWA + Functions).

## 2026-06-25 — Regeneration honours per-incident exclusion, slot length, and re-voice

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live testing of the deployed regeneration flow found three operator changes the web "Revise" dialog sends that the backend silently ignored: `targetDurationSec` (the duration override was dropped — `BuildRegenerationQueueMessage` used the stored `job.TargetDurationSeconds`), `editedIncidents` (per-incident include/exclude — no DTO field, so `System.Text.Json` dropped it; only the mock store honoured it), and `revoiceOnly` (the "Re-voice only" button triggered a full LLM regeneration instead of re-voicing the script). Separately, `editedScript` reached the LLM but the review stage stripped operator wording, so an operator could not get exact words to air.

**Decision:** Wire all three through. `RegenerateJobRequest`/`RegenerateJobCommand`/`RegenerationQueueMessage`/`BroadcastWithTraffic` gain `ExcludedIncidentKeys` + `RevoiceOnly`. `JobsHttpTrigger` maps `editedIncidents` (`Included=false`) → excluded HERE ids. `JobService.RegenerateJobAsync` applies `TargetDurationSec` to the job (made `Job.TargetDurationSeconds` settable) before building the queue message. `CorridorCurator.ExcludeIncidents` drops excluded incidents from the FRESH fetch by id (cleared ones ignored; emptied corridors removed), applied in `TryRefreshTrafficAsync` alongside or without corridor curation. `RevoiceOnly` takes a new `OrchestrateAsync(BroadcastWithTraffic)` branch (`RevoiceExistingScriptAsync`) that synthesises the existing/edited script VERBATIM — skipping the traffic re-fetch and the LLM draft→review→refine loop — still running content-safety and the delivery director, then slot-fill + save.

**Rationale:** Closes the gap between UI affordances and backend behaviour (controls that did nothing). Incident HERE ids are stable across fetches, so id-match exclusion survives the ≤30-min freshness re-fetch (same approach as road-level `CorridorCurator.Apply`). Re-voice gives operators verbatim control of the words on air without disabling the editorial guardrails that the full data-driven Regenerate path still enforces.

**Consequences:** Resolves the rundown-redesign §1.1 "per-incident no-op" finding (P3) and the `editedScript`-not-reflected gap (now served by Re-voice). Shared `ApplyDeliveryDirectionAsync` + `FinalizeAudioAsync` helpers were extracted from the generation path (no behaviour change; all orchestrator tests green). New tests: `CorridorCuratorTests` (+5), `JobMessageBuilderTests` (+2), `RegenerationMappingExtensionsTests` (+2), `JobServiceTests` (+4), and E2E `RegenerationAndFallbackE2ETests` (+3: revoice-verbatim, incident-exclusion, target-duration). Domain/Application/Functions unit suites + the three new E2E cases green. Deploy to dev + on-air re-verification pending PIM Owner activation.

## 2026-06-25 — Bulletins must weave like ATN, not recite data or roll-call roads

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live-HERE scenario matrix (12 condition permutations, 30s, shipped pipeline) critiqued against the ATN corpus (`docs/reference/atn-bulletin-style-samples.md`) showed the generated reads "sounded AI-generated" for two reasons: (1) every quiet tail dumped a flat roll-call of up to 8 clear roads ("Boundary Road, Waterworks Road, Logan Motorway, … are all running well") where ATN sweeps an area; (2) incidents came out as a stack of identical "Road X is [state], with Y minutes" clauses with three minute-counts in a row. Root causes were prompt-side: `prompts/draft.md` said "Name as many of these roads as it takes to fill the slot", and `BroadcastOrchestrator.GoodRunScriptCap` fed 8 roads.

**Decision:** Prompt-side rewrite (+ one constant). `draft.md` good-run guidance (fill + secondary) now: name the two or three roads that matter, sweep the rest into one phrase, group by area — a roll-call is a FAIL. `draft.md`/`system.md` item-flow now require weaving with VARIED item intros and forbid repeating the "Road X is [state], with Y minutes" template. Numeric rule cut to ONE headline figure (a drive-time comparison counts as the one), every other item qualitative, never stacked numbers. `system.md` STYLE DEFAULTS gained an explicit anti-roll-call rule and a BOUNDARY forbidding narration of absent data ("no weather details provided"). `review.md` rejects road-name roll-calls and number stacking; `refine.md` fills by area-sweep + concrete data detail (anchors/lanes/directions), never extra road names or numbers. `GoodRunScriptCap` 8 → 6.

**Rationale:** The ATN ground truth weaves and sweeps; the divergence was entirely a slot-fill/recitation behaviour the prompt was actively teaching ("name as many roads as it takes"). Capping the fed pool curbs the dump at the source; the prompt enforces the on-air shape. Numbers are ATN's scarcest resource (1–2 per read) — one headline + qualitative rest matches the corpus and kills the data-dump feel.

**Consequences:** Verified — deterministic eval (`scripts/eval.sh`, replay) fabrication/style/safety PASS on Sydney/Melbourne/Gold Coast; the area-sweep appears even with no flow data. Live-HERE scenario matrix (all 12 permutations, shipped pipeline) flows and none dumps a road list; numeric stacking eliminated; the monitored-route headline now reads naturally ("the M4 from Parramatta to the CBD") rather than the verbatim route label. KNOWN LIMIT: on sparse, anchor-poor, NO-flow traffic-only data (replay Sydney/Gold Coast worst case) the draft underfills the word estimate because padding levers were removed — production has live flow/good-runs to fill honestly (live matrix filled 65–85 words) and the audio slot-fill + same-day fallback guarantee slot length, so this is a corpus artifact. Operator-curated corridor ORDER and producer off-data CAUSE adherence remain intermittent (model variance; those prompt paths unchanged) — a dedicated hardening pass is the follow-up. No code logic changed beyond the `GoodRunScriptCap` constant; prompts are loaded at runtime.

## 2026-06-25 — Content-limited underrun routes to the fallback chain synchronously, not a hard failure

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-06-24 "exactly slot length" rule makes `BroadcastOrchestrator` reject a take whose natural read cannot fill the slot within the ≤10% slow-down cap + ≤0.3s silence pad (`SpeechDurationOptions`). For genuinely quiet markets (e.g. Darwin, traffic-only, 0 incidents, 2–3 light corridors) the honest read is simply too short — observed on deployed dev jobs `977bafff…` (25.8s natural read for a 30s slot) and `ad8bec73…` (38.2s for 60s). The old path called `MarkJobFailedAsync` and shipped nothing: the job surfaced as `Failed` with a "🚨 Bulletin Failed" notification (wrong signal — the pipeline worked correctly, the market was quiet), and because "Content-limited:" is not a permanent TTS error, `BroadcastQueueTrigger` threw → the queue **redelivered and re-ran the whole job** until poison. The fallback chain existed only in `SchedulePollerService`, which never rescued these because (a) ad-hoc jobs carry no `FallbackDeadlineUtc` so the candidate query skips them and (b) `FillerCartAudioUrl` was empty on dev.

**Decision:** Extract the poller's fallback chain into a shared `IBulletinFallbackService` (`BulletinFallbackService`: last good same-day bulletin for the market/station → else configured filler cart → else none; transitions the job to `FallbackUsed` and persists). The poller now delegates to it (telemetry unchanged). On a content-limited generation result (`ErrorMessages.Broadcast.ContentLimitedPrefix`), `BroadcastOrchestrator` calls the service synchronously: a successful fallback returns Success with the job in `FallbackUsed`; with no fallback available the job is marked `Failed` but `BroadcastQueueTrigger` now drops content-limited failures instead of redelivering (the same fetched content cannot fill the slot on retry). A real evergreen `filler-cart.wav` was synthesised via the pipeline and set as `Broadcast__FillerCartAudioUrl` on dev.

**Rationale:** A quiet market is an expected outcome, not a fault — it should fill the slot from the existing same-day/filler chain rather than air dead or raise a false alarm, and it must never spin the queue. Sharing one chain between the poller and the orchestrator keeps the fallback logic single-sourced (no second convention). `FallbackUsed` already carries the correct notification ("🔄 Fallback Bulletin Used"), DTO mapping, and operator Approve action, so reclassification comes for free once a fallback applies.

**Consequences:** Content-limited jobs with a same-day bulletin or a configured filler now end `FallbackUsed` (slot filled), not `Failed`; no queue-retry storm. New code: `IBulletinFallbackService`/`BulletinFallbackService` (Application), `ErrorMessages.Broadcast`, `BroadcastOrchestrator.HandleContentLimitedAsync`, queue-trigger content-limited drop. Covered by `BulletinFallbackServiceTests` + `BroadcastOrchestratorTests` content-limited cases; full in-process suite green. The synchronous behaviour requires the backend redeployed to dev to take effect; the `FillerCartAudioUrl` config already benefits the deployed poller path. Follow-ups (Tier 2, not done here): pre-flight content-sufficiency check to skip the 4 wasted generate→synthesize attempts; right-size `TargetDurationSeconds` per quiet market; auto-enable weather/fuel for chronically-thin markets.

## 2026-06-25 — Surface WHY a standby bulletin aired (fallback reason), end-to-end

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** With content-limited jobs now routing to the fallback chain, the operator console only showed "Fallback Used" with no explanation — and a failed job's panel mapped a content-limited error to "An unexpected error occurred". Operators couldn't tell a quiet-market standby from a genuine fault. The job record carried the cause only in log strings (fragile to parse client-side); the `FallbackDataDto` exposed just `SourceJobId` + `AppliedAt`.

**Decision:** Record a stable cause token on the job when a fallback is applied (`FallbackReasons`: `content-limited` / `missed-window` / `operator-rejected`), set at the point the application layer applies the fallback (orchestrator, poller, operator reject-to-fallback), persisted on the job entity, and exposed as `FallbackDataDto.Reason`. The console renders a polished, warning-toned `FallbackDetailsPanel` (medallion + calm copy, in the spirit of the empty-hero `Placeholder`) at the top of the review surface: a friendly cause sentence (mapped from the token, with the slot length for content-limited) + the fallback KIND (re-aired same-day bulletin vs generic filler cart, derived from whether `SourceJobId` is set) + applied time/source. The failed-job panel's `friendlyFailureMessage` now maps content-limited to "Not enough live traffic to fill the slot".

**Rationale:** The cause is genuinely unavailable to the frontend except via log-string parsing, so a stable token plumbed through the DTO is the robust source. Presentation copy stays on the frontend (matching the existing `friendlyFailureMessage` pattern); unknown tokens degrade to a generic explanation, so old jobs (empty reason) still read sensibly. KIND is derivable, so it isn't stored twice.

**Consequences:** New: `Job.FallbackReason` (+ persisted column), `reason` params on `ApplyFallback`/`ApplyFillerFallback`, `FallbackReasons`, `IBulletinFallbackService.TryApplyFallbackAsync(job, reason, ct)`, `FallbackDataDto.Reason`, frontend `FallbackData.reason` + `FallbackDetailsPanel`. Covered by `BulletinFallbackServiceTests` (reason asserted) + the existing suites; verified visually in mock mode (job `arn-job-00012`). Requires backend + SWA redeploy to surface on live jobs; jobs created before the backend change show the generic cause.

## 2026-06-26 — Guard per-job Table Storage columns against the 32K-char property limit

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Incident-heavy markets at peak (Melbourne ~34 incidents + 20 corridors, Adelaide ~41) failed to persist their job. Azure Table Storage caps a single string property at 64 KB (32K UTF-16 chars); `GeneratorInputJson` (the deterministic-replay snapshot, already ~22K on light markets) and `AllIncidentsJson` exceed it for busy markets, so `SaveJobAsync` threw mid-pipeline ("property value exceeds the maximum allowed size (64KB)"). The job was marked `FAILED` after the audio had already been synthesised and saved, and the schedule poller's deadline sweep then replaced it with a standby — i.e. a fully-generated, good bulletin silently became a fallback. Diagnosed live on dev (jobs `e5956ffa…`, `726acb…`).

**Decision:** Add a size guard in `TableStorageJobRepository.MapToEntity`: the traffic-derived / replay columns (`IncidentsJson`, `AllIncidentsJson`, `CorridorsJson`, `FlowRoadsJson`, `GeneratorInputJson`) are passed through `FitTableProperty`, which drops a column to `null` (with a warning) when its serialized length exceeds a 30,000-char cap. The bulletin's core, render-essential fields (script, audio URL, measured duration, word timings, status, selected incidents) always persist.

**Rationale:** Never fail an otherwise-good, already-synthesised bulletin because an audit/overlay column is too big. The dropped columns are a replay snapshot (`GeneratorInput`) and a full-area incident overlay (`AllIncidents`) — useful for the regression corpus and the coverage map, but not required to air or review the bulletin. The selected-incident and corridor columns are bounded by bulletin length and effectively never trip the guard.

**Consequences:** Incident-heavy markets now reach `WAITING_APPROVAL` instead of `FAILED`→fallback (verified live: Melbourne + Adelaide regenerated, 30.00s audio, approved; `GeneratorInputJson` dropped to null, all display data intact). Replay/regression capture is lost for the rare oversized job (a warning is logged). `MapToEntity` is now an instance method. Regression test: `TableStorageJobRepositoryTests.SaveJob_OversizedColumn_IsDroppedButTheJobStillPersists`. Follow-up option (not done): move `GeneratorInput`/`AllIncidents` to blob storage to preserve replay on busy markets.

## 2026-06-26 — Weather copy reads like natural radio, not recited fields

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A live full-pipeline read of traffic+weather bulletins showed the weather clause sounding like translated metadata — "with scattered showers, broken cloud and a cool 15 degrees", "partly sunny and mild, 18 degrees, reaching 19 later today". The 2026-06-24 weather rule deliberately constrained the clause to "conditions + temperature only" and forbade wind/humidity/rain-%, which left the writer nothing but labels to stitch and a temperature read like a weather app. ARN's bar is presenter copy, not a field read-out — weather should be woven in naturally, in varied wording, saying what's worth knowing to someone on the road. Scope note (user, 2026-06-26): only Traffic, Traffic+Weather, Traffic+Weather+Fuel are in scope; weather-only/no-traffic is not a product concern.

**Decision:** Rewrote the weather guidance across three prompt layers (supersedes the "conditions + temperature only / skip wind/rain-%" rule from the 2026-06-24 entries). The steer is by PRINCIPLE, not a fixed template — explicitly no canned consequence phrase and no phrase to reuse bulletin-to-bulletin (user: don't hardcode "so roads will slick up"; allow freedom, vary it):
- `prompts/draft.md` — weather is woven in like a presenter would mention it, in the writer's own words and varied every time, saying what's worth knowing to a driver and linking it with a natural connector rather than a tacked-on weather sentence. The current temp is a short casual aside ("sitting around 18"); the weather-app read-out ("18 degrees, reaching 19 later today"), stitched raw labels ("scattered showers, broken cloud and a cool 15"), and tomorrow's Outlook are banned. Illustrative register ("bit of rain about", "gusty out there", "clear run weather-wise", "mostly dry for the run") is given as range, NOT a lookup table to repeat. The `weatherLeads` (alert) open flags the alert in natural presenter language, not the warning verbatim.
- `prompts/system.md` — STYLE DEFAULT: weather is presenter copy, woven and varied, never the same canned line twice; grounded in stated conditions (never invent a hazard); no weather-app temp or outlook read-out.
- `prompts/review.md` — the reviewer expects natural woven presenter copy and flags label-recital / forecast read-out / quoted wind-speed or rain-%; the no-fabrication check allows a consequence that follows directly from a reported condition (rain → wet roads, wind line → gusty) while still treating a NEW unstated condition (fog with no fog, flooding, hail) as fabrication.

**Rationale:** Verified live (gpt-5.4-mini, full pipeline, live HERE) across Sydney/Melbourne/Brisbane/Perth over two iterations. The copy is now natural, woven and grounded, with genuine variety across runs for the same market (Perth: "Rain, low cloud and a cool 13 … with heavy rain expected" → "Perth's sitting around 13, with rain and low cloud about, and heavy falls are on the cards"); Melbourne "it's sunny, cool, 11 degrees" woven into the good-runs line. Prompt-only change — the model already received rain-% and wind in the `{{weather}}` data block; the old rule just forbade voicing them. Fabrication/style/safety clean on the weather copy in all runs.

**Consequences:** Weather copy now sounds like radio rather than recited fields. Two residuals remain (both pre-existing, not introduced here): (1) on an active alert the open doesn't always carry the alert when current conditions are benign — Sydney ignored a "Heavy rain anticipated" forecast alert while currently just "broken clouds", exposing the alert-provenance question (HERE's forecast-alert model vs current conditions / BoM) to be settled in a separate decision. (2) The deterministic fabrication scorer flags cross-streets the writer correctly pulled from a corridor's "Source detail" free-text (Perth: "Drumpellier Drive"/"Grandis Road"/"Vaucluse Avenue") because it indexes only Location-line anchors — a traffic-side scorer gap, unrelated to weather. No code/test change; prompts load from `prompts/*.md` at startup.

## 2026-06-26 — Independent ATN-reviewer agent replaces self-judging in the eval loop

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The bulletin eval's review pack is judged by an agent, not an API model (the built-in LLM judge was removed as too lenient). But when the same agent that tunes the prompts also does the judging, its scores risk bias toward its own work. We want an independent, ATN-grounded reviewer that scores generated scripts consistently and can be leveraged instead of self-inference.

**Decision:** Added an independent `atn-reviewer` agent definition to the Arinco-internal agent configuration (a local development aid, excluded from the delivered repository). It carries a veteran ATN-editor persona + the distilled ATN style fingerprint, and is told to read `docs/reference/atn-bulletin-style-samples.md` as ground truth. It scores the SAME dimensions as the review pack (anchoring, direction, drive_time_headline, idiom, flow, clean_close, fidelity, plus weather) 0–1, names the biggest gap and the layer to change (system/draft/review/refine/summarizer), and lists fabrications. Read-only; explicitly told NOT to read the generator's prompts/decision log (judge cold) and NOT to penalise the deliberately-omitted sign-on/sign-off/sponsor wrapper. Invoked with BOTH the generated script AND its exact source data.

**Rationale:** Verified on two live scripts (Melbourne, Perth): fidelity-correct — it credited "Vaucluse Avenue"/"Drumpellier Drive" pulled from the corridor "Source detail" (which the deterministic fabrication scorer FALSE-flags) and returned 0 fabrications, and on Melbourne noted the script correctly avoided calling incident-bearing roads "flowing well"; critical and unbiased (both "borderline" — flagged templated clause-stacking, weak connectors, weather recited as a label list, missing direction); harness-aligned (per-dimension 0–1 + biggest gap + layer). It runs on a different model family from the gpt-5.4-mini generator, further reducing shared-author bias.

**Consequences:** The eval loop can now get an independent verdict instead of the tuning agent self-scoring. The reviewer's "layer to change" uses the same system/draft/review/refine/summarizer vocabulary as the pipeline. Not wired into `scripts/eval.sh` — invoked on demand; a follow-up could fan it across every market in a review pack and persist verdicts. Output is free-form structured JSON today; locking it with an output JSON schema would make automated scoring uniform.

## 2026-06-26 — Fill the slot by growing the script + speeding up, never slowing the read

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-06-24 'exactly slot length' decision filled underruns by SLOWING the read (WSOLA, up to MaxSlowDownFactor=1.10) then padding. The business owner clarified that exactly-30s is the only hard requirement; slowing was merely one means to it and is NOT required. A slowed read sounds worse (the ARN Dave/Melbourne complaint, job d696c383: 63 words slowed 27.1s->29.81s). Measurement of 251 synthesisHistory reads showed natural reads run systematically short (median 0.87x slot, 78% underran) due to LLM word-count under-production, so a speed-up-only policy needs the word budget biased long.

**Decision:** Fill the slot by GROWING the script (BroadcastOptions.WordTargetOvershoot, deployed 1.10) so the natural read lands at/over the slot, then SPEED UP (pitch-preserving compress) to exactly the slot. Never slow the read: SpeechDuration.MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0 disables slow-fill; MaxSpeedUpFactor=1.10. A read still short after content growth + retries pads <=0.3s or falls back. Deployed to dev (IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01) in appsettings.json. Supersedes the slow-fill disposition of the 2026-06-24 decision; the exactly-slot-length guarantee is unchanged.

**Rationale:** Exactly-30s is the hard playout constraint; HOW to reach it is a quality choice. Speeding a slightly-long read keeps a punchy on-air pace (ARN reads fast), whereas slowing drags and degrades. WordTargetOvershoot=1.10 is the measured fill-rate break-even vs slow-fill (speed-only fallback threshold Achieved*O < Target-0.3 equals slow-fill's Achieved*1.10 at O=1.10), so the change is fill-rate-neutral while removing the slow. Verified live: job c23c7299 grew 77->87 words, read 30.8s, compressed to exactly 30.0s, fresh (WaitingApproval), no slow.

**Consequences:** BroadcastOptions gains WordTargetOvershoot (default 1.0 no-op; dev appsettings.json sets 1.10); threaded through WordTargetCalculator.ComputeWordTargetFromWordsPerMinute and the orchestrator word-budget call. SpeechDuration MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0 + MaxSpeedUpFactor=1.10 in dev appsettings.json. Cost: fast-reader/content-thin markets need more generation retries to grow the script (observed 4 attempts for ARN Dave/Melbourne) and overruns beyond 10% trim a sentence; tune WordTargetOvershoot down or MaxSpeedUpFactor up if churn is high. Eval SlotFillFloor and prompt-band copy still describe the slot floor and remain valid. CONTEXT.md + SDD section 15 updated.

## 2026-06-26 — Good-run roads deduped against active incident corridors (no "shut and flowing")

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The independent atn-reviewer agent caught a listener-facing contradiction in a Gold Coast bulletin — "Pacific Motorway citybound … shut" then "Pacific Motorway … running pretty freely" in the same 30 seconds — that BOTH the deterministic scorer (which rated the bulletin 100%) and the main agent's self-review missed. HERE's flow API reports a road free-flowing on one segment while the incidents API reports a closure/congestion on another segment of the SAME road; neither `BulletinContentSelector.Select` nor `GoodRunPolicy.SelectForGeneration` removed a flow road whose name collided with an active incident corridor, so a road could air as both blocked and clear.

**Decision:** Added `GoodRunPolicy.ExcludeCorridorRoads(flowPool, corridors)` (Domain) — drops any flow road whose `RoadName` exactly matches (case-insensitive, trimmed) an active corridor's `RoadName`. Exact match is correct because `TrafficCorridor.RoadName` is the base road name (direction is a separate field), so it does NOT over-drop genuinely distinct roads (a "Smith Street" incident keeps "Smith Street Motorway" as a good run). Applied at BOTH flow-pool build sites — `BroadcastOrchestrator.BuildFlowPoolAsync` (production) and `BulletinEval.EvaluateAsync` (eval) — so the pool is clean before either selector runs and the persisted Flow tab no longer offers an incident road as a good-run candidate.

**Rationale:** Found and verified by the atn-reviewer feedback loop. Unit tests (`GoodRunPolicyTests`, 4 new): drops the collision, case-insensitive/trim, keeps a distinct prefix road, no-op without corridors; build green, 13 pass. End-to-end: regenerated Gold Coast TWF live — Pacific Motorway now airs as the citybound incident only, good-runs are "Stewart Road and Henri Robert Drive". A FRESH atn-reviewer re-review upgraded the bulletin borderline → would-air (fidelity 0.9→1.0, flow 0.6→0.7, weather 0.7→0.9) and flagged no contradiction.

**Consequences:** A road with any active incident is never also voiced as a good run, in every market and content combo. The loop surfaced the NEXT target: the single headline figure can land on a trivial drive-time (26 vs 25) while the worst delay (a ~13-min congestion HERE tagged "Moderate") goes unquantified — a draft-selection + summarizer-ranking issue (HERE severity labels don't track delay minutes). Next iteration candidate.

## 2026-06-26 — Resolve TTS model per voice from its verified base models (support v3 + v2-family)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** VoicesHttpTrigger hardcoded ResolvedModelId = ModelSelectionOptions.BroadcastModel (eleven_v3) for EVERY voice, ignoring the voice's ElevenLabs high_quality_base_model_ids. ModelSelector.SelectModel likewise defaults to BroadcastModel with only a language-based fallback. So trained/cloned (professional/instant) voices — built on the v2 family — were rendered on eleven_v3, which degrades clone fidelity badly (operator complaint). Dev had 3 profiles all pinned to v3: ARN Marlowe + ARN Hudson (category=professional, base models incl. eleven_multilingual_v2) and ARN Dave (category=generated/Voice Design, no base models, v3-native).

**Decision:** Added Domain VoiceModelResolver.Resolve(verifiedBaseModelIds, preferredModel): empty base list -> preferred (v3-native generated/premade); list contains preferred -> preferred; else best verified base model (eleven_multilingual_v2 > turbo_v2_5 > turbo_v2 > flash_v2_5 > first). VoicesHttpTrigger now sets ResolvedModelId via the resolver, so the per-voice default the studio/profiles/poller see is correct. Operator per-profile model override still wins (persisted on the VoiceProfileVersion, resolved live by the poller). Migrated the two professional clones (Marlowe, Hudson) to eleven_multilingual_v2 via the service PUT; ARN Dave stays v3. Deployed to dev.

**Rationale:** A voice should render on a model it is verified for; v3 is never listed in high_quality_base_model_ids, so a non-empty base list means a v2-family voice that v3 would degrade. Empty base list means a Voice-Design/generated (v3-native) voice. This supports BOTH model families per voice automatically while keeping v3 for the voices designed for it. Verified live: /voices API now resolves Marlowe/Hudson->eleven_multilingual_v2, Dave->eleven_v3; a Marlowe bulletin (job f4d83380) rendered on eleven_multilingual_v2 at exactly 30.0s.

**Consequences:** New Domain.Services.VoiceModelResolver (+ 8 unit tests). VoicesHttpTrigger uses it. No config change (BroadcastModel stays eleven_v3 as the 'preferred'). KNOWN GAP: ModelSelector.SelectModel (the no-profile fallback used by DefaultVoice + JobService when command.VoiceModel is unset) is still not capability-aware — it lacks the voice's ModelIds; acceptable because all real voices use profiles (whose model now defaults correctly) and the web sends the resolved model on manual triggers. Existing profiles saved before this change keep their stored model until re-saved/migrated (Marlowe+Hudson migrated; future ones default correctly). **CLOSED 2026-07-23** — see that day's "ElevenLabs v2/v3 model-family handling" decision: `ModelSelector.SelectModelAsync` now applies `VoiceModelResolver` to this exact fallback path.

## 2026-06-26 — Weather numbers stripped at the data layer (prompt bans alone leaked)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The atn-reviewer loop repeatedly flagged weather over-quoting — reciting wind-speed ("southerlies near 40 km/h"), rain-chance ("64% chance of rain"), and the forecast Outlook ("reaching 12 later today, clouds tomorrow"). Three rounds of prompt tightening (draft/system/review forbidding these) reduced but did NOT eliminate it: across re-runs the same Gold Coast scenario alternated between clean ("a blustery south wind") and leaking ("40 k's an hour"). A capable model reads salient numbers off the data block regardless of instructions — prompt-only bans are stochastic.

**Decision:** Remove the numbers from the prompt entirely so the model can't speak what it never sees:
- `HereWeatherProvider` — `WindDescription` is now qualitative ("fresh/blustery/strong {dir} wind") banded from wind speed, no km/h.
- `ContentFormatters.FormatWeather` — rain renders qualitatively ("Chance of rain: slight / a good chance / likely"), no %; the Outlook line is dropped from the prompt block entirely (it stays on `WeatherReport`/DTO for operator review). Temperature stays — the only weather number.
The prompt bans (draft/system/review weather rules) are kept as defense-in-depth.

**Rationale:** Verified by the loop. Build green; `ContentFormattersTests` (21) + `HereWeatherProviderTests` (9) updated and pass. A fresh full-batch atn-reviewer sweep confirms over-quoting is gone: Gold Coast weather 0.35→0.45 ("blustery south wind … a good chance of rain", no figures), Scottsdale 0.5→0.75 (outlook gone, "an easy cruise"), Melbourne/Perth temp-only — and NO reviewer flagged a quoted wind-speed/rain-%/outlook this sweep (vs the prior sweep where they did).

**Consequences:** Weather can no longer over-quote in any market — structurally impossible, not prompt-dependent. The loop surfaced the next, finer gaps (NOT over-quoting): weather still reads as a label-string in places ("overcast, mild and 18, with a blustery south wind and a good chance of rain") rather than one woven consequence; on an active alert the read sometimes leads with weather as a forecast instead of leading traffic and converting the alert to road advice (the alert-lead/provenance question). Dominant non-weather gaps remain headline severity-ranking (worst item buried under a marginal drive-time) and Gold Coast overlength (~38s overstuffing). Next candidates. Note: the `noTraffic` (weather-only, out-of-scope) draft branch still references the Outlook the block no longer carries — harmless, left as-is.

## 2026-06-26 — Marginal monitored drive-time routes no longer crowned the headline (data-layer split)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The atn-reviewer loop repeatedly flagged the worst item buried under a barely-delayed monitored drive-time route crowned "the headline run" (Sydney "M4 … 30 min, usually 28" leading over a Warringah closure; Gold Coast "Pacific Motorway … bang on 24 minutes" over a citybound standstill). Root cause: `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` labelled EVERY monitored route "Monitored drive-time routes (use for headline when delayed)" and emitted the exact "X min run, typical Y" format even at +1–2 min — the data invited the wrong lead and the word "headline" was echoed as "the headline run".

**Decision:** Split the monitored-route block by delay in `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendMonitoredRouteBullets`: routes delayed ≥5 min ("several minutes") stay headline-eligible with the numeric "X min run, typical Y, N slower" format under a header "lead with one ONLY when it is the worst item on the board"; routes at/near typical (<5 min) render qualitatively with NO minute figure ("running to time" / "running close to normal, only a touch slow") under a header "NEVER the lead, and NEVER voice an X-minute run". Dropped the echo-bait word "headline" from the data block; added "the headline"/"the headline run" to `system.md`'s banned internal-label list.

**Rationale:** Verified by the loop. `TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests` (+1 new on-time test; 37 pass), build green. Fresh full-batch atn-reviewer sweep confirms: Sydney "leads on the closure; M4 correctly NOT crowned — demoted to a closing aside with no figure" (would-air); Gold Coast "leads with the standstill; the commuter route rightly kept as an aside, NOT crowned" (send-back → borderline); no "the headline run" meta-phrase anywhere.

**Consequences:** Trivial near-typical routes can no longer be crowned the lead — the data no longer offers them as headline candidates or as an "X-min, normally Y" figure. Residual finer nuance (Melbourne): among headline-ELIGIBLE items, a meaningfully-delayed monitored route (Monash +7) can still lead over a worse-by-absolute-delay incident (Punt Road, 16-min standstill) — debatable editorially; a follow-on could rank the route's delay against the worst corridor's. The loop's now-dominant remaining gap is WEATHER WEAVING (over-quoting is fixed, but weather still reads as a label-string e.g. "Sprinkles about, broken cloud, 16" rather than a woven driving consequence — layer system), plus idiom flatness / buried magnitudes (draft/refine).

## 2026-06-26 — Weather condition distilled to one primary descriptor (kills label-stringing)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After weather over-quoting was fixed, the loop's next gap was weather "weaving" — the model strung multiple sky labels ("Sprinkles about, broken cloud, 16"). Root: HERE's `description` is a multi-clause string ("Sprinkles. Broken clouds. Cool.") and the model recited the lot.

**Decision:** `ContentFormatters.FormatWeather` distils Conditions to its primary clause (first sentence — "Sprinkles. Broken clouds. Cool." → "Sprinkles") for the prompt block; the full string stays on `WeatherReport`/DTO for operator review. The writer now sees one condition + temperature, not a label string. Per the user's earlier steer, NOT forcing a fixed driving-consequence phrase.

**Rationale:** Verified by the loop. `ContentFormattersTests` +1 (22 pass), build green. Fresh full-batch atn-reviewer sweep: the multi-label stringing is gone — Melbourne "Sunny and 11" (reviewer: "no label-string, no forecast/outlook, no percentages"; weather 0.7), Scottsdale "clear and 7" (0.7), Perth "Overcast and 17, with rain likely" (0.6), Gold Coast "Sprinkles around and 15, with a decent chance of rain" (0.5 — one condition, "broken cloud" dropped). Up from the 0.4 label-strings.

**Consequences:** Weather is now one distilled condition + a casual temp (+ qualitative rain), never a sky-label string. Remaining weather nuance is fine-polish (a casual "a sunny 11 out there" vs a terse "Sunny and 11") and "weave into a driving consequence" — bounded by the "don't hardcode the consequence" steer, so near the acceptable ceiling. The sweep surfaced higher-leverage NON-weather gaps as next: (1) a real fidelity merge-bug — Sydney conflated two distinct Warringah Freeway `Location` lines into one "closed near Brook Street … at the same spot" co-location the data never states (draft); (2) idiom flatness — standstills undersold as "the worst of it"/"in the same boat" instead of severity-bearing slang (draft); (3) Perth weak lead (weather-on-top + buried closure) and Scottsdale underfill + missing directional framing (system).

## 2026-06-26 — Weather woven in with a connecting intro + a grounded comment (not a bare tag)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User feedback after the distillation cycle: even a clean one-condition+temp tag ("clear and 7 degrees", "Sunny and 11") still isn't how a presenter does it — a radio reader INTRODUCES the weather with a connecting line and sometimes throws in a quick comment ("rug up"), not "10 and cloudy".

**Decision:** Prompt-layer (`prompts/draft.md` weather branch + `prompts/system.md` weather STYLE DEFAULT): weather must be brought in with a connecting line ("Weather-wise…", "Out there it's…", "Skies are…") and chatted conversationally, sometimes with a brief comment GROUNDED in the actual condition/temp (cold+clear → "rug up"; fine → "a great one for it"; wet → "keep the wipers going"); never a bolted-on tag. Vary the connector and comment every time (no fixed formula). All prior weather bans hold (temp the only number; no wind-speed/humidity/rain-%; no Outlook). Also carved the comment out of the no-advice BOUNDARY (`system.md` line: the ban targets traffic sign-offs / generic safety advice — "take care out there", "allow extra time" — NOT a brief grounded weather comment), so the HARD boundary doesn't suppress it.

**Rationale:** Prompt-only; verified by live regen. The connector+comment lands when there's room: Scottsdale "A clear, chilly 6 degrees around Scottsdale, so a bit of a rug-up start"; Gold Coast "Out there it's sprinkles and 15, so a bit fresh"; Perth "Perth's under overcast skies and a cool 17, with heavy rain likely". Inconsistent run-to-run (prompt-level, not deterministic) — Melbourne still produced a terse "Clear and 10" the same run.

**Consequences:** Weather now reads more like a presenter (intro + optional grounded comment) on most runs, but the bare-tag fallback still appears intermittently — this is the ceiling of a prompt-level fix for a stylistic behaviour (there is no number to strip here as there was for over-quoting). Acceptable for now; if consistency matters more, options are a stronger few-shot example or a post-draft review check that bounces a bare weather tag. Higher-leverage backlog items (the Sydney Location merge-bug, idiom flatness) remain ahead of further weather polish.

## 2026-06-28 — Same-day continuity must voice an explicit "still ongoing" callback (not just paraphrase)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A two-shot same-day verification (live HERE, Sydney) confirmed the continuity MECHANISM works — the first bulletin of the day gets no `PreviousScript` (the `GetLatestBulletinForMarketTodayAsync` lookup returns None) and every later same-day bulletin is handed the prior script + an incident delta. But the SHIPPED output expressed continuity weakly: run 2 re-phrased the body yet opened with a near-verbatim lead ("Warringah Freeway citybound's shut…") and never said "still", introducing the worst item as if fresh — the exact anti-pattern `prompts/draft.md` warns against. Root: the continuity bullet was outgunned by the louder, earlier LEAD/magnitude rule (which framed the lead item) and the `previousScript` line read as "paraphrase" ("keep continuity … vary the wording") rather than "acknowledge what's still running".

**Decision:** Prompt-only (`prompts/draft.md`). (1) Reframed the `previousScript` line from "keep continuity with it, but do NOT re-read it — vary the wording" to "build on it as an UPDATE, not a fresh report: explicitly acknowledge what's still running from it ('still', 'continues', 'that earlier…') and reflect what's changed, but do NOT re-read it word-for-word — vary the wording". (2) Strengthened the same-day-continuity bullet so a "Still ongoing" item MUST be voiced as continuing ("still shut", "still backed up") and made it bind the lead: "this applies EVEN when that item is the worst one and leads the bulletin: lead with it, but frame the lead as an ongoing situation, not breaking news." Did not touch the dense LEAD line.

**Rationale:** Verified by re-running the live two-shot. Run 1 (first of day, no prior context) stayed fresh: "Warringah Freeway citybound's **closed** at the ramp to Alfred Street North…". Run 2 (prior bulletin handed in) now opens "Warringah Freeway citybound's **still shut** from the ramp … through to the North Sydney toll plaza" + "Hill Road's in a proper standstill **as well**" — the explicit callback the prompt intends. No regression to the first bulletin: with no `previousScript` and an all-"New" delta, neither continuity clause fires.

**Consequences:** Subsequent same-day bulletins now reference the earlier one explicitly, including on the lead item. Prompt-level (not deterministic), so wording will vary run-to-run; if consistency must be guaranteed, a post-draft review check could bounce a subsequent bulletin that re-introduces a "Still ongoing" lead as fresh. Note the `Still ongoing` feed itself is narrow (`IncidentChangeFormatter.IsOngoingWorthMentioning` caps at 2 and excludes standing-footprint roadworks), so on roadworks-only bulletins the only continuity cue is the `previousScript` "build on it as an UPDATE" framing.

## 2026-06-28 — Enforce same-day continuity + closure-severity at the REVIEW layer (not draft-only)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An independent ATN-style review of a 4-bulletin same-day chain (live Sydney) found the prompt-only continuity fix was UNRELIABLE: on identical "Still ongoing" input, bulletin 3 led with "still closed" (pass) but bulletin 2 re-introduced the Warringah closure as fresh AND buried it behind a 3-min minor delay (send-back). Two systemic faults: (a) the reviewer received NO continuity context, so the review→refine loop couldn't catch a continuity miss; (b) the lead ranked on delay-minutes, so a road CLOSURE with a tiny delay number lost the lead to higher-minute congestion and was deflated to "a 2-minute hold-up".

**Decision:** (1) `LlmScriptGenerator.ReviewScriptAsync` now passes `incidentChanges` + `hasPreviousBulletin` to the reviewer. (2) `prompts/review.md` gained two checks: #9 CLOSURE SEVERITY (a closure/blockage is a headline by severity, must lead or be acknowledged at top, framed "shut/closed/avoid", never reduced to a small "X-minute" delay) and #10 SAME-DAY CONTINUITY (gated on `hasPreviousBulletin`: a "Still ongoing" item MUST carry a continuation marker and not be re-introduced as fresh or buried; a "Cleared" item must be briefly closed off). (3) `prompts/draft.md` gained a closure-leads-on-severity bullet after the LEAD rule. The review→refine loop now bounces a continuity/severity miss instead of leaving it to draft variance.

**Rationale:** Verified by re-running the live chain after the change. The previously-failing subsequent bulletin now LEADS with the closure and marks continuity: "Warringah Freeway citybound is **still shut** from the ramp to Alfred Street North through the HT Toll Plaza … and **that earlier** roadworks at Brook Street **are still** in the mix" (was: "John Street's the busiest … Over on Warringah Freeway citybound, the ramp … is closed" — buried + fresh). Bulletin 1 leads "is shut" without deflating to a minute count; bulletin 4 closes off the cleared closure and keeps the toll-plaza standstill as "still backed up". Still prompt/LLM-level so not 100% deterministic (one later bulletin in the run led with the closure but dropped the explicit "still"), but the worst failure (burying + fresh-framing) is now caught by the review gate.

**Independent re-score (atn-reviewer, neutral framing):** before the fix the buried/fresh subsequent bulletin scored would-air **NO** (drive_time_headline 0.25); after, the equivalent bulletin scores would-air **yes** with continuity rated "EXCELLENT", and all four bulletins would air standalone (fidelity ~1.0). The reviewer relocated the one continuity miss to a LATER bulletin that leads with the closure correctly but omits the literal "still" marker (rated would-air-standalone / continuity-send-back) — confirming the burying+fresh failure is gone but the soft "marker-omitted-while-lead-correct" case still slips the gate. Its #1 fix remains: harden review #10 to reject a "Still ongoing" item voiced as "is shut" even when it leads. It also flagged a non-continuity off-style signal — a 5-road bare-name roll-call in the minor tail (draft) — as the next-biggest gap.

**Consequences:** Subsequent same-day bulletins are now far more reliable at leading with and continuing an ongoing closure. The reviewer can flag continuity/severity, so refine fixes them. Residual: the continuation marker is still occasionally dropped while the lead stays correct — acceptable; if the gate must be hard, tighten review #10 to require the literal marker. Two non-continuity ATN gaps the reviewer also flagged remain backlog: the Brook-Street-vs-toll-plaza location conflation (summarizer) and the minor-roads minute-stack (refine adherence).

## 2026-06-28 — Continuity marker made conditional; roll-call resists prompt tuning (needs a deterministic check)

**Status:** accepted (continuity); open (roll-call)

**Context:** Hardening review #10 to require a continuation word on "Still ongoing" items (so a leading-but-unmarked closure stops slipping) over-corrected: the FIRST-of-day read (note = "New", no previous bulletin) started opening "Still shut…", a false continuity marker — the independent reviewer called it the worst error in that chain. Separately, two prompt attempts at killing the minor-roads roll-call (generalised review #3 + a draft sweep bullet + an "even sharing one verb" tightening) did NOT land — bulletins kept naming 4–5 minor roads.

**Decision:** (1) Made the continuity marker CONDITIONAL in `prompts/draft.md`: a "New" item, or ANY item when there is no previous bulletin, is stated plainly ("Warringah Freeway's shut") and NEVER carries "still/remains/continues/that earlier…" — those words are reserved for items tagged Still ongoing / Updated / Cleared. (2) Tightened review #3 to flag 3+ road names even when they share one verb, plus near-duplicate clone clauses.

**Rationale:** Re-ran the live chain. Continuity is now correct end-to-end across the chain: B1 "Warringah Freeway outbound **is shut**" (plain, no false marker), B2 "**still has that closure**", B3 "**still shut**", B4 "Warringah Fwy's **earlier** closure … have **both cleared**" — fresh → still → still → cleared, the intended shape, with varied markers. The B1 regression is gone. BUT the roll-call persisted across both prompt attempts (every bulletin still lists 4–5 minor road names), and B4 still stacked two minute-counts (7 then 6).

**Consequences:** Same-day continuity (the feature under test) now behaves correctly across a multi-bulletin chain — this part is done. The remaining off-style gaps (minor-roads roll-call; minute-count stacking; the earlier M6-Silverwater-Road token split) are NOT reliably fixable by prompt rules — they are LLM-adherence failures that survived explicit prompt + review-prompt instructions. Next step for those is a DETERMINISTIC post-draft check (count bare road names per clause → bounce/auto-sweep at 3+; reject a second exact minute-count; treat each source corridor name as one token), not further prompt nudging. Logged as the recommended approach; not yet implemented.

## 2026-06-29 — Deterministic road-name cap (RollCallDetector + good-run name cap); air-adequacy scoped to ARN usage

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A scenario-matrix air-adequacy audit (judged by independent atn-reviewer agents, fresh + neutral each round) found the minor/clear-road ROLL-CALL was the dominant in-scope defect and that it RESISTED prompt tuning across ~5 attempts (an explicit "HARD CAP — a fourth road name is an automatic FAIL" was ignored repeatedly). Pure prompt-only iteration plateaued at 5/8 scenarios; the holdouts were a strict cap, a data-echo, plus structural/non-scenario cases.

**Decision:** Implemented deterministic, code-level fixes (the only reliable lever for this LLM-adherence class):
1. `Domain.Services.RollCallDetector` — counts road names in code; gates the review→refine loop (production `BroadcastOrchestrator.ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync` + the eval `BulletinEval.ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync`). Rule A: >=4 clear roads = dump (safety net); Rule B: >=3 corridor names in one sentence = minor cluster -> forces a NEEDS_REVISION with a targeted "name two, sweep the rest" directive even when the LLM reviewer approved. Unit-tested (`RollCallDetectorTests`).
2. `ContentFormatters.FormatGoodRuns` — caps the clear-road NAMES exposed to the generator at 2 (+ a "plus N more clear, sweep them" note). The model cannot list roads it was never given; this is what actually killed the all-clear dump (the bounce alone failed there, since on an all-clear the names ARE the content). Verified live: Scottsdale went 8 named roads -> 2 + sweep.
3. Prompt backstops in `draft.md`/`review.md` (closure-no-invented-queue, length under/over, fuel one-headline, ban verbatim data-status echo). The prompt-only ones are unreliable (e.g. the data-echo ban was ignored) — kept as nudges, not relied on.

**Rationale:** Independent re-review confirmed the substantive in-scope traffic reads now air (Melbourne drive-time-led exemplar; Sydney busy/+weather/+weather+fuel clean, swept minor tails). The clear-road roll-call is structurally eliminated via the name cap.

**Consequences:** SCOPE CALL (grounded in ARN usage): we do NOT chase 8/8 across synthetic permutations. The remaining audit "failures" are not quality bugs to fix: (a) a no-traffic weather+fuel-only bulletin is a NON-SCENARIO — ARN runs traffic-first (content defaults to traffic-only; weather/fuel are opt-in and not Release-1); (b) a quiet-regional all-clear (Scottsdale) STRUCTURALLY underfills 30s and routes to the content-limited fallback chain BY DESIGN — its residual data-echo only matters if a fills-the-slot all-clear ever airs (recommended deterministic follow-up: suppress CorridorFormatter's "No significant traffic incidents to report." line when good-runs are present, since the prompt ban is ignored); (c) under/overrun timing is data-dependent and resolved by the production audio fill/compress + fallback, which the script-only eval does not model. Residual: the minor-corridor cluster still occasionally slips the bounce (refiner LLM variance) — the FormatGoodRuns-style upstream cap is the more reliable pattern where applicable. atn-reviewer agent prompt was never modified (kept unbiased; fresh spawn per round).

**Update 2026-06-29 (echo follow-up DONE):** the all-clear data-echo is fixed deterministically in `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.Summarize` — when there are no corridors/monitored routes BUT good-run roads exist, it now returns an EMPTY traffic block (the good-run section conveys the clear state), so the "No significant traffic incidents to report." status line is never handed to the writer to echo. The status line is kept only for a genuinely empty market (no good-runs → content-limited → fallback). Verified live: Scottsdale now reads "Upper Bird Road and Camden Hill Road are both flowing freely, and the rest of the run's clear." — no echo, two names + sweep (still ~7s underfill → fallback by design). 37 summarizer unit tests green; no regression.

## 2026-06-29 — Test environment built as a production mirror; pipeline env-parameterised to Test → Prod promotion; full RBAC (no fallback)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked to stand up the IBP Test environment as a faithful production mirror (private endpoints, ZRS, full RBAC) and to do everything possible on Arinco's side before requesting ARN provisioning. The CI/CD pipeline was prod-only (single `production` Deploy stage, single `arn-traffic-variables` group); dev/sandbox were stood up manually via `deploy.sh`.

**Decision:**
1. `main.test.bicepparam` finalised as a prod mirror: `Standard_ZRS`, 90-day blob soft-delete + 30-day PITR, private endpoints with `dataPlanePublicNetworkAccess='Disabled'`, retention/audit/log-retention params matching prod, and **full prod-style RBAC** — `devAuthFallbackRole` left empty (a non-empty value in test/prod bypasses RBAC). The ARN tenant is pinned (known); only the TEST app-registration client ID + the network IDs remain ARN-pending placeholders.
2. Pipeline refactored to an environment-parameterised **Test → Prod promotion**: a reusable stage template `deployment/pipelines/deploy-stage.yml` is instantiated as `Deploy_Test` (group `arn-traffic-test`, env `test`) then `Deploy_Prod` (group `arn-traffic-variables`, env `production`, `dependsOn: Deploy_Test`). The global variable-group binding moved into the stages.
3. Full RBAC for test/prod via a committed custom-Entra-provider SWA config (`deployment/static-web-app/staticwebapp.rbac.config.json`, tenant pinned) that the pipeline **overlays onto the test/prod SWA artifact only**; dev keeps the built-in provider (deployed via `deploy.sh`), so dev login is not broken.
4. Manual path retained: `deploy.sh ENVIRONMENT=test` (matches how dev was stood up).

**Rationale:** Test is meant to mirror prod and to be promoted into prod, so a single parameterised stage template + Test→Prod gating is the correct CI/CD topology, and full RBAC (no fallback) is what makes test a faithful prod rehearsal. Everything here is deployable on our side without ARN; the remaining inputs are foundation-only.

**Consequences:** Template + all four param files compile and bind clean (`az bicep build`/`build-params`, 2026-06-29); live `what-if` needs PIM-Owner activation (Reader cannot `whatIf`) and was not run. Both deploy stages are inert until ARN delivers the per-env service connection + variable group. The consolidated ARN ask is (subscription/access, TEST app-registration client ID, PE subnet + 5 DNS zone IDs, LAW/action-group/Teams/quota, the Infrastructure & Security SME security sign-off). `deployment/README.md` Pipeline Setup + open items updated; the `arn-traffic-test` group must be created in ADO with the documented variables; ADO environments `test` + `production` need approver gates.

## 2026-06-29 — Test deployed self-served as a private prod-mirror (createNetwork); two template fixes that also protect prod

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** the ARN Technology Lead confirmed (29 Jun) test/prod share the existing IBP subscription (`5e5f8695-…`), env-distinguished by naming — where we already hold PIM-eligible Owner. The directive was to do everything possible on our side before contacting ARN. The only thing Owner cannot provide is the Test AAD app registration (a Microsoft Entra object; a guest with no directory role cannot create one).

**Decision:** Stand up the full Test environment ourselves, deferring only the app registration.
1. New toggleable `deployment/modules/network.bicep` + `createNetwork` param in `main.bicep`: when true it builds a VNet (`10.61.0.0/24`) + Function-integration subnet + private-endpoint subnet + the 5 privatelink DNS zones (linked to the VNet), and feeds those IDs to the Function App + private endpoints. When false (prod default), `main.bicep` consumes ARN's hub-supplied subnet/DNS IDs. `main.test.bicepparam` sets `createNetwork=true`. This makes Test a real private prod-mirror without waiting on ARN's hub.
2. Deploy sequencing for an out-of-VNet operator: deploy with `dataPlanePublicNetworkAccess='Enabled'` (so KV secrets can be written + a queue E2E run), then flip storage/KV/AI to `Disabled` and confirm the VNet-integrated Function still reaches them over the private endpoints.
3. Deployed with a **throwaway AAD client ID** (auth fail-closed) — HTTP API + operator console stay locked until ARN delivers the real Test app registration; the queue/timer pipeline works regardless.

**Two template fixes found during the deploy (both also fix prod, which uses ZRS):**
- **Storage Archive tier is unsupported on ZRS/GZRS** (`FeatureNotSupportedForAccount`). `storage.bicep` now gates `tierToArchive` on `archiveTierSupported` (skips it for zone-redundant SKUs; keeps Cool, which ZRS supports). Dev/sandbox never hit this (they use LRS).
- **Cognitive Services private endpoint raced the account ETag** (`IfMatchPreconditionFailed`) when the PE attached while the AI account's diagnostics/role-assignments were still being written. `main.bicep` now serialises `privateEndpoints` after the role-assignment modules (`dependsOn`). Would otherwise recur on prod's first deploy.

**Rationale:** Owner on the shared sub makes the subscription/RG/network/identity-RBAC all self-serviceable; only the Entra app registration is genuinely ARN-owned. A self-built network island lets Test exercise the full private posture now; prod will use ARN's hub (`createNetwork=false`).

**Consequences:** Live env `IBP-AUE-TST-*` deployed + E2E-verified (queued bulletin → `broadcast_*.wav` 2.2 MB ~25s via HERE + Azure OpenAI MI + ElevenLabs); data plane Disabled, Function host Running over the PEs. SWA `https://polite-flower-0a5e0ce00.7.azurestaticapps.net`. Remaining ARN ask shrank to the Test app registration (+ confirm the `10.61.0.0/24` CIDR before any hub peering; optional central LAW/action-group/Teams; the Infrastructure & Security SME security sign-off gates prod). The self-built Test VNet is an isolated island — reconcile/peer with ARN's hub before relying on hub egress/DNS. Supersedes the foundation-blocker framing of the 2026-06-29 "Test environment built as a production mirror" entry.

## 2026-06-29 — Environments are parked for idle cost via plan scale-down + app stop (park.sh / resume.sh)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Non-prod environments (test especially) sit idle between demos/soaks but the App Service plan (PremiumV3 `P0v3`) bills 24/7 regardless of use — the dominant idle cost. We wanted a simple, reversible way to stop paying for idle compute across ALL environments without tearing them down.

**Decision:** Add `deployment/scripts/park.sh` + `resume.sh`, env-parameterised (`dev|test|prod|sbx`). **park** stops the Function App (halts the poller → no AI/HERE/ElevenLabs pay-per-use), scales the plan `P0v3`→`B1` (~85% off the compute), and disables the env's alert rules + availability test. **resume** scales back to `P0v3`, starts the app, and re-enables alerts. Basic plans don't allow deployment slots, so park first removes the staging slot (only used for blue-green deploys, not normal running; recreated by the next full deploy). Prod is guarded behind an explicit confirmation prompt.

**Rationale:** The plan is the only big always-on cost; scaling to Basic keeps the environment fully intact (SWA hostname, app registration wiring, network, storage all preserved) and reversible in ~1 min, which beats teardown/redeploy for environments used in intermittent bursts. Basic still supports VNet integration + Always On, so the private posture survives.

**Consequences:** Round-trip verified on Test (parked→B1 + app stopped + slot removed; resumed→P0v3 + Running/67 functions/health 200). Park is "minimise", NOT "$0": private endpoints (~$7/mo each), the Static Web App (Standard), Key Vault, storage and the B1 plan keep billing (~half the running cost). For near-zero idle cost, tear the env down (delete the 5 `IBP-AUE-{ENV}-RSG-*` groups) and redeploy — but recreating the SWA changes its hostname, which then needs the app-registration redirect URI re-pointed. A `--sku B1` park is reset to `P0v3` by a full `az deployment sub create` (the template pins the SKU), so park/resume are an operational lever, not IaC state. Documented in `deployment/README.md`.

## 2026-06-29 — ADO pipeline retargeted to Dev → Prod (test excluded); ADO repo brought up to the productionised code

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Azure DevOps repo `ARN-Traffic` (org `australian-radio-network`, project `Traffic POC`, default branch `master`) and its pipeline `ARN-Traffic-CI-CD` (id 108, YAML `/azure-pipelines.yml`) were still the Feb-2026 PoC: `master`'s tip was `05e23e2e3` (2026-02-23), the pipeline last ran on PoC code, the only variable group (`arn-traffic-variables`) carried the old PoC shape (`resourceGroupName`/`deployEnabled`), and only a `production` environment existed (with zero approval checks). None of the productionisation work had been pushed to ADO — the local `Arn` repo (unrelated history, root commit "Initial Arn productionisation baseline") pushed only to GitHub. The repo also carried two divergent pipeline files: the current root `azure-pipelines.yml` (Test → Prod) and a stale `.azuredevops/azure-pipelines.yml` (Dev/Prod, old `rg-arn-traffic-*` naming). ARN also directed that **Test is not a pipeline target** — it is a self-served prod-mirror, deployed manually via `deploy.sh`.

**Decision:**
1. Retarget the pipeline deploy path from **Test → Prod** to **Dev → Prod**. `azure-pipelines.yml` now instantiates `deploy-stage.yml` as `Deploy_Dev` (group `arn-traffic-dev`, env `dev`, `main.dev.bicepparam`) then `Deploy_Prod` (group `arn-traffic-variables`, env `production`, `dependsOn: Deploy_Dev`). Test has no pipeline stage.
2. Parameterise the stage template with `applyRbacConfig` (default true): prod overlays the custom-Entra-provider RBAC SWA config; **dev skips it** to keep the built-in provider + `devAuthFallbackRole`.
3. Triggers + deploy conditions widened to `master` **and** `main` (ADO default branch is `master`; local/GitHub uses `main`).
4. Delete the legacy `.azuredevops/azure-pipelines.yml` so `azure-pipelines.yml` is the single pipeline definition.
5. Bring ADO up to date (executed 2026-06-29): archived the PoC `master` tip `05e23e2e3` to `refs/heads/poc-archive/2026-02` (non-lossy), then cut `master` over to the productionised commit `73718f0e`; created the `dev` ADO environment (id 14) and the `arn-traffic-dev` variable group (id 28, ARN-pending placeholders + tenant pinned). CI now builds the real application instead of the Feb PoC.
6. Gate both deploy stages behind a compile-time `enableDeploy` parameter (default `false`): the deploy stages need ARN's per-env ARM service connection **and** ADO-admin authorisation of the `dev`/`production` environments + variable groups for the pipeline (an Arinco guest cannot self-grant pipeline permissions — `pipelinePermissions` returns 401). With `enableDeploy=false`, automatic CI runs compile to Build + Package only and stay green; deploys activate via a manual run with `enableDeploy=true` once ARN provisioning lands.

**Rationale:** ARN owns the Test environment lifecycle manually, so a Dev → Prod promotion is the correct pipeline topology — dev is the live deploy target, prod is gated behind it. The ADO repo had to be synced because the pipeline was building four-month-old PoC code; archiving the PoC tip keeps it recoverable.

**Consequences:** `master` now serves the productionised app + the new pipeline; the PoC is recoverable at `poc-archive/2026-02`. Automatic CI runs are green (Build incl. Bicep lint + Package). The deploy path is fully wired but dormant until: (a) ARN delivers per-env ARM **service connections** (the existing `arn-traffic-service-connection` is the PoC connection, the Arinco deploy operator is Reader-only), (b) an ADO admin **authorises** the `dev`/`production` environments + `arn-traffic-dev`/`arn-traffic-variables` groups for pipeline 108 and adds approver gates, and (c) `arn-traffic-variables` (prod) gets `aadClientId`/`aadTenantId` added. Then run with `enableDeploy=true`. ADO is reached with the ARN-native identity an ARN-native operations account (the Arinco guest is blocked by org policy `TF909091`). `deployment/README.md` CI/CD section + `docs/CODEMAPS/FILES.md` + CONTEXT updated.

## 2026-06-29 — CI/CD hardening: security scans, frontend gates, caching, build-once, post-deploy smoke

**Status:** accepted
