**Context:** With the ADO pipeline retargeted to Dev → Prod and CI green, the pipeline still lacked the standard quality/safety gates: no dependency or secret scanning, the frontend lint + unit tests were unwired (and broken — vitest mis-collected the Playwright `e2e/*.spec.ts`; `eslint .` had 3 errors), the Functions project was recompiled in a separate stage (not "build once"), there was no dependency caching, and deploys had no post-deploy verification.

**Decision:** Land the near-term hardening batch (all in Arinco's control, no ARN dependency):
1. **Security scans** (blocking): `dotnet list package --vulnerable` (fail on High/Critical), `npm audit --audit-level=high`, and a `gitleaks` secret-scan job with `.gitleaks.toml` allowlisting demonstrated non-secrets (vendored ElevenLabs SDK fixtures, generated doc indexes, public Entra app/tenant IDs, the well-known Azurite key, and gitignored local/build artifacts).
2. **Frontend gates**: wire `npm run lint` + vitest unit tests + `npm audit` into the Web job. Fixes to make them green: `vite.config.ts` vitest `exclude: e2e/**`; an eslint `e2e/**` override (Playwright `use()` ≠ React `use`); `lint` = `eslint .` (check) with `lint:fix` for the autofix; a prettier fix in `App.tsx`; and **pin the vitest TZ to `Australia/Sydney`** (`sameLocalDay` uses the runner's local TZ, so the `earlier-today` test passed on the Aussie workstation but failed on the UTC agent — the pin matches the Australian-operator browser context).
3. **Build once**: publish the tested Functions build with `--no-build` in the Build stage and ship it as the `functions` artifact; the deploy consumes it (no recompile).
4. **Caching**: NuGet + npm + Playwright `Cache@2`.
5. **Post-deploy smoke**: a `Smoke` job in `deploy-stage.yml` runs `deployment/scripts/smoke-test.sh` (`/api/health` + auth fail-closed) after the Function + SWA deploy.
6. **Failure notification + `batch: true`**: a `NotifyOnFailure` stage posts to `TEAMS_CICD_WEBHOOK` (no-op until the URL is supplied).

**Rationale:** These are the highest-leverage CI/CD improvements that need no ARN provisioning, and they catch real classes of regression (vulnerable deps, leaked secrets, broken frontend, TZ-dependent logic, dead-on-arrival deploys).

**Consequences:** Full pipeline verified green end-to-end (run `20260629.14`, 2026-06-29): all gates pass; `NotifyOnFailure` correctly skips on success and the smoke job is exercised only when `enableDeploy=true`. Remaining recommended (not in this batch): SAST (CodeQL/SonarCloud), Bicep PSRule/what-if-on-PR, branch-protection/build-validation policy on `master`, slot-swap + auto-rollback for prod, and supplying the Teams webhook + per-env service connections (ARN). `deployment/README.md` + `docs/canonical/production-readiness.md` updated; `.gitleaks.toml` added.

## 2026-06-29 — CI/CD performance: parallelise frontend with backend + trim critical-path work

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Measured the green run `20260629.14` via the ADO build timeline API: wall ≈ 19 min, and the critical path was almost fully serial — the `Package` (frontend) stage `dependsOn: Build` started the instant the backend job ended, despite having no backend dependency. Backend job 588s (Run tests 190s + backend E2E 216s dominant); frontend job 358s.

**Decision:** Land the agent-independent speed batch (highest ROI, no ARN dependency, no new agent cost):
1. **Parallelise** — `Package` stage set `dependsOn: []` so frontend runs concurrently with `Build` (artifacts are independent; `Deploy_Dev` now `dependsOn: [Build, Package]`).
2. **Coverage on PRs only** — `--collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"` (and the publish task) gated to `Build.Reason == PullRequest`; push runs skip the instrumentation cost.
3. **Cache `func`** — `azure-functions-core-tools` installed to a `Cache@2`-backed prefix instead of reinstalling every run.
4. **Playwright `--with-deps` on cache-miss only** — gated by the browser-cache `cacheHitVar`.
5. **.NET `--vulnerable` scan moved to its own parallel job** (off the backend critical path).

**Rationale:** The frontend↔backend serialization was ~6 min of dead wait; the rest were per-task costs sitting on the critical path. All are reversible and need no extra agents to help (the parallel-agent grant would compound them).

**Consequences:** Verified on run `20260630.1` (commit `572a4e1`): **wall ≈ 19 min → ~8.8 min** (~54% faster). Backend job 588→486s (coverage + scan removed); frontend 358→319s and now overlaps backend; Playwright install + coverage publish correctly `[skipped]`. **Finding: the org has ~2 parallel hosted agents** — the short aux jobs (DependencyScan/Bicep/gitleaks) now queue on the 2nd agent ahead of frontend, so frontend doesn't start until ~3 min in. The next high-leverage step is **raising the parallel-agent ceiling** (Microsoft-hosted grant), which would let frontend start at t=0 and drop the run toward the backend long pole (~8 min, less once the func cache is warm). Splitting backend unit-tests ‖ E2E is the subsequent lever. `azure-pipelines.yml` changed; `deployment/README.md` + `production-readiness.md` updated.

**Follow-up (2026-06-29, free/no-agent only — no parallel-agent grant, no ARN, no cost):** reused the job's Release build for the backend E2E **test project** (`e2e-backend.sh` runs `dotnet test -c Release --no-build` in CI, env-gated; local stays Debug) — backend E2E 216→181s locally 86→57s. Confirmed the func-tools cache now hits (`Install func` `[skipped]`). **Rejected after measuring:** (a) Playwright `workers: 2` — *slower* on the 2-vCPU agent (72s vs 53.6s at 1 worker; the vite dev server + 2 browsers oversubscribe 2 cores — which is why Playwright defaults to 1 worker under CI); reverted. (b) `func start --no-build` reusing the Release output — **broken** (`No job functions found`; func cannot index a foreign-config build), so the host build stays. **Conclusion: ~8.8 min is the 2-agent floor.** The backend is the bind and is now two unavoidable serial ~180s test phases (unit ‖ E2E) plus ~120s build/setup; splitting them needs a 3rd agent (Microsoft-hosted grant — out of scope per "no cost / self-serve only"). Verified green run `20260630.2` (commit `afcb7d9`).

## 2026-06-29 — A selected content source (weather/fuel) MUST appear in the bulletin; traffic flexes to make room

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A deployed Melbourne 30s bulletin (job `27199fa5326f49338ab39724e98bd380`) had weather selected (`ContentSelection.Weather=true`) and successfully fetched (drizzle, 14.5°C, 82% rain) — the data block was rendered into the draft prompt — yet the generated script contained ZERO weather. Root cause: both prompts framed weather/fuel as droppable garnish. The draft fill order was "incidents first, then the flowing roads, weather and fuel"; under a tight 91-word/30s slot with heavy traffic (a Calder Freeway closure + breakdown + 26 km queue and several more incidents), the writer filled the budget with traffic, and `review.md` point 11 (LENGTH) told it to "DROP the weakest items" with no protection for selected sources — so weather, a non-alert weave, was exactly what got cut, and the reviewer never checked that a selected source was present. User directive: "if we choose to include weather, it should include weather — same with fuel." This supersedes the 2026-06-28 "weather/fuel are opt-in / a no-traffic-only bulletin is a non-scenario" scope framing for the *selected-source* case, and refines the 2026-06-01 "exhaust traffic before weather and fuel" ordering: ordering is unchanged (traffic leads, weather woven after, fuel closes), but a selected+fetched source is now mandatory rather than droppable.

**Decision:** Prompt-only change (the template flags `weather`/`fuel`/`includesWeather`/`includesFuel` are already set ONLY when a source is both selected AND fetched, so a failed fetch stays fail-soft and is never mandated):
- `prompts/draft.md` — the target line now states that when a weather and/or fuel block is included, a short woven weather mention and/or the one fuel headline is REQUIRED and MUST appear, and the slot is made to fit by dropping the weakest TRAFFIC item, never by omitting weather/fuel. The non-alert weather branch and the fuel branch open with "was SELECTED … MUST appear — required content, not optional garnish".
- `prompts/review.md` — point 1 now flags NEEDS_REVISION if a selected source carries NO mention at all (weather: no weather mention; fuel: no fuel-price mention); point 11 (LENGTH) drops the weakest TRAFFIC items and explicitly KEEPS the required weather/fuel mentions. The review verdict's issues already flow into the refiner's `{{feedback}}`, so a missing-source verdict actively drives a fix.

**Rationale:** Verified by a deterministic regression replay (`test/corpus/regressions/melbourne-weather-omitted.json`, captured from the job above; data held constant, prompts the only variable). REPLAY on the new prompts: "…The M1 citybound and Bulleen Road outbound are only a couple of minutes back. **It's drizzly and 14, with a fresh north wind.**" — weather now woven in, temperature as the only number, no outlook/rain-%, all prior weather-style rules (2026-06-26 entries) preserved. The `mildura-flowlist` fixture (weather AND fuel) keeps both. `RegressionCorpus_Replay_RegeneratesAndScores` passes.

**Consequences:** When an operator turns weather/fuel on for a market, the bulletin now includes it (on a busy slot, a weak traffic item yields the room). This is a product tradeoff the operator opts into by selecting the source; on a genuinely tight slot, raising `TargetDurationSeconds` gives more room for both. Failed-fetch fail-soft is unchanged (no `weather`/`fuel` flag → not mandated). Prompt-bundled change: the deployed app must be redeployed (prompts load once at startup from `prompts/*.md`) for this to take effect live. No code/test changes; the live replay is the verification.

## 2026-06-30 — Same-day continuity day-window is local-tz, not UTC; manual triggers carry a timezone

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A deployed Melbourne 30s bulletin (job `bbc1684a67d545e694d0b6a2576e129e`) showed an "earlier today" bulletin in the UI but the script never referenced it — no "still", no continuation marker, and `GeneratorInputJson.IncidentChanges` was null. Ground truth: the prior Melbourne bulletin (`27199fa5…`) was created `2026-06-29T23:56:54Z` = `2026-06-30 09:56` Sydney; the new one ran `2026-06-30T00:08Z` = `10:08` Sydney — the SAME Sydney day. Two compounding bugs hid it. (A) `TableStorageJobRepository.GetLatestBulletinForMarketTodayAsync` received a local-day `DateTime today` but built the `CreatedAt` filter as `new DateTimeOffset(today.Y,M,D, 0,0,0, TimeSpan.Zero)` — i.e. UTC midnight of the local date. For an Australian market (UTC+10/+11) that window `[30T00:00Z, 1JulT00:00Z)` excludes any bulletin created in the local morning (previous UTC day) — the prior was missed by 12 minutes. Reproduced live: the buggy window returned only the current job; the correct Sydney window `[29T14:00Z, 30T14:00Z)` returned both. (B) Manual/ad-hoc triggers carry NO timezone — `ToBroadcastQueueMessage` never set `TimezoneId`, the job persists none, and ad-hoc market names ("Melbourne Drive Traffic") don't match any saved schedule. So the continuity `today` fell back to `nowUtc.Date` AND `IncidentStateService.ComputeAndPersistDeltaAsync` returned `None` (timezone failed to resolve) — explaining the null `IncidentChanges`. The scheduled path hit (A) too.

**Decision:**
- New `TimeZoneHelper.GetLocalDayWindowUtc(referenceUtc, timezoneId)` → the `[start, end)` UTC window for the LOCAL calendar day (unresolvable tz → UTC day). `BulletinFallbackService.GetLocalDayWindow` now delegates to it.
- `IJobRepository.GetLatestBulletinForMarketTodayAsync` takes `(market, station, DateTime dayStartUtc, DateTime dayEndUtc, ct)` — UTC window bounds, mirroring the sibling `GetLastSuccessfulJobForMarketAsync`. `TableStorage`/in-memory impls wrap the bounds with `TimeSpan.Zero` and filter directly.
- `BroadcastOrchestrator.EnrichRequestWithJobContext` resolves the effective timezone `request.TimezoneId.Or(job.TimezoneId)` and, when still none, falls back to `BroadcastOptions.DefaultTimezone` ("Australia/Sydney" — the documented "used when a job or schedule does not specify one" default, already used by `HereTrafficProvider`). It SETS that timezone on the enriched request (so the incident delta resolves too) and computes the continuity window via `GetLocalDayWindowUtc`.
- `SchedulePollerService.GetPreviousBroadcastContextAsync` computes the window from `schedule.Timezone` the same way.

**Rationale:** Both halves proven deterministically. `TimeZoneHelperTests.GetLocalDayWindowUtc_AustralianMorning_SpansPreviousUtcDay` asserts the exact scenario window `[29T14:00Z, 30T14:00Z)` and that the prior's `23:56:54Z` `CreatedAt` falls inside it. `InMemoryJobRepositoryTests.…AustralianMorning_FindsPriorFromPreviousUtcDay` proves the repo returns the prior under the local-day window and (regression-lock) returns None under the old UTC-midnight window. Setting `TimezoneId` on the enriched request also fixes the null incident delta for manual jobs (the delta path now runs against the real repo). Full suites green: 374 Application + 775 Infrastructure (22 integration skipped).

**Consequences:** Same-day continuity now works for Australian markets across the entire local day, for BOTH manual and scheduled triggers (previously broken roughly during the local-morning/UTC-evening window each day). Manual ad-hoc bulletins now also compute the incident delta (they were silently `None`), so "Changes since last bulletin" markers and Still-ongoing/Cleared callbacks apply to them. Ad-hoc generates for non-eastern markets without a schedule use the Sydney default (offset differs up to ~2.5h at the boundary for WA/SA) — acceptable for unscheduled one-offs; scheduled jobs use their real per-market timezone. Code change (not prompt-only): requires a backend redeploy to take effect on the deployed app.

## 2026-06-30 — Reject-to-fallback reuses the same-day bulletin (was always filler cart)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An E2E verification on dev found operator "reject to fallback" always aired the generic filler cart, never the most-recent approved same-day bulletin. Root cause: IJobRepository.GetLastSuccessfulJobForMarketAsync returned the single most-recent job whose status was in {WaitingApproval, Approved, Published, FallbackUsed} with audio. The job being reject-to-fallback'd is always a WaitingApproval-with-audio job and the newest, so the lookup returned that job itself; RejectToFallbackAsync's `candidate.JobId != job.JobId` guard then fell straight through to the filler cart without trying the next candidate. Reproduced twice on dev (gen-2 and gen-3) against an approved gen-1.

**Decision:** GetLastSuccessfulJobForMarketAsync now (a) drops WaitingApproval from the eligible status set (a bulletin awaiting approval has not aired and is never a valid fallback source), and (b) takes an excludeJobId parameter so it never returns the job a fallback is being found for. Both callers (JobService.RejectToFallbackAsync and BulletinFallbackService) pass the current job id.

**Rationale:** Fixes the bug at its source (the candidate query) rather than relying on a caller-side guard that only returns a single job and cannot advance to the next candidate. Dropping WaitingApproval also prevents re-airing unapproved content via fallback, a compliance concern since the approver identity is the publication-liability record. exclude-self lets the method return the next-best real bulletin for both the operator-reject and scheduled-poller paths.

**Consequences:** Operator reject-to-fallback now re-airs the most recent approved/published/previously-aired same-day bulletin when one exists, falling back to the filler cart only when none exists (no-dead-air guarantee preserved). Regression tests added (InMemoryJobRepositoryTests exclude-self/WaitingApproval; JobServiceTests reuse-success). Code change: requires a backend redeploy to take effect on the deployed app (the current dev build still has the bug). Verified locally: solution build green and 132 affected-class tests pass.

## 2026-06-30 — Script edit is a self-contained verbatim re-voice with a live slot-fit counter (decoupled from AI regenerate)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Operators editing a bulletin script in the review cockpit had no feedback on whether the edit would fit the slot, and a manual edit fed the AI **Regenerate** path (it became `PreviousScript` + a "preserve wording" hint in `JobService.RegenerateJobAsync`), so the model rewrote the operator's words instead of honouring them verbatim. The verbatim re-voice engine (`BroadcastOrchestrator.RevoiceExistingScriptAsync`, TTS-onwards, no LLM) and per-voice calibrated WPM already existed; the editor just wasn't wired to them, and the "Re-voice only" affordance lived as a secondary button in the Revise dialog (added 2026-06-24, "Wire targetDurationSec/editedIncidents/revoiceOnly").

**Decision:** Editing the script is now a standalone action. A new pure domain service `BulletinEditingBand.Compute(wpm, slot, speed, maxSlowDown, maxSpeedUp)` returns the `{target, min, max}` word band (target = exact-slot read via `WordTargetCalculator`; min = target ÷ `MaxSlowDownFactor`; max = target × `MaxSpeedUpFactor`). `JobsHttpTrigger.GetJob` enriches editable jobs (WaitingApproval/AudioReady with a script + voice) with a `BulletinEditingGuidanceDto` (`EditingGuidance` on `JobDetailDtoBase`), computed from the job's calibrated WPM (`IVoiceCalibrationService`, read-only; uncalibrated → `BroadcastOptions.WordsPerMinute`). The editor shows a live `words · ~est-seconds · slot-fit` counter (success in-band, warning short/long) and a primary **Re-voice · ~20s** action that routes the operator's exact text straight to the verbatim re-voice path (`revoice` in `use-bulletin-review`, always `revoiceOnly:true`, reject-then-regenerate on a waiting job). The edit→AI-regenerate path was removed entirely (clean cutover): `editedScript` no longer rides the AI `regenerate`, the deferred `scriptDraft`/`scriptEdited`/`canRevoiceOnly`/`'script'` change-chip machinery is gone, and the Revise dialog's "Re-voice only" button is removed. AI **Regenerate** stays for incident/feedback/curation changes. Supersedes the script-edit feeding of the 2026-06-24 re-voice decision; the `revoiceOnly`/`editedScript` wire contract is unchanged (now sent only by `revoice`).

**Rationale:** Editing words is an editorial act, not a regeneration request — the operator wants those exact words on air, sized to the slot. The band is computed backend-side from the live audio caps (`SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSlowDownFactor`/`MaxSpeedUpFactor`) so the UI carries no magic numbers and tracks any retune. Guidance is computed at read time (not persisted) so it is authoritative for every job, including pre-existing ones, at the cost of one cheap calibration table-read per editable-job GET. Verified: `BulletinEditingBandTests` (6, incl. 30s@165wpm → 82/75/94 under banker's rounding) + extended `schemas.test.ts` (editingGuidance parse/absence) green; full Domain (673) + Functions (182) backend suites green; frontend build + 428 vitest + the `jobs-review` E2E (live counter recolor short/fits/long, disabled-when-unchanged, verbatim re-voice commit, Revise dialog no longer offering "Re-voice only") all pass.

**Consequences:** New `Domain.Services.BulletinEditingBand` + `BulletinEditingGuidanceDto`; `JobsHttpTrigger` gains `IVoiceCalibrationService`/`IOptions<BroadcastOptions>`/`IOptions<SpeechDurationOptions>` deps. Front end: `editingGuidance` on the job detail (schema + `BulletinEditingGuidance` type), `revoice` on the review hook, counter + Re-voice action on `ReviewScript`, removal of the `'script'` change kind and the Revise "Re-voice only" button; the mock store computes a deterministic band on `GET /jobs/:id`. The advisory counter never blocks submission — an out-of-band edit can still be re-voiced (the audio pipeline routes an unfillable take to the fallback chain). Backend behaviour change: requires a redeploy to take effect on the deployed app.

## 2026-06-30 — Remove per-station GoodRunRoads; good-run eligibility is market PriorityRoad.FlowTier only

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** MarketSchedule.GoodRunRoads (a per-station, per-schedule flat road-name list edited in ScheduleStudio's Good-run roads step) duplicated what the market-scoped PriorityRoad already modelled: PriorityRoad carries an independent BoostIncidents flag and a FlowTier (None/Normal/High/Critical) per road, so a market operator could already choose per-road whether it boosts incidents, competes as a good run, or both, at four strengths. GoodRunRoads had none of that — no tier, no market sharing across co-located stations, and it silently degraded to FlowTier.Normal inside BroadcastOrchestrator.MarkWeightedFlowRoads. The 2026-06-18 decision ('Market priority roads live in the Bulletin-rules hub, not the schedule wizard') kept the two split by scope, reasoning good-runs were genuinely per-schedule; that reasoning did not hold once multi-station bulletin sharing confirmed markets default to ONE shared body across co-located stations, so a per-station good-run list could only ever diverge from its market's shared priority-road list by operator inconsistency, not genuine need.

**Decision:** Delete MarketSchedule.GoodRunRoads and BroadcastContext/GeneratorInputSnapshot.ConfiguredGoodRunRoads entirely (domain model, commands, DTOs, mappings, ScheduleHttpTrigger, table storage column, and the ScheduleStudio 'Good-run roads' step + PriorityRoadsSection component). BroadcastOrchestrator.BuildFlowPoolAsync/MarkWeightedFlowRoads now derive good-run weighting solely from the market's PriorityRoad list (FlowTier != None), with no separate station input. PriorityRoadsManager (Bulletin rules -> Priority roads) is the single road-configuration surface: each road independently toggles 'When blocked' (BoostIncidents) and 'When clear' (FlowTier Off/Normal/High/Critical, product-facing term 'good run' rather than the internal 'flow tier' label). ScheduleStudio's Content step now links to that tab instead of hosting a duplicate editor.

**Rationale:** One road-configuration surface removes an inconsistency trap (a road weighted at the market level but not on a station's own list, or vice versa) without losing any capability — PriorityRoad.FlowTier is strictly more expressive than a flat list (it already has 4 strength levels plus an independent incident-boost axis). Market scope matches the shared-body product direction; station-level config for a market-shared concept was extra editing surface with no product need behind it.

**Consequences:** Operators configure a road's incident-boost and good-run behaviour together in one place. ScheduleStudio loses a step (Good-run roads); a market with no priority roads configured airs no good-runs (previously a station list alone could enable them at Normal tier with no market entry -- migration-affected markets should add the road as a priority road with the desired FlowTier). Verified: backend build clean, Application/Domain/Infrastructure test suites green (372/673/840 incl. skips), E2E project compiles; frontend tsc/eslint clean, vitest 426 pass (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in use-current-user.test.ts). Table storage GoodRunRoadsJson column is now write-orphaned on old rows (harmless, ignored on read).

## 2026-07-01 — Per-route Admin/Operator gate now defers to backend RBAC when SWA carries no custom role

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `bda5657` (2026-06-30) fixed the outer "no app access at all" gate (`hasAppAccess`) to pass through when SWA forwards only its `anonymous`/`authenticated` pseudo-roles — but a user then hit "Admin access required" on `/stations`, `/voices`, `/delivery`, `/pronunciation`, `/operators`. Root cause: `ProtectedRoute`'s per-route gate calls `useIsAdmin`/`useIsOperator`, which still checked only for the literal `Admin`/`Operator` role strings. Dev's built-in SWA provider never forwards those (only the backend's `Auth__DevFallbackRole = Admin` grants access, per-request, API-side); a real admin-assigned dev user was therefore blocked from every admin page by the frontend despite the backend authorising every call. Same failure mode for any test/prod caller signed in via the custom Entra provider before their Entra group membership/app-role assignment lands. The `bda5657` fix was also shipped with a stale unit test asserting the old (pre-fix) `hasAppAccess([])` semantics, masking the gap (`use-current-user.test.ts` had 2 failing tests at HEAD).

**Decision:** Extract the "authenticated but no custom role source" check (`isAuthenticatedWithoutCustomRoles`: requires the `authenticated` pseudo-role present AND every role in the SWA pseudo-role set) and apply it uniformly: `useIsAdmin`/`useIsOperator` return true when the caller has the explicit role OR is authenticated-without-custom-roles, not just `hasAppAccess`. Fixed `hasAppAccess([])` to correctly return `false` (no `authenticated` pseudo-role at all = truly signed out / failed `/.auth/me`, distinct from "signed in, no custom role").

**Rationale:** Same principle as `bda5657`, applied consistently: when SWA cannot see Operator/Admin at all, the frontend has no basis to gate on them, and every backend endpoint already enforces `AuthorizationMiddleware`'s `RouteRoleMatrix` regardless of what the frontend shows. Gating client-side navigation on a role SWA never forwards only produces a false "Admin access required" placeholder in front of an API that would have said yes (dev) or a true 403 the user should see directly rather than a misleading role-name-specific message (unassigned test/prod caller). Fixing only the outer gate and leaving the per-route gate stale was an incomplete application of the same decision.

**Consequences:** Dev: any authenticated user now reaches every route (nav, command palette, direct URLs) and sees admin-only actions/buttons; the backend's per-endpoint RBAC (`Auth__DevFallbackRole=Admin` in dev) remains the actual authority, so behavior is unchanged for API calls, only the frontend stops pre-blocking. Test/prod with the custom Entra provider: a signed-in user with no Operator/Admin app-role assignment yet now also sees the full UI and gets real 403s from the API instead of a client-side "access required" screen — acceptable per the `bda5657` precedent (backend is sole authority) but worth flagging to ARN if they want unassigned users kept out of admin-page UI entirely (would need a real "no role" signal distinct from "role not visible", which SWA does not provide today). Rewrote `use-current-user.test.ts` to cover both the pass-through and true-deny (`hasAppAccess([])`, `['anonymous']`) cases. Verified: frontend `tsc -b` clean, eslint clean, full vitest suite 441 passed / 3 skipped (was 2 failing at HEAD). Frontend-only change: takes effect on next SWA redeploy.

## 2026-07-01 — Bulletin tone reverses to factual/objective; supersedes the 22–26 Jun casual-presenter build

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Between 2026-06-22 and 2026-06-26 the prompt stack (`system.md`, `draft.md`, `review.md`) was deliberately built toward a casual, Aussie-mate presenter voice — slang ("backed up", "crawling", "copping it"), rotating conversational connectors, and woven weather asides ("rug up, it's a cold one"). Fresh feedback from separate conversations with additional ARN staff (2026-07-01, captured in, BFN-001) took the opposite position: since the platform is openly AI-generated, performing human-ness (breath tags, formulaic "naturalness", conversational filler, editorial asides like "it's gonna be a wet one") is what currently reads as synthetic, not less. Concrete examples cited: vague/interpretive language ("knocking around", "in a bit of strife") standing in for a stated fact; redundant phrasing ("shut at the ramp to the Pacific Motorway" restating what "ramp" already implies); the same anchor named twice in one item under different wording.

**Decision:** Reverse direction. Bulletins move to a factual, objective read: state what happened, don't react to it. Phrasing VARIETY is retained — vary the sentence structure and how each fact is introduced, restructuring rather than swapping a synonym — but editorializing, jokes, subjective commentary, vague colloquialisms, and unnecessary asides are cut. This supersedes the STYLE DEFAULTS built in the 2026-06-22 ("weather woven in...") and 2026-06-26 ("weather woven in with a connecting intro...") entries; the underlying anti-fabrication BOUNDARIES and slot-fill mechanics from that period are untouched. Concrete rules riding alongside this reversal: drop a connecting-road clause when a structural term (ramp, on-ramp, interchange) already implies it and no other detail justifies naming the second road; never repeat the same named anchor twice in one item; combine related facts about one item into a single connected clause rather than two bolted-on statements; round a voiced distance/extent to the nearest 5 km, not the nearest 1.

**Rationale:** The casual-presenter direction was validated by ARN content staff at the time, but a second round of ARN feedback found the performed "naturalness" — rotating slang, woven asides, breath-like delivery tags — reads as more synthetic than a plain factual read, not less. Cutting the performance layer while keeping genuine phrasing variety (never repeating a sentence shape) preserves the "doesn't sound like a machine reading data" goal from a different angle: variety in STRUCTURE rather than variety in COLOUR.

**Consequences:** `prompts/system.md`, `prompts/draft.md`, and `prompts/review.md` need a coordinated rewrite (tracked as a single task — splitting it risks an inconsistent mid-rewrite prompt state, since the new rules interact with each other). `DeliveryStylePolicy.OperatorDirected`'s `[sighs]`/`[exhales]` tags are removed as part of the same rationale. The whole batch must be re-verified live via the `arn-live-here-eval` process before deploy — a reversal this size risks regressing the June work's slot-fill and no-fabrication gains if shipped unverified.

**Verification (2026-07-01):** Full BFN-001–015 batch implemented (system/draft/review prompt rewrite, filler-statement library, fill-order field, rounding, breath-tag removal, audio download, fuel-suburb attachment). Build clean; touched suites green (Domain 665, Application 372, Functions 196, Infrastructure 738 excl. one pre-existing unrelated `HereGeoFilter` failure from concurrent uncommitted work elsewhere in the tree — confirmed not caused by this batch). `arn-live-here-eval --full-pipeline --live-here --review` run against live HERE data across sydney/melbourne/goldcoast: fabrication/style/safety all `ok`, target-shape 96–100%. Judged review pack confirms no tone-reversal regression and both the ramp-redundancy rule (BFN-005) and duplicate-anchor rule (BFN-006) hold correctly on live data, cross-checked against real ATN samples (`atn-bulletin-style-samples.md` lines 1311, 1545 — ATN itself names the sole connecting-road anchor after "shut at", confirming the rule is calibrated correctly, not overcorrected). Two pre-existing gaps surfaced (not BFN-* regressions, logged as follow-up): draft.md's sentence-variety enforcement can still repeat "[Road] is [state]" shape under 5+ items; the "brief aside at most" instruction for a running-to-time monitored route can be satisfied by full omission rather than a brief mention. Cleared for deploy.

## 2026-07-01 — Per-voice Delivery Pace Boost — additive WPM control, separate from ElevenLabs Speed

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN voice engineering reported ElevenLabs' native Speed parameter tops out at ~1.2x, is ignored entirely by eleven_v3 voices, and doesn't help reach faster-sounding delivery for hosts who need a punchier drive-time pace. The existing pipeline already GROWS the script via BroadcastOptions.WordTargetOvershoot (global, 1.10 in dev) then compresses via post-synthesis time-stretch up to SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSpeedUpFactor (1.15, 1.10 in dev) -- but that headroom is already fully consumed by the overshoot tuning, and the lever is global, not per-voice.

**Decision:** Added VoiceProfileVersion.PaceBoostWpm (0-40, default 0/no-op), an additive WPM boost over a voice's calibrated speaking rate, applied ONLY to pre-synthesis script sizing (WordTargetCalculator.ComputeWordTargetFromWordsPerMinute gained a paceBoostWpm param) -- never sent to ElevenLabs, so it works identically on v2 and v3. When a voice's boost needs more compression headroom than the configured MaxSpeedUpFactor, a new WordTargetCalculator.ComputeEffectiveMaxSpeedUpFactor widens the PER-REQUEST cap (never the global config) up to a new SpeechDurationOptions.AbsolutePaceBoostSpeedUpCeiling (default 1.35) -- BroadcastOrchestrator computes this and threads it through a new maxSpeedUpFactorOverride param on IAudioPipelineService.SynthesizeWithDurationTargetAsync/FineTuneToTargetDuration, defaulting to null (unboosted voices are byte-identical to pre-feature). BulletinEditingBand.Compute and the Voice workshop's Preview endpoint apply the same math so operator edit-guidance and audition previews stay consistent with production. Editable per voice version in the workshop (new distinct 'Delivery Pace' slider, separate from the ElevenLabs Speed slider) with live compression-ratio feedback; versioned like every other voice setting (a pace-only edit still mints a version); RestoreVersion correctly carries the restored version's boost forward.

**Rationale:** WPM-additive (not a multiplicative overshoot override) matches how radio people actually think about pace (+N wpm) and scales evenly across slow/fast voices. Keeping it off VoiceSettings and out of the ElevenLabs wire payload means it works on every model uniformly, including v3, and never gets bucketed/rejected by the provider's own speed range. A per-request cap override (not a global MaxSpeedUpFactor bump) means voices with no boost configured see zero behavioural change -- verified via full backend + frontend test suites green before and after.

**Consequences:** New: VoiceProfile.MaxPaceBoostWpm=40 constant + domain validation (ErrorMessages.VoiceProfile.PaceBoostWpmOutOfRange); VoiceProfile.ApplyEdit signature changed bool -> Result<bool> (validates the boost range; two call sites + tests updated). BroadcastContextBase/BroadcastQueueMessage/JobVoiceConfig/ResolvedVoice all carry PaceBoostWpm end-to-end from VoiceProfile through the poller to the orchestrator. SpeechDurationOptions moved namespace Infrastructure.Configuration -> Domain.Configuration (Application needs it, Application does not reference Infrastructure) -- config section name/keys unchanged. Web: VoiceProfileFormSchema gained paceBoostWpm (0-40 validated); new DeliveryPaceControl.tsx component; VoiceVariantCard/VoiceVersionHistory surface the boost; mock store mirrors the same compression math. Verified: dotnet build clean, all 4 backend test projects green (2073 tests, 0 failures), web tsc+eslint clean, vitest 445 passed. Default MaxSpeedUpFactor/WordTargetOvershoot config UNCHANGED -- feature is fully opt-in per voice, zero risk to existing bulletins. Not yet audition-tested by ARN for the actual on-air sound quality at high boost values -- recommend a voice-audition.py-style A/B before setting PaceBoostWpm > ~15-20 on a production voice.

## 2026-07-01 — Deterministic style gates hardened: DuplicateAnchorDetector added, review-refine loop always re-verifies

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A 10-script scenario-matrix sample (generated same day as the BFN-001 tone-reversal verification) surfaced concrete regressions despite that morning's clean live-eval pass: BFN-006 (duplicate anchor) reappeared on 2 of 10 scripts (Gold Coast "Pacific Motorway" named 3x; Perth "Kwinana Freeway" repeated in one sentence), and a 6-road roll-call shipped on a Sydney-CBD script despite `RollCallDetector` existing. Root cause traced to `BroadcastOrchestrator.ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync`: with `MaxReviewRefineRetries=1`, the loop reviews once, refines once if needed, then returns the refined script WITHOUT re-checking it against either detector — a refine triggered by a failing gate was never verified to have actually cleared that gate before shipping. Separately, ARN provided strikethrough markup on the generated Perth script (BFN-017–022): prefer "closed" over "is shut"; vary sentence shape across consecutive closures (elliptical/comma-joined, not three parallel "[Road] is closed at [Location]" sentences); cut trailing incident-type restatement ("...for upgrades, including closure and construction"); collapse a repeated corridor name within one sentence (independent corroboration of BFN-006); vary the good-run sweep between naming roads and naming suburbs/areas; translate HERE's raw weather vocabulary ("Sprinkles", "Broken clouds") to natural phrasing instead of passing it through verbatim.

**Decision:** (1) Added `DuplicateAnchorDetector` (Domain/Services), mirroring `RollCallDetector`'s code-level-gate pattern: flags any known road/monitored-route name mentioned 2+ times in one sentence, with longest-match-first masking so two genuinely distinct roads sharing a name prefix (e.g. "Smith Street" vs "Smith Street Motorway") are never conflated. (2) Restructured the review-refine loop (`BroadcastOrchestrator` + the eval harness's mirrored `BulletinEval.ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync`) to check BOTH `RollCallDetector` and `DuplicateAnchorDetector` every iteration, and added a final deterministic re-check (no LLM call) after the loop exits — if either gate still fails, the script ships anyway (a defect here is a quality gap, not a hard failure) but is logged as a warning so it's visible in telemetry rather than silently shipped clean. (3) Bumped `MaxReviewRefineRetries` default 1 → 2 (well within the existing `MaxReviewRefineRetriesCeiling=3`) so a gate-triggered refine gets at least one re-verification pass before the budget exhausts. (4) Added a HERE-condition-vocabulary translation table to `ContentFormatters.FormatWeather` (`NaturalWeatherPhrasing`) covering aviation/METAR-style tokens ("Sprinkles"→"a chance of a shower", "Broken clouds"→"patchy cloud", etc.), falling through unchanged for tokens already natural English. (5) `prompts/draft.md`: added rules for closure-list sentence-shape variety, banning trailing incident-type restatement, and varying the good-run sweep between roads and suburbs/areas.

**Rationale:** BFN-006 regressing on fresh data the same day it verified clean proved a soft prompt instruction alone is not reliable under model sampling variance — it needs the same code-level-gate treatment `RollCallDetector` already uses for roll-calls. The loop restructure closes the actual mechanism that let a triggered-but-unresolved gate ship: with retries=1 there was structurally no way for a refine to be checked. ARN's concrete before/after markup gave unambiguous ground truth for the closure-variety and weather-vocabulary rules, cheaper and more reliable than inferring style from prose feedback alone.

**Consequences:** New file `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Services/DuplicateAnchorDetector.cs` + `test/.../DuplicateAnchorDetectorTests.cs`. `BroadcastOrchestrator.ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync` and `BulletinEval.ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync` must be kept in sync (the eval harness deliberately mirrors production so the two paths can't drift — a lesson already recorded in `BulletinEval.cs`'s own doc comments). `MaxReviewRefineRetries=2` in both `BroadcastOptions` default and `appsettings.json` adds up to one extra reviewer+refiner LLM round-trip on the minority of scripts that trip a gate — acceptable latency/cost for the reliability gain. Verified: full backend suites green (Domain 710, Application 375, Functions 196, Infrastructure 826 excl. 29 skipped live-only), frontend `tsc -b` clean, and a fresh `arn-live-here-eval --full-pipeline --live-here --review` pass across sydney/melbourne/goldcoast shows the exact previously-regressed pattern (Gold Coast Pacific Motorway) now correctly collapsed to "the motorway" on second mention, plus closure-verb variety ("is shut" → "is also closed") — judged review pack:. WALK3-002 (ambiguous-road/suburb disambiguation, from the same-day app-walkthrough feedback) is tracked as a separate follow-on feature, not part of this hardening pass.

## 2026-07-01 — Ambiguous-road/suburb disambiguation shipped as a per-market editable list (WALK3-002)

**Status:** superseded

**Context:** During the 1 Jul app walkthrough, the Gold Coast operator, the ARN content lead, and the ARN voice consult flagged generated bulletins naming roads with no suburb context that a listener can't place — either a genuine name duplicate within a market (e.g. "Marine Parade" exists in both Southport and Miami on the Gold Coast) or a road HERE tags as a major road despite being a locally-known side street (e.g. "Riviera Road"). The existing `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` suburb-append logic is unconditional and passive (`" near {suburb}"` appended whenever `corridor.Suburb` has a value) — it doesn't force the LLM to voice it, and doesn't exist at all for corridors HERE doesn't attach a suburb to.

**Decision:** Added a new per-market editable list, `AmbiguousRoad(Name, Reason?, Enabled)`, mirroring the existing `FillerStatement`/`PriorityRoad` architectural pattern exactly (Domain record → `IAmbiguousRoadsRepository` → `TableStorageAmbiguousRoadsRepository` → `AmbiguousRoadsHttpTrigger` with GET/PUT `markets/{market}/ambiguous-roads` + GET `ambiguous-roads/inventory`, caps 100 roads/80 chars/200-char reason). Threaded live into the generation pipeline via the same parallel-fetch pattern as weather/fuel/guidance (`BroadcastOrchestrator.GetAmbiguousRoadsSafeAsync` → `BroadcastContextBase.AmbiguousRoadNames`). `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` gates on this list: when a corridor's `RoadName` case-insensitively matches an entry, it appends a `[MUST NAME SUBURB]` flag token to that corridor's data bullet (parallel to the existing `[NEW]` flag), and `draft.md` tells the writer that flag makes voicing the suburb a hard requirement — not the general, optional suburb guidance elsewhere in the same prompt. Frontend: a new "Ambiguous roads" tab in the Guidance page's bulletin-rules hub (`AmbiguousRoadsManager.tsx`, mirroring `FillerStatementsManager.tsx`), per-market add/edit/remove rows (road name, optional reason, enabled toggle).

**Rationale:** This is a human-curated list only in this pass — no automated G-NAF/HERE-geocoding duplicate detection wiring (that was investigated and costed in as a ~1-day follow-on, not silently folded into this pass). Gating the LLM's existing suburb-append mechanism with an explicit hard-requirement flag (rather than building a second, separate suburb-injection mechanism) satisfies the ARN content lead's requirement that the suburb lands in the actual script text, and reuses the proven code-level-gate pattern (`RollCallDetector`, `DuplicateAnchorDetector`) for anything that must not depend on the model reliably following a soft instruction.

**Consequences:** New files: `AmbiguousRoad.cs`, `IAmbiguousRoadsRepository.cs`, `TableStorageAmbiguousRoadsRepository.cs`, `AmbiguousRoadsHttpTrigger.cs`, DTOs in `OperatorContracts.cs`, `ambiguous-roads-hooks.ts`, `AmbiguousRoadsManager.tsx`. Modified: `DependencyInjection.cs` (DI registration), `BroadcastContext.cs`/`BroadcastOrchestrator.cs` (pipeline threading), `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.cs` (gate), `prompts/draft.md` (one new guideline sentence), `paths.ts`/`GuidancePage.tsx` (frontend wiring). Verified: full backend suites green (Domain 710, Application 375 incl. 3 new AmbiguousRoad-aware orchestrator tests, Functions 207 incl. 11 new trigger tests, Infrastructure 865 incl. 10 new repo/summarizer tests), frontend `tsc -b`/`eslint`/`vitest` all clean (450 tests passing). Operators must populate this list per market before it has any effect — an empty list (the default for every market today) is a pure no-op, so this ships with zero behavioural change until curated; curation is an ARN content-team follow-up, not part of this engineering task. Automated detection (G-NAF bulk query, HERE geocoding validation) remains an explicit, uncommitted follow-on.

## 2026-07-01 — Coverage-area drawing raised to 5 degrees per side; HERE queries auto-tile past 1 degree, surfaced in the map UI

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Editing a station's Coverage Area with the "Area" (custom polygon) draw tool hard-rejected any shape whose bounding box exceeded 1 degree per side ("Too large. HERE caps the area at ~111 km per side"), surfaced live on Magic FM 89.9 (Port Lincoln): an 11-point ~16,700 km² Eyre Peninsula polygon, a legitimate regional broadcast footprint, couldn't be saved. Root cause: HERE Traffic API v7 genuinely caps a single `bbox`/enclosing-polygon-box query at 1 degree per side and a `circle` filter at 50 km radius (confirmed against `docs.here.com/traffic-api/docs/geospatial-filters-here-traffic-api-v7-concepts`, and independently against the third-party `hereR` R package which documents the identical 1° constraint) — `CoverageArea.CreateBoundingBox`/`CreatePolygon` and the frontend Zod schema enforced that HERE per-request limit directly as the drawable limit, with no tiling to absorb larger shapes and no UI signal that tiling was even a concept.

**Decision:** Split "HERE's per-request tile size" from "what an operator can draw." `CoverageArea.MaxBoundingBoxDegrees` (1°) now documents the per-tile HERE limit only; a new `CoverageArea.MaxShapeSpanDegrees` (5°, mirrored in the frontend as `MAX_SHAPE_SPAN_DEGREES`) is the outer sanity cap `CreateBoundingBox`/`CreatePolygon` validate against. `HereGeoFilter.BuildTiles(area)` splits any bbox/polygon shape over 1° into a grid of ≤1° `bbox:` tiles (circles/corridors always return a single tile — both already fit HERE's limits). `HereTrafficProvider` fans out incidents and flow fetches across every tile in parallel, merges results, and de-duplicates (incidents by id; flow segments, which carry no id, by `(description, length, speed)`). A tile failure degrades to the tiles that succeeded (logged) rather than failing the whole fetch. **New this pass:** the map's live status pill now has four tiers instead of three — `default` (fits one HERE query), a new `info` tier (1°–4° span: shows the box/area metric plus "Exceeds HERE's ~111 km single-query limit — fetched as N separate HERE requests", using the existing `info` design-system token), `warning` (4°–5°: same tiling note plus "Approaching the max size"), and `destructive` only past the 5° hard cap. `tileGridSize`/`polygonTileGridSize` helpers (mirroring the backend's tile-grid math exactly) compute the request count shown to the operator. The bbox editor's drag handles and validation schemas were raised to the 5° cap to match.

**Rationale:** An operator drawing a large regional market should see the real consequence (extra HERE requests, hence extra cost/latency) *before* saving, not discover it as an opaque behavior change. Reusing `info`/`warning`/`destructive` from the existing design system (already used for badges elsewhere) keeps the tiering visually consistent rather than introducing new ad-hoc colors. 5° per side bounds the worst case at a 5×5 = 25-tile grid per HERE call type — comfortably covers any realistic AU regional broadcast licence area without letting an operator mistake fan out to hundreds of calls.

**Consequences:** Circle and corridor coverage are unaffected (already single-tile, no pill change). Bbox/polygon markets over 1° per side now issue N parallel HERE requests per fetch (incidents, free-flowing-roads, corridor-flow-enrichment) instead of one — a real, now visibly-flagged cost/latency increase for large markets, bounded by the 5° cap. Stored coverage areas between 1° and 5° per side that previously failed validation are now valid. No API/DTO shape change. Verified: backend build clean, full non-integration suite green (Domain 711, Application 375, Functions 207, Infrastructure 866/888 incl. skips) including `HereGeoFilterTests.BuildTiles_*` tile-grid tests, `CoveragePolygon_RegionalPeninsulaMarket_AcceptedAndTiled` reproducing the exact Port Lincoln shape, and `GetIncidentsAsync_LargePolygonSpanningMultipleTiles_DedupesAcrossTiles`; frontend `tsc -b`/`eslint`/production build clean, vitest 459 pass including new `tileGridSize`/`polygonTileGridSize` coverage.

## 2026-07-01 — Local Lighthouse performance-regression gate for the web frontend

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** No automated performance testing existed for the web UI beyond bundle-size chunk warnings at build time. A user report of deployed-dev slowness needed a way to separate app-level regressions (bundle bloat, client-side fan-out, over-polling) from infrastructure/network issues, and CI had no gate against reintroducing a class of bug already fixed once (the 2026-06-23 /guidance 28-call fan-out).

**Decision:** Added web/scripts/perf-audit.mjs: Lighthouse (performance category, desktop profile) against a production build (vite build --outDir dist-mock, VITE_USE_MOCKS=true) served via vite preview, across 7 representative routes. Budget-gated on Google's Core Web Vitals 'poor' thresholds (score >=50, LCP <=4000ms, TBT <=600ms, CLS <=0.25, weight <=3MB); breach exits 1. Wired into azure-pipelines.yml (Package/Web job, after Playwright E2E, before build) with the report always published as an artifact. npm scripts: npm run perf (build+audit+gate), npm run perf:nobuild, npm run perf -- --no-fail.

**Rationale:** A production build in mock mode isolates app/bundle cost from backend/network variance (mock data renders real content offline, no auth wall, byte-stable) while still exercising the real optimized bundle (vite dev serves unbundled ESM and would give meaningless numbers). Reusing the existing ux-audit.mjs route/target conventions keeps the two harnesses (a11y/UX vs performance) consistent. Desktop throttling profile (not Lighthouse's mobile default) matches actual usage: operators run this on workstation hardware, not mobile.

**Consequences:** New devDependencies: lighthouse, chrome-launcher. New npm scripts: build:mock, perf, perf:nobuild. web/dist-mock/ and web/perf/ added to .gitignore. CI wall time +~45s (Package/Web job). This harness cannot detect infrastructure/CDN/network issues (see the companion 2026-07-01 finding on SWA regional routing) — it only measures the app's own render/bundle cost. Documented in docs/operations/performance-testing.md.

## 2026-07-01 — Dev SWA is not served from a nearby CDN edge — Standard tier has no edge distribution without a custom domain

**Status:** superseded — resolved by "2026-07-17 — SWA custom domains + enterprise-grade edge (Option A) for all three environments" (option 1 chosen)

**Context:** A user report of deployed-dev UI slowness was investigated via curl/DNS/geolocation tracing (from Melbourne). DNS for brave-desert-09eeae900.7.azurestaticapps.net resolves through azurestaticapps7.trafficmanager.net to an Amsterdam (am2) App Service stamp (132.220.38.112, AS8075 Microsoft, geolocated Amsterdam NL) — NOT East Asia, though az staticwebapp show reports location=East Asia matching deployment/main.bicep's swaLocation param. Static asset requests measured 1.0-3.3s each (TLS handshake alone 0.5-0.9s) from Melbourne, versus <0.4s for the Australia East-hosted Function App backend and <0.4s for control CDN endpoints (Google, Cloudflare) on the same network path. Static Web Apps Standard tier without a custom domain has no CDN edge distribution (Microsoft Learn: enterprise-grade edge, the Azure Front Door integration that provides 118+ edge locations, requires a custom domain with TTL <48h configured first) -- it serves from a single origin via internal Traffic Manager routing that does not necessarily match the region shown in az/portal output.

**Decision:** Not yet decided — recorded as a finding pending a fix decision. Candidate options: (1) enable enterprise-grade edge (~USD 17.52/app/month) once a custom domain is configured -- needs ARN-owned DNS; (2) manually front the SWA's default hostname with Azure Front Door Standard (~USD 35/month + traffic) -- more control (WAF, routing), needs staticwebapp.config.json networking/forwardingGateway changes to lock traffic to Front Door only, does not strictly require a custom domain; (3) move the frontend off SWA to App Service or Storage static hosting in australiaeast behind Front Door/CDN -- largest change.

**Rationale:** This directly affects every Australian user's page-load latency on dev (and will affect test/prod on the same SWA Standard configuration) and was previously undiagnosed -- CONTEXT.md/decisions.md attributed SWA's East Asia region choice to '~100ms latency, closest SWA region to Australia' (ID-03 in the project decision register), which is the region-to-region distance but does not account for Standard tier's lack of edge caching without enterprise-grade edge. The custom-domain prerequisite for the cheapest fix (enterprise-grade edge) is an external dependency on ARN, mirroring the pattern already blocking the Test AAD app registration.

**Consequences:** Needs a decision + ARN coordination (custom domain + DNS) before a fix can ship; not actionable unilaterally. Verification procedure for any fix: re-run the DNS-resolution + IP-geolocation check documented in docs/operations/performance-testing.md and confirm the resolved App Service stamp is in-region (not am2/Amsterdam). Test and Prod environments use the same swaLocation=eastasia parameter (main.test.bicepparam, main.prod.bicepparam) and are very likely to have the identical issue -- worth checking before Test/Prod go live for real users.

## 2026-07-01 — Roll-Call Rule B Needs Connected-Prose Guard and a Mechanical Repair Fallback

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-11 scenario matrix showed two separate defects in RollCallDetector Rule B (3+ known roads in one sentence): (1) false positive — a genuinely well-written sentence where every road carries its own verb/clause ("X has minor delays, Y is congested at Z, and W is slow") was never actually flagged by the shipped code, but the rule's original design intent conflated any 3-name sentence with a bare list, risking future false positives without a precision guard; verified via a direct C# unit test against the exact live sentence. (2) true positive with no fix — Sydney pass-11 shipped "Smithfield Road is at a standstill, while Joyce Drive, Domestic Terminal and Liverpool Road are slow" (4 roads, 3 sharing one trailing verb) because the review-refine retry budget exhausted and RollCallDetector had no mechanical Repair() fallback, unlike IncidentTypeStackDetector which already had one for the equivalent retry-exhaustion case.

**Decision:** Split Rule B's precision: only flag a sentence when at least ALL-BUT-ONE named road lacks its own nearby verb (HasOwnVerbNearby regex check for is/are/has/have/was/were/'s/remains/continues/becomes immediately after the mention) — this passes connected multi-clause prose and only flags true bare lists. Add RollCallDetector.Repair(script, context), a deterministic mechanical fallback mirroring IncidentTypeStackDetector.Repair: it finds the longest run of road names joined ONLY by list connectors (comma / "and" / ", and", nothing else between them) via a ListConnector regex, and collapses everything after the first name in that run to "and a couple more spots" — any road with its own clause breaks the chain and is left untouched. Wire Repair into all three call sites that already had the type-stack mechanical-fix pattern: BroadcastOrchestrator's final post-loop check, BroadcastOrchestrator.FinalizeExpandedScript (the expansion-pass re-gate), and the eval harness's ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync.

**Rationale:** A verb-classification approach (bare vs clean road) was tried first but has an unfixable ambiguity: the LAST road in a true bare list is often immediately followed by the shared trailing verb (e.g. "...Liverpool Road are slow"), so it gets misclassified as having its OWN clause, producing a grammatically broken double-and when collapsed. Connector-adjacency chain detection sidesteps this entirely — it only looks at what textually separates consecutive road mentions, which is exactly the shape of a bare list (comma/and chains) versus connected prose (a verb or detail between mentions), and never needs to decide which road owns which verb.

**Consequences:** RollCallDetector now has parity with IncidentTypeStackDetector: both gates get a guaranteed deterministic fix rather than ship-with-visibility-only when retries exhaust. Rule A (the clear-road all-clean dump) still has no Repair — no live evidence of it ever shipping, deferred until observed. Confirmed via 11 unit tests (RollCallDetectorTests) covering the false-positive fix, the true bare-list case, the exact live pass-11 defect (Repair verified to collapse it and re-Detect clean), a no-op on an already-clean script, and a safe no-op guard when a clean road's clause sits inside the bare-list span (interleaved shape the mechanical pass intentionally does not attempt). Full backend suite green (731/375/207/850 across Domain/Application/Functions/Infrastructure) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Cross-Anchor Overlap Suppression in CorridorAnchors

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-12 scenario matrix (Gold Coast) shipped "Mountain Road has a road hazard at Tamborine Mountain Road, between Tamborine Mountain Road and Henri Robert Drive, with a long queue" — the same place name voiced twice in one breath. Root cause verified via a temp diagnostic test dumping the raw TrafficNarrativeSummarizer prompt: the corridor had TWO Location: lines, "Between Tamborine Mountain Road and Henri Robert Drive" and a separate "At Tamborine Mountain Road", both surviving CorridorAnchors because that method's existing overlap filter (2026-06-xx fix) only checks each anchor against the corridor's Extent field, never against OTHER anchors from the same corridor. Extent was unset here, so no filtering happened at all. DuplicateAnchorDetector does not catch this either — it only tracks the corridor's own RoadName and MonitoredRoutes, not cross-street anchor text.

**Decision:** Rewrite CorridorAnchors (TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.cs) to compute SignificantTokens for every candidate anchor up front, order candidates by token count descending (richer/more-specific anchors like a two-endpoint "between A and B" first), then walk the list accumulating a covered-tokens set seeded from Extent's tokens (if present) and adding each surviving anchor's tokens after it is kept. An anchor is dropped when its tokens are a subset of the running covered set — whether that coverage came from Extent or from an earlier, richer anchor in the SAME corridor.

**Rationale:** The narrower anchor never carries information the richer one didn't already state — voicing the same place name twice reads as a data re-read, not a presenter naming two distinct spots. Ordering by token count first (rather than by incident order) guarantees the more specific anchor is the one kept regardless of which incident the source data listed first.

**Consequences:** Added 2 tests (TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests): Summarize_SecondAnchorRestatingFirstAnchorsPlace_IsSuppressed (the exact live Gold Coast shape, asserts the place name appears exactly once) and Summarize_TwoIncidentsWithGenuinelyDistinctAnchors_BothSurvive (confirms the fix does not over-suppress unrelated anchors). All 50 pre-existing summarizer tests still pass unchanged. Full backend suite green (731/375/207/852) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Add Mechanical Repair() to DuplicateAnchorDetector for Retry-Exhaustion Parity

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-13 scenario matrix (Brisbane) shipped "Seventeen Mile Rocks Road is at a standstill at Seventeen Mile Rocks Road, and Centenary Highway..." — a bare tautological self-reference, the same corridor name voiced twice in one breath with zero new information in the second mention. Verified via a temp unit test that DuplicateAnchorDetector.Detect already correctly flags this (HasDuplicateAnchor=true) — the review-refine retry budget simply exhausted before the model fixed it. Unlike RollCallDetector and IncidentTypeStackDetector (both given a mechanical Repair() fallback earlier this session for the identical retry-exhaustion failure mode), DuplicateAnchorDetector had no Repair() at all — every occurrence shipped with only a ship-with-visibility warning.

**Decision:** Add DuplicateAnchorDetector.Repair(script, context). Deliberately narrow scope: only collapses the SAFE, observed-live shape — exactly ONE anchor duplicated in a sentence, whose LAST occurrence is a bare trailing "at/on/near/along [the] ANCHOR" phrase immediately followed by a sentence boundary (comma or terminal punctuation) — by deleting that trailing phrase whole. Any other shape (a second mention carrying new information via a different preposition like "with"/"to"/"between", or more than one anchor duplicated in the same sentence) is left completely untouched. Wired into all three call sites that already carry the type-stack/roll-call mechanical-fix pattern: BroadcastOrchestrator's final post-loop check, BroadcastOrchestrator.FinalizeExpandedScript, and the eval harness's ReviewRefineAndComplyAsync.

**Rationale:** A bare bare-self-reference has provably zero information content (Detect's own feedback says as much: 'refer back implicitly'), so deleting the trailing repeat is always safe. Genuine second mentions that add a new fact (an extent endpoint, a different cross-street) use a different preposition shape and are excluded by construction rather than guessed at — the same conservative posture as RollCallDetector.Repair's connector-adjacency chain detection: only touch text whose SHAPE proves it is redundant, never infer intent.

**Consequences:** DuplicateAnchorDetector now has parity with RollCallDetector and IncidentTypeStackDetector — all three deterministic gates get a guaranteed mechanical fix rather than ship-with-visibility-only when retries exhaust. Confirmed via 4 new unit tests (DuplicateAnchorDetectorTests): the exact live Brisbane defect collapses and re-Detects clean, a second mention with new information via 'with' is left untouched, a genuine 'from X to Y' extent span is left untouched, and an already-clean script is a no-op. Full backend suite green (735/375/207/852) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Fix Symmetric Gap in CleanAnchor Self-Reference Check for Route-Code Prefixes

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-14 scenario matrix (Sydney, x2 across #1 and #7) shipped 'the Eastern Distributor is in the same shape at M1 Eastern Distributor' — HERE's incident description named the Eastern Distributor corridor's own road prefixed with its route code ('M1 Eastern Distributor'), and the writer voiced it as if it were a second, different place. Verified live: GetCorridorsAsync for Sydney returns exactly ONE corridor named 'Eastern Distributor' — 'M1 Eastern Distributor' is not a distinct road, just the same road with its M1 designation prefixed in the raw incident text. CleanAnchor's self-reference check (IsRoadToken) only tested anchorTokens.IsSubsetOf(roadTokens) — catching an anchor NARROWER than or equal to the road ('At Epping Road' on the Epping Road corridor) but not the reverse: an anchor that contains ALL the road's tokens PLUS an extra route-code token.

**Decision:** Widen IsRoadToken to a symmetric check: a fragment is a self-reference when EITHER its tokens are a subset of the road's tokens (the original case) OR the road's tokens are a subset of the fragment's tokens AND every token beyond the road's own tokens matches a bare route-code pattern (RouteCodeToken: 1-3 letters then 1-4 digits, e.g. 'M1', 'A4', 'B23'). Applied uniformly in both CleanAnchor branches (the plain-location check and the between-A-and-B endpoint check).

**Rationale:** A route code is not new location information — it is the SAME road's own designation, so 'M1 Eastern Distributor' vs 'Eastern Distributor' is exactly the tautology CleanAnchor already exists to strip ('Kessels Road ... at Kessels Road'), just with the extra token on the other side of the containment relation. Restricting the reverse-direction match to ONLY route-code-shaped extra tokens (not any superset) keeps it safe: a genuine cross-street like 'M1 Eastern Distributor at Cathedral Street' still has a non-route-code extra token ('Cathedral', 'Street') and is correctly kept.

**Consequences:** Added 2 tests (TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests): Summarize_RouteCodePrefixedSelfReference_IsSuppressed (the exact live shape, asserts no Location: line at all) and Summarize_RouteCodePrefixedAnchorWithGenuineCrossStreet_KeepsCrossStreet (confirms the fix does not over-suppress a real additional cross-street). All 52 pre-existing summarizer tests still pass unchanged. Full backend suite green (735/375/207/854) before and after. Also hardened prompts/draft.md's existing same-state paraphrase ban (line 33) with the observed live phrase 'the same shape' as an explicit example — the meaning-level ban already covered it but the model found this specific unlisted paraphrase.

## 2026-07-01 — Fixed two real JS/animation-jank bugs found via the runtime performance probe

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User reported 'the actual javascript is what's extremely laggy, the animations, and such' on deployed dev. Investigated with Lighthouse timespan-mode (github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse User Flows), CPU-throttled (4x, median-of-3 to absorb host-load variance) plus raw CDP tracing/V8 CPU profiling for ground-truth cross-checks -- not assertions. Two independent, measured, reproducible bugs found on the On-Air board (the app's most-viewed, continuously-open screen).

**Decision:** Bug 1 (JS re-render cost): QueueBeam, CoverageHome, and ReviewPane each called useSecondTick()/useNow() at their TOP level, forcing their entire subtree (all job rows / all 19 station lanes / the whole review surface incl. JobReviewCockpit) to re-render every second even with zero user interaction. Fixed by isolating the tick to the leaf that actually displays a live countdown: QueueBeam split QueueItem into WaitingQueueItem (owns useSecondTick) vs memoized GeneratingQueueItem/DoneQueueItem; ReviewPane extracted HotterJobBanner as its own ticking leaf; CoverageHome switched to a new useCoarseNow(5) hook (5s-boundary-floored snapshot, imperceptible drift on a 2h+ timeline). Bug 2 (CSS animation jank, the dominant cost): AuroraHero and AuroraWash both animated the CSS background-position property via the animate-aurora Tailwind keyframe -- a main-thread-only property Chrome can never composite, forcing continuous Style+Layout+Paint every frame for as long as the component stays mounted. Fixed by converting both to an oversized layer animating the transform property (translateX) instead, compositor-thread only, via a new aurora-drift keyframe replacing aurora.

**Rationale:** Assertion-first investigation (assuming useSecondTick was the culprit from static reading) was wrong per direct user pushback demanding a real framework; measured with Lighthouse timespan mode plus raw CDP traces plus a reduced-motion A/B instead. The tick-hook fix alone barely moved the number (1911ms to 1860ms); the CSS animation was the dominant cost (idle-onair 1911ms to 519ms, a 3.7x improvement, confirmed via a clean reduced-motion A/B: 1730ms animating vs 276ms frozen). Both bugs are real and independently confirmed, not measurement artifacts -- ruled out via a blank-page control (3ms), a floor-to-boundary fix for a jitter bug in the first useCoarseNow attempt (verified in an eval cell before trusting it), and median-of-3 sampling after discovering devtools CPU throttling multiplies live host performance (single-sample 4x runs swung 460-1570ms under load average 4.6-5.66 on a 16-core box).

**Consequences:** Files changed: web/src/hooks/use-second-tick.ts (new useCoarseNow), web/src/features/onair/components/workstation/QueueBeam.tsx (QueueItem split into 3 memoized variants), web/src/features/onair/components/workstation/ReviewPane.tsx (HotterJobBanner extracted), web/src/features/onair/components/board/CoverageHome.tsx (useNow to useCoarseNow), web/src/components/ui/aceternity/aurora-hero.tsx plus aurora-wash.tsx (transform-based rewrite), web/tailwind.config.js (aurora keyframe renamed to aurora-drift, now animates transform not backgroundPosition). All verified: full vitest (459 pass), full Playwright E2E (33 pass), visual screenshot A/B (aurora drift still looks correct on HomePage and CoverageHome), whole-project eslint clean. New web/scripts/perf-runtime.mjs (Lighthouse timespan-mode probe, 3 scenarios x 2 CPU multipliers, median-of-3 sampling on the gated 4x runs) wired into azure-pipelines.yml as an INFORMATIONAL step (non-blocking, --no-fail) after the existing cold-load perf gate -- deliberately not a hard merge gate given the measured host-load variance even after median-of-3. Remaining audio-review cost (roughly 1500-1800ms during active playback) is confirmed legitimate: AudioWaveformPlayer's intentional 60Hz rAF-driven karaoke-highlight loop, bounded to when audio plays, not ambient.

## 2026-07-01 — Fix Mc-Prefix Road-Name Casing Collapse in RoadNameFormatter

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** RoadNameFormatter.TitleCase title-cases HERE's all-caps road names ('MCEVOY STREET' -> 'Mcevoy Street'), but treats each run of letters as a single word and only upper-cases the first letter — collapsing the internal capital in Mc-prefixed surnames (observed live: 'Mcevoy Street' in one script, correctly-cased 'McEvoy Street' in another render of the identical live corridor, proving the source HERE data can arrive shouting and the naive title-case then mangles it).

**Decision:** Special-case the unambiguous 'Mc' + letter prefix inside TitleCase: when a word-start position is 'M'/'m' followed by 'C'/'c' followed by another letter, emit 'Mc' + upper-cased next letter, then continue lower-casing the rest of the word. Deliberately did NOT special-case 'Mac' — it collides with real all-lowercase-after-prefix names (Macquarie, Mackenzie) that would be wrongly split into 'MacQuarie'.

**Rationale:** The fix is scoped to the exact ambiguity-free case (Mc always capitalizes the next letter in Australian English surnames/place names) and only applies inside the pre-existing all-caps detection branch — NormalizeWord's existing hasLower check means any name HERE already sends correctly cased (mixed-case) is untouched, so this can only IMPROVE an all-caps input, never touch a clean one.

**Consequences:** Added 4 new tests (RoadNameFormatterTests): MCEVOY STREET -> McEvoy Street, MCDONALD ROAD -> McDonald Road, MACQUARIE STREET stays Macquarie Street (confirms Mac is NOT touched), and the bare 2-letter edge case MC -> Mc. All 12 pre-existing tests still pass. Fix lives inside the single shared ToSpeakable/TitleCase path already used by every corridor/anchor/extent rendering call site, so no additional wiring was needed anywhere else.

## 2026-07-01 — Suppress Redundant Rain-Fact Stacking Across Three Independent HERE Weather Fields

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-15 Melbourne scenario shipped 'blustery north wind and likely rain, ...heavy rain anticipated' — the SAME rain fact stated three separate times because HERE's weather response carries it in three genuinely independent fields that all happened to describe rain simultaneously: the text Conditions field ('Heavy rain'), a numeric PrecipitationProbability percentage (88, rendered as 'Chance of rain: likely'), and a text weather Alert ('Heavy rain anticipated'). Confirmed live via HereWeatherProvider diagnostic: Conditions='Heavy rain. Partly cloudy. Cool.', PrecipProb=88, Alert='Heavy rain anticipated' — three fields, one underlying fact.

**Decision:** Add a ContainsRainWord regex helper (rain/shower/drizzle/storm/downpour/precipitation, whole-word) to ContentFormatters. In FormatWeather: suppress the 'Chance of rain:' line entirely when Conditions already contains a rain word (the percentage adds no new fact). Suppress an ALERT line only when it ALSO contains a rain word AND Conditions does too (a genuinely different hazard — heat, wind, a non-rain storm — always survives regardless of Conditions).

**Rationale:** This is a DATA-layer fix, not a prompt fix, because the redundancy is structural (three independent upstream fields correlated on the same underlying weather event) rather than a stylistic choice the model could reliably avoid on its own — draft.md already said 'one condition, one temperature' but had no way to know the three lines it was HANDED described the same thing. Fixing it at the source removes the contradictory instruction (the prompt cannot know all three facts are the same without seeing them) rather than asking the model to infer redundancy across fields.

**Consequences:** Added 4 tests (ContentFormattersTests): the exact live 3-field-rain-stack case is suppressed to ONE rain mention, a rain alert survives alongside a NON-rain condition, a non-rain alert (heat) survives alongside a rain condition, and a non-rain condition still shows its Chance-of-rain line normally. HasMajorAlert on the underlying WeatherReport model is explicitly asserted UNCHANGED (still true) — only the rendered TEXT is filtered, so the weatherLeads prompt branch still triggers correctly. All 29 pre-existing ContentFormatters tests pass unchanged.

## 2026-07-01 — Never State a Bare Incident Count the Writer Cannot Back with Concrete Types

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live scenario matrix shipped vague filler like 'with a breakdown at Ferntree Gully Road and another incident' (Melbourne) because CorridorAggregator.BuildCorridorDescription rendered corridors with 3+ incidents as '{count} incidents including {primaryType}' (e.g. Perth Reid Highway: '4 incidents including road closure', Tonkin Highway: '3 incidents including crash'). This numeric claim told the writer there were unaccounted-for incidents but gave it no type/location for them, so it filled the information gap with 'another incident' rather than naming or dropping the extra facts — the same failure shape as the type-stack and roll-call defects this session already fixed at the data layer (cap the DATA so the writer is never handed more than it can respectfully use).

**Decision:** Rewrite BuildCorridorDescription to never state a bare count. When all incidents on a corridor share one type, describe just that type (matching the single-incident case exactly, e.g. 'road closure'). When 2+ distinct types exist, name up to 2 of them joined with 'and' (e.g. 'crash and heavy congestion') — the same cap the downstream 'Incidents:' line already applies — never a 3rd type and never a number.

**Rationale:** Every word in the resulting Detail: line now maps to a real, nameable type the writer can actually voice — there is no longer a numeric promise ('4 incidents') the concrete material can't back up, which is exactly what invited the vague-filler workaround. Capping at 2 distinct types mirrors the existing Incidents: line cap in TrafficNarrativeSummarizer, keeping the two mechanisms consistent.

**Consequences:** Added 5 tests (CorridorAggregatorTests): single-incident (unchanged behavior), multiple incidents of the SAME type collapse to the type with no count (the exact live Perth Reid Highway shape), two distinct types are both named (the exact live Perth Tonkin Highway shape), 3+ distinct types cap at 2 with no count, and the existing direction-suffix behavior is preserved. All corrected against TrafficTypeMapper's actual label set (crash/road closure/breakdown/hazard on road/lane closure/roadworks/planned event/heavy congestion — note this differs from the separate MapIncidentType vocabulary used for the Incidents:/primary bullet label, a pre-existing inconsistency not introduced by this fix and left out of scope). All 78 pre-existing CorridorAggregator tests pass unchanged.

## 2026-07-01 — Suppress Cross-Sentence Duplicate Anchors Between Sibling Corridors in the Same Bulletin

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live scenario matrix shipped the SAME place name voiced twice across DIFFERENT sentences of the same bulletin: Brisbane's 'Fig Tree Pocket Road is at a standstill... Centenary Highway is also delayed at Fig Tree Pocket Road' and Perth's Tonkin Highway (its own item) reappearing as Reid Highway's cross-street anchor. DuplicateAnchorDetector only catches literal repetition WITHIN one sentence by design; this is a genuinely different shape — one corridor's own road name being voiced a second time as ANOTHER corridor's incident anchor, across sentence boundaries, in the same bulletin.

**Decision:** Thread a sibling-token set through TrafficNarrativeSummarizer's corridor-bullet rendering: AppendCorridorBullets (and the curated-mode equivalent) computes the significant tokens of every INDIVIDUALLY-NAMED corridor's own road (i.e. corridors that survive each tier's cap and will actually be voiced as their own item — a swept/overflow corridor's name is never actually spoken, so it does not count as a sibling). CorridorAnchors then suppresses any candidate anchor whose tokens are a subset of ANOTHER corridor's own road tokens (excluding the corridor itself, matched by name) — extending the existing Extent-overlap and same-corridor cross-anchor suppression added earlier this session to also cover ACROSS-corridor overlap.

**Rationale:** A road already being voiced as its own item elsewhere in the bulletin adds zero new information when it resurfaces as a cross-street anchor for a different item — it is the identical redundancy class the same-corridor fix already targets, just spanning sentence boundaries instead of Location lines within one bullet. Scoping suppression to only INDIVIDUALLY-NAMED siblings (not swept/overflow corridors) avoids over-suppressing genuine new information — an anchor matching a road that will never actually be spoken as its own item is still real, useful location data.

**Consequences:** Added 3 tests (TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests) at the full Summarize() level: the exact live Brisbane shape (Fig Tree Pocket Road voiced exactly once across the whole bulletin), a swept-overflow sibling confirms its name is NOT suppressed (genuine information preserved), and a corridor's own self-reference is confirmed not double-counted against the sibling logic. All 54 pre-existing summarizer tests pass unchanged. Full backend suite green (745/375/207/862) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Correct False Location-Semantics Rule and Add RepeatedPrepositionDetector

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live scenario matrix shipped 'The Warringah Freeway is shut outbound at Brook Street, at the ramp to Alfred Street North' (Sydney CBD) — the identical preposition ('at') stacked twice to introduce two separate anchors, reading as a database list. Root cause traced to draft.md line 36, which INCORRECTLY instructed the writer that two Location lines on one corridor are 'two cross-streets of the SAME item' to be voiced as 'one closure/delay bounded by both spots' ('shut between Brook Street and the Alfred Street North ramp').
