This is factually false: CorridorAnchors (TrafficNarrativeSummarizer) builds at most ONE anchor per INCIDENT — a single incident's own 'between A and B' span is already rendered as one Location line — so two Location lines are GUARANTEED to come from two DIFFERENT incidents on the same road, never endpoints of one span. Following the rule as written was itself a fabrication risk (asserting a bounded closure the data never stated) and, when the model instead voiced them separately, produced the repeated-preposition artifact.

**Decision:** Corrected draft.md line 36 to state the true semantics: two Location lines are two separate incidents on the same road, never endpoints of one bounded closure, and must be connected naturally (varying the preposition/verb) rather than fabricating a span. Additionally built RepeatedPrepositionDetector (mirroring the RollCallDetector/DuplicateAnchorDetector/IncidentTypeStackDetector deterministic-gate pattern established this session) as a defensive CODE-level backstop, since the sibling classes all showed prompt-only fixes regressing live the same day they were strengthened. Detect flags the narrow, structurally unambiguous shape only — the SAME preposition word (at/on/near) introducing two anchors separated by nothing but a comma, via regex backreference. A conjoined 'at X and Y' or a naturally-varied 'at X, with Y also...' is deliberately NOT flagged. Repair swaps the SECOND occurrence for 'and' — the cheapest grammatically safe fix that removes the mechanical repetition without inventing content.

**Rationale:** Fixing the prompt's false premise addresses the root cause (the model was following bad instructions, not making an unprompted error). The code-level detector is a narrower, purely defensive layer for the specific unambiguous artifact shape, added because this session's other three sibling detectors all needed a code backstop after prose-only bans proved insufficient under retry-budget exhaustion.

**Consequences:** Added 11 tests (RepeatedPrepositionDetectorTests) covering the exact live defect, repeated 'near', conjoined-with-and passes, genuine between-A-and-B spans pass, naturally-varied clauses pass, different-preposition pairs on the same road pass, and Repair's swap-to-'and' behavior. Wired into all 3 call sites (BroadcastOrchestrator's mid-loop gate + final post-loop check + FinalizeExpandedScript, and the eval harness's mid-loop gate + final check) with parity to the other 3 detectors. Full backend suite green (756/375/207/862) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Add ImpactStackDetector for Trailing Severity-Word Stacking

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-15 Perth scenario shipped 'Tonkin Highway northbound is congested at Great Eastern Highway and Dunreath Drive after an accident, with heavy traffic and moderate delays' — three severity synonyms (congested / heavy traffic / moderate delays) all restating 'this road is bad' in one sentence. draft.md line 34 already bans stacking 'the type, the impact word and the detail in one breath' in the MAIN clause, but this specific failure landed in a TRAILING 'with X and Y' clause instead — the identical shape IncidentTypeStackDetector already exists to catch for raw TYPE words (BFN-019), now recurring for SEVERITY words.

**Decision:** Add ImpactStackDetector, mirroring IncidentTypeStackDetector's exact structure: a vocabulary of severity/congestion synonyms (congested, heavy traffic, bumper to bumper, crawling, backed up, minor/moderate/heavy/severe delays, etc.), a TrailingClause regex matching a 'with/including X' clause at the sentence end, and a HasStack trigger when 2+ distinct vocabulary words appear in that tail. Added a linking-verb guard (is/are/was/were/has/have/had) that skips the match when the 'trailing clause' text actually contains a second independent clause about a DIFFERENT subject (e.g. '...with minor delays, and Point Road is congested') — without this guard the regex's greedy match spans into a second sentence-like clause and produces a false positive on ordinary multi-item prose. Repair strips the offending trailing clause verbatim, identical to IncidentTypeStackDetector.Repair.

**Rationale:** Same rationale as IncidentTypeStackDetector: the data layer already computes exactly ONE honest qualitative magnitude per corridor (FormatImpact), so a trailing clause restating 2+ synonyms of that SAME magnitude is pure repetition, safe to strip mechanically without losing any fact. The linking-verb guard was added after a synthetic false-positive test caught the greedy trailing-clause regex spanning across an 'and Point Road is congested' second clause — confirming the guard was necessary, not speculative.

**Consequences:** Added 9 tests (ImpactStackDetectorTests): the exact live Perth defect (Detect + Repair both verified), an 'including' variant, a single-impact-word pass (a genuine new fact, not a stack), a clean-sentence pass, the two-different-items false-positive case that motivated the linking-verb guard, an empty-script pass, and Repair's clause-preservation across multiple sentences. Wired into all 3 call sites (BroadcastOrchestrator's mid-loop gate + final post-loop check + FinalizeExpandedScript, and the eval harness) with parity to the other 3 gate-shaped detectors added this session. Full backend suite green (765/375/207/862) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Add FakeLocationDetector for Incident-Type-as-Location Fabrication

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-16 scenarios shipped 'Mitchell Street outbound is closed at a road closure' (Newcastle, reproduced 3/3 in isolation) and 'London Circuit citybound is closed at the road closure' (Canberra) — the writer invented a pseudo-location out of the incident TYPE itself when the corridor's condensed Minor bullet carried NO Location line at all ('Mitchell Street outbound — road closure, road closed', confirmed via live diagnostic). Root cause: draft.md line 36 pressured 'pin every item to its SPOT, once' without covering the no-anchor case, so with nothing real to pin to, the model recited the incident type as if it were a place.

**Decision:** Corrected draft.md line 36 with explicit no-anchor guidance: when a corridor carries no Location line, state the road/direction/condition plainly and move on — never recite the incident type as a fabricated place. Additionally built FakeLocationDetector (mirroring the session's established deterministic-gate pattern) as a defensive backstop: a regex matching '(at/near/on/in) [a/the] TYPE-NOUN [point/location/spot]' against the same incident-type vocabulary IncidentTypeStackDetector already guards. Repair strips the fabricated phrase verbatim, leaving a complete, grammatically correct sentence ('Mitchell Street outbound is closed.').

The vocabulary reuse from IncidentTypeStackDetector keeps the type-noun list as a single maintained set rather than duplicating it with drift risk.

Wired into all 3 call sites (BroadcastOrchestrator's mid-loop gate + final post-loop check + FinalizeExpandedScript, and the eval harness) with parity to the other 5 gate-shaped detectors added this session. Full backend suite green (778/375/207/873) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Fix Extent Self-Reference Abbreviation Mismatch and Extend Same-State Ban List

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-16 Gold Coast scenario shipped 'Helensvale Road citybound is closed from Helensvale Road to Country Club Drive' — the corridor's own road name used as its own Extent span start. Root-caused via live diagnostic: HereTrafficProvider.ComposeExtent already had a self-reference guard, but it used exact string equality — the reverse-geocoded endpoint came back abbreviated ('Helensvale Rd') against the corridor's spelled-out RoadName ('Helensvale Road citybound'), which never compares equal. Separately, Sydney CBD shipped 'Mount Street has a similar hold-up' — a new same-state paraphrase not on the explicit ban list, despite the meaning-level ban in draft.md line 33 already covering it in principle.

**Decision:** Added RoadNameFormatter.IsSameRoad(a, b) — a shared, abbreviation- and direction-suffix-aware road-name comparison (Rd/Road, St/Street, Ave/Avenue, Hwy/Highway, etc.; strips citybound/outbound/etc.) — and switched ComposeExtent's three self-reference checks from exact StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase equality to IsSameRoad. Centralizing this in RoadNameFormatter (rather than a local fix inside ComposeExtent) makes it reusable for the next such cross-field comparison.

All 13 pre-existing ExtentEnrichmentTests and 16 pre-existing RoadNameFormatterTests pass unchanged. The same-state ban-list addition is a soft, unverifiable-by-code fix (semantic paraphrase, same class as the earlier 'the same shape' addition) — flagged as the one fix this session relying on prose reinforcement rather than a deterministic gate, consistent with only building code-level detectors for structurally unambiguous lexical/syntactic patterns.

## 2026-07-01 — Cap Fuel Data to the Single Cheapest-Price Fact — Remove Average/Station-Count from the Prompt

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-17 Gold Coast scenario shipped 'Diesel is cheapest at .74 in Merrimac, with average diesel at .80 across 19 stations' — directly violating draft.md line 47's explicit rule ('NEVER recite the average price, the station count... one price with its location, stated plainly, not a price board'). Root cause: ContentFormatters.FormatFuel fed the average price AND station count to the model for every fuel type despite the prompt already banning their use — a prompt-only restriction on data the model could still see and, under retry/multi-fuel-type pressure, chose to recite anyway.

**Decision:** Removed AveragePrice and StationCount entirely from FormatFuel's rendered output — only FuelType, the cheapest MinPrice, CheapestStationSuburb (if present), and LatestModifiedUtc (if present) are now fed to the writer. The underlying FuelPriceSummary/FuelSummaryDto model fields are UNCHANGED (still used by the operator console/API); only the LLM-facing text rendering was capped.

**Rationale:** Same pattern as every other data-layer fix this session (incident-type cap, corridor description cap, weather rain-fact suppression): when a prompt-only ban repeatedly proves insufficient under load, remove the temptation at the source rather than keep reinforcing prose the model can still route around. The average/station-count fields serve the operator console, not the writer — there is no legitimate reason for the LLM prompt to ever see them.

**Consequences:** Updated 6 pre-existing FormatFuel tests to match the new average/station-count-free output (renamed FormatFuel_FormatsMinAndAvgToTwoDecimals to FormatFuel_FormatsMinPriceToTwoDecimals; removed '(N stations)' assertions from FormatFuel_IncludesLatestModifiedTimestampWhenPresent, FormatFuel_MultipleSummaries, FormatFuel_IncludesSuburbWhenPresent, FormatFuel_OmitsSuburbWhenNull). Added FormatFuel_NeverIncludesAveragePriceOrStationCount as an explicit regression guard with distinct min/average/count values per fuel type so no assertion could pass by numeric collision. All 35 ContentFormattersTests pass. Full backend suite green (779/375/207/873) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Extend MetaLeakDetector Beyond the Literal Word 'data' to Database-Structure Phrases

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-17 Newcastle scenario shipped 'No other problems are logged on the listed roads, so overall flow across the area is steady and moving well.' — database-structure language ('logged', 'the listed roads') describing the SOURCE rather than the road, the same class of violation draft.md line 62 already banned for the literal word 'data', but the specific phrasing wasn't covered.

**Decision:** Broadened draft.md line 62 with explicit examples ('no other problems are logged', 'the listed roads', 'on record', 'in the system' all describe the SOURCE, not the road). Extended MetaLeakDetector (previously a single-word 'data' regex) with a second pattern matching MULTI-WORD database-structure phrase SHAPES — '(are/is/were/was) logged', 'the listed road(s)', 'on record', 'in the system' — deliberately NOT single words like 'logged' or 'listed' alone, which are ordinary English outside this specific shape ('logged on', 'listed for sale').

**Rationale:** Same rationale as every other detector added this session: a prompt-only ban on the CONCEPT (rule 62 already existed) proved insufficient once the model found unlisted specific wording. Phrase-SHAPE matching (not bare word bans) avoids false-positiving on ordinary English uses of the same words — 'logged on' and 'listed for sale' are common phrases that must survive.

**Consequences:** Added 7 tests (MetaLeakDetectorTests): the exact live Newcastle defect, 3 other database-structure phrase shapes ('X are logged', 'on record', 'in the system'), and 3 explicit false-positive guards confirming ordinary English uses of the same words ('logged on', 'listed for sale', 'safety record') are NOT flagged. All 5 pre-existing MetaLeakDetectorTests pass unchanged. Full backend suite green (786/375/207/873) before and after.

## 2026-07-01 — Suppress the Minor Tier to a Count-Only Sweep When a Major Headline Leads

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Editorial-value review of pass-18 (user-driven: "what would not actually provide value to the audience?"). Live scripts named individual minor-delay side streets even when a road was SHUT elsewhere — Sydney: Warringah Freeway closed, then "O'Dea Avenue has minor delays, Lister Avenue also running behind"; Canberra: London Circuit closed, then "Petrie Plaza has minor congestion, Monara Street is also showing minor congestion". A "minor delays" side street changes no listener's route once a closure reshapes it — naming them is fluff that buries the headline. The ATN corpus itself never enumerates sub-threshold items; the gap-analysis doc already flagged "vague filler instead of severity".

**Decision:** In `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendCorridorBullets`, when a Major-or-worse item is present (`major.Count > 0`), the Minor tier is no longer named. It is emitted as a single count-only line under `"Minor (background — do NOT name these roads):"` stating the count with explicit leave-to-drop wording; the minor road names are withheld from the writer entirely (structurally impossible to voice a road never handed over). With NO Major headline (worst item Moderate/Minor), behaviour is unchanged — a quiet market's minor items ARE the story. draft.md gained a companion rule: fold the background count into ONE optional area phrase only if the slot needs length, else DROP it — a shorter, sharper read beats padding.

**Rationale:** Same data-capping pattern as the tier caps and the fuel/incident-type caps: prompt instructions to "drop minor items when busy" proved unreliable under retry load; withholding the data makes the fluff structurally impossible. Threshold is Major (not Moderate) because a 6–15min Moderate delay is still a genuine reroute signal; only sub-threshold Minor items alongside a bigger story are pure noise.

**Consequences:** Added 5 unit tests (major-headline suppresses names + accurate uncapped count + severe-headline suppresses + no-major keeps names + minor-only market keeps names); updated 4 pre-existing tests to the new contract, preserving each one's original intent (label-mapping test promoted its minors to Moderate so all labels still surface; sibling-anchor test made both corridors Major so cross-anchor suppression still fires). Full backend suite green (786/375/207/880). Verified live (pass-19): Canberra/Sydney/Melbourne/Brisbane/Gold Coast all sweep minors to "a few (more) minor hold-ups around town" with zero individually-named minor roads.

## 2026-07-01 — Turn On the Monitored Drive-Time Channel with a Documented Starter Config

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The single most actionable number in ATN reads is the point-to-point commuter drive time ("the M1 from Mulgoa Rd to Church is taking about 28 minutes"). The channel (`MonitoredRouteReporter` → `AppendMonitoredRouteBullets`, headline at ≥5min delay, DI-bound `MonitoredRoutesOptions`) was fully built but had ZERO markets configured, so it never fired in any bulletin. A live diagnostic confirmed a fixed origin→destination run returns real live-vs-typical delay from HERE (M4 Parramatta→CBD 25/23min, Monash 27/25min), unlike per-corridor drive-time (deliberately qualitative-only — the "stacked minute-counts the corpus never uses").

**Decision:** Added a documented `MonitoredRoutes` starter block to `appsettings.json` — well-known metro arterials (Sydney M4/Warringah, Melbourne Monash/West Gate, Brisbane Pacific Mwy) with real endpoints, `Enabled: true`. Keys MUST match a `MarketSchedule.MarketId` (case-insensitive); unmatched markets are a safe no-op. Fixed a latent mismatch: `BulletinEval` keyed the reporter on the internal slug (`scenario.Market`, e.g. "sydney-busy") which never matches a city-keyed config — changed to `scenario.City`.

**Rationale:** Endpoints are verifiable real geography and times are HERE-computed live (never stored/invented), so turning the channel on is honest value, not fabrication. Route SELECTION (which commuter runs matter, and the exact MarketId keys) is genuinely an ARN editorial/config decision — the starter set is explicitly flagged for ARN to confirm/replace, not treated as final.

**Consequences:** Channel verified live (pass-19): "The M4, Parramatta to the city...", "The Monash Freeway into the CBD...", "West Gate citybound is running to time", "The Pacific Motorway into the city..." all surface. They read as asides at present (off-peak deltas <5min, correct behaviour); at peak they become the headline "X minutes" figure. ARN action required: confirm MarketId keys + the commuter runs that matter per market.

## 2026-07-01 — Detour Advice Not Surfaced: Data Genuinely Thin, Code Correct (no change)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ATN reads give explicit reroute advice ("make sure you stick to Ballarat Road instead"). Our `DetourSuggestion` plumbing exists end-to-end (`HereRoutingProvider.GetSafeDetourAsync`, gated on `StartPoint`+`EndPoint` + corridor `DelayMinutes > 0` + incident `SegmentRefs`). A live diagnostic across 4 busy markets (44 corridors) returned ZERO detours.

**Decision:** Make no code change. The gate is correct; the data is genuinely thin. Root cause: (1) most corridors lack Start/End coordinates so drive-time never computes; (2) HERE already reroutes around a closure, so a shut road's own span shows ~0 delay (Warringah closed = 11/10min), failing the `DelayMinutes > 0` gate; (3) when called, `GetSafeDetourAsync` returns "no faster detour" because the main route already avoids the closure.

**Rationale:** ATN-style "take Ballarat Road instead" requires NAMING a parallel arterial — inference/fabrication, not a clean HERE signal. Forcing the gate open or inventing parallel roads would violate the no-fabrication boundary. The honest position is to leave the correct gate in place and surface detours only when HERE genuinely returns a faster safe alternative.

**Consequences:** No code or test change. Documented so a future session doesn't re-investigate the empty detour channel as a bug. If detour advice becomes a hard requirement, it needs a deliberate parallel-arterial data source, not a tweak to this gate.

## 2026-07-01 — Rewrite the Bulletin Prompts From Scratch (Positive-First, Lean, Example-Driven)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Editorial review (user-driven) demanded every sentence carry a concrete, verifiable, actionable fact — no vague "a few more hold-ups around town are affecting local routes", which names nothing and makes a listener worry about a road that's fine. `draft.md` had grown to 21.7KB (~3,500 words) of stacked ALL-CAPS negations; `system.md` 6.8KB; `review.md` 9KB. 2026 prompt-engineering research (grounded): 150–300 word sweet spot, reasoning degrades ~3000 tokens, "lost in the middle" ~30% accuracy drop for buried rules, positive framing beats negation (Pink Elephant), calm beats ALL-CAPS on modern models (target is gpt-5.4-mini), few-shot worked examples beat rule-lists. An independent harness-architect review confirmed a from-scratch rewrite over another patch.

**Decision:** Rewrote the prompt suite. `system.md` (~5KB): one core rule ("every sentence names a road, a spot, and a condition — else don't write it"), a short positive style, chain-of-command, a compact "Never" list, and FOUR worked examples (busy / sparse / all-clear / continuity) using non-capital-city data so the model can't copy content verbatim. `draft.md` (21.7KB → 4.7KB): a per-call fill-funnel (incidents → flowing roads → one standing filler fact → SHORTER READ) with the load-bearing "vagueness is worse than silence — dead air is acceptable, a sentence that names nothing is not" as the top priority, plus a brief positive "Voicing" section (closure-stands-alone, roadworks≠jam, drive-time is the only minute figure, MUST-NAME-SUBURB, continuity) replacing ~40 sprawling bans. `review.md` rewritten vagueness-first with soft word-count (dropped the "rejected" framing) and an always-on guard flagging weather/fuel when NOT selected. `refine.md` aligned: expand only with real data, never a vague sweep. Kept the 3-stage draft→review→refine loop and all deterministic detectors (deferred the architect's pipeline-flatten + detector shadow-retirement as a separate, evidence-backed change).

**Rationale:** The negation-stacked prompt was the root cause of both the fluff and the detector proliferation — a prompt that can't govern forces a code gate per failure. A positive spec + worked examples carries the load; the model imitates a good bulletin rather than dodging 40 bans. Target-only word framing removes the compliance pressure that produced padding.

**Consequences:** Verified across 4 live scenario-matrix passes (20–23, 40 scripts). Pass-23: zero vague-aggregate lines across all 10 markets; every sentence names a road+spot+condition. The rewrite surfaced (and this session fixed) regressions the terse prompt introduced — fabricated weather/fuel on traffic-only reads, a UTC-timestamp data leak, a sign-off, absence-narration, and an internal-term jargon leak (see the two following decisions). Full backend suite green (823/375/207/878).

## 2026-07-01 — Build the Filler-Statement Generation Pipeline (Real Fill Between Data and a Shorter Read)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** BFN-002 shipped only the admin CRUD for per-market evergreen filler statements; the generation-time selection/injection was never built (documented KNOWN GAP at `LlmScriptGenerator.cs`). So `"filler"` in a station's FillOrder was a no-op, and when real data was thin the model manufactured vague aggregates to fill the 30s slot — the exact fluff the user flagged. There was no legitimate content between real data and dead air.

**Decision:** Built the runtime pipeline. New pure `FillerStatementSelector` (Domain): matches enabled statements whose gap range fits the estimated slot shortfall, excludes any voiced in this station's previous same-day script (anti-repeat), best-fit ordered. `BroadcastOrchestrator` fetches per-market filler into `BroadcastWithTraffic.FillerStatements`; `LlmScriptGenerator` selects and injects them into BOTH the draft and the refine/expansion prompts as data-level content the writer MAY reach for (never required, never invented). Seeded 5 sample statements in the eval harness (real, evergreen, nationally-true road facts — school-zone hours, learner phone rules, roadworks limits, child-seat law, keep-left) standing in for admin-authored content.

**Rationale:** The fill hierarchy needs a real rung between "flowing-road detail" and "shorter read". A per-market admin-authored fact carries no fabrication risk (it is persisted truth, not generated), so it lets a sparse market reach length honestly. This is the mechanism that makes "incidents → weather → traffic → filler" hit 30s without fluff.

**Consequences:** Verified live (pass-23): Newcastle (1 incident) and Scottsdale (0 incidents) both fill to ~30s by voicing the seeded school-zone fact after the traffic, with zero vague filler. 12 unit tests for the selector (mutation-verified). ARN action: author real per-market filler statements via the existing admin CRUD.

## 2026-07-01 — Extend MetaLeakDetector to Internal Jargon (corridor / monitored route) With a Lexical Repair

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The leaner rewrite let the model voice our internal data-structure labels on air — live pass-22 Newcastle: "the rest of the run through Newcastle's monitored routes is clear ... on those corridors". A presenter never says "corridor" or "monitored route". The main review loop's meta-leak gate cleared it, but the forced word-target EXPANSION pass (which pads a short read toward the slot) reintroduced the jargon AFTER the loop, and `FinalizeExpandedScript` mechanically repaired every other detector but only LOGGED a surviving meta-leak (it had no `Repair`).

**Decision:** Extended `MetaLeakDetector` with a third regex class for internal jargon (`corridors?`, `monitored routes?`) and added `MetaLeakDetector.Repair` — a safe lexical substitution for that class ONLY ("corridors"→"roads", "monitored route"→"route", case-preserving). Wired the repair into `FinalizeExpandedScript` (production) and the eval's post-expansion sweep, mirroring the other expansion-reintroducible gates. The "data"/database-phrase classes keep no repair (deleting them collapses the sentence) and stay on the LLM-loop + shipped-warning path. Also fed the filler statements into the refine/expansion prompt so a short read pads with a real standing fact instead of jargon-laden sweeps.

**Rationale:** Internal-term jargon is stable banned vocabulary with a clean 1:1 natural substitute — exactly the class that belongs in a deterministic gate with a mechanical repair, not prompt-only. The expansion pass is an ungated refine that reintroduces defects the loop cleared; the non-mechanically-repairable classes needed a last-resort fix at the finalize step.

**Consequences:** Verified live (pass-23): no internal-term leak in any of 10 markets; Newcastle's expansion now voices the real school-zone fact. Detector tests: 37 total in MetaLeakDetectorTests (+25 this session, mutation-verified) — internal-term detection + Repair (substitution, case-preservation, idempotence, data-class-untouched guard). Also removed the fuel-data UTC timestamp from the prompt (`ContentFormatters.FormatFuel`) after the model read "it's 14:33 UTC in the latest fuel reports" aloud; and added a review guard flagging weather/fuel mentions when those sources are not selected (fabrication on traffic-only reads). Full backend suite green (823/375/207/878).

## 2026-07-01 — Deterministic SentenceCloneDetector for Repeated Sentence Shapes and Same-Road Echoes

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live pass-23 Melbourne CBD shipped three back-to-back sentences of an identical template — "King Street is moving freely through the CBD. Collins Street is moving freely through the CBD. St Kilda Road is moving freely through the CBD." The prompt bans cloning a sentence shape, but the model still produced it under sampling variance. `RollCallDetector` only catches a bare LIST inside ONE sentence (Rule A: 4+ clear roads named anywhere; Rule B: 3+ roads in a single sentence), not the same FRAME repeated across separate sentences each with its own road and verb. A related echo also recurred (pass-24): the SAME road opening two near-identical sentences — "Footscray Road is closed at the CityLink Tollway for roadworks. Footscray Road is closed at Sims Street for roadworks." (also Perth's Reid Highway).

**Decision:** Built `SentenceCloneDetector` (Domain) with two triggers and a mechanical `Repair`, wired into all gate points (production main loop + `FinalizeExpandedScript`, and the eval loop + post-expansion sweep), mirroring the other detectors. Trigger 1 — cloned shape: skeletonise each sentence (replace known road names with a placeholder, normalise), flag when one skeleton recurs 3+ times OR a 4+ word frame recurs 2+ times. Trigger 2 — same-road echo: flag when the same known road OPENS 2+ sentences (leading "The" transparent; whole-token boundary so "M1" ≠ "M11 Motorway", "Reid" ≠ "Reidvale"). `Repair` (last-resort, for the expansion-reintroduced clone) keeps the first sentence of each cloned group and drops the later duplicates; the same-road echo is left to the LLM loop to COMBINE ("closed at both X and Y") since dropping a genuine second closure point would lose real information.

**Rationale:** A repeated sentence shape and a repeated lead road are stable, structurally-detectable machine-tells with no legitimate use — exactly the class that belongs in a deterministic gate rather than a prompt-only ban that the model ignores under load. Skeletonisation via the known-road set means two DIFFERENT roads each at their own cross-street (good woven prose) never trip it — only a genuinely reused template or a single repeated road does. The same-road trigger also correctly folds two segments of one road ("the M1 between A and B ... the M1 between C and D") into one mention.

**Consequences:** Verified live (pass-25): the three-way clone gone (one Footscray mention), Melbourne's two M1 segments combined into one sentence, Perth's Reid Highway combined. 13 unit tests (mutation-verified), including the critical false-positive guard that three DIFFERENT roads each leading one sentence is NOT flagged. Also generalised the `MetaLeakDetector` internal-term class from "monitored route(s)" to bare "monitored" (never on-air vocabulary in any form — "monitored run/roads/routes"), repairing by dropping the word with case preservation, after pass-25 leaked "the monitored run across the CBD". Full backend suite green (836/375/207/878).

## 2026-07-01 — Deterministic UnselectedSourceDetector for Fabricated Weather/Fuel on Traffic-Only Reads

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** When weather or fuel is NOT selected for a bulletin (no block reaches the writer), any weather or price line is pure fabrication — no data backs it. The prompt bans it and `review.md` flags it, but the LLM review is probabilistic and let it ship intermittently across live passes (pass-27 Sydney CBD, traffic-only: "It's 18 degrees and mostly cloudy. Unleaded's cheapest at $1.79 in North Sydney."). A no-fabrication failure that ships even occasionally is not air-ready.

**Decision:** Built `UnselectedSourceDetector` (Domain), keyed off `context.Weather.IsNone` / `context.Fuel.IsNone`. Flags a weather signal (a temperature "\d degrees" or a named condition — cloud/rain/fog/sunny/storm/hail/etc.) when weather is unselected, and a fuel signal (unleaded/diesel/petrol, "a litre", "$1.xx") when fuel is unselected. `Repair` drops the offending sentence (weather and fuel are their own sentences, so the traffic content survives). Signals deliberately EXCLUDE road-ambiguous words ("clear", "fine", "wind", "running well") so a normal traffic clear-run never trips it. Wired into all four gate points (production loop + FinalizeExpandedScript, eval loop + post-expansion sweep) mirroring the other detectors.

**Rationale:** Fabricating an unselected source is a stable, structurally-detectable no-fabrication violation — exactly the class that belongs in a deterministic gate rather than a prompt-only ban the model ignores under sampling variance. Keying off the actual `Option.IsNone` state (not content heuristics) makes it precise: a selected source's line is never touched.

**Consequences:** 12 unit tests (weather-only / fuel-only / both fabrication; selected-source never flagged; the critical clear-run false-positive guard; Repair strips only the unselected class). Full backend suite green (848/375/207/879). Note (pre-existing, not from this change): a generic-advice line ("allow extra time") slipped review under sampling on one pass-27 market — a separate prompt+review-gated defect, candidate for its own deterministic gate if it recurs.
## 2026-07-02 — Frozen-Fetch Prompt-Iteration Harness + Data-Cap Fix Batch (BFN reviewer-mindset eval)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Iterating on prompt quality against live HERE mixes two variables — the prompt change and live-data drift — so a prompt "win" could be data luck. A 10-scenario BFN-mindset review of a frozen baseline (2 would-air / 1 borderline / 7 send-back) surfaced systematic failures the deterministic scorers passed: an on-air self-contradiction (a monitored route voiced "running to time" beside a closure on the SAME road), raw HERE abbreviations voiced verbatim ("Gold Coast Hwy to Pacific Mtwy"), prompt-rule violations under sampling variance (wind/rain-chance voiced, two fillers voiced), echo-padding (one closure restated three times), and fabricated fill (invented "all-clear" reassurance, three invented CBD roads that the FabricationScorer PASSED because they existed in tier-suppressed minor corridors the writer never saw).

**Decision:** (1) Built a frozen-fetch eval harness: `ARN_PROMPTS_DIR` env override in `LlmScriptGenerator.LoadPrompt` injects an experimental prompt set per-process without touching the repo tree (a human can edit `prompts/` concurrently); `HereFrozen` (test corpus builders) records ONE live HERE pass across all five typed clients (traffic/geocoding/routing/weather/fuel — `HereReplay` covered only three) and replays it deterministically, so consecutive runs differ ONLY by the prompt/code change; `FrozenScenarioEvalTests` runs the 10-scenario size×density×content matrix and writes a BFN-rubric review pack (objectivity, concreteness, redundancy, anchoring, variety, data-rules, honest-fill, clean-close, fidelity). (2) Fixed the failures at the DATA layer wherever prompt-only enforcement had already failed once: monitored routes suppressed under a same-road closure corridor (`ContainsRoad`); road-type abbreviations + glued tokens ("Alfred StreetNorth") + parenthetical direction qualifiers ("(Southbound)") normalized in `RoadNameFormatter.ToSpeakable`; wind/rain-chance no longer rendered (condition+temp+alerts only); filler candidates capped at 1; the filler gap estimate and the eval fabrication vocabulary both moved to `SelectVoiceableCorridors` (what the writer SAW, not the raw corridor list); the suppressed-minor count-line removed entirely (was voiced as "a few minor hold-ups around town"); contradictory mild Impact labels suppressed under a vivid Detail pace phrase; a closure's "Impact: road closed" line suppressed under its own "road closure" label; `SlotFitPlanner.ExpansionFeedback` rewritten with an unchanged-return escape hatch (echo-padding killer); `MetaLeakDetector` extended with refine-instruction echoes ("listed location", "cut that line"); `RollCallDetector` Rule B moved to 4+ names (three roads sharing one concrete condition is legitimate objective radio), with `Repair`'s collapsible chain kept at 3. Prompt-layer: draft/review/refine hardened (voice-each-item-once, no unsupported all-clear, knock-on-effect fabrication check, place-name spelling check, deterministic diesel, same-condition pairing shape, varied wrap-ups) and merged to `prompts/` (system.md untouched — concurrently owned by the user).

**Rationale:** Every fix follows the established lesson: data the writer never sees is data it cannot voice — capping the DATA beats re-prompting for the failure classes the model breaks under sampling variance. Freezing the fetch is what made each fix attributable; the same 10 scenarios moved 2→10 would-air across 8 replay iterations, then held on a FRESH live fetch (second corpus) after three residual data-residue fixes.

**Consequences:** Full backend suite green (845 Domain / 375 Application / 111 formatter+summarizer Infrastructure targeted, full Infra suite in CI). Harness retained as durable tooling: `FrozenScenarioEvalTests` (record/replay via `ARN_FROZEN_EVAL`, corpus override via `ARN_FROZEN_EVAL_CORPUS`, prompt injection via `ARN_PROMPTS_DIR`); frozen corpora are session-scoped and gitignored (`test/corpus/frozen-eval/`). Residual known noise: run-to-run stochastic wobbles (an occasional paired-descriptor stack, a dropped monitored-route aside under slot pressure) sit inside the would-air band and move between runs — not systematic. The prompt-layer rules assume the CURRENT system.md contract; re-verify after the user's in-progress system.md rewrite lands.

## 2026-07-02 — Filler Selection Becomes Gap-Covering (time-based, per the 1-Jul notes), Not Single-Best-Fit

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The frozen-fetch iteration's one-statement filler cap (a fix for two fillers voiced in a slot that needed one) over-corrected: thin markets shipped 14–18s scripts into a 30s slot (fresh-live eval: Sydney CBD 34w ≈ 14s, Newcastle 38w ≈ 16s). An under-filled script does not air short — production's duration gate routes it content-limited → the generic fallback cart, the exact outcome BFN-002's filler library exists to prevent. The 1-Jul raw notes are explicit that fill is TIME-based ("filler sentence x runs between 12 and 3 [seconds]"), i.e. the fill must cover however much time remains, not "one statement max".

**Decision:** `FillerStatementSelector.Select` rewritten from take-N-best-fit to GREEDY GAP-COVERING: pick the best-fit statement for the remaining gap, subtract its estimated spoken seconds (word count at 2.5 wps — the range says where a statement FITS, the words say what it COSTS), repeat while meaningful gap remains, ceiling `maxStatements = 3` so filler tops up a bulletin and never becomes it. Callsite `maxCandidates: 1` overrides removed. `draft.md` rule 3 and both filler preambles reframed: the handed list is already sized to the gap — voice ALL of them, each exactly once ("work through it" alone still let the model stop at one). `SlotFitPlanner.ExpansionFeedback` now says "EVERY provided standing road fact not already in the script".

**Rationale:** The selector owns HOW MUCH filler (deterministic, gap-arithmetic); the writer owns only the phrasing. Handing the writer a pre-sized list and telling it to voice all of it removes the discretion the model kept exercising toward under-fill. The anti-repeat and enabled/gap-range eligibility filters are unchanged, and a covered slot still yields zero filler (the slot-full guard stays).

**Consequences:** Fresh-corpus replay: word counts moved from `[45,75,72,60,44,79,36,49,40,60]` (5 scripts under 20s) to `[66,75,82,59,71,75,66,65,56,81]` — every market 22–33s around the 30s target, zero fabrication flags, overshoot handled by the audio measure-then-trim path. Selector tests rewritten for the greedy contract (15 green: stop-when-covered, accumulate-until-covered, remaining-gap gates the next pick, ceiling cap); Domain suite 848 green. ARN note: on-air filler variety and coverage now depend directly on per-market library depth — 5 national sample statements produce visible repetition across markets in the eval; each market needs its own authored set (the admin CRUD already supports gap ranges per statement).

## 2026-07-02 — Suppressed Corridors Free Their Airtime to Good Runs; Filler Is Last Resort, Not First

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User review of the delivered 10-script set asked why a Large/Busy market (Sydney, 12 raw corridors) filled with generic road-safety filler. Root cause: BOTH fill-content deciders used the RAW corridor count — the same class of bug already fixed for the filler gap estimate. (1) The eval's `GoodRunPolicy.SelectForGeneration` call read 12 corridors as "slot full" and suppressed generic flowing roads entirely; (2) production's `BulletinContentSelector.Select` let tier-suppressed minors win rundown slots they never render, crowding every flowing road out of the slot ranking. The bulletin's real content had collapsed to 2 voiceable items (1 closure + 1 moderate; 9 minors correctly suppressed under the Major headline), leaving ~18s that skipped straight to generic filler — real, market-specific flowing roads sat unused. Also fixed three delivery nits: "X is a road hazard" label-as-predicate grammar (draft.md spoken-English rule extended), the fuel suburb voiced twice (FormatFuel renders a repeated suburb as "same suburb — say 'there too'"), and "It's a chance of a shower" (BFN-022's noun-phrase mappings flipped to frame-proof adjectives: Sprinkles→"showery", Drizzle→"drizzly").

**Decision:** Moved corridor tiering to Domain as `CorridorTiering` (single source of truth: caps, ClassifyByTier, SelectVoiceable/CountVoiceable; TrafficNarrativeSummarizer now delegates). Eval callsite passes `CountVoiceable` to GoodRunPolicy. `BulletinContentSelector.Select` keeps rundown selection EXACTLY as before (operator visibility: suppressed minors stay in the persisted rundown) but adds an airtime correction: slots consumed by corridors that will not render (selected − voiceable) backfill with the next-ranked flowing roads up to maxGoodRuns. Fill priority is now structural: incidents → flowing roads → filler statements — filler only covers what real content cannot.

**Rationale:** "Busy" is a property of what the bulletin VOICES, not what HERE returns. The label/raw-count divergence produced the worst editorial outcome — generic national facts over real market roads. Backfilling at the selector (not the renderer) keeps the operator's rundown intact while the writer's view gains real fill.

**Consequences:** Domain suite 853 green (new `SuppressedMinors_FreeTheirAirtimeToGoodRuns` contract test; selector rework preserves the prior corridor-selection contract after a first draft wrongly capped persisted corridors — caught by orchestrator boundary tests). Replay (deliver3): all 10 scripts now name real flowing roads before filler (Sydney: "Cumberland Highway and Macarthur Drive are moving freely" replacing one generic fact; filler counts dropped market-wide), 51–91 words ≈ 20–36s, zero fabrication. NOTE: full-solution verification pending — the tree carries concurrent in-flight edits (IDeliveryStyleRepository/IVoiceProfileRepository DeleteAsync without implementations) that block compile; Domain scope verified in isolation.

## 2026-07-02 — SWA Custom Auth Needs a rolesSource Bridge and Post-Link Easy Auth Reapply

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Test sign-in after the ARN Technology Lead's admin consent no longer stopped at Entra. Live `/.auth/me` showed the AAD token audience was the Test app registration (`e47e265d-…`) and carried `claims.roles = Admin`, but SWA `userRoles` still contained only `authenticated` and `anonymous`. `/api/jobs` reached `AuthorizationMiddleware` and returned our JSON 403 because the linked backend authorizes from `userRoles`, not directly from AAD app-role claims. Live Function App `authsettingsV2` also showed a post-linked-backend drift: AAD `clientId`/audience had been rewritten to `481184bc-…` instead of the pinned Test app ID.

**Decision:** Treat ARN role assignment and SWA role forwarding as separate layers. Keep the ARN Technology Lead/ARN responsible for app registrations, app roles, group/user membership, ID-token enablement, and admin consent. In our repo, configure SWA custom auth with `auth.rolesSource = "/api/GetRoles"` and add `RolesSourceHttpTrigger` to copy only known Arn app roles (`Operator`, `Admin`) from AAD token role claims into SWA custom `userRoles`. Exclude `/api/GetRoles` from Function App Easy Auth and from `AuthorizationMiddleware` so the SWA sign-in callback can call it before a caller has backend roles. Add `deployment/modules/function-authsettings.bicep` and run it after `linkedBackend` so the per-environment AAD audience is reapplied while preserving the `azureStaticWebApps` provider required for proxied `/api/*` calls.

**Rationale:** Asking the ARN Technology Lead to "set up roles" again would not fix the observed 403: the role was already in the token. SWA needs an explicit bridge from token claims to `userRoles`. Reapplying authsettings after backend linking makes the IaC idempotent and prevents direct bearer-token auth from silently targeting an unexpected app registration.

**Consequences:** Test/prod RBAC now has three verifiable gates: `/.auth/me.claims` proves Entra assignment, `/.auth/me.userRoles` proves SWA rolesSource mapping, and `/api/jobs` proves backend authorization. Deployment smoke for Test should include fresh logout/login because SWA role assignments are stamped at sign-in. If future app roles are added, they must be explicitly whitelisted in `RolesSourceHttpTrigger`; arbitrary AAD role strings are intentionally ignored.


## 2026-07-02 — Pipeline A/B Harness: Agentic Workflow Shapes Become Config, Not Code

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Session direction shifted from polishing the monolith prompt to questioning the architecture itself: the one draft call carries ~8 responsibilities (selection, ordering, budgeting, pairing, placement, filler policy, phrasing, length), and the iteration history shows every durable fix REMOVED a responsibility from the model. To trial alternative agentic shapes (plan-then-render, small-input stitch) honestly, we needed A/B runs against identical frozen data and identical deterministic gates — with a new approach being an authored config, never a code change.

**Decision:** Built the pipeline experiment harness in the eval layer (`test/.../Eval/Experiments/`): `PipelineConfig` (a `pipeline.json` per arm under `experiments/pipelines/<name>/`, stages: `production` | `plan` | `llm` | `render-items` | `smooth`), `RundownPlanner` (deterministic plan stage reusing the production selection machinery — CorridorTiering for voiceable, single-corridor TrafficNarrativeSummarizer for fact bundles, FillerStatementSelector against the plan's own word gap), `ExperimentLlm` (eval-only Responses client; production keeps one model callsite), `PipelineRunner` (stage interpreter with per-stage audit log and a deterministic fact-lock on the smooth stage: road names + numbers survive byte-identically or the polish is discarded), and `PipelineExperimentTests` (env-gated: `ARN_PIPELINE_EXPERIMENT=1`, filters `ARN_PIPELINE_ARMS`/`ARN_PIPELINE_SCENARIOS`, label `ARN_PIPELINE_LABEL`; writes `output/eval/pipeline-ab-<label>.md` with an aggregate table + per-scenario side-by-side). `BulletinEval` refactored: `BuildContextAsync`/`ScoreAsync` extracted so every arm sees the IDENTICAL context and gates. Scenario matrix extracted to `EvalScenarios` (shared with the frozen-fetch harness). Three shipped arms: `baseline` (production monolith), `stitch` (plan → one small stitching call), `rundown-items` (plan → per-item render with sliding context → fact-locked smooth).

**Rationale:** The frozen corpus + deterministic scorers already existed; the missing piece was pipeline shape as data. Interpreting configs in the eval layer keeps production untouched while the experiment loop (author arm → replay → compare pack) runs in minutes.

**Consequences:** First A/B (10 scenarios × 3 arms, frozen corpus): baseline 7/10, stitch 7/10, rundown-items 5/10 — and the pack surfaced three PLANNER defects the monolith's prose rules already encode (monitored route voiced against its own closed corridor; shared-condition roads cloned per road; filler gap heuristic starving the plan). Fixed structurally in the planner (same-road suppression, adjacent same-condition merge capped at 3, filler selected against the plan's own remaining word budget) + assembly capitalization; 7 deterministic harness unit tests pin them. Second A/B: **stitch 9/10, rundown-items 7/10 vs baseline 7/10** — the small-input stitch arm beat production on its first fixed iteration, supporting the "small input of sequential facts" hypothesis. Infra suite green (909 passed / 29 env-skipped), Domain 853 green. Known residue: rundown-items still shows run-to-run wobble (1 style flag from a lowercase assembly join, fixed after the run); smooth-stage fact-lock never rejected in 20 arm-runs. NOT yet a production migration — the harness is the instrument; promotion of a winning shape into BroadcastOrchestrator is a separate, deliberate step.

## 2026-07-02 — Fix SWA Deploy-Time Overwrite of Out-of-Band AAD App Settings via Key Vault getSecret()

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deploying the rolesSource fix to Test (`main.bicep` redeploy) silently wiped the SWA's `AAD_CLIENT_ID`/`AAD_CLIENT_SECRET` app settings, breaking `/.auth/login/aad` (404) until manually restored. Root cause: `static-web-app.bicep`'s `staticWebAppSettings` resource did a full property PUT with only `VITE_API_BASE_URL` — Bicep never knew about the AAD settings the ARN Technology Lead's app-registration handoff caused us to set out-of-band on 29 Jun, so every redeploy dropped them. First fix attempt (SWA system-assigned identity + `@Microsoft.KeyVault()` app-setting references, mirroring the Function App pattern) proved architecturally wrong: Static Web Apps is not on Key Vault's trusted-services list, and this SWA has no VNet integration, so its managed identity cannot resolve KV references against a `publicNetworkAccess=Disabled` vault — confirmed live (persistent 404 after the identity-based deploy, RBAC role granted, reference syntax correct).

**Decision:** Made `aadClientId`/`aadClientSecret` explicit Bicep parameters on `static-web-app.bicep` (empty by default — dev/sandbox unaffected). `main.bicep` resolves the secret once per deployment via the in-Bicep `keyVault.getSecret('AadClientSecret')` module-param function, gated behind a new `configureSwaAadKeyVaultSettings` bool (true only in test/prod bicepparams). This function is resolved by ARM's control-plane "Azure Resource Manager template deployment service" — a documented Key Vault trusted service specifically for passing secure values during deployment — so it bypasses `publicNetworkAccess=Disabled` regardless of the SWA's own network posture. Required the Key Vault's `enabledForTemplateDeployment=true` (a template-level flag independent of RBAC/network ACLs; set via `key-vault.bicep`), which this vault didn't have and had to be flipped once via CLI before the getSecret()-based deploy would succeed (the flag can't self-activate in the same deployment that first sets it — parameter binding resolves before any resource in the template applies).

**Rationale:** Static/runtime-identity Key Vault references only work for compute with a private network path to the vault (VNet integration, private endpoint, or trusted-service membership) — SWA has none of these. Deploy-time `getSecret()` sidesteps that entirely by resolving through ARM's own trusted control-plane call, matching the same mechanism `aadClientId`/`aadTenantId` already use via bicepparam values. This keeps the fix idempotent (every redeploy sets the identical value) without requiring new SWA networking.

**Consequences:** Verified live end-to-end after the corrected redeploy: SWA `AAD_CLIENT_ID`/`AAD_CLIENT_SECRET` app settings are plain values (not KV-reference strings) matching the Key Vault source; `/.auth/login/aad` returns 302; fresh logout/login round-trip on Test shows `/.auth/me.userRoles` includes `Admin`; `/api/jobs` returns 200. The SWA's system-assigned identity from the reverted attempt persisted (ARM incremental mode doesn't remove properties absent from a redeploy) but holds zero role assignments — inert, left as a known cosmetic leftover rather than spending further cycles forcing its removal via API. Any future SWA app setting sourced from Key Vault MUST use this `getSecret()`-at-deploy-time pattern, not a runtime `@Microsoft.KeyVault()` reference, unless SWA gains a private network path to the vault.

**Follow-up (2026-07-02, same day):** `getSecret()` resolves at ARM parameter-binding, *before* any resource deploys, so a greenfield deploy with the flag `true` fails (`KeyVaultParameterReferenceSecretRetrieveFailed`) when the vault/secret don't exist yet — verified in the compiled ARM: the module param is `if(configureSwaAadKeyVaultSettings, {reference:{keyVault…}}, {value:''})`, so `false` provably never touches Key Vault. Therefore **prod bring-up is two-phase**: `main.prod.bicepparam` ships `configureSwaAadKeyVaultSettings=false` (Phase 1: infra + KV secret seed), then flip to `true` and redeploy (Phase 2: idempotent steady state). Test keeps `true` because its vault + `AadClientSecret` pre-exist. `key-vault.bicep` now sets `enabledForTemplateDeployment=true` so a fresh vault is deploy-readable without the manual CLI flip Test's pre-existing vault needed. Rotation caveat: the SWA setting is a plain deploy-time copy (not a live KV ref), so a rotated secret is stale until the next `getSecret()` redeploy — both runbooks are in `deployment/README.md` ("Production SWA auth bring-up", "Rotating the SWA AAD client secret").


## 2026-07-02 — Pipeline A/B Campaign: `stitch-bo3` (Plan Then Best-of-3) Beats Production 10/10 vs 7/10

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** With the config-driven pipeline harness in place (previous entry), asked to actually trial agentic approaches, not just build the tool: author arms, iterate on my own inference, converge on a champion. Added two general-purpose stage kinds (`best-of`: N parallel samples, deterministic pick; `revise`: detector-grounded single-shot self-correction) and authored four hypothesis arms alongside the existing `stitch`/`rundown-items`/`baseline`.

**Decision:** Ran a 4-iteration campaign (`iter1`-`iter4`, full 10-scenario matrix, live LLM/frozen HERE data each time), fixing what each pack surfaced before re-running:
- **iter1** found `best-of`'s pick-score was blind to 8 of the 9 production detectors (roll-call, duplicate-anchor, meta-leak, type/impact-stack, fake-location, sentence-clone, unselected-source) — it only checked fabrication/sanity/style/underfill, so best-of could pick a candidate revise's own `DetectIssues` would flag. Unified: `PickScore` now IS `DetectIssues(...).Count` (×1000) + word-distance tie-break, giving best-of and revise ONE shared definition of quality.
- **iter1** also found a planner wording bug: the flow item's embedded instruction ("never read... a list") got echoed back as "the rest of the **listed** roads" — reworded to avoid the trigger word.
- **iter2/3** read-through found the weather condition mapping (`ContentFormatters.NaturalWeatherPhrasing`, BFN-022) was only half-converted to frame-proof adjectives (2 of 13 entries) — the SAME source condition rendered "There's some cloud around" (grammatical) in one script and "It's some cloud around" (broken) in another, proven live in-pack. Converted all remaining entries to bare adjectives (`cloudy`, `clear`, `hazy`, `foggy`, `misty`, `dusty`, `smoky`, `snowy`, `partly cloudy`) — this is a production `src/` fix, not harness-only.
- **iter3/4** traced a "1 lingering issue" pattern in `stitch-bo3`'s own best-of samples (all 3 candidates for a scenario scoring 1000+) to a genuine **pre-existing production bug** in `RollCallDetector`: Rule A's "clear road" vocabulary was `GoodRunRoads.Concat(FlowPool...)` — FlowPool is the raw 18-road pre-selection candidate universe, not what the writer was actually offered as clear. A road that existed only in FlowPool (an incident's own cross-street, or a commuter-route road) got miscounted as evidence of a clear-road roll-call purely by name coincidence. Fixed to `GoodRunRoads` only, matching the same "voiceable/selected, not raw" principle already established for `CorridorTiering`/`GoodRunPolicy`/filler-gap this session; regression test added (`Ignores_flow_pool_roads_never_offered_as_clear`).
- Compared 4 arms across the stability runs: **`stitch-bo3`** (plan → best-of-3) and **`stitch-full`** (best-of-3 → revise) both held 10/10 across iter2-4; **`stitch`** (single sample) swung 8-9/10; **`stitch-revise`** (single sample → conditional revise) swung 8-10/10. Auditing revise's actual fix rate across all 40 arm-runs: 3 successes total, **0 in the last 30** — every recent invocation was either "clean, skipped" or "REJECTED, couldn't improve, original kept". Revise's apparent 10/10 runs were the luck of an already-clean single sample, not correction working. `stitch-full` is therefore dominated by `stitch-bo3`: identical quality, one strictly unnecessary extra LLM call.
- **Final showdown** (`stitch-bo3` vs production `baseline`, same fixes applied to both): baseline **7/10** (3 underfill), `stitch-bo3` **10/10** (zero underfill), avg 78 words vs baseline's 72.
- Removed `stitch-revise` and `stitch-full` (proven losers per the harness's own "delete losers" rule); `experiments/pipelines/README.md` names `stitch-bo3` as champion and documents why the other two were killed.

**Rationale:** The campaign's own instrumentation (best-of's per-candidate penalty log) is what surfaced the RollCallDetector bug — candidates scoring 1000+ across MULTIPLE independent samples of the same data pointed at a shared, deterministic, data-scope defect rather than model variance. This is the payoff of grounding "quality" in the SAME detector suite production already trusts: a defect the eval finds is a defect production has too, and vice versa. Single-shot generation (plain `stitch`) is not a reliable production path — the residual defect rate is sampling variance, and revise (grounded, but single-shot) doesn't reliably resolve it in practice; only generate-and-select converts variance into consistency.

**Consequences:** `stitch-bo3` is the evidence-backed recommended default for this quality style, not yet wired into `BroadcastOrchestrator` (deliberately — a production migration is a separate, explicit step per the harness's own scope boundary). Two production `src/` bugs fixed as a direct result of the broader scenario coverage this campaign exercised: `ContentFormatters.NaturalWeatherPhrasing` (frame-ambiguous noun phrases) and `RollCallDetector` (FlowPool-scoped false positive) — both affect the LIVE review-refine loop, independent of this experiment harness. Full suite green: Infra 911/29-skipped, Domain 854, Application 379. `experiments/pipelines/` now holds 4 arms (`baseline`, `stitch`, `stitch-bo3`, `rundown-items`); `revise` stage kind remains implemented and documented but unused by any shipped arm pending a stronger correction design (e.g., feeding the revise call MORE targeted per-issue context, or multi-attempt revise with its own best-of selection).

## 2026-07-02 — ATN-Quality Convergence Loop: Corpus Discipline Becomes Data-Layer Contract; Two More Detector Bugs Fixed

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User challenged the generated sweep phrases ("the rest of the main runs are clear") as information-free airtime; manual analysis of all three ATN corpora (12 metro + 9 regional + 62 Dribble reads) confirmed the phrase appears NOWHERE — ATN clear-claims are anchored to named roads, market-wide sweeps exist only in genuinely quiet markets as the evidenced headline (Darwin names five clear roads), and busy reads simply stop. The old good-runs data block MANDATED the vague sweep. Directed to iterate — ground, generate, critique, rewrite — until consistently ATN quality.

**Decision:** Ran a 7-iteration convergence loop (atn1–atn7) on `stitch-bo3` over frozen data, with a 10-agent independent `atn-reviewer` batch (script + exact source data, no self-critique leakage) at atn4. Changes, in causal order:
- **Corpus discipline into the data layer:** `FormatGoodRuns` is now density-aware (busy ≥3 voiceable: ≤2 names as ONE grouped clause, no residual claims; quiet: up to 4-5 names, the names ARE the story; all-clear: market-wide headline + names as evidence). `RundownPlanner` mirrors the same bands, merges same-state commuter routes ("the West Gate and the Monash are both running to time" — the user's original complaint), splits ≥4 clear roads into two Darwin-shaped groups, and formats names via `ToSpeakable` (atn6 leaked "BOUNDARY ROAD" verbatim). `draft.md` sweep mandate replaced with the named-claim rule.
- **Three more production bugs found by the loop:** (1) `RollCallDetector` Rule A cap now mirrors the data's density bands (a flat cap of 4 false-flagged the exact quiet reads the data mandates — atn1, 4 markets) and is role-aware (a pool road mentioned only as an incident's extent anchor is not a clear-run claim — atn6, Gold Coast, every candidate false-flagged); (2) `DuplicateAnchorDetector` no longer counts a match that is the tail of a longer compound proper name ("Coast Highway" inside "Gold Coast Highway" — atn2, the data's own extent text); (3) `BulletinDataComposer`'s filler header said "may voice ONE" while the gap-covering selection hands 2-3 statements — the independent reviewers correctly flagged 9/10 scripts against the stale contract text.
- **Independent review consensus (atn4: 5 borderline / 5 send-back) drove the last mile:** PSA stacks (9/10 flagged) fixed STRUCTURALLY — the planner now interleaves standing facts between real items (telling the writer to reorder contradicted "voice items in order"; ordering is the planner's job), capped 2 (3 thin), at most one at the close; commuter delay bands now mirror `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` exactly (my looser band UPGRADED "only a touch slow" to "running to time" on air — a genuine fidelity drift the reviewers caught in 2 markets); causes voiced over labels ("has roadworks", never "has a road hazard"); works-lists compressed ("with detours in place", never the data's "closures, speed reductions and detours" recitation); weather as presenter tag; light connectors (Also/Meanwhile/Elsewhere) recognised as corpus house style, not fluff; facts-based item budgets (a bare minor closure is ~5 honest words, not a flat 15 — ended Newcastle's recurring underfill).

**Rationale:** Every durable fix again REMOVED a decision from the model — ordering (interleave), grouping (merge/split), naming (ToSpeakable), status bands (mirror production) all moved into the deterministic planner; the prompt carries only realization rules quoted from the corpus. The independent reviewer batch caught what self-review missed (fidelity drift, contract contradiction) — worth the cost at convergence gates, not per-iteration.

**Consequences:** atn6 + atn7 both 10/10 would-air, zero underfill, zero fabrication, no systematic penalties (one 1021 candidate in 30 = sampling noise best-of absorbed). Scripts now: merged same-state pairs, preserved caveats, spaced reminders ending on exactly one, Darwin-shaped quiet reads, zero vague sweeps. Suites green: Domain 858, Infra 911/29-skipped, Application 379. Regression tests pin all three detector fixes. Known residue: filler variety still limited by the 5-statement eval library (per-market depth remains ARN's content task); `stitch-bo3` remains eval-side — production promotion is still the separate, explicit step.

## 2026-07-02 — Standing Facts Trail the Read (Product-Owner Reversal of the atn5 Interleave)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The atn5-7 planner interleaved standing facts between real items to break up the 3-PSA stacks the independent review flagged. Product owner review of the converged batch caught the cost: Sydney read a reminder mid-bulletin then RETURNED to clear roads — and no ATN read in any of the three corpora resumes traffic after a safety line; ARN's own meeting notes place filler "after a generated bulletin".

**Decision:** Fillers trail all real content (traffic → weather/fuel → reminders, in order, concluding on a filler). `RundownPlanner` appends them; `BulletinDataComposer` header and `stitch.md` state the trailing contract ("never return to a road item after them"). Count caps (2, 3 thin) stay as the stack guard.

**Rationale:** Forward progression is the corpus rule; the PSA-stack pressure is a library-depth problem (5 national samples), not an ordering problem — per-market authored filler sets remain the real fix (already on ARN's content-task list).

**Consequences:** atn8: 10/10 would-air, zero underfill/fabrication, every read concludes on a reminder with the traffic story intact (Sydney: closure → standstills → M4 → clear pair → two reminders). Known accepted residue: thin markets (Scottsdale, Newcastle) still close on 2-3 consecutive reminders until per-market libraries deepen. Minor nit spotted (Newcastle "is under a road closure" — label-echo phrasing) — the known missing "label-as-predicate" detector class, candidate for a future gate.

## 2026-07-02 — Style Rules Become an ARN-Editable Versioned Library; draft.md Voicing Moves to Data

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Engineering had spent weeks hand-tuning the bulletin writer's editorial rules — the six static `## Voicing` bullets plus the "Finish on a complete sentence…" line in `prompts/draft.md`. ARN's content people know radio better than engineering and need to own this layer without a code deploy per wording tweak.

**Decision:** Surfaced the Voicing rules as a versioned, global "Style Rules" library. Domain: `StyleRule`/`StyleRuleSet` aggregate (append-only versions, `Create`/`ApplyEdit`/`RestoreVersion`/`Reconstitute`, mirrors `DeliveryStyle`) plus `StyleRuleDefaults` — the 7 rules copied verbatim from the pre-change `draft.md`, rendered whenever no set is published (fresh environments, storage outage, or every rule disabled) so nothing needs a seeding migration. Persistence: `TableStorageStyleRulesRepository`, single `PartitionKey="StyleRules"`/`RowKey="global"` row, JSON-serialised versions column. Orchestrator: `BroadcastOrchestrator` fetches the published set in the same parallel `EnrichWithMarketContentAsync` fan-out as guidance/filler statements; `LlmScriptGenerator.RenderStyleRules` renders the effective (enabled, defaults-on-empty) list and `draft.md`'s six static bullets became a single `{{{styleRules}}}` render line (the trailing "Finish on a complete sentence" bullet is now `sr-default-7`; its `{{/if}}` closer for `varietyAngle` was preserved). Application: `StyleRulesService` (Get materialises an unsaved "v0 = defaults, unpublished" sentinel; Update/Restore mint through the aggregate) plus a **draft-pass-only, non-persisting preview** (`PreviewAsync`) that runs the real `IScriptGenerator` twice — published rules vs. the editor's unsaved rules — over two embedded canned scenarios ("busy"/"quiet"), mirroring the `VoiceProfilesHttpTrigger`/`DeliveryStylesHttpTrigger` preview precedent. `StyleRulesHttpTrigger` exposes 5 routes (`GET`/`PUT /style-rules`, `GET/POST .../versions/{v}[/restore]`, `POST /style-rules/preview`); no `RouteRoleMatrix` change needed (GET already Operator, non-GET already Admin). Web: a sixth "Style rules" tab in the Bulletin-rules hub (`GuidancePage`) — ordered rule rows (Textarea + example input + enabled switch + reorder/delete), version history with restore, the preview dialog, and JSON export/import for promoting a tuned set dev→test→prod (separate storage accounts per environment).

**Rationale:** Global-only scope (not per-market/per-station) because per-market steering already exists via the Guidance system (`<guidance>`/`<house-style>`, scope precedence station > market > global) — a second per-market style mechanism would duplicate it. The embedded-defaults fallback (not a migration) guarantees every environment — including a brand-new one — renders byte-identical output to the pre-change static prompt until ARN explicitly publishes a change; pinned by a literal fallback-parity test (`RenderStyleRules([])` equals the pre-change six-bullets-plus-finish block verbatim). Preview stays draft-pass-only on canned data (no review/refine, no job persisted) so an editor gets a fast, controlled A/B without HERE credentials or side effects.

**Consequences:** `prompts/system.md`, `review.md`, `refine.md` remain code-owned (safety contract, gate loop, mechanical refine) — only the draft pass's Voicing block is ARN-editable. Job-record provenance is logged only (`StyleRulesVersion` in the `[ScriptGen] Invoking direct model call` log line), not persisted on the job entity — a follow-up if audit ever needs it. Suites green: Domain 878 (+`StyleRuleSetTests`, 14), Application 390 (+`StyleRulesServiceTests`, 11), Infrastructure (+`RenderStyleRulesTests`, 4, including the fallback-parity pin); web build/lint/`vitest run` (496 passed) and a mock-mode smoke test (7 seeded default rules render in the new tab) all green.

## 2026-07-02 — Ambiguous-Roads Curated List Removed; Suburb Retention Now an Automatic Deterministic Gate

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** WALK3-002's curated per-market `AmbiguousRoad` list added no data availability — HERE's traffic feed carries zero locality data, so every incident is reverse-geocoded regardless, and `CorridorAggregator.ExtractSuburb`/`TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` already populate `TrafficCorridor.Suburb` and append `" near {suburb}"` to the source bullet unconditionally, for every corridor, whenever geocoding succeeds. The list's only real function was forcing the model not to drop a suburb it was already given, for the specific roads an admin pre-flagged. After go-live, 10 of 11 markets had an empty list and the eleventh held one test-junk entry — near-zero real adoption. Worse, the `[MUST NAME SUBURB]` flag could fire on a curated road with no suburb data behind it at all, a directive the writer could not satisfy.

**Decision:** Removed the curated list end to end — `AmbiguousRoad`, `IAmbiguousRoadsRepository`, `TableStorageAmbiguousRoadsRepository`, `AmbiguousRoadsHttpTrigger`, the `AmbiguousRoadNames` context property, the `[MUST NAME SUBURB]` flag/threading through `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer`, and the web `AmbiguousRoadsManager` tab. Replaced it with `SuburbRetentionDetector` (`src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Services/SuburbRetentionDetector.cs`), a deterministic gate mirroring `RollCallDetector`/`MetaLeakDetector`'s shape: it checks every corridor with a resolved `Suburb` against the final script, flags any road named without its suburb, and mechanically re-inserts `" near {Suburb}"` after the road's first mention if the retry budget exhausts. Wired into all three places `BroadcastOrchestrator` runs its deterministic gates — the main review-refine loop, the loop's post-exhaustion mechanical-repair pass, and `FinalizeExpandedScript`'s word-target expansion re-check.

**Rationale:** Enforcing retention in code, for every road with resolved suburb data, covers the whole market automatically — no admin has to identify "ambiguous" roads up front, and there is no empty-list gap. The gate only fires when suburb data genuinely exists (`corridor.Suburb.HasValue`), closing the vacuous-directive bug the old flag had. Detect→conditional-Repair→re-Detect mirrors the codebase's established mechanical-fix pattern for a defect class no prior detector covered (an ADDITIVE repair — every earlier repairable detector strips or collapses text; this one inserts).

**Consequences:** Removed: `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Models/AmbiguousRoad.cs`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Interfaces/IAmbiguousRoadsRepository.cs`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure/Persistence/TableStorageAmbiguousRoadsRepository.cs`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Functions/AmbiguousRoadsHttpTrigger.cs`, their test files, `web/src/features/schedules/api/ambiguous-roads-hooks.ts`, `web/src/features/schedules/components/AmbiguousRoadsManager.tsx`. Modified: `OperatorContracts.cs` (DTOs dropped), `BroadcastContext.cs` (`AmbiguousRoadNames` property dropped), `DependencyInjection.cs` (DI registration dropped), `BroadcastOrchestrator.cs` (old wiring removed, `SuburbRetentionDetector` wired into all three gate points), `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.cs` (`ambiguousRoadNames` parameter/flag removed from `Summarize`/`AppendCorridorBullets`/`AppendTierBullets`/`AppendCuratedCorridorBullets`/`AppendCorridorBullet`/`AppendCondensedCorridorBullet`), `paths.ts`/`mock/adapter.ts`/`mock/store.ts`/`GuidancePage.tsx` (frontend wiring and Guidance tab dropped — 5 tabs remain: Editorial guidance, Banned words, Priority roads, Filler statements, Style rules). New: `SuburbRetentionDetector.cs` + `SuburbRetentionDetectorTests.cs` (8 cases, incl. an empty-road-name crash-guard regression). Verified: full backend suites green (Domain 886, Application 390, Infrastructure 905/29-skipped, Functions 209); web `tsc -b`/`eslint`/`vite build`/`vitest run` (496 passed) all green; `grep -ri "ambiguousroad" src/ test/ web/src` zero matches.

## 2026-07-02 — Config-bundle export/import with dry-run diff and prod two-person approval

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN wants to use AI assistants (not just the UI) to create and edit platform configuration: stations/bulletin rules, voices, delivery styles, pronunciation dictionaries, style rules, guidance, safety terms, priority roads, filler statements. Per-entity CSV buttons would scatter the surface and lose cross-entity context (schedules reference library ids), and AI output is untrusted by definition, so a review gate is required before anything applies.

**Decision:** One admin-only config-transfer surface: GET /api/config/export returns ALL editable config as a single PascalCase JSON bundle (current state only, import-shaped, sections filterable); GET /api/config/schema serves a hand-authored JSON Schema documenting every constraint (the AI's instruction manual); POST /api/config/import is DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT and returns a per-entity diff report (Create/Update/Unchanged/Error), applying only with ?dryRun=false. Imports are upsert-only (never delete), all-or-nothing on validation errors, apply in dependency order (libraries before schedules), preserve incoming ids on create for idempotent re-imports, and validate schedule references against existing + bundle-created ids. In prod (ConfigImport__RequireSecondApprover=true, main.prod.bicepparam) an apply parks the bundle as a pending import in the config-imports blob container; a DIFFERENT admin (AAD object id compared) must approve, approval re-plans against current state (409 on drift), and resolved envelopes are archived as approval evidence. Versioned libraries mint new versions through the ordinary service paths, so every import is restorable; unchanged entities are skipped entirely (no ElevenLabs round-trips). Frontend: admin 'Data transfer' page (/config-transfer) with export, dry-run report, apply, and pending-approvals cards.

**Rationale:** A single bundle gives the AI cross-entity context and doubles as environment backup/promotion; the dry-run report is the human review gate that makes AI-edited config safe for non-engineers; reusing the existing command/service validation paths means no second validation convention; the two-person prod posture mirrors the accepted two-gate production deploy approval; blob (not table) storage for pending envelopes avoids the 64KB property cap and keeps an evidence trail.

**Consequences:** Operators/jobs/raw ElevenLabs voices are deliberately excluded (identity, runtime data, external catalogue). Guidance export enumerates scopes from current schedules, so guidance for deleted markets is not exported. Changing a safety term's kind/scope via import is rejected (delete and recreate in the UI). Deletion never happens via import. The JSON Schema is hand-maintained and must be updated when bundle contracts change.

## 2026-07-03 — Poison-queue failures go through the Job state machine; terminal jobs are never clobbered

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Both poison-queue triggers (BroadcastPoisonQueueTrigger, RegenerationPoisonQueueTrigger) set job.Status = JobStatus.Failed by direct property mutation, bypassing Job.MarkFailed(). The job record lost its ErrorMessage, FailedAtStatus, and the StatusHistory audit entry (the approval/compliance trail), and a stale poison message could overwrite an already-terminal (e.g. Published) job. Found in the 2026-07-02 hardening engagement; proven by four failing regression tests before the fix.

**Decision:** Poison triggers call Job.MarkFailed(error, utcNow) and save only when it succeeds. A terminal job is left untouched (logged + alert still sent). This is the invariant for ALL future failure paths: job failure is recorded via MarkFailed, never by assigning Status directly (the Create factory is the one legitimate direct assignment).

**Rationale:** MarkFailed carries the audit side effects (FailedAtStatus, ErrorMessage, StatusHistory entry) and the terminal-state guard; the approver/audit trail is ARN's publication-liability evidence, so gaps in StatusHistory are compliance defects, not cosmetics.

**Consequences:** Poison-queue jobs now surface WHY they failed in the console and audit export. Regression tests: BroadcastPoisonQueueTriggerTests + RegenerationPoisonQueueTriggerTests (RecordsFailureThroughStateMachine, TerminalJob_IsLeftUntouchedButStillAlerts). Grep 'Status = JobStatus.' finds any future bypass.

## 2026-07-03 — Time-stretch streams SoundTouch in put/drain chunks — never one-shot PutSamples

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** WavDurationProcessor.TimeStretchToTarget fed the whole take to SoundTouch in a single PutSamples call and then drained in 4096-frame reads. SoundTouch's internal FIFO drain is quadratic in the buffered tail, so a 33s mono take cost 1.76s wall time and 3.2GB of allocations per bulletin — on the per-bulletin hot path since the 2026-06-26 grow-then-compress policy applies the stretch to essentially every take.

**Decision:** Stream the input in 4096-frame put/drain cycles (drain ReceiveSamples between puts, then Flush and drain the residue). Measured on the same 33s take: 1.76s / 3235MB per call before, 0.26-0.28s / 18.4MB after (6.4x faster, 175x fewer allocations), byte-identical output. Future SoundTouch usage MUST keep the streaming shape.

**Rationale:** Byte-identical output at a 6.4x wall-time and 175x allocation improvement on a per-bulletin path is a pure win; the benchmark (dotnet file-based app driving AdjustSpeed on a synthetic WAV) is repeatable and documented in the code comment.

**Consequences:** Per-bulletin stretch cost drops from ~1.8s to ~0.3s on the Functions worker. The rationale comment in TimeStretchToTarget carries the measurement; regressing to one-shot PutSamples would silently reintroduce the quadratic drain.

## 2026-07-02 — Surface HERE direction, lane state, closure, and freshness on the adjust-page incident rows

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Prior investigation of the HERE API capability surface found TrafficIncident already computes Direction, Summary (lane state), and Comment (road-authority free text) from HERE's incident response, and HereIncidentDetails already parses Criticality — but IncidentMappingExtensions.ToJobIncident silently dropped Direction/Summary/Comment before JobIncidentDto reached the UI, so the adjust page's rundown table (RundownTable.tsx IncidentDetailRow) showed only headline + detail. HERE also returns roadClosed (bool) and entryTime per incident, neither previously parsed. The existing staleness field (HereIncidentDetails.LastUpdateTime -> TrafficIncident.DataTimestampUtc, added for the traffic-data-staleness feature) is empirically always null against real HERE responses: lastUpdateTime never appears anywhere in the captured test/corpus/here/**/traffic-incidents/*.json fixtures across all 6 markets, so it cannot serve as a per-incident freshness signal.

**Decision:** Add RoadClosed (bool) and EntryTimeUtc (DateTimeOffset?, from HERE's entryTime) to HereIncidentDetails and TrafficIncident. Stop dropping Direction/Summary/Comment in ToJobIncident; rename Summary to LaneDetail on JobIncident/JobIncidentDto for clarity.
