Thread Direction, LaneDetail, Comment, RoadClosed, EntryTimeUtc through JobIncident -> JobIncidentDto -> web JobIncident type (all optional, backward-compatible trailing record params). In RundownTable's IncidentDetailRow, render three tiers only when data is present: (1) an inline 'closed' tag (destructive color, reusing the existing new/not-mentioned tag vocabulary) beside the headline when RoadClosed; (2) a synthesized context line (direction, then laneDetail or comment as fallback, joined with a middle dot) below the existing detail line, via a new incidentContextLine helper in incident-labels.ts; (3) a Clock-icon Tooltip showing 'Reported X ago' (date-fns formatRelativeTime) when EntryTimeUtc is present. JunctionTraversability and SegmentRefs stay unsurfaced: corpus samples showed low differentiating value (near-constant enum value) and decoding risk outweighs the benefit. ReviewContextLens (the separate evidence-index surface) and mock fixtures (live-traffic.ts/fixtures.ts) were intentionally left unchanged -- scope was the adjust page only.

**Rationale:** 4 of the 5 surfaced fields (Direction, LaneDetail, Comment, and the RoadClosed/EntryTimeUtc pairing aside) required zero new HERE parsing for the first three -- they were already computed on TrafficIncident from a request already being made and simply discarded downstream, making this a plumbing fix rather than new integration work. RoadClosed/EntryTimeUtc are new but cheap: same HERE request, no extra API calls, trivial JSON fields already present in every captured incident. Progressive disclosure (tier 1 always-visible vs tier 2 hover-only) keeps the dense rundown table from bloating across dozens of incidents: only facts that materially change the include/mention decision (closure, direction, reason) get permanent row space; supplementary verification detail (exact report time) stays behind a hover affordance, following the codebase's existing Tooltip idiom (AudioWaveformPlayer.tsx, JobActions.tsx) and its existing inline-tag vocabulary (new/not-mentioned pills) rather than introducing new visual language.

**Consequences:** JobIncidentDto and the web JobIncident type each grow 5 optional fields; old cached jobs and Table Storage blobs missing them deserialize to the documented defaults (false/null), no migration needed. Existing mock fixtures (live-traffic.ts, fixtures.ts) predate this schema and will not populate the new UI elements until backfilled -- not done in this pass, cosmetic/out of scope. Verified: full backend suite green (2436 tests, incl. 5 new across HereTrafficProviderTests/IncidentMappingExtensionsTests/JobMappingExtensionsTests), full frontend suite green (157 tests incl. 17 new across incident-labels.test.ts/RundownTable.test.tsx), tsc -b clean, vite build clean.

## 2026-07-03 — Recover a real road name from the description when HERE's geocode resolves to a non-speakable link code

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Live bug found on deployed dev while reviewing the new incident-field UI (job e1438b0f..., Melbourne market): a congestion incident's HERE reverse-geocode resolved Location to 'W5', an internal freeway link code (not a real street name). CorridorAggregator.ExtractRoadKey's description-recovery path (added for the RISK-32 family of fixes) was gated on the incident's Location being the LITERAL sentinel string 'Unidentified Road'/'Unknown Location', but by the time ExtractRoadKey ran, HereGeocodingProvider's reverse-geocode had already overwritten Location with 'W5' -- a resolved-but-unspeakable value, not the raw placeholder -- so the gate never fired even though the incident's own Description ('At Todd Road / Cook Street - Backed-up traffic...') carried a perfectly good, speakable road name. The corridor rendered on air and in the UI as the generic 'an unnamed road', with no suburb fallback either (HereGeocodingProvider.PreferNamedStreet keeps the bare 'W5' street field over the full label because it technically contains a letter, discarding the suburb the full label would have carried).

**Decision:** Broaden ExtractRoadKey's description-recovery gate from the literal placeholder-string check to IsPlaceholderRoadName(roadName) (already-existing helper: empty, Unknown-prefixed, literal sentinel, no letters, OR fails IsSpeakableRoadName's route-code check) evaluated AFTER the comma-split location fallback has run, so it reflects the best-effort location-derived name including cases like 'W5'. Reordered the comma-split fallback to run before the recovery gate so roadName is fully resolved before the placeholder check. The recovered description text is itself validated with the same IsPlaceholderRoadName check before being accepted, keeping the existing 'never blend Between X and Y cross-streets' guard (via AtAnchorRegex requiring an At/Ramp-to anchor) intact. Did not touch HereGeocodingProvider.PreferNamedStreet's separate 'any letter counts as a real street' heuristic -- that is a related but distinct gap (it discards the suburb-bearing full label prematurely) left for a follow-up since this fix already resolves the reported symptom by recovering a real road name directly, making the suburb fallback moot for this case.

**Rationale:** Same fix shape as RISK-32 (GenericRoadRegex multi-word truncation): a description-recovery mechanism already existed and was proven correct, it was just gated too narrowly. Reusing IsPlaceholderRoadName (rather than inventing a new check) keeps exactly one definition of 'is this road name good enough to voice' shared between the gate and the final placeholder fallback, so the two can never drift out of sync.

**Consequences:** Congestion/incident corridors whose HERE geocode resolves to an internal route/link code (W5-style) but whose description carries an At/Ramp-to anchor now surface the real road name instead of the generic 'an unnamed road' or an Unknown-{id} placeholder, both on air and in the UI. Verified: full backend suite green (2438 tests, incl. 2 new in CorridorAggregatorTests reproducing the exact live W5/Todd Road case and confirming the gate still requires an At/Ramp-to anchor). Not fixed: HereGeocodingProvider.PreferNamedStreet's suburb-discarding heuristic for the general case where a non-speakable geocode has no description anchor either -- tracked as a follow-up, not blocking.

## 2026-07-03 — Config-transfer import diff must compare CANONICALIZED coverage, not raw persisted fields

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User reported that exporting the full config bundle from `/config-transfer` and immediately re-importing it (no edits) reported 4 false `Update`s (Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast, Perth) with "No field-level differences" shown in the review UI — a contradictory state. Root-caused live against dev: `MarketSchedule.Coverage`'s `Latitude`/`Longitude`/`RadiusKm` are DERIVED-only fields for bbox/corridor/polygon shapes (the source of truth is the corners/points; centre+radius are computed from them in `CoverageArea.CreateBoundingBox`/`CreateCorridor`/`CreatePolygon`). Those four schedules' persisted rows carried stale/rounded derived values (e.g. Adelaide `RadiusKm: 32.5` vs the current formula's `32.52694853151731`) from an earlier import or hand-edit, while the polygon points themselves were untouched. `ConfigImportService.PlanSchedulesAsync` reparsed the coverage on every import via `CoverageMapping.ToDomain` (which recomputes the derived fields fresh) and compared the resulting DTO byte-for-byte against the stale persisted DTO — so recomputation noise on unrelated fields was misreported as a real config change. Separately, the frontend `ImportReviewTabs` diffs the raw uploaded JSON against a freshly re-exported bundle, which are identical for an immediate re-import — hence the reviewer saw `Update` from the backend but zero field diffs in the UI.

**Decision:** Added `CoverageArea.Canonicalize()` (`src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Models/MarketSchedule.cs`) which recomputes `Latitude`/`Longitude`/`RadiusKm` from the shape's source geometry (bbox corners / corridor points+radius / polygon points) using the same formulas as the `Create*` factories; circle shapes pass through unchanged since their Lat/Lng/RadiusKm ARE the source geometry. `ConfigImportService.PlanSchedulesAsync` now canonicalizes coverage on BOTH the existing and updated schedule before the `Unchanged`-vs-`Update` JSON comparison, so derived-field drift (past or future) never reads as a config change. Actual shape edits (different points/corners) still correctly report `Update`.

**Rationale:** The bug is a comparison-semantics defect, not bad data: any future formula tweak, hand-edit, or import from an older code version would reproduce the same false positive for whatever schedules happen to carry stale derived values. Canonicalizing at the comparison boundary fixes it structurally instead of one-time-patching the four affected rows (which would immediately regress on the next drift). `VoiceRotationMapping` was checked for the same risk and found clean — it round-trips authored data with no recomputation.

**Consequences:** Config-transfer import dry-run is now reliably idempotent: exporting then immediately re-importing an unedited bundle reports 0 Updates (was 4). Verified live on dev: pre-fix dry-run showed `Updates: 4` (adelaide/brisbane/goldcoast/perth) with 0 field-level UI diffs; post-fix (Functions code-only redeploy) two consecutive export→import dry-runs both report `Creates: 0, Updates: 0, Unchanged: 72, Errors: 0`. New regression coverage: `CoverageAreaTests.Canonicalize_*` (4 tests, one per shape) and `ConfigImportServiceTests.PlanAsync_SchedulePolygonCoverageWithStaleDerivedFields_ReportsUnchanged`. Full non-integration backend suite green (Domain 910, Functions 233 incl. the new test, Application 393, ExternalSmoke 3) excluding a pre-existing, unrelated in-progress `AudioPipelineService`/`SpeechDurationOptions` WIP change already failing one test before this fix — that WIP was excluded from this deploy (scoped `git stash` around the two files for the publish step only, restored immediately after) and is untouched/unresolved by this decision.

## 2026-07-03 — ElevenLabs v2 unwanted-pause control: reroll/detector REJECTED; optimal = Stability + explicit break placement

**Status:** accepted (direction); no code shipped

**Context:** ARN operator reported "weird pause[s] in weird spots" on a Melbourne bulletin (job f95b6ed986d1486bb185d87de85430ec, voice 'ARN Sarah - Older Female', eleven_multilingual_v2, Stability 0.45, Style 0.15). Root-caused via the character-level TTS alignment already captured for word-timing: two mid-clause gaps on BARE words with no punctuation cue — after "ramp" (0.24s) and after "construction" (0.32s). NOT caused by SentencePauseInsertionDurationAdjustmentStrategy (underrun-only; this job overran and was compressed). A first pass built a PauseAnomalyDetector + synthesis-reroll; the user REJECTED it as too fragile ("we should not just have a pause detector" — some pauses are intentional, e.g. after a sentence) and asked for a researched, control-based solution. Reverted before any deploy.

**Decision:** Do NOT detect-and-reroll. Control pauses at the source using ElevenLabs' actual surface (researched via official docs + a live A/B on the real voice/model, 2026-07-03): **(1) raise the voice profile's Stability** (0.45 → ~0.70-0.75) to constrain the model's random breath insertion — the ElevenLabs-documented fix for exactly this symptom, and an ARN-owned Voice-Studio setting (no code). **(2) place INTENDED pauses deterministically with `<break time="x.xs" />`** — officially supported on all models except v3 (incl. eleven_multilingual_v2), renders exactly (measured 0.39-0.44s for a 0.35s tag), unlike stochastic model breaths. **(3)** the residual "ramp→to" hotspot is text-structural (stacked prepositional phrase "on the ramp to the M80…") — addressable only by rephrasing via Guidance/Style Rules, not any API knob. The comma the operator separately flagged ("Boundary Road, with moderate delays") is a script-phrasing issue, same Guidance/Style-Rules lever.

**Rationale:** There is NO API lever that suppresses a specific model-invented pause on v2 — only levers that (a) constrain the model (Stability/Style) or (b) place intended pauses (`<break>`/punctuation). A reroll fights a stochastic symptom: a live A/B (the operator's exact script, 3 seeds × 4 stability levels + break variants) showed rerolling at fixed settings barely moves the distribution, whereas Stability 0.45→0.90 cut anomalies from 1-3 to 0-2 per take (but flattens delivery), and `<break>` at sentence ends + Stability 0.75 left 2 of 3 seeds fully clean with small residuals (0.21-0.28s). Break tags DO consume credits and "excessive" use causes artifacts (per ElevenLabs) — so auto-injecting them everywhere is a real design tradeoff, not a free win. eleven_v3 would give the cleanest control ([pause]/audio tags) but degrades the Sarah clone (see 2026-06 voice-model-resolver decision) — not free.

**Consequences:** No code shipped; the reroll spike (PauseAnomalyDetector + AudioPipelineService reroll + SpeechDurationOptions fields + tests) was reverted. Durable finding recorded so no future agent re-attempts a pause-detector. **2026-07-03 follow-up — created 5 "(Stable)" voice-profile variants on dev** via `POST /api/voices/profiles` (ARN Hudson/Sarah-Male/Sarah-Older-Female/Sarah-Younger-Female at v2 Stability 0.75; ARN Dave at v3 Stability 1.0 = Robust bucket — pure stability bump, all other settings identical to the source; skipped Marlowe which is already 0.98 and the two Becky test entries). **HONEST MEASUREMENT CORRECTION:** a larger 4-seed live A/B then showed Stability 0.75 does NOT reliably reduce the specific mid-clause micro-pauses (original 0.45 = 6 anomalies vs stable 0.75 = 9, across 4 seeds) — the effect is within run-to-run noise; only ~0.90 showed a weak reduction in the earlier sweep, at the cost of flatter/less-warm delivery. So these variants deliver steadier *overall* delivery (the literal "more stable" ask) but are NOT a reliable fix for the "weird pause" artifact, which is stochastic + text-structural. The reliable pause fix remains deterministic: (a) `<break>` tag placement at intended boundaries [officially v2-supported, renders exactly; needs pipeline handling — breaks aren't spoken words, exclude from word/duration measurement, cap to avoid the artifact/credit cliff], and (b) Guidance/Style-Rules to avoid stacked prepositional phrases ("on the ramp to the M80…") + stray commas. ARN should audition the (Stable) variants by EAR (the >0.20s gap count is a proxy; perceived steadiness/warmth is the real call) — value them for tone consistency, not pause elimination.

## 2026-07-03 — Filler statements: drop admin-entered gap-range fields, derive fit/cost from word count

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** BFN-002's FillerStatement carried admin-entered MinGapSeconds/MaxGapSeconds ("fills gaps of X-Y seconds") that FillerStatementSelector used both to gate eligibility and to rank candidates. User flagged this as redundant on 2026-07-03: the pipeline already estimates spoken duration from word count everywhere else (WordCounter, ISpeechDurationEstimator, WordTargetCalculator), and the selector's own EstimateSpokenSeconds already computed a statement's real cost from its text at the same ~2.5 words/sec rate used elsewhere - the admin-declared range added a number that meant nothing and could silently disagree with the statement's actual spoken length. A statement whose declared MinGapSeconds was set low (or a stray test value) could be force-selected into a remaining gap far smaller than its true word cost, overrunning the slot.

**Decision:** Removed MinGapSeconds/MaxGapSeconds entirely from FillerStatement (Domain), FillerStatementDto (wire contract), the admin HTTP trigger's parse/validate path, ConfigImportService's bundle import/validation/idempotency key, and config-bundle.schema.json. FillerStatementSelector.Select is behavior-changed but signature-unchanged: each round now filters the pool to statements whose OWN EstimateSpokenSeconds (WordCounter.Count(text)/2.5, extracted to a named WordsPerSecond constant) fits within the remaining gap, then picks the largest-cost statement that still fits (best-fit-decreasing), tie-broken by Id. A statement can never be selected into a gap smaller than its real spoken length - the latent overrun bug the old MinGapSeconds check allowed is now structurally impossible. Admins author text only; the web Filler tab's two gap-range number inputs and per-row gap badge are removed, replaced with updated copy explaining automatic length-based selection.

**Rationale:** Matches the project's own established pattern of deleting manually-curated fields that duplicate derivable data (2026-06-30 GoodRunRoads removal, 2026-07-02 AmbiguousRoads removal) rather than asking an admin to guess a number the system can compute more accurately itself. Reduces the admin authoring surface, removes a class of data-entry bug, and keeps a single source of truth for spoken-duration estimation within FillerStatementSelector.

**Consequences:** Deleted: the two gap-validation checks in FillerStatementsHttpTrigger/ConfigImportService (MaxGapSeconds>MinGapSeconds, MinGapSeconds>=0) - no replacement needed, the field they validated no longer exists. Modified: FillerStatement, FillerStatementDto, FillerStatementSelector, FillerStatementsHttpTrigger, ConfigImportService, config-bundle.schema.json, PreviewScenarios.cs, BulletinEval.cs, ExperimentHarnessTests.cs (backend); filler-statements-hooks.ts, FillerStatementsManager.tsx, lib/api/mock/store.ts (frontend). Full backend suite green (Domain 893, Application 393, Functions 230, Infrastructure 907/29-skipped, ExternalSmoke 3); web tsc -b --force clean. Old persisted Table Storage rows carrying MinGapSeconds/MaxGapSeconds JSON deserialize fine (System.Text.Json ignores unknown properties by default) - no migration needed. Dev's 11 seeded market filler-statement libraries (2026-07-03, seeded with the old fields) need re-PUTting without them once this backend redeploys - deferred, needs PIM Owner activation.

## 2026-07-03 — ARN connected Test to their Virtual WAN hub; re-subnetting it ourselves is self-serve, re-homing the hub connection is not

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The ARN Technology Lead told the Arinco deploy operator over Teams (3 Jul) "TST Network now connected for you also" with CIDR `10.241.91.0/24`, then flagged and fixed a naming mistake on the ARN side. Verified directly against the IBP subscription: the ARN Technology Lead created a new VNet `IBP-AUE-TST-VNT-APP01-10-241-91-0_24` (single subnet, `10.241.91.0/24`) inside our own `IBP-AUE-TST-RSG-NTW01`, peered to ARN's Virtual WAN hub (`HV_ARN-AUE-HUB_...` in ARN's separate subscription `33cf6994-ee8e-4b73-b53c-dec3699a49e6`, hub CIDR `10.241.255.0/24`) — peering `Connected`/`FullyInSync`, `useRemoteGateways: true`. This is RISK-08's network path landing. It does not yet reach our actual app VNet `IBP-AUE-TST-VNT-NTW01` (`10.61.0.0/24`, where the Function App and 5 private endpoints live): peering NTW01 to the new spoke with `useRemoteGateways` is rejected by Azure (`RemoteVnetHasNoGateways`) because the new spoke only holds a Virtual WAN hub peering, not an owned gateway resource — gateway transit cannot chain through it.

**Decision:** Two ways to finish this, and they are NOT equally available to us. **(a)** the ARN Technology Lead re-homes the Virtual WAN hub connection directly onto `IBP-AUE-TST-VNT-NTW01` instead of the standalone VNet — requires a write inside ARN's hub subscription (`33cf6994-...`), which we confirmed via `az role assignment list` we have **no access to at all**, so it's an ask, not a plan. **(b)** We re-carve `10.241.91.0/24` into a function-integration + private-endpoint subnet pair ourselves and migrate the Test Function App/PEs into it. Confirmed via `az role assignment list` + a live permissions check (`Microsoft.Authorization/permissions` on the VNet returned `actions: ["*"]`) that we hold **Owner on the entire IBP subscription**, including this VNet — option (b) is fully self-serve, no ARN action needed. **Proceeding with (b) as the default plan** (see the 2026-07-03 "Self-serve by default" policy decision below): Test has no real users and no uptime obligation, so "it's real migration surgery on a working environment" is not a reason to wait on the ARN Technology Lead. Sent the ARN Technology Lead the (a) option anyway as a zero-cost parallel ask — if he flips it first, great, but we do not block on his reply.

**Rationale:** Verified capability against the live Azure API rather than assumed on both sides of the ask — confirmed we're hard-blocked on (a) (zero access to the hub subscription) and confirmed we are NOT blocked on (b) (Owner on the VNet). The Teams exchange ("stuffed up the connection name" / "was this sorted?" / "yep") only confirms ARN considers their side done, not that the path is usable end-to-end.

**Consequences:** EXECUTED + VERIFIED 2026-07-03 — ran option (b) self-serve. Re-carved `10.241.91.0/24` into an integration subnet (`IBP-AUE-TST-SNT-APP01-10-241-91-0_24`, resized to /26, delegated `Microsoft.Web/serverFarms`) + a PE subnet (`snet-pe`, /27); linked all 5 privatelink DNS zones to the hub VNet; moved the Function App VNet integration; deleted+recreated all 5 private endpoints (blob/table/queue/vault/account) in the new PE subnet with fresh DNS zone groups (A-records now on `10.241.91.68/71/72`); started the app. **Health verified all-green** (`/api/health` 200): storage/keyVault/azureOpenAI reachable over the new PEs. **Key finding:** HERE + ElevenLabs initially FAILED ("SSL connection could not be established") because joining the hub made `vnetRouteAll=true` send internet-bound traffic through ARN's hub firewall, which breaks/inspects outbound TLS. Fixed self-serve by setting `vnetRouteAllEnabled=false` (+ `WEBSITE_VNET_ROUTE_ALL=0`): private/RFC1918 traffic (PEs + on-prem Zetta via the hub) still routes through the VNet, while internet SaaS egresses directly — all 5 health checks green after restart. **IaC reconciled** so a redeploy reproduces this (not reverts it): added a `routeAllTraffic` param to `main.bicep`+`function-app.bicep` (default true; gates `vnetRouteAllEnabled`), and flipped `main.test.bicepparam` to `createNetwork=false` + the hub-VNet subnet/PE/5-DNS-zone IDs + `routeAllTraffic=false` (bicep build + build-params clean). Old `10.61.0.0/24` VNet retained (now orphaned, no longer referenced by params) as rollback until a test redeploy confirms the path. **Two open items remain, both genuinely external:** (1) **Zetta reachability itself is unverified** — the on-prem host IP/share is blank in `appsettings.json` and only ARN playout knows it (RFC1918 so it should route via the hub with route-all off — [INFERENCE] pending a real address to test). (2) **Prod route-all governance:** prod is meant to keep `routeAllTraffic=true` (all egress through ARN's hub firewall per their security stance), which then REQUIRES an ARN hub-firewall allowlist (no TLS interception) for the HERE + ElevenLabs domains — a legitimate the ARN Technology Lead/the Infrastructure & Security SME ask for prod, not a dev/test blocker.

## 2026-07-03 — Policy: self-serve by default, ARN engagement is a last resort, agent time is not a constraint

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** While working the Virtual WAN hub connection above, the agent recommended waiting on the ARN Technology Lead to flip a single hub-connection setting rather than doing the equivalent self-serve VNet migration itself, reasoning that the ARN Technology Lead's fix was "5 minutes for him vs. hours for us" and that self-serve migration was risky surgery on a "currently-working, E2E-verified environment." The user rejected both premises: (1) there are no customers on any Arn environment yet — dev, test, and even a deployed prod are not "production" in any sense that matters until real listeners depend on them, so environment breakage has no real cost; (2) agent wall-clock time is not scarce — an agent can spend arbitrarily long on a self-serve path as long as it's converging correctly, so "faster for ARN to do it" is not a valid reason to prefer an ARN dependency. The agent's caution came from general software-engineering conservatism (treating "production mirror" language in the docs as license to be precious about Test) and an unstated default of picking the lowest-wall-clock-time path, neither of which reflects this project's actual risk tolerance or actual constraint (ARN dependencies, not agent hours, are the scarce/blocking resource).

**Decision:** Adopt an explicit engagement posture, recorded in `AGENTS.md` ("Engagement Posture — Self-Serve by Default, ARN Is a Last Resort") so it survives session boundaries: environments are disposable until real usage begins; agent time is never a reason to prefer an ARN ask; before logging anything as "blocked on ARN," verify the blocker is real by checking actual access (RBAC, a live permissions check, or just attempting the operation) rather than assuming; only escalate to ARN when the action requires access, a decision, or physical/on-prem information we provably cannot substitute for ourselves.

**Rationale:** The project's actual scarce resource is ARN dependencies (each one is a blocker on a timeline we don't control, chased over Teams/email with unpredictable turnaround), not agent compute time (cheap, patient, parallelizable). Optimizing for "fewest ARN asks" rather than "least agent effort" is the correct objective function for a pre-launch internal tool being built by a small team with full Azure Owner access.

**Consequences:** `docs/canonical/production-readiness.md`, `docs/canonical/risks.md` (RISK-08),, and corrected to stop framing self-serve-capable work as "blocked on the ARN Technology Lead." Future agents should default to self-serve and treat any drafted ARN outreach as optional/parallel, not a prerequisite, unless the access genuinely doesn't exist on our side.

## 2026-07-05 — Prod deployed self-serve on an island network; ARN inputs become a post-deploy tail

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `main.prod.bicepparam` hard-failed validation by design, waiting on ARN hub subnet/DNS-zone IDs, the prod app registration, LAW/action-group IDs, and retention figures. Test proved the self-build alternative (29 Jun) and the hub migration path (3 Jul).

**Decision:** Deploy prod now with the Test pattern — `createNetwork=true` self-built island VNet (`10.61.0.0/24`, never peered) + own privatelink zones + PEs, `routeAllTraffic=true` (no firewall on the island path), auth phase-1 fail-closed with a throwaway client id, poller inert (zero schedules). Park immediately after smoke verification. Every ARN input becomes a documented post-deploy swap: hub migration (proven on Test), app reg → auth phase 2, channel/receivers/retention params.

**Rationale:** Extends the 2026-07-03 "self-serve by default" policy: nothing about prod infrastructure needed ARN, only its integrations do. A deployed, smoke-verified, parked prod converts four open blockers from "gates deployment" into "gates go-live", and cost while parked is ~half of running.

**Consequences:** Prod exists (`IBP-AUE-PRD-*`, SWA `lively-glacier-054847700`), health-verified through PEs, parked at B1. Full E2E bulletin generation on prod is deliberately impossible until the ARN app reg lands (no valid token audience; the queue entry requires app-created job rows since the poison-hardening) — recorded as the acceptance step for auth phase 2. `deploy.sh` step 2 against a locked KV needs the temporary public-network round-trip, documented in `docs/operations/as-built.md`.

## 2026-07-05 — Teams notifications: object-composed cards, trigger-scoped URLs, notify-on-Failed; interim self-owned channels

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The notification Logic App module had never been deployed anywhere (`deployNotifications=false` everywhere; SoW commits "approval notifications and reminders"). First live bring-up surfaced three latent module defects and one code gap.

**Decision:** (1) Card built as a Compose OBJECT, never a pre-serialised string — interpolated payloads must survive quotes/newlines (`InvalidBotRequestMessageBody` otherwise). (2) Module outputs the TRIGGER-scoped callback URL (workflow-level `listCallbackUrl()` 404s on POST). (3) No `accessPolicies` on the V1 connection. (4) Deterministic job failures notify: `BroadcastOrchestrator.UpdateJobStatus`(→Failed, transition-guarded) and `JobService.MarkJobFailedAsync` now send the Failed card — previously only poison-queue exhaustion alerted. (5) Dev + prod post to self-owned interim channels in the Project B10 team, authorised as the ARN-native identity via `listConsentLinks`/`confirmConsentCode` (no Portal); ARN's ops channel is a 2-param swap + re-consent. (6) CI failures post the same card schema via a SECRET pipeline-definition variable (`TEAMS_CICD_WEBHOOK`; the inline YAML declaration was removed because YAML variables cannot be UI-overridden).

**Rationale:** Proving the pipeline end-to-end (approval/rejected/failed cards live on dev, wiring card on prod) beats leaving a never-exercised module for go-live week; the interim channel removes the ARN dependency from the critical path.

**Consequences:** `docs/operations/notifications.md` is the bring-up/troubleshooting runbook. KV-reference caching means a changed `webhookEndpointUrl` secret needs an app-settings touch, not just a restart. Escalation reminders ride the identical send path (per-schedule notify/escalation minutes). SMS/phone remain blocked on ARN action-group receivers.

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** SoW commits load and performance testing. Running it now would measure a moving target (config and prompts still evolving) and burn real vendor spend per pipeline job.

**Decision:** Build and smoke-validate the harness (`test/load/`: k6 health/api-read/soak + `pipeline_burst.py` vs SLO-3), keep it un-executed until the pre-UAT freeze; runbook + cost controls + execution plan in `docs/operations/load-testing.md`. ## 2026-07-06 — Add FallbackStreak to Job for Chronic-Fallback Diagnosability

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Diagnosing why a deployed job used its fallback required walking Job.FallbackSourceJobId backwards one Table Storage read per hop. A live investigation on 2026-07-06 found the TEST STATION schedule chained through 43 consecutive content-limited fallbacks across 3 days (unbroken since 2026-07-03T04:15) because GetLastSuccessfulJobForMarketAsync treats a prior FallbackUsed job as a valid same-day fallback source (by design, to avoid dead air) and the schedule poller's notification design deliberately suppresses alerts for individual routine content-limited events. Nothing on the job or schedule record surfaced that this was chronic rather than a one-off.

**Decision:** Add an int Job.FallbackStreak field, computed in Job.ApplyFallback (source.FallbackStreak + 1 when the source is itself FallbackUsed, else 1) and Job.ApplyFillerFallback (always 1). Persist it through TableStorageJobRepository.JobEntity, expose it via FallbackDataDto.Streak in the job detail API, and surface it in the web console (FallbackDetailsPanel, BroadcastLogRowDetail) as a chronic-fallback warning when Streak > 1. Also updated the arn-inspect-deployed-job skill to read LogsJson first (a sampling-immune, per-job narrative log richer than Application Insights traces) before falling back to App Insights trace queries, and documented that ApplyFallback overwrites IncidentsJson/AllIncidentsJson/CorridorsJson with the fallback source's stale data.

**Rationale:** FallbackStreak turns an N-hop manual chain walk into a single job read, matching how the operator console and any future LLM diagnosis should recognize chronic vs one-off fallback. The LogsJson-first skill change removes dependence on Application Insights adaptive sampling (host.json samplingSettings.isEnabled=true covers traces), which silently dropped the exact telemetry needed during the live investigation.

**Consequences:** Job.FallbackStreak defaults to 0 (never used fallback) on existing rows read before this change; it only starts populating on fallbacks applied after deployment, so historical streaks before this change must still be reconstructed via the FallbackSourceJobId chain walk documented in the skill. The chronic-fallback notification gap (no alert escalation by streak length) remains open — flagged as a follow-up, not implemented here. FallbackDataDto gained a required Streak field; any other future FallbackDataDto construction site must supply it.

## 2026-07-06 — Bias the Generation Retry Word Target to Overshoot, Not Exact-Match

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Simulation against all 65 real content-limited (FallbackUsed) jobs and 43 real aired jobs in dev (2026-07-06) proved the generation retry loop's closed-loop word-target math (BroadcastOrchestrator.cs, the desiredSyllables/rawTargetWords calculation) has a zero-margin fixed point: it algebraically solves for next-attempt spoken duration == TargetDurationSeconds exactly (syllables cancel out of the formula, confirmed by porting it to Python and reproducing 90.8% of 195 real historical attempt-to-attempt target transitions exactly, 97.4% within 2 words). The deployed SpeechDuration config gives zero tolerance on the short side (MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0, i.e. no slow-down stretch at all) but 10-35% tolerance on the long side (MaxSpeedUpFactor=1.1, AbsolutePaceBoostSpeedUpCeiling=1.35), so aiming dead-center wastes the entire safety margin the pipeline already has. The combined pass/fail histogram of real outcomes showed a hard cliff exactly at ratio~0.99: nothing failed above it, nothing passed below ~0.90, and the 43 passing jobs' own natural-spoken/target ratio averaged only 1.031 (using ~3 of the available 10 percentage points of speed-up headroom). Of the 11 near-miss bucket-3 failures identified in the same audit, the overshoot needed to have passed ranged 0.3%-16.0% (median 9.2%), all within the existing AbsolutePaceBoostSpeedUpCeiling, 6 of 11 within the standard MaxSpeedUpFactor=1.1 alone. Separately, BroadcastOptions.DampingFactor and BroadcastOptions.MaxPerRetryWordShift were found to be dead configuration -- BroadcastOrchestrator used hardcoded private const duplicates instead, so the retry's convergence behavior could not be tuned without a code change and redeploy.

**Decision:** Added BroadcastOptions.RetryOvershootBias (double, default 1.0, deployed at 1.1 in appsettings.json) multiplying the retry loop's desiredSyllables calculation so each retry aims a deliberate percentage past the slot duration instead of exactly at it -- the resulting overrun is absorbed by the existing speed-up/compression path rather than failing as an unrecoverable underrun. Also fixed BroadcastOrchestrator to read the previously-dead BroadcastOptions.DampingFactor and BroadcastOptions.MaxPerRetryWordShift instead of its own hardcoded private const copies, so retry convergence aggressiveness is now tunable via config without a redeploy. MaxSlowDownFactor was deliberately left untouched (ARN does not want slower-sounding audio); the fix operates entirely on the already-safe, already-deployed speed-up side.

**Rationale:** Biasing the retry target toward overshoot costs nothing in audio quality (the same pitch-preserving compression already used for over-length scripts) and is proven, not assumed, to recover a meaningful fraction of near-miss content-limited fallbacks using data from the live system rather than a guess. 1.1 was chosen as a conservative starting point that stays within the standard MaxSpeedUpFactor ceiling (not the wider pace-boost-only ceiling) and is expected to flip roughly half of the historical near-miss failures based on a direct proportional-scaling projection; the true effect (via an actual regenerated attempt, not just scaling) should be measured after deployment.

**Consequences:** RetryOvershootBias only affects jobs that reach the closed-loop retry (i.e. underran on a prior attempt); it does not change catastrophically-thin markets like TEST STATION, which need a coverage/duration fix, not a targeting fix. DampingFactor and MaxPerRetryWordShift are now genuinely live config -- any future change to their appsettings.json values will change retry convergence speed, which previously had no effect. Not yet deployed to dev; needs a redeploy plus a follow-up audit of the fallback rate to confirm the projected improvement.

## 2026-07-06 — Filler statements are unreviewed ARN editorial content, applied post-LLM

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Job ba669493 (TEST STATION, 2026-07-06) content-limited-fell-back with 20 corridors/30 incidents available. Root cause: filler statements were woven into the script by the draft LLM and re-judged by the review LLM alongside real traffic content. TEST STATION's configured filler was all station-promo copy (iHeart app download, DJ-show times, a contest) — review correctly flagged it as NOT FROM DATA/vagueness and cut it, leaving only ~26-67 words of real traffic content, 5-7s short of the 30s slot across all 4 retries. ARN's position: filler statements are their own editorial call (whatever they configure), never a target for AI critique, and should not even be shown to the reviewer to avoid wasted context and this exact failure mode.

**Decision:** Filler statements are removed entirely from the LLM-facing pipeline. LlmScriptGenerator.GenerateScriptAsync (draft) and RefineScriptAsync (refine) no longer read context.FillerStatements or render a fillerStatements argument; ReviewScriptAsync composes its source-data block via BulletinDataComposer.ComposeAllData(context) with includeFillerStatements defaulted false, so filler text never reaches the reviewer. draft.md/refine.md drop their filler data blocks and 'voice the standing road facts' instruction; review.md drops the now-dead 'or the provided standing road facts is legitimate' clause. Instead, BroadcastOrchestrator.GenerateAndSynthesizeAsync appends filler AFTER the full LLM pipeline (generate, review/refine, word-target compliance, safety, delivery-direction) has produced an approved traffic/weather/fuel-only script: it estimates that script's own duration (IDurationEstimator.EstimateDuration), computes the real residual gap against TargetDurationSeconds, calls the unchanged FillerStatementSelector.Select against that measured gap, and appends the selected statements verbatim (space-joined, unmodified) to both the persisted script and the TTS input. FillSource.Filler is dropped from the draft's fillOrder hint (weather/fuel only) since filler is no longer something the writer can choose to reach for. The now-uncalled FillerStatementSelector.EstimateGapSeconds pre-generation heuristic is deleted; the orchestrator's real post-generation duration estimate is strictly more accurate than the old structural guess.

**Rationale:** ARN authors filler text directly via the admin CRUD (FillerStatementsHttpTrigger) and owns responsibility for its content; an LLM review pass second-guessing that content only produces false-positive cuts (as observed) or wasted tokens on a true-positive (also observed, since TEST STATION's filler happened to be junk test fixtures). Moving the append to AFTER the entire LLM pipeline (not just after review) guarantees no LLM call of any kind — draft, review, refine, safety, or delivery-direction — ever sees or can alter ARN's exact wording. It also makes the gap computation strictly better: the old EstimateGapSeconds ran BEFORE the script existed and guessed content cost from structural counts (6s/incident, 4s/weather, etc); the new call site runs after the traffic-only script is finalized and safety-checked, so the gap fed to FillerStatementSelector.Select is the real measured shortfall, not a guess.

**Consequences:** LlmScriptGenerator: GenerateScriptAsync/RefineScriptAsync drop their filler-selection blocks and the FillSource.Filler case in availableFillSources; ReviewScriptAsync's ComposeAllData call drops includeFillerStatements: true. BroadcastOrchestrator.GenerateAndSynthesizeAsync gains a filler top-up step between ApplyDeliveryDirectionAsync and the word/syllable recount, using the already-injected IDurationEstimator + context.FillerStatements. FillerStatementSelector.EstimateGapSeconds is deleted (dead code, no remaining callers); FillerStatementSelector.Select is unchanged and still used from the new orchestrator call site. prompts/draft.md, refine.md, review.md lose their filler-statement blocks/clauses; BulletinDataComposer's includeFillerStatements doc comment now describes eval-pack-only usage. RevoiceExistingScriptAsync (verbatim re-voice) is intentionally untouched — filler never applies there, preserving 'the operator's exact words' contract. Markets whose filler statements are actually non-traffic content (like TEST STATION's promo copy) will now air that content verbatim instead of having it silently cut — filler quality is now entirely ARN's operational responsibility, not a code-enforced gate; TEST STATION's promo filler should be replaced with real standing road facts to get the intended slot-filling benefit.

## 2026-07-06 — FillerStatementSelector cost model must match the caller's calibrated speaking rate

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deploying the 2026-07-06 filler-post-review-append change to dev, then retesting the three markets with the most FallbackUsed/content-limited history (TEST STATION, sydney, portlincoln) surfaced a real gap: TEST STATION (voice Becky, eleven_multilingual_v2, calibrated ~2.3-2.4 words/sec) and portlincoln resolved cleanly, but sydney (voice ARN Hudson, eleven_v3, calibrated ~2.85-2.9 words/sec) still fell back. Root cause: BroadcastOrchestrator now computes the residual gap from the traffic-only script's REAL calibrated duration (IDurationEstimator.EstimateDuration with the voice's actual secondsPerWord), but FillerStatementSelector.EstimateSpokenSeconds still costed candidate filler statements at a hardcoded generic 2.5 words/sec. For a voice calibrated faster than 2.5 wps (i.e. most real ARN voices, which run 150-180+ WPM), the gap computed at the real fast rate is smaller than what the filler-cost model (assuming the slower generic rate) requires to admit even the shortest configured statement, so eligible filler was silently excluded from gaps it would genuinely fit at the voice's true pace. TEST STATION's Becky calibration happened to sit close to the generic 2.5 wps by coincidence, masking the bug there.

**Decision:** FillerStatementSelector.Select gained an optional wordsPerSecond parameter (default 2.5, preserving the eval harness and existing unit-test expectations that size gaps the same coarse way) threaded into EstimateSpokenSeconds instead of the removed hardcoded WordsPerSecond constant. BroadcastOrchestrator.GenerateAndSynthesizeAsync now passes wordsPerSecond: 1.0 / secondsPerWord — the SAME calibrated rate already used to compute fillerGapSeconds via IDurationEstimator.EstimateDuration — so the gap and every candidate's cost are always evaluated on one consistent speaking-rate basis, whatever that voice's real pace is.

**Rationale:** Gap and cost must share units or the comparison is meaningless: a gap sized in 'fast-voice seconds' compared against a cost sized in 'generic 150 WPM seconds' systematically under-admits filler for any voice faster than the generic assumption. Verified live: sydney (ARN Hudson, real ~171-174 WPM) fell back before this fix and filled cleanly to 30.0s with two real filler statements appended after it; TEST STATION and portlincoln, already working, were re-verified unaffected. The default parameter value keeps every pre-existing caller (FillerStatementSelectorTests' 15 Select-behavior tests, the eval harness) byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Consequences:** FillerStatementSelector.cs: Select signature gains wordsPerSecond=2.5 default; EstimateSpokenSeconds takes it as a parameter instead of reading the private WordsPerSecond constant directly (the constant survives only as the default value and doc reference). BroadcastOrchestrator.cs: the filler-selection call site passes wordsPerSecond explicitly. One existing test (FillerAppended_WhenDurationShortOfTarget) needed a realistic per-test voice calibration override (150 WPM, matching its own gap-math comments) plus a scriptRefiner stub, since the shared class-level test fixture's placeholder calibration (20 WPM) is unrelated to filler-cost realism and would have made even a 7-word filler statement look too slow to fit a 10s gap once cost is computed at the real (if placeholder) calibrated rate rather than the old hardcoded constant. TEST STATION's filler statements also had their internal [TEST]/[TEST DRIVE ONLY]/[TEST BREAKFAST ONLY] bracket prefixes stripped via the filler-statements API (same-shape as ElevenLabs v3 audio-tag syntax, which non-v3 models can't interpret and would otherwise try to vocalize literally) — confirmed via TaggedScriptText that the bracket no longer reaches the TTS engine.

## 2026-07-06 — Fallback replay corpus: dev FallbackUsed scenarios reproduce locally with a history-fitted simulated ElevenLabs

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** 58 of 104 dev jobs ended FallbackUsed and every content-limited diagnosis relied on reading LogsJson after the fact; there was no way to run those exact scenarios through the retry/agent loop locally, and iterating on retry-cycle fixes required either live TTS spend or guessing. GeneratorInputJson snapshots only exist on jobs created after 2026-07-06, so the historical inputs had to be reconstructed.

**Decision:** A committed fallback replay corpus (`test/corpus/fallback-replay/`, one fixture per dev FallbackUsed job) plus a replay harness (`test/ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure.Tests/Replay/`) that runs each fixture through the REAL `BroadcastOrchestrator.OrchestrateAsync(BroadcastWithTraffic)` pre-fetched-traffic path — real LLM draft/review/refine/safety agents, real word-target math, real `AudioPipelineService` slot gate — with ElevenLabs replaced by `SimulatedElevenLabsSynthesizer`: per-(voice, model, speed-bucket) OLS fits of duration-vs-syllables trained on the exported dev `synthesisHistory` table (850 real reads, seed committed beside the fixtures). Fixtures were reconstructed from `radioJobs` columns (corridors are the job's own even on fallback jobs; incidents recovered by key where possible, else synthesized from corridor summaries), weather re-parsed from LogsJson lines, fuel re-synthesized at typical prices where dev fetched it, guidance re-composed from the dev `guidance` table, and good-runs/flow-pool re-captured live per unique coverage (7 HERE calls) through the same `BulletinContentSelector` competition the orchestrator uses. Run: `ARN_REPLAY_FALLBACK=1 dotnet test --filter FallbackCorpus_Replay_ThroughRealRetryLoop` (knobs: `ARN_REPLAY_JOB`, `ARN_REPLAY_LIMIT`, `ARN_REPLAY_RETRY_BIAS`/`ARN_REPLAY_WORD_OVERSHOOT` for historical-config replays, `ARN_REPLAY_NOISE_SIGMA` for Monte Carlo duration jitter); one-time re-capture: `ARN_REPLAY_CAPTURE_FLOW=1 dotnet test --filter FallbackCorpus_CaptureFlowPools`.

**Rationale:** Two measurement findings make the simulator as accurate as physics allows: (1) identical-input real ElevenLabs reads spread a mean 2.55s (max 10.7s) — duration is genuinely stochastic, and the per-voice fits' leave-one-out MAE of 0.9–1.7s is at/below that noise floor; (2) the ElevenLabs `speed` setting's duration effect is superlinear (same-day 9Kes reads: 0.43 s/word at speed 1.09 vs 0.31 s/word at 1.2), so rates must be fitted per recorded speed bucket, never normalized by dividing duration by speed. Verified against dev ground truth (replays under historical `RetryOvershootBias=1.0`): near-miss job 9ef6501c reproduced the identical 4-attempt content-limited spiral with the retry-target trajectory matching dev almost exactly ([90,81,78,75] vs [90,80,76,75]) and best fill 26.8s vs dev 29.6s; deep-shortfall, empty-coverage (portlincoln), real-market (sydney), and VoiceId-missing classes all reach the same terminal decision class as dev.

**Consequences:** Retry-cycle changes (overshoot bias, best-take retention, corridor-cap sizing, reviewer prompt changes) can now be A/B measured against the exact scenarios that failed in dev, with data held constant and zero TTS cost — replay-vs-replay comparisons are the signal; dev-vs-replay carries documented per-fixture fidelity notes (`Fidelity` block: incidents recovered vs synthesized, weather/fuel source, good-run recapture). Known limits: good-run/flow data reflects capture time, not the original job's clock; fuel prices are typical values where dev's were lost; the harness applies a filler-cart transition itself (RecordingFallbackService), so same-day-chain semantics are not exercised; the LLM remains a variance source — judge script class, not byte-equality. Side finding for prod: the draft LLM call has no 429 backoff — back-to-back replays surfaced `Draft failed (429 TooManyRequests)` aborting a generation cycle.

## 2026-07-06 — Weather and Fuel enabled platform-wide on dev, superseding the 2026-06 hold

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Manually triggering 1 bulletin per station configuration in dev (12 stations) surfaced 5 content-limited fallbacks (darwin, mildura, queenstown, sydney, TEST STATION) — all genuinely thin-traffic runs whose residual slot gap (1.5-5s) was smaller than any configured filler statement could cover. User asked to enable Weather and Fuel for these stations to give them more real content sources to close the gap. Investigation found a two-tier gate: HereWeatherProvider/HereFuelPriceProvider both check a PLATFORM-WIDE Weather:Enabled/Fuel:Enabled flag before ever looking at a market's own ContentSelection, and both flags were 'false' in src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Functions/appsettings.json — a holdover from the 2026-06 decision that weather/fuel were 'not yet confirmed for Release 1'. This meant TEST STATION's schedule, which already had ContentSelection.Weather=true/Fuel=true configured, was STILL silently getting zero weather/fuel every single run ('Weather data unavailable' / 'Fuel price data unavailable') — per-market ContentSelection was structurally incapable of taking effect until this platform gate flipped.

**Decision:** Set Weather__Enabled=true and Fuel__Enabled=true as IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01 Function App settings (overriding the appsettings.json false default at runtime, no redeploy needed) and restarted the app. Enabled ContentSelection.Weather/Fuel for the 4 markets that didn't already have it (darwin, mildura, queenstown, sydney) via PUT /api/schedules/{market} — TEST STATION's ContentSelection was already correctly configured, it just needed the platform gate. Verified all 5 previously-failing stations now WaitingApproval with real HERE weather ('Weather fetched: ...') and fuel ('Fuel prices fetched: 2 fuel type(s)') data actually landing in the aired script, not just filler.

**Rationale:** The platform flag is a single global boolean — there is no way to enable weather/fuel for only these 5 markets without also making it available to every other market's own ContentSelection (checked: only TEST STATION had Weather/Fuel=true set elsewhere at the time, so no other market was silently affected). ARN explicitly asked to enable it now in this conversation, superseding the earlier 'not yet confirmed for Release 1' hold recorded in the 2026-06 decision. Enabling real content sources (weather ~4s, fuel ~4s of legitimate spoken content) is a more durable fix for these markets' thin-content fallbacks than shrinking filler further, since it works even on days filler alone can't close the gap.

**Consequences:** IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01 app settings gain Weather__Enabled=true, Fuel__Enabled=true (dev only — test/prod appsettings/app-settings untouched, still default false; a future full Bicep redeploy of dev would revert this unless the appsettings.json source default is also updated, since app settings set via CLI are an environment-level override, not a code change). darwin/mildura/queenstown/sydney schedules gain ContentSelection={Traffic:true, Weather:true, Fuel:true} (previously null/default traffic-only). Supersedes the 2026-06 'Weather + fuel not yet confirmed for Release 1' decision for the dev environment; test/prod remain unconfirmed pending the same explicit go-ahead.

## 2026-07-06 — Fallback-reduction changes are judged by the replay panel, not the census; first verdicts recorded

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A full 58-fixture corpus census per config arm takes ~70 minutes of wall time and mostly re-samples LLM noise (50 TEST STATION fixtures share one coverage/voice), so it is the wrong unit for iterating on fallback-rate fixes. Meanwhile the same-arm run-to-run noise had never been measured, so nobody knew what size of improvement was even distinguishable from variance.

**Decision:** A/B iteration runs on the committed stratified panel — `ARN_REPLAY_JOB=panel`, 10 fixtures: 3 near-miss, 3 moderate, 3 deep-shortfall, 1 short-slot, spanning TEST STATION and real markets — executed in ONE test process (`ARN_REPLAY_PAUSE`, default 20s, keeps an arm under the AOAI rate limit) and summarized as one `ARM SUMMARY` line (filled count, mean best-fill, mean attempts). Config arms vary exactly one knob via env (`ARN_REPLAY_WORD_OVERSHOOT`, `ARN_REPLAY_RETRY_BIAS`, `ARN_REPLAY_EXTEND`, `ARN_REPLAY_SLOWDOWN`, `ARN_REPLAY_PAD`). Measured same-config noise band (two extend-on/1.1 runs): ±2 filled, ±4pp mean best-fill — an arm must beat control by >2 fills or >~5pp paired mean fill before it is believed; otherwise run repeats. New `BroadcastOptions.RetryExtendBestTake` (default false) gates the extend-from-best-take retry so it can be trialled per environment.

**Rationale:** First three verdicts prove the loop: (1) `WordTargetOvershoot` 1.1→1.2 REJECTED — paired panel comparison lost 6 fixtures to 3 (mean best-fill 64% vs 70%), consistent with the known mechanism that bigger word asks trigger more aggressive rewrites/gate repairs that net-shorten content-capped scripts; a plausible config change killed in ~20 minutes for zero TTS spend, where the earlier single-fixture win (9ef6501c filling at 1.2) proved to be variance. (2) Extend-from-best-take retries showed NO effect above the noise band (extend-on 2/10@70% and 0/10@66% vs extend-off 1/10@68%) — flag stays default-off pending repeats. (3) The deep-shortfall band (best fills 30-70%) moved for NOBODY in any arm, confirming content supply (corridor slot capacity, good-run admission), not targeting or retry mechanics, is the remaining lever for most fallbacks.

**Consequences:** `FallbackReplayTests` gains the `IterationPanel` constant, comma-list/`panel` job filtering, in-process pacing, and the `ARM SUMMARY` aggregate; `SimulatedElevenLabsSynthesizer` reads the COMMITTED seed (never the mutated work copy) so the duration model cannot drift mid-arm. `BroadcastOptions.RetryExtendBestTake` exists but is off everywhere. Next fallback-reduction work should target the corridor slot-capacity formula (`CalculateMaxCorridors` 5s/item assumption vs ~3s measured), which requires regenerating fixtures with the full 20-corridor fetched pool so selection runs in-replay. Six pre-existing test callsites were updated for the concurrent `JobService` ctor change (`IVoiceProfileService` + logger params); all 162 affected tests pass.

## 2026-07-06 — Per-station LLM model selection removed; single centrally-configured model

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-06-17 decision let operators pick `MarketSchedule.LlmModel` per station from an allowed set of `gpt-5.4-mini` / `gpt-5.4-nano`, plus a parallel, unused ad-hoc override on `POST /broadcast` (`OrchestrationRequestDto.LlmModel`). Investigating a Foundry portal issue on the deployed AI Services accounts surfaced that `gpt-5.4-nano` had never actually been deployed on dev, test, or prod — only `gpt-5.4-mini` exists as a model deployment on any of the three accounts. A live test against the dev `/openai/v1/responses` endpoint confirmed `gpt-5.4-mini` succeeds (HTTP 200) while `gpt-5.4-nano` fails (HTTP 401, no deployment to resolve) with the same token. Azure Foundry's deployment-free "instant access" routing does not rescue this: it is preview-only, region-locked to West US 3 (our accounts are `australiaeast`), and reachable only through a project-scoped endpoint the app never calls (`LlmScriptGenerator` posts to the account-level `/openai/v1/responses`, not `/api/projects/{name}/openai/v1/responses`). No station was ever set to `gpt-5.4-nano` in practice (all 12 dev stations were on `gpt-5.4-mini`), so this was a latent, not active, break — but any operator selecting the second listed option would have silently failed every generation for that station.

**Decision:** Removed the entire per-request/per-station model-override mechanism end to end: `MarketSchedule.LlmModel` (domain field + `LlmModels` allowed-set class + validation), the ad-hoc `OrchestrationRequestDto.LlmModel` / `BroadcastContext.LlmModel` / `BroadcastQueueMessage.LlmModel` carrier chain, the schedule commands/DTOs/config-export-import fields, the Table Storage column, and the frontend `LlmModelSelector` UI + `LLM_MODELS`/`normalizeLlmModel` schema plumbing. `LlmScriptGenerator` now always uses the single centrally-configured `AiSettings:AzureAI:Model` (`AzureAIOptions.Model`, default `gpt-5.4-mini`) for every role (Draft/Refine/Review/Attribute) and every station — `ResolveLlmModel` is deleted, call sites use `_azureOptions.Model` directly. Stale example configs (`appsettings.json.example`, `appsettings.Development.json.example`) that still showed the pre-gpt-5.4 `gpt-5-mini` default were corrected to `gpt-5.4-mini` for consistency.

**Rationale:** A selectable option that silently fails in every deployed environment is worse than no option — it looks supported in the UI but breaks generation for whichever station picks it, with no test or monitoring catching it because nothing exercised that path. Centralizing the model in appsettings (already the mechanism for the working default) gives one source of truth with zero escape hatches, matching how Safety review was already pinned to the global default for a consistent bar. If a second model is wanted later, the documented deploy → eval → cutover trial flow applies to the global config, and any future per-station differentiation should first confirm every candidate model actually has a deployment in every target environment.

**Consequences:** `ScheduleSummaryDto`, `UpsertScheduleRequest`, `ConfigScheduleDto`, and the config-bundle JSON schema no longer carry `LlmModel` — a pre-2026-07-06 exported config bundle containing that field will fail import validation (`additionalProperties: false`); re-export under the new schema. Existing Table Storage schedule rows retain a stray `LlmModel` column that is now silently ignored (schemaless storage, no migration needed). All backend and frontend tests updated; full solution + relevant Vitest suites pass.

## 2026-07-06 — Filler statements are cached audio, not re-synthesized text appended per bulletin

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Filler statements (ARN-authored standing facts) were appended as TEXT onto the traffic script (2026-07-06 'unreviewed ARN editorial content' decision) and re-synthesized via ElevenLabs on every single bulletin that selected them, even though the same statement in the same voice configuration produces byte-identical audio every time. This wasted TTS cost/latency on every repeat use and meant filler duration was only ever a word-count estimate, never a measured fact.

**Decision:** Each (filler statement x voice x voice settings x TTS model) combination is now synthesized once and cached: new IFillerAudioCacheRepository (Table Storage metadata, PartitionKey=FillerStatement.Id, RowKey=cache key) + IFillerAudioCacheService (orchestrates cache lookup, synthesize-trim-normalize-upload on a miss, blob storage under the existing broadcasts container's filler-cache/ prefix) + FillerAudioCacheKey (voiceId + VoiceSettings.GetConfigurationKey + model). BroadcastOrchestrator.GenerateAndSynthesizeAsync now resolves selected filler statements to AUDIO via IFillerAudioCacheService.ResolveAsync before synthesis (not appended as text); the traffic-only TTS call targets TargetDurationSeconds minus filler duration minus inter-clip pause (new PcmAudioStitcher.Concatenate, 0.35s fixed pause); on success the traffic take and filler clips are stitched, fine-tuned to the full slot, and content-limited status is recomputed via a new IAudioPipelineService.IsSlotFilled (extracted from AudioPipelineService.LogWaterfallAndSucceed's existing formula so both paths share one gate). Cache invalidation (FillerAudioCacheInvalidator, diffs old vs new statement Text/removal) is wired into both filler-statement write paths: FillerStatementsHttpTrigger.SetFillerStatements and ConfigImportService's filler-statement apply path.

**Rationale:** The same statement/voice/settings/model combination produces byte-identical ElevenLabs output every time, so re-synthesizing it per bulletin is pure waste; caching also upgrades filler duration from a word-count estimate to a real measured value, letting the traffic-only synthesis target the exact remaining slot instead of guessing. Stitching after synthesis (not before, as text) keeps filler out of the TTS duration-fit loop entirely, matching the 2026-07-06 decision that filler must never pass through any LLM or synthesis judgment call that could distort ARN's own editorial content.

**Consequences:** New Domain files: FillerAudioClip, ResolvedFillerAudio, FillerAudioCacheKey, IFillerAudioCacheRepository, IFillerAudioCacheService, FillerAudioCacheInvalidator. New Infrastructure files: PcmAudioStitcher, FillerAudioCacheService, TableStorageFillerAudioCacheRepository. IAudioPipelineService gained IsSlotFilled and StitchAudioClips (the latter exists solely so BroadcastOrchestrator, which has zero project reference to Infrastructure, never touches a concrete Infrastructure type directly). BroadcastOrchestrator, FillerStatementsHttpTrigger, and ConfigImportService constructors all gained an IFillerAudioCacheService parameter; DI registers it AddScoped (depends on BlobServiceClient/IAudioSynthesizer, both AddScoped, so it can never be AddSingleton). Filler audio resolution runs even for ScriptOnly=true preview jobs (before the ScriptOnly early-return), so a preview also warms the cache. Full solution build clean; Domain/Infrastructure/Application/Functions test suites green after adding IFillerAudioCacheService substitutes/fakes to BroadcastOrchestratorTests, FillerStatementsHttpTriggerTests, and ConfigImportServiceTests.

## 2026-07-06 — Slot capacity derived from configurable per-item speech cost (SlotSecondsPerItem; dev 3.0)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The deep-shortfall band of content-limited fallbacks (best fills 30-70% of slot) did not move under ANY targeting/retry knob on the replay panel — overshoot, retry bias, and extend-from-best-take all left it flat, because `BroadcastOrchestrator.CalculateMaxCorridors` hardcoded `clamp(sec/5.0, 6, 15)`: a 5s-per-item assumption that is ~2x the measured on-air cost (~3s/item at the corpus mean 185 wpm). A 30s slot was capped at 6 rundown items while its word budget demanded ~100 words, so drafts landed at ~48% of target with 14+ fetched corridors sitting unused in the pool — the structural cause of most content-limited fallbacks.

**Decision:** New pure domain service `SlotCapacity.Compute(targetSeconds, secondsPerItem)` (floor 6, cap 15; non-positive input falls back to legacy 5.0) driven by `BroadcastOptions.SlotSecondsPerItem` (default 5.0 = legacy no-op). Dev `appsettings.json` deploys 3.0: a 30s slot now admits 10 rundown items; 15s slots hit the 6-item floor and are unchanged. The replay harness gained `ARN_REPLAY_CAPACITY` (re-runs `BulletinContentSelector` from the fixture's new `FullCorridorPool` — all ~20 fetched corridors, not just dev's selected 6) so capacity changes are panel-A/B-able without touching prod code.

**Rationale:** Panel A/B (capacity 6 vs 10, all else at deployed config): 9/10 fixtures improved or held, 5 materially (paired wins 5:1); the deep-shortfall fixtures moved for the first time under any change (+3.2s, +4.3s, +3.3s of honest content); one near-miss (Gold Coast) flipped to slot-filled at attempt 1 with a 29.9s natural read; mean best-fill 66%→72% (above the ±4pp same-config noise band). The lone regression was the 15s-slot fixture under the blunt fixed-10 override — an experiment artifact the slot-scaled formula does not reproduce (15s at 3.0 → floor 6, identical to legacy). More admitted items also means retries have real material to grow into, compounding with `RetryOvershootBias` and reducing reliance on filler top-up.

**Consequences:** `BroadcastOptions.SlotSecondsPerItem`; `Domain.Services.SlotCapacity` (unit-tested); `CalculateMaxCorridors` becomes an instance one-liner delegating to it; dev appsettings sets 3.0 (test/prod stay legacy 5.0 pending dev soak). Larger rundowns mean slightly larger draft prompts and, on busy markets, more speakable material than the slot needs — absorbed by the existing selection scoring and speed-up/trim path. Needs a dev redeploy to take effect; verify via the dev fallback rate over a full broadcast day and the `[TrafficAggregation] SelectedCorridors` trace. Fixtures now carry `FullCorridorPool` for future selection-level experiments.

## 2026-07-06 — Fabrication verdicts retracted: HERE Comment data is legitimate and wanted; six source-level fixes instead of gates

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 12-station dev sweep's independent reviews alleged widespread LLM fabrication (invented event names, relocated crashes, invented anchors). Full-field verification overturned every allegation: the draft model has no tools/web access, and each "fabrication" traced to real input the review packets had omitted — road-authority `Comment` free-text ("ASICS Gold Coast Marathon 2026" on the closure, "Great Eastern Hwy westbound at Margaret Rd, Glen Forrest…"), incident `Detail` beyond a truncated list, and the MonitoredRoutes config whose on-time template line ("running close to normal, only a touch slow") was voiced near-verbatim. ARN's direction: cause/event detail from HERE is GOOD and must keep flowing to the writer; fix the genuinely wrong behaviors at the source, without adding review gates.

**Decision:** Six source-level changes. (1) `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.MergeBidirectionalClosures` — same-road closure corridors with differing directions merge into one "both directions" corridor (Mildura aired "Walker Road citybound is shut" while the outbound side was also closed). (2) Hot-board suppression of on-time monitored-route asides — name-matching cannot reconcile "Western Motorway" (HERE) with "the M4 from Parramatta to the city" (config), so when any closure or standstill/heavy corridor is on the board, on-time asides are dropped class-wide (delayed routes still render); fixes the Sydney standstill-vs-"touch slow" contradiction. (3) Multi-anchor corridors render a "Locations (SEPARATE spots…)" list so two incidents ~45km apart are never welded into one composite place (Brisbane "near Sandgate Road at Steve Irwin Way"). (4) Market-local daypart: `LlmScriptGenerator.ResolveTimeOfDay(TimezoneId)` feeds `timeOfDay` to draft AND review prompts; with a timezone the daypart is stated and enforced, without one time-of-day words are banned (Darwin/Port Lincoln aired "this morning" at 15:30 local). (5) `NonVehicularIncidentFilter` at the `HereTrafficProvider.FilterAndSortIncidents` chokepoint drops PSP/shared-path/footpath/cycleway works (word-boundary "PSP" match) before corridor formation (Perth burned ~20 words on a bike-path closure). (6) `RateLimitRetryHandler` on the AzureOpenAI HttpClient — 429/503 retry honoring Retry-After, exponential+jitter fallback, 5 tries/90s cap, replacing the old `AddTransientHttpErrorPolicy` that never handled 429 (the 12-way concurrent sweep knocked out review fail-open and shipped unreviewed drafts; same-minute schedule crons would reproduce on a real morning). Plus draft.md: voice HERE-provided causes ("closed for the ASICS Gold Coast Marathon"), never invent one; voice SEPARATE spots separately.

**Rationale:** Every fix removes a wrongness at its origin (data contradiction, missing clock, non-driver data, unprotected quota) rather than teaching the reviewer to catch it later — the reviewer demonstrably already catches drafting fabrication when it is allowed to run. Review packets for any future fidelity audit MUST include incident Comment fields, the MonitoredRoutes section, untruncated incident lists, good-runs, and filler config, or reviewers wrongly convict the writer (this session's initial verdicts did exactly that and were retracted).

**Consequences:** New: `Domain/Services/NonVehicularIncidentFilter`, `Infrastructure/AiProviders/SemanticKernel/RateLimitRetryHandler`. Changed: `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` (merge, hot-board suppression, separate-spots), `LlmScriptGenerator` (timeOfDay arg draft+review), `HereTrafficProvider` (filter callsite), `DependencyInjection` (handler wiring), `prompts/draft.md` + `prompts/review.md` (time-of-day, cause-voicing, separate-spots; review 2b clause). Two pre-existing summarizer tests updated for the new (correct) behavior; suites at 2,600 green. Replay-panel regression gate before deploy; on-air verification: re-run stations sequentially and check daypart wording, absence of on-time asides beside standstills, "both directions" closures, and no PSP items.

## 2026-07-06 — Post-synthesis filler rescue: gap re-derived from the measured read

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Three of twelve manual dev triggers (melbourne, sydney, portlincoln) fell back content-limited despite configured filler. Root cause from job logs: the filler gap is estimated PRE-synthesis from voice calibration (`slot − words × calibratedSecondsPerWord`); calibration ran 20–30% slow (melbourne calibrated ~129 wpm vs 161 wpm measured), so the estimated gap collapsed to ~0, `FillerStatementSelector` (no-overshoot contract) picked nothing, and the pipeline discarded a take whose measured 3.5–4.0s residual the cached filler pool could cover. Empty selection also logged nothing. Compounding: same-day anti-repeat halves the eligible pool on second bulletins, and the residual gap can be smaller than the shortest statement.

**Decision:** After synthesis, when the take is content-limited and the market has filler statements, re-derive the TRUE gap (slot − measured natural read − already-stitched filler) and the voice's TRUE pace (spoken words ÷ measured seconds, clamped 1.0–6.0 wps), and re-run the selector over the not-yet-used pool with `overshootToleranceSeconds = 1.5` — a new opt-in selector parameter that, only when nothing fits WITHIN the gap, closes it with the smallest statement overshooting by ≤ tolerance (small overruns are compressed by `FineTuneToTargetDuration`; underruns beyond the silence pad fail the attempt). Rescued audio joins `resolvedFiller`, so the existing stitch/fine-tune/re-gate path is unchanged. Empty rescue now logs to the job narrative ("Filler rescue: no statement fits…").

**Rationale:** The measured read is ground truth the pipeline already holds at the moment it declares an attempt short; re-rating filler against it costs zero LLM/TTS calls (cached clips) and directly prevents the fallback the filler library exists to prevent. Tolerance is opt-in and bounded so the default selector contract — and every existing callsite — is unchanged.

**Consequences:** Changed: `Domain/Services/FillerStatementSelector` (tolerance param; default 0 preserves prior contract), `Application/BroadcastOrchestrator` (rescue block before the stitch pass + `FillerRescueOvershootToleranceSeconds = 1.5`). Content-limited retries only recur when the filler pool is genuinely exhausted; most calibration-starved underruns become first-attempt fills. Voice-calibration drift is still worth fixing at the source (separate item). Manual-trigger harness note: the schedules API exposes content selection under `Content` (not `ContentSelection`) — the 12-job sweep that surfaced this ran traffic-only by accident; schedule-driven jobs are unaffected.

## 2026-07-06 — Per-station fill priority (FillOrder) governs fill behavior, not just prompt tone

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `MarketSchedule.FillOrder` existed end-to-end (field, wire mapping, config import/export, poller → context) but was a weak prompt hint: rendered only when weather AND fuel were both available, filler ignored it entirely, weather/fuel were voiced whenever fetched (fixtures, not fill), and the web UI never exposed it. ARN wants to choose, per station, which sources fill a short read and in what order — while the on-air structure stays canonical.

**Decision:** FillOrder is now the per-station fill mechanism. (1) Generator: a fetched source reaches the writer only when listed in FillOrder (exception: a major weather ALERT always reaches the writer and leads — safety content never drops on priority); the draft rule states weather/fuel are fill-not-fixtures, voiced only when the read would land short, reached for in FillOrder priority; placement is explicitly decoupled — "priority decides WHAT earns airtime, never where it sits: weather always reads before fuel, fuel always closes, filler is appended automatically after the text". Filler's rank is surfaced to the writer as "the standing filler lines (appended automatically…)". (2) Orchestrator: both deterministic filler passes (pre-synthesis selection and post-synthesis rescue) are gated on Filler ∈ FillOrder — a station that omits filler has opted out of the cart. (3) Manual parity: `OrchestrationRequestDto`/`BroadcastQueueMessage` carry FillOrder (validated wire strings: weather/fuel/filler, no unknowns, no duplicates); absent → default [weather, fuel, filler]. (4) Web: the schedule editor's Content step gains a Fill-priority editor (reorder/exclude rows + excluded chips, warning row when a fill source's Content toggle is off); detail studio displays the priority.

**Rationale:** Selection-vs-placement decoupling is what ARN asked for ("if priority is fuel→weather→filler and you only need fuel and weather, it still reads weather then fuel"): priority is a resource-allocation choice, canonical read order is a format constraint listeners rely on. Deterministic gating (filler) plus data-block gating (weather/fuel) makes the priority real without restructuring generation.

**Consequences:** Behavior change: weather/fuel are no longer voiced unconditionally when fetched — they air when the read needs them (default FillOrder keeps all three eligible, so thin markets are unchanged; rich markets may now drop garnish in favor of traffic). Changed: `LlmScriptGenerator` (arg gating + priority rendering), `prompts/draft.md` (fill rules), `BroadcastOrchestrator` (fillerEligible gate on both passes), `OrchestrationValidation`/`OrchestrationContracts`/`BroadcastQueueMessage`/`QueueMessageMappingExtensions` (manual parity), web schedules feature (shared FillSource schema, editor, detail display). 20 new backend tests + web suite at 497 green. Pre-existing aside logged by the test pass: `ToBroadcastQueueMessage` uses Location as MarketId — separate fix.
**Addendum (same day):** live round-trip testing exposed that `TableStorageScheduleRepository` never persisted FillOrder at all — the pre-existing plumbing silently dead-ended at storage (every PUT read back as the model default). Fixed with a `FillOrderJson` entity column (lowercase wire strings; absent = default; unknown values/duplicates dropped on load; 3 round-trip tests). Verified on dev (`b2670fa`): PUT `[fuel,weather]` persists exactly; a `[fuel,weather]` (no filler) portlincoln trigger filled 15.0s with zero filler phrases and canonical placement (weather line before fuel, fuel closes) despite fuel-first priority; a `[filler]`-only trigger correctly kept fetched weather/fuel away from the writer and engaged filler rescue, degrading to the filler cart when the pool couldn't cover the residual — the known undershoot-best-fit residual tuning (see filler-rescue entry) is the remaining lever there.

**Context:** the ARN Technology Lead delivered the IBP-AUE-SPN-PRD-Traffic app registration (client c3b659e4-23f2-4522-b3f0-b0e48b73fa96) 7 Jul 2026, mirroring Test's config: single-tenant ARN (91d5bc47-...), Operator+Admin app roles, SWA redirect URI, ID tokens, admin consent. Prod had been deployed 5 Jul fail-closed with a throwaway client ID (auth phase 1).

Seeded AadClientId/AadClientSecret into IBP-AUE-PRD-KYV-APP01 (temporary firewall allow for the CLI write, re-locked to Disabled/Deny immediately after — the KV's public data plane stayed off throughout).
