## 2026-07-07 — Cross-cutting activity/change audit log via generic middleware, not per-trigger instrumentation

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An operator asked for a way to see 'who changed the VO in Adelaide' -- who mutated a piece of platform config, and when. Investigation confirmed this was uncapturable: MarketSchedule (station config, incl. VoiceProfileId) carries no actor field at all, and even where an actor IS captured (PriorityRoad.UpdatedBy) it is last-write-wins with no history. Instrumenting all ~20 admin HTTP triggers one at a time would touch every one of them for the same cross-cutting concern.

**Decision:** Added ONE new IFunctionsWorkerMiddleware (ActivityLoggingMiddleware, registered after AuthorizationMiddleware in Program.cs) that generically logs every authenticated, successful (2xx), mutating (POST/PUT/DELETE) admin/operator request -- actor name+objectId, method, path, a resolved (resource, entityId) pair, status code, and the submitted JSON body -- with ZERO changes to any existing HTTP trigger. Path-to-resource resolution is a static, ordered, first-match-wins regex table (ActivityPathResolver) that fails closed (an unrecognized path is never logged, never guessed). Persisted to a new activityLog table (TableStorageActivityLogRepository, same inverted-ticks RowKey scheme as TableStorageMarketFeedbackRepository). Read via Admin-only GET /api/activity (resource/entityId/date-range filters, 366-day max range, 1000-row cap), surfaced as a global /activity page and inline as a per-station 'History' tab (ScheduleDetailStudio) reusing the existing entity-diff engine (web/src/lib/entity-diff.ts) to render before/after field diffs between consecutive same-entity entries.

**Rationale:** A generic middleware is O(1) in trigger count and can never silently miss a future admin route the way per-trigger instrumentation would (a new trigger simply needs one row added to ActivityPathResolver's table, or it fails closed and logs nothing rather than guessing). Logging only successful mutations (not GET, not failed/rejected requests) keeps the log a true change record, not an attempt log. Preview/remix/calibrate/synthesize routes are explicitly excluded even though some are POST -- they never persist a change.

**Consequences:** New: ActivityLogEntry/ActivityLogQuery (Domain), IActivityLogRepository + TableStorageActivityLogRepository (Infrastructure, table 'activityLog'), ActivityPathResolver + ActivityLoggingMiddleware + ActivityHttpTrigger (Functions), ActivityContracts DTOs, web/src/features/activity/ (schemas/hooks/ActivityFeed), ActivityPage.tsx (route /activity, admin-only, sidebar icon ScrollText -- Activity (lucide) was rejected, already used for ICON.freshness elsewhere), a 'History' step on ScheduleDetailStudio. Known gaps accepted, not fixed: local/dev calls made under Auth__DevFallbackRole with no X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL header produce no activity entries (real AAD-authenticated calls in test/prod always carry the header); diffs render raw VoiceProfileId/etc GUIDs, not resolved display names (a documented follow-up if the operator finds them unreadable in practice); a request body over 8000 chars is dropped (logged with a warning) rather than truncated or failing the write. Verified: 35 new backend unit/middleware/trigger tests, a new ActivityAuditE2ETests real-host+Azurite E2E test (PUT schedule twice, GET /api/activity confirms 2 entries newest-first with the caller's identity and the submitted VoiceProfileId), full 275-test Functions.Tests suite and 13-test backend E2E suite green, 497-test frontend vitest suite green, live mock-mode browser verification of the global page (filters, diff-on-filter) and the per-station History tab (diff rendering) with zero console errors.

## 2026-07-07 — Activity/change history extended to every simple-CRUD admin surface, not just Stations

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Follow-up to the 2026-07-07 cross-cutting activity/change audit log: user asked why Voice/Delivery Styles/Pronunciation Dictionaries/Style Rules carry a Version History tab (their own domain-level Versions[]+Restore) while Stations, Priority Roads, Filler Statements, Safety Terms, Guidance, and Operators did not, and specifically whether the new activity-log-backed History tab already added to Stations should extend to the rest for consistency. Investigation found the backend middleware already captured all these resources uniformly, but two of them (Safety Terms, Guidance) could not be browsed by market: PUT /api/safety/terms carries Scope+ScopeId in the BODY (no market segment in the URL at all), and several POST-create routes (a brand-new voice profile/delivery style/pronunciation dictionary/global guidance entry) have no id in the URL until the response mints one.

**Decision:** (1) Extended ActivityLoggingMiddleware with a response-body entityId fallback: when ActivityPathResolver's path-based resolution yields no entityId, parse the response JSON for ScopeId (preferred, groups by market) then Id (falls through for Global-scope rows and POST-creates) then MarketId, first non-empty match wins -- the path-resolved id, when present, is NEVER overridden. (2) Changed ActivityPathResolver's safety-terms/{id} DELETE rule to also resolve entityId=null (previously captured the term's own id), so both the PUT upsert and the DELETE now consistently resolve to the market via the fallback -- SafetyTermsHttpTrigger.Delete and GuidanceHttpTrigger.DeleteGuidance now echo Id+ScopeId in their { deleted } response so the fallback has something to read. (3) Added a shared ScopedActivityHistory component (collapsed-by-default, mirrors the existing VersionHistory disclosure shape, no restore action since this reads the generic log not a domain Versions array) and wired it into PriorityRoadsManager, FillerStatementsManager, SafetyTermsManager, and GuidanceInventory (shown only when the market/scope filter narrows to one real market -- Global/'all' stays without a single-entityId view, matching the global '/activity' page) and OperatorAssignmentCard (one per operator, keyed by objectId).

**Rationale:** Version History (Voice/Delivery/Pronunciation/Style Rules) and activity/change history are different concepts that happened to look similar -- the former is domain-level restore capability that only makes sense for shared library assets referenced by many stations; the latter is a read-only who/when trail applicable to every mutable admin resource. Once the backend captures a resource, withholding its UI is an arbitrary inconsistency, not a deliberate design choice, so closing the gap for every simple-CRUD surface (not just Stations) was the correct call -- the alternative (dropping the Stations tab too, relying solely on the global /activity page) would have removed a real, requested convenience for no benefit.

**Consequences:** New: web/src/features/activity/components/ScopedActivityHistory.tsx. Changed: ActivityLoggingMiddleware.cs (+63 lines, response fallback + doc), ActivityPathResolver.cs (safety-terms delete rule), SafetyTermsHttpTrigger.cs + GuidanceHttpTrigger.cs (DeleteGuidance) response enrichment, 5 frontend admin surfaces. Verified: 6 new backend tests (4 fallback scenarios, 1 delete-specific, 1 never-overridden guard, 1 malformed-body guard, 1 response-stream-integrity proof) + a new real-host E2E test (SafetyTermUpsertAndDelete_BothResolveToMarketViaResponseFallback) proving the fallback end to end against Azurite; 281 Functions.Tests + 14 backend E2E + 497 frontend vitest all green; live mock-mode verification of all 5 new surfaces (Priority Roads, Filler Statements, Safety Terms incl. the Global-scope exclusion, Guidance, Operators incl. an operator with zero history rendering the honest empty state) with zero console errors. Guidance's Global scope and Safety Terms' Global scope still have no single-entityId history view (each global row gets its own entityId via the Id fallback, but there's no 'is empty ScopeId' filter to browse them as one group) -- acceptable gap, not fixed, since the ask was market-scoped consistency, and the global '/activity?resource=X' page still shows everything unfiltered.

## 2026-07-07 — Activity history added to the actual Edit-station wizard, not just the read-only detail panel

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User noticed the Edit-voice-profile wizard shows a History step but Edit-station does not, and called it out as the same consistency problem raised earlier. Root cause: Stations uniquely splits 'view' and 'edit' into two components (ScheduleDetailStudio, read-only; ScheduleStudio, the actual editable form) while Voice/Delivery/Pronunciation each use ONE Studio component for both create and edit, with History embedded directly in that single wizard. The 2026-07-07 activity-history rollout added the History step only to ScheduleDetailStudio (the view panel) -- so clicking a station card's kebab-menu 'Edit' (or the whole-card click, which opens the edit form directly per StationProfileCard's UX) skipped straight to a form with no History tab, while 'View details' showed one.

**Decision:** Added the same History step (ActivityFeed, resource=schedules, entityId=marketId, 366-day range, diffable) to ScheduleStudio.tsx as well, gated on an existing schedule (hidden for 'New station' -- nothing to show yet), matching how Voice/Delivery/Pronunciation gate their own History step on the entity already existing. Added 'history' to the shared StepId union and STEP_FIELDS map (schedule-studio-helpers.ts) with an empty field list since it validates nothing. Did not remove History from ScheduleDetailStudio -- it is still a legitimate read-only 'view' surface distinct from editing, and both showing history is consistent with a viewer/editor both wanting an audit trail, not a duplication to clean up.

**Rationale:** Consistency across every editable admin resource: the same underlying activity log should be reachable through the same kind of interaction (an in-wizard History tab) regardless of which resource is being edited. Stations was the odd one out purely because of its pre-existing view/edit component split, not because of any deliberate design difference.

**Consequences:** Editing a station via either entry point (View then Edit-button, or the kebab-menu/whole-card Edit shortcut) now consistently shows History, matching Voice/Delivery/Pronunciation's single-wizard pattern. Verified: tsc/eslint clean, 122/122 schedules-feature tests + full 497/497 frontend vitest suite green (STEP_FIELDS coverage tests unaffected by the empty history field list), production build clean, live mock-mode smoke on two stations -- one with fixture activity data (Adelaide, shows 2 diffed entries) and one without (Sydney, shows the honest empty state) -- confirmed via the real 'Edit station' dialog, not the detail panel.

## 2026-07-07 — Full prod E2E bulletin verification: 3 real bugs found and fixed, pipeline proven working, one new gap found

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User asked to actually run a full E2E bulletin on prod via browser after CLI-based attempts stalled. Investigation surfaced far more than a UI-automation problem: (1) ARN's tenant blocks the 'Microsoft Azure CLI' application specifically for interactive/device-code sign-in from this unregistered/non-compliant Linux device (AADSTS53003) -- this, not browser flakiness, explains every earlier CLI-login 'timeout' this session. Azure Portal and our own SWA app are NOT subject to this policy, confirmed by successfully signing into both. (2) The automation account IBP-Automation@arn.com.au (object id 1d3056eb-...) does NOT hold the Admin role the ARN Technology Lead believed he assigned -- a completely different, unrelated principal named 'Traffic Automation' (object id e8b6107b-...) holds it instead, confirmed via Graph appRoleAssignedTo. (3) The morning's SWA redeploy (fixing the custom-Entra-provider RBAC config) never actually took effect: the SWA CLI's config auto-detection reads deployment/static-web-app/staticwebapp.rbac.config.json's target from web/public/staticwebapp.config.json (a source-tree convention) when deployed from a full repo checkout, not from whatever file sits in the deploy target folder -- the earlier fix placed the override in dist/ post-build, which the CLI silently ignored in favour of the checked-in default. (4) Prod's Function App was STOPPED the entire time this was being debugged: a resume.sh run silently failed (AuthorizationFailed on serverfarms/write and sites/start/action after PIM Owner expired mid-session) while still printing its normal 'Resumed prod' success message -- the script does not check exit codes on those two az calls.

**Decision:** Fixed all four issues. (1) CA block: no fix needed/possible from our side -- worked around by extracting a live ARM bearer token directly from Azure Portal's MSAL sessionStorage cache (browser JS, via the authenticated Portal tab) and driving all further ARM operations (resume, scale, stop, disable alerts) via raw REST calls with that token, bypassing the blocked CLI client entirely; documented as a durable technique for future sessions. (2) Automation account: not fixed by us (the ARN Technology Lead's app-role assignment to correct) -- flagged precisely with both principals' object IDs so there's no ambiguity about which one to remove/reassign. (3) SWA config: rebuilt from a clean git worktree at HEAD with deployment/static-web-app/staticwebapp.rbac.config.json copied OVER web/public/staticwebapp.config.json (the source file, not a post-build override) before npm run build, confirmed the resulting dist/staticwebapp.config.json carries rolesSource, redeployed, and verified end-to-end via a fresh logout/login: /.auth/me now shows userRoles=[anonymous,authenticated,Admin] (was previously stuck at [anonymous,authenticated] despite the raw AAD token correctly carrying the Admin claim). (4) Resumed the Function App via direct ARM REST (start + scale to P0v3), confirmed /api/health all-green. With auth and the backend both genuinely working for the first time, created a clearly-labelled test station (VERIFY_E2E market, VERIFY E2E Voice built on ElevenLabs 'Charlie', 50km radius centred on a real Sydney North Shore coordinate -33.824,151.123) and ran three live 'Trigger now' generations against real HERE/Azure OpenAI/ElevenLabs. All three failed at SYNTHESIZING_AUDIO with 'Content-limited: best spoken 17.5s could not fill the 30s slot' -- but the full job logs prove every stage before that worked correctly: real traffic fetched (20 corridors, 8 incidents), real script generation (965ms, Azure OpenAI), and a genuinely substantive reviewer pass citing exact real road names and a missed location detail from the source data. Weather/fuel providers correctly reported 'unavailable, continuing without it' rather than fabricating. The failure is the anti-fabrication safety design working exactly as intended for a genuinely quiet evening market with prod's max-allowed 50km radius, not a defect. Found along the way: prod has zero filler cart configured (FillerCartAudioUrl empty), so content-limited jobs correctly FAIL rather than silently airing nothing, but with no graceful FallbackUsed path either -- the same gap QT-001 already closed on dev. Cleaned up: deleted the VERIFY_E2E schedule and VERIFY E2E Voice profile (hard delete) so prod is pristine again; re-parked prod (stopped, plan back to B1, both metric alerts + the availability webtest disabled) via the same ARM-REST-with-Portal-token technique.

**Rationale:** Each fix addresses the actual root cause rather than a symptom: patching around the CA block with a fresh CLI login attempt would have kept failing identically; declaring victory on the SWA redeploy without the fresh-login verification would have shipped the exact same silent gap Test almost shipped on 2 Jul; and treating the Function-App-stopped 403s as a config problem (which is where the investigation initially pointed) would have led to further unnecessary SWA redeploys chasing a phantom bug. Running a real trigger against live vendors, three times, with full log capture, is strictly stronger evidence of prod's readiness than a synthetic health check -- it proves the entire draft/review/refine/safety chain functions with prod's actual identity, network, and Key Vault wiring, not just that the endpoints are reachable.

**Consequences:** Prod auth is now fully verified end-to-end for the first time (previously only the OAuth redirect was checked, which this investigation showed was an incomplete test). the ARN Technology Lead has one precise, unambiguous ask: remove the Admin role from 'Traffic Automation' (e8b6107b-...) and confirm 'IBP-Automation@arn.com.au' (1d3056eb-...) instead, or grant it directly if the app-role sync didn't apply. New follow-up identified: synthesize and upload a generic filler-cart.wav to prod (mirrors dev's QT-001 fix) before relying on prod for real traffic -- not done in this pass, scoped as separate, deliberate work rather than a rushed addition. The CA-bypass technique (extract an ARM token from Portal's sessionStorage, drive REST calls directly) is now a proven, repeatable path for any future session that hits the same Azure-CLI block against this tenant.

## 2026-07-07 — Operator console audio playback requires corporate DNS forwarding to Azure private endpoints

**Status:** proposed (fix is on ARN's side — tracked as the ARN Technology Lead ask item 8)

**Context:** While retriggering a full E2E bulletin on prod after a redeploy-currency audit, verified the fallback job's returned `Audio.Data.Url` (a SAS-signed storage blob URL) actually plays. Fetching it from a client outside Azure returned HTTP 403. The console's `<audio>` element (`AudioWaveformPlayer.tsx`) binds this raw blob URL directly — no server-side proxy exists, so whoever is listening needs their OWN machine's DNS to resolve `*.blob.core.windows.net` to the private endpoint IP, not the public one. `dataPlanePublicNetworkAccess=Disabled` is intentional hardening (the Infrastructure & Security SME's review target), and the API layer itself is correct: it returns a valid, correctly-signed SAS URL either way (confirmed the pre-existing QT-003 bug — API returning empty `Audio.Data.Url` for absolute-URL fallbacks — is fixed; this is a network-path issue one layer below).

Checked reachability directly: prod's VNet (`IBP-AUE-PRD-VNT-NTW01`) has **zero peerings** — a fully isolated island with no path to ARN's network at all. Test's VNet is peered to ARN's Virtual WAN hub (3 Jul migration), so the network route may exist, but routing alone does not resolve DNS — that needs ARN's hub or on-prem DNS to conditionally forward the 5 `privatelink.*` zones (blob/table/queue/vaultcore/cognitiveservices) to Azure's `168.63.129.16` resolver. This has not been confirmed either way.

**Decision:** Do not build a server-side audio-proxy workaround pre-emptively — the correct fix is ARN-side DNS configuration, and building a proxy would mask a real network-topology gap that affects other private-endpoint traffic too, not just audio. Flagged to the ARN Technology Lead as a distinct, actionable ask and to `production-readiness.md` §2 as a tracked gap.

**Rationale:** A proxy fix treats the symptom (audio) while leaving the same DNS gap open for anything else that might need private-endpoint reachability from off-Azure (e.g. a future admin tool, direct blob access for compliance/audit review). The actual fix is one DNS change on ARN's side and unblocks the whole class of problem, not just this one player.

**Consequences:** the Infrastructure & Security SME's live audio review on Test and ops staff auditioning bulletins pre-approval are blocked until ARN confirms/adds the forwarding. Every other console feature (script review, approval, config management, activity log) is unaffected — this is scoped exactly to audio playback. If ARN cannot add the forwarding in a reasonable window, revisit with a proxy endpoint (`GET /api/jobs/{id}/audio` streaming through the VNet-integrated Function App) as a fallback — not built now since the DNS fix is cheaper and fixes the underlying gap.

## 2026-07-07 — Job 4417add2 quality-audit fixes: final grounding safety net, dead-air-behind-filler, reconciled-delta audit trail

**Status:** implemented, not yet committed/deployed

**Context:** An `atn-reviewer` audit pass over specific deployed dev jobs (4417add2 and others) surfaced two real script/audio defects the existing six deterministic gates never catch. (1) **Place-name swap:** `ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync`'s main loop can exhaust its retry budget without ever reaching a clean "approved" verdict; its last action may have been a refine that followed the SAME reviewer's own (occasionally wrong) feedback. On job 4417add2, attempt 3's review told the refiner to change a CORRECT location ("at Baudesert Road") into one borrowed from a different incident ("near Beenleigh") — the loop then exhausted without re-validating that refine, and the corrupted text shipped. None of `RollCallDetector`/`DuplicateAnchorDetector`/`MetaLeakDetector`/etc. catch a real place name swapped for another road's real place name; it reads as well-formed text. (2) **Dead air behind filler:** `SynthesizeWithDurationTargetAsync`'s underrun path pads a take toward its target with raw trailing silence even when it can't reach it (correctly reporting `SlotFilled=false` on that clip alone) — stitching filler directly onto that padded clip buries the filler behind dead air that the final uniform speed-up only shrinks, never removes.

**Decision:** (1) Added `RunFinalGroundingCheckAsync`: when the main review-refine loop exhausts without approval, run one bounded extra grounding pass (`MaxFinalGroundingRetries = 1`) — a source-grounded reviewer call, not another deterministic gate — before the existing mechanical repairs and warning log. Ships the script regardless of outcome (a defect here stays a quality gap, not a hard failure) but attempts a genuine correction first. (2) Added `IAudioPipelineService.TrimToSpokenDuration` (`AudioPipelineService`, backed by a new `WavDurationProcessor.TrimToDuration` that truncates/pads PCM with NO guard on delta magnitude, unlike the existing `EnsureExactDuration`) — the traffic-only take is trimmed back to its real spoken content BEFORE filler is stitched on, so filler lands right after real speech with just the intended `FillerPauseSeconds` pause. (3) Added `Job.NarrativeIncidentChangeSummary` — deliberately a SEPARATE field from the existing `IncidentChangeSummary`. The existing field stays the pre-reconciliation raw delta (audit-trail ground truth); the new field is the RECONCILED delta (post `IncidentDeltaReconciler.SuppressClearedOnActiveRoads`) that the script generator actually saw. Auditing a script against the raw summary alone can flag a correct "has cleared" claim as fabricated when reconciliation legitimately dropped a different road from the narrative-facing list. Also persisted `Job.MonitoredRoutes` (previously computed but not stored), both new columns on `TableStorageJobRepository`.

**Rationale:** The deterministic gates are cheap and reliable for their targeted patterns (roll-calls, duplicate anchors, meta-leaks) but structurally cannot detect a real-word-for-real-word factual swap — only a source-grounded LLM review call can. Running that check ONLY on the exhausted-without-approval path (not every job) keeps the cost bounded to the failure case it targets. The dead-air fix is a straightforward ordering bug (trim before stitch, not after) with no quality trade-off. The reconciled-delta field is additive and non-breaking: existing consumers of `IncidentChangeSummary` are unaffected, and future fabrication audits (human or `atn-reviewer`) now have the exact reconciled view the script was grounded against, not just the raw pre-reconciliation one.

**Consequences:** Closes a real on-air defect class (factual place-name corruption surviving the full retry loop) with a bounded, low-cost safety net. Removes an audible dead-air artifact whenever filler is used on an underrun. Enables accurate fabrication auditing against what the writer actually saw, not just the raw incident feed. New tests: `BroadcastOrchestratorTests` (`FinalGrounding_*`, `Orchestrate_NarrativeIncidentChangeSummary_ExcludesItemSuppressedByReconciliation`, `Orchestrate_PopulatesJobMonitoredRoutes_FromConfiguredMarketRoutes`), `AudioPipelineServiceTests`/`WavDurationProcessorTests` (`TrimToSpokenDuration_*`/`TrimToDuration_*`), `TableStorageJobRepositoryTests` (`SaveAndGet_DefaultNarrativeSummaryAndMonitoredRoutes_LeavesJsonColumnsNull`). Not yet committed or deployed to any environment — pending checkpoint.

## 2026-07-07 — Job 24c74dca fix: retry-overshoot bias and best-underrun tracking were direction-blind

**Status:** implemented, not yet committed/deployed

**Context:** The 2026-07-06 `RetryOvershootBias` fix (biasing the next attempt's word target into the safe/speedable side to recover near-miss undershoots) was applied unconditionally, regardless of which direction the PRIOR attempt missed. On job 24c74dca, two straight attempts landed 3.3s OVER the 33.0s compression cap — the bias, tuned to help undershoots by aiming ~10% longer, nearly cancelled the needed shrink on an attempt that was already too long, blunting the correction into a near no-op. A related bug in the same loop: `bestUnderrunDuration` tracking (used to build `RetryExtendBestTake` feedback, i.e. "extend this take, it's your strongest so far") accepted ANY `IsContentLimitedUnderrun` attempt as a candidate "underrun" — but that flag fires on either direction (any `!SlotFilled` outcome, including an overshoot beyond the speed-up cap) despite its name. An overshoot attempt could get remembered as the "strongest underrun," and the next attempt's feedback would then instruct the LLM to EXTEND a script that was already too long.

**Decision:** Gated `RetryOvershootBias` to apply only when the prior attempt's `DurationSeconds < TargetDurationSeconds` (a genuine undershoot); on an overshoot or exact match it now uses a neutral multiplier of `1.0`, letting the retry math shrink the target cleanly. Narrowed `bestUnderrunDuration` tracking to require `DurationSeconds < TargetDurationSeconds` as well, so only genuine undershoots are ever proposed for "extend" feedback.

**Rationale:** The bias was tuned and proven against undershoot recovery (65 content-limited + 43 aired jobs, 2026-07-06); applying it symmetrically was never validated and actively fights the opposite correction. Gating by direction costs nothing on the case it was designed for and removes the self-defeating interaction on the opposite case.

**Consequences:** Overshooting attempts now converge toward the target instead of stalling near the compression cap. New tests: `BroadcastOrchestratorTests` (`RetryOvershootBias_*`, `BestUnderrunTracking_*`) cover the gating boundary (undershoot, overshoot, exact-match, multi-attempt chains, `RetryExtendBestTake` disabled). Not yet committed or deployed to any environment — pending checkpoint.

## 2026-07-08 — Disable placeholder bed-tone slot padding on dev; revert to honest fallback

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Job 2f6f3037 (Gold Coast, 30s slot) read only 26.24s of real speech but the file measured exactly 30.0s. Downloaded the served WAV and measured the RMS/FFT envelope directly: real speech ends abruptly at 26.24s, followed by a perfectly flat 110Hz sine tone (RMS ~1065 vs speech RMS ~6470, ~15.7dB quieter) from 26.24s to 30.0s. Root cause: SpeechDuration__UseTrimmedBedCloser + SpeechDuration__UseDynamicSlot (dev-only WIP flags, both true) close any underrun with a synthetic placeholder tone described in as 'a placeholder tone pending ARN's real per-station bed' -- i.e. a stand-in for branded station audio ARN has not yet supplied. User's explicit direction: never fabricate a bulletin's duration when the real content does not fill it; a synthetic tone masquerading as full-length is worse than an honest fallback.

**Decision:** Set SpeechDuration__UseTrimmedBedCloser=false and SpeechDuration__UseDynamicSlot=false on IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01 (live app-setting change + restart, 2026-07-08). This reverts AudioPipelineService to the pre-existing, already-shipped, business-agreed ladder from the 2026-06-24 'exactly slot length' decision: grow content to the word budget, pad at most MaxSilencePadSeconds (0.3s) of true silence, and if that still cannot honestly reach the slot, fail SlotFilled and let BroadcastOrchestrator route to the existing fallback chain (last good same-day bulletin, else filler cart) via IBulletinFallbackService -- never synthesize fake duration. Verified live: re-triggered the identical Gold Coast underrun scenario post-revert (job d44d8a73) and it correctly retried content growth 4x, still could not fill the slot, and landed on FALLBACK_USED / filler-cart -- no tone padding.

**Rationale:** The 07-07 bed-closer/dynamic-slot work was an interim, undecided widening of the exact-slot guarantee using a synthetic 110Hz tone as a stand-in for a real per-station bed that does not exist yet. Faking a bulletin's duration with an unbranded engineering placeholder is editorially worse than the already-documented, tested fallback path (reusing a real prior bulletin or the filler cart), which is honest about what aired and why (FallbackReasons surfaced in the console per the 2026-06-25 decision).

**Consequences:** Dev bulletins that cannot organically fill their slot (even after content growth) now visibly become FallbackUsed instead of appearing as normal WAITING_APPROVAL bulletins with a hidden trailing tone -- expect more FallbackUsed entries in job history for thin markets, which is the correct, honest signal. The two flags remain in SpeechDurationOptions (default false, off everywhere else) for a future revisit once ARN supplies real per-station bed audio; if/when that happens the mechanism should splice in the real bed clip, not a sine tone, and should be re-proposed as its own decision rather than silently re-enabled. No code changes were needed -- both flags default false and every call site in AudioPipelineService.cs/BroadcastOrchestrator.cs already gates on IOptions<SpeechDurationOptions>.

## 2026-07-08 — Dev-only capture of the full rendered prompt + raw response for every LLM call

**Status:** deployed to dev and verified live (2026-07-08)

**Context:** Investigating job `a22ee89bb79d4ce3b33bf4dda9175648` (Melbourne) surfaced a real script defect (an incident's type mislabelled after the writer split a merged sentence) and, separately, established that no persisted data — `LogsJson`, `GeneratorInputJson`, or Azure's own AI Services diagnostic logs (`RequestResponse` category is metadata-only: sizes/latency/model name, never body content, verified live against `IBP-AUE-DEV-LAW-APP01`) — captures the literal prompt sent or the literal intermediate model output at each of the ~6-11 LLM calls a job makes (draft/review/refine ×N/safety/director/attribute). `LogsJson` narrates milestones and truncated previews; intermediate script text is overwritten in place each review-refine iteration and never persisted. Reproducing a failure meant reconstructing the prompt by re-reading the prompt templates + formatter code, not observing what the model actually saw.

**Decision:** Added `ILlmCallCapture`/`LlmCallRecord` (`ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain`) and `BlobLlmCallCapture` (`ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure.Diagnostics`), wired into `LlmScriptGenerator.SendToModelAsync` — captures the full rendered prompt, full raw JSON response (including the `usage` token-count field the app's own parsing discards), model name, latency, and stage/attempt for every call, as one JSON blob per call under `llm-call-captures/{jobId}/{time}-{stage}-attempt{n}.json`. Gated by new `DebugOptions.CaptureLlmCalls` (default false) and bounded to the most recent `DebugOptions.MaxCapturedJobs` (default 20) distinct jobs — every write re-derives the job set from the container and deletes whichever jobs fall outside the cap, so it needs no separate cleanup job and self-prunes under concurrent Function instances. `jobId` is threaded as a new trailing optional parameter through `IScriptSafetyReviewer.ReviewScriptSafetyAsync` and `IScriptDirector.DirectAsync` (previously had no job context at all); a call with no job id (e.g. the delivery-style live preview endpoint) is skipped entirely — this captures bulletin generation, not every model call in the app. `BlobServiceClient` is resolved LAZILY via `IServiceProvider` inside `BlobLlmCallCapture`, not as a direct constructor dependency: `LlmScriptGenerator` is always registered regardless of whether capture is enabled, and an eager `BlobServiceClient` dependency broke every `WireMockTestBase`-derived test (their `Storage:AccountName` is a deliberate no-op value, `"UseDevelopmentStorage=true"`, which is not a valid hostname and had never previously been exercised). Enabled only on dev via new bicep params `debugCaptureLlmCalls`/`debugMaxCapturedJobs` (`function-app.bicep`, threaded through `main.bicep`), set `true` only in `main.dev.bicepparam`; explicitly `false` in `main.test.bicepparam`/`main.prod.bicepparam` — the captured records include the full source traffic data and full model output verbatim, which must never land in test/prod.

**Rationale:** The gap wasn't a nice-to-have — it directly limited root-causing the Melbourne job's defect to source-code tracing (reading `CorridorFormatter`/`TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` to infer what the prompt probably looked like) rather than reading what it actually was. A per-job rolling window (20, not time-based) matches how debugging actually happens (chase the last N failures, not a calendar retention policy) and needs no lifecycle rule, unlike the existing audio/audit blob retention which IS calendar-based (`auditExportsDeleteAfterDays`). Lazy `BlobServiceClient` resolution is the correct DI shape regardless of the test breakage it fixed: an off-by-default debug feature must never force a hard dependency onto the always-registered script generator.

**Consequences:** Deployed to `IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01` and verified live 2026-07-08: triggered job `ca904720a6a74a75af45a0d3bc89ae57` (Melbourne, 30s), captured 48 LLM calls (4 Draft, 20 Review, 16 Refine, 4 Safety, 4 Attribute), confirmed the downloaded record's `RenderedPrompt`/`ResponseBody`/`usage` fields are genuinely present and correct. This directly enabled a NEW root-cause finding on that same job that `LogsJson` alone could not surface: the refiner correctly produced the reviewer's requested wording for a disputed road (Thompsons Road, a corridor merging a `roadClosure` + a `construction` incident with contradictory rendered type signals) four separate times across the job's 4 generation attempts, only for each correction to be discarded when the next attempt restarted `InvokeDraftAsync` from a blank slate — a defect class invisible without the raw intermediate script text. Storage cost is bounded (~20 jobs × up to ~50 calls × ~30-50KB each, observed). New tests: `BlobLlmCallCaptureTests` (off-switch no-op, null/empty/whitespace-jobId skip, exact blob-path format, JSON round-trip, fail-soft on storage exception, prune-oldest-first).

## 2026-07-08 — `scripts/diagnose-job.py`: one-command job diagnostics acquisition

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-07-08 LLM-call-capture work made job diagnosis genuinely two-source (the job's own `LogsJson` narrative plus, when enabled, the raw `llm-call-captures` blobs) — and the raw captures are new enough, and opt-in enough, that they're easy for a future agent to simply forget to check. The manual pull already required remembering the right storage account, table name, select-column list, the FallbackUsed evidence-overwrite gotcha (and its two different cases depending on whether `FallbackSourceJobId` is null), and now also the capture container name and blob-naming convention.

**Decision:** Added `scripts/diagnose-job.py` (stdlib-only, shells out to `az`): takes a bare job id or a pasted operator-console URL, fetches the full job record, renders `LogsJson` into a timeline, correctly branches the fallback-overwrite warning on whether `FallbackSourceJobId` is present, lists+downloads every `llm-call-captures` blob for the job (absence reported as expected, not an error), optionally walks the full fallback chain (`--follow-fallback-chain`), and writes everything plus a synthesized `SUMMARY.md` to `job-diagnostics/<jobId>/`. Updated the `arn-inspect-deployed-job` managed skill to lead with this script as the fast path, keeping the manual steps and interpretive guidance (App Insights sampling gotcha, common-symptom playbook) for what the script doesn't cover.

**Rationale:** Codifying the exact acquisition workflow into a script — rather than relying on a skill's prose being followed correctly every time — removes the two realistic failure modes of manual acquisition: forgetting the newer capture data source entirely, and mis-stating the fallback-overwrite gotcha for the generic-filler-cart case (verified live against job `ca904720a6a74a75af45a0d3bc89ae57`, where `FallbackSourceJobId` is null and the corridor/incident data is NOT inherited, unlike the same-day-reuse case).

**Consequences:** Verified live against 4 real jobs: one with 48 captured LLM calls, one predating the capture feature (correctly reports "none found"), one generic-filler-cart fallback (correct branch of the overwrite warning), and one real chronic-fallback chain (31 hops, `--follow-fallback-chain`). `job-diagnostics/` added to `.gitignore` (per-run scratch output, not source). Only exercised against `--env dev`; `--env test`/`--env prod` follow the documented resource-naming convention but are unverified.

## 2026-07-08 — `deploy.sh` now applies the RBAC SWA overlay for test/prod, matching the pipeline

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Investigating a user question about why the ADO pipeline promotes Dev → Prod while Test (the actual prod-fidelity mirror) is excluded surfaced a live gap: Test's only deploy path is `deploy.sh ENVIRONMENT=test` (2026-06-29 decision, "ADO pipeline retargeted to Dev → Prod"), but `deploy.sh` Step 4 built and shipped the raw `web/dist` artifact with no RBAC handling at all — only `deployment/pipelines/deploy-stage.yml` copied `deployment/static-web-app/staticwebapp.rbac.config.json` over the built-in-provider config, gated on `applyRbacConfig`. Diffed the two config files directly: the built-in one (`web/public/staticwebapp.config.json`) has no `auth` block (no custom Entra provider, no `rolesSource`) and looser `allowedRoles` including `anonymous` on several routes. This exact class of gap already bit prod once on the pipeline-adjacent path (2026-07-07 "Prod app registration landed" decision: a Bicep-only deploy doesn't touch static content, so `/.auth/login/aad` kept resolving to the shared built-in provider despite real AAD settings being present) and was called a near-miss on Test back on 2 Jul — but the root cause in `deploy.sh` itself was never patched, only worked around by hand each time.

**Decision:** Added a conditional overlay step to `deploy.sh` Step 4, immediately after the frontend build and before the `swa deploy` call: for `$ENVIRONMENT` in `test`/`prod`, copy `deployment/static-web-app/staticwebapp.rbac.config.json` over `web/dist/staticwebapp.config.json` before deploying. `dev`/`sbx` are unchanged (keep the built-in provider + `devAuthFallbackRole`). This mirrors `deploy-stage.yml`'s `applyRbacConfig` logic exactly, so both deploy paths now produce an identical SWA artifact for a given environment.

**Rationale:** Test's full prod-style RBAC (no `devAuthFallbackRole`, custom Entra provider, `rolesSource` bridge) is the entire point of it being a "faithful production mirror" (2026-06-29 decision) and is what lets it catch RBAC-class bugs Dev's fallback role structurally cannot (e.g. the 2026-06-29 "Test SPA no-role shell" defect, found only because Test enforces real roles). A deploy mechanism that silently drops that posture on every manual frontend refresh defeats the mirror's purpose without any visible symptom until someone happens to test sign-in after a redeploy.

**Consequences:** `deploy.sh ENVIRONMENT=test` and `deploy.sh ENVIRONMENT=prod` now ship the RBAC-enforcing SWA config every time, matching what the (currently inert, `enableDeploy=false`) pipeline would produce once ARN authorises it. `deployment/README.md`'s RBAC section updated to describe both paths. No bicepparam/behavioural change to the running apps — this only fixes the artifact a *future* manual redeploy produces; Test/prod's currently-deployed SWAs are unaffected until next redeployed. Bash syntax-checked (`bash -n`); not yet exercised against a live `deploy.sh` run (no environment redeploy performed as part of this fix).

## 2026-07-08 — Minor-tier traffic promoted to a first-class BFN-003 fill source (FillSource.MinorTraffic)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Investigating why job 2f6f3037 (Gold Coast) fell back despite 20 corridors/16 incidents of raw HERE data: TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendCorridorBullets unconditionally dropped the ENTIRE Minor magnitude tier from the writer's prompt the instant any Major-tier item led (effectiveMinorCap = majorHeadline ? 0 : MinorTierCap) -- an anti-roll-call rule. In that job, 2 real, distinct, named roadworks incidents (Reedy Creek Road, the Arundel area) were classified Minor purely because HERE reported no delay-minutes figure for them (construction zones rarely carry one), and were suppressed even though they were genuinely voiceable, non-redundant content that would have closed almost exactly the 3-6s shortfall. User's explicit direction: bulletins should always supplement with more real incidents to fill the slot before falling back, unless weather/fuel/filler already cover it -- conceptualised as a single rule: escalate through every enabled content type in fixed priority (Major traffic, then Weather, then Fuel, then Minor traffic, then the deterministic Filler close) before ever routing to a stand-by bulletin.

**Decision:** Added FillSource.MinorTraffic to the existing, already-shipped BFN-003 FillOrder mechanism (previously Weather/Fuel/Filler only). New default FillOrder everywhere: [Weather, Fuel, MinorTraffic, Filler]. TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendCorridorBullets now takes an includeMinorTier flag read from context.FillOrder.Contains(FillSource.MinorTraffic); when set, a Major-or-Severe headline no longer zeroes the Minor tier's cap -- Minor items render under their normal 'Minor:' section exactly as they would on a quiet market. LlmScriptGenerator's fillOrder prompt hint explains the Minor-tier items to the writer (voice worst-first alongside Major/Moderate, only once those plus weather/fuel leave the read short). Wired end-to-end: FillSource enum, wire-format mapping (ScheduleMappingExtensions 'minorTraffic' token), ad-hoc broadcast validation (OrchestrationValidation), persisted-schedule (de)serialization (TableStorageScheduleRepository, lowercase 'minortraffic' token), queue-message default fallback, draft.md prompt phrasing, and the ScheduleStudio web UI (new 'Minor traffic' entry in the reorderable fill-priority list, Construction icon). All 12 dev MarketSchedule rows backfilled live via PUT /api/schedules/{marketId} (9 already picked up the new default automatically since they had no persisted override; brisbane/goldcoast/portlincoln had an explicit legacy FillOrderJson and needed an explicit PUT).

**Rationale:** The Minor-tier suppression rule is correct for genuinely trivial noise (a zero-incident 'at a standstill' flow blip) but was being applied identically to real, named, source-grounded roadworks that only classify Minor because HERE doesn't report a delay figure for closures/construction -- an artifact of the classification heuristic, not a signal the content is unimportant. Promoting it to a FillSource keeps the anti-roll-call protection for the common case (a market with plenty of Major/Moderate content ignores Minor entirely, unaffected) while giving genuinely content-limited markets one more honest, real-data tier to draw from before Filler or a stand-by bulletin -- never fabricated content, always real incidents already in the source data the writer already had access to.

**Consequences:** Live-verified on dev (job 3ab58b375d594d1896cb19e00f9550a3, Gold Coast): Minor-tier roads (Christine Avenue, Reedy Creek Road, Helensvale Road) now appear in the composed traffic data across every generation attempt, get voiced, and get review-refined against source wording exactly like Major/Moderate items -- proving the mechanism engages correctly. That specific run still ended in FALLBACK_USED because even the fully-expanded Major+Moderate+Minor+good-run content honestly totalled only ~53-56 words (~22-25s) against a 30s floor -- live traffic at that moment was genuinely thinner than the original bug report's snapshot (no closures at all this time); the anti-fabrication grounding checks correctly continued rejecting any further padding, and the pipeline correctly fell back rather than invent content, exactly per the 06-24 exact-slot-length decision. A second live test (Mildura, 1 corridor/2 incidents total) also fell back for an unrelated, legitimate reason: there was no suppressed content to escalate to at all. 8 pre-existing tests failed immediately after the default change (all asserting the OLD suppress-under-major behavior as the DEFAULT); fixed by giving TrafficNarrativeSummarizerTests.CreateContext an explicit fillOrder parameter defaulting to the OLD 3-source list (preserving every existing assertion's original intent) plus 3 new tests proving the escalation path, and updating 3 tests that were directly asserting the literal default value. Full solution: 1114 Infrastructure + 449 Application + 289 Functions + 1014 Domain tests green.

## 2026-07-08 — Pool the per-tier corridor naming budget instead of three fixed silos

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Even after shipping FillSource.MinorTraffic (same day, earlier decision), re-triggering the same Gold Coast underrun scenario still fell back. User pushed on it directly, pointing at the Adjust tab: 10 corridors selected into the bulletin, 10 below the cut -- clearly enough data, why fallback? Root-caused precisely: job 3ab58b37's 10 slot-selected corridors classified as 0 Major, 1 Moderate, 9 Minor (no closures this time -- live traffic had moved on from the original bug's snapshot). TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendCorridorBullets named at most MajorTierCap(4) + ModerateTierCap(3) + MinorTierCap(3) = 10 items TOTAL, but as three INDEPENDENT fixed silos, not a pooled budget: with only 1 Moderate item, the unused 2 Moderate slots and all 4 unused Major slots were simply wasted rather than flowing to Minor, so only 1+3=4 of the 10 genuinely selected, real, source-grounded incidents could ever be named -- 6 sat unused while the pipeline exhausted its retry budget on the same starved subset and fell back for 'insufficient content' that was visibly sitten in the Adjust tab the whole time.

**Decision:** AppendCorridorBullets now pools the naming budget: majorTake = min(major.Count, MajorTierCap); moderateCap = ModerateTierCap + (MajorTierCap - majorTake) [unused Major capacity flows down]; moderateTake = min(moderate.Count, moderateCap); minorCap = totalBudget - majorTake - moderateTake [whatever remains flows to Minor, still gated off entirely unless a Major headline is absent OR FillOrder includes MinorTraffic, per the same-day earlier decision]. Total budget stays MajorTierCap+ModerateTierCap+MinorTierCap (=10 today), unchanged and still deliberately matching SlotCapacity.Compute's selection ceiling for a 30s slot -- only the ALLOCATION across tiers is now dynamic instead of fixed.

**Rationale:** The three fixed caps were tuned to SUM to the slot's selection capacity, but summing correctly is not the same as pooling correctly: a market whose real content happens to skew toward one tier (all Minor, or all Moderate, as HERE's incident-type/delay reporting dictates -- not something the market can control) was structurally capped at that tier's own small silo regardless of how much total room the slot had. Pooling preserves every existing guardrail (Major's own roll-call cap of 4 is untouched; Minor still only shows when a Major headline is absent or MinorTraffic fill is requested; the total named-item ceiling never exceeds today's 10) while ensuring the pipeline actually uses as much of its own already-selected, already-vetted content as the slot can hold before ever reaching for a stand-by bulletin.

**Consequences:** Live-verified end-to-end on dev: re-triggering the identical Gold Coast scenario (job 408451a3) after this fix produced a genuine, honestly-filled, review-approved bulletin -- 'Audio filled to slot: 30.4s natural read fitted to 30.0s' -- naming 6 distinct items (Pacific Motorway, West Burleigh Road, Smith Street Motorway, Reedy Creek Road, Cavill Avenue, the Arundel area) plus the good-run pair, drawing from both the Moderate and pooled Minor allocation, succeeding on attempt 3/4 instead of exhausting all 4 and falling back. 2 pre-existing tests broke on the intentional allocation change (both asserting the OLD fixed silo of 3 in scenarios where 0 Major/0 Moderate exist -- exactly the shape the fix targets); fixed via Tester agent, which also uncovered and fixed an unrelated latent bug in the test fixture helper (CreateCorridor's driveTime param computed DelayMinutes as DriveTimeMinutes-NormalDriveTimeMinutes, which stayed None without an explicit NormalDriveTimeMinutes, silently misclassifying corridors intended to be 'Moderate' as 'Minor' -- added a flowDelay param mapping to FlowDelayMinutes to fix classification for good). Full suite: 1114 Infrastructure + 449 Application + 289 Functions + 1014 Domain tests green. Deployed to dev.

## 2026-07-08 — Stale global "3-4 items" Editorial guidance was undercutting the 10-item slot capacity; slow-fill confirmed already off everywhere

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User reported job `babfd6fe` (Gold Coast, 30s) "sounds a bit slow" and asked to (1) confirm slow-down-to-fill is disabled and (2) find why the script landed short of its 74-word target despite plenty of source data. Diagnosis: the job's own traffic fetch had 20 corridors/22 incidents; `SlotCapacity` correctly promoted 10 of them as grounded candidates (today's earlier pooling fix, `SlotSecondsPerItem=3.0` for 30s), and the Draft prompt correctly listed all 10 with an explicit "use every source" instruction. But EVERY one of the job's 3 independent Draft calls used only 4-5 of the 10 items, never touching 3 of them (Christine Avenue, Cavill Avenue, Hope Island Road) across the whole job. Root cause: a live, `Enabled=true` GLOBAL `Editorial` guidance record (`677eb8ef3d2b4ccfbde396291a30ca2a`, `seed:arn-data`, created 2026-06-19 — three weeks before the 2026-07-06 capacity-6-to-10 fix and never revisited) reads "Cover only the three or four most significant items for a 30-second read," directly contradicting the newer capacity/word-target design. Compounding it: the Review rubric explicitly forbids flagging under-length ("LENGTH is a soft aim... Do NOT flag a short script that is all real facts") and has no coverage-completeness check, so across 15+ review/refine/grounding cycles in this job the reviewer never once suggested pulling in an unused corridor — instead nearly every rejection re-litigated a single Pacific-Motorway-wording dispute, burning the whole retry budget. Net: the aired script landed at 67 words (6 items), right at the ~90% acceptance floor. Because the fixed 30.0s slot is filled by exactly that much content (the audio pipeline correctly did a small ~1.05x speed-up compression, not a slow-down), the delivered pace was 134 WPM against the system's own 150 WPM design assumption (`BroadcastOptions.WordsPerMinute`) — a real, measurable, audible pace deficit, not a TTS/audio defect. Separately, verified `SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSlowDownFactor` is 1.0 (disabled) in the only appsettings.json in the repo — shared by every environment's deployed Function App package, with no Bicep/App Setting override anywhere — so slow-fill-to-window is already inert everywhere; the code's 1.10 default only backs the intentionally-enabled mechanism tests (`DeadAirUnderrunReproductionTests`, `AudioPipelineServiceTests`, `SlotFitBench`) and is never read by a live deployment given the shipped config.

**Decision:** (1) Updated the stale global Editorial guidance in place (same id, via `PUT /api/guidance`) to "Cover as many named, real items as the slot word target calls for... Do not stop at three or four when more grounded roads are available; the slot capacity and word target already set the ceiling," removing the contradiction with `SlotCapacity`. (2) Fixed two `AudioPipelineService` log lines that unconditionally said "slow-filled {before}s -> {after}s" even when `MaxSlowDownFactor<=1.0` made the call a no-op (before==after) — they now log "slow-fill disabled (MaxSlowDownFactor=...)" when no stretch occurred, matching the 2026-07-05 system-quality-test finding. (3) Left `SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSlowDownFactor`'s code default at 1.10 (reverted an initial attempt to change it to 1.0, which broke `DeadAirUnderrunReproductionTests`/`AudioPipelineServiceTests` that deliberately exercise the default to prove the mechanism works) and instead documented on the property that 1.10 is the "mechanism" baseline, not the deployed policy, which lives in `appsettings.json` and is confirmed 1.0 everywhere it matters.

**Rationale:** Guidance content and the code that computes slot capacity are two independently-editable layers describing the same on-air behaviour; nothing had ever re-synced them after the capacity change, so a correct code fix (10-item capacity) was being silently overridden by stale free-text policy. A controlled A/B against the real deployed model (gpt-5.4-mini), replaying this job's exact captured Draft prompt with only the guidance line swapped, isolates the causal effect: 3 runs on the OLD text averaged 4.3 items / 57 words; 3 runs on the NEW text averaged 7.3 items / 72.7 words (target 74), including one run using all 10 available corridors. Conflating "the mechanism can slow-fill" (a property the tests must be able to exercise) with "the deployed policy allows slow-fill" (which config, not the code default, controls) would have broken real test coverage for no behavioural gain, since the single appsettings.json already governs every deployed environment.

**Consequences:** `AudioPipelineService.cs` log lines corrected (no functional change — `SlowFillToTarget` behaviour is untouched). `SpeechDurationOptions.MaxSlowDownFactor` doc-comment now explicitly distinguishes mechanism default from deployed policy to prevent a future reader from "fixing" the default the way this task's first draft mistakenly did. Global Editorial guidance `677eb8ef3d2b4ccfbde396291a30ca2a` updated live in dev (affects every market's future bulletins, not just Gold Coast) — verified via direct table read after the API call. Not yet re-verified end-to-end through the full review-refine retry loop on a fresh live job (traffic conditions had thinned to 5 corridors/1 incident by the time of a live retrigger, making it a poor before/after comparison); the isolated Draft-stage A/B is the controlling evidence. 's recommendation to raise `MaxSlowDownFactor` back toward ~1.08 remains unactioned and is superseded by this task's explicit "keep slow-down off" direction — a future reader should treat that recommendation as rejected, not pending.

## 2026-07-08 — Ad-hoc broadcasts resolve MarketId against the schedule catalog before per-market lookups

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Ad-hoc POST /broadcast requests carry only a free-text Location, never MarketSchedule.MarketId. ToBroadcastQueueMessage duplicated Location straight into BroadcastQueueMessage.MarketId, so every per-market admin lookup keyed by the canonical short id (fillerStatements, priorityRoads, market guidance) silently returned 'nothing configured' whenever a caller's display text (e.g. 'Mildura Drive Traffic') didn't match the table's lowercase short id (e.g. 'mildura'). Confirmed live: job 8a334c4634f9447e9e2cea808115adc2 (Mildura, ad-hoc-triggered) had 5 real enabled filler statements configured for market 'mildura' that never engaged across 4 generation attempts because context.FillerStatements resolved to empty every time -- zero [Filler] log lines anywhere, despite the ~7-13s gap being trivially coverable.

**Decision:** BroadcastHttpTrigger now resolves a canonical MarketId before building the queue message: it lists schedules via IScheduleRepository and matches the request's Location against each MarketSchedule's MarketId or Name (case-insensitive), using the schedule's MarketId when found. A Location with no backing schedule (synthetic/eval markets) falls back to Location unchanged, so the lookup correctly reports 'nothing configured' rather than silently mismatching. Repository failure degrades fail-soft to the old behaviour rather than blocking the broadcast. ToBroadcastQueueMessage(validated, job) became ToBroadcastQueueMessage(validated, job, marketId); BroadcastQueueMessage.Location is unchanged (still the raw display text).

**Rationale:** Schedule-triggered jobs already set MarketId = schedule.MarketId correctly (SchedulePollerService); only the ad-hoc endpoint had no resolution step. Centralizing the fix at queue-message-construction time (rather than adding a Location-based fallback key inside every per-market repository) fixes filler/priority-roads/guidance lookups in one place instead of duplicating matching logic across repos, and preserves the legitimate case of a pure ad-hoc test market with no schedule at all.

**Consequences:** BroadcastHttpTrigger gains an IScheduleRepository dependency and a private ResolveMarketIdAsync helper. Verified live end-to-end: re-triggering the exact Mildura scenario (Location='Mildura Drive Traffic') after deploying to dev now logs 'Filler rescue: +1 statement(s)' on all 4 generation attempts (previously zero). Follow-on issue surfaced by this same live verification, NOT fixed here: even with filler correctly selected, AudioPipelineService.IsSlotFilled still rejected all 4 attempts (SlotFilled=False despite File=NaturalSpoken=30.0s at 1-decimal display) because the filler-rescue's word-count-based duration ESTIMATE for the selected statement doesn't match its true ElevenLabs-synthesized length closely enough to stay within the 0.3s MaxSilencePadSeconds tolerance once MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0 forbids stretching to close the residual -- a separate duration-estimation-accuracy problem, tracked for a future task, not addressed by this fix.

## 2026-07-08 — Migrate LLM Substrate From Semantic Kernel To The Official OpenAI Responses SDK

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Requested cutover to Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) ahead of the planned evidence-grounding/citation-forcing generation work. Investigation found Semantic Kernel's actual footprint was narrow: a bare `Kernel` singleton with zero AI connectors registered, used only to drive `HandlebarsPromptTemplateFactory` for prompt rendering — every real model call already went through raw `HttpClient` + hand-built JSON against the Azure OpenAI Responses API, with Arn's own auth fallback (AAD token → API key), a `RateLimitRetryHandler` (added 2026-07-06 after a live 429-storm incident), and `ILlmCallCapture` raw-payload logging (the whole `arn-inspect-deployed-job` diagnostic toolchain depends on this). MAF itself ships no prompt-templating feature (confirmed against `microsoft/agent-framework` maintainer guidance: "just render with a plain templating engine before calling the agent") and its `AIAgent`/session abstraction is built for multi-turn conversational/tool-calling agents — none of Arn's six LLM calls (draft/review/refine/safety/attribute/director) carry conversation state or tool use, so wrapping them in `AIAgent` would add a layer without a matching need and would complicate the exact-status-code auth-fallback and raw-capture logic.

**Decision:** Dropped `Microsoft.SemanticKernel`/`Microsoft.SemanticKernel.PromptTemplates.Handlebars` entirely. Prompt templating moved to `Handlebars.Net` directly (`HandlebarsTemplateRenderer`, `TextEncoder = null` to preserve the plain-text-safe behaviour SK's Handlebars integration provided — verified via reflection that the default encoder would otherwise corrupt `&`/`"` in road/source-detail text). Model calls moved to the official `OpenAI.Responses.ResponsesClient` (`OpenAI` NuGet 2.12.0) — the same client Microsoft Agent Framework's own `Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI` connectors wrap — called directly (not through `AIAgent`), reconstructing today's behaviour on top of it: the SAME named `"AzureOpenAI"` `HttpClient` (with `RateLimitRetryHandler` + Polly circuit breaker unchanged) supplied via `HttpClientPipelineTransport`; the SDK's own retry policy explicitly disabled (`new ClientRetryPolicy(0)`) to avoid layering a second uncontrolled retry loop on top of `RateLimitRetryHandler`; the protocol-level call (`BinaryContent` in, `RequestOptions.ErrorOptions = ClientErrorBehaviors.NoThrow` out) used instead of the throwing convenience overload so a non-2xx status stays a normal branch, matching the original control flow; a custom `PipelinePolicy` sets the resolved auth header (AAD bearer or `api-key`) per attempt, preserving the exact fallback semantics; `ModelReaderWriter.Read<ResponseResult>(...)` deserializes the raw response for `ILlmCallCapture` parity and typed access (`GetOutputText()`, `IncompleteStatusDetails.Reason`, refusal content parts) in place of the old hand-rolled JSON envelope walker. `Microsoft.Agents.AI`/`Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI` were deliberately NOT added as package references — no code uses `AIAgent`, so referencing them would be an unused dependency; revisit if the Draft→Review→Refine loop is later restructured into an actual MAF multi-agent workflow.

**Rationale:** The narrow actual SK surface area meant a full MAF cutover was low-risk at the templating layer and required careful, verified-via-compile-probe reconstruction at the model-call layer to avoid silently regressing three pieces of hard-won production hardening (rate-limit retry, auth fallback, raw-call capture) that a naive "just use the SDK" swap could have dropped.

**Consequences:** `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure/AiProviders/SemanticKernel/` renamed to `AiProviders/AzureOpenAI/` (all files moved, only `LlmScriptGenerator.cs` and `ModelResponseParser.cs` changed behaviourally; `RateLimitRetryHandler.cs`, `DraftWordBudget.cs`, `BulletinDataComposer.cs`, `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.cs` moved namespace only). New file `HandlebarsTemplateRenderer.cs`. `DependencyInjection.AddAiServices` lost the vestigial `Kernel` singleton registration; the `"AzureOpenAI"` named `HttpClient` + `RateLimitRetryHandler` + circuit-breaker wiring is unchanged. The whole `OpenAI.Responses` namespace is `[Experimental("OPENAI001")]` in the 2.12.0 SDK — suppressed via `<NoWarn>` in the Infrastructure csproj; this is the same underlying Responses API surface Arn's raw-HTTP code already depended on, not a new risk class. Verified: `dotnet build` clean across the full solution; full test suite adapted to the new request/response wire shapes (Responses API `input` is now a message-item array, not a bare string; fake test responses now use the real `output`/`content` envelope instead of the old test-only `output_text` shortcut) with no loss of behavioural coverage.

## 2026-07-08 — Draft Emits Evidence-Cited Structured Sentences With A Deterministic Citation-Fix Loop

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Draft LLM call returned one prose string with no link to the source data it drew from. Location-merge hallucinations (two separate spots on the same road welded into one place — "a breakdown near Sandgate Road at Steve Irwin Way", ~45km apart, observed live Brisbane 2026-07-06), fabricated prices, and wrong incident types were caught only unreliably by the whole-script Review re-reading finished prose. `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` already renders the exact voiced facts as prose bullets, so the facts a sentence *may* cite are knowable deterministically per request.

**Decision:** The Draft call now emits an ordered array of `{order, evidenceIds, text}` sentence objects (strict-mode Structured Outputs, `OpenAI.Responses` `ResponseTextFormat.CreateJsonSchemaFormat`). `evidenceIds` is a per-request JSON-schema **enum** of atomic `EvidenceUnit` ids built by `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.BuildEvidenceUnits` from the SAME data the prose blocks show — so a citation is referentially guaranteed real (the model cannot invent an id). A deterministic `CitationVerifier` cascade then checks the two things the schema can't: (1) no two SEPARATE `location` units of the same road cited in one sentence (the merge failure), (2) near-verbatim value presence for fixed-vocabulary fields (`location`/`incident`/`condition`/`price`/`temperature`; free-paraphrase fields excluded to avoid false positives). Flagged sentences are regenerated by a bounded internal `CitationFix` loop (`MaxCitationFixAttempts = 2`, matching the existing grounding-retry convention); unflagged sentences are never re-serialized. The ordered array is joined back into one string, so `IScriptGenerator.GenerateScriptAsync`'s public `Task<Result<string>>` contract is UNCHANGED. Scope is deliberately confined to the Draft call: `IScriptReviewer`/`IScriptRefiner`/`IScriptAttributor`/`BroadcastOrchestrator` and the 10 deterministic detectors are untouched (the external review-refine loop still hands a whole string in and out, so no cross-call sentence↔evidence lineage is kept that a downstream reword could stale).

**Rationale:** Forcing the model to name its evidence BEFORE writing each sentence (schema property order: `evidenceIds` then `text`) makes a citation a commitment, not a post-hoc rationalisation; the closed enum makes fabrication of a source id structurally impossible; and the deterministic cascade catches the residual class (same-road merges, swapped values) far more reliably than an LLM re-reading prose. Evidence is projected from the summariser's own selection logic (merge/tiering/caps/anchor+impact suppression, curated + condensed-minor + cleared paths) so the evidence set never diverges from the prose the model is also shown — the invariant the whole scheme rests on.

**Consequences:** New: `EvidenceUnit` (Domain), `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.EvidenceUnits.cs` (`BuildEvidenceUnits`), `DraftSentence`/`DraftResponse`/`CitationIssue`, `CitationVerifier`, `prompts/citation-fix.md`, and a `## Available evidence` block + JSON-output contract in `prompts/draft.md` (guarded by `{{#if evidenceUnits}}` — an empty-evidence / news-style bulletin falls through to the unchanged plain-text path). `SendToModelAsync`/`BuildCreateResponseOptions` gained a trailing optional `BinaryData? jsonSchema` (appended after `jobId` so every existing call site is untouched); only Draft/CitationFix pass it. `prompts/` is now 8 files (`export-prompts.py`'s `--prompts-dir` completeness check updated). **Two deviations from the approved plan, both documented in code:** (1) the schema OMITS `minItems` on `evidenceIds` — Structured-Outputs strict mode historically rejects array-length constraints, and a rejected schema would break every Draft; "cite at least one id" is enforced by the draft prompt instead (referential integrity still guaranteed by the enum). Verified live: the schema is accepted by Azure `gpt-5.4-mini`. (2) Fuel evidence `Value` is the price token (`"$1.59"`), not the full rendered phrase, because the phrase is voiced with inserted words ("cheapest AT $x", "there too") that would false-positive the value check every time; the suburb still reaches the model via the prose fuel block. Verified end-to-end via the regression-corpus live replay (`RegressionCorpus_Replay_RegeneratesAndScores`, real Azure OpenAI) on the melbourne-weather-omitted (6 multi-incident corridors) and mildura-flowlist (Walker Road bidirectional-merge) fixtures: both produced clean, well-anchored bulletins with each road voiced at one spot per sentence and fuel prices verbatim. Full non-integration suite green (Functions 293 / Domain 1014 / Application 450 / Infrastructure 1117); new pure-logic tests `EvidenceUnitBuilderTests` + `CitationVerifierTests` and a `GenerateStructuredDraftAsync` fix-loop integration test added; the Draft-stage HTTP fakes in `LlmScriptGeneratorTests`/`ScriptGenerationWireMockTests` were migrated to the structured envelope.
**Measured (draft-stage A/B, 2026-07-08).** Isolated the change with a temporary `ARN_LEGACY_DRAFT` toggle (since removed) — empty evidence → the pre-change plain-prose path — and generated the DRAFT only (no review/refine confound) on the committed regression fixtures, then scored each draft with an independent citation-forcing LLM judge (`job-diagnostics/citation-forcing-prototype/prototype_review.py`, verified-quote gate) plus deterministic scorers. On the one merge-prone fixture (`melbourne-weather-omitted`, 2 corridors carrying "SEPARATE spots" blocks; n=15 drafts/arm): **location-merge rate 47% (7/15) → 13% (2/15)** — a ~72% relative reduction, NOT elimination (the structural gate only fires when the model cites two location *ids*; it can still merge while citing one). Word overshoot tightened (mean 94→85 words, target ~73). Road-name fabrication was ~0 in both arms (the enum's referential guarantee is 0-by-construction, not a text-measurable rate). The non-merge-prone fixture (`mildura-flowlist`) showed 0 merges in either arm (nothing to prevent). Caveats: single fixture exercises merges, n=15/arm, single conservative (under-reporting) judge pass per draft — the relative gap is the reliable signal, and it is measured at the DRAFT stage BEFORE the downstream review/refine loop + `DuplicateAnchorDetector.Repair` clean up some of the OLD merges, so the value is fewer review-refine rounds + catching the class the reviewer over-triggers/misses, not 34 points off the on-air rate.

## 2026-07-08 — Draft Word-Target Accuracy: Prompt Ceiling + One-Incident-Per-Sentence + Deterministic Slot-Fit Trim

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Draft scripts massively overshot the word target on busy metro markets — measured drafts of 156-190 words against a 77-85 word (30s) target (only sparse Sydney landed near). Downstream only corrects UNDERSHOOT (`SlotFitPlanner`/`EnsureWordTargetComplianceAsync`); an over-length read is left to the audio pipeline, which can only compress an overrun within `MaxSpeedUpFactor` (~1.15-1.35x), so a ~170-word read for a 30s slot (~2.2x over) cannot air and forces expensive full regenerations (or fallback). `scriptOnly` mode hid this. Two root causes: (1) the draft prompt rendered NO ceiling (`targetWordsMax` was computed and passed but never used) and actively licensed overshoot ("Longer is fine when real facts carry it"; "Stopping short is for when the sources are exhausted, not for when they're merely optional"; "Name every Major and Moderate item individually") — an instruction to voice everything on a 20-corridor / 30-incident market; (2) the item-selection caps (`CorridorTiering` 4+3+3=10, tuned to `SlotCapacity` at 3.0s/item) are a COUNT budget, but a real one-incident sentence runs ~5s / ~13 words, so 10 items ≈ 130+ words — and a count budget fundamentally cannot serve both a minor-heavy market (needs ~10 SHORT items to fill the slot) and a closure-heavy one (overshoots at ~6 LONG items). Only a WORD budget adapts to item length; LLM word-ceilings are weakly obeyed (live: 154→116 across prompt iterations, still over).

**Decision:** Three layered changes. (1) `prompts/draft.md`: render `{{targetWordsMax}}` as a hard ceiling ("voice the worst first and stop at the ceiling; what doesn't fit is dropped this read, never crammed in"); require one incident per sentence ("never chain two incidents together with 'and'"); bound the anti-underfill guard to the floor (`{{targetWordsMin}}`) and fill-sources only. (2) `DraftWordBudget.Ceiling(target)` = `target + Math.Max(8, target*3/20)` — the airable ceiling inside the audio speed-up headroom. (3) `DraftWordBudget.TrimToCeiling` — a deterministic post-draft trim on the structured sentence array: keep all short non-incident closers (weather / fuel / good-runs / drive-times / cleared), then keep incident sentences worst-first (already ordered by the model) up to the ceiling, dropping the lowest-priority incidents that don't fit. Wired into `GenerateStructuredDraftAsync` before the sentences are joined; skipped for curated regeneration (operator chose those corridors explicitly).

**Rationale:** The prompt reduces the model's raw over-production and fixes sentence structure, but LLM word-ceilings do not hold reliably. The deterministic trim is the guarantee — and because it is WORD-based on the structured draft the citation-forcing work already produces, it adapts to item length automatically (drops long items, keeps many short ones) where the fixed COUNT caps cannot. It is a NO-OP when the draft is already within the ceiling, so thin / minor-heavy markets are never trimmed and it cannot re-create the content-limited underfill the `SlotCapacity` 6→10 tuning removed. It touches only the Draft internals — `CorridorTiering` / `SlotCapacity` / filler / good-run / fabrication selection are all unchanged.

**Consequences:** New: `DraftWordBudget.Ceiling` + `DraftWordBudget.TrimToCeiling` (pure, unit-tested), a `targetWordCount` param on `GenerateStructuredDraftAsync`, and rewritten budget/fill lines in `prompts/draft.md`. On busy markets weather/fuel (which are FILL, lowest priority) now correctly yield to real traffic once incidents fill the slot — they appeared before only because the illegal overshoot left free room; the fill priority itself is unchanged. The model still over-drafts (raw 122-172 words) — the trim discards the excess, so the extra draft tokens are wasted but correctness is guaranteed; tightening the raw draft further is left to prompt iteration.

**Measured (live, real Azure OpenAI, gpt-5.4-mini, 2026-07-08).** Five markets, 30s / 85-word target, ceiling 97. Raw model draft → deterministic trim (word count Review received) → final: sydney 144→87→90, melbourne 172→83→94, brisbane 158→92→92, perth 122→96→82, adelaide 147→94→90. Every final in [82,94] (within ~10 words of target, all ≤ ceiling) vs the prior turn's finals of 126 / 170 / 161 / 96 / 136. All Approved, safety-passed, reading worst-first with real roads. Trim verified firing (sydney: model drafted 144, Review received 87). Existing draft-path suite (LlmScriptGenerator / WireMock / CitationVerifier / EvidenceUnitBuilder / DraftWordBudget) 102/102 green; new `TrimToCeiling` / `Ceiling` unit tests added.

## 2026-07-08 — Draft Slot-Fit, Follow-Up: Item-Count Aim + Schema maxItems/maxLength

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The `TrimToCeiling` guard (previous entry) guarantees the OUTPUT, but the model still raw-over-drafted ~1.5-2×, wasting draft tokens and leaning on the trim. A survey of the option space concluded the reliable levers are the ones that DON'T require the model to count words: bound the input, or constrain the schema. A live probe confirmed Azure `gpt-5.4-mini` strict Structured Outputs now ACCEPTS `maxItems` / `maxLength` / `minItems` (the SDK's earlier blanket rejection — noted in the prior schema comment — is stale as of 2026-07-08).

**Decision:** Three additions to the Draft call, keeping the trim as the backstop. (C1) `DraftWordBudget.MaxVoicedIncidents(target, evidenceUnits)` estimates how many incidents fit the word budget by walking the SHOWN evidence corridors worst-first and spending a per-corridor spoken-word estimate proxied by unit count (a full major bullet renders more fields → a longer sentence than a condensed minor); rendered in `prompts/draft.md` as a pacing GAUGE ("about N incidents fit — pace detail, still fill to ~target, never stop under the floor"), not a hard stop. Computed over the evidence set rather than `CorridorTiering.SelectVoiceable` (which suppresses minors under a major headline and diverges when `FillSource.MinorTraffic` escalates). (B1) schema `maxItems` = `maxIncidents + 6` — a generous upper bound that kills roll-call pathology without binding a legit read. (B2) schema `maxLength` = 220 chars per sentence — a runaway-compound guard that never clips a legitimate single incident (even a bidirectional-closure lead runs ~160).

**Rationale:** A COUNT cap can't hit a WORD target across regimes (minor-heavy fills at ~10 SHORT items, closure-heavy busts at ~6 LONG ones), so the aim is made length-aware via unit count and framed as a gauge — a hard "voice N and stop" caused undershoot in an early iteration (final 57-71w, under floor) because it fought the fill-to-target intent. The schema caps are UPPER bounds; word precision still rests on the aim + trim. `maxLength` is held constant across the A/B so the measured delta is the aim + `maxItems`.

**Consequences:** New `DraftWordBudget.MaxVoicedIncidents`; a `maxIncidents` param on `GenerateStructuredDraftAsync`; `BuildDraftJsonSchema` gains `int? maxSentences` and always sets `maxLength`; `draft.md` line 3 renders the guarded gauge; the stale "strict mode rejects array-length constraints" schema comment corrected. A temporary `ARN_DRAFT_LEGACY_SIZING` env toggle was added to isolate the A/B and REMOVED after measurement.

**Measured (controlled A/B, live Azure OpenAI, gpt-5.4-mini, 2026-07-08).** Melbourne, corridors held constant at 10, back-to-back within one traffic window (toggle isolating the item-aim + `maxItems`; `maxLength` constant both arms), n=3/arm. Raw draft mean **118 → 80**: aim OFF raws 165/101/89 (huge variance, mean well over the 87 target); aim ON raws 81/74/85 (tight, right at target). Final mean **101 → 88**: aim OFF finals 82/117/103 (one over the ceiling); aim ON finals 97/76/90 (at target). The aim pulls the raw draft onto target AND collapses its run-to-run variance, cutting reliance on the trim and on review-refine churn. Earlier apparent "undershoots" on other markets (brisbane 42w raw) were traffic-variance low-content runs, not the aim — confirmed because the constant-corridor A/B lands at target, not short. Full non-integration suite green; new `MaxVoicedIncidents` unit tests added.

## 2026-07-08 — Bulletin Quality Pass: raw-address / closed-not-shut / daypart / continuity fixes; suburb-disambiguation root-caused

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An independent `atn-reviewer` pass on two live bulletins (deployed Gold Coast job `e62fffd5`, local Melbourne) returned WOULD NOT AIR for both. Facts/direction/tone were on-brief (fidelity 0.7-0.95) — the failures were on-air craft + data hygiene, matching ARN's own feedback: three concrete defects — (1) a raw reverse-geocoded postal address voiced in a cleared line ("Construction at 10, Arundel QLD 4214, Australia has cleared"); (2) closure headlines saying "shut" not "closed" (BFN-017); (3) "this overnight", a broken daypart phrase — plus (4) two bare "Smith Street" / "Smith Street Motorway" names with no suburb (the ambiguity ARN flagged).

**Decision:**
