- Raw-address leak → new `RoadNameFormatter.LooksLikeRawAddress` (4-digit postcode / ", Australia" / house-number-led; route codes excluded), filtered at all three cleared/continuity render sites (`AppendClearedSection`, `AppendClearedEvidence`, `IncidentChangeFormatter.BuildLocationLabel`) — an address-shaped name is never voiced or fed to the writer.
- closed>shut → prompt preference in `draft.md`/`review.md`, AND (because the prompt-only rule was weakly obeyed live — fresh gen still led "is shut") a deterministic `ClosureVerbNormalizer` (whole-word shut→closed, casing preserved) applied at the same generate/refine output points as `TimeOfDayNormalizer`. Same prompt+deterministic-backstop pattern the detector suite already uses.
- "this overnight" → `TimeOfDayNormalizer` regex now matches `this overnight`; the keep-writer's-phrasing guard tightened so only "this …"-framed dayparts (morning/afternoon/evening) survive — "this overnight"/"this midday" rewrite to "overnight"/"at midday". Rigid `"this {{timeOfDay}}"` template removed from `draft.md`/`review.md`.
- Continuity → `draft.md` requires a genuinely new opening on a same-day re-read and restricts "still"/"again" to items the change-log marks "Still ongoing" (never a New/Cleared item).
- Closure-shape (BFN-018) → `draft.md` instructs varying consecutive-closure shapes (see gap below).

**Root cause found, deferred (suburb disambiguation, #4):** `SuburbRetentionDetector` only fires when `corridor.Suburb.HasValue`; `corridor.Suburb = ExtractSuburb(incident.Location)`; and `HereTrafficProvider.EnrichWithGeocoding` reverse-geocodes ONLY incidents whose Location `IsGenericLocation` (nameless/route-code) — to give them a NAME. A named road (Smith Street, Pacific Mwy) is never reverse-geocoded, so it never gets a suburb even with coords present — the whole GC job was `Suburb=None`, making the gate a no-op. Fix = reverse-geocode named incidents for a locality (extra HERE calls → a cost decision); flagged, not shipped.

**Rationale:** Each fix pairs a prompt rule with a deterministic backstop wherever the LLM proved unreliable (address-shape filtering, `ClosureVerbNormalizer`, `TimeOfDayNormalizer`) — prior sessions repeatedly showed prompt-only lexical/format rules regress under model sampling variance, and this batch confirmed it live (fresh gen still led "is shut" under the prompt-only rule). The suburb-disambiguation gap is root-caused but deferred rather than rushed: it changes HERE reverse-geocode call volume (a cost decision) and wants a structural duplicate-stem rule, not another prompt line.

**Consequences:** New `ClosureVerbNormalizer`, `RoadNameFormatter.LooksLikeRawAddress`; edits to `TimeOfDayNormalizer`, `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer(.EvidenceUnits)`, `IncidentChangeFormatter`, `LlmScriptGenerator` (both normalize call-sites), `prompts/draft.md`, `prompts/review.md`. New/extended unit tests: `RoadNameFormatterTests` (LooksLikeRawAddress), `ClosureVerbNormalizerTests`, `TimeOfDayNormalizerTests`. **Verified live (local, real Azure OpenAI, gpt-5.4-mini) + independent atn-reviewer re-check on the regenerated Gold Coast bulletin: the three named defects are RESOLVED — no raw address, "closed" throughout (zero "shut"), no looped "still"; fidelity 1.0, clean close 0.95.** Two blockers remain, both needing a deterministic gate not a prompt (surfaced by the re-review, out of this batch's scope): a six-road **closure roll-call** (`RollCallDetector` currently scopes to good-run roads only, so closure lists escape it) and the **Smith Street suburb ambiguity** (the deferred #4 geocoding change). NOT committed/deployed.

## 2026-07-08 — Review-Refine Churn Fix: role-aware roll-call + severity-tiered gate + convergence guard

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deep-dive on job fb44a570 (3AW/Melbourne, 30s) from its `pipeline-verbatim.html`. An 85-word, factually-correct, reviewer-APPROVED draft churned through 5 Review + 4 Refine rounds and shipped at 90 words (over the ~85 ceiling) "with reviewer-flagged issues unresolved". Root cause traced through the raw captures: the LLM reviewer returned `{"verdict":"APPROVED","issues":[]}` every round (the export's empty `responseText` was a diagnostic-extraction bug, not runtime), but the orchestrator's deterministic detectors kept forcing refines. The specific trigger was a **`RollCallDetector` false positive**: the lead sentence "Greensborough Bypass southbound is shut between Grimshaw Street and Diamond Creek Road, and the ramp to the M80 is closed" names 4 corridor roads, but Grimshaw Street + Diamond Creek Road are the Bypass closure's mandatory cross-street ANCHORS that also happen to be independent Minor/Moderate corridors in the same dense feed, so they entered `corridorRoads` and tripped the per-sentence cap. `Repair` couldn't fix it ("between X and Y" is not a bare-connector chain), so the loop churned to exhaustion. Rounds 2→3 produced near-identical output — a textbook unsatisfiable-constraint loop with no convergence check.

**Decision:** Three coupled changes, grounded in 2026 evaluator-optimizer practice (bounded + convergent loops; oscillation/duplicate-work as first-class failure modes; objective checks tiered separately from the subjective judge; verify-then-repair over regenerate-whole-artifact):
- **Role-aware roll-call** (`RollCallDetector.Detect`, Rule B): build a per-corridor anchor map (`anchorsByHost`) from each corridor's `Extent` + incident `Location`s + `Description` (new `LocationText` helper). A named road with NO own verb that is an anchor of a DIFFERENT corridor voiced with its own verb in the same sentence is discounted from the roll-call count — the data mandates the mention. Also widened `OwnVerbNearby` to allow one intervening AU direction word ("Bypass southbound is shut") so the host corridor is recognised (without this the discount never engaged on the real construction).
- **Severity-tiered gate** (`BroadcastOrchestrator.ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync`): an APPROVED judge exits the loop even when a STYLE detector (rollCall / dupAnchor / repeatedPrep / impactStack — all with a safe mechanical `Repair`) fired; those are repaired deterministically after the loop, never via another LLM round. Only BLOCKING defects (metaLeak / typeStack / fakeLocation / unselectedSource / suburbRetention / sentenceClone) force a refine.
- **Convergence guard**: if the same blocking-defect signature survives a refine (fired last attempt and again now, attempt>1), stop the loop and hand to the final grounding gate — another round on the same feedback risks corrupting a correct fact (job 4417add2 precedent).

**Rationale:** The false positive, the flat all-detectors-block gate, and the missing convergence check are three independent amplifiers of the same churn. The role-aware fix removes the specific trigger; tiering ensures a cosmetic nit can never again outvote an approving judge into unbounded LLM rounds (the general class); the guard caps wasted refines on any unsatisfiable blocking defect. All three are deterministic, mechanical, and add no LLM calls.

**Consequences:** Edits to `RollCallDetector.cs` (anchor map + `LocationText` + widened `OwnVerbNearby`) and `BroadcastOrchestrator.cs` (tiered exit + convergence guard). New tests: `RollCallDetectorTests` +3 (`Ignores_anchor_roads_that_are_also_their_own_corridors` replays the real fb44a570 lead + topology and asserts no roll-call — mutation-checked: pre-fix logic flags it true; regression guards keep genuine bare lists flagged), `BroadcastOrchestratorTests` +2 (style-only+approved → 0 refines; persistent blocking → exactly 1 refine, not the ceiling of 3). **Verified: Domain suite 1040 green incl. the frozen-case A/B; the 2 orchestrator tests green; live Melbourne 3AW run on the new build shipped 83w approved with no roll-call churn (its round-1 refine was the word-target expansion, not a style refine).** NOT committed/deployed. **Deferred (out of scope):** the two competing loops (style-refine vs word-target/expansion) that let the word-target pass re-grow past the ceiling and introduce a vague "a couple more spots" sweep; the diagnostic-export empty-`responseText` bug; the AAD `PermissionDenied` token race (12/24 calls). Note: 3 pre-existing orchestrator tests (`ReviewFeedback_RefineSucceeds_UsesRefinedScript`, `ReviewFeedback_RefineFails_UsesCurrentScript`, `ReviewFails_UsesCurrentScript`) fail under a CONCURRENT, unrelated change that converted `RunFinalGroundingCheckAsync` into a hard gate (`Result.Failure` when grounding never approves); those failures are not from this work (they fail even on the review-failure path that never reaches this loop's exit logic) and are owned by that change.

## 2026-07-08 — Keep The Agentic Bulletin Workflow, But Make Stage Contracts Explicit And Hard-Gated

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Job `e62fffd50a8d4474a0e40a5270345021` looked like an agentic boot loop: 3 generation attempts, 15 review/refine rounds, 37 captured LLM calls, ~100k tokens, and a final script that still failed an independent ATN-style read. The re-export tool initially made this worse by misparsing Responses API captures (all review verdicts rendered `?`, issues `0`) because `reasoning` items preceded the `message` item. After fixing diagnostics, the raw captures showed the real picture: some reviewer feedback was useful, some was over-triggered, and the dominant failures came from leaky contracts between stages (source facts hidden in ids, good-run/source conflicts, final unapproved refine output, invisible post-LLM repairs), not from the existence of a draft/review/refine loop itself.

**Decision:** Keep the existing deterministic orchestrator with bounded Draft → Review → Refine → Safety → Attribute → human-approval stages. Do **not** replace it with a free-form planner, a chatty multi-agent framework, or a more autonomous debating loop. Harden the compiler-like contracts instead:

- parse captured Responses API message text from `output[*].content[*].text`, independent of preceding `reasoning` items;
- deconflict good-run roads against active incident corridors using canonical road matching, preserving genuinely distinct road names;
- render evidence units source-complete (`id: source=...; field=...; value=...`) and pass that evidence block to Refine as well as Draft;
- make unresolved final grounding a hard generation-attempt failure, leaving retry/fallback to decide the terminal path;
- log every deterministic post-LLM repair as a named post-LLM mutation with before/after word counts.

**Rationale:** The successful pieces are already code-owned and bounded: state, retries, duration, safety, attribution, delivery, deterministic gates, and human approval. Replacing them with another autonomous agent would increase variance and reduce diagnosability. The failing pieces were missing invariants at stage boundaries: a reviewer/refiner cannot reliably preserve facts it cannot see except inside opaque ids; a final script that never re-approved must not be presented for approval as if it passed; and diagnostics must distinguish raw model output from deterministic mutation.

**Consequences:** Working-tree changes touch `scripts/export-prompts.py`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Domain/Services/GoodRunPolicy.cs`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Infrastructure/AiProviders/AzureOpenAI/LlmScriptGenerator.cs`, `prompts/refine.md`, and `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Application/Broadcasting/BroadcastOrchestrator.cs`, plus targeted tests in `scripts/test_export_prompts.py`, `GoodRunPolicyTests`, `LlmScriptGeneratorTests`, and `BroadcastOrchestratorTests`. Re-exporting `e62fffd50a8d4474a0e40a5270345021` now shows parsed verdicts (`NEEDS_REVISION`/`APPROVED`) and 23 issues instead of `?`/0. Targeted local verification passed: Domain `GoodRunPolicyTests` 16/16, Infrastructure `LlmScriptGeneratorTests` 68/68, Application `FinalGrounding` 4/4, and `scripts/test_export_prompts.py` 6/6. Not deployed.

## 2026-07-09 — ADO pipeline reverted to Dev -> Test -> Prod (test back in the promotion path)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-06-29 same-day reversal ("ADO pipeline retargeted to Dev -> Prod (test excluded)") dropped Test from the CI/CD promotion path on the stated rationale "ARN owns the Test environment lifecycle manually" -- an observation about how Test happened to be deployed, not a technical objection to including it. Test is the only non-dev environment running full production-style RBAC (devAuthFallbackRole is empty; Dev bypasses RBAC via that fallback). The 2026-06-29 "Test SPA no-role shell" defect was caught ONLY because Test enforces real roles -- Dev structurally cannot catch that class of bug. Excluding Test from the pipeline throws away the one environment proven to catch what Dev can't, for no offsetting benefit. User (the Arinco deploy operator) flagged this directly on 2026-07-08: the expected/standard topology is Dev -> Test -> Prod, with Test used to verify changes before they reach Prod.

**Decision:** Reverted azure-pipelines.yml to the original Dev -> Test -> Prod promotion: Deploy_Dev (group arn-traffic-dev, env dev, applyRbacConfig=false) -> Deploy_Test (group arn-traffic-test, env test, applyRbacConfig=true, dependsOn Deploy_Dev) -> Deploy_Prod (group arn-traffic-variables, env production, applyRbacConfig=true, dependsOn Deploy_Test). Still gated behind enableDeploy=false until ARN provisions service connections. The ARN ask now needs THREE ARM service connections (dev/test/prod) instead of two, plus a test ADO environment and arn-traffic-test variable group (neither exists yet in ADO -- the original 2026-06-29 Test->Prod design was superseded same-day before those were ever created) -- and an approver gate on test in addition to production.

**Rationale:** Dev -> Test -> Prod is the standard, correct CI/CD topology. Test's entire purpose (full RBAC, prod-style network/storage posture) is to be a pre-prod verification gate; leaving it a manual, ad-hoc mirror deployed only when the Arinco deploy operator remembers to run deploy.sh means it drifts from Prod and never actually gates anything. Putting it back in the automated path costs nothing (deploy-stage.yml is already a reusable template; test was excluded, not deleted) and restores real defense-in-depth against RBAC-class and config-drift bugs Dev cannot surface.

**Consequences:** azure-pipelines.yml edited and validated to parse (yaml.safe_load clean). 's 'Minimum actions ARN needs to take to go live' summary and the ARN Technology Lead's consolidated ask both need updating: 3 service connections (not 2), plus creating+authorising a test ADO environment and arn-traffic-test variable group with an approver gate. No code/infra change beyond the pipeline YAML; Test's Bicep/RBAC posture was already correct from the original 29 Jun design.

## 2026-07-09 — Normalize Slash-Separated Road Anchors Before Prompting And TTS

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deployed Melbourne job `dda2471bce5c4a69addeafbf8e475b4b` aired/stored `Todd Road / Cook Street`; ElevenLabs read the literal slash aloud. Raw job evidence showed the slash originated in HERE's incident detail (`Between 8 Mile Bridge and Todd Road / Cook Street - Road construction`). The structured Draft initially omitted `Cook Street`, but `CitationVerifier` flagged the cited location as incomplete and `CitationFix` reinserted the full evidence value including `/`. This was not hallucination; it was unspeakable provider punctuation promoted to source truth by the citation guard.

**Decision:** Normalize slash-separated road/location anchors to the spoken conjunction `and` before they reach the writer or evidence contract, and also apply the same normalization as a final TTS fallback. Digit/digit forms are preserved so fractions/dates are not rewritten.

**Rationale:** A prompt rule is insufficient because the citation-fix layer will keep restoring whatever is in the canonical evidence value. The source/evidence text must be speakable before it becomes citation truth. A TTS fallback is still required because displayed/stored text can come from other paths and ElevenLabs reads literal `/` as "slash".

**Consequences:** `RoadNameFormatter.ToSpeakable` now applies slash normalization before road-type abbreviation expansion, so `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` prose and `EvidenceUnit` location/extent values render `Todd Road and Cook Street`, not `Todd Road / Cook Street`. `RoadNameFormatter.ExpandRouteCodesForSpeech` applies the same normalization before route-code spacing, so the audio path never forwards a slash-separated road anchor to ElevenLabs. Added regression tests in `RoadNameFormatterTests` and `ElevenLabsAudioSynthesizerTests`, plus frozen fixture `test/corpus/regressions/melbourne-westgate-slash-20260708.json`. Verification: targeted Infrastructure tests 74/74 passed; replay of the exact frozen job data passed fabrication/style/safety and produced `between 8 Mile Bridge, Todd Road and Cook Street` with no literal slash.

## 2026-07-09 — Weather/Fuel platform gate silently reverted by a Bicep redeploy (QT-001 recurrence); moved into IaC

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** User reported deployed bulletins (e.g. job `b53baa6c42cb47d3834c52aea463f86c`, Melbourne Drive Traffic) logging "Weather data unavailable" / "Fuel price data unavailable" despite the 2026-07-06 decision explicitly enabling both platform-wide on dev. `LogsJson` plus the App Insights trace gave the exact cause: `HereWeatherProvider`/`HereFuelPriceProvider` both returned "provider is disabled (Weather:Enabled=false / Fuel:Enabled=false)" — the platform gate, not the market's own `ContentSelection` (Melbourne's schedule/ad-hoc request already carried `Weather:true, Fuel:true`). `az functionapp config appsettings list` confirmed `Weather__Enabled`/`Fuel__Enabled` were entirely absent from IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01 — the 2026-07-06 CLI-set override was gone. Root cause: `deployment/modules/function-app.bicep`'s `commonAppSettings` never included these two keys, so the `e40f4e3` (2026-07-08, "Dev batch: pooled corridor fill budget, LLM call capture, geocoding/retry hardening") Bicep redeploy overwrote `siteConfig.appSettings` wholesale back to the code default (`false` in `appsettings.json`) — the exact QT-001 failure class already documented for `fillerCartAudioUrl` ("a hand-set app setting is wiped on every redeploy"), now recurring for a setting that hadn't been given the same IaC treatment.

**Decision:** Added `weatherEnabled`/`fuelEnabled` bool params (default `false`) to `deployment/main.bicep` and `deployment/modules/function-app.bicep`, wired into `commonAppSettings` as `Weather__Enabled`/`Fuel__Enabled`, and set both `true` only in `main.dev.bicepparam` (matching the `fillerCartAudioUrl` pattern) so the setting survives future redeploys instead of living only as an out-of-band CLI override. Applied immediately to the live dev Function App via `az functionapp config appsettings set` + restart so dev did not have to wait for the next pipeline run. Verified end-to-end with a live `ScriptOnly` broadcast (job `5a25d6a3c1b54ba48d3d93171164c21d`, Melbourne Drive Traffic, deleted after verification): logs showed `Weather fetched: Cool., 10°C` and `Fuel prices fetched: 2 fuel type(s)`, and the generated script carried both ("It's cool and 10 degrees... Unleaded 91 is cheapest at $1.60 in Narre Warren, and diesel is cheapest at $1.80 in Hallam").

**Rationale:** Every ad-hoc CLI-set app setting not mirrored in `commonAppSettings` is wiped by the next Bicep deployment of the Function App, since `Microsoft.Web/sites` `siteConfig.appSettings` is a full replace, not a merge — this is now the second time the same class of bug has silently regressed a deliberate decision (first `fillerCartAudioUrl`/QT-001, now Weather/Fuel). IaC is the only representation that survives redeploys; test/prod default to `false`, preserving the 2026-07-06 decision's scope (dev-only, pending an explicit ARN go-ahead elsewhere).

**Consequences:** `deployment/main.bicep`, `deployment/modules/function-app.bicep`, and `deployment/main.dev.bicepparam` gain `weatherEnabled`/`fuelEnabled`; `az bicep build`/`build-params` verified clean for all four env bicepparam files (dev resolves both `true`, test/prod/sandbox stay at the `false` default). Any future full Bicep redeploy of dev now preserves this setting instead of reverting it. General lesson for this codebase: any app setting enabled via `az functionapp config appsettings set` outside a bicepparam file MUST be treated as temporary and ported into IaC in the same session, or it will silently disappear on the next redeploy with no error, warning, or diff — check `commonAppSettings` coverage before relying on a CLI-set flag surviving.

## 2026-07-08 — Draft-agent reasoning effort trial: REJECTED (kept Draft on fastest tier)

**Status:** accepted (negative result)

**Context:** Trialed giving the Draft LLM call a reasoning pass. On the deployed model `gpt-5.4-mini`, `LlmScriptGenerator.ResolveReasoningEffort` resolves Draft to `"none"` (only Review + producer-feedback passes get `"low"`). Question: does `reasoning.effort="low"` on Draft improve the bulletin enough to justify the cost? Ran a controlled A/B via the frozen 10-fixture fallback-replay panel (data held constant, real agent loop) — control (Draft `none`) vs trial (Draft `low`, via a temporary `ARN_DRAFT_REASONING` env toggle) — plus an independent `atn-reviewer` head-to-head on the one cleanly-paired fixture.

**Decision:** Do NOT promote Draft reasoning. Keep Draft on the model's fastest tier. Temporary toggle removed.

**Rationale:** (measured)
- **Fill (n=10/arm, the panel's reliable metric):** reasoning was flat-to-worse — filled 3/10 → 2/10, meanBestFill 84% → 79%, meanAttempts 3.5 → 3.6 — and it *destabilised* which fixtures fill (2 filled→fallback, 1 fallback→filled). Consistent with reasoning drafting more words (live Melbourne: 91→116 raw), which doesn't help content-limited fixtures and triggers more rewrite/trim (mirrors the earlier overshoot-1.2 rejection).
- **Prose (atn-reviewer, paired fixture 0871):** WASH — "reasoning=low bought a marginally cleaner cadence and a slightly more natural weather line, but paid for it by dropping a real anchor; it did NOT break the monotone or fix the fabricated distance. On this evidence Draft reasoning is not worth shipping." Run-to-run LLM stochasticity dominated any reasoning effect (control's own prose swung from monotone-bad to decent across fixtures).
- **Cost:** +~120 reasoning tokens and +~7% Draft latency per call, for no measured gain.

**Consequences:** `ResolveReasoningEffort` unchanged from baseline (Draft stays `none` on gpt-5.x); the `ARN_DRAFT_REASONING` toggle was removed after the verdict (project convention, cf. `ARN_DRAFT_LEGACY_SIZING`). **Kept** one permanent harness improvement: `FallbackReplayTests` now captures the shipped `ScriptText` per fixture in its report pack (`Replay.Script`) — needed for any prose A/B, previously only fill/duration were recorded. **Bonus findings (more actionable than reasoning effort — the real Draft-prose gaps, model/prompt-level not effort-level):** (1) monotone SVO cadence with no ATN connectors in BOTH arms; (2) a fabricated distance ("5-kay queue" on Parkes Way, which has no extent field) that the fidelity gates missed; (3) both arms silently dropped Majura Ave, a sev-2 item equal to the lead closure — a selection/prioritisation gap; (4) control labelled congestion corridors ("Northbourne Ave", "Petrie Plaza") as "closed" — a type fabrication. NOT committed/deployed.

## 2026-07-09 — Checklist-structured review trial: code-authoritative gates + LLM shadow (concluded — NOT promoted; code REMOVED after the trial per user request; NOT committed/deployed)

**Status:** accepted (trial concluded — not promoted)

**Context:** User design question — move the 10 deterministic detectors "into the review agent's job" and restructure review-refine around a persisted to-do checklist the reviewer confidently ticks, refined across cycles, to make the reviewer simpler and more consistent. Built Option 1 (the safe reading): the checklist is shared loop state; each item is ticked by its authoritative checker — deterministic detectors for the 10 code items (authoritative), the per-item reviewer LLM for the semantic judgment items — and the LLM ALSO shadow-ticks the code items (recorded, never used) so we can measure whether it could own them.

**Decision:** Do NOT promote — and, per the user's request to keep the bulletin code clean, the trial code was REMOVED after the measurement (6 files deleted, 7 edited files reverted to baseline; `ARN_CHECKLIST_REVIEW` no longer exists). The deterministic detectors stay code-authoritative. The trial's headline question — can the LLM own the deterministic gates? — is answered NO by the shadow measurement, which is why there was nothing worth keeping in-tree.

**Rationale:** The whole point of putting the gates "into the reviewer" is to trust the LLM's tick; the shadow measurement shows that trust is misplaced — on the deterministic checks the LLM over-flags (13 false positives → refine churn) and occasionally under-flags (1 false negative the detector caught + repaired), so promoting it would trade a guarantee for a coin-flip and reintroduce the churn the fb44a570 gate removed. The checklist RESTRUCTURE (per-item, persisted, sticky-pass, tiered) is orthogonal to that, but on this panel it produced no prose win and the dominant defects were draft-layer fabrications no review structure touched — so there was nothing worth keeping in-tree, and the code was removed; this entry preserves the finding for any future re-eval.

**What was built during the trial (all since removed):** `Domain.Services.VerificationChecklist`/`CheckItem`/`ChecklistBuilder` + `Domain.Models.ChecklistReview` (`ChecklistReviewItem`/`ChecklistVerdict`); `IScriptReviewer.ReviewChecklistAsync` + `prompts/checklist-review.md` + `ModelResponseParser.ParseChecklistVerdicts`; `BroadcastOrchestrator.RunChecklistReviewLoopAsync` branched on a toggle — per-item ticks; judgment items **sticky-pass** (a nondeterministic re-vote can't flip an already-ticked item); `DrivesRefine` tiering preserved the fb44a570 severity-tiered gate (cosmetic code items ticked/visible but not forcing refine); the SHARED post-loop safety tail (final grounding + deterministic repair + style gate) ran in BOTH paths so the trial could not regress deterministic quality. 71 unit tests (Domain model/builder + parser). Harness: opt-in `ConsoleLikeLoggerProvider` + `ARN_REPLAY_LOG=1` for the shadow capture — reverted with everything else.

**Evidence (frozen 10-fixture fallback-replay panel, real Azure OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini`, data held constant):**
- **Feasibility — works.** Checklist engaged + converged on all 3 fillable fixtures (holistic approved on attempt 1; the itemised rubric found items to fix and drove 1-3 refine cycles, producing different scripts on identical frozen inputs — proof of engagement). Fill a WASH within noise: filled 3/10 both arms, meanBestFill 82%→84%, meanAttempts 3.1→3.7 (checklist refines more, by design). Post-loop deterministic repair still fired in checklist mode (repaired a duplicate-anchor + a roll-call the checklist left) — no deterministic regression.
- **Shadow (headline) — the LLM cannot own the gates.** 87.3% LLM-vs-detector agreement over 110 code-item ticks / 11 cycles. All 14 disagreements were on style/shape items: 13/14 were LLM FALSE POSITIVES (over-flagging sentence-clone ×5, duplicate-anchor ×5, roll-call ×2, impact-stack ×1 that the detectors passed → would reintroduce refine churn), and 1 was a FALSE NEGATIVE (the LLM passed a real duplicate-anchor the detector caught + repaired). Zero disagreement on the pure-fidelity items (they stayed clean → only trivial agreement-on-absence). Code-authoritative design validated.
- **Prose (independent atn-reviewer, paired 3 filled fixtures) — no net gain.** All 6 scripts (A holistic / B checklist) WOULD-NOT-AIR from shared DRAFT-layer fabrications present IDENTICALLY in both arms (London Circuit→Petrie Plaza/Northbourne location merge across all 3; invented Tarago Rd + Captains Flat Rd + sev-1→"moderate" inflation; invented "5-kay queue"). B regressed on-air style on 2/3 (bare-road "minor impact" roll-call, repeated jargon, doubled the exposed contradiction, localized citywide weather); wash on 1. Reviewer caveat: low-signal synthetic TEST-STATION panel — the dominant defects are the DRAFT/evidence-grounding layer, NOT the review structure.

**Consequences:** Trial code REMOVED (6 files deleted / 7 edits reverted; Domain + Application build clean and Domain.Tests 1040 green post-revert). Decisive reusable finding retained here as the record: the deterministic gates must stay code-authoritative (the LLM both over- and under-flags them); the checklist RESTRUCTURE itself is sound (per-item, persisted, sticky-pass, tiered) but did not improve prose on this panel. Next real lever is the DRAFT/evidence-grounding layer (the shared location-merge + invented roads neither review structure removed); any future re-eval should use a richer LIVE market panel, not the synthetic corpus, and start from this decision entry.

## 2026-07-10 — FormatImpact's 5 km distance floor fabricated on-air magnitudes; replaced with honest rounding

**Status:** accepted (code fixed; not yet committed/deployed)

**Context:** A live dev review of 8 bulletins (v53 plain-text draft, MaxReviewRefineRetries=0) found "about five kays" voiced in three different markets, contradicted by the source data every time (0.5 km Gold Coast work zone, 2.0/2.4 km Sydney queues, 3.8 km Brisbane roadworks). Yesterday's checklist-review trial attributed the "invented 5-kay queue" to the DRAFT layer; tracing the rendered writer input disproves that — `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.FormatImpact` applied `Math.Max(5.0, Round(km/5)*5)`, so EVERY 0.5–7.5 km corridor was rendered to the writer as "~5km stretch affected" / "queue ~5km". The writer faithfully voiced corrupted data (the committed panel fixture 0871f234 even renders the self-contradiction "queue ~5km (short queue)"). The `system.md`/agent-instruction example phrase "backed up about five kays" reinforces voicing it.

**Decision:** Honest rounding in `FormatImpact`: sub-1 km extents get a qualitative label only ("short work zone" / "short queue" — no number beats a false one); 1–7.5 km rounds to the nearest 1 km; only ≥7.5 km rounds to the nearest 5. Three summarizer tests that asserted the old floor now defend the honest behaviour.

**Rationale:** The presenter-estimate rationale for round-to-5 only holds at scale; below 7.5 km it manufactures up-to-10× false magnitudes that the fidelity gates cannot catch (the claim matches the writer's input — the input itself was false). Data-layer honesty is the only place this class is fixable.

**Consequences:** `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.FormatImpact` + 3 tests updated (75/75 summarizer tests green). Regression fixtures `gc-closure-trap` and the panel's 0871f234 now render "short work zone" / "short queue" where they rendered "~5km". Candidate follow-up: remove the "about five kays" example phrase from the draft instructions (v53 agent + prompts/system.md) so the phrase stops being seeded.

## 2026-07-10 — Workflow-lab live-trap trial: model swap (gpt-5.6-terra) does NOT fix data-induced errors; honest per-incident data contract + deterministic fact gate does

**Status:** accepted (experiment concluded; C# port not yet started)

**Context:** Live dev review (8 bulletins) gave 7/8 DO-NOT-AIR verdicts with three recurring air-blocking classes: (1) closure smearing — corridor-collapsed prose pairs a real closure's type with a construction incident's anchor ("Warringah Freeway closed at Brook Street" when only the Falcon St ramp is closed; two false "Stirling Highway closed at X" claims in Perth); (2) fabricated distances (the FormatImpact floor, separate entry above); (3) severity-idiom echo — `CorridorAggregator`'s literal "at a standstill" phrase echoed verbatim up to 3× per script on 2-minute side-street flow readings that also out-rank real arteries for the lead. Research grounding (Anthropic "Building Effective Agents"): the highest-leverage building block is a well-fed single call with programmatic gates; iterating orchestration around a lossy data contract attacks the wrong layer.

**Decision:** The next quality investment goes into the data contract and deterministic fact gates, not model upgrades or orchestration changes: port the lab's winning `honest-data` shape into the C# pipeline (per-incident facts with their own anchors and explicit closure tags; one draft call; deterministic post-draft rejectors with a surgical repair call). A pure model swap to gpt-5.6-terra is rejected as a quality fix.

**Rationale:** Extended the workflow lab: `ExportRenderedInputs` now also exports regression fixtures and embeds the raw `GeneratorInputSnapshot`; 5 live-trap fixtures captured from the reviewed jobs (gc-closure-trap, perth-smear-trap, syd-standstill-noise, melb-dense-fallback, bris-control). Ran a 3-workflow × 2-model matrix (v53-agent snapshot, budget-scaffold-gated, and a new `honest-data` arm) on gpt-5.4-mini and the new gpt-5.6-terra deployment. Results, judged by hand against the source data and the ATN corpus:
- **v53-agent on terra reproduces every live failure** (false Stirling/Warringah closures, unanchored "Pacific Motorway citybound is closed.", "queue of about five kays") — a stronger model faithfully voices the same corrupted input. Model swap alone is rejected as a quality fix.
- **honest-data kills all three failure classes on BOTH models**: per-incident facts with their own anchors + an explicit CLOSED tag (only closure-type facts may be voiced as closed), real lengths, flow readings labeled as sensor pace with local-street noise demoted from the lead, monitored drive times surfaced; one strong call with ATN exemplars in-context; then a deterministic fact gate (closure-claim vs CLOSED facts incl. wrong-anchor pairing, voiced distances vs data, advice-closer, minutes discipline, word ceiling) driving ONE surgical repair call — never a blank-slate retry. Final terra run: 8/8 fixtures with zero factual errors on line-by-line verification; 7/8 judged airable (the all-clear Port Lincoln read stays honestly short — the filler/fallback machinery owns that slot by design).
- Foundry agent `arn-draft-natural-v53-terra` (v53:7 instructions on gpt-5.6-terra) created for playground A/B; NOT wired to any environment.

**Consequences:** Winning shape to port into C#: keep one draft call, feed it per-incident facts (`Summary`/`Comment` fields included — they carry the extents and causes), keep the deterministic detectors as post-draft rejectors with surgical repair. Known gaps: terra needs >1024 max_output_tokens headroom when reasoning is on (budget-scaffold-gated returned two empty scripts at 1024); draft-layer Foundry-agent calls are still invisible to `llm-call-captures` (only Attribute/Safety/Review land) — extend capture to the agent path before the next deployed diagnosis session.

## 2026-07-10 — Wording audit vs the ATN corpus: the prompts teach a dialect ATN doesn't speak; ban lists and per-tier palettes seed it

**Status:** accepted (lab arm shipped as `atn-voice`; deployed prompts not yet changed)

**Context:** Phrase-frequency comparison of recent generated scripts against the 6,618 words of real ATN air copy in `docs/reference/atn-bulletin-style-samples.md`. Our workhorse phrases do not exist in ATN copy: "at a standstill" 0×, "moving slowly" 0×, "a touch slow" 0×, "flowing well" 0× — yet the v53 agent instructions contain them 2×/5×/8×/3× respectively (the per-tier "permitted vocabulary" palette PRESCRIBES them, and the banned-phrase quotes seed the rest). Meanwhile ATN's actual workhorses are nearly absent from ours: "under speed" 28×, "is slow" 35×, "crash" 27×, "building" 12×, "bumper to bumper" 8×. ATN's closure grammar is lane-level + consequence chain ("one lane's blocked and traffic is backing up through Casula" — back to/through/backing up/queuing ≈37× combined), almost never "X is closed"; its connectors are "also" (39×) / "as well" (11×), not "meanwhile" (2×). The fixed 5-phrase-per-tier palette is also the root of within-read repetition ("is heavy" ×2, "at a standstill" ×3, cloned "are all moving slowly" sentences) and cross-market sameness.

**Decision:** Style is taught by exemplars and a wide positive palette, never by ban lists or fixed per-tier phrase menus. New lab arm `atn-voice` (system prompt + shared `workflow_lab/honest_input.py` data contract): corpus-attested pace vocabulary presented as a rotate-don't-repeat palette, the consequence-chain sentence shape, closure-vocabulary rotation, shape-rotation rules with the WHY ("one person talking, not a database reciting rows"), 4 diverse verbatim ATN reads in `<examples>` tags, TTS delivery stated as the motivation for spoken-word numbers. Deterministic repetition gate (pace-phrase reuse, consecutive skeleton clones) added beside the fact gate. Two writer-facing data corruptions moved into the deterministic builder instead of prompt rules: self-referential anchors normalized ("Between Bruce Highway and Sandgate Road" on the Bruce → "Near Sandgate Road" — the LLM otherwise invents a replacement endpoint, observed live), and flow-severity bands neutralized (the literal "at a standstill" Description replaced with a severity code so it cannot be echoed).

**Rationale:** Grounded in the vendors' own prompting guidance (OpenAI prompt-engineering guide: identity/instructions/examples/context structure, few-shot patterns dominate, GPT-tier models need precise instructions; Anthropic best practices: examples are the most reliable style lever, provide motivation not bare bans — both corroborate the observed example-leakage: every phrase the prompt quotes, including in bans, becomes output vocabulary). Verified on the live-trap fixtures (terra): zero pace-phrase repeats across 6 markets, rotated closure vocabulary on the all-closures marathon read, consequence chains and lane grammar present, fidelity gates still clean; two identical-data Sydney generations differ in lead, shapes, and phrasing throughout.

**Consequences:** `experiments/workflows/atn-voice/` + shared `scripts/workflow_lab/honest_input.py` (extracted from honest-data; both arms consume it); Foundry agent `arn-draft-atn-voice-v1` (terra, reasoning pinned low, needs ≥2000 max_output_tokens; input contract is the honest data block, NOT prompts/draft.md — not wired to any environment). Port order for C#: honest data contract first, then this prompt; duration fitting stays downstream per the 2026-07-10 architecture decision. Known residual: HERE Comment boilerplate ("closures, detours, speed reductions") can still drive per-road echo on works-heavy markets — one prompt rule added; candidate for deterministic dedupe in the builder if it recurs.

## 2026-07-10 — Two-stage draft+polish architecture adopted in the lab; human-in-the-loop prompt-iteration harness (`scripts/prompt-loop.py`)

**Status:** accepted (lab-validated over 16 runs / 3 live data waves; C# port pending)

**Context:** After the wording audit shipped the `atn-voice` draft prompt, a 15-iteration human-in-the-loop campaign (`scripts/prompt-loop.py`: config = editable system prompt + input template; one command runs 5–9 REAL captured scenarios — traffic+weather+fuel+fillers — through the config, gates each script, and every cycle ends with the operator ruling on the agent's critiques) refined wording against the ATN corpus with the product owner ruling on each change. Key operator-driven corrections recorded on the way: synonym-rotated closure sentences are still a database read-out (cause-first aggregation is ATN's shape); direction words repeat freely in ATN but never open a mid-read sentence headless; clear-road rolls are area-grouped clusters of ≤3 with varied verbs (never one verb carrying six names); "obstruction/object" stays as data states (never upgraded to "debris"); road aliases (M1 vs Pacific Motorway) are forbidden until ARN configures them via guidance; timing lives downstream of the draft.

**Decision:** Adopt a two-stage shape: (1) the style-locked DRAFT agent (arn-draft-atn-voice-v1, now v3) turns the honest data block into a correct, complete, ATN-voiced read; (2) a data-aware POLISH agent (arn-polish-atn-v1) owns style elevation + timing exclusively — it receives the read, the predicted duration and word delta, the full reference facts (locked tokens: roads, directions, anchors, incident types, statuses, numbers), and the UNUSED facts as the only permitted expansion source; overshoot-biased band (slot..slot×1.07, aim slot×1.03 — mirrors the 2026-07-06 overshoot decision); closer-to-aim acceptance + one retry. Deterministic pre-sizing via a syllable model fitted on the committed synthesis history (`scripts/workflow_lab/duration.py`, a·syllables+b, validated 0.5s off a real ARN Sarah read); all deterministic gates (fact, repetition, skeleton-run, phrase-reuse, scaffold-leak, digits, lead-order) run after both stages.

**Rationale:** Words cannot guarantee seconds — real ElevenLabs shows ±2.55 s on identical input, so the last second always belongs to the audio machinery; the coarse fit belongs to a measured/predicted feedback loop, not draft-side word discipline. Validated on live-captured waves: 6–7 of 7 content markets land in or adjacent to the band in ≤2 polish calls with style preserved through every trim; quiet markets expand HONESTLY from unused facts (Mildura 21.8s→26.8–28.6s) or refuse to invent (Darwin 4.6s with zero unused facts → filler/fallback correctly owns the slot). A blind (data-free) rewrite stage was rejected: even the minimal fit pass drifted an incident type ("object"→"debris") once, so the polish stage must always carry the reference facts and run behind the gates.

**Consequences:** `scripts/prompt-loop.py` + `experiments/prompt-loop/config/` (system.md, polish-system.md, fit-system.md, input-template.md, fillers.json, config.json); `scripts/workflow_lab/duration.py`; honest_input builder hardened during the campaign (self-referential anchors, ramp carriageway rendering, micro-segment merge, digit-name respell, neutral flow bands, weather-alert flag still open). Foundry: `arn-draft-atn-voice-v1:3` + `arn-polish-atn-v1` (terra, reasoning low, ≥2000 max tokens), wired to nothing. True-sample fixtures: `full-*`, `fresh-*`, `pm-*` in test/corpus/regressions. Known remainders for the C# port: Perth-style stubborn over-length needs the existing deterministic trailing-trim as backstop; Darwin-class markets need the deeper ARN filler bank (editorial ask, deliberately held); weather-ALERT lead handling in the honest builder.


## 2026-07-10 — Variation layer: seeded shape plans + gold-reference exemplar rotation; agreed register is "every phrase informs"

**Status:** accepted (lab-validated; part of the prompt-loop config)

**Context:** Requirement: near-identical inputs must yield audibly different bulletins so listeners never hear the same read twice, without any fidelity cost. Research grounding: automated-journalism precedent (AP/Wordsmith) solves this with seeded branching over bounded STRUCTURAL variation spaces, never lexical randomness (which trades against faithfulness — hallucination-in-NLG survey); vendor guidance confirms in-prompt examples dominate induced structure. Register question settled against the corpus: ATN's colour is almost all load-bearing (severity idiom, change framing, local-pattern knowledge — pure attitude is ~3 phrases in 6.8k words), reconciled with ARN's 2026-07-01 factual/objective ruling as the phrase test: "every phrase must tell the listener something about the road — pace, change, reach, cause, or pattern; attitude-only phrases are cut."

**Decision:** (1) Nine gold-reference reads written under that register (experiments/prompt-loop/config/gold-references.json) — targets for diffing and the exemplar pool. (2) Seeded Variation Plan per read (hash of scenario+run): lead treatment (bound to item 1), rhythm register, chain placement, tail shape, and a rotated 2-exemplar subset of the gold references injected with the data — structure varies, facts never. (3) incidentChanges surfaced into the honest data block as the one licensed source of change framing ("that earlier breakdown's cleared"). (4) `prompt-loop.py repeat <scenario> -n N` = the variety proof: N consecutive reads on identical data with previous-script anti-repeat.

**Rationale:** Verified on pm-sydney ×5: all five factually clean, all lead item 1 (per the continuity rule: same worst incident keeps the lead, the shape changes), pairwise word-sequence similarity 59–76% with rotating phrasing/verbs/tails. Builder hardened again along the way (paired both-direction closures merged into one fact — stops per-direction length recitation; second-generation scaffold de-seed after "clean sensor readings" leaked to air).

**Consequences:** Variety at the sentence/phrasing level is proven; item ORDER stays data-ranked by design (matches ATN continuity). Known limits recorded honestly: two of five proof reads still twin in the opener shape (LEAD_TREATMENTS has 3 options — widen if operator wants harder rotation); the repeat harness runs draft-only (timing owned by polish in the full pipeline); Darwin-class empty feeds remain the held editorial filler-bank ask. C# port surface unchanged from the two-stage adoption entry, plus: gold refs ship as content, variation plan is ~30 lines of orchestrator code, incidentChanges already exists in the pipeline (IncidentChangeFormatter) and only needs wiring into the honest block.
## 2026-07-10 — Functional-core / honest-edge convergence: inject time, narrow catches, extract pure decisions, and honestly metric fallbacks

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An audit of Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Functions, and web for Result/Option consistency, exception boundaries, deterministic seams, fallback observability, and oversized units identified several concrete issues: a pure extraction candidate in priority-road boost logic, missing fallback-activation metrics, non-deterministic timestamps in poison-queue and voice-calibration paths, and overly broad malformed-data exception handling in `GeneratorInputJson`.

**Decision:** Pure decisions live in Domain services and have no ambient dependencies. Ambient time (e.g. `DateTime.UtcNow`) is injected via `Func<DateTime>` parameters in the Domain and `TimeProvider` in Infrastructure, enabling deterministic tests. Expected malformed external or persisted data (e.g. a JSON parse failure on a job payload) becomes a logged absence or a `Result<T>` failure — not an exception. Programming errors (null-ref, argument-out-of-range in production code) are not caught; they surface naturally. Activated fallbacks and unavailable-fallback decisions each emit distinct, honest metric names so monitoring can distinguish a healthy fallback from a genuine absence.

**Rationale:** The five delivered slices are each small, testable, and provably behavior-preserving: `PriorityRoads.EnabledIncidentBoostNames` is a pure extraction; operator fallback activation plus no-fallback stage metrics add observability without changing control flow; poison-queue failure metrics and injected timestamps fix a non-deterministic gap; injected `VoiceCalibration` clock with required timestamp makes calibration tests reproducible; `GeneratorInputJson` malformed-data handling narrowed to `JsonException` via `SafeJson` removes false-positive catches without suppressing the one real failure mode.

**Consequences:** Failure-semantics changes found by audit were deliberately deferred where behavior preservation was not provable — especially the non-HTTP exception swallowing in `GlobalExceptionHandlingMiddleware`, which was not changed. No frontend source was changed; its only silent-catch candidate would alter visible behavior without a proven contract. All three pre-existing StyleRules test failures (1 Application, 2 Infrastructure) are unrelated to this work and remain as-is.

## 2026-07-10 - Config-defined agent-pipeline engine in the lab (SOLID decomposition, A/B-able architectures)

**Status:** accepted (lab harness; informs the C# port)

**Context:** Iterating on agent *architectures* (not just prompts) required code edits per experiment.
Now `scripts/workflow_lab/pipeline.py` + `experiments/prompt-loop/config/pipelines/*.json` define entire
architectures as config: llm stages (system prompt file, input template, candidate fan-out `n`, `when`
condition, `accept` policy) and deterministic ops (`budget_plan`, `predict`, `select_best`,
`trim_transforms`, `gates`, `fit_context`) from a registry. Run via `prompt-loop.py pipe <name>`.
SOLID mapping: one stage = one transformation (S); new architecture = new JSON, new capability = one
registry entry (O); all stages share the bag->bag contract so LLM and deterministic fitters are
interchangeable (L); templates may only reference declared bag keys - undeclared access raises,
preventing scaffold leak (I); stages depend on injected duration model / gate suite / client (D).

**Decision:** Use the config-defined workflow lab as the canonical experimentation surface for comparing agent-pipeline architectures before porting a winning shape into C#. Pipelines declare LLM stages and registered deterministic operations in JSON; the budget-plan pipeline remains an experiment until its coverage-aware trimming and final-sizing order defects are resolved.

**Rationale:** Architecture experiments must be reproducible and comparable without bespoke control-flow edits. The shared bag-to-bag contract and injected stage dependencies keep experiments modular, while the first controlled A/B showed both measurable duration/gate gains and concrete integration defects that the declarative stage order makes straightforward to isolate.

**First A/B (run-022 two-stage vs run-024 budget-plan, same 9 scenarios):** budget-plan
(det sentence budgets -> 3 decorrelated candidates -> det select -> det trim transforms + trailing-trim
-> gates) put chronic over-length markets in band deterministically (Perth 30.7s first time) and
repaired Brisbane 2->0 gates, at ~1.9x call cost. Two integration defects found and owned: (1)
trailing-trim dropped Perth's fuel line - the backstop must be coverage-aware (protect mandated
Traffic/Weather/Fuel content, drop only optional facts); (2) GateRepair placed after final sizing
re-lengthened Adelaide to 33.3s - repair must precede final sizing or acceptance must be composite
(fewer gates AND duration not worse). Both are one-line config/op fixes - which is the point.

**Consequences:** architecture experiments are now one JSON file + one command; the winning pipeline
shape and its stage/op vocabulary are the direct spec for the C# port's stage interfaces.

## 2026-07-10 — Queue Failure Policy: Boundary Between Application Result Values and Host Retry/Poison

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Queue-triggered functions (broadcast, regeneration) caught the host-level exception boundary and the application-level Result values in the same place, with no explicit policy deciding which failures are acknowledged and which are retried. This made it unclear whether a `Result` failure from the orchestrator would silently succeed (poisoning the job's state) or trigger a host redelivery storm.

**Decision:** Application/core orchestration errors remain `Result` values — the orchestrator, its sub-services, and domain operations never throw on business failures. A new `QueueFailurePolicy` at the Functions boundary classifies the orchestrator's `Result.Error` string into: (1) **acknowledge and return** for content-limited, content-safety-violation, terminal-state, and permanent TTS errors; (2) **throw `InvalidOperationException`** for all other (transient/unknown) failures, allowing the Azure host to redeliver. Malformed queue messages throw immediately for bounded host retry then poison. Unexpected non-HTTP exceptions propagate through the global middleware (which re-throws them for host retry/poison handling rather than swallowing). Unexpected HTTP exceptions are caught by the same middleware and translated to structured 500 responses. Broadcast poison persistence uses `FunctionContext.CancellationToken` so the job state is cancelled at the host boundary without an additional domain call.

**Rationale:** This separates two concerns that were previously conflated: the application's own error taxonomy (Result values, a domain concern) and the host's retry/poison protocol (a Functions-boundary concern). By keeping orchestration logic free of `throw` on business failures and concentrating the classify-or-throw decision in one policy, the Functions layer can evolve its retry policy without touching application or domain code. The string-prefix classifier is explicitly temporary pending a phase-4 structured error taxonomy.

**Consequences:** `QueueFailurePolicy.ClassifyOrThrow` is the single chokepoint for all queue-trigger error decisions in both `BroadcastQueueTrigger` and `RegenerationQueueTrigger`. The current string-prefix matching (`ErrorMessages.Broadcast.ContentLimitedPrefix`, etc.) will be replaced by a structured error-type enum in phase 4. Global middleware now distinguishes HTTP context (structured 500 response) from non-HTTP context (re-throw for host handling), eliminating the prior silent-swallow class of non-HTTP exceptions. Phase 3 will prove these paths survive Azurite-backed local E2E without relying on deployed dev.
## 2026-07-10 - Translation layer at the data boundary (deterministic HERE-vocabulary normalizer)

**Status:** accepted (lab: scripts/workflow_lab/normalize.py; C# port: same taxonomy as a
normalizer stage feeding the data block builder)

**Decision:** Add a deterministic translation layer (scripts/workflow_lab/normalize.py) at the
_fact_text funnel: a closed spoken-safe lexicon every raw HERE string passes through before any
prompt; the DATA-SPEAK gate stays as the backstop for unmapped labels.

**Context:** Every stage that saw feed text was a leak vector, and best-of-N selection Goodharts
whatever gates don't cover.

**Rationale:** Raw HERE worksite labels kept reaching air across the whole campaign ("Services
Locating", "Contraflow", "Hazardous driving conditions", "Approach with care") - every stage that
saw feed text was a leak vector, and best-of-N selection Goodharts whatever gates don't cover.
Decision: a single-responsibility DETERMINISTIC translation layer at the one funnel every raw
string passes through (_fact_text). Closed spoken-safe lexicon; meaning-preserving register
translation only ("Services Locating" -> "utility crews", "Contraflow" -> "traffic directed both
ways on one side", severity/enforcement tags dropped). NOT an LLM stage - an LLM translator would
move the leak boundary upstream and add a fabrication surface. Unknown labels pass through and are
caught by the DATA-SPEAK gate (demoted to defense-in-depth backstop) and reported so the taxonomy
grows from telemetry.

**Evidence:** run-026 leaked 2 label classes; run-028 (layer active) 1 partial ("Hazardous driving
conditions" beat the first regex); run-029 zero. Downstream prompts unchanged.

**Consequences:** agents consume a simpler, closed vocabulary; jargon leaks die by construction
rather than by gate; the taxonomy is the single place ARN editorial can adjust feed renderings.
Known open item: GateRepair-after-sizing can still re-lengthen a read (Cairns 34.7s run-029) -
stage-ordering fix pending in the pipeline config.

## 2026-07-10 - ATN convergence campaign: certified 3/9 -> 6/9 AIR; detection complete, enforcement completion bounded by retry budget

**Status:** accepted (lab; the gate suite and pipeline order are the C# port spec)

**Decision:** Adopt the full deterministic detection suite + enforcement mitigations listed below
as the shipped lab pipeline and the C# port spec; accept that the remaining per-wave consistency gap
is a retry-budget property to be closed in the production port, not by further prompt iteration.

**Context:** Autonomous refinement campaign (runs 034-060, two independent atn-reviewer
certifications) toward "legitimately matches ATN samples, consistently air-ready".

**Rationale:** Evidence below - certified trajectory, complete detection, bounded enforcement.

**Achieved, certified independently:** pass rate doubled 3/9 -> 6/9 AIR with the verdict
"the six passing reads would air on an ARN station tonight without a flinch - the writer's
voice, calibration, and grounding discipline are now ATN-grade". Zero fabrications in any
certified wave. Variety proof: 42-59% pairwise similarity on identical data, four distinct
opener shapes, item-1 discipline held. Timing: content markets consistently inside the
30-32.1s overshoot envelope or the slow-fill band.

**Detection layer (complete, all deterministic):** consequence-first corridor re-ranking
(closure > major delay/incident > incident > congestion > maintenance trivia) + MUST-voice
tagging; COVERAGE, SELECTION (trivia-never-displaces), MINUTES (incl. compound word-numbers),
META-LEAK (provenance language), HAZARD + HAZARD-OMITTED (reassurance inversion), CLOSED-OMITTED,
TAIL-ORDER, HEADLESS-STATUS (mid-sentence), DATA-SPEAK, CITE (per-sentence fact citations with
short-form + continuation matching), digit->words speller, clause-aware duplicate-anchor/roll-call
mirrors. Every class the reviewer caught in either certification now fires as a gate, verified
offline against the exact failing scripts.

**Enforcement layer (the honest boundary):** one-shot GateRepair clears violations ~60%;
per-wave fully-clean oscillates 4-8 of 9 under LLM sampling variance. Mitigations shipped:
composite repair acceptance (repair -> deterministic trim -> judge), consequence-protected
trim with least-consequence fallback, envelope-tolerant sentence drops (never for <=1s
overshoot), and a final RATCHET stage (ship the best artifact of the run - monotonicity
guaranteed). Residual: 1-3 flags/wave, dominated by roll-call/phrase-reuse style class and
enforcement-completion misses. The remaining consistency gap is a RETRY-BUDGET property, not
a prompt property: the lab allows 2 repair attempts; production's port with the detectors as
unconditional rejectors and a real retry budget closes it. Darwin stays structurally unairable
pending the ARN filler bank (editorial dependency, held).

**Consequences:** prompts (justified-system.md et al) + gate suite + pipeline JSON are the
port-ready spec; the two certification reports (agent://AtnWave2Review, agent://AtnFinalCert2)
are the acceptance baseline; review packs archived per wave.

## 2026-07-13 — Populate dev station schedules from ARN workbook

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The downloaded ARNTN Bulletin Workings workbook contains the current station clock rows in its 2026 June Update sheet. Dev already had MarketSchedule records, including a stale Cairns KIIS 90 duplicate, and the confirmed pilot identity is KIIS 90s in Sydney plus 4CA in Cairns.

**Decision:** Update existing dev MarketSchedule rows rather than creating frequency duplicates: map KIIS 102.3 to Adelaide, KIIS 97.3 to Brisbane, KIIS 1011 to Melbourne, KIIS 1065 to Sydney (renamed KIIS 90s), and Gold 96FM to Perth. Import weekday/Saturday/Sunday clock times as newline-separated five-field cron lines and set each report duration from the workbook. Remove the stale cairns-kiis90 row; retain the existing cairns-4ca row because the workbook has no 4CA timing row.

**Rationale:** The schedule API and CronParser accept five-field cron expressions and compound newline-separated clocks, while the workbook times include seconds that cannot be represented by the deployed parser. Reusing stable market keys preserves coverage, voices, pronunciation dictionaries, content selection, and other station settings; removing the stale duplicate prevents Sydney KIIS 90s from remaining configured in Cairns.

**Consequences:** Dev now has workbook-derived clocks for five existing markets, with seconds truncated to the supported minute precision. The 4CA pilot schedule remains its prior dev clock until a 4CA-specific workbook row is supplied. Generated documentation indexes must be refreshed after this decision.
