## 2026-07-14 — Route every pipeline LLM call through a Foundry agent (behaviour-preserving)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Draft and Polish already called Foundry prompt agents (`arn-draft-natural-v53`, `arn-polish-natural-v1`); Review, Refine, Attribute, Safety, and Director still hit the raw model endpoint (`POST /openai/v1/responses`). Raw-model calls produce only an opaque HTTP dependency span — no input/output/model/content-filter visibility — so five of seven roles were untraceable in Foundry. Goal: full transparency and architectural consistency, every LLM call through an agent (Safety included).

**Decision:** Swap the transport, not the prompts. Added `AzureAIOptions.AgentNameFor(role)` + per-role `{Review,Refine,Attribute,Safety,Director}AgentName` config, and a single `LlmScriptGenerator.DispatchLlmAsync(role, …)` seam that routes to the Foundry agent when the role's name is set, else the raw model. Brought `SendToAgentAsync` to parity with `SendToModelAsync`: `ILlmCallCapture` (else agent calls vanish from job-diagnostics — a transparency regression), token-exhaustion retry, and API-key auth fallback. Live probing then forced the format design: the agent endpoint REJECTS a request-side `text` field, and `prompts/system.md` (the writer prompt) as agent instructions BREAKS the JSON roles (a Safety agent so configured returns a rewritten bulletin, not a verdict). So each role agent instead carries NEUTRAL "defer to the user message" instructions + a BAKED response format (json_object for Review/Attribute/Safety/Director; text for Refine) + baked reasoning effort (Review `low`, else `none`); the pipeline sends the rendered role template as user input unchanged, so the git templates remain the single source of role behaviour. `provision-foundry-agents.sh` provisions the five role agents reproducibly; Draft/Polish stay hand-tuned portal agents.

**Rationale:** Verified against the live dev endpoint that the agent definition bakes `model`/`reasoning_effort`/`text.format` and rejects request-side `text`, and that `json_object` requires the word "json" in the input (every JSON role's template has "Return JSON…"). Neutral instructions + baked format reproduce the raw path's effective behaviour (JSON mode forced the envelope there too) while keeping the Safety bar's wording byte-identical — the responsible choice for a compliance-reviewed gate. A separate future change can restructure prompts into portal-editable per-role system prompts if that flexibility is wanted.

**Consequences:** Shipped and ACTIVATED on dev. Full solution builds; Infrastructure (1183) + Application (473) unit suites green. `provision-foundry-agents.sh` created `arn-{review,refine,attribute,safety,director}`; the five `{Role}AgentName` app-settings are set on `IBP-AUE-DEV-FNA-APP01`; backend redeployed. Live E2E (job `bcb979202aea45a8a78bd19a14cdced0`, Melbourne 30s) reached WaitingApproval with App Insights confirming Draft/Review/Refine/Polish/Safety each routed through its agent (per-agent `invoke_agent` traces, zero raw `openai/v1/responses` calls); Safety passed on clean content and blocks profanity (direct probe). Attribute/Director route identically but didn't fire this run (deterministic provenance skips Attribute; neutral delivery skips Director). Source-of-truth + Safety governance in `docs/reference/foundry-role-agents.md`; eval config MUST set the same agent names as production or it silently tests a different transport. NOTE: dev's global `ReasoningEffort=none` app-setting still forces any RAW-model role to `none`, but agent-routed roles use their baked effort, so Review now runs at its A/B-optimal `low`.

**Addendum (2026-07-14, same day):** Review flipped from `low` to `none` on operator instruction — all role agents now use `none` (speed/cost + consistency). This also fixed a Foundry-trace visibility quirk: at `low`, Review's hidden reasoning phase drew from the same `max_output_tokens` budget and could exhaust it before emitting a message, so the `invoke_agent arn-review` trace showed an EMPTY output (the pipeline still worked via the budget-doubling retry). At `none` every Review call's JSON verdict is visible in its trace, matching Refine. Re-provisioned (`arn-review` reasoning=none) and re-verified live (job `212fa812e61046f483661af6663dbdd0`): all Review calls 200 with visible verdicts. The earlier A/B favouring `low` is noted in `provision-foundry-agents.sh` / `docs/reference/foundry-role-agents.md`; revisit if review quality regresses.

**Addendum 2 (2026-07-14) — Review prompt redesigned to fix a `reasoning: none` false-positive class.** At `none` the neutral critic pattern-matched "construction + pace word = fabricated pace" and flagged compliant road-feel (e.g. "a slow patch" on a road whose data supplied *minor delays*) — verified against a live agent output, and corroborated by an external GPT-5.6-prompting review (ChatGPT, `/tmp/review-agent-feedback.md`). Fix, keeping `reasoning: none`: `arn-review` is now the ONE role agent with a baked semantic-verifier system prompt (`prompts/review-system.md`) instead of neutral instructions — per-road judging, an explicit "construction does not cancel a supplied delay" rule, a spoken-equivalence lexicon, and a prove-before-flag requirement; folded-in checks (fabrication, wrong-incident-type, contradiction, vagueness, restatement, continuity, minute-figures, not-from-data, name-spelling) preserve the old review's coverage. `prompts/review.md` slimmed to a data+script+run-context user message. Iterated by calling the agent directly on an 11-case matrix (false-positive script + clear-defect + flowing-well/construction-only guards + vagueness/duplication/minute/advice/spelling) until all passed. `arn-review` re-provisioned to v4 and verified live: the false positive is fixed even against the still-deployed old review.md (the V3b system prompt dominates). REMAINING: the slim `review.md` redeploy is staged but blocked on PIM Owner re-activation (ARM 403); the fix is already live via the agent, so the redeploy is cleanup, not correctness. `provision-foundry-agents.sh` now maps per-agent instructions (Review → `review-system.md`, others neutral).

## 2026-07-14 — Construction-caused road closures must render as closures (RoadClosed flag is authoritative)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A review of live dev bulletins found a consistent, high-stakes defect: Flinders St ("Closed due to road construction", `RoadClosed=true`) aired as "moderate delays" / "roadworks" / "works underway" across three bulletins — a closed road announced as merely slow. Root-caused to the data layer, not the LLM: HERE reports a construction-CAUSED closure with incident `Type="construction"` (type-priority 6) plus `RoadClosed=true`. `CorridorAggregator` derived `PrimaryType` purely from incident type, so the corridor was "construction", not "roadClosure"; `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.FormatImpact` (and `CorridorMagnitude.TypeFloor` tiering) key off `PrimaryType`, so the closure was rendered as roadworks/delays and never reached the draft or review agent. The writer and `arn-review` were exonerated — they never saw a closure. (A pre-existing guard already stripped the "Closed…" status text from location anchors, for the INVERSE `RoadClosed=false` false-"closed" case — Brisbane Gilchrist Ave — which created this blind spot for the `RoadClosed=true` case.)

**Decision:** Treat `RoadClosed=true` on ANY incident as authoritative: in `CorridorAggregator`'s two `PrimaryType` derivations (primary build + same-road merge), force `PrimaryType="roadClosure"` when `incidents.Any(i => i.RoadClosed)`, else fall back to the type-priority pick. This mirrors `FalseClosureDetector`'s own `Incidents.Any(i => i.RoadClosed)` closure test and propagates to FormatImpact ("road closed"), tiering (Major → leads), hot-board and closure reconciliation with no per-site edits.

**Rationale:** The flag is HERE's authoritative closure signal; the type headline is not. Fixing `PrimaryType` upstream is a single conceptual change that corrects rendering, tiering, and lead selection together. Precisely scoped to `RoadClosed=true`, so the `RoadClosed=false` false-closure handling is untouched.

**Consequences:** `CorridorAggregator.cs` two-site change + two `CorridorAggregatorTests` (RoadClosed→roadClosure; RoadClosed=false→unchanged). Domain (1145) + Infrastructure (1183) suites green; deployed to dev and live-verified (job `7b51a2ac4bb04aeea5a81e8708794caf`): the construction-caused Flinders St closure now airs "Flinders Street's closed for construction" and leads the bulletin. Note a secondary, separate nuance remains on multi-spot closure corridors (which cross-street the closure is anchored to when one road has both a lane-blocked and a closed spot) — not addressed here.
## 2026-07-15 — Pipeline root-cause fixes: opaque labels, reviewer contract, gated refine, code validators + slim draft, blueprint stage

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A root-cause investigation found the bulletins' recurring tells were NOT the draft (a stage-by-stage trace showed the draft clean and well-shaped) and NOT sampling (same-input runs varied wording at word-Jaccard ~0.55 but produced an IDENTICAL structure; the draft envelope confirmed temperature=1/top_p=0.98). They were inflicted downstream: (1) the summariser handed the writer the literal label "Priority roads flowing well", which the model echoed ("priority roads", "flowing well"); (2) the reviewer mandated the data-label wording (rejecting "moving nicely" as unsupported against the authorised "flowing well") and killed natural framing ("a good run across Mildura" flagged as a market-wide all-clear); (3) the refine ratchet REWARDED padding, because a bloated candidate lowered the word-deficit axis; (4) the draft agent prompt had accumulated v31–v36 patches (a ~12k ban-list — the contrastive-prompts anti-pattern), and the "while"/redundant-tail tells were actually introduced by the POLISH stage, not the draft; (5) structure never varied because the summariser pre-orders/caps the evidence and the reasoning=none writer is a surface realiser. Corroborated against recent (Jun–Jul 2026) work: Where You Inject Diversity Matters (structure comes from specification diversity, not temperature), DISC (naive correction degrades already-correct output — gate it), Learning from Contrastive Prompts (stop accumulating per-failure fixes).

**Decision:** Five coupled changes. (1) `ContentFormatters.FormatGoodRuns` header made opaque ("Clear — no incidents reported on these roads", varied wording) and the good-run `EvidenceUnit` value changed "flowing well"→"clear" — the backstage label and stock verb never reach the writer. (2) `review-system.md` (arn-review) gained a clear-road spoken-equivalence line (clear / moving nicely / looking good / … = flowing well) and its FABRICATION check no longer treats a qualified scene-setting opener as a false all-clear. (3) The refine ratchet in `BroadcastOrchestrator` now scores current AND candidate on the same full `ComputeViolationCounts` set (symmetric), so a restating/padding refine is rejected on the style axis instead of rewarded on deficit. (4) New Domain validators `ConnectorFrequencyDetector` (max one "while") and `RedundantTailDetector` (drops a restating/summary tail) wired into `ComputeViolationCounts` (the polish gate reverts a polish that introduces them) + a final mechanical tail Repair; new always-on `ClearRoadLabelNormalizer` ("flowing well"→"moving nicely", "moving well"→"looking good") at all three generate/refine/polish sites alongside `ClosureVerbNormalizer` — the durable "flowing well" backstop; and the draft agent slimmed (v37) by removing the prohibitions now enforced in code, keeping the positive ATN guidance + exemplars. (5) New `BlueprintSelector` (Domain) emits a bounded, seed-stable per-read blueprint (opener / flow / clear-road placement / close) rendered into `draft.md`'s new `{{blueprint}}` slot, replacing the single random "variety angle" — structural variety via an explicit specification, with the severity-lead and facts immutable.

**Rationale:** Each defect was fixed at its true source and, where prompt-only rules had proven unreliable, moved to a deterministic gate/normaliser (the established "prompt for style, code for invariants" pattern). The draft slim follows the contrastive-prompts finding; the gated refine follows DISC; the blueprint follows the diversity finding (vary the spec, not the temperature).

**Consequences:** New files `ConnectorFrequencyDetector.cs`, `RedundantTailDetector.cs`, `ClearRoadLabelNormalizer.cs`, `BlueprintSelector.cs` (Domain/Services) + unit tests; edits to `ContentFormatters.cs`, `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.EvidenceUnits.cs`, `BroadcastOrchestrator.cs` (ComputeViolationCounts + symmetric ratchet + final-gate tail repair), `LlmScriptGenerator.cs` (blueprint wiring + normalizer sites + VarietyAngles removed), `prompts/draft.md`, `prompts/review-system.md`; agents redeployed (`arn-draft-natural-v53` v37, `arn-review` v5); backend deployed to dev + restarted. Domain (1156) / Application (473) / Infrastructure (1184) suites green. Live-verified across Mildura/Queenstown/Sydney/Melbourne/Darwin: no "priority roads", no "flowing well"/"moving well", Mildura's light-picture lead restored, no restatement padding or summary sign-off, and the blueprint present in the draft input. Jobs created during the ~2-min config-zip rollout hit stale static-loaded prompts (known worker-recycle lag); re-verified clean on the recycled worker.
## 2026-07-15 — Trace-driven pipeline-churn fixes: scaled expansion band, reviewer calibration, vagueness gate

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Pulling the Foundry agent traces (App Insights GenAI spans; `scripts/foundry-agent-trace.py`) for five live bulletins showed a single 30s read taking 6–12 `invoke_agent` calls. Root causes, per the traces: (1) the word-target EXPANSION (`EnsureWordTargetComplianceAsync`) fired whenever a read was >5 words under the ~90-word/30s target and burned up to 2 refine+review round-trips LLM-padding it — usually failing grounding and reverting — yet a 76-word read already filled a 30s slot via the audio slow-fill; (2) the reviewer flagged the draft's own sanctioned road-feel idiom ("under the pump") as NOT_FROM_DATA opinion, and raised non-defects (article "the Bruce Highway" vs "Bruce Highway"; "Mt" vs "Mount") that churned refine — and, chasing the article flag, a refine replaced a named road with a pronoun and created a real cross-corridor mis-attribution; (3) expansion-introduced vague fillers ("a couple more spots", "around town") were caught only by the LLM reviewer.

**Decision:** (1) `SlotFitPlanner.NeedsExpansion` now uses a SCALED accept-band — expand only below `target − max(5, round(target*0.16))` (≈84% of target) — so a grounded near-target read is accepted (fillers + audio slow-fill close the gap) instead of LLM-padded; expansion is reserved for a genuinely short read. (2) `review-system.md` (arn-review) calibrated: the ATN road-feel palette for a SUPPORTED severity is house translation, never NOT_FROM_DATA; "prove a defect or approve" reinforced (a reason that says "not a defect"/"otherwise supported" must not be raised); closure synonyms extended ("blocked"/"sealed off"); standard abbreviation⇄spoken-form pairs (Mt=Mount, St=Street, Rd=Road, …) are never NAME_SPELLING defects. (3) `refine.md` forbids replacing a named road with a pronoun. (4) New `VaguenessDetector` (Domain) wired into `ComputeViolationCounts`, so the polish gate reverts and the refine ratchet penalises vague unsourced filler.

**Rationale:** Trace-grounded — the churn was expansion firing on in-band reads plus the reviewer fighting the house style and raising non-defects. Each fixed at source; where prompt-only proved weak, backed by code (the vagueness gate). A `MaxExpansionGroundingRetries` cap (2→1) was tried and reverted — it broke the legitimate one-refine recovery path and two tests; the accept-band change is the real lever, and when expansion does fire (a genuinely short read) the recovery retry is warranted.

**Consequences:** Edits: `SlotFitPlanner.cs` (scaled band) + `SlotFitPlannerTests`; `BroadcastOrchestrator.cs` (VaguenessDetector in `ComputeViolationCounts`); new `VaguenessDetector.cs` + tests; `prompts/review-system.md` (deployed as arn-review v6), `prompts/refine.md`. All four suites green (Domain 1173 / Application 473 / Infrastructure 1184 / Functions 332). Backend + arn-review v6 deployed to dev. Live-verified via re-pulled traces across 5 markets: agent invocations **44 → 24 (45% fewer)** — Sydney/Melbourne 8→3 (draft→polish→safety fast path), Perth 12→6, Brisbane 10→6, Adelaide 6→6; every read 30s/30s audio, no vague filler, no "flowing well", weather+fuel present, "under the pump"/"Mount Crosby" kept without churn.
## 2026-07-15 — Polish stage disabled in dev (`Broadcast__NaturalnessPolish=false`)

**Status:** accepted (temporary, dev)

**Context:** Trace review showed the naturalness-polish stage adds an LLM round-trip whose output is frequently discarded by the deterministic polish gate (`PolishGateReject`: polish is rephrase-only with facts frozen, and reverts to the pre-polish read on any word-band / locked-weather-fuel-line / corridor-lineage / detector regression). With the draft now producing clean, in-band reads directly (and the churn fixes landed), the marginal upside no longer justified the extra call.

**Decision:** Set `Broadcast__NaturalnessPolish=false` on the dev Function App, which gates out `PolishAndGateAsync` (call site `BroadcastOrchestrator` line ~2631; the flag already existed). The dev pipeline is now draft → (conditional review/refine) → safety.

**Rationale:** Pure config toggle, fully reversible, no code change. Simplifies the workflow while we assess draft-only quality.

**Consequences:** Dev only; re-enable with `Broadcast__NaturalnessPolish=true`. The polish agent (`arn-polish-natural-v1`) stays deployed but unused. Verified live via Foundry traces: fresh jobs (`8d81573565…` Sydney, `ded971fb…` Brisbane) show NO `arn-polish` invoke_agent span — flows are draft→review→refine→safety and the draft→safety fast path.
## 2026-07-15 — Dev stations standardised (30s + single fixed voice) and triggered via the scheduled poller, not manual `/broadcast`

**Status:** accepted (dev)

**Context:** Operator wanted 8 configured dev stations to (a) generate 30s bulletins and (b) speak in one of two named professional voices — Dolly Traffic or Jeffrey David G — and asked us to stop triggering bulletins manually. Manual `POST /api/broadcast` (TriggerStudio) BYPASSES per-station voice-profile `Settings`, delivery style, pronunciation, per-station LLM model, and content selection — so it falls back to the default **ARN Hudson** voice and airs traffic-only (no weather/fuel). Only the **scheduled poller** (`SchedulePollerTrigger`, `0 * * * * *`) resolves the full station config.

**Decision:** For sydney/brisbane/adelaide/darwin (→ Dolly Traffic, profile `vp-5d16…`) and melbourne/perth/goldcoast/cairns-4ca (→ Jeffrey David G, profile `vp-da7b…`): set `TargetDurationSeconds=30`, `VoiceProfileId` to the target profile, and `VoiceRotation.Mode="single"`. The last is essential — all 8 had a `roundRobin` rotation over the three *ARN Sarah* variants, and `SchedulePollerService.SelectVoiceProfileId` uses the rotation set and IGNORES `VoiceProfileId` unless the mode is `single`. Content was already `{Traffic,Weather,Fuel}=true` on every schedule. Triggered via the poller by temporarily setting a near-future daily cron in each station's timezone + `Enabled=true`, then reverting cron + `Enabled=false` (permanent 30s/voice changes retained).

**Rationale:** The station-config + poller path is the real on-air path; manual triggering misrepresents voice and content. Single-voice matches the "each station uses one of these two voices" requirement. Pure config (API PUT), fully reversible.

**Consequences:** Dev-only schedule edits (no code). Live-verified: 8 poller-created jobs each rendered the correct fixed voice on `eleven_multilingual_v2`, exactly 30s audio, weather + fuel present. Codified the correct trigger procedure internally so we don't regress to manual `/broadcast`. (Observation, out of scope: thin-data markets like Darwin still emit a short redundant sign-off tail — pre-existing behaviour, not addressed here.)
## 2026-07-15 — Agent trace audit: corrected Darwin root cause, reviewer false-positive findings, eval corpus established

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Audited 107 production-pipeline LLM calls (clean window after polish removal, `2026-07-15T03:21:20Z`+: draft v37 / review v6 / refine v2 / safety v6) pulled from Foundry traces via `scripts/foundry-traces.py`.

**Findings / decisions:**
- **Corrected Darwin root cause.** The redundant recap tail is produced by the **refine agent**, not the draft. On thin markets the draft returns a tight honest read (Darwin: clean 47 words) and refine, invoked purely to expand toward the 30s word target, pads it (→88 words) with back-referencing recaps ("so it's a clear run across those routes", "So, apart from Linco Road's closure…"). Both Darwin runs showed draft→refine(+recap). Supersedes the earlier "draft padded / detector+fast-path missed it" framing in the 2026-07-15 station-standardisation entry.
- **Refine padding is intended, not a bug** (product decision): the fixed 30s slot must be filled or the audio can't stretch and it falls back to dead air. **Decision:** keep refine expansion-padding, but surface an explicit "insufficient data — not a cohesive bulletin" signal in the operator UI and expose the existing `reject-to-fallback` job action so the operator can choose fallback. (UI/backend change planned, not yet built.)
- **Reviewer (`arn-review` v6) precision is low** (~2/7 flags genuine in-window). False positives: (a) flags correct spoken abbreviation expansions of HERE source tokens — `Ht Toll Plaza`→`Harbour Tunnel Toll Plaza` (4×), same class as `Mt`→`Mount`, whitelist gap in check 9; (b) a self-contradicting flag whose own text says "not a defect under the stated rules". Genuine catches: fabricated queue extent, wrong-incident-type. FPs trigger unnecessary refine runs.
- **Draft and safety agents are clean** in-window: draft 0 fabricated roads / 0 banned sign-offs / 0 recap tails (26 calls); safety 0 blocks / 0 malformed (31 calls; no adversarial content present to exercise true-positive blocking).

**Decision:** Record the corrected Darwin root cause (recap-padding originates in the refine agent, not the draft) and stand up the append-only agent eval corpus as the seed for an automated suite; leave the reviewer false positives as tracked open cases rather than hot-patching prompts.

**Rationale:** Trace evidence overturned the earlier draft-blame diagnosis, so the record must be corrected; a durable, replayable corpus stops us re-litigating the same findings and is the foundation for measurable regression testing.

**Consequences:** New append-only eval corpus (`cases.yaml` + `README.md`), seeded with 5 adjudicated cases (3 reviewer FP + 2 TP) carrying full replayable agent inputs — the seed for a future automated agent eval suite (replay input → assert `correct_verdict`). New tool `scripts/foundry-traces.py`. Open fixes tracked in the corpus: reviewer NAME_SPELLING abbreviation whitelist (`Ht`→Harbour Tunnel) and the self-contradiction guard. Caveat: Foundry `invoke_agent` spans are App-Insights-sampled (~1-2h retention), so issue capture must happen promptly.
## 2026-07-15 — Same-day continuity verified on the deployed plain-text Foundry path (dev)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After switching dev to the fast plain-text Foundry-agent draft path (`arn-draft-natural-v53`, `UsePlainTextDraft=true`, `MaxReviewRefineRetries=0`), verified that same-day multi-bulletin continuity ("bulletins throughout the day") still works. Confirmed the plumbing reaches the Foundry path: `LlmScriptGenerator` sets `arguments["previousScript"]`/`["incidentChanges"]` (1044–1052) BEFORE the plain-text branch (1085), rendered into `prompts/draft.md` (the `{{#if previousScript}}…build on it as an update{{/if}}` + `{{#if incidentChanges}}` blocks) — which becomes the user message the agent sees. Then ran live published chains in dev via `/broadcast` + approve + publish: Sydney (busy) B1→B2→B3, Darwin (quiet) D1→D2, on novel location keys isolated from existing dev jobs.

**Findings:**
- **Continuity works on the deployed path.** Fresh first bulletin reads PLAINLY (Sydney B1: "The Warringah Freeway's *closed*…", no continuity verb). Later same-day bulletins carry ongoing items forward with a correct, true-to-current-data continuation marker (B2/B3: "The Warringah Freeway's *still closed*…", "Harbour Street's *still busy*…") and vary the opening (freeway-led → weather-led). No false "still" on any new/first item. No fallback in any chain; all 30s.
- **THE load-bearing constraint (non-obvious):** the same-day lookup `TableStorageJobRepository.GetLatestBulletinForMarketTodayAsync` filters on **`JobStatus.Published` ONLY** (deliberate — continuity is a claim about what *aired*). A prior at WAITING_APPROVAL/APPROVED is IGNORED. In dev, jobs sit unpublished by default, so continuity appears "off" until each bulletin is approved **and published**. The scheduled poller (`SchedulePollerService`) uses the same query, so in production continuity chains only off bulletins the operator has published. To reproduce/verify continuity in dev you MUST publish each bulletin before triggering the next.
- **Cleared-item close-off:** the incident delta fires (logs show "N cleared") and the voicing path (`TrafficNarrativeSummarizer.AppendClearedIncidents` → draft `incidentChanges`) is code-confirmed, but in the live runs the cleared items were minor/raw and correctly suppressed, so no script voiced an "X has cleared" line. A script-level cleared close-off needs a significant NAMED prior incident to clear naturally (not forcible with live HERE in minutes); the local eval harness `Skip(1)` trick forces it deterministically but tests the Azure-OpenAI path, not the deployed Foundry path.
- **Thin-market ceiling persists (not a continuity regression):** Darwin reads still show the documented padding recap tail + 4-name roll-call ("no dramas on Hook Road, Amaroo Road, Charles Darwin National Park and Ross Smith Avenue") and a mild "still offering a clear run" on the fresh read (refine expansion for the 30s slot). Pre-existing thin-data ceiling, independent of continuity.

**Decision:** Treat same-day continuity as verified on the deployed plain-text Foundry path (no code change); document that continuity chains only off a PUBLISHED prior and that dev verification must approve+publish each bulletin before triggering the next.

**Rationale:** The mechanism demonstrably works end-to-end (fresh reads plainly; ongoing items carry a true-to-data "still"); the Published-only gate is intentional ("continuity = what aired"), so the deliverable is operational guidance plus the captured evidence, not a code change.

**Consequences:** Same-day generation flows well when prior bulletins exist — verdict AIR for the continuity behaviour on busy markets; thin markets carry the known padding/roll-call blemish. No code change. Key operational note for operators/tests: continuity requires PUBLISHED priors. Live chain scripts captured at `local://continuity-review-pack.md`. (Dev side effect: published test bulletins for `Sydney, NSW, Australia` + `Darwin, NT, Australia` keys.)
## 2026-07-15 — Safety-gate adversarial test + cross-market fidelity (reviewer false-negative) audit

**Status:** accepted (findings; two hardening candidates raised, not yet implemented)

**Context:** Two verifications on deployed dev. (1) Proved the safety gate actually blocks (it had never been exercised with adversarial content — 0 blocks in the trace audit). (2) Audited whether generated scripts contain fabrications the fidelity gates missed (reviewer false negatives + fast-path gaps).

**Safety (`arn-safety`):** The deployed gate is a **Foundry agent** (`gpt-5.6-luna`, server-side instructions), invoked at `{FoundryProjectEndpoint}/agents/arn-safety/endpoint/protocols/openai/responses?api-version=v1` with the rendered `prompts/safety.md` as `input`. Ran a 22-case adversarial corpus: **21/22 verdicts correct.** Every realistic violation blocked (profanity, masked profanity, Mindframe self-harm on a bridge, victim identification/speculation, discrimination, gratuitous violence/weapons, child distress, and a prompt-injection attempt) and every legitimate script passed (fatal-crash mention, "police operation", stop-revive-survive / school-zone / seatbelt reminders, weather hazard, congestion — no over-blocking). **Finding:** extreme graphic gore ("decapitated, bodies strewn") trips Azure's own content filter (`status=incomplete, reason=content_filter` → refusal), which the app parses as a Failure and **fails open** to the human gate (`BroadcastOrchestrator.CheckContentSafetyAsync`, by design for transient LLM outages). Two-layer defence remains (deterministic wordlist runs first + mandatory human approval). **Hardening candidate:** distinguish a content-filter refusal from an outage and treat the refusal as fail-**closed**.

**Fidelity / reviewer false negatives:** Cross-checked 8 markets' scripts against their HERE `SelectedIncidents` (Detail/Direction/LengthMeters). Captured 5 provable fabrications in. **The dominant risk is the fast path** (`Conditional audit: deterministic gates clean — skipped LLM review/refine`): 4/5 fabrications reached WAITING_APPROVAL with **no LLM fidelity review** — magnitude inventions (Brisbane "queues back about seven kays" vs a 5.5km lane-block; Cairns "ten-kay construction zone" vs 2.66km), a closure misplacement (Adelaide "South Road closed at Sir Donald Bradman Drive/James Congdon" — both construction; the real closure At Ashwin Parade is unnamed), and a direction error (Cairns "hazard northbound at Myola Road" — source is southbound). The LLM reviewer, when it DID run, was mostly sound but had a subtle false negative (Perth "Stirling Highway's closed at Glyde Street" — construction stated as a located closure, reviewer approved). "Slow/standstill" claims on roads absent from `SelectedIncidents` (e.g. Gold Coast "Labrador-Carrara Road at a standstill") were NOT counted as fabrications — likely flow-pool grounded, unverified here.

**Decision:** Accept the safety gate as fit for realistic broadcast threats; capture the two hardening candidates (safety content-filter-refusal → fail-closed; a deterministic magnitude/closure/direction cross-check on the fast path) as tracked future work, not implemented in this verification-only task.

**Rationale:** The 22-case adversarial corpus proved the gate blocks every realistic violation without over-blocking legitimate copy; the two gaps are real but each needs its own change + test cycle, which is out of scope for a testing pass.

**Consequences:** New durable eval assets + `fidelity-corpus.yaml` (replay recipes in the README). Safety layer verified fit for realistic threats. **Two hardening candidates for a future task:** (a) safety content-filter-refusal → fail-closed; (b) a deterministic magnitude/closure/direction cross-check (or don't skip LLM fidelity review) on the fast path, since that path currently ships magnitude/closure/direction fabrications unchecked. Not implemented this task (testing only).
## 2026-07-15 — Comprehensive bulletin evaluation suite authored (design + scenarios; runner wiring deferred)

**Status:** accepted (dataset + metric contract in place; execution is a follow-up)

**Context:** The pipeline quality has been verified ad-hoc (continuity, safety, fidelity audits) but every check was a manual spot-check with no versioned dataset or regression gate. Researched 2026 eval best practice (Future AGI *2026 LLM Evaluation Playbook*; Braintrust *Hallucination Evaluations 2026*; *AI Agent Testing Guide 2026*; arXiv 2601.22025, 2606.29920) and surveyed the existing `test/…/Eval` infrastructure (the 10-scenario `EvalScenarios.Matrix`; `Fabrication/Duration/Style/Safety/Pronunciation/Sanity/TargetShape` scorers; `FrozenScenarioEval`/`ScenarioMatrixEval`/`RegressionEval`/`FallbackReplay` harnesses).

**Decision:** Authored a comprehensive evaluation suite as **data + spec, nothing executed** (per the task): (master spec — six-layer + agent-five-layer models mapped to Arn's draft/review/refine/safety/director trajectory, unified case schema, 11 dimensions → failure-modes → scorers → gate tiers, LLM-as-judge rubric design, CI thresholds, ground-truth model, governance) plus (55 designed scenario cases across fidelity, continuity, style, duration/slot, thin-market, fallback, content-permutations, pronunciation/voice, robustness, operational-pipeline). The three existing corpora become the production-promotion targets feeding the same suite. Reuses the existing scorers/harnesses rather than rebuilding.

**Rationale:** 2026 practice treats eval as versioned infrastructure (dataset → metrics → judge → CI gate → observation → closed loop) and insists on trajectory-level scoring + failure-mode-annotated cases for multi-agent systems — exactly Arn's shape. Building the dataset + metric contract first (without running) lets the team review scope/schema before investing in runner wiring, and every case is grounded in a real observed failure mode or a 2026 taxonomy gap.

**Consequences:** New docs: `EVAL-SUITE.md` + `suite/` (9 files, 55 cases), indexed from. Not wired to a runner yet — execution reuses the existing `Eval` harnesses + frozen HERE fixtures and is the next step (plus a new `ContinuityScorer` referenced by the continuity cases). Hard-gate floors set for the safety (block-recall 1.00) and fidelity (fabrication 0) subsets; soft gates + drift alarms for style/thin-market/content/pronunciation.
## 2026-07-15 — `arn` master testing CLI created (tools/ArnCli); C#/.NET; all groups working

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The repo's test/trigger/eval/diagnose tooling was scattered across ~30 scripts (bash + Python) + ~8 env-gated `dotnet test` harnesses + a dozen skills, with ~20 `ARN_*` env vars as the only interface. The goal: one CLI, built exclusively for LLM use, that explores/edits/runs tests against any env with any fixture, selectively mocks ElevenLabs/HERE/OpenAI, pulls full App Insights logs/traces for a bulletin, and profiles — per.

**Decision:** New project **`tools/ArnCli`** (net10, `AssemblyName=arn`, in the `.slnx`), language **C#/.NET** — because the generation pipeline + scorers are unavoidably .NET (run them in-process, no boundary), the ops surface ports to native Azure SDKs, and it shares the real `Domain` types. Dependency-free BCL arg dispatcher (no `System.CommandLine` — instant startup, no beta churn). LLM contract enforced: uniform `arn <group> <verb>`, `--json`, `--dry-run`, exit codes (0 ok · 1 failure · 2 usage · 3 infra). Ten groups, all working: **native** in-process `env`/`scenarios`/`fixtures`/`report`/`safety`; **orchestrated** (clean flags → the existing engine via `Process.Start`, streamed) `run`/`trigger`/`job`/`perf`/`prompt`. Scope excludes voice audition/candidates, deploy, diagrams, status reports (per operator).

**Rationale:** In-process C# beats a Python front door + subprocess for the eval engine (the heart). Orchestration-first makes every command work end-to-end immediately with one uniform surface, while deferring the native rehoming (retiring the scripts) — the `arn` interface stays fixed as engines fold in. `--dry-run` lets the LLM verify a command's resolved invocation without spending creds/time.

**Consequences:** `tools/ArnCli` builds clean (0 warnings). Verified: `--help` tree, `--json`, exit-code contract, `scenarios validate` (76 cases, no dupes), `fixtures list`, `report scorecard` (63 found), and **`safety check` live vs deployed dev** (clean→safe/exit0, profanity+speculation→blocked/exit1). Orchestrated commands `--dry-run`-verified to resolve to the correct underlying invocation (eval.sh / dotnet test / diagnose-job.py / foundry-agent-trace.py / arn-api.sh / test-bulletin.sh / test/load/run.sh / gepa/prompt-loop/tune). Not yet done: native rehoming of the orchestrated engines (so the scripts can be deleted) + the two open decisions (CI depth; `prompt` optimisers as first-class verbs vs research scripts). No existing script deleted yet — they are the engines `arn` drives.
## 2026-07-15 — `arn` CLI reversed to Python (supersedes the C# build earlier today)

**Status:** accepted (supersedes "arn master testing CLI created (tools/ArnCli); C#/.NET" above)

**Context:** Right after building `arn` in C# (`tools/ArnCli`), re-examined the language choice. The C# case rested on running the eval pipeline **in-process** — but eval runs are LLM-bound (seconds–minutes), so a subprocess boundary to .NET costs ~nothing, making that benefit marginal. Meanwhile the *majority* of the tooling being consolidated (diagnostics, triggers, perf, all optimisers) is already Python.

**Decision:** Rebuild `arn` in **Python** — `tools/arn/arn.py` (stdlib + pyyaml, no build step). Deleted `tools/ArnCli` and removed it from the `.slnx`. Same LLM contract (uniform `arn <group> <verb>`, `--json`, `--dry-run`, exit codes 0/1/2/3, SIGPIPE-safe). Native in-process Python: `env`, `scenarios`, `fixtures`, `report`, `safety` (HTTP → deployed `arn-safety`), `job list`, `trigger` (dev). Orchestrated (streamed subprocess): `run` (dotnet test / eval.sh), `prompt` (optimiser scripts), `perf`, `job get/logs/traces/captures/bulletins`, `trigger` (local), `fixtures capture`. The one genuinely-C# thing (pipeline + scorers) stays a `.NET` subprocess behind `arn run`.

**Rationale:** Python absorbs the already-Python tooling **as native code instead of rewriting it against SDKs** → less work, more scripts retired sooner. **No build step + instant startup** is a real daily win for a tool the LLM invokes constantly. Two languages exist either way (the app is C#, the optimisers Python); a Python front door just puts the CLI in the same language as the majority of what it wraps. The in-process-eval advantage that justified C# is negligible for long, LLM-bound eval runs.

**Consequences:** `tools/arn/arn.py` — compiles + runs with no build. Live-verified vs deployed dev: `safety check` clean→`{safe:true}`/exit0 and profanity+speculation→`{safe:false}`+itemised violations/exit1; native `job list`→87 real jobs via mgmt token; `scenarios validate` (76 cases, no dupes); `fixtures list`; pipe-safe (`| head`). Orchestrated commands `--dry-run`-verified to resolve to the correct invocation. Design doc flipped to Python (§4, §7, §8-decision-1, status banner). Remaining: native rehoming per §7 (extract a `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Evaluation` .NET binary for `arn run`; port `diagnose-job`/`foundry-agent-trace`/`test-bulletin`/`pipeline_burst` into native `arn`, then delete them) + the two open decisions (CI depth; `prompt` optimisers as first-class verbs). Scripts not deleted yet — they are the engines `arn` drives.

## 2026-07-15 — Foundry eval `arn-bulletin-smoke` ran green (real scores); code graders deferred

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Asked to trigger a real run of the cloud eval. A run surfaced Foundry's preview grader-execution contract in three layers, each fixed in turn.

**Decision:** Ran `arn-bulletin-smoke` over `arn-golden` (3 rows) with an independent judge `gpt-5.6-terra` (generator is `luna`). Fixes discovered by iterating real runs: (1) the Python-grader sandbox **bans the `compile` token** → rewrote the 6 code evaluators to inline `re.findall(pattern,…)` (no `re.compile`), re-registered v2; (2) the sandbox then required a **top-level `grade(sample,item)`** — my `code_text`+`entry_point` module shape has none, so the code graders can't run as-is; (3) LLM graders needed a **judge deployment** (`initialization_parameters.deployment_name`) or they 401, and the `azure_ai_evaluator`→custom-prompt-evaluator path returned "Invalid or missing numeric result". Resolution: the runnable `arn-bulletin-smoke` (`eval_6c2de5d5fca640c89422b92f5065a036`) uses the proven native **`score_model`** criteria for the 3 LLM judges (rubric + `gpt-5.6-terra` + range [0,1] + threshold 0.6), data trimmed to the string columns the judges use (avoids `score_model`'s strict schema rejecting booleans). Result: `errored=0`, 1 pass / 2 fail — continuity follow-on 0.97, safety 1.0 (no over-block), ATN-style 0.56–0.9 (weather-led open dinged).

**Rationale:** LLM judges are the capability Foundry uniquely adds and they now run reliably as `score_model`; the deterministic code checks already run locally + in the C# suite, so deferring their in-cloud port (a `grade()`-contract rewrite) loses no coverage while unblocking a real scored run now.

**Consequences:** `arn-bulletin-smoke` = 3 LLM-judge `score_model` criteria, runnable + green. The 6 code evaluators stay registered (catalog, v2, compile-free) but are NOT in the runnable eval — follow-up: rewrite each as a self-contained `grade(sample,item)` Python grader and add back. The 3 grader `.grader.yaml` files gained an explicit JSON score directive (supersedes the old "no output block" note). SDK lives in the `~/.venvs/foundry-eval` venv, not committed.
## 2026-07-15 — Foundry evaluation suite built out per-contract (8 evals, deterministic-first)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Build a real Foundry evaluation suite (Foundry side only) from the ChatGPT/Microsoft-Learn best-practice research: split by contract, deterministic-first, judges independent.

**Decision:** Restructured into a version-controlled, per-contract suite: `evals/<contract>/{eval.yaml,gates.yaml}`, `graders/python/*.py` (self-contained `grade(sample,item)`), `graders/prompt/*.md` (score_model judge prompts), `datasets/*.seed.jsonl`, and two config-driven drivers — `scripts/build_suite.py` (idempotent create/replace of every cloud eval object by name via `/openai/evals`) + `scripts/run_suite.py` (run + aggregate + apply gates, CI exit code). Built 8 eval objects in the dev project: `arn-final-bulletin-v1` (blocking: 3 python deterministic graders [target_shape, style_structural, gazetteer] + 3 score_model judges [atn_style, safety_broadcast, continuity_semantic]), `arn-style-diagnostic-v1` (non-blocking style microscope, recreated from the frozen rubric), and per-agent contracts `arn-{director,trajectory,safety,review,rewrite,attribute}-contract-v1`. Deterministic checks moved to native **`python`** graders (the sandbox contract our earlier `code_text`+`entry_point` catalog evaluators couldn't satisfy); subjective checks use **`score_model`** with the judge pinned to `gpt-5.6-terra`.

**Rationale:** Splitting by contract keeps hard deterministic gates from being averaged into subjective quality and makes per-stage failures visible; `python` graders are the Foundry-native way to run our deterministic checks in-cloud without a C# endpoint (out of scope for a Foundry-only build); `score_model` is the reliable LLM-judge route (the `azure_ai_evaluator` custom-prompt path returned "invalid numeric result").

**Consequences:** All 8 verified running in dev: final-bulletin scores real (safety 1.0, continuity 0.99, style 0.84; deterministic checks correctly fail the short/roll-call/ungrounded seed rows), director 3/3 + trajectory 3/3 GATE PASS, and the judge contracts discriminate (safety fails all 3 unsafe cases, review catches 3/4 injected faults, attribute flags the invented duration). The 4 agent-contract evals run on small **seed** datasets and are non-blocking until expanded to labelled/trace-derived corpora with agent-output comparison (a 3-5 row seed can't prove a 2% bound). `atn-style-rubric-v53` frozen (metadata update rejected by the API, so archival is by convention — it is not in `build_suite.py`). Interim `arn-bulletin-smoke` deleted (superseded by `arn-final-bulletin-v1`). Legacy (single-suite) is superseded by `evals/*/`. Still to build: trajectory-from-traces, continuous/scheduled prod eval, trace→dataset. Drivers need `az login` + PyYAML (venv `~/.venvs/foundry-eval`). `README.md` + `agent-metadata.yaml` updated.
## 2026-07-15 — Red-team hazard panel: safety filter is remit-scoped; blocking suite has factual/format blind spots

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Expand the suite with a broad hazard taxonomy and find what the safety filter (and the suite) miss.

**Decision:** Added `arn-redteam-v1` (`evals/red-team/`, non-blocking diagnostic) — the full final-bulletin grader panel over a 20-condition hazard dataset (`datasets/red-team.jsonl`) spanning safety (victim-ID, profanity, Mindframe, graphic, discrimination, defamation, sub-judice, illegal-advice, PII, alarmist), factual (invented road, wrong direction, invented duration, stale/cleared), operational (roll-call, data-speak, advice-padding, over-length) and injection (prompt-injection, garbled) remits. Also hardened `build_suite.py` to **create-then-delete-old** (a delete-then-create rebuild had transiently dropped `arn-style-diagnostic-v1`).

**Rationale:** A red-team across remits shows, per condition, which grader catches it — isolating the safety filter's true scope from genuine suite gaps.

**Consequences:** (findings) The **safety judge caught all 10 broadcast-compliance hazards** (0.00–0.25), generalising even to defamation/sub-judice/PII/illegal-advice not named in its rubric. It correctly PASSED the factual/operational faults (they are not compliance issues). Real gaps exposed in the **blocking** `final-bulletin` panel: (1) **wrong-direction** — `gazetteer` only checks road-name membership, not carriageway, so a reversed closure passes; owner is `review-contract`, not in the blocking panel. (2) **invented-duration** — caught by nothing in the panel; owner is `attribute-contract`. (3) **advice-padding** — the `atn_style` judge passed it (0.78); its owner `clean_close` lives only in `style-diagnostic`. (4) **`arn_style_structural` regex bug** — it does not match motorway shorthand (`M1/M2/M5`), so a motorway roll-call passed the deterministic gate (the `atn_style` judge caught it at 0.18). (5) the `over-length` test row wasn't actually long enough to trip `target_shape`, and `target_shape` checks word-count not measured audio. Follow-ups: promote `review`+`attribute` graders into the blocking path (wrong-direction/invented-duration are high-danger on-air), fix the road regex to include motorway codes, add `clean_close` to `final-bulletin`. + `agent-metadata.yaml` updated.

## 2026-07-16 — ATN alignment: weather never leads, drive-time is delay-only, palette variety is seed-shuffled

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Review of two dev bulletins (Gold Coast, Melbourne) against the ATN corpus surfaced three divergences from real ATN style: (1) a weather ALERT forced the bulletin to open with weather, but no ATN sample in any of the four corpora leads with weather — it is always a brief closer, present in ~37% of reads; (2) a monitored drive-time was voiced with its raw total, distance, and a "typical X, Y slower than typical" comparison, but ATN either states the total alone or, more usefully for an unscripted listener, only the delay ("around 10 minutes on top of your trip"); (3) regenerating with identical inputs produced near-identical descriptor choices ("a touch slow" every minor road) because the draft agent is a reasoning model (no usable temperature lever) and the ATN phrasing palette was static text in a fixed order, so the model's ordering/primacy bias always reached for the first-listed phrase.

**Decision:**
- Removed the `weatherLeads` override (`LlmScriptGenerator` no longer sets it; the `{{#if weatherLeads}}` lead directive is gone from `prompts/draft.md`; the orchestrator log line is now "Weather alert detected" with no ordering claim). An active alert still REACHES the writer even when a station's `FillOrder` omits weather (safety inclusion) — it just no longer leads.
- `TrafficNarrativeSummarizer` emits a delayed monitored route as "about N min slower than usual" (the delay only) instead of "N min run (typical M, D slower than typical), Xkm". The total-time and distance are no longer voiced.
- Added `PaletteSelector` (Domain/Services), mirroring `BlueprintSelector`: it renders the ATN road-feel palette with each severity tier's phrase order shuffled per job seed (JobId), injected into `prompts/draft.md` as `{{{palette}}}`. Deterministic per job (replay/diagnostics stable), varied across jobs so descriptor selection is unbiased at the population level. The shuffle uses multiply-shift (high bits), not `% (i+1)` — an LCG's low bits are non-random and biased the first-listed phrase to lead ~50% of seeds instead of ~11%.
- Reconciled the draft "GROUP, THEN ROTATE" rule with system.md's existing shared-condition grouping (cap 3, say the condition once): group same-state roads first, rotate vocabulary only across the separate sentences. Removed the raw label "minor delays" from the palette so it is not double-blessed against the data bullet.

**Rationale:** Structural and lexical variety on a reasoning model come from varying a seeded specification, not temperature (same lesson as `BlueprintSelector`). Data-side grouping of same-state minors was tried and reverted — it flattened genuine variety and the user wanted creative rotation, not forced collapse. The `RepeatedStatePhraseDetector` (already wired into `BroadcastOrchestrator`) remains the safety net that catches a roll-call the draft still occasionally produces.

**Consequences:** Gold Coast now leads with traffic and rotates minor descriptors ("a touch slow" group + "moving slowly" tail); weather sits after traffic. Melbourne's drive-time reads "about six minutes slower than usual". Residual Melbourne repetition traces to a genuine duplicate-corridor data bug (`City Link` vs `CityLink` as two corridors) in `CorridorAggregator`, tracked separately. New `PaletteSelectorTests` (4) lock the reproducible-per-seed / varied-across-seeds / no-phrase-lost contract. Summarizer and weather-alert tests updated to the new contracts.
## 2026-07-16 — Safety eval gated by confusion matrix, not pass-rate

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `arn-safety-contract-v1`'s adversarial dataset is ~79% unsafe-by-design, so the Foundry portal's native "Overall score" (a pass-rate: rows scoring >= threshold) reads upside-down — it showed 21% (4/19) even though the safety judge was scoring every unsafe bulletin correctly LOW. A low pass-rate is the *goal* on an adversarial set; the portal can't know that.

**Decision:** Expanded the safety dataset to 19 safety-remit cases (blatant + evasive: coded victim-ID, implied/euphemistic suicide, masked profanity, dog-whistle discrimination, soft defamation, cause-speculation, sub-judice, glorification, injection-slur) plus 4 airable "over-block" controls (factual fatal, police operation, injuries, truck rollover), each labelled `expected: safe|unsafe`. Taught `scripts/run_suite.py` to read `expected` and compute a **confusion matrix per criterion** — miss_rate (unsafe that slipped) and over_block_rate (safe wrongly flagged) — and added a `gates.yaml` `confusion:` section (`arn_safety_broadcast`: miss_rate max 0.0, over_block_rate max 0.02).

**Rationale:** For an adversarial/contract eval, pass-rate is meaningless; the safety-relevant metrics are false-negatives (misses) and false-positives (over-blocks). Gating on those makes the CI number correct even though the portal's raw pass-rate stays inverted.

**Consequences:** `run_suite.py safety-contract` now reports both the raw pass-rate AND the confusion metric; on the 19-case set the judge scored **15/15 unsafe caught, 0/4 over-block, 100% agreement — GATE PASS** (nearest edge: cause-speculation 0.55, just under the 0.6 flag line). The **Foundry portal still shows ~21%** — that is the native OpenAI-evals pass-rate and is inherently upside-down for adversarial data; trust the `run_suite`/CI confusion output, not the portal headline. Optional follow-up: split into an unsafe-panel + safe-panel so each run's native pass-rate reads right-way-round; and swap the proxy judge for the real safety-agent verdicts. The safety filter itself has no blind spot on this set — the earlier "misses" were a scoping error (non-safety hazards mixed in).
## 2026-07-16 — Safety eval split into label_model must-block / must-air panels (clean 1=pass/0=fail)

**Status:** accepted (supersedes the confusion-matrix approach in the prior entry for the portal-facing metric)

**Context:** The `score_model` safety eval produced a 0-1 score, so the Foundry portal showed a *pass-rate* that read upside-down on a mixed adversarial set (21%). Wanted a native 1=pass/0=fail the portal displays correctly. Researched Microsoft's Azure OpenAI Graders doc: `label_model` outputs **Pass/Fail via `passing_labels`** (not a score); `string_check` returns 1/0 deterministically; `score_model` is the 0-1-with-threshold we had. A single grader's pass/fail is fixed per criterion, so one grader over mixed safe+unsafe rows can't read right for both.

**Decision:** Replaced `arn-safety-contract-v1` (retired + cloud-deleted) with **two single-intent `label_model` panels** sharing one classifier prompt (`graders/prompt/airability_classifier.md`, labels `[airable, block]`, judged independently — the expected label is NOT shown to the judge, so no leak): `arn-safety-must-block-v1` (15 unsafe rows, `passing_labels:[block]`, gate rate ≥1.0 = zero misses) and `arn-safety-must-air-v1` (4 airable over-block controls, `passing_labels:[airable]`, gate rate ≥0.98). Added `label_model` support to `build_suite.py`; reverted the interim confusion-matrix logic in `run_suite.py` (obsolete + it mis-reads label_model passed-semantics).

**Rationale:** Splitting by intent makes each panel's native pass-rate meaningful (100% = correct), so the portal headline is right without leaking the answer to the judge or post-processing in CI. `label_model` is Microsoft's documented mechanism for exactly this.

**Consequences:** Both panels verified 100% — must-block 15/15 blocked, must-air 4/4 aired, GATE PASS — and the Foundry portal now shows a clean, right-way-round number (1=pass, 0=fail). Suite is now 10 active evals. The classifier is still a proxy for the production safety agent; the rigorous end-state remains `string_check(agent_verdict == expected)` once real per-row safety-agent verdicts are harvested. `datasets/adversarial-broadcast.seed.jsonl` stays as the combined source that splits into the two panel files. `README.md` + `agent-metadata.yaml` updated.
## 2026-07-16 — Foundry eval API can't pin judge temperature → LLM-judge safety gate is non-deterministic

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Tried to make the safety `label_model` gate reproducible by pinning `sampling_params: {temperature: 0, seed}` on the grader (per general OpenAI-evals guidance).

**Decision:** (finding) **Confirmed the field is silently dropped by the Azure Foundry eval API.** A create+GET probe shows a `label_model` grader stores only `[id, input, labels, model, name, passing_labels, type]` — `sampling_params`/`temperature`/`seed` do not persist; Microsoft's own `sample_evaluations_graders.py` sets no temperature on `label_model` either. At runtime the judge still ran at `temperature: 1.0` (visible in every result `sample`). Direct consequence: on a re-run, `unsafe-subjudice-soft` **flipped from `block` to `airable` — a real miss (14/15)**. So an LLM-judge gate here cannot be made deterministic via the eval API. Removed the dead `sampling_params` from `build_suite.py` and left a NOTE.

**Rationale:** A hard safety gate must be reproducible; a grader that can flip a verdict run-to-run can't be trusted to block. Since the platform won't let us pin the judge, determinism has to come from the grader TYPE, not its sampling.

**Consequences:** The `label_model` panels stay as a **non-blocking monitoring signal** (they still surface subtle hazards an LLM catches — sub-judice, implied suicide). The **hard gate** must move to a deterministic grader: either `string_check(agent_verdict == expected)` over the real safety-agent's recorded per-row verdict (fully reproducible, no judge), or a `python` grader for the deterministically-detectable hazards (profanity wordlist incl. masked, phone/rego regex, explicit victim-name patterns) with the LLM judge kept advisory. `sub-judice` is the weakest-caught category (it hedged even when it did block) and is the first to fail — it needs an explicit deterministic or tightened rule. Follow-up: implement the deterministic layer; do not gate release on the LLM judge alone.

## 2026-07-16 — Repo-wide cleanup: stale `gpt-5.4-mini` / `arn-draft-natural-v53` references corrected to `gpt-5.6-luna` / `arn-draft`

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Deployed dev runs `gpt-5.6-luna` via the `arn-draft` Foundry agent (renamed from `arn-draft-natural-v53` on 2026-07-15), but many current-state artifacts still named `gpt-5.4-mini` as the model and `arn-draft-natural-v53` as the agent. A local fixture replay had even silently run on `gpt-5.4-mini` because `local.settings.json` still pointed at the old `cog-arntraffic-prd-aue` PoC endpoint — masking the true production behaviour.

**Decision:** Corrected every CURRENT-STATE reference to the live values; left dated historical records unchanged. Updated: app config (`appsettings.json` default `Model` → `gpt-5.6-luna`; `local.settings.json` repointed to the dev Foundry endpoint + luna so local replays match dev); IaC (`main.bicep` `aiModelName`/`aiModelVersion`/roleModelDeployments and the dev/test/prod bicepparams → `gpt-5.6-luna` / `2026-07-09`; `ai-services`/`function-app` module defaults + example); tooling defaults (`scripts/workflow-lab.py`, `scripts/workflow_lab/runner.py`, `scripts/test_export_prompts.py`, and all `experiments/workflows/*/workflow.py` `DEFAULT_MODEL` → `gpt-5.6-luna`, leaving the two deliberately-`gpt-5.6-terra` arms); the load-bearing `experiments/foundry-eval/foundry_native/foundry_client.py` `GENERATOR_AGENT` → `arn-draft`; current-state docs (`architecture.md`, `solution-design.md` §6.1 integration table, `infrastructure-visualisation.html` model cards); and the cost estimates (`cost-estimate/*` model name → `gpt-5.6-luna` with an explicit pricing-basis caveat, since luna's per-token rate is not in the public calculator — figures still reflect the gpt-5.4-mini rate pending re-cost).

**Rationale:** Stale current-state references mislead future agents/humans (and already caused a wrong-model verification). Dated records (decisions log, `CONTEXT.md`, meeting decks, eval-history snapshots, historical trial-sibling agents like `-idiom-patch`/`-terra`) are append-only history and were preserved; a rename note was added to the primary eval-history doc. Cost figures were not fabricated — the model NAME is corrected and a caveat flags that the dollar basis is still the mini rate.

**Consequences:** A redeploy from IaC now converges dev/test/prod on `gpt-5.6-luna` (previously the bicep would have reverted the manually-set luna app-setting to mini). Local replays via `export-prompts.py` now use luna, matching dev. Remaining `gpt-5.4-mini` strings are intentional: dated history, the cost-estimate pricing-basis caveat, and generated indexes (`docs/_data.js` etc., refreshed via `scripts/docs.py generate`). Follow-up noted separately: the earlier palette work re-added ATN-non-native phrases the 2026-07-10 audit flagged, and luna's cost line needs re-costing when its rate publishes.
## 2026-07-16 — Foundry eval suite hardened for CI/CD: env-parameterized scripts, deterministic tier, judge canary, promotion gate, pipeline wiring

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The suite was dev-hardcoded, judge-variance-fragile (the evals API drops `sampling_params`, so `gpt-5.6-terra` judges run at default temperature), had no free tier for frequent runs, no judge-drift detection, a statistically thin must-air panel (4 rows), noisy red-team aggregates, and no CI/CD integration.

**Decision:** (1) Shared (env slug/endpoints/token; `--env dev|test|prod` on build/run/harvest, unknown env rejected). (2) `run_suite.py` grew `--gates PATH`, `--repeats N` (per-criterion medians: `median_low` for pass-rates, `median_high` for fail/error counts — ties round toward failure), output-item pagination (`after` cursor), count-consistency refetch, and a row-scaled poll deadline. (3) New free deterministic eval `arn-final-bulletin-det-v1` (3 python graders) with golden + drift gate profiles. (4) New `arn-judge-canary-v1`: 8 real transcribed on-air ATN Sydney reads through the `arn_atn_style` judge (floor 6/8) — if real ATN copy stops passing, the JUDGE moved. (5) `safety-must-air` expanded 4→20 airable-trap rows (verified 20/20 air; must-block 19/19 holds). (6) Red-team trimmed to hazard-relevant criteria (structural/gazetteer/safety); shape/style/continuity on hazard snippets were pure noise. (7) `gates.promotion.yaml` floors from the 46-row production baseline; gazetteer fabrication = hard block. (8) `promotion_gate.py`: real-bulletin panel via the scheduled poller (`arn trigger --via poller` per market, ThreadPool), 75% health threshold, settle-wait, harvest+filter to panel jobs, gate with the promotion profile; exit 0/1/2 = pass/quality-fail/infra-fail; snapshots and force-restores schedules if a trigger's revert fails. (9) `cleanup_project.py` purged 28 orphan `eval-data-*` datasets (REST) and the 9 stale catalog evaluators (REST is read-only for evaluators; deletion via SDK `beta.evaluators.delete_version`). (10) Pipeline: `enableEvalGate` parameter (default false, RBAC-gated like `enableDeploy`) compiles in `EvalGate_Golden` (PR path-gated golden gate), `EvalGate_Test` (promotion gate between `Deploy_Test` and `Deploy_Prod`, which then depends on it), and scheduled `EvalDrift` (nightly deterministic drift over harvested production output; weekly full-judge + canary) via. Deleted superseded assets: `register.py`, `run_eval.py`, `suite_to_jsonl.py`, `evaluators/`,, empty `evals/safety-contract/`.

**Rationale:** Judge variance is real (canary repeats measured 8/8, 8/8, 6/8 on identical input) — medians over repeats + a deterministic free tier + a drift canary make gates trustworthy; the promotion gate grades what actually ships (poller-path bulletins with full station config), not synthetic rows.

**Consequences:** All verified live on dev: build idempotence (12 objects, run history preserved), det tier free (`per_model_usage: []`), pagination to 138 rows, ADO preview compiles all three parameter permutations with correct stage graphs, promotion gate end-to-end `GATE: PASS` on a real sydney/brisbane/melbourne panel. Golden gates no longer rate-gate `arn_target_shape` (the 3-row seed deliberately contains sanctioned-short reads that the word-count proxy flags — 0/3 verified; shape floors live in the drift/promotion profiles). Known data gap: adelaide jobs persist empty `GeneratorInputJson` (all jobs, systemic) so adelaide cannot be evidence-graded or used in promotion panels until fixed. Test-env activation = flip `enableEvalGate` once IBP-TST connection + Foundry/Storage RBAC exist (documented in the parameter comment).
## 2026-07-16 — Oversized job JSON columns gzip-compressed instead of dropped (root cause of adelaide's missing generator input)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Every adelaide job persisted an EMPTY `GeneratorInputJson` (perth/melbourne intermittently), making a whole market invisible to eval harvest, regression capture, and promotion panels. Root-caused via App Insights `[JobPersist]` warnings (adelaide 32.5 K, perth 31.7 K, melbourne 30-31 K chars): `TableStorageJobRepository.FitTableProperty` DROPPED any traffic-scaled JSON column over the 30 K-char Table Storage cap. The drop is per-save and silent at the API surface; App Insights adaptive sampling hid the warning for most saves.

**Decision:** Oversized columns are now gzip-compressed and stored as `"gz:" + base64(gzip(json))` (~5-8x reduction; JSON never starts with `gz:`, so detection is unambiguous). Read side expands transparently for all five compressible columns (Incidents/AllIncidents/Corridors/FlowRoads/GeneratorInput). Drop-with-warning remains only as the last resort when even the compressed form exceeds the cap. Python consumers updated: decompresses `gz:` values; `tools/arn/arn.py job save` expands all `gz:` columns at export so `job.json` and every downstream diagnostic keeps seeing plain JSON.

**Rationale:** The snapshot exists for deterministic replay and evidence-grading of shipped bulletins — dropping it for exactly the busiest (most eval-relevant) markets inverted its purpose. Compression keeps the single-entity model and needs no blob overflow or schema change.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev: fresh adelaide job `38f43727` persists `gz:` (11,459 chars, previously dropped), harvest yields a full evidence row (15 K evidence chars, 58 allowed names) that grades 3/3 on the deterministic tier, and `arn job save` exports plain JSON. Unit contract: oversized snapshot round-trips compressed; incompressibly-oversized still drops safely (1,177 Infrastructure tests green). Historical rows persisted before the fix remain empty — unrecoverable. Along the way, two tool breakages from today's `Job_{market}` partition migration were fixed: `harvest_dataset.py` now queries legacy `'Job'` AND `'Job_*'` partitions (excluding `JobIndex`), and `arn.py _job_entity` excludes the same-RowKey `JobIndex` stub that made `job save` export an empty entity.

## 2026-07-17 — HERE browser map key served from an authenticated endpoint, never bundled

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A security audit found the operator console's HERE evidence map read its key from `import.meta.env.VITE_HERE_API_KEY`, so Vite inlined it into the public static bundle. The deployed dev SWA served the key in `/assets/OnAirPage-*.js` to any anonymous internet caller, and it was the SAME key as the backend's paid HERE REST secret (`Here__ApiKey`) — a shared, quota-drainable credential exposed unauthenticated.

**Decision:** The browser map key is now a SEPARATE config value, `Here:MapApiKey` (app setting `Here__MapApiKey`, Bicep param `hereMapApiKey`, empty by default), served at runtime by a new authenticated endpoint `GET /api/map-config` (`MapConfigHttpTrigger`). GET defaults to the Operator role in `RouteRoleMatrix`, so only authenticated operators receive it; it is never inlined into the bundle. `HereLocationMap` takes the key as an `apiKey` prop fetched via `useMapConfig()`. When the key is empty the console renders the keyless Leaflet `LocationMap` (both maps are lazy-loaded). The server-side paid REST key (`Here__ApiKey`) stays server-only and is never returned to any client.

**Rationale:** A HERE Maps JS key must reach the browser to render the map, but it must not be (a) exposed to anonymous callers via a public bundle, nor (b) the same credential as the paid backend REST key. Serving a separate, domain-restrictable key from an authed endpoint removes the anonymous exposure and decouples the two credentials, while a plain (non-Key-Vault) app setting is appropriate because the value is intentionally browser-visible and low-sensitivity once domain-restricted.

**Consequences:** Verified: production `vite build` no longer contains the key in `dist/`; `MapConfigHttpTrigger` unit tests assert it returns `MapApiKey` and never leaks the REST key (350 Functions tests green); frontend lint + 215 jobs/api tests green. **Operational follow-up owned by ARN (NOT code):** (1) rotate the previously-exposed key `1K8-hupE…` in the HERE console — treat as compromised; (2) mint a separate HERE JS/Maps key, domain-restricted to the console hostnames + Maps services only, and set it as `hereMapApiKey` per env; (3) the backend REST key stays in Key Vault (`Here--ApiKey`). Until `hereMapApiKey` is set, the console uses the keyless Leaflet basemap (no functional loss for evidence review). Also in this pass: `Scriban.Signed` test-only pin bumped 7.2.0 → 7.2.5 (clears GHSA-q6rr-fm2g-g5x8 / GHSA-6q7j-xr26-3h2c); a `web` `overrides` pin lifts the dev-only `@opentelemetry/core` (via lighthouse → @sentry/node) to `^2.8.0`, taking `npm audit` to 0 with lighthouse's perf API still importing cleanly.

## 2026-07-17 — Playout delivery via SFTP-enabled blob drop (BlobDrop transport); test wired end-to-end

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN playout's vendor SFTP question stalled for weeks, so ARN adopted 'set it up and try it': the ARN Technology Lead provisioned SFTP-enabled storage account ibpauetststaftp01 (IBP-AUE-TST-RSG-STA01, HNS, local user svctraffictst scoped lrdcw to container 'informationbulletins') and handed over credentials 2026-07-17. The app's only delivery implementation was the PoC-era SMB writer (Zetta.Enabled=false everywhere), and nothing could push to the new drop.

**Decision:** New Zetta:Transport option (Smb default | BlobDrop). IDeliveryFileWriter replaces ISmbFileWriter; ZettaFileDeliveryService stays the transport-agnostic orchestrator (market code, filename, safety checks); new BlobDropFileWriter uploads the WAV natively as a blob via managed identity + TokenCredential (Storage Blob Data Contributor granted by new roles-delivery-drop.bicep) — the playout side pulls the SAME file over the account's public SFTP endpoint. No SFTP client in the app. New Bicep params zettaEnabled/zettaTransport/zettaDropAccountName/zettaDropContainerName (QT-001: IaC-not-CLI); test bicepparam enables BlobDrop against ibpauetststaftp01. A new optional blob PE ({namePrefix}06, roles + PE both conditional on zettaDropAccountName) reaches the drop privately since the integration subnet routes only RFC1918 (vnetRouteAllEnabled=false). SFTP credentials stored in IBP-AUE-TST-KYV-APP01 as SftpDelivery--Username/--Password (vendor-facing only; the app never uses them).

**Rationale:** Blob-SFTP duality means our side writes blobs natively (MI, no password, no SFTP library) while the vendor keeps plain SFTP pull — the simplest transport that satisfies both. PE over vnetRouteAll=true because the env is PE-everything already and Route All would push HERE/ElevenLabs internet egress through a subnet with no NAT gateway. Extending ZettaOptions rather than a new config section keeps one delivery convention.

**Consequences:** PROVEN end-to-end on test 2026-07-17: POST /broadcast -> real pipeline (HERE+OpenAI+ElevenLabs) -> approve -> publish -> SYD_TRAIN_TRAFF.wav (2.6MB RIFF, 30.0s) pulled back over SFTP with the vendor credentials. En route, found+fixed a latent test-env defect: *.services.ai.azure.com NXDOMAINed in-VNet (Foundry endpoint) — network.bicep now creates 7 privatelink zones (added openai + services.ai), the AI Services PE zone group registers all three AI hostname families, test bicepparam pins the two new zone IDs. Easy Auth ARM-audience exclusion on test (SEC 2026-07-16) was temporarily lifted via az rest during commissioning and RESTORED + verified (api:// audience only; Auth__DevFallbackRole deleted; drop-account firewall back to Deny with zero IP rules). Remaining before vendor go: ARN playout/vendor egress IPs whitelisted on ibpauetststaftp01, vendor SFTP pull confirmation, filename model sign-off ({MarketId}_TRAIN_TRAFF.wav overwritten cart), password rotation after onboarding, prod drop account when promoted.

## 2026-07-17 — CI brittleness: local verification must mirror the CI gate set (verify.sh + pre-push hook)

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Master went red (builds 2496/2497). Root cause: one large multi-concern commit (087e2d6, "resolve all 23 findings") was verified locally with `tsc + build + vitest` but never with `lint`, `backend E2E`, or `perf` — the exact three CI-only gates it broke. The fast-failing frontend Lint step (eslint-plugin-prettier: a ConfirmDialog wrapper added to ScheduleStudio without running prettier → 96 errors) masked two further regressions until it was fixed: backend E2E (3 tests hitting 087e2d6's intended new market-existence 404 guards + the publish-requires-delivery + aired-job-non-deletable behavior changes) and the /stations perf budget (Radix alert-dialog eagerly mounted → TBT 604ms > 600ms). A separate contributor: an 8-day-stuck zombie build (2382, inProgress since 2026-07-09) permanently held one of only ~2 hosted concurrency slots, starving the queue.

**Decision:** (1) Add `scripts/verify.sh [--quick|--full]` — a local mirror of the azure-pipelines.yml gate set. Quick = backend build+unit, web lint+tsc+vitest+build; Full = quick + backend E2E + web perf + bicep lint + gitleaks. (2) A tracked pre-push hook (`scripts/hooks/pre-push` via `core.hooksPath`, auto-wired by the root `prepare` script / `scripts/install-hooks.sh`) runs `verify.sh --quick` on every push; bypass only with `git push --no-verify`. (3) The three unmasked failures were fixed at the source, not by moving goalposts: E2E tests seed a market for the new 404 guards + assert the aired-job-non-deletable guard; E2E env sets `Zetta__Enabled=false` (coherent with its Console/local audio — blob-download delivery cannot work against local output); ConfirmDialog is lazy + render-on-open (stations TBT 604ms → 58ms).

**Rationale:** "Green locally" had no single definition — commit messages variously cited "tsc/build/vitest" or "tsc/eslint/vitest", and nothing local ran E2E or perf. A runnable, tiered verify script gives "green" one meaning; the fast pre-push subset catches the common (lint/compile/unit) class without an 8-minute push, while `--full` is available before web/Functions-heavy pushes and is what CI enforces. Fixing the failures at source (not raising the perf budget or disabling gates) keeps the gates meaningful.

**Consequences:** verify.sh --full is green locally (backend build+unit, web lint/tsc/vitest/build, backend E2E 15/15, web perf all routes under budget). The publish→delivery behavior change (087e2d6: a delivery failure leaves the job Approved for retry, never Published-but-undelivered) and the aired-job-non-deletable guard are now covered by E2E assertions. Real Zetta/BlobDrop delivery E2E coverage (blob output + Zetta enabled, mirroring test/prod) remains a follow-up that aligns with week-9 A1.2 (Zetta E2E from TEST). Operationally: cancel builds stuck inProgress beyond a few hours (they hold concurrency slots).

## 2026-07-17 — SWA custom domains + enterprise-grade edge (Option A) for all three environments

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-07-01 finding (status now superseded) diagnosed 1.0-3.3s static-asset loads from Melbourne: the SWA Standard default hostnames route via Traffic Manager to an Amsterdam stamp, and Standard tier has no CDN edge without enterprise-grade edge, which hard-requires a custom domain (learn.microsoft.com/azure/static-web-apps/enterprise-edge). The default hostnames are also stakeholder-visible (Teams deep-links, walkthrough deck) and read as untrusted random names. Fronting options were costed: Option A (custom domain + enterprise-grade edge, ~USD 17.52/app/month) vs Option B (Front Door Premium + MSAL auth rework, ~USD 310+/month). arn.com.au DNS is hosted on Azure DNS in an ARN subscription we cannot see or write to, so the CNAME is a one-record external ask to ARN per environment.

**Decision:** Adopt Option A on all three environments, dev first. Names (content-agnostic, codename-independent): bulletins-dev.arn.com.au -> brave-desert-09eeae900.7.azurestaticapps.net, bulletins-test.arn.com.au -> polite-flower-0a5e0ce00.7.azurestaticapps.net, bulletins.arn.com.au -> lively-glacier-054847700.7.azurestaticapps.net. IaC shipped 2026-07-17: static-web-app.bicep gains customDomainName (Microsoft.Web/staticSites/customDomains, cname-delegation) + enableEnterpriseEdge (union-merged enterpriseGradeCdnStatus, only set when true so a redeploy never force-disables edge) + consoleHostname output; main.bicep threads swaCustomDomain/swaEnterpriseEdge and derives opsConsoleBaseUrl + CORS origins (both hostnames) from the effective console hostname. Rollout per env is TWO deploys once the CNAME exists: (1) set swaCustomDomain and deploy (CNAME validation only works while edge is disabled - edge-enabled apps require dns-txt-token for new domains), (2) after the domain validates, set swaEnterpriseEdge = true and deploy again. Step-by-step values are commented in each main.<env>.bicepparam.

**Rationale:** Option A fixes both the latency and the trust/naming problem for ~USD 18-53/month total with zero application change, while Option B's Front Door Premium base fee (~USD 330/month) is not justified before prod go-live; the auth simplification half of Option B remains available later and is orthogonal. Functional names (bulletins.*) outlive the internal 'Project B10' codename; DNS should not encode codenames. The two-step deploy sequencing is forced by the validation-method constraint, not a choice.

**Consequences:** Blocked on ARN creating three CNAMEs (TTL <= default 3600s is fine; must be < 48h) - same external-dependency pattern as the Test/Prod AAD app registrations. Until then swaCustomDomain stays '' and deploys are no-ops for this feature. After cutover: Webhook__OpsConsoleBaseUrl and CORS switch to the custom domain automatically on the next deploy; linkedStaticWebAppHostname in function-authsettings.bicep intentionally stays the DEFAULT hostname (it is the SWA provider registration clientId, an identity, not a URL). Old default hostnames keep serving - zero-downtime addition. Verification per env: re-run the DNS/geolocation check in docs/operations/performance-testing.md and confirm an in-region (non-am2) edge POP + asset loads < 0.4s from Melbourne. Costs +USD 17.52/app/month once edge is enabled. SWA private endpoints must never be added while edge is on (mutually exclusive).

**Addendum (2026-07-17, later same day) — DNS path explored, deferred pending ARN:** All routes around the ARN DNS dependency were investigated and the outcome is: wait for ARN. (1) Self-serve is impossible — Owner on the IBP sub cannot help: the arn.com.au zone lives in an ARN subscription we cannot even enumerate (resource graph across all visible subs returns zero DNS zones; our only ARN Sub role is Contributor on the old PoC RG ARN-AUE-RSG-TNP), and a same-named zone created in the IBP sub would receive no traffic without parent NS delegation (DNS chain of trust, not RBAC). (2) arinco.com.au REJECTED by user — consultancy domain must not carry the client's product (it is also GoDaddy-hosted, not writable by us anyway). (3) Buying arnbulletins.com via App Service Domain (~USD 12/yr, GoDaddy-resold, billed to + owned by the IBP sub, auto-linked Azure DNS zone, availability CONFIRMED 2026-07-17) is fully viable and self-serve same-day, but the user chose NOT to purchase yet — preference is to sort DNS properly with ARN (three CNAMEs, or better a one-time NS delegation of bulletins.arn.com.au to an IBP-sub Azure DNS zone, which makes all future records self-serve). arnbulletins.com remains the documented escape hatch if the ARN ask stalls: it costs nothing to adopt later, and the SWA supports multiple custom domains so nothing is foreclosed. Test/prod custom Entra app registrations will each need the redirect URI https://<domain>/.auth/login/aad/callback added at their cutover; dev's built-in provider needs nothing.
