**Context:** With the three gates in place (2026-07-27, earlier decision) the harnesses reported 51 axe violations across 26 targets, 5 style-drift roles, 104 knip findings and 12 console errors. Root-causing them showed the counts were misleading in both directions. Understated: `03-review-adjust` in ux-audit and `review-adjust` in perf both pointed at `arn-job-00008`, an id with no mock fixture, so both had spent their entire life measuring the job-not-found error page while reporting as covered - the Adjust tab, the heaviest surface in the app, had never been audited or scored. Four routes (/delivery, /pronunciation, /activity, /config-transfer) were never crawled at all. Overstated: 77 of the 134 failing nodes were colour-contrast tracing to nine fg/bg pairs, `region` was one element repeated on 20 pages, and 98 of the 104 knip findings were barrel or internal-only exports with zero runtime cost.

**Decision:** Fix the root causes and, separately, fix the instruments that under- or over-reported. COVERAGE: ux-audit 20->26 targets, perf 7->12 routes, both review-adjust targets repointed at a real fixture, and a new `assertRouteCoverage()` that derives the expected set from src/lib/routes.ts and exits 1 on a gap. COLOUR: treat every semantic/status token as serving three measurable roles - fill under its -foreground, chip text on a 10-20% tint of itself, and plain text - and solve each to the AA floor instead of choosing it. That forced three structural changes: 16 light tokens re-tuned (the light ramp was inherited from dark and failed in BOTH directions), a new `--<token>-on-tint` step because in dark a fill must stay dark for white while chip text must out-run the tint and one value cannot do both, and per-theme `-foreground` values. Opacity on a text token is now a lint error, because a ramp solved to the floor has no headroom by construction. The same reasoning bans container opacity for de-emphasis. STRUCTURE: fix ARIA at the source and in the type system where possible - Slider joins SelectTrigger in requiring an accessible name, the review cockpit's Tabs now owns its panels, CommandDialog's title moved inside its content. INSTRUMENTS: `ACCEPTED_VARIANTS` in the drift digest and `ignoreExportsUsedInFile` in knip, so a settled decision stops being re-reported.

**Rationale:** A count is only worth acting on if it maps to causes. Nine contrast pairs and one misplaced heading explained 93 of 134 nodes, so the work was small once root-caused - and conversely, two harness targets silently measuring an error page meant the most complex screen in the product carried unknown risk while the dashboard read green. Fixing instruments alongside defects is the same discipline applied to the linter tiers earlier the same day: a report nobody can act on decays into one nobody reads, and 104 knip findings or a permanently-flagged h1 tier are exactly that. Solving colour rather than choosing it is what makes the result durable: the values are reproducible from the constraints, the constraints are written down, and the lint rule that guards them cites its own measurements.

**Consequences:** axe 51 -> 0 across 26 targets x 8 variants (light and dark). All 12 Lighthouse routes at accessibility 100 and agentic-browsing 100, performance 88-97. Style-drift roles 6 -> 3, the remainder being wrapper margins rather than type. knip 104 -> 6, and the 6 name a real gap: delivery styles and pronunciation dictionaries have restore-version API paths with no UI, where voices has both. 596 web tests green. Real defects fixed along the way that no one had reported: mock mode was 502-ing on every job-review page because resolveAudioSrc prefixed /api onto static /mock asset paths; the paused-station card rendered all of its own text at 3.10:1; the guidance composer's five type names had lost the one-line hints that TYPE_HINT had been maintaining unused. Deliberately NOT fixed, with reasoning recorded in vite.config.ts: vendor-map (47 kB gz) is a static import of the entry chunk so all 12 routes download leaflet and 10 never render a map - every route component is lazy and the entry takes exactly one leaflet binding, so naming the importer needs a bundle analyzer and guessing risks the map. Costs: a second colour step (`-on-tint`) that authors must reach for on tinted chips, and a light theme that is materially less vivid - the semantic values now land on Tailwind's own 800-level text steps, which is the same answer reached from the other direction.

## 2026-07-28 — Audio-pre-review suspect words get reversible operator verdicts, applied as a read-time lens

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** AudioPreReview.Compare flags any script word the Scribe transcript spells differently, so Australian place names whose orthography and phonetics diverge (Keilor -> 'Keeler', Prahran -> 'Pran', Cheltenham -> 'Cheltnum') flag on EVERY bulletin precisely because they were said correctly. Verified live against the real comparer. ARN asked for a hover action to resolve a flagged word as correct or not correct so it stops recurring. Critically, a pronunciation-dictionary rule cannot fix this class: the comparison reads the canonical script text (AudioFinalizer.cs:258), while the alias substitution happens provider-side at synthesis, so neither side of the comparison changes.

**Decision:** Two independent actions on each suspect-word chip. 'Sounded fine' records a per-market VerifiedPronunciation (new Domain record + IVerifiedPronunciationRepository + TableStorageVerifiedPronunciationRepository on table verifiedPronunciations + VerifiedPronunciationsHttpTrigger at markets/{market}/verified-pronunciations with a verified-pronunciations/inventory aggregate), mirroring the PriorityRoad whole-list-PUT pattern. 'It was said wrong' appends an alias rule to the dictionary the bulletin aired with, reusing useUpdatePronunciationDictionary with zero backend change. The verdict list is applied as a PRESENTATION LENS at read time: AudioPreReview.Compare and job.PreReview are untouched and keep the raw unfiltered suspect list forever. Write route is Operator (not Admin) and market-scoped via IMarketAccessService. Verdicts are gated on role, never on the bulletin's canEdit.

**Rationale:** Filtering at generation would be a one-way door: the suspect word would never reach the job record, so un-verifying a mistaken verdict could only affect future bulletins while past ones stayed silently wrong. Filtering at display makes every verdict fully reversible and retroactive, and costs nothing because the only server-side consumers of SuspectWords are one job-log line and its severity (AudioFinalizer.cs:319-331) - status and notifications never depended on it. Three reversal layers, in the order an operator needs them: an Undo action on the success toast (misclicks), verified chips that COLLAPSE BEHIND A DISCLOSURE RATHER THAN VANISHING so the reversal affordance sits exactly where the mistake was made on every later bulletin, and a Verified-words tab on /guidance for bulk review. Suppression that erases its own evidence is undiscoverable, so a wrong verdict could never be noticed. Operator-owned rather than Admin-owned because operators do the listening; gating removal behind Admin would strand them with a mistake they cannot fix, and ActivityLoggingMiddleware already supplies accountability for free.

**Consequences:** New files: VerifiedPronunciation.cs, IVerifiedPronunciationRepository.cs, TableStorageVerifiedPronunciationRepository.cs, VerifiedPronunciationsHttpTrigger.cs, SuspectWordChip.tsx, use-pronunciation-verdicts.ts, verified-pronunciation-hooks.ts, VerifiedPronunciationsManager.tsx, plus two test files. Modified: OperatorContracts.cs (DTOs), ConfigValidationLimits.cs (200 words / 80 chars / 200-char notes), DependencyInjection.cs, ActivityPathResolver.cs (verified-pronunciations resource), AuthorizationMiddleware.cs (PUT -> Operator), AudioPreReviewBadge.tsx, ReviewBulletin.tsx, GuidancePage.tsx, paths.ts, toast-action.ts (optional undo action), mock adapter/store/dev-data. VerifiedPronunciation.NormalizeWord and the web pronunciationKey are a CROSS-LANGUAGE contract and must stay byte-identical; both are tested. Two real UI bugs found and fixed while building: Radix dismissed the popover when clicking its own anchor (chip exempted via onInteractOutside), and opening it blurred the chip and closed it under the cursor (blur now only closes when the pointer has left). Deliberately NOT added to the config-transfer bundle - a verdict is operational triage state, not portable configuration.
## 2026-07-28 — Operators directory is live from Entra and market access is deny-by-default

**Status:** superseded (2026-07-28 — see "Operators are token-first; Graph is optional enrichment" below)

**Context:** The Operators page previously depended on a hand-maintained
operator allow-list, while a missing `operatorAssignments` row meant that an
Operator was unrestricted. The new directory integration needs to show current
Entra role holders without copying directory data into Table Storage. Market
scope remains the only persisted identity fact: `{objectId -> markets}` in the
existing `operatorAssignments` table.

**Decision:** Read Operator/Admin role holders live from Microsoft Entra on every
Operators request and merge them with persisted assignment rows. A directory
principal without a row is shown with no markets; an assignment without a
current directory principal remains visible as an Assignment entry when Graph
is unavailable. Admins remain unrestricted. An Operator with an assignment row
can access exactly those markets, while an Operator without a row can access no
stations. Assignment-store errors fail closed with an explicit error rather
than granting access.

**Rationale:** Entra is the source of truth for who holds an application role,
so mirroring it would become stale identity data and create a second authority.
Deny-by-default is the safe interpretation of an absent station assignment;
with that policy, failing open on an assignment-store error would be a
privilege escalation. The flip was safe to make on 2026-07-28 because the
live `EntraOperatorDirectory.ListRoleHoldersAsync()` run, using an interactive
identity against both TEST and PROD registrations, returned the correct 8
principals in each environment with correct roles and group attribution.

**Consequences:** Operators now need Microsoft Graph application permission on
each environment Function App managed identity for the live directory list.
The least-privilege choice and consent ownership are recorded below. If Graph
is unavailable, the page reports the directory status and degrades to persisted
assignments rather than silently showing an empty list. An admin must assign
markets to each new Operator before that person can access a station.


## 2026-07-28 — Operators are token-first; Graph is optional enrichment

**Status:** accepted (supersedes "Operators directory is live from Entra and market access is deny-by-default" above)

**Context:** The earlier deny-by-default decision made an absent `operatorAssignments` row an access denial and made the live Graph directory read foundational to the Operators page. That created a deadlock: the Function App managed identity had no Graph consent, so the directory was empty, the manual add path had been removed, and an admin could not grant access to anyone. Station scoping is a wrong-station misconfiguration guard, not a security boundary; Entra app-role authorization remains the access control.

**Decision:** Make the Operators model token-first. Entra app-role grants access; on the first `GET /api/operators/me` call, the app self-registers the signed-in principal when no assignment row exists, creating an empty-market assignment with the principal's display name. Existing rows keep their markets; only a missing or changed display name is refreshed. An empty market list means **unscoped** (all markets), never denied. Assignment-store errors fail open with a warning. Graph (`IOperatorDirectory`/`EntraOperatorDirectory`) remains optional enrichment: the full-outer-join list and unchanged DTOs stay in place, and `DirectoryStatus: Unavailable` is non-fatal because self-registered people still appear.

**Rationale:** Reading each customer tenant's directory would force per-tenant admin consent as a SaaS onboarding gate; token claims require no consent, so directory reads must enrich, never underpin, access or operator discovery. The reversal removes the consent deadlock while preserving Entra as the authority for who may sign in. Deny-by-default is deferred until multi-station BAU, once assignment rows and operational station ownership exist; it must be revisited then as a deliberate policy change, not enabled by an incidental Graph or Table Storage failure.

**Consequences:** Admins are unrestricted. Operators with a non-empty market list are narrowed to those markets; operators with no row or an empty list are unrestricted. Removing access means removing the Entra app role, not clearing a station list. Graph consent still adds pre-population before first login and role provenance, but is not a blocker to the console or to self-registration.

## 2026-07-28 — Use least-privilege Graph permissions for the Operators directory

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `EntraOperatorDirectory` makes four Graph reads: the API service
principal and its `appRoleAssignedTo` data, transitive group membership, and
basic display name/UPN data for directly-assigned users. The Function App
managed identities need ARN tenant admin consent before these reads work.

**Decision:** Grant `Application.Read.All`, `GroupMember.Read.All`, and
`User.ReadBasic.All` as application permissions to each TEST/PROD Function App
managed identity. Keep `Directory.Read.All` only as a single-grant fallback
if ARN prefers one permission over three.

**Rationale:** Three narrow grants match the code's actual reads and avoid a
tenant-wide directory read. The live implementation already returned the
correct role holders when run with an interactive identity; consent is the
only missing MI capability. A self-grant attempt returned `403
Authorization_RequestDenied`, so this is an ARN tenant-admin action.

**Consequences:** ARN must grant/admin-consent the permissions in the ask
tracker's §10 commands for both environments, then verify the MI assignments.

## 2026-07-28 — Pre-review state is annotated once, in the script — the badge row becomes a counter

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The first cut of the suspect-word verdicts put per-word chips in the badge row under the audio player, while the script separately highlighted words carrying a pronunciation-dictionary rule. On a real dev bulletin a word with BOTH (Toorak, Keilor) rendered twice, in two places, with two different affordances. ARN's feedback on the deployed build: 'why do we have the highlighting of the words AND the top where it says 1 word to verify... this is confusing. Could we even leave this in the highlighted words on its own.' The chips also duplicated a capability the script already had: script words are click-to-seek via AudioSeekContext, which is all the chips' click did.

**Decision:** One mark per span of the script, built by the new web/src/features/jobs/lib/script-marks.ts. buildScriptMarks merges three sources into a single non-overlapping ScriptMark list: dictionary substitutions (offsets already resolved), audio-pre-review suspect words (located by word-boundary case-insensitive search), and unconfirmed figures (located by literal substring, safe because the backend captures Match.Value verbatim). A mark can carry BOTH a dictionary facet and a review facet, so the Toorak case is one highlight with one popover explaining both. New ScriptWordMark component replaces BOTH the display-only PronunciationWord and the action-carrying SuspectWordChip, which are deleted. Colour encodes state: amber = needs an ear, muted = verified, primary = dictionary rule only. AudioPreReviewBadge is now a counter plus a 'did the check run' signal, with NO per-word chips.

**Rationale:** The script is where the words already are, already anchored, already click-to-seek — a second rendering could only ever repeat or contradict it. Counting from the SAME marks the script renders makes the status line structurally unable to disagree with the highlights. Merging the two facets is the part that actually fixes the reported confusion: it is not enough to move the chips into the script, because a word with a rule AND a flag would still carry two overlapping marks. The one thing the badge keeps is a count, because without it an operator must visually scan every sentence to learn whether anything needs attention, and the clean state needs somewhere to say the transcript check ran at all.

**Consequences:** New: web/src/features/jobs/lib/script-marks.ts (+ 17 tests) and web/src/features/jobs/components/ScriptWordMark.tsx. Deleted: PronunciationWord.tsx, SuspectWordChip.tsx. Modified: ScriptRenderer (pronunciationMarkers prop becomes scriptMarks + markActions + markDictionaryName), PronunciationScriptEditor, ReviewScript, ReviewBulletin, AudioPreReviewBadge (rewritten as a counter, tests rewritten). A flagged word the script no longer contains (edited after synthesis) cannot be marked in situ, so buildScriptMarks reports it via unlocatedWords/unlocatedFigures and the badge names it — dropping it silently would hide a real warning. The accessible name on a mark composes state AND the substitution, preserving the a11y contract the existing ReviewScript tests defend; the 'Pronunciation dictionary' label moved from the popover title onto the substitution block it actually describes. 642 web tests green.

## 2026-07-28 — One pronunciation rule per word, enforced at the mapping choke point

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An operator corrected 'Toorak' from the review cockpit twice and ended up with THREE alias rules in the Melbourne Roads dictionary (Toor-rak, Toorak, Tworack) — reported with a screenshot on 2026-07-28. Root cause: addRule appended unconditionally. The compounding failure is why it happened twice: findPronunciationMatches resolves overlapping candidates by lowest ruleIndex, so the ORIGINAL curated rule (index 4) kept winning and both corrections were dead on arrival — the operator saw no change and corrected again. Nothing in Domain, the trigger, or config import prevented duplicates either, because PronunciationRule.Signature includes Replacement, so two rules for one word have different signatures.

**Decision:** Three changes. (1) The review-cockpit quick-fix now UPSERTS: it replaces an existing alias rule for the same word in place, and only appends when none exists (use-pronunciation-verdicts.addRule). (2) PronunciationRuleMapping.ParseRules rejects a rule set containing two rules of the SAME type for the same StringToReplace (case-insensitive), naming both replacements in the error. Alias + phoneme for one word stays legal — the provider applies whichever the model supports, so they can never both take effect. (3) PronunciationRule.CreateAlias rejects a respelling equal to the word itself, which changes nothing on air and only pads the list. Popover copy now states what each action changes: the verdict says 'Does NOT change how it is said', the dictionary action says 'Changes what listeners hear'.

**Rationale:** The bug was mine, but the invariant was always missing: two alias rules for one word is never intentional, and the failure mode is silent — the provider applies one and the other is dead, which is strictly worse than an error. Enforcing at ParseRules covers the studio editor, the quick-fix and config import from one place rather than three. Rejecting rather than silently de-duplicating is deliberate: which respelling to keep is a content decision an operator must make, and a silent collapse would discard someone's intended correction. Allowing alias+phoneme for one word preserves the existing legitimate pattern.

**Consequences:** Existing stored dictionaries containing duplicates now fail to SAVE until cleaned (reads are unaffected). The dev Melbourne Roads dictionary was cleaned in place: v3 21 rules -> v4 19 rules, keeping the original curated 'Toorak -> Toor-rak' that matches the dictionary's house style; the two artefacts were removed and remain recoverable via version history. New tests: PronunciationRuleMappingTests (7). Both guards verified live on dev with a 400 and an actionable message. Deployed to dev.

## 2026-07-28 — The handover documentation site is the deliverable; the branded pack shrinks to a signed cover

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Operations Handover Pack was a 15-section Typst PDF carrying operational detail, six hand-copied architecture PNGs and a table of repository paths, alongside docs-site/, a working Starlight site publishing 25 pages. Two artefacts described the same thing at different depths, and the PDF's copied assets were already a week stale against architecture/images/. The audience manifest also carried a third value, AUD_ADD, meaning 'ARN-facing but not in the PDF's received-documents table', which only existed because that table was the received list.

**Decision:** The documentation site is the received documentation set and the primary handover artefact: 37 pages in five groups (start-here 6, operate 13, architecture 3, testing 9, governance 6), with every architecture figure and a current console screenshot set published. The Typst pack shrinks to a five-section signed cover (what is handed over, the documentation set, open items, top limitations, acceptance and sign-off) that names the site and carries no figures. The audience classification collapses to two values, AUD_ARN and AUD_INT. The site ships by both routes: an Azure Static Web App IBP-AUE-{ENV}-SWA-DOC01 on dev and prod, and an offline zip attached to the signed cover.

**Rationale:** One place for detail is the only arrangement in which detail cannot drift. Images are copied into the site at build time from architecture/images/ and web/audit/after/ rather than hand-copied, so a figure cannot go stale behind a duplicate; source documents reference them through a diagram:/screenshot: scheme the sync resolves and validates, because a relative path cannot be correct both in docs/ and in the synced tree. Both delivery routes are needed because access-and-accounts.md records that the Arinco identities holding this engagement's access lapse at engagement end, so ARN must not lose the documentation with them. AUD_ADD died with the table that gave it meaning.

**Consequences:** is the single audience manifest with two values; build-docs-site.py filters on AUD_ARN and exits non-zero on an ARN-facing document with no placement, an unknown image token, or an image absent from both its live source and the tracked cache. Because the live image sources are gitignored and CI has neither the LikeC4 toolchain nor a browser audit run, the published subset is mirrored into a tracked cache at docs-site/assets/ that the sync refreshes from the live source whenever it is present: one refresh path, no hand copying. Ten new ARN-facing pages were authored (platform overview, glossary, first day, quick reference, dependencies, known limitations, FAQ, open items, acceptance, architecture diagrams). The docs SWA has no AAD configuration by design, mitigated by a noindex meta tag. A Bicep parameter cannot gate a pipeline job, so deployDocsSite exists twice, in the bicepparam and in the variable group, and they must be kept in step. The first pipeline run after enabling provisions the SWA and skips the deploy, because DOCS_SWA_DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN only exists once the app does. DOC01 is a new instance suffix to mention to the ARN Technology Lead.

## 2026-07-28 — Review changes apply through the cheapest sufficient pipeline; a pronunciation fix reaches the current bulletin

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked what should happen after fixing a pronunciation in the review cockpit, and what happens when pronunciation and evidence changes are mixed. Two defects surfaced while mapping it. (1) JobMessageBuilder built PronunciationLocator from the job's PINNED PronunciationVersionId, so any regenerate or re-voice replayed the dictionary version the job aired with — a rule changed during review could never take effect, a silent no-op of the same class as the duplicate-alias bug. (2) The dictionary edit was fire-and-forget: it updated the library, said 'applies to future bulletins', and left the bulletin under review untouched with no way to fix it in place.

**Decision:** Every queued change now resolves to the cheapest pipeline that satisfies it, and the most expensive queued change wins: pronunciation rules and verbatim script edits need only re-voice (TTS, ~15s), while evidence/curation/instructions need a full regenerate (LLM + review + TTS, ~1 min). `applyKindFor` derives this and the Revise footer reads 'Re-voice · ~15 sec' or 'Regenerate · ~1 min' accordingly. A saved rule writes to the dictionary IMMEDIATELY (a library asset stands alone and is versioned/reversible) but queues as a pending ReviewChange of the pre-existing, previously-unused `pronunciation` kind, so N fixes plus script edits batch into ONE apply. A new `RefreshPronunciation` flag on the regenerate request/command/queue message makes JobService resolve the dictionary's CURRENT version; default false keeps stale-recovery republishes byte-faithful. The marked word shows 'Queued: will say X — re-voice to apply' until applied.

**Rationale:** Cost, not category, is what the operator is deciding under an on-air clock: calling a pronunciation fix a 'regenerate' burns ~45 extra seconds AND rewrites a script they already read and approved, while calling an evidence change a 're-voice' would silently not apply it. Writing the dictionary immediately but keeping its bulletin effect pending is the honest split — the rule is worth keeping even if the bulletin is abandoned, but the audio still says the old thing until re-voiced. Refreshing the locator only on an explicit operator act preserves the deliberate historical-replay guarantee the pinned version exists for; every failure to resolve (dictionary gone, storage down) falls back to the pinned locator rather than dropping the dictionary and disabling every other rule mid-review.

**Consequences:** Backend: RefreshPronunciation added to RegenerateJobRequest/RegenerateJobCommand; JobService gains IPronunciationDictionaryService and ResolveCurrentPronunciationAsync; JobMessageBuilder takes a pronunciationOverride. 8 test construction sites updated. 5 new JobService tests cover refresh, the faithful default, and all three fallbacks. Frontend: PronunciationEdit + applyKindFor + pendingPronunciation in use-bulletin-review; ScriptMark gains pendingReplacement; ReviseDialog is two-speed; 11 new applyKindFor tests. A terminal bulletin passes no onEdit, so no un-appliable chip is queued and the toast says 'applies from the next bulletin' instead. Mock fixture dev-job-287d14a0 seeded with suspect words so the whole flow is exercisable in mock mode. 3,318 backend and 657 frontend tests green.

## 2026-07-28 — Re-voice carries the script the regeneration reset destroys, and records the dictionary version it actually used

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Edge-case sweep of the 2026-07-28 pronunciation-apply feature against dev found the headline path dead on arrival, plus three quieter defects. (1) Job.RequestRegeneration clears ScriptText, and JobMessageBuilder reads job.ScriptText as the PreviousScript fallback that RevoiceExistingScriptAsync synthesises from. The pre-existing script-editor re-voice always supplies EditedScript so it never hit this; a pronunciation-only re-voice supplies none, so EVERY such apply failed with 'Re-voice requested but there is no existing script to synthesise' - and because the reset had already wiped ScriptText, the failure permanently destroyed the job's script (observed on dev job 95b0192a, left at 0 characters and unrecoverable). (2) Only ScriptGenerationEngine persisted the pronunciation pin, and a re-voice never runs it, so a refreshed re-voice synthesised with the new version while the record still claimed the old one - the same provenance hole already fixed once for DeliveryStyleId in the very same method. (3) pronunciationEdits used plain useState while every sibling sub-hook uses useResetOnChange, so a spent chip survived the apply, re-arming refreshPronunciation and keeping the apply button live with nothing to apply. (4) The script-editor re-voice never forwarded refreshPronunciation, silently discarding a queued rule. A fifth, pre-existing gap surfaced while probing validation: pronunciation rules had no length cap at all, and a 5000-character replacement was accepted by dev.

**Decision:** Capture job.ScriptText into a local BEFORE RequestRegeneration and pass it to the queue message as a last-resort PreviousScript, gated on RevoiceOnly - on a full regenerate PreviousScript means 'the operator's edited wording, preserve it' and same-day continuity already travels on PreviousScriptContext, so resurrecting the old script there would change what the LLM is told. Persist PronunciationDictionaryId/VersionId in SaveFinalBroadcastResultAsync from the context the synthesis call was actually handed, beside the existing DeliveryStyle provenance. Key pronunciationEdits on `${jobId}:${status}` - status is exactly the apply transition, whereas lastUpdatedAt churns on background polls and would wipe a queue mid-edit and lose a failed apply's retry. Forward refreshPronunciation through the script-editor re-voice, and memoise pendingPronunciation so the buildScriptMarks memo stops rebuilding every mark each render. Cap rules at MaxWordLength 80 (matching MaxVerifiedPronunciationLength) and MaxReplacementLength 200 in PronunciationRule's factories - the single choke point every write path already funnels through - mirrored as maxLength on both operator inputs.

**Rationale:** The re-voice failure was invisible to every gate that existed: unit tests mocked the orchestrator, mock mode never runs it, and the only pre-existing caller of the re-voice path happened to supply the one field that masked the bug. It took a real dev run to surface, which is why both backend fixes now carry tests that were each verified to FAIL when the fix is reverted. Refreshing the synthesis version without recording it is worse than not refreshing at all: the pin exists so a stale-recovery republish reproduces what aired, and a silently-wrong pin makes the cockpit cite the wrong version and the republish produce different audio. The length cap belongs in the domain rather than the form because the review cockpit turned rule creation from a studio task into a one-click operator action on every bulletin, and these rules ship to ElevenLabs on every synthesis and are read aloud verbatim wherever the word appears.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev, not just in tests. Job d4cbdb5b re-voiced successfully with RefreshPronunciation and moved v1 -> v5 (script preserved at 536 characters, previously a hard failure); the control without the flag stayed pinned at v1; a job with no dictionary refreshed harmlessly. Full operator loop driven on the deployed SWA against real dev: fixing Keilor minted Melbourne Roads v6 with exactly one Keilor rule, the mark read 'Queued: will say Kee-lor - re-voice to apply', the footer read 'Re-voice - ~15 sec', and after apply the job pinned v6, the popovers read version 6 / 'Kee-lor', and the chip cleared. Terminal bulletins still queue nothing and say 'applies from the next bulletin'. 3,326 backend and 662 frontend tests pass (12 new). Six of seven rule-validation guards already held (no-op, duplicate alias, empty word, empty replacement, whitespace replacement, unknown type); only the length cap was missing. That cap is committed and unit-tested but NOT yet deployed: dev Owner is PIM-eligible via GROUP membership, so the CLI token needs re-authentication to carry the claim, and Conditional Access blocks the device-code flow - it needs an interactive az login by the user.

## 2026-07-28 — Pronunciation version history is trimmed to fit the Azure Table property limit

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Restoring a rule on dev after edge-case testing returned HTTP 500 with a raw storage error: PropertyValueTooLarge. Pronunciation version history is append-only and every entry stores a FULL rule snapshot (~3.5KB for the 19-rule Melbourne Roads dictionary), serialised into a single VersionsJson column. Azure Table caps one property at 64KB / 32K UTF-16 chars, so the ceiling is roughly NINE versions. Melbourne Roads reached 31,551 of 32,768 chars (v10) and the next save was rejected. The failure mode is a deadlock rather than a degradation: the only way to shrink the history is to write the entity, and writes are exactly what the overflow rejects - so once a dictionary tips over, no operator can add, fix or remove a single rule for that market ever again through the API, and recovery needs direct Table Storage access. This gap predates the review-cockpit work, but that feature is what makes it likely: adding a rule went from a deliberate studio task performed occasionally by an admin to a one-click action available to any operator on any bulletin, and every save mints a version. Dev was recovered by pruning the entity directly.

**Decision:** Trim version history by SERIALISED SIZE, not by count, in TableStoragePronunciationDictionaryRepository.MapToEntity: drop the oldest snapshots until VersionsJson fits a 24,000-char budget, always retaining at least the current version, and log a warning naming the retained range. Size-aware rather than count-aware because one version's cost scales with the rule count, so any fixed N is wrong for a large dictionary. The budget deliberately sits below the 32,768 limit so a subsequent full version still fits.

**Rationale:** A silently-truncated audit tail is strictly better than a dictionary that can never be edited again, and ElevenLabs still holds every published version, so the trimmed entries are a local convenience copy rather than the system of record. The limit is an Azure Table property constraint, so it belongs in the repository: the domain aggregate should not know how it is persisted, and the trim has to apply to every write path (studio, review cockpit, config import) which all funnel through this mapper. Keeping the current version unconditionally matters because reconstitution fails on an empty version list - MapToDomain logs 'corrupt, no versions' and drops the dictionary from the library entirely, which would be a far worse outcome than losing old snapshots.

**Consequences:** A dictionary older than roughly six versions loses the RULE SNAPSHOTS of its earliest versions; version numbers, ElevenLabs ids, change notes, authors and dates for retained entries are unaffected. A job pinned to a trimmed version no longer resolves its dictionary highlights and renders without pronunciation marks rather than failing. 4 new Infrastructure tests cover the short-history, long-history, oldest-dropped-current-kept and single-enormous-version cases. Dev recovered: Melbourne Roads pruned from 10 versions / 31,551 chars to 5 / 18,104, writes confirmed working again, and Mickleham restored to 'Mikulum'. NOT yet deployed - the dev credential needs an interactive re-login (see the same-day re-voice decision). Two related gaps are recorded but NOT fixed, because both are cross-cutting design choices: dictionary writes have no optimistic concurrency, so two operators saving different words from a stale read silently lose one of them (reproduced on dev - operator A's rule vanished, both PUTs returned 200); and full history retention would need the versions blob moved out of the table row.

## 2026-07-28 — The handover site is rewritten for ARN, and a build-time leak guard keeps it that way

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The documentation site published 37 documents, of which only four had been written for ARN. The rest were Arinco engineering working notes reclassified as client-facing. A client-readiness audit measured the result: a metadata strip on all 37 pages exposing our repository layout and documentation-harness vocabulary, 334 repository paths in page bodies, 17 pages naming individual consultants or staff, 16 citing internal identifiers such as DEF-004 and SG3, 113 uses of the word poller, 75 visible placeholders, and a decision log of 3,960 lines carrying workshop attendance and our own scope decisions. Two of the ten published diagrams were marked engineering exploration in our own registry, and a C# source path and an SDD section reference were burned into a third.

**Decision:** Nine documents are withdrawn from the published set and reclassified internal: the decision log, the SG2 solution design, the success criteria, the risk register, the project brief, the three test-harness documents and the printed session handout. Three replacements are written for ARN: a solution overview, twelve curated design decisions, and a proven-capacity page. Every surviving page is rewritten against a language contract. The information architecture becomes six groups organised by reader, not five organised by our filing. The per-page provenance strip is deleted, the Arinco logo leaves the header for a footer colophon, and three diagrams are withdrawn while system-context is redrawn as a manual orthogonal render so all seven published figures share one visual language.

**Rationale:** Reading for leaks does not scale past a handful of pages and does not survive the next author, so the language contract is enforced by the build rather than by discipline. scripts/build-docs-site.py now fails on eleven classes of leak, on a link to an unpublished document, and on a reference to an unpublished image. That took the site from 583 detected leaks to zero. The vocabulary substitutions matter for the same reason the leaks do: a term we coined inside this project, or lifted from a C# type, teaches ARN our codebase instead of using the language their own broadcast and Azure people already speak. Grouping by reader rather than by internal category means a content operator never has to walk past the incident runbook.

**Consequences:** The published set is 31 pages in six groups: start-here 5, console 3, operate 10, how-it-works 4, assurance 6, handover 3. Adding an ARN-facing page means an AUD_ARN entry in the shared manifest, a PLACEMENT entry, and passing the guard. A leak is a content bug: weakening the guard to make a build pass is the wrong move, and an exemption in ALLOW needs a reader-facing justification. SAFE_IDENTIFIERS carries the Key Vault secret names and app settings that look like C# types but are operational facts. Only manual orthogonal renders are published, never auto-layout exports, and render specs are checked for internal text because a caption baked into a PNG cannot be fixed by editing prose. The withdrawn nine remain in the repository ARN inherits and stay in our own SG3 evidence; they are simply not published.

## 2026-07-28 — A re-voice preserves the evidence snapshot it is about to re-read, and priority-road Enabled is honoured

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A pipeline-wide audit for silent no-ops (config that is read, carried, and then never affects the bulletin) found two live defects and disproved several suspected ones. (1) A re-voice destroyed the entire evidence trail. JobService.RegenerateJobAsync calls Job.RequestRegeneration for BOTH pipelines, and that reset clears the script, corridors, incidents, flow roads and delivery provenance on the assumption a fresh traffic fetch will repopulate them. A re-voice never fetches: BroadcastOrchestrator returns to AudioFinalizer.RevoiceExistingScriptAsync before TryRefreshTrafficAsync runs. AudioFinalizer then wrote Weather/Fuel/GoodRunRoads/FlowRoads back from a context that carries none of them, blanking those too. Measured on dev: two re-voiced jobs held 0 incidents / 0 good runs / no weather / no fuel while an untouched job held 10/6 and a full regenerate held 25/6. The operator console showed '0 incidents cited . 0 sourced . heuristic matching' beside a script making eight specific road claims, so the review cockpit's whole purpose - check the words against the evidence before approving - was defeated on every re-voiced bulletin. (2) PriorityRoad.Enabled was declared, persisted, round-tripped through config import and documented as 'skipped at generation time', but no consumer ever read it: PriorityRoads.EnabledIncidentBoostNames filtered on BoostIncidents alone and FlowPoolBuilder on FlowTier alone. Switching a priority road off in the manager kept it boosting incidents and driving good-run selection.

**Decision:** Give Job.RequestRegeneration a `preserveEvidence` flag, set for RevoiceOnly, which keeps the script, tagged script, delivery provenance, corridors, incidents, flow roads and sentences while still clearing error/attempt/audio/duration and transitioning to Requested. Guard AudioFinalizer's Weather/Fuel/GoodRunRoads/FlowRoads writes behind `!context.RevoiceOnly` so a re-voice cannot overwrite them with the empties its context carries. This supersedes the earlier priorScript capture: ScriptText now survives the reset, so JobMessageBuilder's existing job.ScriptText fallback reads the real words and the extra parameter is removed. Separately, make Enabled load-bearing in both places that decide what a priority road does.

**Rationale:** The reset's clearing behaviour is right for a full regenerate - stale corridors must not mix with a fresh fetch - and wrong for a re-voice, which re-renders words that are already fixed and whose evidence still describes them exactly. Distinguishing the two at the reset is better than repopulating afterwards, because it keeps a single source of truth and avoids a second write path. Guarding the AudioFinalizer writes as well is deliberate belt-and-braces: the reset protects the record, the guard stops the finaliser undoing that from an empty context, and either alone would leave half the trail missing. Honouring Enabled follows the documented contract rather than changing it: a manager offering an on/off switch that does nothing is worse than no switch.

**Consequences:** Verified on dev after deploy: re-voicing a job holding 25 incidents / 6 good runs / weather / fuel preserved all of it (previously all zeroed), and the console now reads '25 incidents cited' where it read '0 incidents cited'. 3,333 backend tests pass; 6 new, and the two evidence guards were each verified to FAIL when preserveEvidence is forced off. DISPROVED during the audit, recorded so it is not re-investigated: regeneration does NOT drop editorial guidance, style rules, weather or fuel. Three independent traces concluded it did, because OrchestrateAsync(BroadcastWithTraffic) has no direct FetchMarketContentAsync call - but TrafficEvidenceBuilder.TryRefreshTrafficAsync ends with ApplyMarketContent(FetchMarketContentAsync(...)), and it always runs on a regenerate because the reset empties the corridors. Proven on dev: a full regenerate moved Weather/Fuel from absent to present. STILL OPEN, reported not fixed: RegenerationQueueMessage carries no DeliveryStyle/DeliveryStyleId/DeliveryStyleVersion/PaceBoostWpm (the scheduled BroadcastQueueMessage carries five such fields), so a regenerated bulletin is voiced with the neutral default policy - code-confirmed but not runtime-verified, as no dev schedule has a delivery style assigned. Filler statements are appended AFTER the safety gate and pass neither the banned-word filter nor the LLM reviewer. PriorityRoads.IsMatch is a substring match, so 'M1' matches 'M11'. Three prompt arguments (goodRunsAreFill, includesWeather, includesFuel) are computed and passed but appear in no template.

## 2026-07-28 — Delivery style is pinned through regeneration, dictionary writes are ETag-guarded, and priority-road matching respects word boundaries

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Three defects from the pipeline audit, each chosen by ARN over the alternatives offered. (1) RegenerationQueueMessage carried no delivery fields at all where the scheduled BroadcastQueueMessage carries five, so every regenerate fell back to DeliveryStylePolicy.Neutral and silently lost the station's configured delivery. The job pins only a style id and version, never the policy, so the policy has to be looked up. (2) Pronunciation-dictionary writes had no optimistic concurrency: two operators who each loaded the dictionary and saved a DIFFERENT word both received HTTP 200 and one rule vanished with no warning (reproduced on dev). The review cockpit made this likely by turning rule creation into a one-click action on every bulletin. (3) PriorityRoads.IsMatch tested bare substring containment in both directions, so a priority road named 'M1' also boosted M10, M11 and M12.

**Decision:** Delivery: carry the pinned policy on the regeneration message and add a RefreshDelivery flag mirroring RefreshPronunciation — default replays the exact version the bulletin aired with, the flag takes the style's current version. The lookup MUST happen before Job.RequestRegeneration, which clears DeliveryStyleId/Version on a full regenerate; reading them afterwards yields neutral, the same trap that destroyed ScriptText. A pinned version that no longer exists falls back to the style's current policy rather than to neutral. Concurrency: ETag/If-Match on the existing whole-list PUT rather than a new single-rule endpoint. The repository does a conditional UpdateEntityAsync with bounded retry, a stale revision returns OperationalFailure.Conflict('pronunciation.revision_mismatch'), and the trigger maps it to HTTP 409. Because a 409 would otherwise force an operator to retype a one-click fix, the review cockpit's addRule refetches on the first conflict, replays its single-word replacement onto the fresh rule list and retries exactly once before surfacing an error. Matching: containment must start and end on a token boundary, keeping 'M1' matching 'M1 Pacific Motorway' while dropping M10/M11.

**Rationale:** Pinned-by-default plus an explicit refresh is the contract already established for pronunciation, and having two per-station libraries behave differently would be worse than either behaviour alone. ETag was chosen over a single-rule endpoint because it also protects the studio's genuine replace-the-list semantics and reuses the pattern jobs already use for approve/publish; the cockpit auto-retry buys back the UX the naive 412 would have cost, since a one-word delta always replays cleanly onto a fresh list. Word-boundary matching keeps the looseness that exists for short corridor keys and removes only the false positives. Filler statements were deliberately left OUTSIDE the safety gate and a verbatim script edit on a full regenerate deliberately remains a prompt hint rather than a guarantee — both were reviewed and accepted as-is, so re-raising them is not a new finding.

**Consequences:** 3,353 backend and 670 frontend tests pass; 15 new. Every new guard was verified to FAIL when its fix is reverted, including one weak test caught in review: the cockpit retry test mocks a plain {status:409} object and so only exercises one branch of isConflictError — it passes with the ApiError branch disabled. ETag verified LIVE on dev: two writers sharing a snapshot now produce 200 then 409, and the first operator's rule survives where it previously vanished. Delivery is unit-verified only. A live end-to-end was attempted and is BLOCKED BY DEV CONFIG, not by the fix: no dev station uses a v3 voice, so DeliveryDirector skips tagging entirely, no tags are produced, and DeliveryStyleId is legitimately never persisted. Delivery styles are therefore inert across all of dev today regardless of this change. The DeliveryStylePolicy wire type is already proven to round-trip on BroadcastQueueMessage, which carries the same type on the scheduled path. The RefreshDelivery flag has no UI trigger: nothing in the review cockpit edits a delivery style (DeliveryPanel only displays it), so frontend plumbing would be dead code until such an affordance exists. Config import stays un-guarded by design — it supplies no client ETag and relies on a server-side read-modify-write — and DELETE keeps its pre-existing unconditional idempotent path.

## 2026-07-28 — Custom metrics declare their dimension names; handover docs state only what is deployed

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A primary-source audit of the 31 ARN-facing handover pages found that ApplicationInsightsBroadcastMetrics.SafeTrack called GetMetric(name) without dimension names. Application Insights therefore discarded every dimension VALUE on the metric stream while still emitting the metric, so customMetrics.customDimensions was always empty. Consequences, all verified live against dev: the -poison-queue and -synthesis-failures scheduled-query alerts could never match a row (35 real synthesis failures in 30 days went unalerted), the Queue Status and Cost Tracking workbooks could not label a series, and the Pipeline Latency workbook percentiled the per-minute SUM rather than the per-bulletin mean, reporting orchestration_total p99 as 254.66s against a 240s objective when the true p99 was 117.0s. Separately the audit found ~40 doc claims that were false, stale or over-specific about capability that does not exist.

**Decision:** Fix the telemetry at the source rather than caveat it in prose: SafeTrack now declares dimension names via GetMetric(name, dim1, dim2) and passes values to TrackValue, and both latency workbook queries use valueSum/valueCount. Six regression tests in ApplicationInsightsBroadcastMetricsTests assert the dimension contract on both the metric and event streams; five of the six fail if GetMetric loses its dimension names. Handover docs then state what is deployed with no apologetic caveats, and any claim about a capability that does not exist is deleted rather than hedged. Workbook descriptions were trimmed to the panels that actually exist, which closed the monitoring-view defect.

**Rationale:** The alternative was to strip the poison-queue and synthesis-failure alerts from eight ARN-facing doc sites and drop the per-station cost and queue labelling, leaving ARN with two dead alert rules, two mislabelled workbooks and nothing in the documentation pointing at them. Declaring the dimension names is a single method change that makes four separate capability claims true at once, so it removes monitoring debt instead of hiding it. Deleting rather than hedging keeps the pages readable: a handover reader needs to know what the platform does, not a catalogue of things it half-does.

**Consequences:** Poison-queue and synthesis-failure alerts now bind to real series and will fire on threshold breach. Queue Status labels broadcast, regeneration and poison depth; Cost Tracking splits by station. Pipeline Latency and SLO 3 now agree. Splitting any objective by station needs no code change: the event stream already carries Properties.market, documented in slo.md. Production alert rules remain disabled while parked and standing subscription Owner remains with three service principals and the supplier guest account, so both are now before-go-live rows in open-items.md. RISK-23 and RISK-25 are closed, RISK-28 restated to the real residual (the standby recording is wired and serving but is not ARN-approved content), RISK-33's corridor cap corrected to the slot-derived clamp(6,15). Defect 2 closed by the description trim; the map-link defect narrowed to the Review tab only, since Adjust has working links with tests.

## 2026-07-29 — Bug-bash remediation wave one: storage ceiling, silent data loss, and contract correctness

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A systematic bug bash of dev on 2026-07-28 found 35 defects (6 critical, 12 high, 8 medium, 9 low; full list in ). ARN's constraint for this wave was explicit: fix only what is OBJECTIVELY wrong - never intended behaviour, never system prompts, and nothing that could regress a working path. That test excluded 16 findings and selected 19. The selection was evidence-based, not judgement-based: four exclusions were reversed after checking the console makes them unreachable (PriorityRoadsManager.tsx:162 filters blank names and line 194 de-duplicates; mappers.ts:59 always sends Location), and one candidate was withdrawn entirely after the code showed `market` was never a supported query parameter on /api/jobs.

**Decision:** Storage: one shared VersionHistoryTrimmer now serialises every versioned library's history, replacing the pronunciation-only trim. Style rules, voice profiles and delivery styles had NO trim at all. When even the current version alone exceeds the ceiling, trimming cannot help (dropping it would make the record unreconstitutable), so the write is refused with an actionable OperationalFailure.InvalidInput instead of an opaque storage 500; TableRepositoryBase additionally strips Azure's RequestId/Time diagnostic tail while KEEPING the human-readable first line, because the HTTP layer still matches 'not found' and 'conflict' in message text. Silent data loss: priority roads validate-then-build (blank names and duplicates are 400s, and the count limit now describes the payload rather than the survivors), in both the trigger and the import plan builder. CoverageResolver no longer substitutes a hardcoded Melbourne for a missing Location, which makes OrchestrationValidation's own 'Location is required' check reachable for the first time. ScheduleService.ValidateCronAndTimezone is now shared by the interactive path and the import planner, and ConfigImportPlan.ToReport counts OUTCOMES rather than planned actions. LibraryReferenceGuard blocks deleting a voice profile, delivery style or dictionary a station still references, naming the stations, and fails CLOSED when the schedule list cannot be read. Contracts: bulletin duration bounded to 5-600s; regenerate concurrency returns 409 not 400; DeleteJob gained the market guard every sibling already had; /synthesize validates VoiceId at the boundary; settled statuses get their own approve-refusal wording; and the approval countdown passes showHours so a two-hour deadline no longer reads '120:00 left'.

**Rationale:** The objectively-wrong test is sharper than 'no behaviour change' and it is what made most of this wave safe: silently discarding an operator's input under a 200, reporting a create that never persisted, and two write paths to one table enforcing different rules are not designs anyone chose. Where the evidence genuinely conflicted it is recorded rather than papered over - two tests asserted the Melbourne default, so someone did intend it when Melbourne was the only market; with 13 stations a caller who omits the field silently airing Melbourne traffic is indefensible, and both tests were inverted with the history in the comment. Deliberately NOT fixed: the FlowTier default (the console defaults new roads to 'high', which AGREES with the DTO, so only unreachable paths disagree), free-text market minting (the endpoint is designed for free text), the cron minimum (a policy value, not a bug), the dev auth bypass and fail-open market scoping (both deliberate and commented), export section coverage (needs the import side too), and the domain Approve guard (AudioFinalizer.cs:200 legitimately approves mid-pipeline in ScriptOnly mode).

**Consequences:** 3,387 backend and 674 frontend tests pass, zero warnings, eslint and prettier clean. Every new guard was proven to FAIL when its fix is reverted, including at the real call site rather than only against the helper - the first countdown test passed under sabotage because it exercised the formatter directly, so it was rewritten against useWaitingBadge itself. Verified live on dev after deploy: the style-rules record that sat at 30,866 of 32,768 chars (94.2%, one edit from permanent bricking) took a real write successfully and trimmed to 18,909; a throwaway delivery style survived 15 content-varying edits where edit #6 previously returned 500 and bricked the record; restore now answers a clean 404 for a trimmed version instead of 500; deleting melbourne's in-use dictionary returns 409 naming KIIS 101.1; blank and duplicate roads return 400; POST /broadcast without Location returns 400; import rejects a bad cron and timezone; duration 99999 and 0.001 return 400; concurrent regenerate returns 409; /synthesize without VoiceId returns 400. Regression sweep: auth still 401s anonymously, all 12 read endpoints 200, create/edit/delete round-trips work, deleting an UNASSIGNED dictionary is not over-blocked, export/import is still idempotent at 82 Unchanged, and a full bulletin still generates end to end (WAITING_APPROVAL with audio in 24s). Two latent test-data bugs surfaced and were fixed: ConfigImportServiceTests used a 6-field cron the real Cronos parser rejects (passing only because the stub returned true unconditionally - the stub now delegates to the real parser), and the pronunciation trim test was rewritten to cover all four libraries. Also removed: the dead 72-line Messages.cs duplicate error catalog, the now-unused CoverageOptions, the empty Auth__DevFallbackRole app setting in PROD, and the orphaned empty voiceCalibrations table. 16 findings remain open by design and are itemised in the bug-bash document.

## 2026-07-29 — POST /api/broadcast requires a voice; the DefaultVoiceName fallback is deleted

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** POST /api/broadcast accepted a request with no voice fields at all and JobService.CreateJobAsync silently substituted Broadcast:DefaultVoiceId + Broadcast:DefaultVoiceName. That name was a fiction: commit 042ae6e (2026-06-16) snapshotted 'ARN Hudson' into config after renaming ElevenLabs voice oKDz3nEzNfwKIVvUwPs0 in the account, and the account was later renamed back to 'Peter Michael - Australian Male VO'. Nothing reconciled the two. Four dev melbourne jobs (2026-07-25 00:54, 2026-07-28 05:53/13:15/15:17) therefore aired in Peter Michael's voice, labelled 'ARN Hudson' in the job record, the logs and the operator console, with Settings null and no pronunciation dictionary. The trigger was 'arn trigger' whose --via post default sent only Location/TargetDurationSeconds/Content. OrchestrationValidation.Validate checked location, duration, coverage, settings shape, content and fill order but never the voice, so the ad-hoc path was the only write path with no referential integrity: PUT /api/schedules and config import both already 400 a dangling VoiceProfileId.

**Decision:** A broadcast must name its own voice. OrchestrationValidation.Validate now rejects a request where both VoiceProfileId and VoiceId are absent or blank (OfWhitespace already collapses empty strings). BroadcastHttpTrigger validates the reference exists: an unknown VoiceProfileId 400s (mirroring ScheduleHttpTrigger), and an unknown bare VoiceId 400s against the provider voice list, fail-soft only when the list itself cannot be fetched. JobService.CreateJobAsync no longer reads DefaultVoiceId/DefaultVoiceName at all, and a named VoiceProfileId that cannot be resolved is now a hard failure instead of a logged warning plus a default-voice job. Broadcast:DefaultVoiceName is DELETED from BroadcastOptions, appsettings.json and appsettings.json.example. Display names are resolved server-side and never invented: profile name, then the TTS provider's real name for the voice id, then the caller-supplied VoiceName, then the raw id. StationConfigResolver's last-resort poller fallback resolves its name from the provider too. Every non-web caller of POST /api/broadcast now sends a voice: arn trigger gained --voice and otherwise resolves the market schedule's VoiceProfileId, and test-bulletin.sh, export-prompts.py and pipeline_burst.py do the same or fail loudly.

**Rationale:** Voice is per-station configuration in this product, so a silent global fallback has no legitimate use: it exists only to let an under-specified request succeed while producing something nobody chose. Rejecting at the boundary also converts a wasted full pipeline run (traffic fetch, four generation attempts, review, safety, then a TTS failure) into an instant 400. Deleting DefaultVoiceName rather than merely correcting it removes the whole class of bug: any hardcoded display name is a snapshot of a mutable provider-side label, and ModelSelector already fetches and caches the live voice list in the same call, so the truth was always in hand and unused. Broadcast:DefaultVoiceId survives because previews and deep-pipeline calibration guards genuinely need an audition voice with no job in scope.

**Consequences:** POST /api/broadcast is a breaking change for any caller that omitted a voice: it now returns 400 'A voice is required: supply VoiceProfileId (preferred, resolves the profile's full tuning) or VoiceId.' The web Trigger Studio was already compliant (its zod schema requires voiceProfileId and voiceId at min(1)). IVoiceProvider is now a constructor dependency of JobService, BroadcastHttpTrigger, StationConfigResolver and (threaded through) SchedulePollerService. Verified: full backend suite green (Domain 1305, Application 579, Functions 442, Infrastructure 1267, Architecture 14, ExternalSmoke 3) plus 15/15 E2E against a live Functions host, and a live smoke test on a local host with the fake provider confirmed all four rejections by exact message, 202 on both accepted shapes, and that a caller-supplied VoiceName of 'Totally Made Up Voice' is overridden by the provider's real name.

## 2026-07-29 — Hardcoded mirrors of live lists are the bug class; audit register created

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The ARN Hudson fix exposed a pattern rather than an incident: a config value snapshotted a provider-side label, the label changed, nothing reconciled them, and a green test suite never noticed. A systematic sweep on 2026-07-29 checked every externally-meaningful identifier in the repo against its live source (ElevenLabs voices and models, Foundry deployments, deployed app settings, Key Vault secrets, live schedules, HERE endpoints) and found five more of the same shape plus several open items.

**Decision:** Fixed in place: the two fabricated pilot voice ids in production-readiness.md (Dolly Traffic is 081vkDcbgbIsSiFEYxT0, Jeffrey David G is a1SQPk93LAMHsGM41p6S); gpt-5.4-mini in both example appsettings (deployed model is gpt-5.6-luna); LlmScriptGenerator.CityMappings, which told the LLM five live markets were called Goldcoast, Cairns-4ca, Portaugusta, Portlincoln and Demo-coast, now keyed by every live MarketId with a regression test over all 13; FakeVoiceProvider's fake names, which paired real voice ids with names ElevenLabs has never used; and scripts/voice-audition.py, marked SUPERSEDED because one of its two finalists no longer exists at the provider. The full register including open items lives at docs/reference/config-drift-audit-2026-07-29.md.

**Rationale:** Each of these is a hardcoded mirror of a list that lives somewhere else, so each will drift again. Recording the primary-source command for every check next to the finding makes the audit repeatable rather than a one-off. The items left open all need either an ARN fact (the Zetta market code for 4CA Cairns) or a decision we should not make unilaterally (deleting billed Foundry deployments, redeploying dev, seeding a Key Vault secret), so they are registered rather than guessed at.

**Consequences:** New doc docs/reference/config-drift-audit-2026-07-29.md carries the register, the re-run commands, the open items and an explicit checked-and-clean list. Four HIGH/MEDIUM items remain open: cairns-4ca has no Zetta market code so it would deliver cairns-4ca_TRAIN_TRAFF.wav; AadClientSecret is a Key Vault reference to a secret that does not exist in the dev vault; deployed dev app settings predate two bicep revisions (Broadcast__UseAudioProxy false vs true, Zetta__DropFileShareName absent); and per-role Foundry deployments plus three orphan deployments total 5,680 TPM of provisioned but unreferenced capacity. Latent: nothing refreshes a voice profile's stored BaseVoiceName when the provider renames a base voice.

## 2026-07-29 — Config drift open items resolved; per-role model wiring planned, terra is not an orphan

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-07-29 drift audit left five open items. Under the AGENTS.md self-serve posture each was retested for whether the blocker was real. Four were self-serve and are now closed. Two of the original gradings were wrong: AadClientSecret was graded HIGH but main.bicep:187 already documents that dev deliberately never populates it, and the 'three orphan Foundry deployments, 5,380 TPM' finding was wrong on both counts because gpt-5.6-terra is the pinned judge for the .foundry eval suite that the CI EvalGate stage runs, and every deployment is GlobalStandard so idle capacity is a rate limit rather than a billed reservation.

**Decision:** Closed self-serve: (1) ZettaOptions.ResolveMarketCode now returns null for an unmapped market and ZettaFileDeliveryService fails the delivery naming the market and the setting to add, instead of silently shipping a file under the raw market id; (2) the AadClientSecret app setting and clientSecretSettingName were removed from function-app.bicep and function-authsettings.bicep and from live dev, because Easy Auth runs Return401 as a pure resource server and never performs an authorization-code exchange, the only real consumer being the SWA custom Entra provider which main.bicep feeds via getSecret at deploy time; (3) Broadcast__UseAudioProxy and Zetta__DropFileShareName were set on live dev to match bicep and test, which exposed and fixed arn job audio assuming an absolute SAS URL and therefore already being broken against test and prod; (4) VoiceProfilesHttpTrigger now resolves each profile's base voice name from IVoiceProvider so a provider-side rename cannot leave the UI showing a stale name. Left open: confirming the Zetta market codes with ARN, and wiring the per-role model deployments, for which the plan is to have function-app.bicep emit AiSettings__AzureAI__{Role}Model from the roleDeployments map it already receives and never reads.

**Rationale:** A silent wrong-named playout file cannot be noticed; a failed delivery can, so failing is strictly better even while the correct value is unknown. Removing an unused secret reference is better than seeding a credential nobody consumes, and it was verifiable: auth was re-tested after the change and behaves identically. Aligning dev with bicep rather than redeploying avoided shipping unrelated in-flight work from the shared working tree. The per-role wiring is deliberately left as a plan rather than done, because it is a capacity-isolation decision rather than a defect, and because the audit's own cost justification for it evaporated once the deployments were confirmed to be consumption-billed.

**Consequences:** ZettaOptions.ResolveMarketCode returns string? and its single caller treats null as failure; one existing test that asserted the old fallback (DeliverAsync_UnmappedMarket_UsesMarketIdAsIs) encoded the bug and was replaced. VoiceProfilesHttpTrigger takes IVoiceProvider. Live dev no longer has an AadClientSecret app setting and its authsettingsV2 no longer names clientSecretSettingName. The 6 Zetta market codes already in use were never ARN-confirmed either - they came from the PoC vendor and ARN's own handover doc says GC where our config says GLD for Gold Coast - so the ARN ask is to confirm all 13, not just supply the missing 7. Full backend suite green (Domain 1310, Application 580, Functions 499, Infrastructure 1291, Architecture 14, ExternalSmoke 3) and 15/15 E2E against a live host.

## 2026-07-29 — Bug-bash remediation wave two: security posture, remaining silent data loss, and input bounds

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Wave one (2026-07-28) fixed 19 of the 35 bug-bash defects and left 16 open by design. ARN then selected 13 of those 16 for wave two and answered the four questions that had blocked them: dev stays deliberately open (harden prod only); a minimum cron interval should exist; an unknown broadcast Location should be accepted but flagged rather than rejected; and FlowTier should align on 'none' with unknown tiers rejected. The remaining three (#20 prompt-injection sanitising, #21 un-approve, #34 mixed time formats) stay open.

**Decision:** Security: the dev RBAC bypass now has two independent guards. main.bicep passes `contains(['dev','sbx'], environment) ? devAuthFallbackRole : ''`, so a non-empty value in a test/prod bicepparam is structurally inert; and StartupSafety.IsUnsafeAuthBypass aborts host startup when the setting carries a value on a site whose WEBSITE_SITE_NAME contains -TST-/-PRD-. WEBSITE_SITE_NAME was chosen over a new app setting because Azure always sets it and no configuration change can remove it; an ABSENT site name (local dev, E2E host) stays permissive, so the guard only ever refuses a positively identified test/prod deployment. MarketAccessService now fails CLOSED when a caller's scope cannot be READ - the assignment lookup threw, returned a failure, or a non-admin arrived with no object id - by returning Some(empty) rather than None; the opt-in policy is untouched, so an operator with no assignment row is still unrestricted and no working caller loses access. MarketAccessGuard's null-principal branch is deliberately left permissive and now carries the reason: it is the dev bypass's load-bearing path and is unreachable in test/prod because AuthorizationMiddleware already returned 401. Silent data loss: a blank schedule Name/Station is a 400 instead of a silent no-op (null still means 'not supplied'); a body MarketId contradicting the URL is a 400; a Location matching no schedule still generates but returns a Warning and writes a Warn-level job log; and an unreadable style-rules record returns an actionable failure instead of None, which previously meant 'no rules configured' and silently fell back to code defaults for every bulletin. Bounds: a MINIMUM CRON INTERVAL of 2 minutes, measured by walking real occurrences through the Cronos parser rather than pattern-matching the minute field; schedule Name/Station capped at 120; Unicode control/format characters refused in operator-authored single-line names via a shared OperatorTextGuard; /synthesize script capped at 5,000 characters; FlowTier defaulting to 'none' across all three routes with unrecognised tier strings rejected instead of coerced. Config export/import gained VerifiedPronunciations, OperatorAssignments and VoiceCalibrations. Job.Approve now requires WaitingApproval or FallbackUsed, and the ScriptOnly path transitions through WaitingApproval explicitly rather than relying on the weak guard.

**Rationale:** The cron floor is the decision worth recording. It was drafted at 5 minutes on the explicit advice that 'no plausible real schedule comes near it, so it only ever catches a typo'. That advice was WRONG, and a live export/import round-trip against dev proved it: adelaide's compound expression fires 15:59 then 16:02 - a real 3-minute gap around a news break - so a 5-minute floor would have rejected adelaide's live programming on its next save. The error came from reading the individual cron LINES rather than the compound expression they combine into; a compound cron's firing rate is a property of the whole expression. Measured across every dev schedule the tightest real gap is 3 minutes (adelaide), next is perth at 8, and the rest are 10-15. The floor is therefore 2: it still refuses every-minute (the actual typo risk, ~19,000 generations a day across 13 markets) while preserving every real schedule with headroom. adelaide's verbatim compound cron is now a regression test. On fail-closed scoping: not knowing someone's scope is not the same as them having none, and widening access is the wrong way to resolve the difference; but the opt-in policy (no assignment row = unrestricted) is a deliberate product choice and was left alone precisely because changing it would lock out the only registered dev operator. ambiguousRoads was deliberately NOT added to config transfer: it has zero code references in src/ or web/src and the per-market disambiguation feature (WALK3-002) is still unbuilt, so exporting it would mean inventing a model for a table nothing reads.

**Consequences:** 3,700+ backend tests and 674 frontend tests pass; build is 0 warnings with TreatWarningsAsErrors; eslint, prettier, tsc, bicep lint, gitleaks and the web perf budget all pass; ./scripts/verify.sh green on three consecutive full runs including the backend E2E lane. Every new guard was proven to FAIL when reverted, at the real call site: the cron floor (5 tests), blank/oversized/control-char fields (7), body MarketId (1), unknown FlowTier and U+202E road names (4, HTTP and import), the script cap (1), the unconfigured-market flag (1), the auth bypass (3), and the round-trip idempotency invariant (1). Verified live on dev after deploy: every-minute and */1 crons are refused while */2, */5 and adelaide's real 45-line compound expression are accepted; clearing Name or Station returns 400 while an omitted field still leaves the stored value intact; a body MarketId of 'sydney' against /schedules/zz-wave2 is refused and a matching one is accepted; a 121-character name and a U+202E name are refused at 120 and 0 respectively; FlowTier 'BOGUS' returns the valid-values list and an omitted tier now stores 'none' (previously 'high'); a 5,001-character script is refused and 5,000 succeeds; Location 'Sydnye' returns 202 with a Warning and a Warn-level job log while 'melbourne' returns neither; approving a Published/Approved/Rejected job returns 409 with the settled-status message while a WaitingApproval job still approves; and export now carries 12 sections with the round trip reporting 118 Unchanged and 0 errors. Regression sweep: anonymous callers still get 401, all 12 read endpoints 200, priority-road and dictionary write round-trips work, deleting an unassigned dictionary is not over-blocked, and a full bulletin still generates end to end (WAITING_APPROVAL with audio in ~66s). Dev state restored and re-verified on 8 integrity checks. Three more permissive test doubles were found and fixed while doing this: ScheduleServiceTests' cron substitute returned a constant next-run (making any interval rule untestable), ScheduleHttpTriggerTests stubbed ICronParser entirely (so no cron rule was exercised at the HTTP layer), and ConfigImportServiceTests' FakeCronParser stubbed CalculateNextRun to a fixed +30 minutes. All three now delegate to the real Cronos-backed parser. Three E2E fixtures used '* * * * *' as a convenience cron and were corrected; the one that needs the poller to fire uses '*/5' with the 15-minute lead time. Still open by design: #20 prompt-injection sanitising (the U+202E guard incidentally blocks the newline vector for names, but not the broader case), #21 un-approve, #34 mixed time formats, and #6 dev anonymous access itself - /api/config/export (77KB) and /api/operators remain anonymously readable on the dev SWA hostname at ARN's direction. One item shipped WITHOUT an automated test: the unreadable style-rules failure (#11) cannot be exercised without corrupting the live singleton, and the list-shaped libraries were deliberately left returning None for an unreadable row because making GetAsync fail there would render a corrupt item undeletable - a worse failure mode than the one being fixed.

## 2026-07-29 — Frontend bug hunt: fix nine UI defects, three of them silent data loss

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A UI bug hunt (axe already clean at 0 violations across 26 targets, so the pass targeted behaviour) found nine real defects via knip, the audit corpus and five reviewer agents, each then re-verified by the lead agent. Three were reproduced live in a browser. The worst: in interval mode the Start/End time inputs carry no step, ScheduleFormSchema never checked that minutes were :00, so an off-the-hour time like 06:15 validated fine, buildCronFromCalendar returned a null cron, handleSubmit toasted and RETURNED, and because ScheduleStudio.handleSave only keeps the studio open when onSubmit REJECTS, the dialog closed exactly as it does on success while zero requests were sent - discarding the operator edit across every step.

**Decision:** Validate cron expressibility by CALLING buildCronFromCalendar from ScheduleFormSchema.superRefine rather than restating its rules, and make use-schedule-actions THROW on a null cron so the studio cannot close on a no-op save. useStyleRulesEditor.handleRestore now calls setRules with the restored rules: setting loadedVersion alone made the sync effect guard match on refetch, so the editor kept the pre-restore draft and the next Save wrote it back over the restore. VoiceWindowSchema gained extraVoiceProfileIds so window voice ids the editor cannot show round-trip instead of being deleted by a whole-policy replace PUT; picking a voice clears them, which is explicit. regenerate() tracks whether the reject committed and says so, because JobService.cs:592 OnlyRejectedCanRegenerate means reject-first is mandatory and cannot be reordered or undone. The three gallery pages open the studio for a new ?open= id instead of only stripping it. The audio player stopPropagation()s keys it handles and resets isPlaying/currentTime when the blob path changes. PendingConfigImportApiSchema.Report is nullable, mirroring PendingConfigImportDto.Report, and the card shows a query error instead of an empty list. Voice duplicate sends paceBoostWpm. One shared createWindowId in day-track.ts.

**Rationale:** Two rules came out of this. First, a submit path must FAIL LOUDLY: a handler that returns normally after declining to act is indistinguishable from success to any caller that closes on resolve, which is how a total edit loss looked like a save. Second, validate by calling the producer, not by copying its rules - restating the :00-minute and start<end constraints in zod would have drifted from the cron builder on the next change. Reject-then-regenerate was deliberately NOT reordered: the backend only regenerates a REJECTED or FAILED job, so the pair is ordered by contract; the honest fix is to name the half-completed state and leave feedback uncleared so the retry (which now skips the reject, the job already being REJECTED) resends it. The multi-voice truncation was graded latent, not active: no window-level multi-id exists in current fixtures, so it is reachable only via a config-transfer import or a direct API write - but the frontend was still contradicting a backend model that takes a list per window.

**Consequences:** tsc, eslint, oxlint, prettier and vite build all clean; 674 frontend tests pass; knip no longer reports the two dead version-restore path exports. Each browser-proven bug was re-proven fixed against the live mock server: 06:15 now disables Save and flags the Schedule step (was: enabled, no error, dialog closed, no request); the command palette opens the studio while already on /voices (was: nothing); k no longer navigates the queue (was: /jobs/arn-job-00007 to /jobs/287d14a0); playing then switching jobs via the in-app j shortcut leaves the player on Play at 0:00 with the new duration (was: stuck on Pause with the karaoke highlight pinned to word zero); and restoring a populated style-rules version loads its 8 rules into the editor.
