Sending both parameters makes the latency fix effective at the API boundary without changing the backend contract or removing operators' ability to browse older jobs in History. A 500-row cap remains bounded even if a market exceeds the expected daily volume.

**Consequences:** On-air, Home, active-shell, and earlier-today surfaces now load only recent jobs and no longer scan the full table. History can still page backward beyond 24 hours. The UI adds one bounded request parameter pair to ordinary jobs polling; the focused frontend regression test asserts the status, 24-hour from window, and limit=500.

## 2026-08-20 — Event Ledger reads only its existing 30-day fold window

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Event Ledger already discarded jobs older than 30 days after loading them, but EventLedgerService.ListRecentJobsAsync called the unbounded IJobRepository.ListJobsAsync first. GET /ledger/{market} and GET /jobs/{id}/delta therefore scanned the entire radioJobs table on each cache miss, despite the fold's fixed time window.

**Decision:** Page through IJobRepository.ListJobsPageAsync using LastUpdatedAt between now minus FoldWindow and now, with a 500-row page size and the existing composite timestamp/row-key cursor. Preserve the existing CreatedAt-based 30-day cutoff after each page, and retain the 45-second shared cache.

**Rationale:** The repository already has the correct bounded storage query and cursor semantics for newest-first windows. Reusing it removes the full-table scan without changing the folded event set, cache behavior, API shape, or the older-job semantics of the ledger.

**Consequences:** Ledger and job-delta reads now issue bounded time-window queries and can span multiple pages when a market has more than 500 recent updates. The existing unbounded job-list overload remains available to watchdog paths whose correctness requires seeing all active statuses. Added an application regression test proving the 30-day bounds, 500-row paging, cursor advance, and absence of the unbounded repository call.

## 2026-08-20 — Test airs for real too, and playout arming becomes a per-station switch

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A large batch of changes is ready and production must NOT receive them: production is to stay frozen at the last known-good build as the fallback, while operators still get an environment carrying the new code that can air for a real pilot station. Networking was never the obstacle — since 2026-07-24 delivery is Files REST over OAuth on 443 with the Function App's managed identity, so nothing reaches into ARN's network, and `roles-delivery-drop.bicep` already grants both slot identities Storage Blob Data Contributor + Storage File Data Privileged Contributor at ACCOUNT scope on `ibpauetststaftp01`. Test's `rgStorageName` IS `IBP-AUE-TST-RSG-STA01`, where the drop account lives, so test could already write the live share; only two app settings held it back. The real obstacle is the file name: ARN playout's 2026-07-30 convention is one file per station, same name every time, at the share root, and he DECLINED a separate test folder because his autoloader wildcard-matches per market. Two environments delivering the same station therefore write the identical path, and Zetta returns no on-air receipt, so nobody could audit which environment aired.

**Decision:** Two changes, together. (1) `main.test.bicepparam` sets `zettaEnabled = true` and `zettaDropFileShareName = 'informationbulletins'` — the live share. `main.prod.bicepparam` is NOT touched, and no code or config is deployed to production. The isolated `informationbulletins-test` share still exists and the autoloader still does not watch it; test simply no longer writes there. (2) `MarketSchedule.PlayoutEnabled`, a per-station arming switch surfaced as **Send to playout** on the station cards, the station table (its own sortable column) and the station-editor footer. `JobService.PublishJobAsync` checks it before the delivery call and returns the new `FileDeliveryStatus.SkippedStationDisabled`, logging "Send to playout is off for this station" instead of claiming delivery. Delivery now needs BOTH gates: the environment-wide `Zetta:Enabled` and the station's own flag. The flag defaults TRUE and an absent Table column rehydrates as true (`bool?` on the entity, `?? true` in the mapper), because every station that predates the flag was airing. It fails OPEN if the schedule row cannot be read. `ConfigScheduleDto.PlayoutEnabled` is optional and absent means "leave arming alone", so promoting a config bundle between environments cannot re-arm or disarm a station.

**Rationale:** Arming had to be a runtime, operator-editable switch rather than IaC, because the whole point is that ARN operators move a station between environments unattended while the author is on leave — the poller's own query is `PartitionKey eq '<pk>' and Enabled eq true`, so pausing was already runtime, and arming belongs at the same level. It had to be SEPARATE from `Enabled`: pausing stops a station generating, which is not what "don't air from here" means — the held-back environment must keep generating so an operator can compare the two and switch. Defaulting to false would have been the "safe" reading and was rejected: it would have silently taken both live pilot stations off air the moment the build deployed, which is a worse failure than an over-armed station, and the honest guard against over-arming is that the operator sees the state on every card. The per-station gate is what makes enabling test acceptable at all — without it, arming test would have meant every test publish racing production for the same file.

**Consequences:** Test stops being a place where a broken scenario is harmless: a publish in test for a station armed in test reaches that station's live library. The UAT documents that promised otherwise were corrected in the same change (`uat-plan.md`, `uat-scenario-sheet.md`, `integration-test-plan.md`, `handover-handout.md`, `dependencies.md`, `production-readiness.md`, `deployment/README.md` — whose playout section was ALSO stale, still claiming production was pinned false after the 13 Aug re-enable — and task-board A4, now closed). Markets other than the two pilot stations still cannot reach playout from any environment: they have no code in `zettaMarketCodesJson`, and delivery fails loudly rather than inventing a name. A duplicated station starts both paused and held back. New tests: 3 domain (armed by default on Create AND Rehydrate; holding playout back does not pause; omitting it leaves arming untouched), 3 application (held back publishes without touching the share and logs the station-specific line; armed delivers; unreadable schedule still delivers), 3 web (each switch acts on its own row, the playout switch does not fire the pause handler, a held-back station reads Off without reading Paused). Solution builds 0 warnings / 0 errors; Domain 2137, Application 863, Functions 819, Architecture 14 green; web 1219 Vitest green, tsc clean. Verified in the browser on the mock build: both switches carry distinct accessible names, a click flips the copy to "Off — generates and publishes, nothing reaches playout", and the change round-trips through PUT → store → GET (toggled in the cards view, read back Off in the table view). NOT done here and deliberately separate: nothing is deployed. Deploying test, re-truing its crons from the UAT grid to the ATN clock, and arming the first station are operator/deploy steps.

**Dev/no-playout environments (found by asking what this does on dev, before deploying):** dev sets NO zetta params, so it inherits `zettaEnabled = false`, and `DeliverAsync` checks that gate FIRST — before the deadline, the download and the market-code resolution. Delivery behaviour on dev is therefore completely unchanged: every publish still ends `SkippedDisabled` with the same "disabled in this environment" log. But because the station flag defaults to ARMED, all 14 dev stations would have rendered "On — a published bulletin reaches playout" on an environment that has never been able to deliver — a false statement about what a publish does, and the same inert-control/false-copy class the 2026-08-10 UI feature audit caught. Fixed by teaching the console the environment gate: `GET /api/map-config` (already the authenticated client-runtime-config endpoint, per `paths.ts`) now also returns `PlayoutEnabled` = `ZettaOptions.Enabled`, and the station card and table read it. When the environment cannot deliver the card reads "This environment never sends to playout" and the table cell reads "Env off" with a title, in warning colour, for every station regardless of its own flag. Absent in the response reads as enabled, so a console against an older backend keeps its previous behaviour rather than newly claiming playout is off. The switch stays EDITABLE there on purpose — never take away an operator's ability to set config, just stop the UI lying about the effect. Verified in the browser against a mock reporting `PlayoutEnabled: false`: 14 cards, zero occurrences of "a published bulletin reaches playout", switch still editable; and restored to `true`, the per-station copy returns. +1 Functions theory (both gate values) and +1 web test pin it.

**Deployed to DEV 2026-08-20 and verified live (nothing deployed to test or production).** Code + SWA only via `deploy.sh --skip-infra`: dev needed no infra change, `Zetta__Enabled=false` and the other `Zetta__*` settings already existed, and skipping infra also avoided applying unrelated in-flight Bicep edits. 134 functions loaded (expected 134 — this change adds no function), all Key Vault references resolved, `/api/health` 200 on every check. Evidence, in order: `GET /api/map-config` returns `{"HereApiKey":"","PlayoutEnabled":false}`; all 15 dev stations return `PlayoutEnabled: true` from Table rows that have NO such column, proving the absent-column default against real storage; `PUT /schedules/adelaide {"PlayoutEnabled": false}` persisted and left every other field intact (Enabled, duration, voice profile, the 44-line cron). **Both delivery branches were then proven with real bulletins generated end to end on dev (HERE + Azure OpenAI + ElevenLabs, 30.0s each).** Held back — job `6e0808d1d43a4e61b395dc9286c521d8`: PUBLISHED, log `Send to playout is off for this station — audio retained in storage, not sent to playout`. Re-armed — job `2e200b0d0d764a209812f1c6247e35e1`: PUBLISHED, log `Playout delivery is disabled in this environment — audio retained in storage, not sent to playout`, i.e. the pre-existing environment path is untouched and the two skips are distinguishable in the audit log. On the deployed console: 15 station cards, 15 "This environment never sends to playout", ZERO "a published bulletin reaches playout"; the table's new Playout column reads "Env off" per row; clicking the switch wrote through the deployed SWA to the deployed API to real storage (adelaide flipped, toast "Send to playout off — this station will not reach playout from here"). Dev was returned to the state it was found in: all 15 stations armed, `cairns-4ca`/`sydney`/`test` the only enabled schedules. Note for scripted callers: approve/publish take the revision token in the BODY as `ExpectedEtag` (an `If-Match` header is ignored and returns 428), and the job GET exposes it as `Etag`, not `ETag`.

**PROVEN ON TEST 2026-08-20 against a REAL delivery-enabled environment, with nothing reaching Zetta (production untouched throughout).** Dev could not prove the armed branch — its environment gate masks the station gate — so test was deployed with `zettaEnabled = true` but `zettaDropFileShareName` TEMPORARILY pointed at `informationbulletins-test`, the sibling share ARN's autoloader does not watch. Everything else was real and identical to production: same drop account, same managed identity and Files-REST-over-OAuth write, same `{MarketId}_TRAFF` pattern, and test carries prod's own market codes (`[SYD]KIIS90s`, `[CAI]STAR1027`). Pre-flight: `what-if` showed 0 Deletes and 1 additive Create (`sourceParseReports` table, from already-deployed multi-source code), both test schedules were DISABLED so no poller could fire, and both shares were empty. Deploy: 134 functions (matching dev), all Key Vault references resolved, health 200.

Both test stations `PlayoutEnabled = false` and their schedules still disabled, set BEFORE test was pointed back at the live share, so no publish path could write during the change window. `zettaDropFileShareName` restored to `informationbulletins` in IaC and applied by an infra-only redeploy (never `az ... appsettings set` — QT-001). Test is now one operator toggle from airing, and cannot air until someone makes it.

One delivery, one file, isolated share, matching timestamps. (Unrelated pre-existing artifact, NOT from this work: the `informationbulletins` BLOB container still holds `SYD_TRAIN_TRAFF.wav` from 2026-07-19, the BlobDrop/SFTP trial, under the pre-convention file name.)

Three independent reasons it is not a risk: the test MI's grants are at **ACCOUNT** scope (`az role assignment list --scope <account>` confirms `Storage File Data Privileged Contributor` on `ibpauetststaftp01`, not on a share), so the share name is not an authorization boundary; the identical identity, `ShareClient`, `ShareTokenIntent.Backup` and `GetRootDirectoryClient()` path just performed a successful READ against that exact live share (`GET /markets/{m}/playout-tray` → 200, `enabled:true`, resolving `[SYD]KIIS90s_TRAFF.wav` and `[CAI]STAR1027_TRAFF.wav`); and production's own MI has written that share repeatedly (30 Jul, 11-12 Aug) through the same code.
