Fading the audio's own tail is correct for both outcomes and removes the case analysis that produced the bug. This also closes the gap left by TrimAfterSpeech being conditional: the retime is the last stage to touch the tail and the only one guaranteed to run, so it is the right place for the guarantee. Deliberately NOT addressed here: the alignment-absent branch also skips trailing-inhale removal, so eleven_v3's appended breath gets compressed into the read rather than cut - a quality issue on the same branch, not this defect.

**Consequences:** Verified live on test job d054b415 via the scheduled poller, on the SAME branch that produced the fault (trace: TrimTail 22.720->22.718, AdjustSpeed 22.718->22.000, no TrimAfterSpeech). Last non-zero sample went -283 -> -1 and peak in the final 2ms 1100 -> 32 against an unchanged body peak of 27571, with 'by' still ending at 22.000. Deployed to dev and test. Backend suites green: Application 879, Domain 2254, Functions 834, Architecture 14, Infrastructure 1554 passed against its 5 pre-existing failures. SEPARATE UNFIXED FINDING: job 23b9bb1c's record references a blob named after a different job - jobs/23b9bb1c.../audio/broadcast_20260824_043528_c372df81....wav - and both jobs converged on an identical script. Two concurrent sydney jobs (the 04:31 scheduled one and c372df81 from a poller trigger) appear to have cross-contaminated. Not investigated.

## 2026-08-24 — The script editor's mirror is one metric-neutral text flow, so the caret cannot drift

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The edit-script mirror (PronunciationScriptEditor) painted the draft as one flex row per sentence with min-h-7 (28px) while the text ran at leading-relaxed on text-base (26px). Every visual line therefore pushed the mirror 2px below the transparent textarea it sits on, and the offset accumulated: measured by overlaying the textarea's own glyphs in red under the mirror's in blue, an eight-short-sentence draft had the caret sitting ~14px - half a line - above the words the operator was reading. Horizontally the same class of defect was latent: ScriptWordMark carries px-0.5, and inline padding adds 4px of advance width, so every glyph after a marked word (e.g. the Sydney dictionary's Warringah) sat right of its caret. The per-line rows existed only to host a lineGutter prop that no caller had ever passed.

**Decision:** The mirror is now a single whitespace-pre-wrap, wrap-break-word block rendering one flat run of inline nodes over the whole draft - newlines included - and marks inside it get -mx-0.5 to give back their padding. The dead lineGutter prop, its pr-[8.25rem] textarea reservation, the per-line EditorLine machinery and the redundant rows attribute are gone. ReviewScript.test.tsx now asserts the invariant that actually matters: the mirror's textContent equals the textarea's value.

**Rationale:** Line boxes were the only thing that could accumulate an offset, so deleting them removes the defect class rather than tuning min-h-7 to match a line-height that any future type change would break again. wrap-break-word is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a textarea breaks an over-long token mid-word by UA rule and a plain div does not. The rule for anything painted in the mirror is now stated once, at the renderer: colours and backgrounds only, never padding, font size or margin.

**Consequences:** Verified in the mock app by rendering both layers in opposing colours: the eight-short-line case and a draft carrying tags plus a Warringah mark both overlay with no fringe, and the mark's respell popover still opens on hover. Same pass cleaned the edit toolbar: the 'cannot use delivery tones' paragraph became a labelled warning icon in the space the mode toggle occupies, the tone palette's redundant 'Inserts at the cursor.' span folded into its InfoHint, and ScriptAssist's aria-describedby no longer points at a hint node that only the content mode renders. arn-job-00007 now carries the Sydney Roads dictionary it would really have, so the mock corpus finally exercises the in-script mark path. web suite 1258 passed, eslint and Tailwind conformance clean.

## 2026-08-24 — Trigger now reaches the Operator, closing the last stale isAdmin gate over a market-scoped route

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked why the operator console has no "Trigger now" button in the test environment. Nothing about it was environment-specific. POST /api/broadcast became market-scoped Operator on 2026-08-13 (RouteRoleMatrix; BroadcastHttpTrigger resolves a canonical MarketId then runs EnsureMarketAccessAsync BEFORE CreateJobAsync, so a refused caller leaves no job behind), but StationProfileCard.tsx and StationProfileTable.tsx still withheld the control behind useIsAdmin, carrying a comment that read "Trigger now (POST /broadcast), Duplicate and Delete are Admin-only server-side". That comment was accurate when written on 2026-08-11, when the route WAS Admin and market-unguarded, and was never revisited when the grant landed two days later. Dev cannot show the divergence: Auth__DevFallbackRole=Admin plus the built-in SWA provider make useIsAdmin() true for every authenticated dev caller, so the button appeared for everyone. On test and prod, which forward real Entra app roles through the custom provider, an Operator saw a station they may edit, publish for and approve bulletins on, but could never generate one for. This is the third instance of the same class after bookends (2026-08-13) and POST /jobs/{id}/rewrite (2026-08-13): a frontend role gate outliving the backend grant it mirrored.

**Decision:** Removed the useIsAdmin gate from "Trigger now" in both StationProfileCard (footer button) and StationProfileTable (row actions menu), leaving Duplicate and Delete Admin-only in both. Nothing else changed, because the market boundary was already built: useScopedSchedules partitions stations by the operator scope, StationProfileCards renders the remainder under an "Outside your markets" heading, and every out-of-scope card and row already desaturates and disables its actions, so an operator is offered a trigger only where EnsureMarketAccessAsync would allow it. Corrected the stale comment in both components, and the AuthorizationMiddleware class doc, which still listed "trigger ad-hoc broadcasts" as an Admin-only power; it now describes Operator as everything market- or job-scoped plus shared speech-library curation, and Admin as the unscopable surfaces plus every DELETE. Corrected three ARN-facing docs that told operators the control was withheld: operator-guide.md, first-time-sign-in.md role table, functionality-catalog.md 5.2.

**Rationale:** The trust boundary that makes this safe is the market guard, not the role, which is the same reasoning that moved publish, retone and audition to the Operator on 2026-08-05 and PUT /api/schedules/{marketId} later. Withholding a control whose backend route is Operator is the exact inverse of the 2026-08-05 bug bash finding 9, where Rewrite and Audition rendered against Admin routes and 403d: an affordance that always fails is bad, and an affordance that is silently withheld despite being permitted is equally bad, because the operator concludes the platform cannot do it. Triggering also pairs with the publish grant, which otherwise lets an operator put a bulletin to air but never make one. Duplicate and Delete stay Admin for the reason they always did: standing a station up is an onboarding act and deleting one stops its automatic bulletins with no undo.

**Consequences:** A scoped Operator can now generate an ad-hoc bulletin for an assigned station, and an unscoped Operator for any station, which is consistent with their existing ability to act on any job. Six regression tests lock the operator path across the card and the table (Trigger now present and dispatching the right marketId, disabled with "Outside your assigned markets" on an out-of-scope station, Duplicate and Delete still absent); five of the six were proven to FAIL with the isAdmin gate reinstated. Dev cannot verify this - the dev fallback makes every caller Admin - so it was proven against the mock build with VITE_DEV_USER_ROLES=operator: 15 station cards each offering Trigger now, no "New station", the row menu reading View details / Trigger now / Edit with no Duplicate or Delete, and a full trigger through the studio (voice, coverage, content toggles) returning a "Bulletin triggered" toast. Re-checked with VITE_DEV_USER_ROLES=admin: 15 triggers, New station present, the full five-item menu intact. Test and prod behaviour follows from the same code once deployed; confirm on test with a real Operator-role account after the next release. Two environment problems were found and are NOT fixed by this change: /tmp is mounted usrquota and the 13 GB /tmp/arn-vanilla scratch checkout has exhausted the quota, so every node write to /tmp fails with EDQUOT and vitest suites fail at import with "Unknown system error -122" (pre-existing; reproduced at HEAD without these changes); and ~/.local/share/ngrep/shims precedes /usr/bin in PATH, so verify.sh internal grep calls return semantic-search output instead of grep results and every lane log is replaced by an ngrep result dump, which manufactures bogus gate failures.

## 2026-08-24 — Dropping a sentence must clear the back-reference it orphans

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked why dev job 54befeec (Cairns, 2026-08-24) opened 'Checking out the roads... Roadworks are ALSO slowing the Bruce Highway at Edmonton and Gordonvale' - an additive connective in the first thing said about the roads. The draft was CORRECT: Captain Cook Highway roadworks were sentence one and the Bruce Highway sentence genuinely added to them. Review then proved the Captain Cook claim unsupported ('major delays' against supplied moderate), its sentence-scoped refine cited an unsupplied evidence id (r5:direction), and ScriptReviewLoop dropped the sentence rather than ship a claim review had disproven. The right call - but the drop promoted the next sentence and left its back-reference pointing at a sentence that no longer existed. Every surviving sentence was individually clean and individually grounded; only their ORDER made one of them wrong, which is precisely what a per-sentence gate cannot see.

**Decision:** Added OrphanedConnectiveDetector (Domain/Services/Detectors): finds the first sentence that names a road the market's own data carries - skipping the LLM-written opener, which names no road, and weather/fuel lines - and flags an additive connective in it ('also', 'as well', a leading 'Meanwhile,'/'Elsewhere,'). Unlike ConnectorFrequencyDetector's contrast connectors this is repairable, because each shape is a pure DELETION that leaves grammatical prose and changes no claim. Both sentence-drop sites in ScriptReviewLoop now route through one new helper, RepairAfterDrop, which re-splices required fixtures AND clears the orphaned back-reference, so the two sites cannot drift apart; the job log names whichever repair fired.

**Rationale:** The connective is only wrong relative to what precedes it, so the check belongs on the assembled read after a sentence is removed - the same positional reasoning as SectionOrderDetector. Anchoring 'first claim' to road names from context.Corridors (via the same whole-word test SectionOrderDetector uses) avoids having to classify the opener heuristically, and makes the gate silent by construction on reads that name no known road. Deletion-only repair means no LLM round-trip and no risk of altering a fact.

**Consequences:** Domain suites 2254 -> 2262; the new tests replay the aired Cairns read verbatim and pin the negative cases: a legitimate 'also' after a real prior claim is untouched, weather/fuel ahead of the claim do NOT count as prior items, and a read naming no known road is left alone. Application 879, Functions 834, Architecture 14 green; Infrastructure at its 5 pre-existing failures. NOTE on process: an earlier 'clean build' in this session was a FALSE NEGATIVE - the workstation had exhausted swap and csc was dying with SIGBUS (exit 135), so dotnet build printed no errors while compiling nothing. Two real compile errors surfaced only after freeing memory and pointing TMPDIR off the full tmpfs. Treat a build that prints neither errors nor a 'X -> path.dll' line as not having run.

## 2026-08-24 — The script editor is one frame: tool rail, script, measure rail

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Edit mode stacked three separately bordered blocks - a headed 'Ask for a change' card, the editor box, then a loose word counter - plus a fourth hairline above the action buttons. ARN read the assist card as bolted on, and it was: the operator had to cross a border to connect the instruction they typed with the script it rewrites. The card also carried a permanent paragraph ('Changes what the bulletin says. Checked against this bulletin's evidence before you see it.') duplicating the InfoHint beside its own heading, and a second InfoHint sat on the tone palette one row below.

**Decision:** ReviewScript now owns ONE bordered surface in edit mode: an h-8 tool rail across the top (lever toggle or the withheld-tone warning icon, the instruction field, Rewrite, then the caller's tone palette and a single help hint), the frameless script in the middle, and a measure rail at the bottom (word count, slot fit, pronunciation-version warning). ScriptAssist renders as that rail rather than a section with its own heading, border and background, and takes a `trailing` slot so the caller's manual tools land on the same line. PronunciationScriptEditor is deliberately frameless - textarea and mirror both border-0 - and the frame carries the script's focus indication via `has-[textarea:focus]`, deliberately NOT `focus-within` (typing an instruction would light the whole surface) and NOT `:focus-visible` (Chromium withholds it from a programmatically focused textarea, which is exactly how edit mode opens). The permanent hint paragraph, its dead ModeSpec field, the second InfoHint and the duplicate hairline above the buttons are gone.

**Rationale:** A toolbar is what this always was - a tool pointed at the text directly below it - and the repo's own convention for a toolbar that feels misplaced is to relocate it to sit with the content it acts on. Merging the two help hints follows from the merge: 'how do I change this script?' is one question, and the answer covers both levers and the manual tag. Where a paragraph and a tooltip said the same thing, the tooltip won, because the rail has to stay one line tall.

**Consequences:** Verified in the mock app against real computed geometry, not screenshots: textarea and mirror rects identical to 2dp (429.33/439.33/534.67/224) with padding 8/12 and border 0 on both, mirror textContent equal to the textarea value, the eight-short-line overlay still fringe-free, and the rail wrapping to three rows at a 390px viewport with zero horizontal overflow. Frame border measured as ring/70 with the caret in the script and neutral with the caret in the instruction field (measured with CDP focus emulation on - an unfocused tab never matches `:focus`, so the naive check reads as a false negative). SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED in the same pass: the editor's autosize depended on `value` alone, so a width change never refit it - once the evidence rail mounted beside the script the box sat at 224px holding 276px of text and silently clipped the last line behind the frame. A width-only ResizeObserver now refits it; measured 703px/224, 595px/224, 535px/276, never clipped. web suite 1264 passed, eslint and Tailwind conformance clean.

## 2026-08-24 — Citations must be zipped against the SELECTOR's item order, not the draft's

**Status:** accepted — hotfixed to dev + test 2026-08-24 05:58Z

**Context:** Dev and test both stopped producing usable bulletins during the afternoon pilot session.
Symptoms: every generation attempt burned the full 4-attempt budget, jobs took 120-150s instead of
~50s, the review agent fired on every read where it had previously passed first time, and reads
collapsed to a single item plus filler or failed outright (test `b0dc8785` MISSED, `efb219ba`
FAILED; dev `cb5ada8a` Failed after 33 LLM calls / 70,045 tokens / 103s of model time). Onset was
sharp — test had 0 grounding failures across the 11 jobs before 04:52 and failures on essentially
every job after. A rollback of BOTH environments to clean `HEAD` (7a45c230) did **not** clear it,
which ruled out the day's in-flight deploys; `check-foundry-agent-drift.sh` reported all 8 role
agents matching git in both environments, which ruled out prompt drift.

**Root cause:** `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator.GenerateScriptAsync` zipped the selector's chosen
variants against `parsedItems` — the RAW draft order. `SelectOptimalCombination` re-orders its input
first (`EffectiveItemOrder` = `DedupeSameEvidence` then `LeadWithTheWorstDisruption`) and returns one
variant per item **in that order**. Whenever the draft's own order was not already worst-first, every
sentence was therefore emitted carrying a DIFFERENT item's `evidenceIds`. Proven from dev
`cb5ada8a`'s own captures: the draft cited correctly (`r4`→M5 Milperra, `r3`→M4 Homebush, `r5`→
Mitchell Road closure), but the sentence reaching RefineSentence as order 1 was Mitchell Road's text
carrying `r4`. Review and the grounding gate then correctly rejected it; refine failed on the
unsupplied ids, the sentence was dropped, and the read collapsed. Latent since the selector gained
re-ordering — it only bites when the draft's order differs from worst-first, which is why it
surfaced when the incident mix thickened at afternoon peak, on both environments at once.

**Decision:** Derive `orderedItems = EffectiveItemOrder(parsedItems)` in the caller and zip the
selected variants against that. `EffectiveItemOrder` is pure and deterministic, so re-deriving it
returns exactly the list the selector worked on. The assembled read itself was already correct — only
the citation map was crossed.

**Rationale:** The alignment contract belongs where the two lists meet. The selector's own tests
already knew the order changes (`StructuredMatrixSelectorTests.Score` re-derives `EffectiveItemOrder`
before scoring); only the production caller did not.

**Consequences:** Verified three ways. (1) `CitationAlignmentTests` drives the generator with a draft
whose closure sits second — passes with the fix, and without it fails with the exact production
symptom ("Mamre Road ... must carry its OWN evidence"). (2) Fixture replay of the real failing dev
payload (`test/corpus/regressions/citation-crossing.json`, built from `cb5ada8a`): the aired read was
one item plus filler; the replay under the fix produced seven correctly-grounded items (Mitchell
Road, Sir Reginald Ansett Drive, Lyons Road crash, Mamre Road, Church Street, Warringah Freeway,
Dacey Avenue). (3) Live after deploy: dev `63684f38` and test `ba29989a` both 1 attempt, 40-75s,
22.0s, 0-1 grounding flags, against 4 attempts / 120-150s / 9-12 flags immediately before.
Suites: Domain 2251, Application 874, Functions 832, Infrastructure 1566 (the same 5 pre-existing
failures reproduce with this change stashed).

**Both environments now run clean `HEAD` + this fix only.** The day's other in-flight backend work is
deliberately NOT on them — including the station-line trim holdback, so the KIIS closer can again be
trimmed on a `prosody-trim` read. That trade was taken knowingly: a missing closer is cosmetic, a
collapsed or failed bulletin is not. Re-landing that work should ride with its own deploy once
committed, and note it also carried the `trimOvershot` tightening that took test's content-limited
failure rate from 0/15 to 4/11 (one MISSED slot) — that threshold (0.3s, inside eleven_v3's own
render variance) wants re-tuning before it goes back.

**Adjacent defect seen and NOT fixed:** test `ba29989a` voiced Mitchell Road twice in one read.
`DedupeSameEvidence` keys on the exact evidence-id set, so two items about one road with different id
sets both survive. Separate from this incident.

## 2026-08-24 — Drive times moved to Adjust: Sources is the non-traffic panel

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The `Drive times` card added to `ReviewSources` on 23 Aug was the fourth part of the
monitored-route fix (test job cb5eadd4 aired a correct, HERE-measured M4 drive time that the console
flagged "No source found. Verify manually."). Challenged on placement, and the panel's own doc
comment settles it: Sources exists to verify every **non-traffic** claim — weather, fuel, good runs —
"the same role the incident index plays for corridors". A drive time IS traffic. Landing it there
required rewording that purpose from "besides traffic" to "besides incident traffic", which is the
tell that it never belonged.

**Decision:** `ReviewSources` reverted to its pre-`25ece3fa` state (an exact −79/+9 inverse; that
commit's only change to the file was this feature). New `DriveTimesCard` on the ADJUST surface, in
the left column above `RundownTable` — market-level measured facts above per-road detail. Read-only
and deliberately compact: a monitored route is configured per station, not curated per bulletin, so
unlike every row in the rundown beside it there is nothing to toggle or reorder, and a run two
minutes off its usual does not warrant hero numerals. Not folded INTO `RundownTable`, which is a
drag-to-reorder, toggle-per-row table; non-interactive rows inside it would be the only ones that
do nothing.

**Rationale:** Two surfaces, two jobs: Review is for reading and deciding, Adjust is where the
measured road numbers already live (jam factors, scores, boosts). The evidence-rail alternative keeps
verification in the reading column and costs no tab switch, which is the one real argument against
this — but it puts raw per-route numerals back beside the script, which is what made the card feel
misplaced. Adjust wins on information architecture; the cost is a tab switch to check a drive-time
claim.

**Consequences:** The verdict copy had to move with it. `sentence-status.ts` marks a route-matched
sentence `sourced` with a note naming where the evidence is; leaving it as "the Sources panel" would
have had the console point an operator at figures that were no longer there — **worse than the
original defect, which at least admitted it did not know.** Now reads "in the Adjust tab", with the
`provenance.ts` contract comment corrected to match and both assertions updated.

**The test suite could not catch that.** `sentence-status.test.ts` asserts the note STRING; nothing
asserts the panel it names actually renders. The revert alone passed 1264 tests while the UI
contradicted itself. Cross-component copy references are unguarded here.

**Mock mode could not show it either.** `live-traffic.ts` (the recorded corpus) carries no
`MonitoredRoutes`, so the card had never rendered outside a deployed environment — which also made an
earlier "confirmed gone from Sources" check vacuous, since it was never there in mock. Two routes
added to the Sydney job fixture with figures mirroring a real dev reading (31/28/+3, 16/15/+1).
Verified on the Adjust tab in mock mode.

## 2026-08-24 — A re-fit must re-enter generation with the BARE body, and the duplicate-edge guard must see through delivery tags

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev + test 2026-08-24 06:37Z

**Context:** Test `b322bc0c` aired the station closer twice: "…Partly cloudy, 15 degrees. That's KIIS
traffic and weather together, powered by. That's KIIS traffic and weather together, powered by." The
job log shows the path exactly — a ceiling trim before synthesis, the trimmed read coming back at
19.8s for a 22s slot, `content-limited`, then `Generation attempt 2/4: re-fitting validated script
(extend 1/1)` with a second `Delivery style applied`.

**Root cause — two defects, and it needs both.** (1) `validatedPlain`/`validatedSynth` are documented
in `ScriptGenerationEngine` as the "PRE-BOOKEND read — the base an underrun extends and re-fits …
so a Phase-1 re-fit wraps the bare body again instead of wrapping an already-wrapped take twice",
but two sites reassign them AFTER `BulletinBookendComposer.Compose` has run (the predictive-fit trim
and the ceiling trim). So the extend base is already wrapped. (2) `Compose` calls
`StripDuplicateEdge` precisely to absorb that, and it would have: replaying the guard against the
real strings, the trailing-outro match succeeds on the plain text. It fails on the VOICED text,
because line 1240 assigns the tagged `voicedSynthScript`-derived string to the plain `script`
variable and a delivery tag on the closer breaks the token comparison.

**Decision:** (1) Peel the station's lines at the single choke point where an already-composed script
re-enters the composing path — the `preValidated` branch now runs both scripts through
`BulletinBookendComposer.StripBookendEdges`. Chosen over fixing the six assignment sites because one
of them (the predictive-fit bail at ScriptGenerationEngine:1043-1052) returns `validatedPlain` as the
SHIPPED script, where the bookends must stay. (2) `StripDuplicateEdge` now skips inline delivery-tag
tokens when matching an edge; only tag tokens are skipped, so a genuinely different tail is still
left alone, and the cut is taken at the matched run's outer boundary so a tag decorating the removed
copy goes with it.

**Rationale:** The invariant is "a body entering `Compose` carries no bookends". Enforcing it where a
composed script can re-enter is one line of defence; making the existing guard work on the voiced
form is the second. Either alone would have prevented this read, which is why both are worth having.

**Consequences:** Three new `BulletinBookendComposerTests` cases (tagged duplicate closer, tagged
duplicate intro, tagged non-matching tail left alone). With the tag filter disabled they reproduce
the defect verbatim — "Now looking over Sydney. [warmly] Now looking over Sydney. …". Suites: Domain
2265, Application 878, Functions 834, Infrastructure 1568 (the same 5 pre-existing failures).
Verified live after deploy: test `84fd759a` APPROVED, 1 attempt, 25.7s wall, 22.0s, four traffic
items and exactly one closer; test `e40de045` 1 attempt, one closer.

**Still open, separate:** dev `1c957b0c` failed content-limited with the duration model predicting
32.4s/29.2s/29.4s against measured natural reads of 19.4s/19.0s/19.4s — a ~67% over-prediction on the
boosted ARN Sarah voice. The ceiling trims a read that never needed trimming, the trimmed read
underruns by ~2.5s, and with `MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0` there is no slow-fill to close it. That is the
in-flight `trimOvershot` policy meeting a miscalibrated predictor, not this defect.

## 2026-08-24 — The Desk's omissions never took effect: one event-key space, enforced at the fetch

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN reported that Mamre Road and the Warringah Freeway aired on test job
`e3ca6840e0194cc595bcb2b8fdcfc649` despite both being Omitted on the Desk. They were not the only
ones: all seven of that job's selected incidents carried an Omitted verdict. The Desk's enforcement
path — `DeskOmissions.Apply`, called from `TrafficEvidenceBuilder.ApplyDeskOmissionsAsync` — compared
the raw `TrafficIncident.Id`, while the verdicts the Desk writes are keyed by
`EventLedgerFold.EventKey`, i.e. `SourceRecordIdentity.StableEventKey` (`here:original:{originalId}`).
Two independent mismatches: the source-qualified prefix, and HERE re-stamping `Id` on every revision.
The filter's own diagnostic proves it, on every fetch in every market:
`[DeskOmissions] sydney: 14 verdict(s), 14 omitted, 0 matching 16 fetched incident key(s)`. No
operator omission has ever kept an event off air since the feature shipped.

**Decision:** One key space, one derivation: `SourceRecordIdentity.EventKeyFor(identities, fallback)`.
The ledger fold, `IncidentStateService.StateKey` and `DeskOmissions` all route through it, and the
diagnostic log now reports keys in that same space so "0 matching" can never again mean "comparing
different things".

**Rationale:** The derivation already existed in three hand-copied places and the enforcement path was
a fourth, divergent one. A verdict is only worth anything if the thing enforcing it keys the same way
the thing recording it does, so that has to be a single function, not a convention. Matching the raw
id as a fallback was rejected: `EventKeyFor` already falls back identically on both sides for records
with no source identity, and accepting bare ids would reintroduce the cross-feed collision the
source qualifier exists to prevent.

**Consequences:** Three tests reproduce the defect verbatim when the matcher is reverted to `i.Id`:
two new `DeskOmissionsTests` cases (a HERE record revised since the verdict; an unrevised record that
must match the qualified key and NOT the bare id) and `BroadcastOrchestratorDeskOmissionTests`, whose
records now carry HERE-shaped identities — its earlier fixtures used matching bare ids on both sides,
a shape no HERE record has, which is why the seam test passed while production matched nothing.
Suites: Domain 2267, Application 878. Existing verdict rows need no migration: they were always
written in the stable-key space (`EventLedgerFold` has had one key derivation since it shipped).

**Verified live on dev**, deployed 07:32 UTC, five consecutive poller bulletins on sydney. The
`[DeskOmissions]` counter tracked the verdict store in lockstep as verdicts were set and cleared —
`2 matching` (the two pre-existing operator verdicts, Mitchell Rd and The Crescent, dropped for the
first time ever) → `3` after omitting Church St `here:original:4021163310322524631` → `4` after
omitting Wakehurst Pkwy `here:original:2943406945916533716` → back to `2` once both were cleared.
Each drop is named in the log, absent from the job's `SelectedIncidents` AND its stored pool, and the
two sibling Church St records kept airing throughout, so enforcement is per RECORD, not per road.
Clearing a verdict returned the event to the next bulletin's pool, so nothing sticks. Baseline
`4ec88e10` (pre-verdict) vs `e234aa5a`/`98921eda` (post-verdict) vs `96f906309` (cleared) are the A/B.
Not on test or prod: the fix sits in a tree carrying unrelated in-flight work.

## 2026-08-24 — The duration corpus is a maintenance task, and the shape model earns its keep over WPM

**Status:** accepted — recalibrated and deployed dev + test 2026-08-24 07:04Z

**Context:** Dev bulletins on KIIS 90s were failing `Content-limited` after burning all four
generation attempts (~150s). The ceiling gate predicted 32.4s for reads that measured 19.4s, trimmed
to the predicted rate, and the trimmed read then underran the slot with only 0.3s of silence pad to
close it. The prediction came from the `yngV6X6u…|sp0.97|pb20` calibration row — **6 samples**, the
least-sampled row in the table, with the largest residual (1.99s) and a leave-one-out MAE of 1.623s
against 0.689s for its 25-sample unboosted sibling.

**A hypothesis that was tested and REJECTED.** `PaceBoostWpm` never reaches the TTS call — it only
widens the compression ceiling and inflates the word target — so keying the calibration on it looked
like splitting the corpus along a dimension that cannot affect the natural read. Leave-one-out says
otherwise: pooling the pb0 and pb20 rows made prediction WORSE on both (pb20 1.623s → 1.743s, pb0
0.689s → 0.722s), and the harvest shows the boosted reads genuinely run at 136 wpm against 144 wpm
unboosted. The split is real and stays. Recorded because the physical argument is persuasive and
wrong, and someone will make it again.

**Decision:** Re-harvest and re-fit. `build-duration-dataset.py` + `emit-duration-calibration.py`
against dev picked up the reads generated since the corpus was last built. No logic changed and the
stage-A shape coefficients are byte-identical; only rows that gained samples moved.

| row | samples | scale | residual | LOO MAE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `yngV6X6u…` sp0.97 pb20 | 6 → 9 | 0.4376 → 0.4288 | 1.99 → 1.72 | 1.623s → **1.207s** |
| `EF2rFRNHqb…` sp0.97 pb0 | 39 → 46 | 0.4017 → 0.4000 | 1.008 → 0.968 | 0.780s → 0.756s |
| fleet, sample-weighted | | | | 0.886s → **0.867s** |

Verified live: dev `cc48efcd` and test `0818e28d`/`beb8ec5f` all shipped on ONE attempt with zero
grounding failures. On dev the allowance moved 24.6s → 24.8s, the ceiling 42 → 45 words, and the
natural read 19.4s → 21.4s — the same input that failed now fills the slot.

**Is the shape model worth it over plain WPM?** Measured, identical LOO folds, 167 predictions:

| model | MAE | p90 | bias | within 1s | over-predicts >2s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| static 150 wpm (the `legacy-150wpm` path) | 1.669s | 3.300s | −0.863 | 38% | 6% |
| per-voice WPM | 1.334s | 2.776s | −0.104 | 45% | 11% |
| per-voice syllable rate | 1.242s | 2.493s | −0.081 | 53% | — |
| per-voice character rate | 1.023s | 1.937s | −0.060 | 60% | 5% |
| shipped token-additive shape | **0.867s** | **1.734s** | −0.036 | **68%** | **5%** |

Shape beats per-voice WPM by 0.467s MAE, 95% paired-bootstrap CI [0.346, 0.587], winning on all 8
fingerprints and 65% of individual reads. Over-prediction is the dangerous direction (it over-trims
into a content-limited failure), and the severe tail halves: 11% → 5% of reads over-predicted by
more than 2s. **Keep the model.** Worth knowing though: a one-parameter per-voice CHARACTER rate
reaches 1.023s and the same 5% tail, so ten of the eleven shape coefficients buy the last 15%.

**Rationale:** The failure was a data problem, not a logic problem, and the cheapest correct response
to a badly-determined scale is more samples — not a new formula and not a tuning fudge. Measuring the
WPM alternative at the same time settles whether the model's complexity is load-bearing before anyone
proposes simplifying it away during an incident.

**Consequences:** (1) Re-harvesting is now a recurring maintenance task, not a one-off — the pb20 row
is still the weakest at 1.207s and only reaches the ~0.87s asymptote with more reads. (2) The corpus
is **dev-only**: test and prod storage are private-endpoint and unreachable from a workstation, so
the environments carrying real pilot traffic never feed the model that governs them. Harvesting from
inside the network would roughly triple it. (3) The structural limit stands — the best available
predictor has p90 1.73s while `MaxSlowDownFactor=1.0` leaves only `MaxSilencePadSeconds` (0.3s) of
slack below the slot. No amount of prediction tuning fits inside that; the slack has to come from
compression headroom or from content the selector can add or drop.

## 2026-08-24 — Per-station traffic-source switches live on editorial settings, as a denylist

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Traffic SA has returned a deterministic 403 to our Azure egress since 2026-08-19: AWS WAF at their CloudFront distribution, verified 2026-08-24 by running the identical request from the dev Function App's own outbound IP (20.92.68.208) with three different User-Agents and against the service root - all 403 'Request blocked.', while the same request from an Australian residential IP returns 200 with live data in 0.25s. It is an IP-reputation block, not a URL, credential or header problem, and not CloudFront geo-restriction (that block page names the country; ours does not, and we are routed to the SYD PoP). All three environments share one outbound IP set, so dev, test and prod are equally blocked. Separately, DependencyInjection registered all six authority feeds so 'callers ask every jurisdiction', and TrafficEvidenceBuilder fanned out to every one with no geographic gating: both captured job-diagnostic exports carrying the failure are market=sydney, so Sydney bulletins were requesting South Australian traffic, failing, and writing an operator-visible failure line every time. 137 blocked requests in dev and 60 in test over 14 days, 100% failure, with no negative caching because only successful fetches populate the officialfeed cache.

**Decision:** A nullable DisabledTrafficSources denylist on EditorialSettings, gating the fan-out in TrafficEvidenceBuilder.GetCachedCorridorsCoreAsync. A disabled feed is not requested and reports SourceFetchOutcome.Skipped, which the console already drops as normal operation. Chosen over a new field on BulletinContentSelection because EditorialSettings is already resolved at BroadcastOrchestrator.cs:199, BEFORE the traffic fetch at :209; already overlays Global -> Market -> Station per field, so 'per station' needed no new scoping; and already rides GeneratorInputSnapshot.EditorialSettings onto every job, so the setting is auditable for free. That avoided touching the schedule DTO, the ScheduleEntity column, the queue message and TriggerStudio. A DENYLIST, not an allowlist: unset must mean 'every feed on' (the prior behaviour), and a feed added later must light up everywhere instead of staying silently off until all fifteen stations are edited. Null means inherit and an empty list is a deliberate 'consult everything' that overrides a wider denylist, so a station can opt back in to a source its market switched off. The set of disableable ids has exactly one owner, Domain/Services/OfficialTrafficSources; HERE is deliberately absent because it is the primary provider and BulletinContentSelection.Traffic already decides whether a bulletin carries traffic. Unknown ids are rejected by EditorialSettings.Validate at save time.

**Rationale:** The domain already had the vocabulary and the console already had the behaviour: SourceFetchOutcome.Skipped is documented as 'Not consulted: the source's jurisdiction does not cover this market', source-diagnostics.ts labels it 'Not applicable', visibleSourceDiagnostics() filters it out entirely, and the mock fixtures already shipped victraffic and tasalert as Skipped. The feature was ~70% built and only the backend gate was missing, so emitting Skipped removes the operator-facing noise with zero frontend change. Reusing EditorialSettings also matched the precedent that MaxCorridors set: an editorial setting that governs which DATA reaches the writer, not merely wording. The registry exists because the 2026-07-30 configurability audit (F-2) found MaxCorridors defined in six places with two of three copies able to drift silently, and the save-time id rejection because OperatorsHttpTrigger records the same trap for market ids, where an unknown value 'saves cleanly but then 403s the operator on every route with no signal at save time'.

**Consequences:** Sydney and Cairns, the only enabled markets, can stop consulting Traffic SA and the recurring '403 (forbidden)' line leaves the evidence rail. The semantics are deliberately asymmetric: off is silent, but a source left ON that fails still reports Failed and stays visible, so this cannot become a way to mute a broken authority - the failure mode that let the QLDTraffic demo-key degradation (RISK-36) go unnoticed. The denylist enters the corridor cache key, because two stations can share a market, a coverage shape and the 3-minute bucket while disagreeing about sources, and omitting it would serve one station's evidence to the other. TryRefreshTrafficAsync resolves settings from the repository rather than off the context: OrchestrateAsync calls that refresh BEFORE it resolves editorial settings, so trusting context.EditorialSettings left the gate inert on the whole queue path - caught by BroadcastOrchestratorSourceToggleTests, which asserts the feed is never REQUESTED rather than merely filtered. Storage adds a DisabledTrafficSourcesJson column (Table storage has no collection type); an absent or unparseable value reads back as inherit, never as an empty denylist. This does NOT restore SA data: adelaide, portaugusta and portlincoln are configured markets that would run HERE-only, which re-creates the RISK-30/35/36 mode where authorityCoversRoad is false and stale HERE closures air undemoted. The remedy for those is an allowlist from SA DIT, and a static egress IP to make it durable.

## 2026-08-24 — An excluded record is an input to the fetch, not a filter over its result

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Fixing the Desk's key space earlier the same day made omissions bite for the first time, and
that exposed the defect underneath. `DeskOmissions.Apply` dropped the record from an already-aggregated
corridor with `corridor with { Incidents = surviving }`, but every corridor-level field is derived by
`CorridorAggregator` from ALL members and was never re-derived. Dev job `e234aa5a`: Church Street carried
a 639 m northbound record and two 20 m records with no direction between them; the big one was omitted,
and the corridor still read `Direction: northbound`, `TotalLengthKm: 0.7` (639 m of it the omitted
record's), an unchanged `ImpactScore` of 209.3, plus `OfficialEvidences: [272218]`,
`OfficialCrossStreet: Great Western Highway` and `Sources: [here, livetraffic-nsw]` — all of them the
killed record's. The bulletin then aired "**Northbound** on Church Street at Granville". `ClaimGate` never
got a say: the claim was made from the corridor header, not from a surviving fact. Two knock-ons: the
omitted record kept inflating `ImpactScore`, so it could still win the corridor a slot under
`CalculateMaxCorridors` and displace a real item; and the console's corroboration chip cited an authority
record the operator had killed. `CorridorCurator.ExcludeIncidents` — the rundown's per-regeneration
exclude — had the identical line and the identical defect.

**Decision:** `IncidentExclusions`, resolved BEFORE the fetch and threaded into it:
`ITrafficProvider.GetCorridorsAsync(area, maxCorridors, ct, exclusions)` filters raw records at the
`IncidentEligibility.IsWithheld` gate, i.e. before `AggregateByRoad`; `CorroborationOptions.Exclusions`
filters authority events at fusion's boundary so an omitted authority record neither becomes an
official-only corridor nor rides along as a receipt; and the set's `FetchToken` enters the corridor cache
key. It carries both operator key spaces — the Desk's ledger event keys and the rundown's raw record ids
— and accumulates `Drops` so the caller can log what was held back and why. `DeskOmissions` and
`CorridorCurator.ExcludeIncidents` are deleted; there is now one exclusion path, not three.

**Rationale:** The cache-key comment already stated the principle for the disabled-source denylist: "part
of the identity of the fetch, not a filter applied after it". Exclusion is the same kind of thing, and for
a stronger reason — the corridors are AGGREGATED, so a set built while an event was omitted describes a
different world from one built while it was not. The alternative, re-deriving the corridor after removing
a member, was rejected: it either duplicates `CreateCorridor`'s logic in a second place (the duplication
that caused this bug) or has to guess which fields came from aggregation and which from the later flow,
suburb, extent, priority and fusion passes. `GetIncidentRoadNamesAsync` is deliberately NOT
exclusion-aware: an omitted record is unaired, not absent, so its road must stay out of the good-run pool.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev, deployed 08:35 UTC. The Church Street scenario reproduced exactly
(3 records, only the 639 m one directional) and after omitting it the corridor left the evidence entirely
— once its inflated 639 m and impact were gone, the surviving 40 m pair ranked below the 26-corridor
storage cap, which is where it always belonged. Dacey Avenue then showed the re-derivation directly:
members 2 → 1, `TotalLengthKm` 0.3 → 0.2, `ImpactScore` 203.9 → 193.1, `Direction` still `eastbound`
because the SURVIVOR is eastbound. Note the authority receipt `284411` correctly stayed: that record has
no verdict of its own and independently matches the surviving corridor by road name — before this change
it was retained by accident on a stale corridor, now it is re-matched from scratch.
Tests: `IncidentExclusionsTests` (8) covers the invariant "an excluded record is indistinguishable from
one never fetched", field by field; reverting to post-hoc filtering fails 2 of them. `TrafficEvidenceFusion`
gains the omitted-authority-record cases. `HereTrafficWireMockTests` covers the provider honouring the
parameter — but NOT the pre-vs-post ordering, because that fixture supplies no segment topology so every
record resolves to a placeholder road name and never shares a corridor; the ordering guard is the domain
invariant. Suites: Domain 2279, Application 882, Functions 834, Infrastructure 1573 (the same 5
pre-existing failures). Still open, and ARN's call: an omission lapses when HERE re-issues the event under
a new `originalId` (dev's ledger shows the same physical event omitted under two keys three times over),
and an id-less authority record is keyed by a content hash over its window and detail text, so a window
roll drops the omission.

## 2026-08-24 — Editorial-settings audit: 13 of 15 knobs are consumed, 2 are inert

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Asked whether every knob on the Bulletin rules editorial-settings panel actually does anything. The repository has form here: the 2026-07-30 configurability audit found CorridorSelectionOptions never bound at all (F-1) and MaxCorridors defined in six places (F-2), and the 2026-08-10 UI feature audit found 16 broken or no-op surfaces. Verification was also impossible from logs: MarketContentFetcher logged only corridors, driveTime and the three tier caps - 5 of 15 fields - so the four continuity caps, the guidance cap and the entire slot-fit envelope had no audit trail, and an operator who saved them had no way to confirm the bulletin resolved what they saved.

**Decision:** The resolved-settings log line now names EVERY field, with `*` marking fields that persist and resolve but are read by no consumer, so the line can never be mistaken for proof that an inert knob took effect. Verification method, repeatable: PUT all fields at Market scope with distinctive in-bounds values, trigger a bulletin, then read the `[MarketContent] ... editorial settings resolved from N row(s)` trace plus the behaviour traces (`[TrafficAggregation] SelectedCorridors=`, `standing guidance: N in effect, M dropped`, `[WavProcessor:AdjustSpeed] ... tempo`). Resolution and CONSUMPTION are proven separately: a cap only proves itself when it BINDS, so a second pass sets values low enough to change observable output.

**Rationale:** Proven consumed on dev 2026-08-24 by making each setting bind: DisabledTrafficSources (both listed feeds reported Skipped); GuidanceMaxDirectives ('9 in effect, 0 dropped' at cap 11, then '3 in effect, 6 dropped' at cap 3 - impossible under the shipped default of 8); MaxCorridors with the tier caps (SelectedCorridors 7-of-17 at cap 9, collapsing to 1-of-15 at cap 2 with tiers 1/1/1); MaxSpeedUpFactor (tempo 1.2080, above the deployed 1.15 ceiling, so only the 1.28 override permits it); MaxSlowDownFactor (tempo 0.8293 = a 1.206x slow-down, impossible under the appsettings-pinned 1.0 'never slow the read' default). MaxSilencePadSeconds and MaxSafeOverrunTrimSeconds are INERT by static proof: every production read is SpeechDurationOptions - `_durationOptions.MaxSilencePadSeconds` in AudioPipelineService and ScriptGenerationEngine, `durationOptions.MaxSafeOverrunTrimSeconds` in AudioDurationFineTuner - and nothing reads the EditorialSettings members. The 2026-08-24 commit 'the slot-fit envelope is ARN-tunable from the console' wired 2 of the 4 it added; the working pair reach the pipeline as maxSpeedUpFactorOverride / maxSlowDownFactorOverride parameters and the other two have no override channel. A dynamic test alone would have MISREAD this: a 6.24s overrun was trimmed despite the 4.5s default, but AudioDurationFineTuner derives its window as Math.Max(configured, target * (speedUpOverride - 1)) = Math.Max(4.5, 8.4), so the speed-up override explains it entirely and the trim knob contributed nothing.

**Consequences:** Every editorial setting is now auditable from one trace line per bulletin. The two inert knobs were REMOVED from the console rather than left live: `maxSilencePadSeconds` and `maxSafeOverrunTrimSeconds` are gone from `EditorialSettingsPanel`'s `FIELDS`, so nothing can set them and a save actively clears any value an earlier build stored (they are absent from the whole-record upsert, so the backend writes null and a stale value cannot keep reading as ARN-configured on `/effective`). Two frontend tests guard it — the two wired slot-fit inputs must exist, the two unwired ones must not. Hidden rather than shown-and-disabled because these four decide whether a read that misses its slot is stretched, padded, compressed or sent to the standby cart: an operator who raised the silence pad to stop the 05:55 Sydney slot falling to the cart would reasonably believe they had mitigated dead air, and would be wrong. A control that lies about on-air behaviour is worse than one that is absent, and handover is days away. The domain field, DTO, storage column, validation and the `*` marker in the log line all stay, so wiring them later is additive and the API/config-transfer path is unchanged. To wire: thread `maxSilencePadSecondsOverride` and `maxSafeOverrunTrimSecondsOverride` through `IAudioPipelineService.SynthesizeWithDurationTargetAsync` (already 14 parameters) AND `IsSlotFilled` — or the slot-filled check will disagree with the padding decision — down to `AudioDurationFineTuner`, mirroring the working pair, then re-add both entries to `FIELDS` in the same change. Note the files that matter (`IAudioPipelineService`, `AudioPipelineService`, `AudioDurationFineTuner`) are all at HEAD; only `ScriptGenerationEngine`, which holds the silence-pad read and the synthesis call, carries in-flight work. `MaxSlowDownFactor` — the lever the cart-fallback analysis actually pointed at — already works, so the immediate on-air pain is covered. Two settings also remain resolved-but-unexercised rather than inert: `DriveTimeHeadlineThresholdMinutes` needs a delayed monitored route, and the four continuity caps need a prior published same-day bulletin with incident deltas.

## 2026-08-24 — Reproducing four "live defects" locally retired three of them as stale-build artifacts

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Inspection of dev jobs `9c0938fd` (sydney) and `4cc766fc` (cairns), generated three minutes after the 09:47:30Z deploy, produced a five-finding defect list. Four concerned one aired read carrying two sentences that share the tail "a breakdown has one of two lanes closed": the LLM reviewer never ran on sydney (no `Review-refine attempt` line, while cairns has one), the deterministic detectors were therefore the only gate, and the selector had chosen the cloned phrasing over a varied alternative that was on the same draft menu. Code reading supported all of it — `SentenceCloneDetector` groups by exact skeleton and substitutes only road names, and `SentenceShapeDetector`'s frame check compares sentence OPENINGS, so neither can see a shared tail.

**Decision:** Reproduce before fixing. Each finding was written as a test against the verbatim aired script, the job's own captured draft menu, and the station's real content selection. Three of the four then failed to reproduce: `ComputeViolationCounts` scores that read style=1, so the gate routes it TO the reviewer; the selector rejects the clone unprompted. Both trace to the phrase floor in `SentenceShapeDetector` (`RepeatedStatePhrase`, 3-5 word repeat across 2+ sentences, commit `25ece3fa` at 02:12Z), which the selector shares through `EvaluateQualityPenalty`. It was committed seven hours before the deploy, so the running build at 09:50Z was NOT the deployed tree. Only the fourth reproduced and was fixed: `ParseItems` kept byte-identical variants, so item [0]'s menu held one real option.

**Rationale:** The planned fix for the other three was a shared-subsequence measure inside `SentenceCloneDetector`. Reproduction showed that would have been a fifth guard duplicating a fourth — the precise accretion pattern the finding criticised — added to close a gap the tree had already closed, in response to output from a build nobody can identify. The tests were kept as regression guards rather than deleted: they pin that a cloned read must never present to `ConditionalAudit` as clean, that a varied read still must (or the fix silently buys quality by spending an LLM call per bulletin), and that the selector and the review gate keep sharing one definition of a machine-tell.

**Consequences:** Variant dedupe is case-insensitive on trimmed text, matching the `evidenceIds` dedupe directly above it; spoken output decides sameness, so casing does not. Suites: Domain 2279, Application 884, Infrastructure 1575 with the same 5 pre-existing failures, Functions 834. The stale-build conclusion is now evidence-backed rather than suspected, which promotes build stamping from housekeeping to the prerequisite for trusting any future job inspection: three of today's five findings were artifacts of diagnosing an unidentifiable binary, and that cost was paid before a line was changed.

## 2026-08-24 — A word-target expansion may not add a weather or fuel line

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev

**Context:** Dev `f553c893` (cairns-4ca) aired the temperature twice: "It's cloudy, with temperatures around 23 degrees." immediately followed by "Cloudy, 23 degrees in Cairns." The read was content-limited (19.1s of natural speech for a 22s slot), so `EnsureWordTargetComplianceAsync` sent sentence 1 to the refiner to grow it. The captured call shows the refiner answering with `evidenceIds: [weather:condition, weather:temperature]` — restating a fixture the closing line already carried. The expansion instruction explicitly forbids this ("Never restate what the read already covers"), and `EnsureExpansionIsGroundedAsync` reviewed the result and approved it.

**Decision:** `ContentSourceSignals.AddsFixtureLine(before, after)` — weather and fuel are fixtures that air at most once, so no rewrite may raise either count. The expansion loop composes the candidate read with the patch applied and discards the patch when it adds a fixture line, logging the reason and continuing to the next sentence. The existing skip at the top of the loop (`IsWeatherLine || IsFuelLine`) is untouched: it stops an existing fixture being EXPANDED, and never saw this case, because the sentence being grown was traffic.

**Rationale:** Every guard on this path is sentence-local, and both sentences were well formed alone — the defect exists only in their relationship, so only a whole-read count is decisive. The check is deterministic and reuses the signals the detectors already share, rather than adding a gate or another LLM pass to a path that had already spent eleven calls on this bulletin. It also declines to make the LLM the enforcer of a rule the prompt states: the same "forbidden by instruction, unenforced" shape produced the cloned tail, the duplicated closer and the dropped suburb.

**Consequences:** A content-limited read that has nothing honest left to add now stays short and slow-fills, which is the documented, preferred outcome ("never invent content to hit a number"). Introducing a FIRST weather line still returns true from the helper — the fill path never asks it, and the expansion path is right to refuse, so the caller keeps the decision. Five Domain tests pin it against the aired strings, including the two that must still be allowed: growing a traffic sentence with a supplied cross-street, and rewording the single weather line in place. Suites: Domain 2284, Application 884, Infrastructure 1575 (5 known pre-existing failures), Functions 834.

## 2026-08-24 — Suburb retention is judged per ROAD, not per corridor

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev

**Context:** Both cairns-4ca bulletins today (`f553c893`, `7d4664af`) shipped `Warning: script shipped with an unresolved style gate`, and the user had already reported the same symptom on test ("Richmond Road and Marsh Road are flagging, but there's no location reference for it"). The gate was `SUBURB DROPPED` on `"Bruce Highway" (near Gordonvale)`. Cairns supplies two Bruce Highway corridors, Edmonton and Gordonvale; the read named the road once, placed at Edmonton, because the writer is instructed to group a road's spots into one item and the secondary-item cap trimmed the rest. `Detect` looped per CORRIDOR, so naming a road once made the read liable for every suburb that road carries anywhere in the data.

**Decision:** Group corridors by road name. A road named in the script is satisfied when the script mentions ANY of that road's data suburbs; only a road named with none of them is flagged. `Repair` now shares the same definition through `RoadIsPlaced`, so the gate and its mechanical fix cannot disagree about what "placed" means.

**Rationale:** The gate's purpose, per its own summary, is that a listener can PLACE a road the writer named — one correct suburb does that. The old rule demanded the suburb of a spot the bulletin deliberately dropped, which is unreachable by construction: voicing Gordonvale is exactly the content the word budget removed, and `Repair` rightly declined too, because its already-placed guard refuses to stack "near Gordonvale" onto "Bruce Highway near Edmonton". A gate that cannot be satisfied does not raise quality — it burns both refine attempts (three sentence patches on `f553c893`, all rejected by the ratchet), spends the LLM budget, and ships the warning anyway, which trains operators to ignore the warning that matters. This narrows one genuine catch: a read that voices two spots on one road and places only the first now passes. That case needs sentence-level attribution to judge properly and is not what was failing.

**Consequences:** Four new Domain tests pin the aired strings plus the guarantees that must survive — a road named with none of its suburbs is still flagged, the single-corridor case is unchanged in both directions, and each road is judged on its own suburbs so a placed road is never reported alongside an unplaced one. The ten pre-existing `SuburbRetentionDetectorTests` pass untouched. Suites: Domain 2288, Application 884, Infrastructure 1575 (5 known pre-existing failures), Functions 834.

## 2026-08-24 — A slot whose air time has passed is recorded as missed, not generated

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev

**Context:** Test produced 21 MISSED slots in one morning and **20 of them generated a real script first**. `Job.ScheduledForUtc` is the slot's AIR time, and `ZettaFileDeliveryService` refuses to write to the playout share once it has passed — deliberately, since the 2026-08-11 incident where a restart sweep wrote 15 expired slots' stale audio to production. `SchedulePollerService` derived every deadline from `schedule.NextRunUtc` and dispatched with no check that the slot was still reachable. Job `d06dfc18` was created at 07:45:02 for a 07:45:00 slot: it drafted, synthesised, took the generic filler cart, was auto-approved by the deadline sweep at 07:46:00, and delivery was refused 61 seconds past the deadline. Every stage behaved exactly as specified; the slot was unreachable before the first of them ran. Measured discriminator over today's test jobs: MISSED were created a median 9.6 minutes AFTER their curation deadline (5/5), PUBLISHED a median 3.4 minutes before it (1/8 late).

**Decision:** After building the job and before publishing to the broadcast queue, compare the clock to `scheduledForUtc`. When the slot has already aired, mark the job `Missed`, save it, and return. The `finally` block still releases the schedule lock and advances `NextRunUtc`, so a lost slot never costs the station its later ones.

**Rationale:** The slot is lost either way — this does not save it. What it removes is the spend (a full draft/review/safety pass plus a TTS render, per expired slot) and a misleading record showing a bulletin that was generated, approved and then refused, which reads like a delivery fault rather than a slot that was gone before it started. The job is still written, as `Missed`, so the gap stays visible rather than silently disappearing. Semantics confirmed against a healthy dev job before changing scheduling behaviour: created 12:01:02, curation 12:04:00, fallback 12:11:00, air 12:14:00 — a 13-minute lead, matching the console's "goes to playout at 10:14 pm; if not approved by 10:11 pm the standby cart is sent".

**Consequences:** The two shared helpers in `SchedulePollerServiceTests` had pinned `NextRunUtc = Now − 5 min`, i.e. an already-aired slot, as the stand-in for "due"; they now use a realistic `+13 min` and the whole 100-test file passes. Three tests added, two of which fail with the guard disabled (verified by disabling it); the third pins that an expired slot still releases the lock and advances the schedule, and passes either way by design. **The upstream question is still open and is the more important one:** why the poller reached those slots after their air time at all. It is not answerable from test telemetry — App Insights holds no traces for test before roughly 11:00 today, though the job records prove the app was generating throughout the morning. That observability gap should be closed before the next pilot window, or the next occurrence will be equally unexplainable. Suites: Domain 2288, Application 887, Infrastructure 1575 (5 known pre-existing failures), Functions 834.

## 2026-08-24 — The retry loop corrects its prediction from its own measured renders

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev

**Context:** Dev job `6c3ebefb` spent 95 seconds and four ElevenLabs renders shipping a 22.0s bulletin. The sequence: predicted 27.7s, trimmed to 50 words, measured 19.3s, content-limited; predicted 21.8s, measured 19.3s, content-limited; predicted 26.1s, trimmed to 52, measured 18.5s, content-limited; predicted 26.7s, synthesised 58 words, measured 21.4s, shipped. The model claims ~0.48 s/word for this voice; it reads at ~0.386. Every trim was the ceiling correcting an overrun that did not exist, and every trimmed read then underran and was retried. Measured across ten dev bulletins: a single-attempt bulletin is 36-52s, and each extra attempt adds 15-25s, almost all of it TTS (`med=9780ms` per render). The same oscillation is already documented on job `43395fe5` (143s, 3 rounds); the fix then denominated the allowance in seconds rather than words, which corrected the units but not the source of the error.

**Decision:** `SpokenDurationCorrection` (Domain, pure) turns a predicted-versus-measured seconds-per-word pair into a clamped multiplicative factor, folded across attempts. `ScriptGenerationEngine` holds one per job in each of its two attempt loops, applies it to the model's prediction before `ResolveCeilingTarget`, and returns the rate the ceiling acted on via `GenerationAttemptOutcome.PredictedSecondsPerWord` so the next attempt can measure against it.

**Rationale:** Each render is a measurement of this exact voice reading this exact copy — strictly better evidence about its pace than the pooled model — and the loop discarded it, because the calibrated rate is read once before the first attempt (`ScriptGenerationEngine:74`) and never revisited. A rate rather than a total is compared, so the comparison survives the trim changing the word count. Bounds of 0.6-1.4 let a real 20-40% error be corrected in one step while stopping a freak render from driving the next attempt into a slot it cannot fill; eleven_v3 re-renders the same input within about ±12%, so a factor near 1 is noise. The correction cannot license an overrun: a read that is long even at the measured pace is still trimmed, which is pinned by test.

**Consequences:** This attacks latency, not quality — the reads were already correct, they just cost three renders too many. It does not fix the underlying calibration error (the dev voice's row is still the fleet's weakest at 9 offline samples), but it stops that error compounding within a job. Six tests drive `ResolveCeilingTarget` with job `6c3ebefb`'s verbatim numbers: the uncorrected prediction trims a read that fits and the trimmed word count cannot fill the slot at the measured pace; the corrected prediction reaches `prosody-fits` at the full 58 words, which is what attempt 4 proved. Suites: Domain 2288, Application 893, Infrastructure 1575 (5 known pre-existing failures), Functions 834.

## 2026-08-24 — The dead bulletin-generation paths are deleted; there is one generator and no flag selecting it

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** An audit of the generation path found the same defect nine times over: a boolean option whose
DEPLOYED value was identical in every environment but DIFFERENT from the code default, so the branch the
default selected had never executed in production and yet still had to compile, be reviewed, and be reasoned
about. had already named four of them on 30 July
("their legacy branches are permanently unexercised code"); nothing was actioned.

`Broadcast__UseStructuredMatrix` was the severe case. `grep -rn UseStructuredMatrix deployment/` returned
NOTHING — the flag that selects the entire generation architecture existed only as a hand-applied app setting,
`true` on dev and test, **UNSET on prod**. Prod therefore resolved to the legacy `LlmScriptGenerator` draft
path while every quality fix since 19 Aug targeted `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator`. Prod additionally
carried `UsePlainTextDraft=True` (bypassing the structured schema and CitationVerifier entirely) and no
`RefineSentenceAgentName` (sentence-refine on the raw model) — a third distinct pipeline shape.

The comprehension cost was measurable, not theoretical. An agent reading the repo in its recommended order
hits `ARCHITECTURE.md:158-163`, `MODULES.md:243` and `FILES.md:596` — all describing draft/review/refine
through `LlmScriptGenerator` — plus a code default of `false`, and concludes the legacy path is production.
`FILES.md:637` gave the actual production generator the purpose `—` (empty). The correcting fact lived at
`decisions.md:6310`, ~5,900 lines after the entry that established the belief it corrects.

**Decision:** `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator` is the ONLY `IScriptGenerator`; the selecting flag is gone,
not defaulted. Ten flags were deleted along with the branch their code default selected, each keeping the
behaviour all three environments already ran: `UseStructuredMatrix`, `UsePlainTextDraft`,
`DecoupleDurationFit`, `RetryExtendBestTake`, `PredictiveFitGate`, `DeterministicProvenance`,
`SkipTaggedSafetyRecheck`, `ConditionalAudit`, `NaturalnessPolish`, `DraftCandidateCount`. Removed with them:
`IScriptAttributor`, `IScriptPolisher`, `CitationVerifier`, `DraftCandidateSelector`, `StyleExamplesService`,
`StyleExamplesCache`, `AzureSearchOptions`, `CitationIssue`, the 268-line classic duration-fit loop, and the
`BroadcastOrchestrator.PolishGateReject` forwarder that existed only so a test could reach it.

`LlmScriptGenerator` is now purely the non-draft role provider: 1993 lines / 9 interfaces -> 900 lines /
6 interfaces, no method over 128. The prod defect is fixed: `refineSentenceAgentName` is wired through the
bicep and set in all three `.bicepparam` files.

**Rationale:** Prod is a frozen temporary fallback that will be replaced by test's configuration, so the
legacy path had no future and keeping it cost only comprehension. Measuring per-METHOD size rather than file
size showed where the real debt is: `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator` is 1125 lines across 25 methods with
nothing over 118 and is healthy, while `ScriptGenerationEngine` had 81% of its 1995 lines inside two methods.
File length was the wrong metric all along.

**Consequences:** −5,053/+648 over 69 files, 17 deleted. Build 0/0. Domain 2288, Application 879, Functions
834, Infrastructure 1492 pass — its 4 failures were proven pre-existing at `0fcd5aa4` by running them in a
clean worktree, not assumed. Deployed to dev from a detached worktree at `0817b6a0`.

Live proof on dev: sydney `f13d565e` exercised the extend-then-regen loop and had its LLM review SKIPPED by
the clean-detector gate; cairns `c1a11f5b` and `7897d98c` ran review, applied a deterministic section-order
repair and landed 22.0s exactly. Both markets behaved identically in shape to their pre-change baselines
(sydney skipped review before AND after, cairns ran it before AND after), and the LLM captures show
Draft/Review/Safety with NO Attribute and NO Polish — direct evidence those stages are gone.

**Two lessons worth carrying.** (1) Tests pin defaults, not production: 13 Application tests failed on
removal because they asserted the dead branch, two by literally setting `DecoupleDurationFit = false`. They
were adapted to reach the same subject through the surviving path (raise `TargetWordCountOverride` so
`SlotFitPlanner.NeedsExpansion` is true; set `MaxContentExtendRetries = 0` to force fresh regen) — none was
deleted, because every subject survived. (2) `what-if` disproved an assumption mid-flight: the bicep does NOT
manage the production slot's `appSettings` (no delta on that resource), so a deploy will NOT drop a removed
key. The 8 orphaned settings were deleted explicitly on dev with `az functionapp config appsettings delete`;
test and prod still carry them, inert.

**Open:** test/prod not deployed; the `arn-polish`/`arn-attribute` Foundry agents still exist server-side
though nothing provisions or calls them; `prompts/{draft,citation-fix,style-exemplars}.md` are unread by code
and retained pending an eval-gated cleanup (flagged in `prompts/README.md` rather than silently left).
Next, in order: DI-register the four orchestrator collaborators so the engine is testable at all, then split
`ReviewAndRefineScriptAsync` (1014), `GenerateAndSynthesizeAsync` (926) and `TryGenerateValidBroadcastAsync`
(454), then replace `JobLog(At, Level, Message)` with a structured stage event.

## 2026-08-24 — The flow pool is the pipeline's largest stage, and it is a cold-cache artifact

**Status:** accepted — instrumentation deployed dev

**Context:** A per-operation App Insights audit of one bulletin (237 sampled dependency
calls, ~470 after sampling correction) showed the pipeline's own stage metrics accounted
for only 24s of a 60.7s `orchestration_total`. Job-log timing across 50 single-attempt dev
bulletins put 40% of a clean bulletin in a pre-LLM phase split roughly evenly between the
HERE fetch (8.1s) and an unnamed 8.3s block between the "Traffic fetched:" and "Incident
changes:" log lines. That block had no `TrackPipelineStage` call, so its cost could not be
attributed to a network call or to local compute.

**Decision:** Stage-time the three operations inside it — `priority_roads`, `flow_pool`,
`incident_state` — before proposing any optimisation.

**Rationale:** Optimising an unmeasured phase is guesswork. The candidate explanations —
a slow HERE flow fetch, the segment-identity resolve, the incident state diff, or local
ranking over ~964 rows — imply completely different fixes (cap concurrency, cache
durably, batch the table writes, filter before resolving), and three of the four would
have been wasted work. One stopwatch per operation costs nothing on the critical path
(`IBroadcastMetrics` is allocation-light and never throws) and settles it in one deploy.

**Consequences:** Measured immediately on dev, cold workers vs warm, same build:

| stage | cold | warm |
|---|---|---|
| `flow_pool` | 20.26s | **0.52s** |
| `traffic_fetch` | 8.63s | 5.21s |
| `tts_synthesize` | 10.88s | 10.79s |
| `script_generate` | 6.96s | 5.67s |
| `incident_state` | 0.11s | 0.09s |
| `priority_roads` | 0.01s | 0.01s |
| `orchestration_total` | 62.67s | 41.15s |

`flow_pool` is the single most expensive stage in the pipeline when cold and the cheapest
measurable one when warm — a 39x spread, matched by HERE map-attributes calls falling from
816 estimated to 18. The whole 20s is the segment-identity resolve for ~964 flow rows
against a cold `IMemoryCache`; road geometry is static, so every one of those lookups is
recomputing an answer that cannot change.

Two attributions in the earlier analysis were WRONG and are retracted: `incident_state`
(0.09s) and `priority_roads` (0.01s) are free. The "incident diff is as expensive as the
network fetch" reading came from bracketing them with `flow_pool` between two log lines.

**Open:** how often the cold path is hit. App Insights request sampling retains ~17 of
today's 70 bulletins, so cold-start frequency cannot be back-filled; the new stage metric
makes it answerable from here. A durable segment cache is worth exactly 20.3s on the first
bulletin per market after any worker restart, and nothing at all on a warm one — so the
frequency decides whether it is worth building.

## 2026-08-25 — Structured evidence citations carry their owning corridor into Review

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Draft agent can cite atomic evidence such as a cross-street, lane count, or detail without repeating the parent road. The backend persisted those EvidenceIds, but sentence CorridorKeys were derived only from road-name mentions and the web decoder discarded EvidenceIds, so valid location-only claims appeared unused in the Review evidence rail (live dev job 4e843a3c, checked 2026-08-25).

**Decision:** Resolve every structured Draft or sentence-patch evidence ID to its owning corridor road while the allowed evidence units are available, merge those owner keys into persisted JobScriptSentence.CorridorKeys, and retain EvidenceIds in the web contract. For historical jobs without owner keys, the Review lineage path may conservatively recover traffic-backed sentences from incident source text only when persisted traffic EvidenceIds are present.

**Rationale:** The atomic evidence ID is the authoritative citation; forcing presenters to repeat a parent road would make natural cross-street wording worse and still would not expose field-level citations. Propagating the deterministic EvidenceUnit.SourceKey preserves the existing Review panel contract for new jobs, while the narrow legacy fallback makes the fix effective for already-persisted jobs without weakening ordinary heuristic provenance.

**Consequences:** New structured jobs cite the correct incident row even when the script names only its location. Existing jobs with EvidenceIds but empty CorridorKeys are recoverable in the Review panel. The frontend now retains EvidenceIds for future field-level evidence rendering, and tests cover the Shorter Avenue / King Georges Road regression.

## 2026-08-24 — The slow-down A/B passed on the panel and did not reproduce live; the live cause is identical re-renders

**Status:** accepted (finding) — dev carries `MaxSlowDownFactor` 1.05 as an unvalidated proposal

**Context:** With `flow_pool` explained (cold-cache), retries were the remaining recurring
cost: 31% of dev bulletins, ~2 TTS renders each at ~10.8s and ~$0.106 apiece. The fit gate
is asymmetric — `MaxSpeedUpFactor` 1.15, `MaxSlowDownFactor` 1.0 — and
`SpeechDurationOptions` gives the retry tolerance as `T x (1 - 1/factor)`, which at 1.0 is
exactly zero. Every underrun, however small, forces a full regeneration.

**Decision:** A/B the slow-down cap on the committed 10-fixture replay panel before
proposing it to ARN, then verify live.

**Rationale:** The gate is a product decision (ARN's standing policy is "never slow the
read"), so it needed measurement rather than argument, and the replay harness A/Bs it in
~4 minutes per arm against real agents with zero TTS cost.

**Consequences:** The panel result was unambiguous — control (1.0) filled 9/10,
meanAttempts 2.3; treatment (1.05) filled 9/10, meanAttempts 1.3, paired 6 wins / 0 losses
/ 4 ties, fidelity gate 5/5 in both arms.

**It did not reproduce live.** Eight dev bulletins on 1.05 averaged 2.00 attempts against
a 1.44 baseline. The setting was confirmed live (no app-setting override; deploy finished
14:36:19, triggers ran 14:40+). Reading the logs rather than the aggregate explains it:
the live retries were mostly NOT the case 1.05 addresses.

- `1e93eb2f` and `a6bc547c` filled the slot on attempt 1 ("Audio filled to slot"), then
  the **pace floor** fired on word count alone and re-rendered to a byte-identical read.
- `269daada` was genuinely content-limited but with a 1.9s gap; 1.05 buys only 1.05s, so
  it still retried. The code's own default of 1.10 buys 2.0s and would have covered it.
- In all three, every retry synthesised the SAME word count as the attempt before it
  (54/54, 58/58, 51/51/51) and could only produce identical audio. Four wasted renders,
  ~40s and ~$0.40, across three bulletins.

The pace-floor branch already carries a comment warning about precisely this ("extending
it can only re-overrun and re-trim to a byte-identical read: a wasted render", measured on
job 175950d0, 2026-08-04). The 2026-08-04 fix covered the post-trim route; these three took
a different one, and the guard still compares only word counts, never asking whether the
slot was already filled.

**Open:** the highest-value next fix is cause-agnostic — refuse to synthesise when the
about-to-be-rendered word count is unchanged from the previous attempt, since the audio
cannot differ. It subsumes the pace-floor waste, the extend-that-does-not-extend, and any
future variant. Whether `MaxSlowDownFactor` should be 1.0, 1.05 or the 1.10 default is
still ARN's call and should be decided on audio, not on these numbers.

## 2026-08-24 — A slot miss is priced by what the audio stage can do about it, not by how far off it is

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev, verified live on the reproduced market

**Context:** Dev job 8a42269daada (cairns-4ca, 22s slot) burned four ElevenLabs renders.
Attempts 1-3 each synthesised 51 words for 20.1/20.1/20.3s and were rejected as
content-limited; attempt 4 took 56 words, ran 24.1s and fitted to 22.0s. Reading the
captured draft menus showed 56 words is the ALL-CONCISE read — the cheapest combination
that voices every item — and it was on the menu at every attempt. 51 words sits below the
menu's own floor, so it is reachable only by dropping an item.

**Decision:** `SlotMissSeconds` charges by fittability, not by distance. Reads inside
`[slot - MaxSilencePadSeconds, slot x 1.13]` are free and chosen on coverage; outside it,
either direction costs 8/second.

**Rationale:** The old model charged undershoot 1x and overshoot 2x-8x, reasoning that
"slow-filling a short read sounds natural". ARN runs `MaxSlowDownFactor` 1.0 — there is no
slow-fill. An undershoot past the 0.3s pad is unrecoverable and costs a full regeneration
(~17s, ~$0.10); an overshoot inside `MaxSpeedUpFactor` 1.15 is absorbed by compression for
free. The model charged the recoverable failure up to eight times more than the
unrecoverable one, so the selector reliably shed content into the only outcome the
pipeline cannot fix.

**Consequences:** Two constants are measured, not chosen, and both were found by
disagreement between instruments:

- Rewarding the FULLEST fitting read parks every read on the compression cliff — panel
  fidelity fell to 3/5. Reads are centred in the window instead.
- Raising the out-of-window charge to 20/second satisfied the isolated 31-menu comparison
  but dropped panel fidelity to 2/5. **When the isolated selector harness and the
  full-pipeline panel disagree, the panel wins** — it runs real agents, real slots and the
  real retry loop.

Final, 10-fixture panel with `MaxSlowDownFactor` left at 1.0:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| filled | 9/10 | **10/10** |
| fidelity gate | 5/5 | 5/5 |
| dev-fallbacks recovered | 4/5 | **5/5** |
| meanAttempts | 2.3 | **1.3** |
