31 captured production menus: unfittable seconds 31.5s -> 16.2s, items dropped 6 -> 6.

**Live verification** — cairns-4ca, the reproduced market, now takes ONE attempt on both
runs (was four): the selector chooses 53 words at a predicted 23.3s, deliberately over the
slot, and compression lands it at 22.0s.

The 1.05 `MaxSlowDownFactor` proposal from earlier today is reverted. This fixes the cause,
so ARN's "never slow the read" policy stands untouched.

`SelectorReplayComparisonTests` asserted distance from the slot, which was the right proxy
only while landing ON the slot was the objective. It now asserts what actually costs a
re-render: a fittable read must stay fittable, a drop must buy a fit, and total unfittable
seconds must not grow.

**Open — two OTHER causes, confirmed distinct, still live:**

1. **Boundary noise against zero tolerance.** Adelaide read 30.0s for a 30s slot and was
   declared content-limited three times, then the same 30.0s passed on attempt 4. With
   `MaxSlowDownFactor` 1.0 the tolerance is exactly zero and only the 0.3s pad separates
   pass from regenerate, which is below the render-to-render noise floor.
2. **A miscalibrated voice.** Sydney job ff7ba1e7 predicted 26.8s -> 31.9s -> 33.9s while
   measuring ~0.447 s/word — over-predicting by roughly 43%, so the word ceiling
   over-trimmed into an underrun on every attempt and the job failed. The 2026-08-24
   in-job correction fires (observed 1.00x -> 0.99x -> 0.95x on adelaide) but only after
   the first render, and cannot rescue a pooled model that starts this far off.

Neither is the selector; both sit downstream of it.

## 2026-08-24 — Dev evaluation of the slot-miss repricing: measurably better, and it isolates what is left

**Status:** accepted (measurement) — selector fix `636fe15d` live on dev

**Context:** The selector change was verified on one market. This is the population result,
isolated so the selector is the only variable: both windows already carry the 2026-08-24
in-job duration correction, and the post sample was taken after a warm-up wave so it is not
measuring cold-start.

**Decision:** Keep the change. Treat the residual as two named causes, not as noise.

**Rationale:** A single-market verification cannot distinguish "fixed" from "got lucky",
and the earlier 8-job batch was confounded by cold workers and mixed causes.

**Consequences:**

| | n | attempts/blt | 1-attempt | renders/blt | short/blt | median gen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre (13:10-15:37) | 25 | 1.88 | 48% | 1.88 | 0.64 | 61s |
| post (warm eval) | 21 | **1.38** | **81%** | **1.38** | **0.38** | **38s** |

Renders per bulletin -27% (the direct ElevenLabs cost line), median generation -38%,
single-attempt rate 48% -> 81%. No style-gate regressions.

Every residual failure was read individually and NONE is the selector:

1. **The silence pad is not applied to the ordinary path — a bug.** `underrunTolerance` is
   `target x (1 - 1/MaxSlowDownFactor)`, which is exactly ZERO at the configured 1.0, and
   `MaxSilencePadSeconds` (0.3s) is consulted only on the post-trim branch. So a 0.04s
   shortfall forces a full regeneration. Three of sixteen content-limited rejections in the
   eval had a displayed gap of 0.0s — reads that filled the slot were regenerated. The
   comment above the branch already asserts "the silence pad closes the remainder"; on this
   path it never gets the chance.
2. **A miscalibrated voice.** Sydney predicted 26.8s -> 31.9s -> 33.9s against a measured
   ~0.447 s/word, so the ceiling over-trimmed into an underrun on every attempt.

Sizing the tolerance question against those same sixteen rejections: 6/16 (38%) would pass
at `MaxSlowDownFactor` 1.05, and **12/16 (75%) at the code's own 1.10 default**. Adelaide
produced 28.2-30.0s of speech for a 30s slot four times running and still failed the
bulletin — a 94-100% fill discarded and regenerated.

**Open:** fix (1) first; it is a bug against existing configuration rather than a policy
change, and it needs no sign-off. (2) and the tolerance value remain ARN's call, but they
should now be argued from these numbers rather than from taste.

## 2026-08-24 — The silence-pad fix is correct in principle and regressed in practice; it is reverted

**Status:** accepted — reverted on dev, NOT promoted

**Context:** The ordinary underrun path never consulted `MaxSilencePadSeconds`. With ARN's
shipped `MaxSlowDownFactor` of 1.0 the tolerance was `target x (1 - 1/1.0)` = exactly zero,
so a 0.04s shortfall forced a full redraft and re-synthesis; three of sixteen
content-limited rejections in a dev batch had a displayed shortfall of 0.0s. Making the pad
a floor on the tolerance is, on the code's own documented reasoning, obviously right.

**Decision:** Revert it. Do not promote it.

**Rationale:** It measured WORSE on dev, and the result replicated against a control.

| dev window | n | attempts | 1-att | short/blt | failed | median | corridors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A pre-selector baseline | 25 | 1.88 | 48% | 0.64 | 0% | 61s | 10 |
| B selector only | 21 | 1.38 | 81% | 0.38 | 5% | 38s | 9 |
| **C selector + pad** | 18 | **2.06** | 44% | **1.17** | **11%** | 58s | 8 |
| **D selector only, repeat** | 14 | **1.50** | 64% | **0.36** | **0%** | 35s | 8 |

C is the outlier and D restores the improvement at the SAME median corridor count, so the
window was not content-starved and the cause is the change itself. Widening a tolerance
cannot mechanically increase retries, which means the effect is indirect — most likely
through `IsContentLimitedUnderrun`, which also drives candidate retention and the
extend-without-redraft path, so marking a short read "not content-limited" appears to stop
the loop banking and extending the take that would have filled the slot.

**Consequences:** The bug is real and still live. It is NOT to be reapplied as written. The
next attempt must treat the underrun flag's two jobs separately — "should this attempt be
rejected" and "should this take be banked and extended" are currently the same boolean, and
only the first should widen.

**Live proof of what NOT to trust:** the isolated unit tests all passed and the replay panel
sat inside its noise band (fidelity 4/5, 5/5, 5/5 across three runs). Only a controlled
before/after against live dev traffic exposed it. For anything touching the retry loop, the
dev A/B is the gate — not the panel, and certainly not unit tests.

## 2026-08-25 — Road identity: a table gap was causing a merge, and a route code was destroyed before the table could use it

**Status:** accepted — deployed dev, NOT promoted (A/B confounded; see Open)

**Context:** ARN reported seeing "M1" and "Pacific Mwy" as separate rows in the adjust tab.
Investigating the population strategy for an operator alias library surfaced a second, worse
defect underneath it.

**Decision:** Fix both in code before building any operator-facing control.

**Rationale:** An operator override whose failure mode is a silently merged corridor should
not be the primary mechanism for a defect a rule can close permanently across 15 markets.

**Consequences:**

1. **A gap in a hand-maintained table was causing a MERGE.** `CanonicalRoadKey` drops a
   leading route code, which is right while the remainder identifies the road
   ("M1 Eastern Distributor" = "Eastern Distributor") and catastrophic when it does not:
   "M7 Motorway" reduced to "Motorway", as did M5, M11 and M12. Dev sydney carries M7 x14,
   M5 x7, M11 x2, M12 x1 — four motorways on one grouping key, with `CreateCongestionCorridor`
   SUMMING their delays and lengths. M2/M4/M8 escaped only because the alias table happens to
   carry explicit entries. Now collapses to the code itself. **Fails closed: a table miss can
   lose a designation, never merge two roads.**
2. **The route code was destroyed before the curated list saw it.** HERE returns
   "M1 / Pacific Mwy"; the provider kept only what followed the slash, so the string offered
   to `RoadDesignationAliases` was "Pacific Mwy" — deliberately absent, because bare "Pacific
   Motorway" is the M3 in Brisbane. The table already held "M1 Pacific Mwy" -> "M1". Code and
   name are now rejoined and offered together; a miss falls through to historic behaviour, so
   it is fail-safe for the eleven markets with no entries.

Also: weather alerts are naturalised like conditions already were, since four of eleven test
bulletins paired a dry condition with raw "Heavy rain anticipated" at 57% precipitation
probability and operators rewrote every one. Unknown alerts pass through untouched.

**Live proof on dev:** sydney now emits `M1` x3, `M5` x2, `M7` x3 as distinct designations.
Before, M1 did not appear at all and M5/M7 collapsed into "Motorway".

**Two corrections I made mid-investigation, recorded because both were expensive:**
- I claimed a live seven-motorway collapse from a PYTHON SIMULATION of the normaliser. The
  real normaliser is better than the simulation and my first test passed, so I retracted it.
  The retraction was also wrong: the collapse is real, but only for codes absent from the
  alias table, and I had picked three covered codes as examples. **Simulating a normaliser
  instead of calling it cost two wrong conclusions in a row.**
- The 615 distinct sydney road names are not a curation burden: real normalisation already
  unifies abbreviations and route-code prefixes. The residual needing human judgement is
  about five roads, not 484.

**Open — the A/B is CONFOUNDED and this must not be promoted on it.** The after-window ran at
11:12 AEST peak with corridors median 20 / incidents median 28, against a before-window at
8 / 13 — 2.5x the content. Attempts 1.50 -> 1.72 and failures 0% -> 11% are not attributable;
both failures were content-limited underruns from the two known residual causes. A matched
comparison must be taken at the same time of day, by reverting for one wave and re-applying
for the next, before this goes near test.

## 2026-08-25 — Official-feed polygon boundaries are exact, not enclosing-radius approximations

**Status:** accepted — implemented and test-proven, not deployed

**Context:** Official NSW, QLD, VIC, WA and SA adapters downloaded statewide payloads and
filtered geometry only against the station's derived enclosing circle. Sydney's polygon therefore
accepted Barrenjoey Road and other records outside the drawn licence boundary. HERE already
post-filtered polygon results, but retained shapeless records that could not be verified.

**Decision:** Keep the radius as a cheap pre-filter, then apply exact polygon intersection to every
geometry-bearing official event and HERE incident. Point-on-boundary is included; a polyline that
crosses the polygon is included; empty geometry fails closed for polygon coverage. TasALERT remains
outside this geometry path because its RSS records have no coordinates and require jurisdiction
gating.
**Rationale:** The enclosing circle is only a retrieval optimisation. Treating it as the
station boundary admitted real Sydney records outside the operator-drawn licence area. Exact
geometry is cheap relative to the network fetch and can fail closed when a source has no shape.

**Consequences:** Polygon-based official events and HERE incidents now share the same exact
boundary semantics. Missing-geometry HERE records are dropped for polygons rather than being
silently treated as in-area. Bbox/corridor official-feed geometry and geometry-less TasALERT
remain separate follow-up concerns.

**Evidence:** The permanent boundary regression suite covers NSW incidents/roadworks, QLD GeoJSON,
VIC GeoJSON, WA and SA ArcGIS, HERE congestion, line/polygon intersection, boundary points,
outside-radius controls and shapeless HERE data. `dotnet test ... --filter Category=BoundaryTrial`
passes 11/11 after the change; official-feed golden tests pass 10/10.

**Open:** Deploy to test and run a fresh Sydney/Cairns bulletin. Existing jobs and Sydney's
historical TasALERT incident-landscape rows are immutable snapshots and need separate regeneration
or cleanup. Exact geometry for bbox/corridor official feeds and TasALERT jurisdiction
applicability remain follow-up work if those shapes/sources are enabled.

## 2026-08-26 — Use scalar projections for job list reads

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** TEST App Insights showed point Table Storage reads are fast, while ListJobs repeatedly scanned wide radioJobs rows and rebuilt complete Job aggregates even though list responses contain only scalar summary fields.

**Decision:** Route ListJobs through a scalar JobListItem projection that selects only list fields and maps directly to JobSummaryDto; retain the full JobEntity mapper for detail, generation, fallback, and ledger correctness paths.

**Rationale:** This removes decompression, JSON deserialization, and domain reconstruction from the highest-volume read path without changing the public response contract or canonical job storage.

**Consequences:** The list repository now owns a lightweight projection contract and its equivalence tests. Indexed feed and persisted ledger projections remain the next architectural performance wave; until then the summary path still scans matching rows.

## 2026-08-26 — Fit Facts, Not Finished Prose, in a Clean-Room Substitutable Workflow

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The deployed pipeline writes sentences first and assembles a bulletin afterwards, creating a measured contradiction between its authoring and review contracts. `prompts/agents/arn-draft.md:5-6,48-52` instructs the writer that sentences are the read in returned order and should pick up from the sentence before, while `prompts/review-system.md` instructs the reviewer to treat position-dependence as a defect and to judge whether a sentence COULD sit anywhere. `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator.LeadWithTheWorstDisruption:893` reorders the traffic block despite the draft prompt promising nothing reorders. The fitter drops finished sentences with only a log line at `:407-414`, and `OrphanedConnectiveDetector` inspects only the first traffic claim, so a mid-read orphan is caught by nothing.

**Decision:** Add a clean-room workflow in three projects: `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Workflow/`, `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Workflow.Hosting/`, and `test/ArnBulletinGenerator.Workflow.Tests/`. Invert the pipeline to `EVIDENCE -> MEANING -> SELECTION -> DISCOURSE -> WORDS -> VERIFICATION`, with the governing rule that the fitter fits facts, never finished prose. Use `IBulletinWorkflow` as the substitutable seam (`Id`, `Description`, and `RunAsync(WorkflowRequest) -> WorkflowOutcome`); trial another architecture by registering another implementation and naming it in configuration. Use three LLM roles, `plan`, `compose`, and `ground`, in place of six agents.

**Rationale:** Fitting facts rather than prose removes the whole defect class: selection can add or remove semantic content without stranding a connective or invalidating sentence ordering, and one composer writes the complete read after selection. The plan is authored once so the semantic intent is stable, while the fit loop re-runs to adjust selected facts, composition, verification, and duration within bounded iterations. Grounding has three states, `Supported`, `NotSupported`, and `Contradicted`, because unsupported claims and contradicted claims have different evidence conditions and the caller must decide what an unsupported claim costs. Prompts are sent explicitly on every call rather than living server-side so each trace contains the complete input and the workflow's contract is inspectable and reproducible.

**Consequences:** The clean-room workflow is additive; nothing in the airing pipeline was modified. Word estimation now happens BEFORE prose exists, which is strictly less information than the deployed history-calibrated predictor that measures finished text. This is the single largest accuracy risk in the design. It is isolated behind `IDurationOracle`, and the starting `WordEstimator.FieldCosts` table is explicitly a calibration placeholder to be fitted against measured reads. A re-fit now costs a full compose call, where the old fitter re-selected over existing prose for free. `StagedWorkflowOptions` bounds this at 3 fit iterations and 1 revision. `arn-review` as a style judge and `arn-refine-sentence` are deliberately absent: the refiner's contract forbids writing a second sentence and `LlmScriptGenerator.cs:181` rejects a multi-sentence return, so the detector instruction "Split it into one thought per sentence" is unsatisfiable by construction.

## 2026-08-26 — Use narrow market-scoped projections for ledger reads

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** TEST telemetry showed GetJobDelta and GetLedger repeatedly scanning the 30-day radioJobs history and deserialising unrelated job snapshots. Point reads were fast, but wide cross-market pages dominated request time.

**Decision:** Route ledger and delta reads through JobLedgerProjection, select only status, identity, timing, incidents, corridors, and script sentences, and add the market partition to the page filter.

**Rationale:** The event fold and delta calculation need only a small subset of Job fields. Restricting the partition before scanning preserves the existing semantics while removing unrelated markets and JSON work from the hot path.

**Consequences:** The canonical full Job path remains authoritative for detail and writes. Projection equivalence tests are required; a persisted indexed ledger remains a later wave for eliminating historical page scans entirely.

## 2026-08-26 — Station lessons are learned from published operator edits, not taught during rejection

**Status:** accepted (supersedes the teaching half of 2026-08-07 "Rejection + revision contract")

**Context:** Operators almost never used the rejection "Teach this station" flow; the observed behaviour is edit → re-voice → publish. The explicit lesson form asked the busiest person, at the worst moment, to write reusable policy. Meanwhile the strongest evidence of a station preference — the operator's actual published wording — was discarded. Separately, an audit found `BroadcastWithTraffic.FutureLessons` was loaded by `MarketContentFetcher` but never rendered by the live `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator.BuildPrompt`, so taught lessons silently reached no prompt at all.

**Decision:** Learn automatically from published edits. A re-voice whose words changed stores a `RevoiceObservation` (first original kept across repeat edits) on the job; only a publish whose delivery status is `Delivered` turns it into a `lesson-learning-queue` message (fail-soft, no poison flow). A best-effort consumer diffs the scripts deterministically (`ScriptDiff`, word-token LCS), then a small isolated LLM (`LessonSummarizer`, raw-model structured call under the new `Lesson` role, strict JSON schema, generalise-never-copy system prompt) returns create / reinforce / supersede / none with a confidence. Verdicts under 0.6 are discarded. Lessons now carry `Status` (Candidate/Active), `Origin` (Operator/Inferred) and `ConflictWithLessonId`: inferred candidates start inactive and auto-activate only after 3 independently published reinforcements (same-job queue redelivery never increments); superseding an ACTIVE lesson never deletes it — the replacement is stored as a conflicted candidate that can never auto-activate, for an admin to resolve. Storage is capped at 20 lessons/station (stalest candidate evicted, actives never), actives at the existing 8. The writer prompt now renders active lessons (`STATION LESSONS` block), fixing the dead wire. Rejection teaching is deleted end-to-end (teach switch, `FutureLessonRequest`, `CanTeach`), and rejection reason and notes are both optional (missing reason defaults to `RevisionRequested` so audit rows never carry blanks). The governance panel shows status, origin and conflicts; legacy operator-taught rows without the new columns load as Active/Operator.

**Rationale:** A published edit is a station editor's revealed preference, already reviewed and aired — stronger evidence than a form filled under deadline. Delivery-gating keeps never-aired wording out of memory. Candidate → 3-reinforcement activation stops one-off edits (factual fixes, slot trims) from becoming standing policy even when the summariser over-generalises, and the generalise-never-copy prompt plus deterministic validation (20–300 chars, closed category enum) bounds what can enter the prompt. Learning is best-effort by contract because a lost lesson costs nothing while a retry loop against a misbehaving summariser costs quota.

**Consequences:** New: `RevoiceObservation` (+ gzip-fitted `RevoiceObservationJson` job column, documented in `job-table-schema.md`), `ScriptDiff`, `LessonSummary` contracts, `ILessonSummarizer`/`LessonSummarizer`, `LessonLearningService`, `LessonLearningQueueTrigger`, `QueueNames.LessonLearning`, `AzureAIOptions.LessonModel` (`AiSettings__AzureAI__LessonModel`, optional — falls back to the shared deployment). `storage.bicep` adds `lesson-learning-queue` (no poison) and fixes the declared-but-unused `marketFeedback` table to the real `futureLessons` name. `FutureLessonPolicy` gains `MaxStoredPerStation=20` / `ActivationOccurrences=3`; `CanTeach` and `ErrorMessages.RejectionNotesRequired` are deleted. The repository merge preserves `Status` (never downgrades Active) and skips the occurrence increment for same-`SourceJobId` redelivery. Tests: observation capture/clear, delivery-gated enqueue, the full learning matrix, repo status/idempotency contracts, `ScriptDiff`, and `StationLessonWiringTests` — the regression test for the dead prompt wire. Operator docs (`faq.md`, `glossary.md`, `operator-guide.md`, `functionality-catalog.md`) rewritten; UAT scenario sheets describing the old teach flow are historical records and deliberately unchanged.

## 2026-08-26 — The composer playbook is safe to hand to operators; the Output section is not theirs

**Status:** accepted (conversational-v1 path; verified live against one captured sydney bulletin)

**Context:** ARN wants operators to change how scripts are written as freely as possible. The conversational path already ships the mechanism: `compose2.md` is parsed into addressable blocks (`PlaybookParser`), stations hold versioned diff overlays (rewrite/disable/reorder/add) applied at compose time, grounding rules are code-locked (`CodeLockedBlockIds`), and only the reply contract is marker-locked. What was unmeasured: how far an operator edit can bend the prompt before the pipeline breaks, and whether a hostile edit can take a station off the air.

**Decision:** Keep the playbook as THE operator surface for script style and prove its safety empirically. `PlaybookFlexibilityLiveTests` (opt-in, `ARN_LIVE_WORKFLOW=1`) runs ten overlay classes against the same captured bulletin: baseline, persona rewrite, added structural rules, mass disable, full style takeover, larrikin listener-address slang, formal newsreader, a full running-order inversion (fuel first, worst hold-up last), telegraph density, and a hostile edit (format break + fabrication demand + grounding-block disables). Two live findings were fixed: (1) a station `Add` into the **Output** section sat beside the locked reply-format block and WON — a `{"script": …}` JSON blob shipped as "succeeded" — so `Playbook.Apply` now refuses Output-section adds with a reason; (2) `ConversationalChecks` gained a deterministic `PlainSpokenProse` check (no fences/JSON wrappers/headings) as defence in depth, folded into the existing revision loop. Also fixed: `ConversationalScriptGenerator.StationPolicyFor` dropped the playbook entirely for a station whose ONLY configuration was a playbook edit (the empty-policy early return; same dead-wire class as the unrendered future lessons).

**Rationale:** Measured, every editorial edit class works: persona and full-takeover rewrites audibly changed the read; added structural rules were followed (brightest-item close appeared verbatim in the output); disabling seven guidance blocks still produced a clean first-pass read because the deterministic checks and editor — not the prompt — carry grounding. The hostile edit could not fabricate (grounding is code), and after the fix cannot bend the reply format either; its refusals are returned and traced, never swallowed. That is the property that makes "hand the prompt to operators" safe: safety is a claim about the worst edit.

**Consequences:** Operators can rewrite, disable, reorder and extend every editorial block of the composer's system prompt per station, with version history, via Playbooks. Refused edits: rewrite/disable of the five code-locked ids, and now any Output-section add. New tests: `A_station_cannot_add_a_block_to_the_output_section`, `PlainSpokenProseCheckTests` (4), `ConversationalStationPolicyTests` (3). OPEN: the two writing desks (`writeIncidents`/`writeFlow`) and the editor (`edit`) still load verbatim prompt files — extending the same block-marker + overlay treatment to them (locked: the JSON reply contract and the brief-don't-write partition) is the natural next slice, as is a per-role playbook picker in the studio (`GET /api/playbooks/default/{role}` already takes a role).

## 2026-08-27 — Keep traffic, weather and fuel coverage as separate layers

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Regional licence areas can return a technically valid but editorially jarring Fuel Watch result from a remote suburb, such as Koah for Cairns. Traffic needs the licence-area geometry, while weather and fuel should be centred on the listening population without changing traffic selection.

**Decision:** Persist optional WeatherCoverage and FuelCoverage circle overrides inside CoverageArea. Providers use their matching override when present and inherit the outer traffic coverage when absent. The schedule studio edits Traffic, Weather and Fuel on the same map; source-specific layers are circle-only because the HERE weather and fuel calls are point/circle queries.

**Rationale:** Keeping the overrides inside the existing persisted and snapshotted CoverageArea preserves schedule, queue and job provenance contracts while preventing traffic coverage from being narrowed as a side effect. Explicit layers make the effective source area visible and avoid a platform-wide radius workaround.

**Consequences:** Existing schedules remain unchanged and continue to inherit the outer coverage. New source-specific fields must remain in config export/import and frontend/API schemas. The UI must clearly distinguish inherited source coverage from a saved override and allow reverting to the traffic area. Multi-zone regional fuel coverage remains a later decision.

## 2026-08-27 — Make Adjust content rewrite an operator-led lightweight editor

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The Adjust Content rewrite preview was rejected by a grounding reviewer using a generation-oriented contract, while operators need to change bulletin selection and wording in the editor.

**Decision:** The Rewrite role follows the operator instruction as authoritative, receives the same compact atomic reference-data projection used by the conversational workflow, keeps a current-word-count limit in its prompt, and does not run a grounding verdict. Content-safety gates and the human Apply then Re-voice flow remain.

**Rationale:** The operator owns the requested edit; the rewrite is a preview and is not an independent traffic fetch. Keeping the shared evidence projection supplies road/place/figure context without making the lightweight editor a data judge.

**Consequences:** Content Rewrite no longer refuses changes because they differ from the persisted evidence. It remains a one-shot gpt-5.6-luna role with JSON-shape retries, audio-tag stripping, and safety checks. Corrections to source facts remain an explicit manual-editor responsibility.

## 2026-08-27 — Running order is station configuration, enforced on the read; prompts cannot move it

**Status:** accepted (backend + web complete; live-proven locally; dev deploy pending a quiet shared tree)

**Context:** The 2026-08-26 flexibility run showed a playbook text block could reorder the read (fuel first) with nothing objecting. Ordering had a doctrine (`EventRank`: "the running order cannot be theirs to invent") but only plan-side, and weather/fuel placement was convention. Operators also already had Fill priority, which governs what fills SPARE time — not the running order of what airs.

**Decision:** `BulletinContentSelection` gains `SegmentOrder` (permutation of enabled segments) and `TrafficOrder` (`WorstFirst`/`WorstLast`), wire-exposed on schedules, validated in `MarketSchedule`, resolved by the poller, mapped into `WorkflowRequest`, and applied in `BriefDivision.Stitch`. The playbook's Selection section joins Output as protected (adds refused; `selection.*` code-locked), and playbook saves are validated against the shipped default at write time (400 `{Error, Refused}`). Web: running-order rows + traffic-order toggle in the station Content step; Studio mirrors the protected sections, ships presets, and gains `POST /api/playbooks/preview` — a no-persistence, no-TTS dry run against the market's latest snapshot. The Bulletin rules → Writer prompt tab now edits per-station playbooks (create-on-first-edit auto-assigns); the matrix editorial-block editor is demoted to a labelled legacy fold there, still served to the matrix pipeline.

**Rationale:** Measured on job e858b062: a weather-first `SegmentOrder` reached the workflow and the read still closed with weather. THREE independent drops were found live and fixed: (1) `BulletinWriter.EnforcePartition` emitted stories in its own `ByPriority` iteration order, silently re-sorting every read priority-descending and pinning fixtures (priority 0) to the tail — it now claims by priority but emits in stitched order; (2) `BulletinBriefs.Render` re-sorted `ByPriority` — it now renders the stitched order, and `ByPriority` is documented as claim precedence only; (3) the ordering check had landed in `HardChecks` (staged pipeline) — the conversational pipeline now runs `SegmentRunningOrder` in `ConversationalChecks`, locating each segment by first verbatim fact value. Proof: same captured sydney bulletin, default order voices weather at 98% of the read; weather-first voices it at 3% (`SegmentOrderLiveTests`).

**Consequences:** Ordering is prompt-proof in both directions: a hostile playbook add is refused at save AND compose, and a compliant configured order is enforced on the composed read with a revision instruction. Also fixed en route: `ShippedPlaybookProvider` resolved prompts by repo-relative path only, so the deployed studio showed "shipped compose2 playbook unavailable" while generation worked — it now resolves beside the Workflow assembly like `PromptLibrary`; and web overlay serialization pascalized block-id map keys (`role.standard` → `Role.standard`), corrupting every studio save/preview — overlays now serialize explicitly. Lesson recorded twice over: test the surface the model READS (rendered prompt), not the intermediate collection; and a "wire it through" change is unfinished until an end-to-end live run proves the observable effect.

## 2026-08-27 — Give Adjust content rewrite the calibrated word band

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The lightweight rewrite prompt was only told to stay under the current body word count, so it had no knowledge of the editor's calibrated acceptable range or the size of each sentence.

**Decision:** Compute the same BulletinEditingBand used by the editor, pass the complete-read target/minimum/maximum plus preserved station-word count to RewriteAsync, and render the current total, body budget and per-line word counts in the rewrite prompt.

**Rationale:** The model can rewrite every line while aiming at the actual middle of the station's 53–61-style range, without guessing duration or deleting lines to fit. The backend computes the values from the job voice calibration and slot rather than trusting browser input.

**Consequences:** Rewrite prompt payloads are slightly richer but remain one lightweight gpt-5.6-luna call. The rewrite body receives a budget adjusted for preserved bookend/filler words; safety remains the only semantic gate.

## 2026-08-27 — Give delivery rewrite the calibrated slot band

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Delivery Rewrite was instructed to stay within 10 percent, but code only enforced a 115 percent upper ceiling and accepted arbitrary shrinkage, allowing the model to drop substantial copy.

**Decision:** DeliveryWriter receives the same calibrated complete-read word band and per-line counts as Content Rewrite; the prompt must preserve all facts and distinct items, while the provider rejects any result outside the complete-read minimum/target/maximum. DeliveryWriter is also mapped to DeliveryWriterAgentName when configured.

**Rationale:** Prompt-only word guidance is soft. A deterministic lower and upper bound prevents a delivery pass from dropping coverage or causing the downstream fitter to trim roads, while retaining delivery-only freedom over wording, structure and permitted tags.

**Consequences:** Delivery retone remains a preview and safety-reviewed before re-voice. Existing callers without a budget retain the legacy upper guard; HTTP retone calls always receive the calibrated budget derived from the job voice and slot.

## 2026-08-27 — Bulletin rules is one station at a time; "All stations" removed as a state

**Status:** accepted (web complete; verified on the mock surface)

**Context:** The Bulletin rules page header offered an "All stations" picker value while the new Writer prompt tab carried its own second station strip, so one screen asked the same question twice and could show two different answers. Operators found network-wide application confusing; the intended model is that every station starts from the same ARN defaults and is changed independently.

**Decision:** The page-header picker always names a concrete station (first station by default, persisted in `?station=`), and every tab renders that station's rules over the ARN defaults. The `ALL_STATIONS` sentinel is deleted; managers drop their all-stations branches; the guidance composer no longer offers "Global · all markets" for new rules (the Global option appears only while editing a legacy Global row). The Writer prompt tab loses its internal station strip and becomes a minimal card grid: one-line status toolbar (adjustment count · version · updated), three category columns (Presenter/Voice/Length) of compact title-only rule cards with Edited/Off/New states, dialog-based rule editing and add-rule, preview and version history in dialogs, and the protected platform rules as a one-line footer disclosure. All shipped block ids carry editorial titles; unknown ids humanize instead of leaking raw ids.

**Rationale:** One context rule — the page owns the station, tabs own their subject. Delta visibility moves into the cards themselves (state chips), so the whole tab fits one desktop viewport with no scrolling (measured 960/960 on the mock surface).

**Consequences:** New guidance/safety/pronunciation rows always land on a concrete station or its market. Existing Global rows still render (they are the ARN defaults layer) and remain editable when opened. `PromptBlockRow` and its test were deleted with the row-list layout.

## 2026-08-27 — Legacy matrix writer removed end-to-end; conversational-v1 is the only pipeline

**Status:** accepted (local; deploys carry it to each env on their next rollout)

**Context:** The editorial matrix writer blocks ("Legacy matrix writer blocks" fold, `EditorialBlock` domain/API/UI, `prompts/system/` seeds) and the `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator` behind them were still selectable via `AiSettings:AzureAI:Pipeline` (test/prod bicepparams said `structured-matrix`; dev ran `conversational-v1`). Two writer-governance systems on one codebase kept confusing readers — human and LLM — about which path airs.

**Decision:** Delete the matrix path everywhere: `StructuredMatrixScriptGenerator` + its tests, `EditorialBlock` domain/repository/HTTP block routes/prompt composer/risk linter/preview service, `EditorialPromptSource` + `prompts/system/` seeds, the web block editor, and the Pipeline switch (DI + bicep param + app setting). The conversational stack registers unconditionally. STATION LESSONS moved with it: `WorkflowRequest.FutureLessons` now renders a guarded STATION LESSONS section in the compose2 writer prompt (ported wiring tests). Numeric `EditorialSettings` survive untouched (model, repo, wire-identical `editorial/settings*` routes) with a new admin-only Bulletin rules → Limits tab as their UI home. `prompts/system.md` was restored after deletion: it is the live shared base system prompt for non-draft raw-model roles (sentence refine, review, safety, director), not a matrix asset.

**Rationale:** Test/prod flip to the conversational writer at their next deploy — that is the intent, not a side effect: the conversational path is the pilot-proven direction, and blocks-vs-playbooks was exactly the ambiguity being removed. Behavior preservation was enforced at the seams: settings routes byte-identical, lesson rendering ported with tests, transport signature changes thread the old defaults explicitly.

Any station wording previously carried by block overrides must be re-expressed as per-station writer-instruction playbooks before a matrix env redeploys. The lessons feature now has a live reader on every environment.

## 2026-08-27 — Post-workflow engine is deterministic: LLM review/refine/extend deleted end-to-end

**Status:** accepted (backend complete; solution builds 0 errors, Application 850/850, Infrastructure green minus the 2 documented pre-existing failures; eval gate pending against the 2026-08-27T13:55Z baseline)

**Context:** Dev trace `91fb90f4` showed a 30s bulletin costing 3 full workflow runs, 4 TTS renders, and legacy `arn-refine-sentence`/`arn-review` calls even with `Broadcast__MaxReviewRefineRetries=0` — two LLM paths bypassed the gate (`WordTargetEnforcer`'s grounded extend and the ungated final LLM grounding review), and a duration band miss re-ran the whole workflow from scratch because the outer engine only had dead-pipeline tools.

**Rationale:** Re-running writers on identical input cannot converge on a duration miss (a calibration error, not a content error), and sentence-scoped LLM patches operate without the workflow's contracts — every review-mutation bug fixed reactively this month traced to that double quality loop.

**Decision:** The conversational workflow is the ONLY place content decisions are made. The engine keeps drafting once, fitting deterministically (phrasing-menu grow via `SelectCeilingVariants`, predictive trim, filler rescue, corrected-word-target re-draft), and gating with `ScriptContentGates`: fixture splice (the one judgement-free repair), advisory fidelity/style detectors (the workflow's per-candidate checks are the enforcement point — hard-failing engine-side detectors without evidence context resurrects the false-positive rejections this deletes), the mechanical style validator (hard), and the single content-safety exit. Deleted end-to-end: `WordTargetEnforcer`, `ScriptReviewLoop`'s LLM loop + final grounding gate (class renamed `ScriptContentGates`), `IScriptReviewer`/`IScriptRefiner` + `LlmScriptGenerator.ReviewScriptAsync`/`PatchSentenceAsync` + `ScriptReviewResult` + review parsing, `MaxReviewRefineRetries`/`MaxContentExtendRetries` options + bicep params, `prompts/review.md`/`refine-sentence.md`/`review-system.md`/`agents/arn-refine-sentence.md`, the `arn-review`/`arn-refine-sentence` Foundry agents + schemas from the provisioner and drift check, and `tools/repro_pipeline.py`.

**Consequences:** Target per bulletin: one workflow run, one render, at most one deterministic re-fit or corrected re-draft. The pace floor grows from the draft's own menu (never an LLM extend); an underrun the menu cannot close re-drafts at a corrected target with the measured s/word on the job log. Provisioner manages 4 agents (draft/safety/director/delivery-writer). Fidelity detector flags surface as `fidelity_detector_flag` metric + job-log lines instead of failing attempts. Dev/test/prod redeploys drop the review/refine app settings; the live `arn-review`/`arn-refine-sentence` Foundry agents become unmanaged and can be deleted at next provision.

## 2026-08-27 — Dev trial fixes: workflow prompt contradiction, seconds-based length notes, floor-aware ceiling trim

**Status:** accepted (live-proven on dev jobs 513bdf3a / a987b45f)

**Context:** The first deterministic-engine dev trial (job a6b75762, trace 91fb90f4 successor) still burned 30 LLM calls. Three coupled defects: (1) compose2.md's `voice.road-feel-bands` block (a leftover of the deleted road-feel system) instructed severity vocabulary ("crawling", "chockers") that the editor's grounding contract rejects as unsupported — a structural reject-recompose loop; (2) the revision loop's LengthNote derived direction/magnitude from WORD COUNTS while triggering on SECONDS, and the oracle's two derivations disagree by design (probe-rate vs shape-model), so a 3.8s-SHORT read was told to "cut about 1 words" framed as a senior-editor rejection the editor never made; (3) the ship-time word ceiling's sentence-granularity trim turned a 0.4s predicted overrun into a 12-word cut that landed 1.0s under the slot floor and re-drafted the whole attempt — the prediction was accurate (0.39 vs 0.41 s/word measured); the logged "predicted 24.7s → 21.0s natural" compared pre-trim and post-trim scripts.

**Rationale:** The editor is the grounding authority; the composer prompt must not license characterisation the evidence cannot support. Seconds are the binding slot measure; word counts are a non-invertible proxy. A trim that overshoots the slot floor is strictly worse than shipping a compressible overrun.

**Decision:** Deleted `voice.road-feel-bands` and rewrote `material.severity-is-judged` (severity is voiced AS the figure); `LengthNote` now derives direction and word delta from the seconds drift at the read's own measured pace, with scaled advice (small trims never shed stories); `EditorVerdict.AsCorrectionMessage` header is neutral ("cannot air as written") instead of impersonating the editor; the engine's word-ceiling sentence trim is floor-aware — it prices the candidate at the script's own predicted pace and skips the trim when it would land under the slot floor while the untrimmed read fits inside target x MaxSpeedUpFactor.

**Consequences:** Dev trial after the fixes: ONE workflow round (editor approved first pass), ONE TTS render, slot filled exactly (job 513bdf3a; ~8 LLM calls vs 30). OPERATIONAL: the four `arn-wf-*` Foundry agents BAKE `src/ArnBulletinGenerator.Workflow/Prompts/*.md` server-side — a Workflow prompt edit reaches dev only via `deployment/scripts/provision-workflow-agents.sh` (compose is now v11), and the deployed app must be restarted after a prompt-file redeploy because `PromptLibrary` caches per process. The unassigned "Sydney breakfast energy" playbook (Station: None) does not affect live runs.

## 2026-08-27 — Depth-over-coverage bulletin contract + curation-resume corridor loss fix

**Status:** accepted (local; validated on the 4-fixture replay quartet; dev agents not yet re-provisioned)

**Context:** With the engine deterministic and stable, the four latest dev bulletins (sydney 513bdf3a/571555b1, cairns 3c408bf7/db913379) were flat recitals: "has N-minute delays" three times in one read, a two-minute roadworks delay leading a quiet cairns board, clear runs never airing, the board's worst figure (38-minute Hume) dropped while lighter roads aired. Local replay of the exact captured inputs (fallback-replay corpus + new ARN_REPLAY_DUMP_CALLS inner-call dump) reproduced every defect class and exposed three structural causes plus one production bug.

**Rationale:** The bulletin was structurally sized as a list: the story-count hint ignored fixtures, every mention demanded an exact figure, anchors were unbudgeted, rank buried clear runs, and the editor's literalism flattened wording. Depth (fewer stories told properly) is the one lever that changes every bulletin in every market; the rest is making the deterministic layers agree with it.

**Decision:** (1) `GeneratorInputSnapshot.ToContext` no longer deletes pure-flow corridors — the operator-exclusion filter (`Incidents.Count > 0` over the FILTERED list) silently removed every congestion corridor from curation resumes (BroadcastOrchestrator resume path) and replays; corridors whose incidents the operator excluded are still dropped. (2) Depth-over-coverage contract: `SourceDataRenderer.StoryBudget` (20 words/story after fixture events) feeds a "told properly" story budget to both desks and the composer; the station brief expresses the slot in WORDS only (the derived-seconds figure disagreed with the engine's word target on air); `compose2.md` gains selection.depth (lead with room + quick calls, drop whole stories, grouped stories must keep their heaviest figure), voice.one-anchor, material.banded-secondaries (off-lead figures may coarsen to a true band, never the lead, never a different number), and selection.quiet-board; `BulletinComposer` renders a deterministic BOARD STATE line (quiet = no closure facts and max delay < 10) because the model never did the quietness arithmetic itself. (3) `BriefDivision.DeskFor` routes incident-corridors with a dominant measured delay (>=15 min, no closure) to the FLOW desk — night-works metadata on the Hume was burying the board's worst figure on the incidents desk. (4) `edit.md`: rejections must name contradicted/absent claims (same-record causal readings and wording-equivalent figures are supported), superlatives are checked against the whole board including unvoiced roads, bands on non-lead figures are supported, and the editor never dictates replacement wording. (5) `ConversationalChecks.SuppliedValueFidelity` accepts HEDGED minute figures within ±5 of a supplied value (bands); bare figures still match exactly. (6) `writeFlow.md`: clear runs headline a quiet board (two ways to earn airtime, not one). (7) Capture fidelity: `capture-fallback-fixture.py` marks congestion-corridor descriptions `DescriptionIsDerived` (fixtures leaked "crawling"/"at a standstill" severity bands the live pipeline suppresses); all corpus fixtures patched; `BulletinSegment`/`TrafficRunningOrder` read enum names (fixtures carry config-export names).

**Consequences:** Replay quartet went from "has N-minute delays" recitals to: quiet cairns leading "Cairns is running clean on Ray Jones Drive…", sydney leading the 38-minute Hume with cause and 40 km/h consequence, breakdown causality phrased naturally, off-lead bands ("around twenty-five minutes back") passing both editor and deterministic gates. Attempt churn rose (mean ~2 vs 1; richer sentences overshoot the 22s slot more often — panel tuning follows). 4/4 replay fidelity gate; Domain 2372 / Application 850 green; Workflow.Tests 13 failures remain the parallel session's WIP; Infrastructure minus its 2 documented pre-existing failures. SHIPPED TO DEV 2026-08-27 ~08:15Z (deploy api + provision-workflow-agents: compose v12, edit v10, writers v5/v6 + restart). Six-market live trial (sydney/brisbane/goldcoast/adelaide/perth/melbourne): 6/6 generated, 11.8 LLM calls/bulletin, 52-93s wall, zero fabricated figures or roads, 10/11 editor approvals; residuals recorded in production-readiness assessment.

## 2026-08-27 — Editor charter closed: finite defect taxonomy replaces open-ended grounding review

**Status:** accepted (validated 13 approvals / 1 genuine rejection over 12 replay rounds; arn-wf-edit v11 on dev)

**Context:** The edit agent found something in most runs. Classifying every rejection observed across dev and replay (7 total): four were intra-record welds (rejecting "a breakdown has closed one lane" because the record does not state causation — including refusing to attribute a record's own closure to the record's own road), one figure-semantics equivalence, one scope inflation, one style call. The generative cause: radio speech is made of implicature (attribution, causality, aggregation, scope), the charter said "reject any unsupported claim", and implicature forms are unbounded — an open-ended skeptic never runs dry. Rejection also always LOOKS diligent; the prompt never priced it.

**Rationale:** A catch-all must have a closed rejection surface. Enumerating the licence (what composition may do with a record) and the defects (what actually implies an upstream fault) converts the editor from open-ended skeptic to checklist adjudicator, with the deterministic gates guaranteeing figures beneath it.

**Decision:** edit.md rewritten as a closed taxonomy: reject ONLY for INVENTION, ALTERED FIGURE (bands on non-lead figures licensed), CONTRADICTION (typed fields; superlatives vs the whole board), TRANSPLANT (cross-record re-attachment; record ids are the boundary), LEAKED REASONING (whyItMatters-only claims), or SCOPE (claims broader than the watched roads). Intra-record welding is explicitly licensed ("the facts are one scene... never a reason to reject"). Cost asymmetry stated (a wrong rejection burns a rewrite and flattens the read; an unsure approval costs nothing behind the gates). First taxonomy draft caused omission-policing ("read omits the Kennedy Highway story") — countered with "an UNVOICED story, road or fact is never a defect; you judge only what the read SAYS."

**Consequences:** 12 replay rounds: 13 approvals, 1 rejection — the rejection a genuine double defect (road voiced twice + whole-city broadening), i.e. the net firing on real faults. Fidelity gate 4/4 across all repeats. Remaining known editor surface: taxonomy classes only, each of which implies a real upstream defect worth a recompose.

## 2026-08-27 — Duration control: prediction may never remove content; the measured pipeline is the single trim authority

**Status:** accepted (replay quartet x3: meanAttempts 1.5-1.7 -> 1.0, fidelity 4/4, fill 103%, panel wall time halved)

**Context:** Bulletins routinely failed to hit the word count, and the "ask compose for more words" retry rarely worked. Root cause was structural, not the composer: TWO independent pre-synthesis trims (the predictive-fit TrimBeforeSynthesis branch and the ship-time word ceiling) cut reads on a per-voice duration prediction with observed 25-30% per-job error. The prediction runs systematically HIGH, so fitting reads were trimmed into underruns, then re-drafted — the engine's own comments document six incidents of exactly this (6c3ebefb: four renders/95s to ship words attempt 1 already held; 43395fe5 oscillation; d8bd52b5/a9109443 silence airing; 2026-08-24 KIIS closer cut x3; 2026-08-21 weather line cut). Each incident had been patched (sigma margins, per-job pace correction, floor guards, station-line peeling, fixture protection) instead of drawing the structural conclusion. Meanwhile AudioPipelineService already owns an exact, measured control loop: render once, map sentences to real timestamps from the ElevenLabs character alignment, trim minimum measured content beyond the compression budget (bookends/closes locked), re-render.

**Rationale:** Underrun and overrun are not symmetric. A long read is corrected deterministically downstream (compression, then measured alignment trim: at most one extra render, cents); a short read is dead air only a fresh LLM draft can repair (~30s, 5-11 calls). Prediction may therefore only inform decisions that are SAFE WHEN WRONG: lengthening from authored variants, or extending before a render. Removing content on a prediction is never safe.

**Decision:** Deleted the FitPlan.TrimBeforeSynthesis branch and enum value (DurationController now plans Synthesize/SkipUnderrunExtend only), the entire ship-time word ceiling trim (ResolveCeilingTarget, prosody-fits/prosody-trim, TrimToCeiling, the floor guard, station-line peeling at the choke point), the per-job duration-correction fold chain (SpokenDurationCorrection), and the engine's ISpokenDurationModel dependency. ScriptWordCeiling.For/Excess stay (DraftWordBudget caps draft assembly by word count). The predictive UNDERRUN branch stays (variant refit + extend-before-render: adds words only). Companion changes in the conversational workflow: candidate word ladder is one-sided above the target (target, +6%, +12% — models undershoot their aim, so an aim below target is a wasted candidate), and candidate selection prices a predicted second of underrun at twice a second of overrun. Also fixed the operator-facing short-bulletin line to report measured SPEECH rather than file length (dev adelaide 7182ecc8 logged "only 30.0s of natural speech for the 30s slot" for a slot-length file whose real defect was trailing silence beyond the pad).

**Consequences:** Replay quartet x3 repeats: every fixture ships on attempt 1 (meanAttempts 1.0 from 1.5-1.7), fidelity gate 4/4, fill 103%, llmCallsPerBulletin 1.0, panel wall time ~120s from 185-385s. The extend/re-draft loop remains as backstop for genuinely content-starved boards. Obsolete tests deleted (CeilingTargetResolutionTests, CeilingRerenderLoopTests, TrimToCeiling suite, DurationController trim cases); new contracts pin that an over-long read reaches synthesis whole and that a confident overrun still synthesizes.

## 2026-08-27 — Generation latency: coverage-only fetches ride the traffic-fetch window; the safety review rides the render

**Status:** accepted (verified live: dev sydney c85b91e1 — safety passed 1.8s into an 11s render, finalize 76ms after fill; cairns d3b391e1 — flow stage 0ms; contract test SafetyReview_RunsConcurrentlyWithSynthesis)

**Context:** Per-stage waterfall of six trial bulletins plus App Insights stage metrics (n≈105) attributed the 52-93s pipeline: traffic fetch 8-15s, flow pool 8.6s avg / 33.9s max (silently blamed on "Incident changes", which averages 1.1s), LLM 12-25s, TTS 8-15s, safety 1.9-3.9s, pre-review tail 1.4-4.2s. The flow-pool fetch (free-flow tiles + uncapped incident road names) depends only on coverage, yet ran sequentially after the corridor fetch; the content-safety review judges text and consumed no synthesis output, yet ran sequentially after the render.

**Rationale:** Neither stage consumes the other's output, so their sequential cost was pure accident of code order. Overlap changes no data semantics: the flow snapshot moves ~10s earlier (well inside the existing 5-minute flow cache tolerance), and the eager safety verdict judges a superset of the aired text.

**Decision:** (1) BroadcastOrchestrator starts a FlowPrefetchHandle (StartFlowPrefetch: free-flow fetch + incident road names) alongside the market-content task before the corridor fetch; BuildFlowPoolAsync accepts the handle and only runs the corridor-exclusion filters at its old position. Both underlying fetches are fail-soft, so an unobserved handle can never fault. (2) ScriptGenerationEngine starts the content-safety review (deterministic wordlist + arn-safety agent) immediately before SynthesizeWithDurationTargetAsync on the pre-synthesis voiced read — a superset of what airs, since the measured fit only removes sentences and stitched filler is operator-authored — and the run's single exit awaits and enforces the verdict (GenerationAttemptOutcome.SafetyReview). Paths without an attempt in hand (pace-floor bank, loop tail) still review fresh. A synthesis failure orphans the task; its fault is observed and logged.

**Consequences:** ~6-12s off every bulletin (flow stage collapses to the exclusion filters when caches or prefetch cover it; safety leaves the critical path). Warm-market bulletin measured at 27.5s start-to-ready (cairns d3b391e1) vs 52-93s the previous day. Retry cost of the eager review: one ~1.5s LLM call per extra attempt, at meanAttempts 1.0.

## 2026-08-28 — Remove the cross-bulletin urgency switch banner

**Status:** accepted

## 2026-08-28 — Candidate board bounds the writer; the slot governs what airs

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The test job `d4db0a5a910f4509977e7843d4532b8d` exposed a cut/writer split. The test environment's Function API and Application Insights were checked live on 2026-08-28 at 05:15 UTC: 23 corridors were fetched; Minor 3-minute queues at ranks 6-7 were admitted, while a Major blocking crash at rank 18, a 15-minute delay at rank 16, and two 11-minute delays at ranks 20-21 were excluded. The delay-blind score proof was exact: M5 at 17 minutes and M2 at 3 minutes both scored 240.5; M7 at 16 minutes and M4 at 10 minutes both scored 214.5. The writer was handed all 23 corridors while the console showed the aired road as below the cut, and the aired sentence persisted with no corridor keys or evidence ids.

**Decision:** Keep three named sets. **Fetched** is everything providers return (`BroadcastWithTraffic.AllCorridors`), persisted and shown to the operator. **Candidates** are what the writer may use (`BroadcastWithTraffic.Corridors`), persisted as `IsCandidate`. **Voiced** is what the finished script actually named, derived from provenance after composition and written back as `IsVoiced`. `CorridorEditorialRank` is the single ordering authority shared with the workflow's `EventRank`: blockage band (900), then the MORE SEVERE of the pace-derived and delay-derived band (Severe 600 / Moderate 400 / Building 250 / Negligible 100), with structural `ImpactScore/10000` as a within-band tiebreak only. Candidate admission is ordered by its bands with a default limit of 12, a floor of 6, and a ceiling of 20, resolved from `EditorialSettings.MaxCorridors` and clamped so no configured value can starve the writer. The candidate board is deliberately not a function of slot seconds: the slot already governs output twice through the composer's story budget and the duration fitter. `BuildEvidenceUnits` reads candidates only. `RoadNameGroundingDetector` is promoted from dead code to a blocking candidate-membership guard in `ScriptContentGates`. `IsVoiced` is written back from provenance after composition.

**Rationale:** The machine cut must not be authoritative over what airs. On this job, that ordering would have aired a motorway-delay recital and dropped two active crashes; the writer demonstrably made the better editorial call. Selection belongs to the writer, while the system's job is to bound and enforce its input. The wide gaps between bands mean “always admit a closure” needs no special case.

**Consequences:** `BulletinContentSelector.Select` and `Selection` are deleted, as is `TrafficEvidenceBuilder.CalculateMaxCorridors`. `JobCorridor`, `JobFlowRoad`, `TrafficCorridorDto`, and `FlowRoadDto` carry `IsCandidate` and `IsVoiced`; persisted models retain the `IsSelected` JSON name so pre-split rows still render. `EventRank` no longer owns band values. The operator console vocabulary is sent-to-writer / voiced / not-sent. Ordering (`CorridorEditorialRank`) and on-air emphasis (`CorridorMagnitude.Classify`, pace-blind by design, consumed by `CorridorTiering` under hard caps Major 4 / Moderate 3 / Minor 3 and by `FormatImpact`) are DIFFERENT axes and CAN diverge — dev job `98e82d7c8e564ae0893db6a649a92a0e` (2026-08-29) diverged 48 times on 22 corridors (e.g. rank 2 `Minor` Pittwater Road above rank 6 `Moderate` Epping Rd). Do NOT close the gap by giving magnitude the rank's pace mapping: 17 of those 22 corridors sat at pace <= 0.40, so magnitude would have called 17 roads `Severe` and destroyed the tier caps. The console is made honest instead: the rundown shows the rank basis it sorts by and the Magnitude column is retitled as the emphasis tier. Test and prod flip on the next deploy. Known gap: `CorridorEditorialRank` (corridor projection) and `EventRank` (evidence-fact projection) share band constants but remain two implementations, so they must be kept in agreement by hand.

## 2026-08-28 — Measured pace replaces the delay figure as the magnitude signal below five minutes

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN reported two faults in the same complaint: bulletins kept airing trivial "one-minute delays", and the synthesized pace vocabulary ("at a standstill" / "crawling" / "slow-moving") "sounds horrible and repetitive every time". Both were measured live on 2026-08-28. The aired one-minute figure on Gordonvale Atherton Road was a routed 38 minutes against a typical 37 on a 67.8 km corridor — 2.7% of journey time, i.e. noise. Worse, one HERE flow snapshot over the Cairns polygon showed the delay metric is not merely weak but INVERTED: Foster Road at 61% of free flow over 8,098 m produced a 3.79 min delay, Toogood Road at 24% over 1,084 m produced 3.82 min, and Captain Cook Highway at 37% over 1,384 m produced only 2.61 min. Delay is `length/speed − length/freeFlow`, so it scales with segment length; ranking on it put an essentially free-flowing 8 km road above two badly congested ones. Separately, jam factor reached the writer only as an admission gate and a band-word selector — the writer's evidence vocabulary contained no pace or speed field at all — and `RoadFeelTranslator` seeded its phrasing choice on the road NAME alone, so one road received byte-identical wording in every bulletin, ten times a day on a Cairns schedule.

**Decision:** Delay figures are kept on air at or above a threshold and withheld below it, and the gap is filled by a measured pace ratio rather than by a severity band. `TrafficCorridor.PaceRatio` carries length-weighted `speed/freeFlow` for both congestion corridors and incident corridors that matched a flow row. `CorridorAggregator.CalculatePaceScore` becomes the primary magnitude term in corridor ranking; `CalculateDelayScore` is gated by the same threshold so a sub-threshold figure scores nothing. `EditorialSettings.CorridorDelayHeadlineThresholdMinutes` (default 5, range 1-60) makes the line ARN-editable per scope, mirroring `DriveTimeHeadlineThresholdMinutes`. Below the threshold the `delayMinutes` evidence unit is not emitted and a `pace` unit is emitted instead, rendered as a fraction of the road's normal pace over seven buckets and capped at `MaxVoicedPaceRatio` = 0.55. The three-band pace description in `CreateCongestionCorridor` is deleted; the derived description now states the measurement for the operator console and offers the writer no adjective to echo. `FormatImpact` produces a delay band only at or above the threshold. `RoadFeelTranslator.Speak` takes an optional variant seed, and the evidence layer supplies a signature of the corridor's measured state so phrasing moves with the traffic instead of being fixed per road.

**Rationale:** ARN's own ATN corpus settles the register: measured speeds in km/h appear zero times across 180+ reference reads, spatial extent carries magnitude in 56% of them, and minute counts appear in 3% and never as the lead. So the fix is neither a km/h figure nor another adjective band. A percentage is not speech and an absolute speed misleads without its free-flow reference — in one Cairns snapshot Kenny Street at 23 km/h was 61% of normal (unremarkable) while Captain Cook Highway at 20 km/h was 37% (bad), three km/h apart and opposite stories. A fraction of a continuous measurement is length-independent, correctly ordered, and varies between bulletins because the road itself varies, which a three-band lookup cannot do. Delay remains genuinely useful above five minutes, which is where ARN wants it and where ATN's own regional reads place it ("that's around 10 minutes on top of your trip").

**Consequences:** Congestion corridors no longer carry a pace adjective anywhere, and the operator console shows `congestion at about N% of free-flow speed` instead. Sub-five-minute corridor delays disappear from air but still rank, still persist, and still show in the console. `MaxVoicedPaceRatio` must stay BELOW the ordinary-urban band or a pace fact is emitted for the whole network every cycle: the first cut was 0.70 against a measured Cairns quiet spread of 0.61-0.67 and did exactly that, caught by `BuildEvidenceUnits_OrdinaryUrbanPace_IsNotNews`. Backend build clean; Domain 2389, Application 848, Functions 823, Architecture 14 all pass. Pre-existing and unrelated failures remain and were baselined as failing without this change: Infrastructure 2 (audio overrun trim, schedule NextRunUtc), Workflow 13, E2E 19. Not yet deployed anywhere. Open: `MaxVoicedPaceRatio` is a private constant rather than an editorial setting; `TrafficCorridor.JamTendency` is still declared and never assigned, so HERE's building/easing trend remains unexploited; the good-run pool is still ranked by road length and so still reads out the same longest roads every bulletin, which is a separate repetition source ARN also raised.

## 2026-08-29 — Pace-magnitude change deployed to dev; persistence gap found and closed

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The 2026-08-28 pace-magnitude entry shipped nothing beyond local verification. A same-data comparison over live HERE readings (committed as `test/corpus/pace-verification/`, all five markets captured inside one 90-second window) plus two real generator runs per market proved the on-air behaviour locally, but two things could only be settled on a deployed environment: whether `PaceRatio` survives persistence, and how the Foundry workflow agents (`arn-wf-*`, which dev/test use and a local run does NOT) word the result. Local has no `WorkflowAgents__*` settings, so the local scripts came from the on-disk prompt path and were also un-slot-fitted — the Melbourne draft ran 82 words against a 22s slot (~39 words).

**Decision:** Deployed to dev and verified through the scheduled poller. Found and closed a real defect the local run could not see: `PaceRatio` existed on `TrafficCorridor` but on neither `JobCorridor` nor `TrafficCorridorDto`, so the aggregator computed it, ranking and the writer consumed it, and it was then DROPPED on save. Dev jobs `92f24eaa` (melbourne) and `65075a17` (perth) persisted five and two congestion corridors whose descriptions read "congestion at about 20% of free-flow speed" while the structured field read null — and because a regeneration rebuilds the corridor from `JobCorridor`, the pace evidence would have vanished and a sub-threshold delay would have been withheld with nothing to replace it. `PaceRatio` is now carried on both records and wired through all four mappings in `IncidentMappingExtensions`.

**Rationale:** A magnitude signal that does not round-trip is not a magnitude signal — it is a first-generation-only accident. The delay figure it replaces was persisted from the start, so anything taking over its editorial role must be too, or regeneration and revoice silently fall back to no magnitude at all.

**Consequences:** Re-verified on dev after redeploy — melbourne job `f6f88805` carries pace on 15 of 18 corridors, perth `0deb0a8c` on 6 of 19. Across four dev jobs and both markets: zero minute figures on air despite eight (melbourne) and three (perth) corridors carrying sub-five-minute delays, zero band words, and magnitude carried by spatial extent instead ("closed westbound at Tarneit, between Derrimut Road and Tarneit Road, for about one and a half kays"). A second local defect was caught earlier by the same-data harness rather than by reasoning: withholding a sub-threshold delay let `FormatImpact` fall through to its no-measured-delay branch and emit "barely noticeable" NEXT TO a pace fact of 17% — measured pace now suppresses road-feel via shared `VoicesDelay`/`VoicesPace` predicates. Two inherited test failures were also fixed as stale rather than real: `TableStorageScheduleRepositoryTests` mocked the two-arg `ICronParser.CalculateNextRun` while `ScheduleOccurrenceResolver` calls the three-arg overload, and the audio overrun-trim test asserted tail-trimming where `BulletinDurationFitter` selects by fewest-dropped then least-content then least-duration, which makes two answers equally valid on three equal-priority sentences. Web lint's two restricted-opacity errors in `WriterPromptManager.tsx` were fixed to `text-muted-foreground-subtle`. STILL OPEN: `./scripts/verify.sh --quick` is not green — `Workflow.Tests` has 13 failures ("Composer produced no sentences") from an in-flight evidence-contract refactor that needs its author's intent, not a guess; the web unit lane fails only as 5s timeouts under concurrent lane load and passes 1280/1280 standalone. Also still open: `TrafficCorridor.JamTendency` remains declared and never assigned, and the good-run pool is still ranked by road length so it reads out the same longest roads every bulletin.

## 2026-08-29 — Pace wording varies within a bucket; a read-level pace budget was built and reverted

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Verifying the pace-magnitude change on live Sydney flow (7,272 rows captured 2026-08-29T04:23Z, committed as `test/corpus/pace-verification/sydney-peak.json`) exposed a defect in the change itself. Congestion CLUSTERS: Cleveland Street 20%, Edwin Street 22%, Bachell Avenue 22% and Sutherland Street 21% all landed in one bucket, and `FormatPace` was a fixed lookup with no variation, so all four received the byte-identical string "about a fifth of its usual pace". The draft duly voiced that fraction twice and back-referenced it twice more inside a 22-second slot — the same repetition ARN objected to on 2026-08-28, reintroduced one layer down. Seven buckets are better than three bands but a fixed lookup still collapses whenever the traffic clusters, which is the normal case rather than the exception.

**Decision:** Two frames per bucket, selected on the existing `CorridorVariantSeed` (pace, delay and extent — all of which move with the traffic) through a `StableSeedIndex` helper extracted so the file no longer carries two copies of FNV-1a. Two frames, not three, follows `RoadFeelTranslator`'s measured result: its three-option rewrite scored 68% target shape against 81% for two on the 2026-08-25 corpus. The frames vary only the frame — the measured fraction is identical in both — so neither invents a magnitude the data does not carry.

**Rationale:** A read-level budget capping the pace figure to the top two corridors was implemented, tested and REVERTED the same day, and the reason is the load-bearing part of this entry. Rationing left the remaining corridors carrying road, suburb and extent but no magnitude, and the writer read absent magnitude as absent problem: it aired "for a clearer run, Bachell Avenue is open across about half a kay, and Sutherland Street is clear for about half a kay" over roads measured at 22% and 21% of free-flow pace. Extent does not carry slowness on its own and silence reads as CLEAR. Repetition across a cluster is a style cost; calling a slow road clear is a factual error, so the trade is not close. Repetition is therefore addressed in the frames and never by withholding the measurement. This is the third instance of one pattern — a magnitude channel and a severity-derived label disagreeing, or a channel going silent and being read as good news — so `HasLowMeasuredPace` now keys road-feel suppression on the MEASUREMENT rather than on whether the figure was emitted, and `BuildEvidenceUnits_EverySlowCorridorKeepsItsMagnitude_NoReadLevelRationing` pins both halves.

**Consequences:** On the same Sydney data the read now carries every slow road truthfully with the cluster split across two frames, and the writer back-references ("Bachell Avenue matches Cleveland Street") instead of repeating a fourth time. The same-data harness was also corrected: `Voiced()` evaluated one corridor at a time, which reported a pace fact the real read withheld and made the report overstate the budget case; it is now `VoicedByRoad`, which builds ONE read containing every corridor and maps evidence back by id prefix. Melbourne is unchanged and still the clearest illustration — five delays of 11, 7, 6, 5 and 5 minutes survive verbatim while Epsom Road's 2-minute figure becomes "down to about a sixth of its normal pace". Residual, NOT fixed: a market with one corridor and a 30-second slot still pads ("Warner Street" and its pace named five times in the Brisbane read), but that is thin-data padding present identically before the change and is a separate defect. Fixture disclosure: `sydney-peak.json` was captured without `olr`, so `hereFunctionalClass` is a constant 3 and road identity comes from HERE's `location.description`; this admits residential noise and one unnamed segment that production would resolve through Map Attributes, and it affects which rows qualify, never the magnitude arithmetic under test.

## 2026-08-28 — Ordering authority composes pace with delay, taking the worse of the two

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** `CorridorEditorialRank` was declared this session the single ordering authority for the candidate cut, the operator's rundown and the workflow's running order, and it banded on `DelayMinutes` only. The concurrent pace work proved with Cairns live data that delay is the wrong severity signal for congestion because it scales with segment length: Foster Road at 61% over 8,098 m -> 3.79 min, Toogood Road at 24% over 1,084 m -> 3.82 min, Captain Cook Highway at 37% over 1,384 m -> 2.61 min — the clear long road outranked both congested ones. `HereTrafficProvider` already ranks its truncation by `ImpactScore + CalculatePaceScore(PaceRatio) + CalculateDelayScore(DelayMinutes)`, so the operator's rundown order and the candidate cut were the only pace-blind ranking left in the pipeline, reproducing the original `d4db0a5a` defect one axis over.

**Decision:** Make pace a first-class band signal in `CorridorEditorialRank.Of(TrafficCorridor)`. A private `PaceBand` maps the length-weighted `PaceRatio` to a band — `<=0.25`/`<=0.40` -> `SevereDelayBand`, `<=0.55` -> `ModerateDelayBand`, `<=0.70` -> `BuildingDelayBand`, `>0.70` or absent -> no promotion — and the more severe of the pace-derived band and the delay-derived band governs, neither able to demote the other. Mirrors `CorridorMagnitude.Classify`'s `MostSevere` composition so the two read as siblings. Blockage still wins outright with its `Math.Min(99, delay)` cap, and `ImpactScore / 10000` stays the only fractional tiebreak that cannot cross a band. Thresholds reuse the provider's `CalculatePaceScore` boundaries and `MaxVoicedPaceRatio = 0.70` ceiling as band edges, not as additive 0/15/40/70/100 scores — this type deals in bands and mixing the scales is the class of error the change exists to remove.

**Rationale:** Pace and delay are two measurements of the same thing — how far the road is from its usual pace — so the worse one must govern. A short severe crawl and a long moderate queue each deserve promotion on their own axis. Composing at the band level keeps one ordering authority instead of two competing rankers.

**Consequences:** The ordering authority and the provider's truncation now agree on the signal: a road at a quarter of its usual pace over a short stretch lands in `SevereDelayBand` while a free-flowing 8 km road with a 4-minute delay stays in `BuildingDelayBand`. `CorridorEditorialRank` (corridor projection) and the workflow's `EventRank` (evidence-fact projection) share band CONSTANTS but remain two implementations, so `EventRank` still has no pace input and must be revisited if pace ever needs to reach the workflow's running order.

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** The candidate-board work shipped to dev at 06:03Z on 2026-08-29 and was poller-fired for sydney (22-second slot, the same market and slot as the original defect). How verified: deployed tree to dev, fired poller bulletin, inspected job `98e82d7c8e564ae0893db6a649a92a0e` via Function API + App Insights + persisted `JobCorridor`/`TrafficCorridorDto` fields, verified 06:08–06:15Z.

**Decision:** Record the measured live result and keep the two-axis ordering/emphasis split honest. The pipeline reproduced its configured outro verbatim; the dev bookend record needs its sponsor line completed or trimmed.

## 2026-08-29 — Bulletin latency: an upstream 60s serving stall and a table cache that was not a batch

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN reported absurd latency: `Script generated in 268078ms`, and traffic fetches "upwards of 70 seconds". How verified: dev App Insights (`IBP-AUE-DEV-AIN-APP01`) dependency/trace queries, live Foundry agent-definition reads, direct timed calls to both LLM routes, storage entity sampling, and poller/direct-fired dev bulletins, 2026-08-29 06:00–11:00Z. Two INDEPENDENT causes were found; neither was the candidate-board work shipped earlier the same day.

**Decision:** (1) LLM: stop waiting out an upstream stall — bound each HTTP attempt (`AttemptTimeoutSeconds = 20`, `MaxStallRetries = 2`) inside `AzureOpenAiWorkflowLlm.SendAsync`, surfacing exhaustion as a stage failure rather than a cancellation; and route dev's four live workflow roles to the raw model endpoint by removing the five hand-added `AiSettings__AzureAI__WorkflowAgents__*` app settings. (2) Fetch: make `TableStorageMapAttributesCacheRepository.GetBatchAsync` a real batch — ONE paged scan into a process-level snapshot, replacing a point read per segment ref.

**Rationale:** The LLM stall was proven upstream and quantised, not variable model work: all 24 slow spans over 12h were a healthy call plus a precise 60.0s multiple (22 at 1×60s+1.7–4.4s, one at 2×60s+1.4s, one at 3×60s+1.6s that ended `server_error` with empty output), with a hard empty corridor between 15s and 45s that variable compute cannot produce. Ruled out with evidence: throttling (53 requests, all 200, zero 429s), prompt size (1,915–3,247 input tokens), output size (16–96 tokens), reasoning (all 14 live agents `reasoning_effort: none`; captures show `ReasoningTokens: 0`), CPU (plan peak 53%), and our client (no Azure AI SDK in `src/`; the `chat`/`invoke_agent` spans carry `cloud_RoleName=responsesapi`, pods `otlptoappinsights-*`, `sdkVersion=aifoundry-v1.0`, so they are Microsoft's own server-side telemetry). Job `69cd1b3650754c78aebd0e06f1b270bc` shows it inside one composer round: three candidates issued in the same second on identical 3,415-token prompts returned in 2,533ms, 2,597ms and 64,367ms. The fetch cause was ours: HERE itself was never slow (per-call averages 188–1,850ms, max 2.6s), but a bulletin resolves map identity for every flow segment in the market (8,751–25,998 measured) and each ref was a separate table point read, so App Insights recorded 51,000–86,000 table round-trips for a SINGLE bulletin and 1,000–2,900 cumulative seconds of table latency. A scan is the right shape because the partition key is degenerate — first four characters of the URL-escaped ref, and every HERE ref starts `hrn:`, so all rows escape to `hrn%`; sampling 1,000 live rows returned ONE distinct partition key, which also rules out OR-filtered key queries against 60,000+ rows in one partition.

**Consequences:** Measured on dev after deploy. Traffic fetch sydney 58,288ms -> 4,326ms and melbourne 38,308ms -> 2,548ms; "Flow pool built" 20,704ms -> 4ms; table round-trips per bulletin 84,916 -> 414; HERE-call concurrency 0.34–0.51 -> 1.10 as the dead time between calls disappeared. One scan loads 132,945 segments in 10,948ms per process and overlaps the HERE calls. `Script generated in` 268,078ms -> 8,484ms/16,479ms.
