Also fixed en route: dev's composer had been running a STALE prompt, because the agent route discards the rendered `systemPrompt` (`body["instructions"]` is set only under `if (!viaAgent)`) — live `arn-wf-compose:14` carried 6,422 bytes against 7,983 on disk, which also meant the per-station `PlaybookOverlay` feature was inert on dev while the trace claimed "Station playbook applied". NOT fixed, carried forward: TEST still has all five `WorkflowAgents__*` settings and so keeps both defects, while PROD has none and already runs the raw route — dev and test were exercising a different code path from prod; the raw route produces no Foundry portal traces (the documented trade); the degenerate partition key is left in place because re-keying would strand 60,000+ rows and force a full refetch; `/api/health` still reports `azureOpenAI` as `Healthy: true` with `Detail: "HTTP 401"`, which cannot distinguish a working credential from a broken one.

## 2026-08-29 — Candidate grounding must reduce phrase-named channels or it rejects its own evidence

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Dev job `5e613a74559f49c2a6580969af196ba7` failed ALL FOUR generation attempts and produced no audio, rejecting `M4` each time. How verified: job timeline plus the four `compose2` captures, 2026-08-29 07:41Z.

**Decision:** Before matching the script, reduce the fetched-only name list by the roads that candidate ROUTE PHRASES name, using the same `ScriptProvenanceMapper.MapRoadPhraseSpans` matcher the script side uses.

**Rationale:** The claim that the candidate vocabulary is "assembled from every road collection the writer legitimately received" was false for collections that name roads inside a phrase. `MonitoredRouteStatus` carries only a phrase `Name` — "the M4 from Parramatta to the city" — so exact set membership added the phrase but never the bare corridor `M4`, which sat outside the candidate cut. The rendered prompt had itself supplied `driveTime: the M4 from Parramatta to the city — 3 min slower than typical`, so the writer voiced exactly what it was given and the gate rejected it. This was a real false-positive class in a BLOCKING gate, which the original entry had claimed did not exist.

**Consequences:** Sydney regenerated clean (`Script generated in 14004ms`, broadcast ready) where it had hard-failed. Both directions still compare our own vocabulary through one server-owned matcher, so no prose extraction is introduced. Any NEW phrase-shaped evidence channel must be reduced the same way or it becomes a false rejection; the class doc now says so.
## 2026-08-29 — Traffic fetch: the HERE APIs were never slow; the cost was our own round-trips

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN reported traffic fetches "upwards of 70 seconds". How verified: dev App Insights dependency profiling per `operation_Id` (call counts, per-call durations, wall span vs sum, concurrency factor), storage entity sampling, and before/after direct-triggered dev bulletins, 2026-08-29 07:00–13:20Z.

**Decision:** Three changes, in descending measured value. (1) `TableStorageMapAttributesCacheRepository.GetBatchAsync` becomes ONE paged scan into a process-level snapshot instead of a point read per segment ref, with `SaveBatchAsync` feeding the snapshot. (2) The authority feeds are STARTED alongside the HERE request in `TrafficEvidenceBuilder.FetchCorridorsUncachedAsync` and awaited after it, via a new HERE-independent `HarvestOfficialFeedsAsync`. (3) The snapshot scan names the six columns it reads rather than selecting every column.

**Rationale:** Per-call HERE latency was never the problem — measured averages `/v8/routes` 383ms, `smap/segments` 824ms, `multi-revgeocode` 667ms, `/v7/flow` 1,063ms, `/v7/incidents` 1,030ms, max 2.6s anywhere, against only ~20–37 HERE calls per bulletin. The cost was Azure Table Storage: resolving map identity for every flow segment in the market (8,751–25,998 measured, deliberate since it is what stops a flow row being named from its label) issued one point read each, so App Insights recorded 51,000–86,000 table round-trips for a SINGLE bulletin. At 32-way concurrency and ~28ms that is ~813 waves ≈ 23s, which is exactly the observed "Flow pool built: … in 20704ms". The partition key made it worse: it is the first four characters of the URL-escaped ref and every HERE ref begins `hrn:`, so all rows escape to `hrn%` — sampling 1,000 live rows returned ONE distinct partition key, i.e. a single hot partition, which also degraded 28ms → 39ms under four concurrent bulletins and rules out OR-filtered key queries against 60,000+ rows in one partition. The feeds ran strictly after HERE with a 5s budget (`OfficialFeedTimeoutSeconds`), so a slow jurisdiction could add five seconds to a fetch that had already collected everything else; profiling showed them as the LAST three calls, starting only once all HERE work finished.

**Consequences:** Measured on dev. Table round-trips per bulletin 84,916 → 414. Traffic fetched sydney 58,288ms → 2,948–3,042ms warm, melbourne 38,308ms → 2,948ms, brisbane 1,493ms; "Flow pool built" 20,704ms → 5–730ms. HERE-call concurrency 0.34–0.51 → 1.10 as the dead time between calls disappeared. The one-time per-process scan loads ~133,000 segments in 9,214ms (10,948ms before the column projection) and overlaps the HERE calls, so a cold process now costs ~12.5s and a warm one ~1.5–3.0s. The overlap is guarded by a BARRIER test (`Official_feeds_are_fetched_alongside_the_here_request_not_after_it`) rather than a stopwatch: the fake traffic provider refuses to return until the feed has been entered, so re-serialising the feeds fails the test instead of merely getting slower — verified by re-applying the old shape and watching it go red. NOT done, and the next lever if the cold path matters: the scan is 133 sequential 1,000-entity pages (~70ms each), so the only ways further down are re-keying the partition by HERE tile id so a market loads only its own tiles (~26k rows, ~2s) — which would strand ~133,000 existing rows and force a one-time refetch from HERE of ~406 map-attribute calls per market — or warming the snapshot at host startup, which needs an `IHostedService` and the repo has none. Both are deliberately left as decisions.
## 2026-08-29 — Length is not an LLM problem: the revision loop stops chasing the slot

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Audit of the conversational agent workflow — how the agents co-operate, what each costs, and how often they re-run. How verified: 241 LLM-call captures across 13 dev jobs plus per-job timelines, then the same measurements repeated after the change, 2026-08-29 13:00–06:40Z.

**Decision:** An out-of-band read no longer triggers a revision in `ConversationalBulletinWorkflow`. Only a deterministic check failure or an editor rejection earns a compose-plus-review round trip. When a revision happens for one of those reasons the length note still rides along, so the composer is told about the slot; it just never causes the trip. Underrun protection moves to where it is MEASURED rather than predicted — the engine's content-limited-underrun signal on synthesised audio.

**Rationale:** The loop was optimising a target that was itself wrong, so it could not converge. Measured: of 42 revision calls, **31 (74%) listed length as their ONLY reason**, 9 mixed length with editorial and just 2 were purely editorial; 8 of 13 jobs spent BOTH revisions and shipped out-of-band regardless, making the "budget" a fixed two-round tax rather than a convergence mechanism. Job `07a833d1` asked four times over at 102, 93, 98 then 83 words and the read priced at 33.6s every time. The predictor is not the problem and this is the load-bearing measurement: on job `4ac7095e` the syllable model priced a 92-word read at 38.8s and the voice delivered **38.7s — 0.3% error** — against a slot the workflow had been handed as 34.0s for a 30-second bulletin. The word budget is 15% generous because words-per-minute cannot know that THIS read carries more road names than the calibrated average (`metrics.WordsPerMinute` is already syllable-derived, so this is irreducible uncertainty before prose exists, not a defect). Biasing long is therefore correct — the one-sided candidate ladder exists precisely because overrun is absorbed by the deterministic slot fitter while underrun is dead air. What was incoherent was ALSO treating overrun as an LLM problem: the design declared the fitter would handle it and then paid an LLM to pre-empt it, so the same defect was funded twice.

**Consequences:** Measured on dev after deploy, three markets. LLM calls per bulletin 11–12 → **7–8** (`compose2` ×5 → ×3, `edit` ×3 → ×1); agent time 21.2s → 13.6–16.5s; `Script generated in` 15,677/16,087/15,003ms → **8,690/7,255/6,562ms**, roughly halved, which is also ~35% off the token bill. Slot fitting is unchanged (14.5–32.8s) as expected — it now does the length work once instead of after two failed LLM attempts. Two superseded-contract tests were rewritten rather than deleted: `An_over_long_but_clean_read_ships_without_spending_a_revision` pins the new behaviour, and `A_rewrite_that_breaks_the_copy_is_caught_rather_than_shipped` re-pins the original hard-won guarantee (nothing ships unreviewed) under an editorial trigger instead of a length one. NOT fixed, carried forward with evidence: an outer generation retry re-runs the ENTIRE workflow including the writers on unchanged evidence (`5e613a74` ran `writeFlow`/`writeIncidents` 5× each, 51 calls total; `07a833d1` 64 calls against a modal 11) — reuse is not obviously safe because fresh briefs may be what lets a grounding rejection succeed, so it needs its own measurement; slot fitting remains the largest single stage at ~39% of a bulletin; and the 3-candidate fan-out still pays max-of-three under `Task.WhenAll`, now bounded by the 20s per-attempt deadline.
## 2026-08-30 — Handover cleanup: unreachable pipeline, unused detectors, dead knobs and dead agents removed

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Pre-handover simplification pass. Every target was verified unreachable before deletion, not inferred from naming. How verified: reachability greps over `src/`, `test/`, `tools/`, `deployment/` plus live Foundry agent listings and dev app settings, 2026-08-30.

**Decision:** Delete the `staged-v1` workflow and the id-based `WorkflowSelector`; delete five detectors with zero call sites; delete three configuration knobs read nowhere; delete eight Foundry prompt-agents nothing requests, along with their provisioning and config plumbing.

**Rationale:** Each item was provably dead, and dead code that LOOKS live is worse than absent code for a team inheriting the system. `staged-v1` could not be selected because `workflowId` was hardcoded to `conversational-v1`, yet it carried thirteen BLOCKING `HardChecks` (citation, authorisation, duplicate-claim) that an auditor would reasonably read as guarding air. The five detectors — `RoadNameGroundingDetector`, `FragmentDetector`, `OrphanedConnectiveDetector`, `HazardBlockageDetector`, `RepeatedFuelSuburbDetector` — had tests and Repair methods but no call site, so they presented coverage that did not exist. `WordTargetHardLimit`, `SlotSecondsPerItem` and `IncidentStateOptions.DefaultSource` each had exactly one reference, their own declaration: an operator could set them and change nothing, and `appsettings.json` was in fact setting `SlotSecondsPerItem` to 3.0 against a documented formula that no longer runs. `LlmScriptGenerator` requests only "Safety", "Director", "DeliveryWriter" and "Rewrite", never "Draft", so `DraftAgentName` and `arn-draft` were unreachable despite 42 published versions.

**Consequences:** Dev Foundry agents 14 → 6 (`arn-safety`, `arn-director`, and the four `arn-wf-*` the TEST environment still names). Deleted definitions were exported before removal. Removed from code: `StagedBulletinWorkflow`, `StagedWorkflowOptions`, `HardChecks`, `WorkflowSelector`, the staged `Planner`/`Grounder`/`Composer`, `GroundingReport`/`AtomicClaim`/`ClaimStatus`, the orphaned `compose.md`/`ground.md`/`plan.md` prompts and `plan.json`/`compose.json`/`ground.json` schemas, the five detectors, the three knobs, and `DraftAgentName` with its bicep/bicepparam/main.json plumbing. `CheckResult` was moved to its own `Model/CheckResult.cs` because it shared a file with the deleted grounding types and is live in `ConversationalChecks`. `AddBulletinWorkflows` no longer takes a `workflowId` and registers exactly one `IBulletinWorkflow`. Gates after the pass: build 0 errors / 0 warnings, 5,478 unit tests pass. NOT done deliberately: `prompts/agents/arn-draft.md` and `ShippedPlaybookProvider` are LIVE shipped-playbook assets whose filename merely echoes a dead agent — renaming them would change an asset path that may appear as a persisted playbook role key, so the naming inconsistency is recorded rather than fixed under a deletion pass. TEST still carries the five `WorkflowAgents__*` settings, which is why the four `arn-wf-*` agents survive; aligning test with prod would let them go too.

## 2026-08-30 — Handover cleanup II: one owner per setting, factual detectors made blocking

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Second pre-handover pass, this time on configuration and prompt-asset ownership rather than dead code. Two parallel read-only audits mapped every configuration source and every prompt/asset resolver. Both produced findings that were WRONG and were caught by re-verification before any deletion: `ElevenLabsOptions.VoiceSettings`/`TextSettings` were reported dead but are read at `ElevenLabsAudioSynthesizer.cs:23-34` and `ElevenLabsClient.cs:639-640`; `OfficialFeedsOptions.Enabled` was reported dead but is read at `ValidityProbeHttpTrigger.cs:28`. The rule that held: an audit claim is a hypothesis, and the grep that disproves it is cheaper than the incident.

**Decision:** (1) Promote the three FACTUAL fidelity detectors — `FakeLocation`, `FalseClosure`, `UnselectedSource` — from advisory to BLOCKING in `ScriptContentGates`, keeping every omission/style detector advisory. (2) Fix the `directorAgentName` IaC defect. (3) Delete configuration surface with no reader. (4) Fix the playbook role-casing defect. (5) Correct documentation that misstated where prompts live and which LLM roles exist.

**Rationale:** The three promoted detectors assert facts the evidence contradicts — an invented place, a closure the typed data denies, weather or fuel with no source — so airing them is a factual error, not a style miss. Blocking them is affordable because it was MEASURED first, not assumed: over 93 replayable historical bulletins plus 14 generated on the day, `FakeLocation` tripped 0/93 and 0/14, `FalseClosure` 0/93 and 0/14, `UnselectedSource` 1/93 and 0/14. `suburb dropped` (2/14) and `meta leak` (1/14) stay advisory because at those rates a full re-attempt (agent workflow plus a TTS render, ~25-35s) is a real cost against a lower-stakes defect. Enforcement stays in `ScriptContentGates` rather than moving into the workflow because `FalseClosure` and `UnselectedSource` need `BroadcastWithTraffic`, which `NormalizedInput` deliberately does not carry — the Workflow project is a clean room over event-shaped evidence, and a ~0% rate makes the expensive path affordable enough to keep that boundary intact. The `directorAgentName` finding was the most dangerous: the parameter was declared in `main.bicep`, threaded into `modules/function-app.bicep` and set in all three bicepparams, but the app setting was NEVER emitted — only `SafetyAgentName` was. The live dev app happened to carry `AiSettings__AzureAI__DirectorAgentName=arn-director` from an earlier deploy, so the Director stage really was running through its Foundry agent while IaC said otherwise; a clean redeploy would have silently dropped it to the raw model with no error. Deleting the parameter would have been the wrong repair, because `prompts/director.md` is live and the agent exists — reproducibility was the thing missing, so the emit was added. The playbook role bug was a two-layer casing fault: `SupportedRoles` is camelCase because the values double as prompt FILENAMES, but both `BulletinPlaybook.Create` and `ShippedPlaybookProvider.GetDefault` lowercased the role and then compared case-sensitively, so `writeFlow` and `writeIncidents` failed the membership check, and the lowercased name was then interpolated into `Prompts/{role}.md` producing `writeflow.md` against a case-sensitive filesystem. Two of five playbook roles could not be created or resolved.

**Consequences:** `ScriptContentGates.DetectViolations` now returns `(Blocking, Advisory, Style)`; a blocking hit emits a new `fidelity_reject` metric and fails the attempt. Five tests pin the split, including the regression guard that an advisory-only finding still ships. Two orchestrator tests were corrected, not weakened: their fixtures voiced weather and fuel while supplying neither, which is exactly the state the gate now rejects, so the fixtures were given the sources their scripts speak (`PaceFloor_TrimmedTake` word counts are load-bearing, so the context was fixed rather than the script). Added `BulletinPlaybook.CanonicalRole`, matching case-insensitively and returning the canonical camelCase entry, used by both call sites. Deleted with no reader: `IncidentStateOptions.LengthChangeToleranceMeters`, `DurationPredictionOptions.FallbackSyllablesPerWord` (its live sibling `FallbackSyllablesPerSecond` kept), `CorridorSelectionOptions.MaxCorridors` (the unrelated live `EditorialSettings.MaxCorridors` untouched), `AzureAIOptions.DeliveryWriterAgentName` and its `AgentNameFor` arm, `AzureAIOptions.DraftModel` and its `ModelFor` arm, the `AzureSearch` block and the `ReviewModel`/`RefineModel`/`AttributeModel` keys in `appsettings.json`, and the `proseExtractModel` bicep parameter with its pass-through, app setting and three bicepparam values. `AgentNameFor` now has exactly two live arms, `Safety` and `Director`, matching the two agent settings the dev app carries; `DeliveryWriter` and `Rewrite` still dispatch as roles but always take the raw-model path, which was already true in every environment. Stale settings naming deleted agents and properties were removed from the dev Function App. `OfficialFeedsOptions.Enabled` was KEPT and documented as gating only the validity-probe endpoint, naming `BroadcastOptions.OfficialFeedsEnabled` as the pipeline master gate, because the old doc called it the "master switch for everything consuming the official feeds" — the exact trap. `prompts/README.md` claimed "every prompt the system uses lives in this directory"; there are two trees with different resolvers (`ARN_PROMPTS_DIR` is honoured by the Infrastructure `PromptLibrary` and ignored by the Workflow one), so the README now states the real split. `architecture/model.c4` described an Azure OpenAI "ProseExtract role" that exists nowhere in `src/`. `docs/reference/foundry-role-agents.md` still documented the deleted Draft and delivery-writer agents. Verified after deploy: dev generated Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane bulletins to `Broadcast ready` at 30.0s with zero fidelity rejections, matching the measured expectation. NOT changed, deliberately: the `WordTargetOvershoot`/`RetryOvershootBias` code defaults disagree with `appsettings.json` (1.0 vs 1.15, 1.0 vs 1.1) and the docs were corrected to say so rather than moving live tuning values before handover; test and prod still carry the older agent settings and need their own verified pass; `Zetta.FileNamePattern` remains `{MarketId}_TRAIN_TRAFF` in `appsettings.json` against `{MarketId}_TRAFF` in bicep (bicep wins in every deployed environment) and needs ARN confirmation because it is an on-air playout filename.

## 2026-08-30 — Detector `Repair()` surface deleted: 16 unreachable methods and their tests

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Fifteen detectors exposed a public `Repair(...)` "mechanical last-resort fix", plus `EvidenceRestatementDetector.RepairSentences`. Verified before deleting: ZERO `.Repair(` call sites in `src/` or `tools/` — the only callers were ~60 assertions in the detectors' own tests. The XML docs read as though the methods act ("`Repair` relocates PURE supplementary sentences to the tail", "inserts \" near {Suburb}\" after the FIRST whole-word mention"), so the codebase advertised a self-healing mechanism that no pipeline path could ever invoke.

**Decision:** Delete all 16 members, their tests, and their orphaned private helpers. Preserve every assertion that stands on its own without `Repair`; delete any test method left with no Repair-independent assertion.

**Rationale:** This is the same defect class the 2026-08-30 first cleanup entry recorded when it deleted five detectors: "they had tests and Repair methods but no call site, so they presented coverage that did not exist." Keeping them was worse than absent code for a team inheriting the system, because green tests over an unreachable method read as a working safeguard. The alternative — wiring `Repair` into the three newly-blocking detectors to avoid a full re-attempt — was considered and rejected: mechanically editing a script before air is a broadcast-standards decision, and stripping a sentence shortens the read against a slot ARN declared must not carry dead air. The measured rejection rate for those three (at most 1 in 93 bulletins) makes the reject-and-redraft path affordable anyway, so there was nothing to optimise.

**Consequences:** Domain test count 2369 → 2313. Removed with the methods: `MetaLeakDetector`'s repair-only `EmptyProvenanceClause`/`ReportedAdjective`/`ReportedCopula` regexes and `ReplacePreservingCase`; `RollCallDetector`'s `BareChainMin` and `ListConnector`; `DuplicateAnchorDetector`'s `TrailingSelfReferencePreposition` and `TryRepairSentence`; `SplitClearRunDetector`'s `ExtractRoads`/`JoinRoads`; `RepeatedPrepositionDetector`'s and `FakeLocationDetector`'s `SentenceSplit`; `SuburbRetentionDetector`'s `AlreadyPlacedRegex`; `SecondaryItemCapDetector`'s `SweepSentence` and `MaxSweepNames`; `EvidenceRestatementDetector`'s `FindDuplicateIndexes`. `SecondaryItemCapDetector.Item` dropped its repair-only `Index` and `Tier` fields, which also removes a per-item magnitude-tier lookup from `Detect`'s hot path. Seven cross-referencing XML `<see cref>` doc comments were reworded, since a dangling cref to a deleted member is CS1574 under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`. Two corrections were made to subagent work during this pass: one agent rewired `SuburbRetentionDetector.Detect` to call `RoadIsPlaced` (previously Repair-only) purely to avoid an unused-member warning — the condition was restored to the original `suburbs.Any(s => Mentions(script, s))`, which reuses the already-computed list instead of re-deriving it per road, and `RoadIsPlaced` was deleted; another proposed replacing `Detect(Repair(x))` assertions with hand-written "clean" inputs, which would have authored new tests rather than preserving coverage, and was corrected to delete those assertions outright. Characterisation tests tied to real on-air incidents (the 2026-08-24 ARN section-order script, the Newcastle meta-leak, the cairns multi-spot suburb finding) kept their detection halves and their explanatory comments; only the repair assertions went.

## 2026-08-30 — Zetta aligned to deployed truth; `sentence shape` gate KEPT after it proved load-bearing

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Two follow-ups after the handover cleanup. (1) The Zetta playout filename had three disagreeing definitions. (2) The `sentence shape` style detector fired on 14 of 14 live dev bulletins and, being advisory, never changed an outcome — it looked like pure noise and removal was approved.

**Decision:** Align every Zetta definition to the value the deployed environments actually run, and make `MarketCodesJson` the sole source of market codes. Do NOT remove `SentenceShapeDetector` — investigation while removing it proved it is the only gate that catches a real defect class.

**Rationale:** ZETTA — read live 2026-08-30: dev, test AND prod all carry `Zetta__FileNamePattern={MarketId}_TRAFF`, and test/prod carry `Zetta__MarketCodesJson={"sydney":"[SYD]KIIS90s","cairns-4ca":"[CAI]STAR1027"}`. No environment sets any per-key `Zetta__MarketCodes__*`. The repo disagreed twice: the `ZettaOptions.FileNamePattern` default and `appsettings.json` both said `{MarketId}_TRAIN_TRAFF`, and `appsettings.json` shipped a legacy six-entry `MarketCodes` map (`sydney`→`SYD`, plus MEL/BNE/ADL/PER/GLD). That map was the dangerous one: it is a SECOND source for an on-air filename whose values are a different SHAPE from the real codes (`SYD` versus `[SYD]KIIS90s`), it was never confirmed by ARN, and `ResolveMarketCode` consulted it whenever the JSON map missed. A file written under the wrong name does not air and nothing reports it, which is precisely the failure the existing bicep comment said must never happen ("an unmapped market must fail delivery, never guess a name") — while the package defaults quietly contradicted it.

SENTENCE SHAPE — the removal was reverted on evidence, not preference. `ClonedReadRoutingTests` is a REGRESSION GUARD over dev job `9c0938fd`'s actually-aired script, and it is a DISCRIMINATING PAIR: the cloned read ("a breakdown has one of two lanes closed" repeated across the M4 and M7 sentences) must be flagged, while the same read with varied phrasing must present as clean. With the detector removed the cloned read scored zero findings across blocking, advisory and style — no other gate sees it, because `SentenceCloneDetector` needs a four-word shared frame after road-name skeletonisation and this echo is shorter. So the "100% of bulletins" observation measured NOISE, not absence of signal: the detector discriminates correctly on the one case we have ground truth for, and live reads apparently do all carry one of its three shapes. The correct follow-up is to TIGHTEN it so the signal is usable, not to delete the only check for short cloned tails and repeated opening frames.

**Consequences:** `FileNamePattern` is now `{MarketId}_TRAFF` in the code default, `appsettings.json`, both bicep params and both test/prod bicepparams — one value everywhere, matching live. `ZettaOptions.MarketCodes` and its fallback branch in `ResolveMarketCode` are deleted; `MarketCodesJson` is the only source and an absent market fails delivery. `HealthHttpTrigger`'s operator-facing message previously instructed engineers to `set Zetta__MarketCodes__<marketId>`, which after this change would have done nothing at all — it now names `Zetta__MarketCodesJson` and states that an absent market fails rather than guessing. The delivery tests now assert the REAL convention (`[SYD]KIIS90s_TRAFF.wav`) instead of the fictional `SYD_TRAIN_TRAFF.wav`, with melbourne and darwin kept deliberately unmapped so the refusal guarantee still has teeth. Two Zetta tests went: `DeliverAsync_JsonMapWins_OverAPerKeyCodeForTheSameMarket` is obsolete because there is no second map to win over, and `DeliverAsync_MalformedJsonMap_LeavesThePerKeyCodesIntact` was rewritten as `DeliverAsync_MalformedJsonMap_RefusesRatherThanGuessing` since malformed JSON now resolves nothing. Test and prod Azure environments were NOT touched, per instruction — this is a repo-side alignment that makes a future deploy reproduce what they already run. `SentenceShapeDetector`, its tests, its `ScriptContentGates` wiring, the `StationLines` helper, its three `test/corpus/subpar-reads.json` entries and the doc references in `RoadFeelTranslator` and `EvidenceLabelVocabularyTests` were all restored to their prior state; the detector remains ADVISORY and its noise level is recorded as open work.

## 2026-08-30 — Slot fitting made band-aware; an empty briefing desk can no longer air silently

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** 40% of dev bulletins (8 of 20) overran badly enough to force a full TTS re-render, measured at 14.4s median (audio phase 14.8s clean vs 29.2s trimmed). Diagnosis over 20 jobs and 104 captured composer calls: the re-render trigger is exactly `slot x MaxSpeedUpFactor` (1.15), and the conversational workflow could not see it. `WordTargetOvershoot = 1.15` was baked into `baseWordTarget`, which became `TargetWordCountOverride`, which became `WorkflowRequest.TargetSeconds` — so the workflow's "on target" already sat ON the compression ceiling, leaving no margin for the composer's own length variance. That variance is the real driver: median adherence -3.0% (models slightly UNDERSHOOT, as the design assumed) but sigma 19.3%, against a 6% candidate ladder step. 12 of 20 fan-outs produced lengths that did not even follow aim order.

**Decision:** Give the workflow the true slot AND the fitter's ceiling as an explicit band; select the longest candidate inside the band rather than the closest to a point; allow exactly ONE directive revision when a read breaches the ceiling; state the aim and a numeric cap in the composer prompt. Separately, stop an empty briefing-desk reply from degrading a bulletin silently.

**Rationale:** Aim tuning alone cannot work, and the sweep proves it: no multiplier satisfies both failure modes, because underrun is the EXPENSIVE one — `UseTrimmedBedCloser` is off (code default, configured nowhere), so underrun tolerance is only `MaxSilencePadSeconds` = 0.3s and exceeding it costs a whole extra generation attempt. Centring on the slot cut re-renders to 20% but pushed under-slot to 40%. The lever is variance, not the centre. Selection is where it is cheapest to fix: everything inside the band is equally airworthy because the fitter compresses it for free, so keeping the longest in-band draw uses the slot fully while never crossing the fail line. The one revision is justified because revision calls are measurably the accurate call shape — adherence sigma 11.9% with median 0.0%, versus 19.3% for an initial compose, since the note names an explicit delta — and cost ~2.4s against 14.4s for a re-render. It is capped at one because the earlier failure (job 07a833d1, four asks at 102/93/98/83 words pricing 33.6s every time) was a LOOP against a target that was itself wrong; the target is now the true slot. The pace-boost path was audited and left alone: its aim ratio is 1.168 against a fitter ceiling of 1.33, so it was already inside the band, and the 8% margin is protective — removing it to "deliver the full boost" would trade a free overrun for a re-render.

**Consequences:** Measured on dev over 12 bulletins after the change: **re-render rate 40% -> 8%** (1 of 12), 12 of 12 reached air, zero fallbacks, fit-time median 14,956ms. Two bulletins went content-limited (3 and 4 attempts) and both recovered — that is the underrun side of the trade, visible and bounded. Added `BroadcastWithTraffic.BodySlotSeconds`/`BodyCeilingSeconds` (the ceiling uses `fitterMaxSpeedUpFactor`, deliberately wider than the aim ceiling, because it is what actually decides compressibility), `WorkflowRequest.MaxSeconds`/`EffectiveMaxSeconds`, band-spanning candidate aims, `InBand` selection, and a numeric "land between N and M words" instruction. `ComposeCandidateCount` was raised 3 -> 5 and REVERTED the same day: at four markets concurrently it put 20 simultaneous completions on the model instead of 9 and empty completions appeared for the first time (2 of 42 compose2, 1 of 3 writeIncidents) against ZERO in 221 captured calls beforehand. **That exposed a latent fault worth more than the change that found it.** Every failure path in `BulletinWriter` softened to `BulletinBriefs.Empty`, and the only guard was for TOTAL zero stories — so dev adelaide job `369b0c37` aired "Clear runs are the story across Adelaide" over three unreported road closures (West Thebarton Road, South Road, Everard Avenue), all three present in the incident desk's own prompt, after that desk returned an empty completion with no API error in 1346ms. All seven composer candidates were correct; the flow story was the only one they were given. An empty desk reply now retries once and is then handled ASYMMETRICALLY: a lost FLOW desk still degrades (the read keeps reporting every obstruction — the original "a desk that fails costs its own stories" guarantee, preserved), while a lost INCIDENTS desk fails the attempt, because flow-only does not merely omit the closures, it asserts the opposite. Verified live: job `67b3c7f7` hit the empty reply, retried, recovered, and aired all three closures with clear runs demoted to one clause. The empty completions themselves remain UNEXPLAINED — one recurred at 3 candidates and 2-market concurrency (1 of 9 writeIncidents), so load is correlated but not proven causal; they are now loud instead of silent, which is the property that matters. NOT done: splitting the composer into sections, which the analysis showed buys the same variance reduction as 3 -> 5 candidates (sigma/sqrt(S)) at the cost of more desk calls — precisely what surfaced this fault — so it is deferred until empty replies are understood.

## 2026-08-30 — Empty LLM replies root-caused: a transient HTTP 500 retried nowhere

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Empty model replies appeared in dev for the first time on 2026-08-30 (2 of 42 `compose2`, 1 of 3 `writeIncidents`) against ZERO in 221 captured calls beforehand, and one silently dropped three road closures from an aired Adelaide bulletin. The initial hypothesis was concurrency: `ComposeCandidateCount` had just gone 3 -> 5, putting 20 simultaneous completions on the model instead of 9. That hypothesis was WRONG and the measurement disproved it.

**Decision:** Retry transient 5xx and 408 in `AzureOpenAiWorkflowLlm` with the existing throttle backoff, not just 429.

**Rationale:** Replaying one real `writeIncidents` prompt against the deployed dev endpoint: 3 failures in 112 calls = **2.7%**, and the rate was **load-independent** — 1 of 40 at concurrency 2 and 1 of 40 at concurrency 16. The failure is `HTTP 500 "The server had an error processing your request"` returning in ~1.2s, which matches the empty captures' 0.9-1.3s signature exactly. The capture blob records no error field, which is why the cause was invisible: `ParseResponse` correctly returned a failure, `BulletinWriter` softened it to `BulletinBriefs.Empty`, and the capture showed only an empty `ResponseBody`. Nothing retried it — this client is registered via `AddHttpClient<AzureOpenAiWorkflowLlm>` with no `RateLimitRetryHandler` (which covers only 429 and 503 anyway, and says so in its own doc), and the in-class loop covered only 429. At 8-13 LLM calls per bulletin a 2.7% per-call rate means a **~22-30% chance any bulletin loses a stage**; with the retry budget of 4 that falls to effectively zero. This matters far more in production than dev: many stations share cron minutes, so the call volume per minute is much higher, and every one of those calls was one 500 away from a silently degraded read.

**Consequences:** Transient 5xx/408 now retry with the same exponential backoff as 429, pinned by a theory across 500/502/503/504 plus a test that a sustained 500 still surfaces as a failure after the budget rather than looping. Dev after the fix: 12 of 12 bulletins reached air, 0 re-renders, 0 empty-reply degradations. Two further findings came out of chasing this. First, the numeric "HARD LIMITS: never exceed N words" composer instruction added earlier the same day was WITHDRAWN: it correlated with the style gate rejecting reads for speaker labels ("Remove speaker labels like 'Alex:'"), 0 occurrences across 20 pre-change jobs against 4 across 24 after, and each rejection re-drafts — a generation attempt (~25s) costs more than the 14.4s re-render the cap was meant to avoid, so the cure was worse than the disease. Length is left to the band and the ceiling-aware selection, which need no prompt pressure. Second, the workflow's underrun trigger was looser than the audio path's real tolerance: `DurationToleranceSeconds` is 1.5s, but with slowing disabled, the bed closer off and a 0.3s silence pad, anything more than ~0.3s short is content-limited. That left a 1.2s band where the workflow called a read fine and the engine then failed it — brisbane lived there (29.3-29.5s reads against a 30s slot, four attempts, failed), and passed 4 of 4 beforehand only because the OVERSHOT target made the same read look 5s short and bought a revision by accident. The trigger now uses the engine's 0.3s pad, mirrored as a constant because the Workflow project is a clean room and must not depend on `SpeechDurationOptions`. Raising the aim floor from 4% to 10% was tried first and made brisbane WORSE (2 of 3 failed against 1 of 3), which is what proved the fault was the trigger and not the aim; the floor is back at 4%. Brisbane now escalates 59 -> 65 -> 67 words and lands on 30.0s.

## 2026-08-30 — The authority's reason reaches the writer, and the primary incident type stops vanishing

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Bulletins were voicing the hazard and nothing else. Measured across 536 story briefs from dev captures: only 9 carried an incident-type word and **every one of them was "hazard"**. Separately, 68% of story briefs offered the composer three or fewer fact fields and 34% offered only `road`/`suburb`/`detail`. Two distinct causes, both in the evidence builder rather than the model.

**Decision:** Emit the road authority's own incident CATEGORY (and named project) as a spoken `reason` fact, and emit the corridor's PRIMARY incident type unconditionally instead of only its secondaries.

**Rationale:** Official feeds were never the problem — Live Traffic NSW is live in dev (`sources=['here','livetraffic-nsw']`, ~2 corridors per job carrying `OfficialEvidences`) and its payload is rich: for the Warringah Freeway corridor it published `Category: "SCHEDULED ROADWORK"`, `SubCategory: "Warringah Freeway Upgrade"`, `IsPlanned: true`, three advice tags and the authority's own prose. `AppendOfficialContentEvidence` exposed **three of roughly twenty fields** — `lanesClosed`, `reduced speed`, and ONE `advice` tag — and the one it took is the weakest: advice tags are generic ("plan your journey", "check signage") and the code's own comment warns they read as a machine tell, while `Category`/`SubCategory` — the actual reason, in closed vocabulary — was discarded. Worse, the type word the writer DID receive was wrong. The primary label was emitted nowhere: only secondaries were, filtered to exclude the primary, on the assumption that the primary always travelled via the corridor Description into the `detail` unit. It does not — `detail` is withheld whenever the Description is DERIVED, which is most of the time. So on the Warringah Freeway the primary `construction` -> "roadworks" silently vanished and a secondary HERE `roadHazard` ping became the only type word offered, producing "a hazard" for a signed, planned, named infrastructure project. Mapping goes through `TrafficTypeMapper` so the value is closed vocabulary and an unmapped category returns null and is simply not voiced — never a guess, because this value is read aloud. The authority's `Detail` prose is deliberately NOT used: it is long, provider-formatted, arrived truncated mid-sentence in the sample, and baking prose into an evidence value puts words in the writer's mouth, the same defect the speed-limit unit already records. `IsPlanned` is subsumed rather than emitted separately — `Category` already distinguishes scheduled roadworks from a crash, and a redundant field is prompt bloat on a brief that already runs to eight facts.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev sydney after deploy. The composer now receives `reason: scheduled roadworks for the Warringah Freeway Upgrade` on the City West Link corridor and `reason: scheduled roadworks` plus `incident: roadworks` on Mitchell Road, and the aired read carried it: *"Mitchell Road at Erskineville has scheduled roadworks."* Every corridor now offers its primary type — `incident: road closure` on the closure stories, `incident: congestion` on the congested ones — where previously those stories offered no type word at all. Added `TrafficTypeMapper.MapAuthorityCategory` with 11 mapped categories and explicit null for absent, "OTHER", "UNKNOWN" and the literal string "null" (which the NSW payload sends for an absent SubCategory, and which a plain null-or-whitespace guard would have voiced as "roadworks for the null"). New tests cover the mapping table, the null cases, the reason-plus-project composition, the unmapped-category omission, and the primary-plus-secondary type emission. No `WordEstimator` cost entry was added for `reason`: unknown fields fall back to `valueWords + 1`, which is more accurate than a fixed table entry for a variable-length value. STILL OPEN from the same investigation and not addressed here: `EndTimeUtc` remains unvoiced and MUST stay so (it is a rolling placeholder — every span an exact whole number of hours, all ending the same calendar day, so voicing it would be fabrication), while `StartTimeUtc` is genuine (irregular offsets, median 22.1h) and would support a "closed since" fact; and `MinVoicedExtentMeters = 300` suppresses extent on 67% of closures, where a 250m closure is meaningful even though sub-300m congestion is noise.
## 2026-08-31 — Manual trigger queue feedback uses a canonical acknowledgement and adaptive polling

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Operators reported that a manually triggered bulletin could take several seconds to
appear in the On air queue as `Generating`. DEV evidence on 2026-08-31 separated the clocks:
recent `ListJobs` p50/p95 were 220/282 ms, sampled broadcast acknowledgements were all 202 and
201–1,107 ms, the queue host can wait up to its configured 2-second polling interval, and the
browser's list requests were roughly 10 seconds apart. The generation work itself is deliberately
asynchronous and is not part of the acknowledgement-to-paint contract.

**Decision:** Return the just-persisted `JobSummaryDto` in the 202 response beside `JobId`. The
frontend trigger mutation immediately upserts that canonical `REQUESTED` row into compatible
mounted list caches, then invalidates those caches for storage reconciliation. Keep the app-shell
notification feed narrow, and add a separate `useLiveJobs` feed containing pipeline statuses for
the selected workstation fallback. Any jobs list switches from its caller's idle cadence to the
3-second active cadence while it contains a pipeline row; quiet lists retain the 10-second default.
Do not introduce an always-on SSE/SignalR connection in this change.

**Rationale:** A client-side placeholder would guess server-resolved station and market fields,
while a list-only refetch leaves a perceptual gap. Returning the server's own projection makes the
first row exact and cache insertion is immediate, while invalidation preserves eventual agreement
with Table Storage. Separating `useLiveJobs` avoids making badges, alarms and desktop notifications
carry every generating job. Adaptive polling gives near-real-time stage movement without multiplying
quiet-page traffic. True push needs authenticated subscriptions, transition publication,
reconnect semantics and an explicit fan-out/cost decision; it is a separate measured phase.

**Consequences:** A mounted queue can show the requested row as soon as the trigger acknowledgement
arrives and refresh it at most every 3 seconds while generation is in flight. Older clients may
ignore the additive `Job` field; the frontend treats it as optional during rollout and falls back
to normal invalidation. The 2-second queue pickup and backend generation duration remain real,
visible delays rather than being hidden behind a synchronous HTTP request.

## 2026-08-31 — The history predictor averaged neighbour durations instead of pricing a rate, and halved the composer's word budget

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A dev perth read (job fc6a6ab8) came out listy — "Mounts Bay Road has congestion about a kay long. Winthrop Avenue has congestion about half a kay long." — while a second perth read minutes later (fccd0a62) was fluent prose. Same market, same station, same 30-second slot. The compose2 captures showed why: the listy job's composer was told **"about 42 words"** and the fluent job's **"about 85"**.

**Decision:** `HistoryBasedDurationPredictor` now derives a seconds-per-syllable RATE from its neighbours and prices the requested length with it, instead of returning a weighted average of the neighbours' achieved durations.

**Rationale:** `InterpolateDuration` computed `weightedDuration += (record.AchievedDuration / record.Speed * speed) * weight` and returned `weightedDuration / totalWeight` — the `targetSyllables` argument was never used. The result is "how long did reads of roughly this length take", which is only the right answer when the text being priced is itself roughly that length. It is not: `CalibratedDurationOracle.SecondsPerWord` prices a fixed 27-word, 44-syllable probe, while the history holds nothing but 30-second bulletins (median 116–132 syllables). The probe was therefore handed a full bulletin's duration and the voice looked twice as slow as it is. Measured against the 400 real dev records, the SAME 30-second slot budgeted **25, 26, 36, 66 or 80 words** depending only on which `(model, speed)` bucket `FindClosestBySyllables` matched — a 3.2x spread against a true 72 — because the defect's severity depends on whether that bucket happens to contain any short reads. After the fix every bucket returns **70–83, centred on 74**, which is what the engine independently computes from the measured 148 wpm and what the static-rate path returns. That is why removing the delivery style appeared to fix the read: it changed the bucket, not the writing. The knock-on was not merely a wrong number. A 42-word budget reaches the composer as "write one cohesive bulletin of about 42 words" for a read that must still carry weather and fuel, so it cannot be obeyed; the model answered with a run of telegraphic equal-weight clauses and the read still fell short of the slot, drawing a filler rescue that appended "Please stay alert out there and stick to the speed limit." Listiness, the filler and the undershoot were one defect. `InterpolateSyllableTarget` had the same shape — averaging neighbour syllable COUNTS, so a 14-second body asked against 30-second history was answered with a 30-second read's worth of syllables — and is fixed the same way. The speed normalisation was also inverted (`/ record.Speed * speed` makes a slow read look fast; duration is inversely proportional to speed, as `StaticRateDurationPredictor` prices 6 syllables at 1.034s at speed 1.0 and 2.069s at 0.5) and is now `* record.Speed / speed`; it is inert while the repository filters neighbours to the requested speed and wrong the moment that filter widens. Verified that `synthesisHistory.AchievedDuration` stores the NATURAL pre-fill read, not the compressed one, so the learned rate is not self-poisoned.

**Consequences:** Deployed to dev and measured over three perth reads before and after, on the same market and story set. Clause-length spread — the sharpest listiness signal, 12 on the fluent reference read and 2–3 on the listy ones — moved from `{12, 2, 3}` to `{10, 7, 11}`: the bimodal lottery became consistent prose. Filler rescue went from 1/3 to 0/3. The aired read for the exact corridors that produced the listy version now groups and subordinates: "Road closures are affecting Burswood: Craig Street is closed, although both ends are still reachable, while Victoria Park Drive is closed at Graham Farmer Freeway." Every existing predictor test kept passing because all of them seeded neighbours within ~10 syllables of the text being priced, the one regime where averaging and rate-pricing agree; the single far-regime test asserted only `ExpectedDuration > 0` while its own comment documented the intended contract ("12 / 5.75 = 2.09s"), so it passed while the value was an order of magnitude wrong. That test now asserts the rate contract, `PredictDuration_ExactMatch_ReturnsHistoricalDuration` was re-pointed to the rate (its old range only held because averaging ignored the requested length) and both now take their syllable counts from `SyllableCounter` rather than a comment's guess, which was wrong in both cases (12 vs 17, 169 vs ~156). A new test pins linear scaling with length, the property `CalibratedDurationOracle` depends on when it divides a probe's duration by its word count. NOT ADDRESSED: the slot-fit failure mode has flipped direction rather than disappeared. Correcting the budget from 42 to 74 removed the undershoot, and the composer's habit of exceeding its aim by ~11% now lands on the high side — reads measure 35.1s natural against a 30-second slot and 1 of 3 was trimmed (88 -> 77 words) where previously 1 of 3 drew filler. The rate is unchanged and the new mode is editorially better (a real story dropped rather than generic advice invented), but `WordTargetOvershoot = 1.15`, `UndershootFloorBias` and the candidate band were all tuned while the predictor under-budgeted and are now aiming long against a correct number: measured, the aim wants to be ~62 words for a natural 30-second read, not 74. That re-tune needs its own sweep across markets rather than a guess.

## 2026-08-31 — One calibrated word target, carried; and a plausibility floor under the probe

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Fixing the history predictor's rate arithmetic removed the 3.2x budget spread but left the underlying fragility: the engine computes a word target from the voice's calibrated rate, then the conversational workflow throws it away and re-derives its own from seconds by pricing a 27-word probe. Two answers to one question, and the read is sized against whichever the workflow happened to compute. `BulletinBriefs.RenderBrief` already carried the comment "the word target is the engine's (bookends already subtracted, voice-calibrated)" — a documented invariant that the code did not honour.

**Decision:** The engine emits `BroadcastWithTraffic.BodySlotWords` — the true body slot in words, at its calibrated rate, with both the overshoot and the pace boost removed — and the workflow consumes it as `WorkflowRequest.SlotWords`, falling back to the oracle only when no caller supplied one. `CalibratedDurationOracle` additionally refuses any probe-derived rate outside 90–240 wpm and defers to its fallback.

**Rationale:** The number belongs to the stage that owns the calibrated rate. Re-deriving it downstream is what made the predictor defect damaging rather than merely wrong: the engine had sized the perth body correctly at 74 words throughout, and the workflow's independent 42 is what reached the composer. Carrying it also removes the probe from the aiming path entirely for scheduled broadcasts — a probe is the shortest text the predictor ever sees, so it sits at the edge of the data where any modelling error surfaces first, which is exactly what happened. The ad-hoc and manual paths still have no engine sizing pass, so the fallback stays. NATURAL words, not boosted: the workflow reasons in natural seconds, pricing candidates with a natural-pace predictor against `BodySlotSeconds..BodyCeilingSeconds`, and the boosted count IS that ceiling by construction (a +16 wpm boost on a 148 wpm voice is the same 1.11 ratio the fitter's widened cap carries). Passing the boosted count first — measured live on perth job 5754146257, Gold 96FM with `PaceBoostWpm=16` — aimed the composer at 82, it wrote 89, and the read was trimmed to 79: the aim-at-the-ceiling fault reappearing in a new place, because a ~11% length variance against an aim ON the ceiling overruns about half the time. The boost still buys its extra content, through the ceiling rather than the aim. The plausibility band is deliberately generous — deployed voices measure 148 to 190 wpm — because its job is to catch a broken derivation, not to second-guess a fast read; the pre-fix predictor returned rates implying 54 wpm, which no news voice reads at.

**Consequences:** Verified on dev across three markets after deploy. Perth, the market that produced the listy read, now lands **30.4s natural against a 30-second slot with no trim and no filler** (aims 85/79/73 against an engine target of 74); adelaide 32.6s, no trim, no filler. Brisbane drew a content-limited retry on a genuinely quiet board — 3 corridors and 4 incidents — where filler correctly DECLINED ("no statement fits the measured 0.7s gap") and the retry recovered; that is the mechanism working, not a sizing miss. The workflow trace now records `source`, `oracleWords` and `oracleDrift` on its slot decision, so the two derivations can be compared from a job record instead of inferred from capture blobs — the diagnostic that cost the most time here. Tests: the workflow's preference for the caller's number and its fallback when none is supplied; five oracle guard cases including the exact 54-wpm shape of the defect and the 190-wpm fastest deployed voice that must NOT trip it; and a domain invariant pinning natural < boosted with the headroom equal to the fitter's widened cap, so a change to the calculator cannot silently put the aim back on the ceiling. STILL OPEN: `WordTargetOvershoot = 1.15`, `UndershootFloorBias` and the candidate band remain tuned against the old under-budgeting predictor. They are now aiming long against a correct number, and the sweep to re-fit them is the next slot-fit task — not attempted here, because it would have confounded the measurement above.

## 2026-08-31 — The slot-fit re-tune was measured and rejected: sigma 19.3% was the aim moving, not the composer

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** After the predictor and slot-sizing fixes, `WordTargetOvershoot`, `UndershootFloorBias` and the candidate band were all still tuned against measurements taken while the workflow was under-budgeting, so they were the obvious next target. A first measurement over 18 candidates from three dev jobs put composer adherence at median **-7.4%**, which implied every ladder rung was landing seven per cent short and the fix was to divide each aim by the measured adherence.

**Decision:** Rejected. The ladder keeps plain aims. The only change kept is that a single-candidate run and a revision now aim at the ladder's floor rung (`targetWords * 1.04`) instead of exactly the slot.

**Rationale:** The -7.4% was a small-sample artefact. Re-measured over **30 candidates across 7 jobs** the bias is **-1.2%** (mean -1.0%, sigma 7.7%; first-attempt draws only: -1.2%, sigma 6.3%) — the composer hits its aim. The original 18 came from three jobs and were dominated by one thin-board brisbane run whose ten calls were retries deliberately aiming lower. A Monte Carlo over the re-measured distribution (bias -1.2%, sigma 7.7%, ceiling +15%, three draws) scored the proposed correction at **80.7% clean fits against 92.0%** for plain rungs: inflating every aim by 7.5% raised overruns from 7.6% to 19.3%. Shipping it would have been a regression, and it was reverted before deploy. The wider lesson is worth more than the change: the **sigma 19.3%** figure that justified the band-spanning ladder in the first place was never composer variance. It was the workflow re-deriving its own aim per job from the probe oracle, which moved the target between jobs and markets; the spread of AIMS was being read as spread of ADHERENCE. At the true sigma of 7.7% the ladder's ~5.5% step is just under one standard deviation, so the rungs are neither a precise ladder nor pure draws, and the existing +4%..+15% placement is already near the optimum the model finds. A second false lead is recorded for the same reason: two baseline trims looked like they had fired on reads needing only 6-8% compression, which would have been a real defect. They had not — the job log's "Ns natural read" is measured AFTER the trim, and reconstructing the pre-trim reads (78 words at 31.8s post-trim implies ~34.9s; 84 at 32.3s implies ~35.7s) put both genuinely past their ~34.5s ceiling. The trim was correct.

**Consequences:** Eight bulletins before and eight after, same four markets. After: 0 trims, 0 filler rescues, 0 content-limited against 2/1/1 before, and 3.3 compose calls per job against 4.3. **This is NOT attributable to the change** and is recorded as noise, not a win: Fisher one-sided p = 1.00 on the trim counts, the kept change touches only the revision path which just 1 of 6 jobs reached, and the runs are confounded by the resolved voice differing between them — within the BEFORE set alone a perth read of 35.5s natural passed clean while one of 32.3s trimmed, which is only possible if the ceiling moved, i.e. a different pace-boosted voice profile resolved. Cross-run comparisons of natural seconds are therefore invalid unless the resolved voice is pinned, which is the measurement lesson for any future sweep. The floor-rung change for revisions is kept on first principles rather than measurement: a lone or last draw aimed exactly at the slot lands under it about half the time given a symmetric spread about zero bias, and undershoot is the failure nothing downstream absorbs. What the model says is actually available, if this is revisited: a fourth candidate buys 92.0% -> 96.7% clean at the cost of one more LLM call per bulletin, and lowering the top rung from +15% to +10% buys 92.0% -> 94.0% at the cost of filling less of the slot. Neither is worth spending without a voice-pinned harness to measure it.

## 2026-08-31 — Qualitative voicing moves from the emitter to the desk, and derived measurements stop being airable

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A brisbane read aired "roadworks on Milton Road at Sylvan Road are barely noticeable", and a melbourne read collapsed two roads into "Roadworks on Footscray Road and the Calder Freeway are barely noticeable" — the identical phrase for both. The phrase came from `RoadFeelTranslator`, which mapped the `minor impact` band to a **two-option** palette and picked between them by hashing the road name. Two options cannot cover three roads in one band, so by pigeonhole the wording repeats: 50% for two roads, 75% for three, 87.5% for four. Separately, a `road feel` value existed at all only to say a road's impact was negligible, so the read was spending slot words announcing a road in order to say it was not worth announcing.

**Decision:** Code stops choosing spoken wording for qualitative state. The emitter hands over the MEASUREMENT (`ImpactMeasurementTranslator`, replacing `RoadFeelTranslator`), the writing desk authors the voicing in a new `StoryBrief.Condition`, and the measurement itself is marked `DeskOnly` so it informs the desk and never reaches the composer as airable copy.

**Rationale:** The palette existed for a real reason — an earlier emitter handed over the raw band and the writer echoed "minor impacts are reported" to air — but the response was wrong in kind. The answer to internal jargon leaking is not to pre-write the English in code; it is to hand over something factual and let an agent that can see the whole board phrase it. The emitter sees one corridor at a time, so it cannot know that three roads share a state and belong in one sweep; the desk sees every event at once and is the only stage that can. That is the entire purpose of having a normalisation pass before the composer, and `StoryBrief` had deliberately been left with no `Facts` member — for the good reason that a desk which COPIES values turns 57% of its reply into a transcript of its prompt, but with the consequence that no agent anywhere was permitted to re-voice anything, so a code-chosen phrase reached air verbatim by construction. `Condition` reopens that channel for interpretation only, and is the one string the composer may voice uncited. Two guards make that safe: `DeskConditionCarriesNoFigure` rejects any condition carrying a quantity, including the spoken pace fractions `FormatPace` emits (a desk writing "about a third of its usual pace" from impression would be asserting a measurement, and shifting a third to a fifth would be falsifying one), and the completeness invariant now pins that every band `EvidenceLabelVocabulary` knows maps to a measurement carrying no label. The four bands excluded upstream (`road closed` and the three voiceable-delay bands) are mapped to empty deliberately rather than omitted, because a mapping that relied on that upstream condition staying in sync would leak the raw band the day it drifted.

**Consequences:** Verified live over two rounds on dev. FIRST round exposed two faults and both were fixed before the second. (1) `with no delay measured` AIRED VERBATIM on brisbane df18a7d8 — the measurement is worse jargon than the phrase it replaced, and the same mistake in a new place: a value written in code reaching air unchanged. Fixed by `EvidenceUnit.DeskOnly`/`EventFact.DeskOnly`, withheld from the composer's AVAILABLE FACTS in `BulletinBriefs.Render` and nowhere else, so the desk still reads it in the source block. (2) The route-versus-corridor dedup was widened from `IsClosure` to all corridors, and brisbane df18a7d8 then aired "Pacific Motorway at Holland Park West ... are both clear!" beside "The Pacific Motorway into the city is one minute slower" — the partner mention was a GOOD RUN, not a corridor. Both pools are now excluded. SECOND round, four bulletins across brisbane, melbourne and perth: `barely noticeable` gone, `no delay measured` gone, no road named twice in any traffic body, and 19 desk-authored conditions with **zero verbatim repetition**. The desk groups as intended — "Roadworks are in place around Toowong, but the roads are still getting through" is one observation covering the roads that previously each drew the identical phrase. Kept for the record: the repetition was already known and delegated in a comment to `SentenceShapeDetector` and `RepeatedStatePhraseDetector`, which are ADVISORY, which is exactly why it aired — a known cost handed to a gate that cannot stop it is not a mitigation.

## 2026-08-31 — Every bulletin sounded the same because the evidence layer was a phrase library

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Bulletins kept voicing the same things the same way — "down to about a third of its normal pace" in read after read, and "with no delay measured" surviving the previous round's fix. Measured over eight dev bulletins, several evidence fields had a vocabulary of ONE in practice: `access` was "the ends of the road are still reachable" in half of them, `measured impact` was "no delay measured" in half, and `reason` was the broken "roadworks for the Planned roadworks" in half. `pace` had seven bucket values and two frames each — fourteen fixed strings for the entire system, forever.

**Decision:** Evidence values carry the MEANING, not the wording. `FormatPace` emits the fraction and the anchor that stops it inverting ("a third of normal speed") and nothing else; the severity band is not emitted in any wording, to anyone; the access note is a two-word token; and the composer's `material.values-are-exact` block now distinguishes a value's meaning from its presentation.

**Rationale:** The mechanism was not the composer ignoring "vary how sentences open". `material.values-are-exact` told it, correctly, that a value carrying a figure must survive exactly — and `pace: about a third of its usual pace` contains a figure, so the WORDING rode in on the back of the measurement and survived with it. No instruction about variety can beat an instruction to copy. The same applies to every field whose value was written in this repository: the composer was doing exactly as asked. This is the third iteration on one fault and each earlier step moved it rather than fixing it — raw band, then a spoken palette, then a plain measurement, then a desk-only measurement whose register the desk then adopted ("moving without a measured hold-up"). The lesson, now recorded in the code: ANY English string we supply is copied by whatever reads it, desk or composer. So the fixes are to supply no string, or to supply one so short it cannot be a clause. Deliberately NOT adopted: ARN's suggested "though no delays are measured", which reads better than what aired but is the same mistake — a better phrase chosen in code is still a phrase chosen in code, and it would air identically in every bulletin that hit the branch. Deliberately NOT done: adding phrasing examples to any prompt. The composer prompt lost the positive phrasing examples in its severity block instead, along with the minute-count register they pushed, which contradicted ARN's own corpus (minute counts appear in 3% of 180+ reference reads and never as the lead).

**Consequences:** Verified live across four markets and three deploy rounds. Pace: **six distinct voicings from six instances** — "carrying congestion at a fifth of normal speed", "down to a fifth of normal speed", "moving at a quarter of normal speed", "congested for about half a kay, with traffic down to a sixth of normal speed" — against fourteen fixed strings before. None of `of its usual pace`, `no delay measured`, `barely noticeable`, `the ends of the road are still reachable` or `for the Planned roadworks` reaches air. A general invariant replaces the translator-completeness test it retired: no emitted evidence value may carry any label in `EvidenceLabelVocabulary`, checked across every field rather than one. Four tests that encoded the palette design were rewritten to the new contract rather than deleted, each carrying the measurement that superseded it — including two whose assertion was that corridors in one pace bucket must NOT read alike, which is now false by design: they carry the same value because they measured the same, and the sentences differ because the composer writes them. Also fixed: `reason` required only that the authority's SubCategory differ from its Category, which let "PLANNED ROADWORK" + "Planned roadworks" through; it now requires a genuine proper noun sharing no word with the reason. RESIDUAL, honestly: the anchor "of normal speed" recurs across reads by design, because dropping it lets "a third of normal speed" be rewritten as "a third slower", a different and much smaller claim — four fixed words instead of a whole clause. And the access token change is NOT verified on air: no closure with local access appeared in the final sample, so it is proven only in unit tests.

## 2026-08-31 — Per-condition voicing becomes ARN's, keyed by the incident classes the console already shows

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked to configure how each kind of thing is spoken — congestion one way, closures another, hazards another — with rules like "say chockers for anything with jam factor above 5", rather than us tuning wording on their behalf. The mechanism for this was the strongest part of the system and completely unreachable: `PlaybookOverlay` already supports rewrite, disable, reorder and add over any addressable block, and `PlaybookFlexibilityLiveTests` had proven ten overlay classes including a full style takeover and a hostile edit that could not fabricate because grounding is in code. But no per-condition block existed anywhere; the `voice.road-feel-bands` block that `StationPolicyFor`'s own comment says carries road-feel vocabulary is absent from `compose2.md`; `VoicePolicy` is deliberately returned empty on this path; overlays were applied only to the composer; and the writer desks — which now own qualitative voicing — had no block markers at all, so the studio had nothing to show for them.

**Decision:** The canonical incident classes become a published contract in `IncidentClassCatalog`, and each one gets an addressable voicing block in the desk prompts, keyed `voice.<classid>` by the same ids ARN sets priority boosts against. The desks are block-marked end to end and resolve station playbooks through a shared `StationPlaybook.Resolve`. The class and the measured speed fraction travel to the desk as `DeskOnly` facts so a threshold rule can be evaluated.

**Rationale:** Keying the blocks to the incident-priorities ids means "how do we say a closure" and "how much does a closure matter" are the same word in the console, in storage and in the prompt. The catalogue is treated as published rather than internal because renaming an id orphans a market's boosts AND a station's wording edits at once — silently, since an overlay naming an unknown block is refused, not failed. The classification already existed as a private helper in `TrafficEvidenceBuilder`, where it lived just long enough to add a score bonus and was thrown away, so nothing downstream could be configured per class; it is promoted and the class now travels with the evidence. The measure is handed over as a NUMBER rather than a band because the whole point of the surface is that the judgement is ARN's — a band would be ours. It cannot reach air: `DeskOnly` keeps it from the composer and `DeskConditionCarriesNoFigure` rejects a condition that states it. Guidance is written as CONDITIONAL rules, never a word bank, because the previous attempt at this feature injected `RoadFeelPalette` as authoritative vocabulary and measured WORSE — severe wording on a one-to-three-minute board went 7/10 injected against 0/10 uninjected, the palette having primed the very words it listed. Grounding and the response contract stay system-owned, which is exactly what makes handing the voice over safe.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev across brisbane, melbourne and perth. The incidents desk receives its ten per-class blocks in the system prompt and sees `class` (Breakdown, Closure, Congestion, Crash, Roadworks observed) plus `speed fraction` (0.19–0.64 observed); the flow desk receives its congestion, clear-run and drive-time blocks; the composer sees neither desk-only fact. Two dead wires fixed on the way: `ResolvePlaybookAsync` returned the overlay and DISCARDED the playbook's role, and `StationPolicyFor` then keyed it to "compose2" unconditionally — so a `writeIncidents` or `writeFlow` playbook, both long listed in `SupportedRoles` and both editable in the studio, had its edits applied to a prompt without those block ids and returned as refusals. A station saw a saved playbook that changed nothing. The role now travels on the queue message and the context. Invariants added: the catalogue must match the web's `CANONICAL_INCIDENT_CLASSES` byte for byte, and the incidents-desk prompt must define a voicing block for every class — the check that makes the feature real, since ARN can only configure a class it can address. The provider-type theory was rewritten after inventing `brokenDownVehicle`, which HERE does not emit (`disabledVehicle`), and which `Contains("break")` would not have matched anyway; it now uses `TrafficTypeMapper`'s real vocabulary. STILL OPEN, and both matter for the ask as stated: (1) the measure exposed is the corridor's pace ratio, 0..1 of free-flow, NOT HERE's 0..10 jam factor — "jam factor above 5" is expressible today only as "speed fraction below about 0.5", because `JamFactor` lives on `FlowRoad` and is not carried onto the corridor; (2) `MarketSchedule.PlaybookId` is a single playbook, so a station can target ONE role at a time and cannot yet edit both desks and the composer at once. (3) The studio's ability to render the newly-marked desk prompts is inferred from the block markers and `SupportedRoles`, not verified in the UI.

## 2026-08-31 — ARN-configurable per-condition voicing: the plumbing was dead in four places

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** ARN asked to configure how each kind of condition is spoken, per station, with threshold rules like "say chockers above jam factor 5". The playbook mechanism already existed and was proven flexible, but nothing had ever exercised it on a role other than `compose2`, so the wiring for the desks had never run.

**Decision:** Ship the per-condition blocks keyed to `IncidentClassCatalog`, surface them in the Writer prompt tab under an agent selector, and carry the playbook's target ROLE from resolution through to the workflow.

**Rationale:** Verified live rather than by unit test, which is the only reason it works: every individual piece passed while the feature did nothing on dev. The role was dropped in FOUR separate places, each a hand-copy that a new field is invisible to — `StationConfigResolver.ResolvePlaybookAsync` returned the overlay and discarded `playbook.Role`; `ConversationalScriptGenerator.StationPolicyFor` keyed the dictionary to "compose2" unconditionally; `QueueMessageMappingExtensions.ToBroadcastQueueMessage` passed `Playbook` without `PlaybookRole` on the ad-hoc path; and `BroadcastRequest.CreateWithTraffic` hand-copies thirty fields onto the context and copied `Playbook` but not the role. `JobWatchdog` resolved the role into a local and never passed it. The visible symptom in every case was identical and silent: a `writeIncidents` overlay applied to the composer's prompt, whose block ids it does not share, returned as REFUSALS — so a station saw a saved playbook that changed nothing. Refusals are recorded on the trace, which is why this took four rounds of dev triggers to find rather than four minutes.

**Consequences:** Proven end to end on dev. A melbourne playbook targeting `writeIncidents` with `voice.roadworks` rewritten to "always call a roadworks site CONE COUNTRY" reached that desk and no other (the flow desk's prompt showed none of it), the desk applied it — "CONE COUNTRY southbound at Siddeley Street" — and it AIRED: *"Spencer Street southbound roadworks at Siddeley Street in Southbank are adding ten minutes, and CONE COUNTRY is affecting the southbound run."* A perth playbook targeting `writeFlow` reached the flow desk only, which used "A DREAM RUN". One further fix was needed to get from desk to air: the composer had been told this session that a value's WORDING is not its to keep — correct for values written by code, wrong for the desk's condition, which carries the station's configured voice. Melbourne's "SHUT TIGHT" duly aired as "closed tight". `HOW IT IS BEHAVING` is now the single labelled exception: keep the words or drop the story, never restate. GAP FOUND AND NOT CLOSED: congestion can reach EITHER desk — `BriefDivision.DeskFor` sends a corridor to the incidents desk when an incident sits on it, so perth's Orrong Road arrived there classed `Congestion` at a 0.37 speed fraction, while the only `voice.congestion` block lives on the flow desk. The flow desk held the rule and never saw the road; the incidents desk saw the road and had no rule. Congestion is the one class both desks legitimately hold, so "every class on exactly one desk" — the invariant added to stop ARN having two switches for one behaviour — is wrong for it specifically. Resolving it properly needs multi-role playbooks per station, because a shared block edited on one desk cannot reach the other while `MarketSchedule.PlaybookId` holds a single playbook.

## 2026-08-31 — One station playbook configures every agent: the role qualifier moved inside the overlay key

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** A station's playbook targeted exactly one agent, carried as `BulletinPlaybook.Role` and threaded to the workflow as a `PlaybookRole` field travelling beside the overlay. ARN configures voicing per condition, and conditions are split across two desks plus the presenter, so one station needed one playbook that reaches all three. `MarketSchedule.PlaybookId` is a single id threaded through fourteen sites plus config transfer, import validation and the library usage check, so "several playbooks per station" was the expensive shape.

**Decision:** Qualify the block id inside the overlay: `writeIncidents/voice.roadworks`. `PlaybookOverlay.ForRole(role)` narrows an overlay to one agent — its qualified keys stripped of the qualifier, plus any unqualified keys — and each stage calls it. `PlaybookRole` is deleted from `BroadcastQueueMessage`, `BroadcastContextBase`, `AdHocStationConfig`, the queue mapper, the poller, `JobWatchdog` and `PlaybookPreviewService`. `StationPolicyFor` now offers the one overlay to every supported role and lets each stage narrow it. `BulletinPlaybookService.ValidateOverlay` validates once per role against that role's shipped prompt and refuses an edit only when NO role recognises it, so a typo still fails while a legitimate three-agent overlay passes.

**Rationale:** The alternative was a per-role overlay map on the persisted aggregate, changing `BulletinPlaybookVersion`, its stored JSON, the DTOs, the HTTP surface and the web types — roughly twenty files against five. But the deciding argument was robustness, not size. A field beside the overlay was lost by four independent hand-copied conversions in a single afternoon, each failing identically and silently: the station's edit landed on a prompt without those block ids and came back as a refusal, which presents to ARN as a saved playbook that changes nothing. Information held inside the overlay cannot be dropped by a conversion that forgets a field, because dropping it means dropping the overlay. Unqualified keys stay valid for every role so playbooks written before qualification keep working; their ids exist in exactly one prompt, so a stray match is a no-op refusal rather than a misapplied edit.

**Consequences:** Verified live on dev with three stations configured simultaneously — melbourne, perth and adelaide — each holding ONE playbook that rewrote `writeIncidents/voice.roadworks`, `writeFlow/voice.clear-runs` and `compose2/voice.variety` with station-unique marker phrases. All nine rendered system prompts carried their own marker and none of the other eight, so there is no cross-agent or cross-station leakage; all 52 shipped blocks across the three agents reached their prompt, the only difference being the one rewritten block per role. Every station aired its own markers and no foreign ones, melbourne airing two agents' edits in one read: *"MELBO OPENER Spencer Street southbound at Southbank has roadworks near Siddeley Street, with a ten-minute delay. MELBO CONES are affecting southbound traffic near Siddeley Street."* In the deployed UI each agent tab marks exactly its own edit — Incidents desk "Roadworks and Construction", Flow desk "Clear Runs", Presenter "Vary the delivery" — and saving one agent preserved the other two agents' keys in the stored overlay.

Two findings came out of the live runs. First, all six desks initially put the station's phrase in the story `subject` rather than `condition`; `subject` is a routing label that is never voiced, so the instruction was followed and nobody heard it. The per-class voicing preamble on both desks now states that a block's wording is for `condition` and that `subject` is never copy, which moved placement from 0 of 6 desks to 5 of 6. Second, `voice.congestion` existed only on the flow desk while `BriefDivision.DeskFor` routes a corridor to the incidents desk when an incident sits on it, so a congestion-classed road could reach a desk holding no congestion rule. The block now exists on both desks with different text, and `IncidentClassCatalogTests` no longer demands exactly one desk per class — it requires every class to be configurable somewhere and any dual-desk class to say DIFFERENT things on each, since a queue an incident caused and a queue with nothing behind it are different editorial situations while identical text would be the duplication the original invariant was right to forbid.

## 2026-08-31 — Route every LLM role through versioned Foundry agents for observability

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** LLM calls were invisible. The `dependencies` table's slowest HTTP row
was 2,458ms and contained no LLM calls at all; capture blobs retained only a ~2
